[RESOLVED 2026-08-11 -- see resolution below.] ANALYZE_TRADE'S past_date GATE COMPARES A CITY-LOCAL target_date AGAINST UTC's CURRENT DATE -- REJECTS LEGITIMATELY-STILL-OPEN SAME-DAY MARKETS FOR ~4-8 HOURS EVERY EVENING, PER CITY
Priority: High -- this is analyze_trade's own gate, the live/paper TRADE-ENTRY
  path (order_executor's upstream signal source), not a settlement-only
  concern. Broader blast radius than the sibling entries that found it:
  every same-day HIGH/LOW/between market, every city, not just between-bucket.

Problem:
  weather_markets.py's analyze_trade(), ~line 10585:
    assert target_date is not None
    if target_date < datetime.now(UTC).date():
        ...
        _count_gate("past_date")
        return None  # market target date already passed
  `target_date` is derived from the ticker and represents the market's
  CITY-LOCAL trading day (parse_city_date()). Comparing it against
  `datetime.now(UTC).date()` is wrong whenever UTC's calendar date has
  already rolled over past midnight but the city's local calendar date has
  not -- true for every US city this bot trades (all negative UTC offsets)
  during a multi-hour window every evening: roughly 20:00-23:59 local for
  EDT (UTC-4), 19:00-23:59 for CDT (UTC-5), 18:00-23:59 for MDT (UTC-6),
  17:00-23:59 for PDT (UTC-7) -- i.e. UTC-midnight through each city's own
  local midnight. During that window, target_date (still "today" locally)
  is < UTC's already-rolled-over date, so the gate incorrectly treats a
  market that is still legitimately trading today as already past and
  rejects it outright.

  Live-verified, reproducible right now (checked 2026-08-10 00:15 UTC =
  2026-08-09 20:15 EDT): `tests/test_gaussian_prob.py::
  TestBetweenMarketGaussian::test_between_yes_lock_end_to_end_real_metar_
  lock_in` fails with `gate=past_date target=2026-08-09 today=2026-08-10`
  for a NYC market that should still be tradeable. Confirmed via `git
  stash` (running the same test against unmodified master, commit
  efd11f3) that this is NOT caused by the sibling session's between-bucket
  diff -- it reproduces identically on master alone, purely a function of
  wall-clock time when the test happens to run. This makes it an
  intermittent, wall-clock-dependent failure: it will appear to "pass"
  again once UTC rolls past the affected window, which is exactly why it
  had apparently gone unnoticed -- CI/local runs outside the affected hours
  see nothing wrong.

  NOT independently verified by this filing: (a) whether any other gate in
  analyze_trade or elsewhere in the codebase shares this same UTC-vs-local
  date comparison mistake -- only this one call site was found, by
  accident, via a failing test; a deliberate sweep for `datetime.now(UTC
  ).date()` compared against a city-local target_date elsewhere has not
  been done. (b) whether settlement_monitor.py's own 17:00-19:00 local
  window check is affected -- it uses a different, already city-local-only
  comparison (`_MONITOR_START_HOUR <= local_now.hour < _MONITOR_END_HOUR`
  against `datetime.now(ZoneInfo(city_tz))`), so it is NOT obviously
  exposed to this same bug, but that has not been explicitly proven here.
  Whoever picks this up should re-verify both before scoping the fix.

What it would look like:
  Compare target_date against the CITY-LOCAL current date, not UTC's --
  e.g. `datetime.now(ZoneInfo(_CITY_TZ.get(city, "America/New_York"))).date
  ()`, mirroring the city-local "today" pattern already used elsewhere in
  this same function (_metar_lock_in's own `_local_today`, a few hundred
  lines away) and in settlement_monitor.py. `city` is already in scope at
  this point in analyze_trade. Needs its own test(s) pinning the exact
  UTC-rollover-vs-local-evening window per representative timezone (EDT/
  CDT/MDT/PDT), not just a single wall-clock-dependent assertion like the
  one that surfaced this.

Why not now:
  Out of scope for the between-bucket AC3 fix that found it: a completely
  different gate/function (analyze_trade's past_date check, not
  _metar_lock_in or _check_between_settlement), a different bug class
  (UTC-vs-local date comparison, not instantaneous-vs-daily-extreme), and a
  much broader blast radius (every same-day market, every city, not just
  between-bucket) that deserves its own dedicated investigation and test
  sweep rather than a drive-by fix bundled into an unrelated change.

When to revisit:
  No blocking dependency. High priority given real trade-entry impact --
  recommend picking this up soon; it silently suppresses legitimate
  same-day trade signals for several hours every evening, for every city,
  and its wall-clock-dependent nature means it can sit unnoticed in CI
  runs that happen to execute outside the affected window.

Resolution (2026-08-11):
  Root cause fixed in weather_markets.py: analyze_trade() now computes
  `_local_today` once, early in the function, via
  `datetime.now(ZoneInfo(_CITY_TZ.get(city or "", "America/New_York"))).date()`
  (try/except falling back to UTC on ZoneInfo failure, with a warning log),
  and reuses that single value at every days_out/past-date comparison in
  the function -- the past_date gate itself, the hurricane_count/
  storm_order/generic days_out ceiling gates, and the two downstream
  days_out recomputations feeding edge_confidence/sigma scaling.
  _analyze_hourly_trade() (a separate function analyze_trade calls) gets
  its own equivalent local computation via its own coords/tz parameter.

  Explicitly left unchanged, re-verified rather than assumed:
  _forecast_uncertainty() no longer even has a UTC dependency to leave
  alone -- see the M1 finding below, it was simplified to a pure function
  of days_out instead. _days_out_from_close_time() compares two UTC-based
  quantities (close_dt.date() vs UTC today) and is genuinely a different,
  self-consistent bug class -- left as-is (see L4 below for a nuance worth
  noting, not fixing).

  Scope grew substantially past the single named gate, via an opus
  effort=high review (spawned per this project's standing 28-step
  workflow) that traced every consumer of analyze_trade's target_date/
  days_out, not just the literal call sites named in this entry's
  original filing:

  Sites fixed in THIS change (same live trade-entry payload analyze_trade
  already produces, or a split-brain this change itself would otherwise
  have introduced -- both same-payload per the workflow's adjacency rule):
    - weather_markets.py analyze_trade(): past_date gate,
      hurricane_count/storm_order/generic days_out ceiling gates (3
      sites), two downstream days_out recomputations feeding
      edge_confidence/sigma scaling.
    - weather_markets.py _analyze_hourly_trade(): its own days_out calc.
    - weather_markets.py _forecast_uncertainty(): changed signature from
      target_date to days_out -- both real call sites (inside
      _compute_ensemble_prob and the MOS-sigma-fallback path) already had
      a correctly-computed city-local days_out in scope, so this function
      no longer needs (or has) any datetime dependency at all. The
      TestUtcTodayDate test pinning it to UTC was rewritten as a pure
      value-mapping test; its class docstring now scopes what the class
      actually still guards (UTC vs naive system-local, not UTC vs
      city-local).
    - weather_markets.py fetch_temperature_pirate_weather(): the
      is_historical UTC-vs-target_date check that decides forecast vs
      time-machine endpoint -- same bug class already fixed in its sibling
      fetch_temperature_weatherapi(), now consistent.
    - nws.py nws_prob(): days_out (feeding the NWS sigma ladder) was still
      UTC-based even though target_date/city/coords are the same
      city-local values analyze_trade passes in.
    - mos.py fetch_mos()/fetch_mos_best(): added an optional
      `tz: str | None = None` parameter (both call sites -- weather_
      markets.py's analyze_trade and trade_cycle.py's pre-warm -- now pass
      `_CITY_TZ.get(city)`) so the MOS sigma lookup and NAM/GFS model
      routing key off city-local days_out too. None (unknown caller)
      preserves the old UTC-only behavior.
    - tracker.py log_prediction(): now prefers analysis["days_out"]
      (analyze_trade's own, now-corrected value) over recomputing from
      UTC -- recomputing would otherwise create a NEW split-brain this fix
      would have introduced (paper.json's days_out vs the predictions DB's
      disagreeing during the rollover window), not merely leave an old bug
      in place. Falls back to the old UTC-based clamp only when analysis
      lacks a "days_out" key.

  Deferred to a NEW backlog entry (below) rather than fixed here: main.py's
  _feature_importance_days_out and monte_carlo.py's is-past check --
  genuinely separate consumers (model-training feature logging, standalone
  simulation) per the same adjacency test, not the live trade-entry
  payload this change is already touching.

  Explicitly NOT a defect, left as-is: _days_out_from_close_time() (see
  L4 note in the new backlog entry below for a related nuance worth
  documenting).

  Testing: every fixed site got its own new, hand-mutation-tested
  regression test (reverted the fix, confirmed the specific test fails,
  restored, confirmed it passes again) -- not just a suite-wide pass/fail:
    - tests/test_weather_markets.py::TestPastDateGateCityLocal (3 tests):
      same-day-market-not-gated, genuinely-past-market-still-gated, and
      the generic days_out ceiling, all pinned at a fixed 2026-08-10
      00:30 UTC instant across NYC/Chicago/Denver/LA (EDT/CDT/MDT/PDT).
    - tests/test_weather_markets.py::TestUtcTodayDate: rewritten pure
      value-mapping test for _forecast_uncertainty's new signature.
    - tests/test_weather_markets.py::
      TestFetchTemperaturePirateWeatherHistoricalRouting: forecast-vs-

    - tests/test_nws.py (new file): nws_prob's sigma ladder.
    - tests/test_mos.py: fetch_mos's sigma lookup, fetch_mos_best's

    - tests/test_tracker.py: log_prediction prefers analysis["days_out"],
      falls back correctly when absent.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-17 -- re-verified against HEAD before starting (all line numbers had drifted slightly but the bug and both call sites were confirmed unchanged); see resolution note below.] main.py's _feature_importance_days_out AND monte_carlo.py's is-past CHECK STILL COMPARE A CITY-LOCAL target_date/DATE STRING AGAINST UTC TODAY
Priority: Site 1 (main.py) stays Low -- cmd_today only runs on a human's
  manual `today`/`t` invocation (main.py:7056, 9365, 9579), never from
  cron/watch, and feeds only feature_importance's offline training log.
  Site 2 (monte_carlo.py) is RE-PRIORITIZED to Medium -- re-verification
  found `simulate_portfolio` is NOT just a standalone simulation as
  originally framed here: `portfolio_var()` calls it directly, and
  order_executor.py's `_auto_place_trades` (the function placing every
  paper AND live trade on each cron/watch cycle) calls `portfolio_var()`
  as a pre-trade risk gate against `MAX_VAR_DOLLARS` (default $200,
  enabled unless explicitly overridden) -- so this bug genuinely reached a
  live-trade-gating decision, not just a reporting inaccuracy. Because the
  bug always excludes trades in the same direction (UTC-today >=
  city-local-today, never earlier), the effect was one-directional: during
  the daily UTC-rollover window, a still-open position could be wrongly
  dropped from the VaR simulation, UNDERSTATING projected risk and making
  the gate more permissive than intended for that window -- narrow and
  one-directional, but a real safety-gate integrity gap, not merely
  cosmetic. Original filing's "neither gates a live trade entry" framing
  for Site 2 was wrong; corrected here.

Problem:
  main.py ~line 2552 (_feature_importance_days_out):
    return (_date_fi.fromisoformat(target_date_str) - _utc_today_fi()).days
  target_date_str is analyze_trade's own target_date.isoformat() (city-
  local, from parse_city_date()) -- comparing it against utils.utc_today()
  means the feature-importance days_out logged for model training is off
  by one during the same ~4-8h evening window every day, and now also
  disagrees with the (post-fix) days_out in the same analysis dict this
  function is fed from.

  monte_carlo.py ~line 317:
    _is_past = _date_mc.fromisoformat(_tdate) < _utc_today()
  Same shape: _tdate is a city-local date string, compared against UTC
  today.

  NOT independently verified by this filing: whether either site's
  downstream consumer (model training, simulation output) is sensitive
  enough to this off-by-one to matter in practice, or whether it washes
  out in aggregate given both errors are always in the same direction
  (UTC-today is always >= city-local-today, never earlier) and bounded to
  ~4-8h/day. Whoever picks this up should check the actual magnitude of
  impact before assuming this is worth the same priority as a live-trade
  fix.

  Also noted by the same review, informational only, NOT a defect:
  weather_markets.py's _days_out_from_close_time() (used for monthly rain/
  snow/hurricane-next-event's own days_out ceiling gates) is correctly
  UTC-vs-UTC internally consistent (compares close_dt.date(), itself UTC,
  against UTC today) -- genuinely a different bug class from this entry,
  correctly left alone. Worth knowing though: Kalshi's close_time for a
  market described as closing on a given city-local-ET date is an
  evening-ET instant whose UTC date is the FOLLOWING day (e.g.
  "2026-09-15T03:59Z" is 23:59 ET on Sep 14 -- see weather_markets.py's own
  comment near line ~9418), so close_dt.date() slightly OVERSTATES the
  ET-local days-out by one until ~20:00 ET on the market's final day.
  Immaterial against the months-scale RAIN_MAX_DAYS_OUT/SNOW_MAX_DAYS_OUT/
  HURRICANE_MAX_DAYS_OUT ceilings this gates, and the direction is
  conservative (biases edge_confidence/time_kelly_scale down, not up) --
  not worth a code change, just worth knowing if this area gets touched
  again.

What it would look like:
  main.py: thread the city (already available via the enclosing scope --
  check the actual call site) through to a ZoneInfo-based local-today
  computation, mirroring analyze_trade's own `_local_today` pattern.
  monte_carlo.py: same pattern, if the city is available at that call

Priority: Low-Medium -- affects only the `_persistence_prob` fallback path

Problem:

[RESOLVED 2026-08-10] SETTLEMENT_MONITOR.PY'S OWN BETWEEN-BUCKET LOCK HAS THE SAME AC3 BUG THE JUST-FIXED weather_markets.py ONE HAD -- AND IT AUTO-CLOSES REAL PAPER POSITIONS
Priority: Medium-High -- not the live-money entry path (that's analyze_trade/
  order_executor, unaffected by this), but settlement_monitor.py's signals ARE
  consumed automatically: cron.py:1415 acts on any settlement-lag signal with
  confidence >= 0.80 by closing the matching OPEN PAPER POSITION outright
  (`_sig_conf >= 0.80 and _sig_ticker in _open_by_ticker`) -- no human review.
  A wrong signal here doesn't just skip a trade opportunity (this entry's
  sibling's failure mode); it forces an incorrect settlement on a position
  that was already open, which corrupts the graduation Brier score and P&L
  history those paper trades feed into.

Problem:
  settlement_monitor.py's `_check_between_settlement()` (~line 164) and its
  only caller `check_city_settlement()` (~line 210) lock a between-bucket
  settlement signal using ONLY the instantaneous METAR reading
  (`obs["current_temp_f"]`), with:
  - No daily-extreme lookup at all (doesn't touch min_temp_f/max_temp_f --
    which, separately, were themselves silently None until this session's
    metar.py field-name fix landed; even a well-intentioned attempt to add
    daily-extreme logic here before that fix would have kept falling back to
    the instantaneous reading anyway).
  - No hour gate INSIDE `_check_between_settlement()`/`check_city_settlement()`
    themselves -- CORRECTED same day after re-reading `run_settlement_monitor()`
    (~line 299) more carefully: it DOES restrict invocation to a 17:00-19:00
    local per-city window (`_MONITOR_START_HOUR`/`_MONITOR_END_HOUR`, ~line
    92-93) before ever calling into this code, so the original framing here
    ("can fire at any hour") was wrong and has been corrected -- the failure
    scenario below is re-derived to fall inside that real window. The
    remaining gap is real: for most cities the daily high typically peaks
    mid-afternoon (2-5 PM), BEFORE this window even opens, so a 17:00-19:00
    reading is very often already cooling PAST the true peak -- the window's
    existence doesn't fix the instantaneous-vs-extreme conflation, it just
    narrows when it can bite.
  - A YES lock that fires on ANY instantaneous in-band reading with zero
    clearance requirement (`_check_between_settlement`'s own docstring:
    "Clearance only affects confidence, not the lock condition").
  This is functionally the exact "compares current_temp_f to the bucket
  instead of the daily high" bug (AC3) that got weather_markets.py's between
  branch disabled on 2026-06-29 -- reimplemented independently in this
  module, which was never touched by that disable or by this session's fix.
  The docstring's own claim -- "Lock logic (mirrors _metar_lock_in in
  weather_markets.py)" -- is false today (and was arguably already stale
  before this session, since it never matched the ACTUAL pre-disable
  _metar_lock_in implementation's date-guard or clearance requirements
  either; not re-verified against the pre-ceda79d code).

  Concrete failure scenario (independently verified live via
  `check_city_settlement`'s actual code AND `run_settlement_monitor`'s real
  17:00-19:00 gate, not asserted): HIGH-series between market, band
  [85.5, 87.5]. The day's actual high, 86.5°F (a real YES), occurred at
  15:00 -- before the monitor's window even opens. By 18:00 (inside the
  real 17:00-19:00 window) the station has cooled to 76.0°F, a ~10.5°F
  afternoon-to-evening drop plausible after a cold-frontal passage or
  thunderstorm outflow, not a routine every-day swing but a real,
  recurring one. clearance = 85.5 - 76.0 = 9.5 >= _SETTLEMENT_MARGIN_F +
  1.0 (2.0) -> locks NO at confidence min(0.95, 0.60 + 9.5*0.03) = 0.885.
  cron.py's >= 0.80 auto-execution threshold fires and force-closes the
  open YES paper position at a loss -- on a position that was actually
  going to win. (The YES side of this same bug is architecturally capped at
  confidence 0.75 for a 2°F-wide band -- min(0.95, 0.70 + clearance*0.05)
  with clearance bounded at the band half-width, 1.0°F -- always under
  cron's 0.80 threshold, so in practice only the NO direction currently
  auto-executes from this bug. This is the exact same "confidence formula
  capped below the threshold that matters" bug shape independently found
  in the sibling weather_markets.py entry's between_edge gate -- worth
  keeping in mind when re-deriving the fix here, since a naive port of
  that fix's margin numbers could reproduce the same unreachable-ceiling
  mistake in a new place if not re-checked against THIS module's own
  0.70/0.05 confidence formula, which differs from weather_markets.py's
  _dynamic_lock_in_confidence.)

What it would look like:
  Same fix shape as the weather_markets.py sibling entry, scoped to this
  module: key `_check_between_settlement()` off a real daily extreme
  (min_temp_f/max_temp_f, now available thanks to this session's metar.py
  fix) instead of current_temp_f. The 17:00-19:00 caller-side window
  (`run_settlement_monitor`) does NOT need an hour gate added inside this
  function the way weather_markets.py's 14:00 gate did -- that window
  already exists and is the wrong kind of guard to add a second one of;
  what's missing is using the daily extreme AT ALL. Re-derive safe NO/YES
  lock conditions using the same monotonic-safety reasoning (NO only on
  the side the running extreme has already irreversibly cleared; YES only
  with real margin against the one at-risk edge, and re-check the actual
  achievable confidence range against THIS module's own 0.70/0.05 YES
  formula and 0.60/0.03 NO formula -- not weather_markets.py's
  _dynamic_lock_in_confidence -- before picking a margin). Whether to
  literally share code with weather_markets.py's
  `_metar_lock_in` between branch or keep a parallel implementation (this
  module's return shape / signal-building pipeline differs) is a real design
  choice for whoever picks this up -- not decided here.

Why not now:
  Out of scope for the sibling entry's own fix: genuinely separate module,
  separate call chain (main.py -> run_settlement_monitor -> check_city_
  settlement, not analyze_trade), separate consumer (cron.py's settlement-lag
  auto-execution, not order_executor's trade-entry path), and its own

When to revisit:
  No blocking dependency -- metar.py's max_temp_f/min_temp_f fix (this same

RESOLUTION (2026-08-10):
  Shipped the fix shape described above, KEY DESIGN DECISION per user
  AskUserQuestion: parallel implementation, not shared code with
  weather_markets.py's _metar_lock_in between branch (this module's flat
  dict return shape and simpler HIGH-only scope didn't justify the
  refactor risk of touching bded3d6's already-shipped code for a shared
  helper).

  `_check_between_settlement(current_temp_f, lower_f, upper_f, max_temp_f)`
  now takes a 4th param and keys the lock off max_temp_f (the running daily
  high), not current_temp_f. NO locks only once max_temp_f (falling back to
  current_temp_f only when max_temp_f is None) has cleared the upper edge by
  >= _SETTLEMENT_MARGIN_F + 1.0 (2.0)°F -- monotonically safe, and the ONLY
  safe NO direction for a HIGH-only market (the old code's symmetric "below
  the lower edge" NO branch is gone entirely -- that was the actual bug: a
  running high sitting below the band does NOT preclude the true high from
  still rising into or past the band later). YES locks only from a REAL
  max_temp_f (never the current_temp_f fallback) with >= half the band width
  of clearance to the at-risk upper edge. `comp_temp = max(current_temp_f,
  max_temp_f)` when max_temp_f is available, hardening against the two
  independently-cached METAR fetches momentarily disagreeing.

  SCOPE EXPANSION mid-session, surfaced via AskUserQuestion and user choice:
  a first opus review round found that metar.py's existing max_temp_f/
  min_temp_f fields (which both this fix's first draft AND the already-
  merged weather_markets.py sibling, bded3d6, depend on) are NOT a true
  running daily extreme -- they're the METAR API's maxT/minT remark-group
  fields, populated ONLY on synoptic-hour (00Z/06Z/12Z/18Z) reports and each
  covering only that report's own preceding 6-hour window. Live-verified
  against aviationweather.gov (KDEN: maxT populated on only 2 of 15 hourly
  reports). User chose to fix the root cause rather than ship a narrower,
  YES-lock-disabled version: added `metar.fetch_metar_daily_extreme(station,
  city_tz, target_date, extreme)` (+ private `_fetch_daily_temps_f`/
  `_extract_temp_f`/`_extract_obs_time` helpers, + a new `_DAILY_OBS_CACHE`,
  15-min TTL, keyed on station+local-date), which fetches a 30-hour window
  of historical METAR observations and computes the TRUE running extreme
  LOCALLY by filtering to the target local calendar date and taking max/min
  of each reading's own temp field -- ignoring the sparse maxT/minT fields
  entirely. Wired into BOTH this module's _check_between_settlement AND
  weather_markets.py's _metar_lock_in (both the above/below AND between
  branches, retroactively correcting bded3d6's own reliance on the same
  sparse fields for its already-shipped between-YES and LOW-market NO
  locks).

  Two rounds of independent opus review (effort: high) before push, matching
  the sibling entry's own precedent given the expanded scope:
  - Round 1 found the metar.py windowed-max root cause above (the scope-
    expansion trigger) plus a fragile float-precision accident: the YES
    branch's confidence ceiling is 0.7999999999999999 < cron's 0.80
    threshold by 1 ULP, not a real designed margin -- documented, not
    "fixed," since changing it either way is a separate design call.
  - Round 2 (after the metar.py scope expansion) found and this session

[RESOLVED 2026-08-09] BETWEEN-BUCKET MARKETS (KXHIGH*-B##.5) ARE PERMANENTLY UNTRADEABLE -- METAR LOCK-IN WAS DISABLED AFTER 2 REAL LOSING TRADES AND NEVER FIXED
Priority: Medium -- not a live-money bug today (fails closed, ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE
  has been False this entire history), but a real, permanent gap in market
  coverage with a known real cost: 2 confirmed losing paper trades before it
  was disabled. Between-bucket tickers (e.g. KXHIGHCHI-26AUG10-B86.5) are,
  per the existing code comment at the gate itself, "Kalshi's most numerous
  temperature-market type" -- this entire class has been silently retired
  from trading since 2026-06-29 (see history below), over 6 weeks before
  this entry was filed.

Problem:
  analyze_trade()'s between-bucket gate (weather_markets.py:10773-10786)
  requires metar_locked=True before a between market can trade at all --
  the reasoning being that plain ensemble sigma (3-5.5°F) is too wide to
  price a ±1°F band with any edge, so only a same-day METAR-confirmed
  observation can justify a trade. _metar_lock_in()'s own "between" branch
  (weather_markets.py:10011-10024) unconditionally returns `False, 0.0, {}`.

  Real history, verified via `git log -S`/`git show`, not assumed from the
  current code comment alone:
  - 2026-06-25 (`e395392`): between-market lock-in WAS live at this point,
    comparing the instantaneous current METAR temp against the [lower,
    upper] bucket (YES if inside the band, NO if >3°F outside either edge,
    confidence via the same _dynamic_lock_in_confidence() above/below
    markets use). It had a date-guard bug: an obs_time near midnight UTC
    converts to ~7 PM the PRIOR local calendar day, so the code was
    comparing yesterday evening's declining temperature against today's
    2°F-wide window before today's actual high had even occurred. Confirmed
    real losing trades from this: "OKC B91.5, SATX B91.5 placed Jun25 05:35
    UTC -- lost Jun25 when actual highs reached 91-92F despite midnight
    temp of ~85F" (both paper trades -- ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE was False the
    entire time order-execution code has existed, well before this date).
    Fixed same day with a local-date guard (compare obs_time's local DATE
    to target_date, not just the hour).
  - 2026-06-29 (`ceda79d`, 4 days later, a broader "close grade-audit-
    flagged correctness bugs" pass), a SECOND, deeper flaw was found even
    after the date-guard fix: the between branch compared the
    INSTANTANEOUS current_temp_f to the bucket, not the running DAILY HIGH
    -- labeled "AC3 violation" in that commit's message. This matters
    because a between market's daily high can still rise later in the day
    even if it's inside (or below) the band right now, the same monotonic-
    safety issue the above/below branch already solves for LOW markets
    (see the `_is_low_mkt` block a few lines above the between branch) but
    never got solved for the two-sided between case. Rather than fix this
    properly, the entire between branch was disabled and its now-
    unreachable implementation code deleted (`git show ceda79d --
    weather_markets.py` shows the full removed logic for reference).
  - `tests/test_phase2_batch_d.py::TestBetweenLockInDynamicConfidence
    .test_between_lock_in_disabled` (added by the same 2026-06-29 commit)
    pins the disabled state and states the re-enable condition: "it
    compares current_temp_f to the bucket instead of the daily high...
    Re-enable only once METAR observations track a daily high/low
    equivalent for between markets."

  THE ACTUAL GAP, verified live in the CURRENT code (not just the history
  above): that re-enable condition already has its infrastructure built and
  has had it since BEFORE the disable -- confirmed by reading the parent
  commit of `ceda79d` (`git show ceda79d^:weather_markets.py`), where the
  above/below branch already computed `_daily_ext = _metar_obs.get(
  "min_temp_f")` or `.get("max_temp_f")` (the exact "daily high/low
  equivalent" the disabled test asks for) completely unchanged by that
  commit. The between branch has simply never been updated to use it --
  nobody has revisited this in the 6+ weeks since. This is NOT a missing-
  infrastructure blocker; it's an unapplied fix sitting right next to
  working reference code the whole time.

  Two more things worth knowing before starting, both re-verified live in
  the current code:
  - The ensemble-based (non-metar-locked) probability path for between
    markets already exists and works: _compute_ensemble_prob()
    (weather_markets.py:5751) has its own between-specific branch
    (weather_markets.py:5867-5874, a Gaussian-CDF probability over the
    [lower, upper] bracket) -- but it's unreachable dead code today, since
    analyze_trade's daily path (weather_markets.py:10932) is gated shut by
    the lock-in check above before ever reaching it, and the only other
    caller (_analyze_hourly_trade, weather_markets.py:9807) never
    constructs a "between"-type condition per its own docstring.
  - The between-bucket gate's own comment (weather_markets.py:10771)
    claims "NO bets already require >3°F clearance (enforced in
    _metar_lock_in)" -- this describes INTENDED design, not current
    behavior; _metar_lock_in's between branch has zero clearance logic of
    any kind today (it returns immediately). Don't trust that comment as a
    description of what's live.

What it would look like:
  Swap the disabled branch's dependence on `current_temp_f` for
  `_daily_ext` (same pattern the above/below branch already uses ~30 lines
  above it, weather_markets.py:9975-9979: `_metar_obs.get("max_temp_f")`
  for HIGH markets, `min_temp_f` for LOW), then re-derive the YES/NO lock
  conditions against that daily extreme instead of the instantaneous
  reading:
  - NO lock (safe/monotonic): daily-high-so-far has ALREADY exceeded the
    upper edge by margin -- a running daily max cannot decrease, so this
    can't reverse. (The original deleted implementation's NO branch also
    fired when daily-high-so-far was BELOW the lower edge by margin --
    that direction is NOT monotonic-safe, mirroring exactly the unsafe
    direction the existing `_is_low_mkt` block already rejects for LOW
    markets. Don't reintroduce it.)
  - YES lock (the genuinely hard, still-unsolved part): daily-high-so-far
    being inside the band right now does NOT mean it stays there -- it can
    still rise and exit on the high side later. This is real design work:
    options include requiring a late-enough local hour that further rise
    is unlikely, a wider inside-band margin than the existing 3°F, or
    concluding YES may only be safely lockable very close to end-of-day.
    This is the actual "dedicated design work" the original disable
    comment referred to -- scoped now to specifically the YES side, not
    the whole feature.
  The already-built _compute_ensemble_prob between-branch (see above)
  means the NON-metar-locked ensemble path likely needs no new work --
  the gap is specifically the metar_locked=True path.

Why not now:
  Disabled 2026-06-29 as a safety fix after a real correctness bug was
  found (not a scope decision made when the feature was first designed --
  it was live and trading before that). Never revisited since; never filed
  as its own backlog entry until now -- it only existed as code comments
  and a test docstring for 6+ weeks.

When to revisit:
  No specific trigger condition -- this is buildable now, independent of
  any other in-flight work, and the "missing infrastructure" the disabling
  test's docstring implies is blocking it has actually been available the
  whole time (see "THE ACTUAL GAP" above). Whoever picks this up should
  start by reading `git show ceda79d -- weather_markets.py` for the exact
  deleted implementation, re-derive the monotonic-safety asymmetry for the
  NO side (straightforward, mirrors the existing LOW-market fix) before
  attempting the harder YES side, and confirm live via `py main.py cron`
  (TRADING_PAUSED=true, no order-placement risk) that between-bucket
  tickers stop hitting the "between_no_metar" gate counter.

What shipped:
  _metar_lock_in()'s "between" branch (weather_markets.py) re-enabled, keyed
  off the daily extreme (_metar_obs["max_temp_f"]/["min_temp_f"], selected by
  ticker HIGH/LOW prefix -- between-buckets exist for both daily-high and
  daily-low series, not just KXHIGH*), never the instantaneous current_temp_f
  -- the exact AC3 violation that got the original implementation disabled.
  Per-observation local-date guard restored (the actual e395392 OKC/SATX
  fix, lost when ceda79d deleted the whole branch). NO-side lock is
  monotonic-safe (fires only once the running extreme has ALREADY cleared
  the opposite edge by the existing 3.0°F margin -- cannot reverse), mirrors
  the existing LOW-market above/below fix, and explicitly does NOT
  reintroduce the deleted implementation's unsafe below-lower-edge-for-HIGH-
  markets direction. YES-side lock (this entry's actual open design
  question) requires the daily extreme inside the band with clearance to the
  one at-risk edge (the edge the monotonic direction hasn't already
  foreclosed) of at least half the band width -- decided, per explicit user
  direction ("what would give us the best chance of making money"), to reuse
  the SAME 14:00 hour gate as above/below markets rather than add a bespoke
  later cutoff: _dynamic_lock_in_confidence's existing hour/clearance scaling
  already prices a marginal early lock into a smaller Kelly stake, so an
  artificial delay would only cost real, price-able edge without adding
  safety a continuous confidence score doesn't already provide.

  TWO INDEPENDENT ROUNDS of Agent(opus, effort=high) review before push (the
  first a 3-agent parallel review scoped by lock-in logic / downstream gate /
  test quality, at the user's explicit request given the size of this
  change; the second a single focused re-verification of the first round's
  fixes) found 7 real bugs in the first draft, all fixed:
  (1) HIGH -- metar.py's fetch_metar() read nonexistent API fields
  "minf"/"maxf"; the real aviationweather.gov payload has no Fahrenheit
  extreme field at all, only "maxT"/"minT" in CELSIUS (verified against a
  live API response: KJFK maxT=32.8, minT=25.6). max_temp_f/min_temp_f had
  been silently None for EVERY METAR observation ever fetched in this
  codebase's history -- affecting the existing above/below branch too, not
  just this new between branch -- so the "already-built infrastructure" this
  entry's own first version described was itself broken the whole time.
  Fixed by reading the real Celsius fields with proper conversion (same bug,
  same fix, also applied to dew_point_f: real field is "dewp" not "dwpf"/
  "dwpt"). New regression tests in tests/test_metar.py pin the real field
  names against the actual captured live payload shape.
  (2) HIGH -- analyze_trade's downstream "between_edge" gate (added in
  a24d547, before between lock-in was ever live) compared
  metar_lockout["current_temp_f"] (the instantaneous reading) against the
  band, while the lock itself was decided on the daily extreme -- the exact
  instantaneous-vs-extreme conflation (AC3) the branch was disabled for,
  relocated one level down into this gate. Fixed by surfacing a new
  "comp_temp_f" key in _metar_lock_in's return dict (the value that actually
  decided the lock, for ALL locked branches -- above/below too) and having
  the gate (and analyze_trade's forecast_temp assignment, which was also
  silently recording the instantaneous reading and polluting the per-city
  station-bias learner -- pre-existing for above/below, fixed here since
  it's the same line) read comp_temp_f instead.
  (3) HIGH -- the YES-lock's confidence calculation passed the NO-side
  _margin (3.0°F) to _dynamic_lock_in_confidence instead of the actual
  in-band margin that gated the lock (_yes_inband_margin, half the band
  width) -- since the in-band clearance can never reach 3.0°F on a narrow
  band, the confidence's clearance factor was always exactly zero, making
  confidence (and therefore Kelly stake) invariant to how safe a given lock
  actually was. Fixed by passing _yes_inband_margin; a dedicated test
  verifies the two margins produce numerically different confidence values
  and catches the swap directly.
  (4) MEDIUM -- the between_edge gate's own threshold was hardcoded at
  1.5°F, but a 2°F-wide band caps the two-sided min-distance-to-either-edge
  at 1.0°F (exactly centered) -- 1.5°F was mathematically unreachable and
  silently rejected every YES lock, forever, uncaught because the whole
  branch was disabled from before this gate was even written. A second
  review round found that a naive current_temp_f->comp_temp_f swap in the
  same fixed formula created a NEW pathology (a ~0.25°F-wide accidental
  sliver once composed with the in-function YES margin); final fix derives
  the threshold as (_hi - _lo) / 8.0, independently re-verified (by the
  second review round) to be non-vacuous and non-redundant against the
  in-function margin for a real 2°F band.
  (5) LOW/test-quality (several, all fixed together) -- an ambiguous ticker
  ("?") silently defaulted to HIGH-market logic instead of refusing to lock;
  a YES lock could fire off the current_temp_f fallback when no real daily
  extreme was available (unlike the NO branches, which stay sound under that
  fallback -- current_temp_f is always a valid bound on the true extreme in
  the NO direction, but says nothing about the extreme in the YES direction);
  a malformed "between" condition missing lower/upper would have silently
  defaulted to a fake [0.0, 0.0] band and fired a confident wrong NO lock,
  now newly reachable since the branch used to return before ever getting
  there -- all 3 now fail closed, each with a dedicated test. ~15 new/
  rewritten tests added: NO/YES boundary mutation tests at both band edges
  (inclusive >=/<=, matching check_metar_lockout's own convention), a
  band-width-proportional-vs-hardcoded-1.0 margin discriminator (wide-band
  test), a LOW-market mirror of the "don't reintroduce the deleted
  implementation's unsafe direction" regression guard (previously HIGH-only),
  a 0.0°F daily-extreme `is not None` vs truthiness mutation test, a 14:00
  hour boundary pair, and a true end-to-end test driving the REAL (unmocked)
  _metar_lock_in all the way through analyze_trade -- the earlier drafts of
  the between_edge gate tests all mocked _metar_lock_in wholesale and
  hand-picked comp_temp_f/current_temp_f independently, which is exactly why
  finding (2) above was invisible to them.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-09] LIVE EXIT PARTIAL-FILLS WERE LOGGED BUT NEVER RECONCILED -- POSITION QUANTITY DRIFTED FROM WHAT WAS ACTUALLY STILL OPEN
Priority: Medium -- live-order-adjacent (order_executor._exit_live_position),
  but ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE is False today so no real position has ever hit this
  path. Picked up while re-checking the "[PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-07-19]
  PAPER AND LIVE POSITIONS ARE TWO LEDGERS WITH ADAPTER GLUE" entry's own
  deferred trigger ("when the next live-position feature lands, using it as
  the third consumer that validates the interface") -- re-verified live that
  no such feature had landed since 2026-07-19, and partial-fill
  reconciliation (already flagged by that entry as "the likeliest" next
  feature, and already sitting as a concrete, non-hypothetical scope note in
  _exit_live_position's own docstring) was picked, per explicit user
  decision, to ship FIRST and serve as that third consumer -- the Position
  read-model itself remains separately unstarted; see that entry for its own
  current status.

Problem:
  _exit_live_position() places an IOC (immediate_or_cancel) SELL to close a
  protected live position; Kalshi's IOC orders can legally partial-fill
  (match what's immediately available, cancel the rest). Previously, a
  partial fill was logged at ERROR ("Manual review needed") and NOT
  reconciled -- the original position row's tracked fill_quantity stayed at
  the full original amount, so the next cycle's _get_live_open_positions()
  would still see the full original quantity as open, risking a future
  protective exit trying to sell more contracts than actually remained.

What shipped:
  execution_log.record_live_partial_exit(order_id, filled_count) -- an
  atomic UPDATE ... SET fill_quantity = COALESCE(fill_quantity, quantity) -
  ? (a relative decrement computed in SQL, not a Python read-modify-write of
  an absolute total) that reduces the original position row's tracked
  fill_quantity by exactly the sold amount, leaving settled_at/exit_price/
  exit_reason/pnl untouched so the position stays open at its new smaller
  size for get_filled_unsettled_live_orders() to keep surfacing next cycle.
  _exit_live_position()'s partial-fill branch now computes the sold
  portion's fee-adjusted P&L (same fee convention as the full-exit branch:
  fee only discounts a genuine gain, never a loss) and realizes it
  immediately via add_live_loss(), same as a full exit, then calls
  record_live_partial_exit() and returns False (position not fully closed,
  remainder retried next cycle -- matches the existing "will retry next
  cycle" semantics already used for the zero-fill case).

  A second, pre-existing bug found by adjacency while writing the first
  integration test (not introduced by this change, but on the exact same
  query path being modified): a filled EXIT order's own logged row is
  itself live=1/status='filled'/settled_at=NULL on ITSELF -- indistinguishable
  in shape from a genuine new entry fill, for BOTH full and partial exits --
  so get_filled_unsettled_live_orders() (and thus _get_live_open_positions())
  would misidentify every live exit order as a brand-new phantom open
  position on the very next call, forever (nothing else ever sets
  settled_at on the exit order's own row). Verified order_type could NOT be
  used as a discriminator instead -- a legitimate taker-cross ENTRY order
  (_replace_live_order) also logs order_type='market'. Fixed by adding a new
  closes_position_id column (migration v17, _SCHEMA_VERSION 16->17), set via
  log_order(..., closes_position_id=position["id"]) only on the exit order's
  own logging call in _exit_live_position, and excluded via "AND
  closes_position_id IS NULL" in get_filled_unsettled_live_orders()'s query.
  Confirmed against the real production execution_log.db: schema at
  user_version=16 with 0 live rows today, so this is a clean upgrade with no
  phantom rows to backfill.

  Independent Agent(opus, effort=high) review before push found 3 more real,
  in-scope issues on the same payload this change already touches, all
  fixed in the same pass:
  (1) MEDIUM -- get_today_live_spend() (feeds the MAX_DAILY_SPEND gate that
  hard-blocks new entries) summed quantity*price over every non-failed/
  canceled/amended live row, including exit orders' own rows -- a SELL that
  reduces existing exposure isn't new capital deployed (matching the
  reasoning _exit_live_position already applies by skipping this same gate
  for exits), and this fix's own closes_position_id column made the
  omission newly compound: a position whose IOC exit partial-fills every
  cycle logs a fresh exit-order row each retry, each one inflating the
  counter again. Added the same "AND closes_position_id IS NULL" filter
  there.
  (2) MEDIUM -- record_live_partial_exit's first version computed the
  remaining quantity in Python (read fill_quantity, subtract, write the
  absolute result back) -- a genuine read-modify-write race: two processes
  (e.g. cron and a concurrent `watch --auto --live`) reacting to the same
  stale position could both read the same pre-decrement value and each
  write the same wrong "remaining" total, silently losing one of the two
  reductions. Changed to the atomic SQL decrement described above, and the
  function's own parameter renamed from remaining_quantity (an absolute
  target) to filled_count (a delta) to make the contract self-evident.
  (3) LOW -- a docstring claim that fill_quantity had exactly one reader on
  an open-position row was false (order_executor._poll_pending_orders'
  settlement loop also reads it on the same row shape) -- the resulting
  behavior was verified still correct by the reviewer, but the false claim
  itself was corrected since it would mislead whoever touches this next.
  4 more LOW findings were process/documentation only (log severity for a
  reconciled partial fill bumped WARNING, per-branch phantom-position test

  presence test's expected-columns set was stale, and this entry itself

  1 LOW/informational finding (hoisting entry_price/id reads to the top of
  _exit_live_position means a malformed position dict now raises before the
  gate check and before order placement, instead of after a live order was

  IMPROVEMENT over the prior ordering (fail before risking a live order, not
  after), and is unreachable today regardless since the only real producer,

[RESOLVED 2026-08-17 -- see resolution below.] AGGREGATE-ONLY P&L ACCOUNTING FOR PARTIAL LIVE EXITS UNDER-REPORTS PER-TRADE TAX CSV AND THE DASHBOARD'S total_pnl SUMMARY
Priority: Low -- reporting/accounting completeness only, not a live-order
  safety gate; today's aggregate daily total (execution_log.get_today_live_loss(),
  fed by add_live_loss()) IS correct in real time. ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE is False,
  so there is no live data to under-report yet.

Problem:
  A live position row's own pnl/settled_at are only ever written at that
  row's FULL closure (record_live_early_exit()/record_live_settlement()) --
  true before the partial-fill reconciliation fix above and still true
  after it, by design (the position isn't closed, just smaller). This means
  a partial exit's realized P&L is reflected immediately in the day's
  aggregate total (add_live_loss) but never becomes its own row anywhere,
  so two per-position/per-trade views silently miss it going forward:
  execution_log.export_live_tax_csv() (per-trade tax reporting -- a position
  that had one partial exit and one final full exit would show only the
  final exit's smaller-quantity P&L, not the true combined total) and
  execution_log.get_live_pnl_summary()'s today_pnl/total_pnl fields (the
  dashboard's headline P&L numbers), both of which SUM(pnl) only over rows
  where settled_at IS NOT NULL.

Recommendation (not yet actioned -- filed for later decision):
  If/when this needs fixing, the likely shape is either (a) give each
  partial exit its own lightweight settled row (a "closed_quantity" child
  row referencing the original position, mirroring how closes_position_id
  already links an exit order to what it closed) that both export functions
  can SUM(pnl) over alongside the original row's eventual final-closure
  pnl, or (b) a dedicated running total column on the original position row
  that both functions read instead of a single point-in-time pnl. Needs a
  design decision (AskUserQuestion) before implementing either -- explicitly
  deferred rather than guessed at when this entry was filed, since
  ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE being off means there's no real urgency forcing the
  choice yet.

Resolution (2026-08-17):
  Re-verification before implementing found option (a)'s "child row" already
  exists: order_executor.py's _exit_live_position() logs a fresh row per
  exit attempt via execution_log.log_order(..., closes_position_id=
  position["id"]) BEFORE placing the order (line ~1230), so every partial
  exit already has its own row -- it just never got settled_at/pnl written
  to it. This made (a) a much smaller change than either option as
  originally scoped, and the AskUserQuestion (asked twice, second pass with
  full technical detail per option) confirmed (a) over (b).

  Two changes:
    - order_executor.py's partial-fill branch (~line 1287) now also calls
      execution_log.record_live_early_exit(log_id, exit_price, reason,
      partial_pnl) targeting the EXIT ORDER's own row (log_id), not the
      position's row (position["id"] stays open/untouched, unchanged from
      before -- still needed so the remainder keeps surfacing for a future
      exit attempt).
    - execution_log.py's export_live_tax_csv() SELECT gained a self-LEFT
      JOIN (orders AS pos ON pos.id = o.closes_position_id) and two COALESCE
      fixes: quantity now reads COALESCE(fill_quantity, quantity) (a partial
      exit row's own `quantity` is the originally-REQUESTED IOC amount, not
      what actually sold), and price now reads COALESCE(pos.price, o.price)
      (a partial-exit row's own `price` is its OWN exit price, not the
      position's entry price -- the join pulls the true entry price from
      the referenced position row; falls through to the row's own price
      unchanged for ordinary settlement/full-exit rows, which have no
      closes_position_id match).
    get_live_pnl_summary() needed ZERO changes -- its SUM(pnl) already
    aggregates any row with settled_at+pnl set, so it automatically picks up
    the newly-settled partial-exit rows once the first change above lands.

  Tests: three new tests in tests/test_live_execution.py's TestExitLivePosition

Problem (as originally filed 2026-08-09 -- expanded/superseded by the
  2026-08-17 UPDATE below, kept for history):
  main.py's cmd_order (the manual buy/sell CLI command) logs via
  `log_order(ticker, side, int(count), price, order_type=action)` --
  positionally, with no live=True keyword at all, so even a manual order
  against the REAL client is logged as live=False by default. Two
  compounding gaps if this path is ever used for a real live sell: (1) it
  never passes closes_position_id, so it would reintroduce the exact
  phantom-open-position bug the sibling entry above just fixed for the
  automated path, and (2) it never reduces the original position's
  fill_quantity on a partial fill either, so a manual partial-fill exit
  would leave the position's tracked size wrong the same way the automated
  path did before that fix. Whether gap (nothing marked live=True) is itself
  a bug or intentional (e.g. cmd_order may be paper-only in practice, or
  gated elsewhere before reaching here) was NOT investigated -- flagged
  as-is from the opus review that surfaced it, not independently re-verified
  against cmd_order's full call graph.

Recommendation (2026-08-09, superseded by the 2026-08-17 UPDATE below):
  First confirm whether cmd_order's sell action can actually reach a real
  live order today (trace its full call graph and any live/paper gating
  around it) before deciding whether this needs the same closes_position_id
  + fill_quantity-reduction treatment _exit_live_position now has, or
  whether it's genuinely paper-only and this is a non-issue.

UPDATE 2026-08-17 (full investigation completed, no code changed yet --
  this is the deferred trace the 2026-08-09 filing asked for):

  Reachability, corrected: the 2026-08-09 Priority's "No live order has ever
  gone through this command (ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE is False)" cites the WRONG
  gate. cmd_order never checks ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE at all -- that flag only
  gates cron.py's graduation check (cron.py:332) and order_executor.py's
  separate micro-live auto-trading path (order_executor.py:3163-3172).
  cmd_order's real gate is trading_gates.pre_live_trade_check() (called at
  main.py:4522-4528, guarded by `getattr(client, "base_url", None) !=
  DEMO_BASE` at main.py:4521), which requires LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true
  (trading_gates.py:69-70) -- confirmed unset in the live .env (only
  KALSHI_ENV=prod is set there), so the "hasn't fired yet" bottom line
  holds, but for a different reason, and the two flags are NOT coupled --
  someone could flip LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true for an unrelated reason
  without realizing it also arms cmd_order's buy/sell path.

  Also: main.py's KALSHI_ENV=prod startup banner (main.py:9328-9350) prints
  "Live orders are NOT placed by this command -- only `watch --auto --live`
  can" (main.py:9344) for every command OTHER than `watch --auto --live`,
  including `buy`/`sell` -- its own guard (`_live_orders_possible`,
  main.py:9333, `cmd == "watch" and "--auto" in args and "--live" in args`)
  is entirely independent of cmd_order's real gate (pre_live_trade_check).
  The moment LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true, this banner statement is FALSE for
  cmd_order specifically -- an operator could have live orders active via
  cmd_order with the console actively (and wrongly) reassuring them
  otherwise. (The banner's own code comment, main.py:9330-9332, repeats the
  same wrong-gate reasoning the original 2026-08-09 filing made.)

  The real bug, traced through cmd_order's full post-fill path
  (main.py:4568-4688) -- bigger than the original title:
    1. main.py:4568 -- `log_order(...)` never passes live=True.
       execution_log.log_order's `live` kwarg (execution_log.py:170)
       defaults to False. Confirmed: EVERY order placed through cmd_order,
       even a real one sent to the live API via client.place_order()
       (main.py:4571), is logged live=False in execution_log's orders table.
    2. main.py:4637 -- after ANY successful fill, BUY or SELL alike (no
       branching on `action`), cmd_order unconditionally calls
       paper.place_paper_order() "for P&L/Brier tracking" (see the print at
       main.py:4653-4656). place_paper_order (paper.py:885) has no `live`
       parameter and no concept of "this fill closes an existing position"
       -- confirmed it always appends a brand-new row to paper_trades.json's
       `data["trades"]` list (paper.py:981-1015, id = max existing + 1) and
       deducts from the SIMULATED paper balance (paper.py:1027,
       `data["balance"] -= cost`), never the real account. One nuance the
       first-pass writeup missed: place_paper_order has a duplicate-open
       guard (paper.py:964-979) that raises ValueError if an unsettled
       paper_trades.json row already exists for that ticker -- so a SELL of
       a position that was itself already phantom-recorded via a prior
       cmd_order BUY gets blocked (caught by cmd_order's own try/except at
       main.py:4686, prints a warning, no second phantom row). The "SELL
       silently opens a NEW phantom position" failure mode is real
       specifically for the more common real-world sequence: a live
       position opened automatically via `watch --auto --live` (which never
       touches paper_trades.json -- it uses execution_log/LivePositionStore
       exclusively) and then manually closed via cmd_order sell. In that
       sequence there is no existing paper_trades.json row for the ticker,
       so place_paper_order succeeds and creates a brand-new OPENING trade
       at the sell's side/price.
    3. That same paper_trades.json store is what
       paper.check_paper_position_exits() (paper.py:1438) and
       paper.check_model_exits() (paper.py:2286) manage on EVERY automated
       cron/watch cycle -- confirmed called every cycle at cron.py:1683
       ("check_paper_position_exits() also runs from watch's automated
       loop", per that line's own comment). Their exit function,
       paper.close_paper_early() (paper.py:1261-1296), only ever updates the
       JSON file (settled flag, balance, pnl) -- confirmed by reading its
       full body: no client.* call anywhere in it.

  Put together: a real live BUY placed via cmd_order is invisible to every
  live-position mechanism (execution_log's live=1 rows, LivePositionStore,
  _exit_live_position) and instead gets absorbed into the ordinary paper
  simulation. The very next cron/watch cycle's stop-loss/model-exit check
  will find it, decide to exit it, and call close_paper_early() -- which
  silently marks it "closed" in the bot's own books and credits the
  SIMULATED balance, while placing NO real sell order against Kalshi. The
  actual live position remains open and completely unmanaged on the real
  exchange, indefinitely, with the bot believing it's closed. A cmd_order
  SELL of a position that was opened automatically (the common case)
  compounds this differently: it creates a phantom NEW opening paper
  position at the sell side/price instead of closing anything -- the exact
  phantom-open-position bug class this repo's `_exit_live_position` fix
  already resolved for the automated path, now reachable again via this
  separate manual entry point.

  Re-prioritized: this is not "Low, manual-only, dormant." It's a real,
  reachable-the-moment-one-env-var-changes bug where the bot's own
  protective-exit automation can silently abandon a real, unmanaged live
  position while believing it closed it -- a genuine capital-loss risk, not
  a bookkeeping gap. Treated as High, live-order-safety tier, same weight as
  the DEMO_BASE smoke test entry (L5410) this repo already has flagged High.

Recommendation (2026-08-17, supersedes the 2026-08-09 one above -- needs a
  design decision, not a quick patch):
  The 2026-08-09 filing's proposed fix (add closes_position_id +
  fill_quantity reduction to mirror _exit_live_position) assumed cmd_order
  already uses the live-position machinery, just incompletely. It doesn't
  use it AT ALL. The real question: should a real live fill from cmd_order
  route through execution_log/LivePositionStore (log_order with live=True,
  no place_paper_order call for the buy side; for sell, look up the
  matching open live position via
  execution_log.get_filled_unsettled_live_orders() and call
  record_live_early_exit()/record_live_partial_exit() with
  closes_position_id, mirroring _exit_live_position exactly) instead of
  paper.place_paper_order() -- so it gets picked up by the SAME automated
  protective-exit scanner real positions from `watch --auto --live` use?
  This is a real architecture decision (does cmd_order become a second real
  entry point into the live-position system, duplicating logic
  _exit_live_position/_auto_place_trades already have, or does it call into
  a shared helper factored out of those?) that needs AskUserQuestion before
  any code is written -- do not guess at the shape.
  Also needs handling: what happens to a REAL fill recorded via cmd_order
  BEFORE this fix ships -- any historical rows already silently living in
  paper_trades.json as phantom paper trades need a data audit, not just a
  go-forward code fix. Confirmed currently moot only because
  LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED has never been set true in this environment -- verify
  that assumption again before treating it as safe to skip.
  Scope boundary: does not touch order_executor._exit_live_position or
  _auto_place_trades themselves -- both already correctly use the live-
  position machinery; this entry is entirely about cmd_order's own,
  structurally different (and wrong) recording path.
  Tests needed: prove a real (mocked live) cmd_order buy creates a row in
  execution_log with live=1, NOT a paper_trades.json row -- plus a positive
  control proving today's actual behavior (a paper_trades.json row IS
  created, execution_log stays live=0) so the bug is provably reproduced
  before it's provably fixed. Same for a sell correctly resolving
  closes_position_id against an existing live position instead of creating
  a new phantom entry. Mock LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true the way
  tests/test_trading_gates.py's `_PROD_ENV` fixture already does
  (`{"KALSHI_ENV": "prod", "LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED": "true"}`), since none of
  this is reachable without it.

RESOLUTION 2026-08-17:

  ARCHITECTURE (confirmed via AskUserQuestion before any code was written,
  per this entry's own Recommendation above): cmd_order's live fills now
  route through execution_log/LivePositionStore instead of
  paper.place_paper_order(). A new shared helper,
  execution_log.record_live_exit_fill(position, fill_count, exit_price,
  reason=None) -> (pnl, fully_closed), was extracted from
  order_executor._exit_live_position's inline fee-adjusted P&L formula so
  both the automated exit scanner and cmd_order's manual sell use the exact
  same math -- _exit_live_position was refactored to call it too (pure
  refactor; its own 105-test suite, tests/test_live_execution.py, passes
  unchanged, confirming behavior-preservation). Live orders are placed
  immediate-or-cancel (time_in_force="immediate_or_cancel") instead of the
  prior GTC default -- a deliberate, AskUserQuestion-confirmed trading-
  behavior change for the manual live path specifically (it can no longer
  place a patient resting limit order); demo/paper mode keeps GTC,
  unaffected either way. For a live SELL with no matching tracked live
  position, the fix places the order regardless (it still reaches the real
  exchange) but does NOT mirror it into paper -- confirmed via
  AskUserQuestion, see the ROUND 2 fix below for what "recorded correctly"
  actually required.

  ROUND 1 -- first opus review (effort: high) on the initial implementation
  found it was structurally correct but did not actually work, plus several
  real adjacent bugs:
    H1 (the fix silently never worked): Kalshi's real order-status enum is
      resting/canceled/executed -- there is no "filled". The code stored
      Kalshi's raw status string directly; execution_log.
      get_filled_unsettled_live_orders() hardcodes `status = 'filled'`, so a
      live position placed via cmd_order could never surface to the
      protective-exit scanner regardless of anything else the fix did.
      FIXED: route through order_executor._kalshi_status_to_internal()
      before writing to execution_log or deciding control flow, matching
      every other live-order call site's existing convention.
    H2 (partial-fill-then-cancel silently dropped): a `status in ("rejected",
      "canceled"): return` early-return fired before any bookkeeping ran,
      discarding a genuine partial fill. FIXED: gate on the TRANSLATED
      status instead of the raw one.
    H3 (position unmanageable even once visible): log_order() never passed
      close_time (positions._passes_exit_gates fails CLOSED without it,
      never exits) or entry_prob (order_executor._check_live_model_exits
      skips a position with entry_prob None). FIXED: pass both (only when
      the analysis fetch succeeded, same as every other optional field
      already threaded through cmd_order) plus forecast_cycle.
    M4 (no quantity reconciliation): a sell for more than the matched
      position's tracked quantity would inflate computed P&L past the
      position's real size. FIXED: clamp fill_count to position["quantity"]
      inside record_live_exit_fill.
    M5 (no concurrency guard): record_live_early_exit/record_live_partial_exit
      had no settled_at guard, so a manual sell racing the automated
      cron/watch exit scanner against the same position could double-settle
      or double-count P&L. FIXED (first pass): WHERE settled_at IS NULL,
      both functions return a bool, record_live_exit_fill raises
      RuntimeError on a lost race instead of silently succeeding.
    M8: an unrelated pre-existing test assertion (assert reason == "ok" in
      test_client_prod_base_url_reaches_full_gate) was accidentally orphaned
      while editing the file. Restored.
    All new tests originally mocked an unrealistic "status": "filled" Kalshi
    API response -- exactly why H1 shipped undetected. Fixed to use real
    "executed"/"canceled" values throughout.

  ROUND 2 -- a SECOND independent opus review (effort: high) of the
  round-1-fixed diff found the fixes themselves had two more severe bugs,
  proven via empirical reproduction (not just static reading), plus a
  subtler race the round-1 guard didn't close:
    NEW-H1 (worse than the original bug): the "no matching position, record
      it anyway" design for an unmatched live sell wrote live=1/
      status='filled'/settled_at=NULL/closes_position_id=NULL -- EXACTLY the
      shape get_filled_unsettled_live_orders() reads as an open LONG
      position. A real reduce-only sell would be misread as a brand-new
      entry the bot just bought, and the protective-exit scanner would later
      place a REAL exit sell against it -- an actively wrong phantom
      position, not just an invisible one. FIXED: immediately self-settle
      that row (execution_log.record_live_early_exit with a distinct
      "unmatched_sell" exit_reason and pnl=0.0 -- unknown, not a real claim,
      since there's no tracked entry_price to compute one against) so it
      can never be read as open, while still preserving the historical
      record that the sell happened.
    NEW-H2 (crash risk): the round-1 RuntimeError-on-lost-race was never
      caught by _exit_live_position's own two call sites. Uncaught, it would
      climb through LivePositionStore.exit() into the watch/cron loop, which
      has no generic exception handler (only KeyboardInterrupt) -- crashing
      the ENTIRE live process from a race on just ONE position, leaving
      every OTHER live position unprotected until manual restart. FIXED:
      both call sites now catch RuntimeError, log, and return
      True/False as appropriate (matching the existing "lost this cycle,
      retry next" pattern already used for an unfilled/illiquid IOC).
    NEW-M2 (a race the settled_at guard didn't close): Writer A partially
      exits a position (settled_at deliberately stays NULL); Writer B,
      holding a STALE snapshot from before A's write, computes a full-close
      off the stale (larger) quantity -- the settled_at-only guard doesn't
      catch this since the row isn't settled yet. FIXED: record_live_early_exit
      gained an optional expected_quantity parameter (compared against
      COALESCE(fill_quantity, quantity) in the same UPDATE's WHERE clause,
      optimistic-concurrency style); record_live_exit_fill's full-close
      branch always passes it. record_live_partial_exit also gained a
      `COALESCE(fill_quantity, quantity) >= filled_count` guard so a stale
      DELTA can never drive fill_quantity negative (this doubles as the fix
      for NEW-L2: a negative/zero fill_quantity is falsy, which
      _get_live_open_positions()'s `fill_quantity or quantity` fallback
      would have silently misread as "nothing tracked, use the full
      original quantity" -- resurrecting an already-reduced position at its
      stale original size).
    NEW-L6 (defensive): wrapped the live-position lookup in try/except so a
      DB read failure can't block placing a real exit sell (mirrors
      _exit_live_position's own "blocking an exit is exactly backwards"
      reasoning).
    NEW-L9: threaded cycle=order_executor._current_forecast_cycle() through
      to client.place_order() so a manual cmd_order retry gets the same
      server-side idempotency dedup the automated paths already have
      (previously fell back to a random UUID, no dedup).
    NEW-M5: strengthened the pre-existing "Analysis failed" warning with an
      explicit second warning when a LIVE buy proceeds with no close_time --
      the position will have NO automated stop-loss/breakeven coverage,
      not just "won't be tracked in Brier/P&L" as the original message said.
    All fixes re-tested; two NEW tests needed their own fix after landing
    (a wrong assertion value, and a pytest-environment-specific teardown
    PermissionError traced to reading results back via a raw `with
    execution_log._conn()` block instead of the existing get_order_by_id()
    helper -- confirmed via two clean standalone reproductions outside
    pytest that the underlying execution_log logic itself has no real
    resource leak; this was a test-artifact fix, not a production one).

  ACCEPTED, EXPLICITLY REASONED LIMITATIONS (not fixed, per-finding
  reasoning stated rather than silently dropped):
    NEW-M1 (multiple open live positions can legally share a ticker+side --
      order_executor.py's own _get_live_open_positions callers already
      assume this is possible; root cause is the paper-only duplicate/
      exposure blindness this session also filed as its own entry, see
      below): a cmd_order sell only closes the OLDEST matching position --
      closes_position_id is a single column, not a list, matching every
      other exit mechanism in this codebase (_exit_live_position also only
      ever closes one position per call). A full fix needs either schema
      support for closing multiple positions with one order or preventing
      the duplicate-entry root cause in the first place. Mitigated with an
      explicit operator-facing warning when it happens, rather than silently
      leaving the others untouched with no signal.
    NEW-M4 (degraded place_order response): if Kalshi's V2 create succeeds
      but the internal get_order() follow-up fails, place_order() returns
      the raw create response, which has no status/fill_count_fp -- a live
      IOC order that genuinely filled would be recorded status="pending",
      fill_quantity=0. The recovery machinery
      (_recover_pending_orders/_poll_pending_orders) heals this for a BUY
      (an ordinary entry-shaped row) but has no closes_position_id
      awareness, so a matched SELL would not resolve automatically -- the
      same underlying gap that justified going IOC in the first place, now
      one layer deeper (a degraded API response on top of an already-narrow
      case). Narrow enough (two independent failure conditions must both
      occur) and architecturally big enough (would mean teaching the shared
      poller about closes_position_id, which this entry's own scope
      boundary already excludes) to file rather than fix here if it
      recurs -- not filed as a new entry yet since it has never been
      observed, only reasoned about.
    NEW-L1 (a raw "rejected" status, which _kalshi_status_to_internal
      doesn't recognize -- Kalshi's real vocabulary is resting/canceled/
      executed, "rejected" isn't real Kalshi wording -- falls through to
      "pending" rather than a terminal state): self-healing via the normal
      pending-recovery path, just a slightly misleading interim label.
    NEW-L3 (record_live_early_exit/record_live_partial_exit's `return
      cur.rowcount > 0` sits outside the `with _conn()` block): correct
      today because _conn() returns a bare sqlite3.Connection (commits on
      __exit__, never closes) -- matches execution_log.add_live_loss's own
      existing established pattern of reading a result inside `with` and
      returning it after.
    NEW-L4 (Brier/prediction tracking still fires on a manual live SELL,
      logging an entry-shaped prediction for what is actually an exit):
      pre-existing behavior, unrelated to this fix's live/paper routing
      change, just more visible now that it's the only tracking left running
      on the live path.
    NEW-L8 (P&L uses the user's typed limit price, not an achieved fill
      price): matches _exit_live_position's own existing convention exactly
      (same field, same assumption) -- consistent, not a new gap, and
      conservative in direction for a sell (Kalshi fills at limit-or-better).
    M6/NEW-M3 (paper.check_position_limits' exposure caps never read
      execution_log): filed as its own entry below (see
      "paper.check_position_limits' EXPOSURE CAPS ARE STRUCTURALLY BLIND...")
      -- corrected 2026-08-17 same session to state precisely that removing
      cmd_order's accidental (and separately wrong) paper-mirror write IS a
      real regression for cmd_order's own exposure-cap coverage specifically,
      even though the root architectural gap is repo-wide and pre-existing.

  TESTS: 185 tests across the three directly-touched files (tests/
  test_execution_log.py, tests/test_trading_gates.py, tests/
  test_live_execution.py) -- all pass, all newly added ones proven to
  actually catch a revert of the fix they cover (IOC via
  assert_called_once, status translation via the
  _get_live_open_positions() assertion in the partial-fill test, the
  NEW-H1 phantom-position fix via an explicit settled_at + empty-
  open-positions assertion, M4/NEW-M2 clamping/races via dedicated
  concurrent-writer tests in both directions, M8 via the restored
  assertion, NEW-H2 via two dedicated tests proving _exit_live_position
  itself never raises through a lost race). Wide regression sweep across
  every test file touching the changed modules (main.py, order_executor.py,
  execution_log.py, paper.py): 1246 passed. ruff + ruff format + mypy clean
  on all three changed source files.

  BANNER WRONGLY CLAIMS ONLY `watch --auto --live` CAN PLACE LIVE ORDERS --
  FALSE FOR cmd_order (buy/sell) ONCE LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true
Priority: Medium -- informational/console-accuracy only, no trading-
  behavior impact by itself, but directly adjacent to a live-safety gate:
  it can give an operator false confidence that live orders aren't active
  via cmd_order when LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true has, in fact, armed it.

Problem:
  main.py's KALSHI_ENV=prod startup banner (main.py:9328-9350) computes
  `_live_orders_possible = cmd == "watch" and "--auto" in args and "--live"
  in args` (main.py:9333) and, when False, prints "Live orders are NOT
  placed by this command — only `watch --auto --live` can" (main.py:9344)
  for every OTHER command, including `buy`/`sell`. This check is entirely
  independent of cmd_order's actual gate (trading_gates.pre_live_trade_check(),
  called at main.py:4522-4528) -- the moment LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true, this
  banner statement is false specifically for cmd_order, which places real
  orders via the same client.place_order() call `watch --auto --live` uses.
  The banner block's own code comment (main.py:9330-9332) repeats the same
  wrong-gate reasoning ("cron/loop never pass live=True... ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE
  is hard-disabled") the original 2026-08-09 filing of the sibling entry
  made -- ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE is irrelevant to cmd_order, which cmd_order
  never checks at all.
  Discovered during the 2026-08-17 investigation of the sibling entry above;
  filed separately since fixing cmd_order's recording path (that entry)
  does nothing to correct this startup message.

Recommendation (not yet actioned -- filed for later decision):
  Broaden `_live_orders_possible` to also cover `cmd in ("buy", "sell")`
  when LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true -- mirroring cmd_order's own real gate
