[RESOLVED 2026-08-18 -- fixed together with AUD-0001/AUD-0002/AUD-0005/
  AUD-0009/AUD-0012 (2026-08-18 max-depth audit batch-01, same root cause);
  see Resolution below]
  paper.check_position_limits' EXPOSURE CAPS ARE STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO REAL
  LIVE POSITIONS -- paper.get_open_trades() IS THE ONLY SIGNAL THEY EVER READ
Priority: Medium -- a real, repo-wide gap (not specific to cmd_order or to
  this session's fix), but confirmed EMPIRICALLY MOOT today: zero live=1
  rows have ever existed in execution_log (verified via direct query,
  2026-08-17 -- same check the sibling entry above already ran), so there
  is currently no live exposure for these caps to have missed.

Problem:
  paper.get_total_exposure() (paper.py:1620-1623) and
  paper.get_ticker_exposure() (paper.py:1626-1629) both compute their
  totals exclusively from `sum(t["cost"] for t in get_open_trades())` --
  paper.py's own JSON store. paper.check_position_limits() (paper.py:3447),
  the SINGLE shared enforcement point for per-market/portfolio/city-date/
  directional/correlated-group exposure caps across every manual and
  automated placement path in this bot (per its own docstring, "#2: those
  three caps were previously enforced only inside portfolio_kelly_fraction()
  ... every manual order path ... could silently exceed them"), calls
  get_total_exposure() at its MAX_TOTAL_OPEN_EXPOSURE check (paper.py:3645)
  and has no other source of exposure data anywhere in its body. Neither
  function has ever read execution_log for real live positions.
  Confirmed this is NOT specific to cmd_order: order_executor._auto_place_trades
  (the fully-automated `watch --auto --live` path) branches live vs. paper
  as a mutually exclusive if/else (order_executor.py:2966 calls
  _place_live_order for the live branch; order_executor.py:3014-3049 is the
  separate paper `else` branch that calls place_paper_order) -- a live entry
  NEVER also mirrors into paper.place_paper_order(). So exposure caps have
  been structurally blind to the automated live path's own positions this
  entire time, independent of anything cmd_order does.
  Surfaced by this session's cmd_order fix only because, PRE-FIX, cmd_order's
  bug (unconditionally calling place_paper_order() for every live fill,
  buy or sell) happened to ALSO feed this exposure-cap signal as an
  accidental side effect of the recording bug -- never a deliberate
  mechanism, and never true for the automated live path. Post-fix,
  cmd_order's live buys correctly stop writing to paper, which removes that
  accidental signal and brings cmd_order in line with how _auto_place_trades
  has always behaved.

  CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (2nd opus review, NEW-M3): the line above ("not a new
  regression") undersold this. The ROOT architectural gap (exposure caps
  never reading execution_log at all) is genuinely pre-existing and
  repo-wide, but for cmd_order SPECIFICALLY, the fix is a real, concrete
  behavior change: pre-fix, a manual live buy had SOME (wrong in other
  ways, but present) exposure-cap coverage via the accidental paper-mirror
  write; post-fix, it has NONE. That a differently-broken automated path
  already had zero coverage doesn't make removing cmd_order's own
  (accidental) coverage a non-event for cmd_order's own operators -- it is
  a regression for that one path, just one whose root cause and fix both
  belong here rather than in the sibling entry. Still empirically moot
  today (LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED unset), which is why this wasn't treated as
  blocking, but stated precisely rather than downplayed.

Recommendation (not yet actioned -- filed for later decision):
  If/when this needs fixing, get_total_exposure()/get_ticker_exposure()
  (or check_position_limits() directly) would need to also sum cost across
  execution_log's live=1, settled_at IS NULL rows (order_executor.
  _get_live_open_positions() already builds exactly this shape) alongside
  paper's get_open_trades() -- a real design question (one combined
  cross-ledger total vs. two separately-capped totals; whether the
  per-city/date/directional/correlated-group checks, which walk paper's
  trade list structurally, need the same treatment) that needs
  AskUserQuestion before implementing, not guessed at here. Given this is
  currently empirically moot (no live positions exist to be missed), there
  is no urgency forcing the choice.

Resolution 2026-08-18 (batch-01 of the max-depth audit -- see AUD-0001's own
  entry below for the full multi-file fix; this entry's exact recommendation
  was implemented):
  Chose the "one combined cross-ledger total" design via AskUserQuestion
  (the design question this entry's own Recommendation flagged as needing
  one) -- added paper.get_all_open_positions() = get_open_trades() +
  order_executor._get_live_open_positions(), and pointed
  get_total_exposure()/get_ticker_exposure()/get_city_date_exposure()/
  get_directional_exposure()/get_correlated_exposure() at it, PLUS
  check_position_limits()'s own separate inline existing_cost computation
  for the per-market cap (a second blind spot this entry didn't call out by
  name, caught by this session's own test suite). The per-city/date/
  directional/correlated-group checks get the same treatment automatically
  since they walk the same combined list -- no separate design needed for
  that half of the open question.
  _get_live_open_positions() also gained city/target_date backfill (parsed
  from the ticker via weather_markets.parse_city_date) since the raw
  execution_log rows have neither, and the city/date-keyed caps can't see a
  live position without them.
  get_open_trades() itself was deliberately left unchanged -- it has 14
  other callers (P&L reporting, paper-only position management, dashboard
  stats) that require paper-only semantics.
  Tests: tests/test_batch01_live_position_visibility.py (30 tests, incl.
  mutation tests reverting to the pre-fix get_open_trades()-only behavior
  and confirming they'd miss a live-only position). Full repo regression
  sweep across every test file referencing the touched functions: 1193
  passed, 0 failed.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-05] ~13 NON-SAFETY-CRITICAL FILES STILL BYPASS paths.py -- WORKTREE CRON RUNS SILENTLY HIT A STALE LOCAL data/ CACHE
Priority: Medium -- no live-money or trade-correctness impact (DB, paper
  trades, and backups all correctly route through paths.py already), but a
  real, reproduced-today source of spurious API rate-limiting and
  worktree-vs-main-clone cache divergence whenever cron/watch/analysis is
  run from a git worktree (this project's standard dev workflow).

Problem:
  `f94a44b` ("fix(paths): route safety-critical state through paths.py, not
  worktree-local paths", 2026-08-03) fixed the *safety-critical* subset of
  this bug class -- kill switch, black swan, live_config.json, learned/city/
  seasonal/condition weights, execution_log.db, and cron.py's periodic-task
  gate sentinels -- by migrating cron.py, main.py, web_app.py,
  weather_markets.py, calibration.py, monte_carlo.py, execution_log.py,
  cloud_backup.py, config.py, param_sweep.py, and sigma_audit.py to import
  paths from paths.py's single source of truth instead of constructing
  `Path(__file__).parent / "data"` locally (which resolves to *that
  worktree's own* throwaway data/ dir, per paths.py's own docstring warning
  against exactly this pattern).

  That fix was explicitly scoped to safety-critical state, not every file.
  Re-grepped 2026-08-04 for the same anti-pattern
  (`Path\(__file__\)\.parent\s*/\s*["']data["']`) and found it's still
  present in: climatology.py, hurricane_climatology.py, backtest.py,
  alerts.py, feature_importance.py, circuit_breaker.py, acis_snow.py,
  acis_precip.py, ab_test.py, ml_bias.py, notify.py, pdf_report.py, and
  kalshi_ws.py, plus a handful of non-safety-critical spots still remaining
  in main.py/weather_markets.py/web_app.py (export dirs, debug endpoints,
  forecast snapshot/ensemble cache dirs).

  Live-reproduced same day running `py main.py cron` from a worktree
  (`cron-output-analysis-06b2db`) for output analysis: the worktree's own
  local `data/` had only 8 of 20 cities' `climate_*.json` cache files
  (stale/incomplete, likely dating from whenever this worktree was
  created), vs. the main clone's complete, fresh (2026-08-01) set of 20.
  `climatology.py`'s `fetch_historical()` read `cache.exists()` against the
  worktree-local path, found it missing for the other 13 cities, and made
  live calls to `archive-api.open-meteo.com` -- which came back 429 (Too
  Many Requests) for all 13, so those cities silently got `None` for their
  climatology baseline that cycle (`fetch_historical: API failed for X and
  no cache exists -- returning None`). No trades were misfired (nothing in
  this list feeds live-order gates), but it's wasted/rate-limited API calls
  every worktree cron run, a degraded model input for whichever cities miss
  the cache, and a forked climatology/ML-artifact/forecast-cache state
  between the worktree and the main clone that never reconciles.

  Opus review (2 parallel agents, effort=high, scoped by subsystem --
  "hot path" cron/watch/web files vs. "data/ML/offline" files, matching
  f94a44b's own 2-review precedent) found 13 issues total, all addressed:
  - HIGH: weather_markets.py's forecast/ensemble disk-cache paths had NO
    test isolation, and both have an `atexit`-registered flush -- proven
    LIVE: 9 fake NYC/Chicago/Dallas forecast entries (obvious fixture
    payloads, e.g. flat 65.0/50.0 highs/lows) had already landed in the

    redirect at fixture teardown, which happens BEFORE the interpreter's

  - MEDIUM: the same class of issue for `main.py`'s crash log -- `main.py`

    insurance, not a fix for a known failure -- this migration makes
    `paths` import much earlier/more widely, so a mkdir failure here is
    closer to a total-import-crash path than it used to be), and a
    paths.py comment that overstated the FORECAST_CACHE_PATH bug's
    real-world impact was qualified to note it was never actually live in
    the deployed configuration (cwd and `__file__` already agreed there),
    only in worktree/manual-cwd runs.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-04] GFS_LOCKOUT_MINS=90 DOESN'T MATCH REAL GFS PROPAGATION DELAY -- BLOCKS ~25% OF EVERY DAY FOR WEAK PROTECTION
Priority: Medium -- real, measurable opportunity cost with no confirmed
  safety benefit; not a live-money issue today (cron places paper trades
  only, live=False) but worth fixing before it matters more.

Problem:
  Found 2026-08-03 while analyzing a live cron run: order_executor.py's
  `_in_gfs_update_window()` (order_executor.py:69) blocks all multi-day
  (`days_out >= 1`) trade placement for 90 minutes after each of GFS's 4
  daily init times (00/06/12/18 UTC), per the `GFS_LOCKOUT_MINS` env var
  (default 90). The docstring's rationale: "Open-Meteo may be serving the
  previous model run [for] ~90 min" after each init.

  That 90-minute figure does not match GFS's real production/propagation
  timeline. Verified two ways, both re-checked against raw source data (not
  a summarizing tool) to be sure:
  1. NCEP's own production status page (nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/nwprod/
     prodstat/), parsed directly: even the FASTEST downstream GFS product
     ("12hr PRODUCTS") doesn't complete until T+3h41m-3h55m after cycle
     start (e.g. 12z 2026-08-03: complete 15:40:45, cycle start 12:00). The
     full run (F000-F384) completes at T+5h10m-5h14m, consistent across
     all 4 cycles checked that day.
  2. Open-Meteo's own docs (open-meteo.com/en/docs/single-runs-api), exact
     quote pulled from raw HTML: "typically 4-6 hours for global models
     (e.g. ECMWF IFS, GFS) ... a run initialised at 00 UTC is generally
     accessible from approximately 04-06 UTC onwards."
  A live spot-check (curl against Open-Meteo's Single Runs API) found
  2026-08-03's 12z run still not indexed at T+7h17m, while the 06z run
  (T+13h17m) was -- consistent with "hours, not 90 minutes" as the right
  order of magnitude, though this specific API is a separate archival
  pipeline from the live "latest" endpoint the bot actually queries, so
  it's corroborating rather than definitive on its own.

  Net effect: the gate releases multi-day trading ~3.5-4.5 hours before the
  new GFS run has actually likely propagated, while still costing real
  opportunity -- 90 min x 4 cycles/day = 6h/day (25% of every day) with
  ALL multi-day trades blocked regardless of which specific ticker/field is
  actually stale. Concretely: today's cron run (2026-08-03 18:57-18:59 UTC,
  inside the 18:00-19:30 UTC lockout from the 12z run) blocked 8 of the 10
  edge signals found that scan purely on this gate (the other 2 were
  rejected separately for kelly-too-small).

  No incident or bad trade motivated this gate -- checked the introducing
  commit (`4ddf974`, 2026-06-28, "feat(risk): block multi-day trade
  placement during 90-min GFS model update window", empty body) and did a
  broader backlog sweep (stale forecast / race condition / dates around
  2026-06-25-29) -- nothing found. Appears to have been preemptive/
  speculative defensive coding, not a response to demonstrated harm, given
  this project's otherwise thorough incident documentation elsewhere.

Recommendation (not yet actioned -- filed for later decision):
  Drop the clock-based gate rather than widen it. Widening to match the
  real ~5-6h delay would block multi-day trading for ~20-24h/day (4 cycles
  x 5-6h), which guts the strategy far more than the staleness risk it
  would prevent. There is no live signal in Open-Meteo's response that
  indicates which run is currently being served (checked: the JSON has no
  run-timestamp/generation metadata field), so a clock-based window can't
  be made accurate without becoming this costly.

  A more principled replacement already exists in embryonic form:
  `run_trend_delta`/`run_trend_jumpy` (tracker.py:222-223, "FORECAST
  RUN-TO-RUN TREND SIGNAL") already tracks actual forecast-run stability
  per-ticker via the Previous Runs API, log-only today while its
  correlation with forecast error is being validated (weather_markets.py:
  6332-6336). If that correlation holds up, gating on measured run
  instability (a real signal) is the defensible successor to guessing from
  wall-clock time -- not a fixed window.

What it would look like:
  1. Trace all call sites of `_in_gfs_update_window()` (currently just
     order_executor.py's `_auto_place_trades()`, per a grep on 2026-08-03,
     but re-verify at implementation time) -- matches this project's
     established "trace all call sites for a safety gate" pattern (see
     backlog's repeated TRADING_PAUSED/PAPER_MIN_EDGE/kill-switch history).
  2. Remove the gate and its `GFS_LOCKOUT_MINS` env var (or leave the var
     as an inert no-op with a deprecation note, if anything external still
     references it -- check .env.example and COMMANDS.md too).
  3. Update/remove `tests/test_execution_stability.py::
     test_gfs_window_disabled_with_zero_lockout` and any sibling GFS-window
     tests accordingly.
  4. Full regression sweep on order_executor.py and its test file.

Why not now:
  Filed for later decision rather than implemented immediately -- user
  asked to record the finding, not act on it this session.

When to revisit:
  Whenever picking up general backlog items, or specifically alongside any
  future work that validates/graduates `run_trend_delta`'s correlation
  with forecast error (weather_markets.py's own open research question) --
  natural pairing since that's the suggested replacement signal.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-03] CMD_TODAY'S "[P] PLACE" PATH HAD NO GATE CHECK AT ALL
Priority: was High -- a real, reachable-today gap in the one remaining
  manual order-placement path this project's repeated "trace all call
  sites" pattern (see [[feedback_trace_all_call_sites]]) hadn't yet covered.

Problem:
  Found during the hurricane season-count model's opus review (backlog.txt
  "HURRICANE MARKETS -- SEASON-TOTAL COUNT MODEL SHIPPED SHADOW-ONLY"):
  main.py's `cmd_today()` ("what should I do today?" interactive
  recommender) has a "[P] Place" prompt that calls `paper.place_paper_order()`
  directly with NO gate check of any kind -- not `is_trading_paused()`, and
  not `paper.check_position_limits()`. This matters specifically because
  `check_position_limits()` is where city/date exposure caps, directional
  caps, correlated-group caps, AND every current shadow-only gate
  (`_rain_gates_active()`/`_snow_gates_active()`/
  `_hurricane_count_gates_active()`) actually live -- `analyze_trade()`
  itself computes a full real analysis regardless of any of those gates, by
  design (so calibration data keeps accumulating). Every OTHER manual
  placement path in main.py (`cmd_order`, `cmd_paper`, `_quick_paper_buy`)
  already checks both; this one fell through the same "reachable without
  analyze_trade()'s own gates" shape this project has hit and fixed
  repeatedly for those three paths (see the "HURRICANE MARKETS" entries'
  own history) -- except here it's not "reachable without analyze_trade()"
  (analyze_trade() DOES run), it's "analyze_trade() ran but nothing
  downstream re-checked the gates it doesn't itself enforce."
  Confirmed pre-existing for rain and snow (both already shadow-gated
  before this session); the hurricane season-count model made it a THIRD
  affected market family, which is what surfaced it.

What shipped:
  Added both checks to the "[P]" branch, mirroring `cmd_order`'s exact
  calling convention: `is_trading_paused()` checked first (blocks outright
  with the same message text every other manual path uses), then
  `paper.check_position_limits()` called with the real `ticker`/`qty`/
  `price`/`city` (from the already-enriched `best_m["_city"]`)/
  `target_date_str` (from `best_a["target_date"]`, already an ISO string --
  analyze_trade()'s own return-dict convention)/`side` -- failing OPEN on
  an exception (logs a warning, skips the limit check) rather than hard-
  blocking, matching `cmd_order`'s own established precedent for this exact
  call (itself opus-reviewed before). Position-limit check runs after the
  existing Kelly-sizing (`qty < 1`) and daily-spend-cap checks, immediately
  before the real placement call.

  Independent opus review (single agent -- scoped to match this fix's size,
  not the 3-parallel-agent setup the hurricane model itself used) found 3
  issues before commit, all fixed:
  - MEDIUM: `check_position_limits()` alone isn't enough, because its own
    fail-open exception path runs BEFORE its shadow-gate checks would have
    fired -- `cmd_order`/`cmd_paper`/`_quick_paper_buy` all pair it with
    direct refuse-outright guards (`is_hurricane_count_ticker`/
    `is_hurricane_ticker`/`_KXRAIN_MONTHLY_CITY`/`_KXSNOW_MONTHLY_CITY`) for
    exactly this reason -- their own comments say so explicitly. Without
    them, a `check_position_limits()` exception (a corrupt
    `paper_trades.json`, say) would fail open onto a shadow-only market
    same as before this fix, just narrowed to the exception path. Fixed by
    adding the same four direct guards, in the same order, before the
    `check_position_limits()` try block.
  - LOW: the limit-check-failure branch used a bare `return`, cutting off
    the runner-up display every OTHER refusal branch (and the placement-
    exception branch) leaves intact. Fixed by restructuring into an
    `if/else` so only the actual placement attempt is skipped, not the
    rest of the function.
  - LOW: the test helper's `_analysis(city=...)` parameter was dead code
    (city flows to `check_position_limits()` via `best_m["_city"]`, never
    from the analysis dict) -- removed.

  15 new tests in `tests/test_p1_remaining.py` (`TestCmdTodayPlacementGates`):

[RESOLVED 2026-08-02] VAR-CONVENTION LITERAL HAND-COPIED ACROSS 7+ FILES BEYOND analyze_trade()
Priority: Low -- no current behavior bug (all copies are logically
  equivalent today), but a real instance of this codebase's recurring
  hand-copied-convention-drift failure shape (TRADING_PAUSED, the
  disputed-row filter, PAPER_MIN_EDGE, the kill switch).

Problem:
  Found by an independent opus review (2026-07-31) while closing backlog.txt
  "NO MARKET-TYPE SEAM": that pass consolidated analyze_trade()'s own two
  `var = "min" if "LOW" in series else "max"` literals into a new
  `_daily_var_from_series()` helper, but the review found the identical
  literal/logic still separately hand-copied well beyond those two sites --
  backtest.py:453 (exact-shape copy: `var = "min" if "LOW" in ticker.upper()
  else "max"` followed by `condition["var"] = var` on the next line,
  feeding the same downstream contract, in a module that already imports
  from weather_markets), weather_markets.py's own `_metar_lock_in()`
  (`_is_low_mkt = "LOW" in ticker.upper()`, same file, different function
  from the two just consolidated), tracker.py:3952 (whose comment literally
  reads "Matches analyze_trade's own logic: var = ..." -- a self-documented
  hand-copy), tracker.py:3443, paper.py:1165, order_executor.py:2391,
  consistency.py:79, and main.py:6709. `_daily_var_from_series()`'s
  docstring was corrected the same session to stop overclaiming "single
  source of truth" codebase-wide -- it only covers analyze_trade()'s own
  two call sites.
  No behavior is currently wrong: all copies are logically equivalent
  today (one style quirk noted -- tracker.py tests "HIGH" first where the
  new helper tests "LOW" first, which only diverges on a ticker containing
  both substrings, which doesn't exist in this codebase's real ticker
  vocabulary). The risk is a future maintainer editing
  `_daily_var_from_series()` believing it changes the convention
  everywhere, when backtest.py and the other 6 sites would silently keep
  behaving on the old, separate copy.

What it would look like:
  Move the convention into a genuinely shared module (weather_markets.py
  already is one, but tracker.py/paper.py/order_executor.py/consistency.py/
  backtest.py/main.py would all need to import from it, or from a smaller
  shared location if a weather_markets.py import isn't appropriate for one
  of them -- check for an import cycle before picking). Replace all 9 real
  copies (2 already done in analyze_trade(), 7 remaining) with calls to
  the one shared function.

Why not now:
  - Genuinely out of scope for the pass that found it -- that pass was
    explicitly scoped (via AskUserQuestion) to "the two remaining literals"
    inside analyze_trade(), and this is a much larger, cross-file change
    touching paper/live settlement code (paper.py, order_executor.py,
    consistency.py) in multiple modules, not a rider on an unrelated fix.
  - No live bug exists today to force it -- all 9 copies currently agree.

When to revisit:
  - Whenever any of the 7 remaining sites is next touched for its own
    reason (backtest.py, tracker.py x2, paper.py, order_executor.py,
    consistency.py, main.py) -- migrate that site to the shared helper as
    a low-risk rider, rather than waiting for a dedicated cross-file pass.
    Treat "a 10th copy gets added somewhere" as a forcing signal to stop
    deferring and do the real consolidation.

RESOLVED 2026-08-02: re-read all 7 cited sites' actual code (not just this
  entry's own framing) before touching anything, and found the "9 real
  copies, all consolidatable" premise had overclaimed uniformity in two
  different ways:
  - consistency.py:79 and main.py:6709 check the same "HIGH"/"LOW"
    ticker substrings, but for a genuinely different purpose -- determining
    a market's condition DIRECTION ("above"/"below", or a broader
    display/grouping ticker-type), not which daily temperature VARIABLE
    (min/max) to fetch. These were never actually this convention;
    left untouched.
  - tracker.py's 2 sites have real, non-identical fallback logic for a
    ticker matching neither HIGH nor LOW. One site (audit_settlement)
    falls back further to cond_type (above/below) and finally
    `return False` (skip settlement) when cond_type is neither -- reachable
    for a non-monthly precip ticker or any ticker whose condition resolves
    to something other than above/below (e.g. "between") while its own
    ticker text also contains neither HIGH nor LOW; the other
    (backfill_emos_data) defaults straight to "max" for between-markets.
    Forcing both into a single shared function that always returns
    "max"/"min" would have silently changed behavior for the
    precip/unknown-skip site -- a real bug, not a refactor. (Opus-review-
    corrected, 2026-08-02: an earlier draft of this note claimed the
    neither-match case was reachable via hourly KXTEMPxxxH tickers --
    wrong; both tracker.py sites return early for hourly/monthly-rain/snow
    tickers before ever reaching this code. That reachability claim
    actually describes paper.py's own site, one of the 4 direct callers,
    not a tracker.py fallback site -- see _var_from_ticker_prefix()'s own
    corrected docstring in weather_markets.py for the precise trace.)
  Design decision (user confirmed via AskUserQuestion after a first-pass
  menu got "review these and ask again"): extract only the genuinely
  identical substring-check portion into a new `_var_from_ticker_prefix()`
  in weather_markets.py, returning None (not a guessed default) when the
  ticker matches neither -- callers needing a fallback OR it with "max"
  (the 4 genuine matches: backtest.py, weather_markets.py's own
  `_metar_lock_in`, paper.py, order_executor.py -- all now call this
  directly, zero behavior change), while tracker.py's 2 sites call it for
  just the substring check and keep their own distinct fallback tail
  exactly as before. `_daily_var_from_series()` (analyze_trade()'s own
  helper from the prior session) now delegates to this too, so there is
  now genuinely one shared implementation of the actual duplicated logic,
  not seven.
  9 new tests (TestVarFromTickerPrefix x5 in test_weather.py; 4 new
  regression tests in test_tracker.py covering the cond_type "above"
  fallback, the return-False/skip path, the cond_type "below" fallback,
  and ticker-prefix-wins-over-cond_type -- none had real coverage before
  this), every new assertion mutation-tested (reverted, confirmed the
  predicted symptom, restored). An independent opus review (before push)
  caught 2 real gaps in the first mutation-testing pass -- the "below"
  arm and the prefix-wins-over-cond_type precedence both survived every
  mutation originally tried -- closed with the last 2 of the 4 tracker.py
  tests, both confirmed via the same mutate-revert cycle. The review also
  caught the hourly-ticker reachability misattribution corrected above,
  and one more docstring gap: _daily_var_from_series()'s own prior body
  was LOW-only (no HIGH check), unlike the new HIGH-first
  _var_from_ticker_prefix() it now delegates to -- unreachable in
  practice (this codebase's real tickers are mutually exclusive on
  HIGH/LOW) but a real difference in shape, now documented on that
  function specifically rather than covered by the general "order
  doesn't matter" claim that's true of the other 4 sites but wasn't of
  this one. 924 tests pass across every touched file's test suite
  (test_backtest.py, test_paper.py, test_trading.py, test_tracker.py,
  test_weather_markets.py, test_weather.py, test_live_execution.py);
  dead-code and config-divergence guards also re-run clean. ruff check,
  ruff format, and mypy all clean on all 7 changed source files.

  stopped it suggesting `backfill-emos` at that stage, since backfill rows
  can't move this count).

  Built the actual confirmation gate the "process/safety concern" above was
  about: `py main.py emos-train` is now a dry run by default -- it fits and
  prints a/b/c/d but does NOT write emos_params.json (the file whose mere
  existence is the only switch weather_markets.py checks). A new

  prompts a typed 'yes' confirmation (mirrors the accuracy-override CLI

  `emos-deactivate` (reverts to the ensemble/climatology blend + T-scaling,
  also confirm-gated) for symmetry with accuracy-override/-clear/-status --
  deactivation previously meant manually deleting a file with no tooling.

  Deliberately did NOT run `emos-train --activate` as part of this session
  -- this entry's own "What it would look like" text requires verifying the
  resulting calibration curve (`py main.py validate`) beats the current
  T-scaling baseline before trusting EMOS live, which is a separate,

  Independent opus review (effort=high) of the first-pass gate found 5
  HIGH + 9 MEDIUM + 11 LOW -- every finding was in the coupled T-scaling
  half or the revert path, not the confirm-prompt mechanism itself, which
  it confirmed was solid. All addressed, none deferred:

  check the file's mtime on every call (cheap stat, reload only on real

  an EMOS-covered condition type (weather_markets.py calls

[RESOLVED 2026-07-31 -- re-examined via the standing 17-step workflow;
  decided against changing counting semantics]
  COUNT_SETTLED_PREDICTIONS() COUNTS RAW ROWS, NOT DISTINCT
  TEMPERATURE-OBSERVATION EVENTS
Priority: was Low -- a real design question, not a live-money-critical gap
  (doesn't change today's live gate outcomes; ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE/F3 clear
  either way at current counts), but the codebase already has an explicit,
  opus-reviewed precedent for the opposite choice on a sibling function.

Problem:
  tracker.count_settled_predictions() (tracker.py:1866) joins
  multiday_predictions to outcomes_valid on ticker and counts every
  matching ROW, not distinct settlement events. A city/date pair with
  multiple ladder-bracket tickers that all settle from the same real
  observation (e.g. multiple above/below/between brackets on the same
  city+date) each contribute their own +1, so the live-trading maturity
  gate's count can overstate how many independent real-world observations
  actually back it. This is the exact same shape count_settled_snow_
  predictions() (tracker.py:1926) was deliberately hardened against
  (opus-review-caught 2026-07-30, same day): "Denver's own KXDENSNOWM
  ladder alone has 7 sibling brackets that all settle from the SAME real
  snowfall observation for a given month, so a raw-row floor could clear
  the 20-sample threshold with as few as ~3 real months of data, not 20
  independent real-world observations." That function now counts DISTINCT
  (ticker prefix, year, month) accrual events instead of raw rows.
  count_settled_predictions() was NOT given the same treatment -- it
  still counts raw rows, same as count_settled_rain_predictions()
  (tracker.py:1898), whose own docstring explicitly accepts this as a
  known, deliberate tradeoff: "rain has 11 cities' worth of decorrelation
  across those rows, and changing its counting semantics now would shift
  an already-accumulating live gate's count out from under it."
  count_settled_predictions() is in the same position as rain's counter
  (already live/shipped, changing its semantics now would shift an
  already-accumulating gate), which is likely why it was left alone --
  but that reasoning was never stated for this function, only inferred.

What it would look like:
  Either (a) leave as-is and explicitly document the same "already live,
  changing semantics would shift an accumulating gate" reasoning rain's
  counter states, so a future reader doesn't mistake the omission for an
  oversight, or (b) redesign to count distinct temperature-observation
  events (city + date, or ticker-prefix + date depending on how directly
  correlated same-day above/below/between brackets on one city really
  are) the way snow's counter now does -- a bigger, live-gate-semantics-
  changing decision that needs the user's input on whether the maturity
  gate should measure "settled rows" or "independent observations."

Why not now:
  Found via adjacency while fixing the condition_type filter gap (a
  different, narrower bug) -- this is a separate, larger design decision
  about what the gate should actually measure, not a bug with an obvious
  single fix. Changing the counting semantics now would also change
  ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE/F3's live count again (a second change to the same
  gate in the same day), which deserves its own explicit user decision
  and its own dedicated verification pass, not a drive-by bundled into
  the condition_type fix.

What was decided:
  Re-verified live data (2026-07-31, data/predictions.db): 61 raw rows vs.
  60 distinct (city, market_date) pairs -- only ONE apparent duplicate
  (Dallas, 2026-05-19). Investigating that single case changed the
  conclusion entirely: it is NOT a duplicate ladder bracket at all -- it's
  `KXHIGHTDAL-26MAY19-T83` and `KXLOWTDAL-26MAY19-T69`, the day's HIGH and
  LOW temperature markets, which are two genuinely independent real
  observations that happen to share a city+date. A naive `(city,
  market_date)` distinct-event key -- the direct analog of what count_
  settled_snow_predictions() does with (ticker prefix, year, month) --
  would have silently merged those two into one event, which is a new
  correctness bug, not a fix: the `var` column that should distinguish
  high/low is mostly NULL on live data (53/61 rows), so the only reliable
  signal is the KXHIGH/KXLOW ticker prefix, which would need its own parser
  (mirroring snow's `_parse_monthly_ticker_month`) to do this safely.
  Correctly grouping by (city, market_date, high-or-low-from-ticker-prefix)
  gives 61 distinct events against 61 raw rows -- there are ZERO actual
  duplicate-ladder-bracket rows in live data today. The snow precedent
  doesn't carry over as cleanly as it first looked: snow's 7 KXDENSNOWM
  sibling brackets are near-redundant restatements of one monthly accrual
  number, while temperature's above/below brackets on a given city+date+
  high-or-low are today, in practice, one row each -- no observed
  duplication to fix.
  Also surfaced during review: count_settled_predictions()'s own docstring
  already commits it to counting "the same population F3's own calibration
  math (calibration.py) ... already train on" -- calibration.py's grid
  search and get_multiday_calibration_cli both train on raw rows with no
  dedup. Switching this counter to distinct-event counting would break that
  stated alignment, trading one mismatch (vs. snow's precedent) for another
  (vs. this function's own calibration-population contract).
  Decision (via AskUserQuestion, user confirmed after the KXHIGH/KXLOW
  finding changed the calculus): leave as raw-row counting. Documented the
  full reasoning above in count_settled_predictions()'s docstring
  (tracker.py:1866) so a future reader doesn't mistake the omission for an
  oversight, matching rain's counter's existing precedent of stating its
  tradeoff explicitly. Added a regression test (tests/test_tracker.py,
  `test_count_settled_predictions_counts_raw_rows_not_distinct_events`,
  mutation-tested against a distinct-event implementation to confirm it
  actually catches that regression) locking in the decision so a future
  change can't silently flip this semantics without the test failing.

When to revisit:
  If live data ever shows the same city+date+high-or-low combination
  settling more than once (i.e. real ladder-bracket duplication, not a
  high/low pair) -- that would be the actual trigger condition this entry
  was watching for, and did not find as of 2026-07-31.

[RESOLVED 2026-07-27 -- found live during a cron output review, root-caused,
  fixed same session]
  SAFE_IO -- EMERGENCY-COPY FALLBACK SILENTLY CLOBBERED THE ORIGINAL FILE
Priority: was High once found -- a crash-safety utility used by 20+ callers
  across the codebase (including paper.py's live trade-state file) had its
  entire safety guarantee silently defeated by default, for every real
  caller, in exactly the failure scenario (contested/locked file) where it
  matters most.

Problem:
  A live cron run on 2026-07-27 hit a Windows file-lock collision writing
  `data/forecast_sigma.json` (`climatology.py`'s `load_all_sigmas()`) --
  `safe_io.atomic_write_json()`'s 3 retry attempts all failed with
  WinError 32/2/5, then it fell through to its "emergency copy for manual
  recovery" path and logged success. Investigated because the run also
  showed persistent rain-market anomalies (see the RAIN MARKETS entry
  above) and this ERROR-level log line stood out as worth checking, not
  assumed safe just because cron exited 0.
  Traced `safe_io.py`'s fallback logic (added by commit `335ded8`, "Batch S:
  R28 + P2-H", intended to make the emergency copy "operator-visible" by
  landing it in the monitored `data/` dir instead of system temp): when a
  caller omits `fallback_dir`, the first candidate is `project_root() /
  "data"` -- but every real target file already lives in that exact
  directory (`DATA_DIR`, defined identically in `climatology.py`,
  `acis_precip.py`, `backtest.py`, etc.), so `emergency_path = fb_dir /
  path.name` resolves to the SAME path as the file that just failed 3
  atomic-write attempts. The "emergency copy" was actually a plain
  non-atomic `open(path, "w")` overwrite of the live file -- silently
  defeating `atomic_write_json`'s entire crash-safety purpose (temp-write +
  fsync + rename) in precisely the scenario it exists to protect against.
  Grepped every call site (20+: `paper.py`'s live trade-state `DATA_PATH`,
  `circuit_breaker.py`'s kill-switch state, `weather_markets.py`'s forecast
  caches, `climatology.py`, `acis_precip.py`, `alerts.py`, `ab_test.py`,
  `param_sweep.py`, `kalshi_ws.py`, `monte_carlo.py`,
  `settlement_monitor.py`, `main.py`) -- NONE pass `fallback_dir`, so this
  was a universal, not file-specific, gap. Tonight's actual outcome was
  benign (the lock was transient; the plain overwrite happened to succeed
  with correct data, verified by re-reading `forecast_sigma.json` after the
  run) -- but a crash or another process interrupting that non-atomic write
  could have left any of these files (including live trade state)
  truncated/corrupted with only a buried ERROR log to show for it. The only
  existing test for this path
  (`test_atomic_write_emergency_copy_written_on_failure`) explicitly passes
  a distinct `fallback_dir`, so the real-world default-omitted-fallback_dir
  behavior had never been exercised.

What was fixed:
  Default emergency candidate changed from `project_root()/"data"` to a
  dedicated `project_root()/"data"/".emergency"` subdir -- preserves P2-H's
  original "operator-visible, monitored location" intent while guaranteeing
  no collision with any real target file (none live in `.emergency/`), with
  zero caller changes needed across all 20+ call sites.
  `cleanup_data_dir()` (main.py) only globs `data/*.json` non-recursively
  and already skips dot-prefixed entries at the top level, so
  `data/.emergency/` is invisible to its 2-day-retention sweep -- recovery
  copies won't get silently deleted (independently re-verified by the
  opus review below, not just asserted).
  Added a belt-and-suspenders guard in the fallback loop itself: any
  candidate (default or explicitly-passed `fallback_dir`) that resolves to
  the same path as the original target is skipped with a warning rather
  than written to, so an explicit-but-colliding `fallback_dir` can never
  reintroduce the same class of bug.
  Considered and rejected two alternatives (via `AskUserQuestion`): renaming
  the file in place (`forecast_sigma.json.emergency`) fixes the same bug but
  buys nothing extra over the subdir approach and forces an unrelated
  test-assertion change; reverting to temp-only fallback regresses P2-H's
  operator-visible intent and, without the belt-and-suspenders guard,
  doesn't close the underlying class of bug (an explicit colliding
  `fallback_dir` would still trigger it).

  Independent review (opus, effort=high) before push found the core fix
  correct but surfaced real gaps in the first pass, all addressed:
  - HIGH: the two new tests didn't isolate `project_root()` to a tmp dir in
    every case, so a real test run wrote actual recovery-copy junk into
    THIS repo's own `data/.emergency/` (reviewer reproduced it: a genuine
    `paper_trades.json` emergency copy could be silently overwritten by a
    routine `pytest` run). Fixed by patching `project_root` in every
    affected test (`test_safe_io.py` and, once the fix made it possible to
    even notice, a pre-existing, previously-unrelated test in
    `test_infrastructure.py` -- `test_atomic_write_raises_on_double_failure`
    -- that had the identical gap, exposed only because this fix introduced
    a new subdirectory for it to silently create in the real repo).
  - MEDIUM: the `AtomicWriteError` message claimed "Emergency copy written
    to None" when no copy could be written at all (disk-full-everywhere
    case) -- fixed with an explicit truthful branch plus a dedicated ERROR
    log line, and a new test forcing total failure (`os.replace` mocked to
    fail unconditionally) to pin the accurate message.
  - MEDIUM: the emergency copy itself was a plain non-atomic `open(path,
    "w")` with no fsync -- weaker durability than the primary write it
    exists to back up, and two processes failing on the same target
    simultaneously could interleave-corrupt it. Fixed by giving the
    emergency copy the identical temp+fsync+`os.replace` discipline as the
    primary write, with its own pid-suffixed temp name.
  - MEDIUM: root-caused the likely actual trigger of tonight's incident --
    the primary write's temp filename (`.{name}_{attempt}.tmp`) has no
    per-process component, so two processes racing to write the same target
    (exactly what Windows lock contention implies) could share one temp
    file and interleave-corrupt it before an atomic rename installs the
    corruption "successfully." Fixed by adding `os.getpid()` to the temp
    name; verified `paper.py`'s own stray-temp-file cleanup glob
    (`.paper_trades.json_*.tmp`) still matches with a pid inserted.
  - Self-caught during the fix for the above: giving the emergency copy its
    own temp+replace step introduced a new leak -- on emergency-write
    failure the temp file was never cleaned up (reproduced live: a stray
    `.paper_trades.json_<pid>.emergency.tmp` was left in this repo's own
    `data/.emergency/` after a single test run). Fixed with the same
    `os.unlink` cleanup-on-except the primary write already had; added a
    dedicated regression assertion (glob-checks both the tmp-isolated dir
    and real system temp for leftover `*.tmp` files) and mutation-tested it
    by temporarily removing the cleanup and confirming the new assertion
    catches it.
  - LOW: `circuit_breaker._save_state`'s failure log bumped from WARNING to
    ERROR -- under the old bug a same-path clobber meant CB/kill-switch
    state usually landed on disk anyway despite the "failure"; after this
    fix a failed save now genuinely loses that cycle's state.
  - LOW: fixed the second new test's docstring (wrongly claimed the
    colliding candidate falls through to "system temp" -- it actually falls

  SAFE_IO -- NOTHING MONITORS data/.emergency/ FOR REAL RECOVERY COPIES
Priority: was Low -- a genuine emergency copy landing there today is only
  visible via one buried ERROR log line; the fix above stopped the

Problem:
  Once `atomic_write_json()`'s emergency-copy fallback actually works (see

What was fixed:

  correct fit -- a log line alone doesn't solve "an operator would only

  would silently blank out the ENTIRE result (caught by cron's outer
  `except Exception`, logged at DEBUG) at exactly the moment a real file
  needs recovery; fixed by moving `fromtimestamp` inside the per-entry

[RESOLVED 2026-07-31 -- send_system_alert()'s cooldown only, per explicit
  user scope decision; alert_strong_signal()'s per-ticker cooldown
  deliberately left in-process, see resolution note below]
  NOTIFY.SEND_SYSTEM_ALERT()'S COOLDOWN IS IN-PROCESS MEMORY ONLY, DOESN'T
  SURVIVE A FRESH CRON PROCESS
Priority: Low -- affects operational alert spam, not trading correctness;
  none of `send_system_alert()`'s 3 current callers (prod reminder,
  dead-man's-switch, the emergency-copy monitor above) have actually spammed
  a real operator yet.

Problem:
  `notify._last_notified` (the dict `send_system_alert()`'s 6h cooldown
  reads/writes) is a plain in-process module-level dict, never persisted to
  disk. CORRECTED 2026-07-31 (user caught this before any implementation
  started): the original framing below cited Windows Task Scheduler
  specifically -- live-verified via `schtasks /Query` that zero Kalshi-
  related scheduled tasks are actually registered on this machine; cron is
  manual-only until the VM migration (`cmd_schedule_cycles()`, `main.py`,
  only ever *prints* the schtasks commands for the user to register by
  hand, it doesn't register them itself, and nobody has run those commands
  here). The real root cause is invocation-mode-agnostic, not specific to
  Task Scheduler: every `py main.py cron` invocation -- manual or scheduled
  -- is a fresh Python process, so the cooldown dict starts empty every
  single time and never actually suppresses a repeat alert across separate
  invocations, only within one long-lived process (`main.py`'s `loop` /
  `watch --auto` modes). This makes it, if anything, MORE immediately
  relevant during the current manual-only operating mode than the original
  "Task Scheduler" framing implied -- re-running `py main.py cron` by hand
  within 6h of a real alert firing hits this exact gap, which is a normal
  thing to do manually, not a future-only scenario. `AUDIT_PLAN.md`'s P1-7
  already fixed this exact class of bug for `circuit_breaker.py`'s state,
  but `notify.py`'s cooldown was never covered by that fix. This matters
  more for a condition that persists until fixed (an unrecovered emergency
  copy sits in `data/.emergency/` until a human deletes it -- every cron
  invocation in between, manual or scheduled, would alert again) than for
  one that self-clears (the dead-man's-switch's own trigger condition
  resets the moment cron next completes successfully).

What it would look like:
  Persist `_last_notified` to disk (e.g. via `safe_io.atomic_write_json`,
  matching the pattern P1-7 already established for circuit breaker state)
  so the cooldown survives across separate process invocations -- manual or
  scheduled -- not just within one long-lived process.

When to revisit:
  Whenever a real emergency copy or another `send_system_alert()`-gated
  condition actually fires and the operator (manually or via a future
  scheduled task) re-runs cron within the 6h window, spamming a repeat
  alert in practice -- not urgent today since none of the 3 current
  callers have fired for real yet, but no longer gated on the VM
  migration/Task-Scheduler transition as the original framing implied.

RESOLVED 2026-07-31: scoped via explicit AskUserQuestion decision before
  writing any code -- persistence covers send_system_alert()'s cooldown
  only, not alert_strong_signal()'s per-ticker trade-signal cooldown
  (which stays in-process, deliberately). Research before deciding found a
  second, independent reason beyond "matches the original ask": alert_
  strong_signal()'s real duplicate-alert guard is `previous_tickers`
  (main.py's watch loop state, itself in-process-only) -- persisting just
  `_last_notified` for trade signals wouldn't even achieve full restart-
  safety on its own, since `previous_tickers` would still reset on a fresh
  process and treat every currently-strong ticker as "new" regardless.
  Shipped: `paths.NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_STATE_PATH` (`data/.notify_cooldowns.json`)
  + `notify._system_cooldown_elapsed()`, mirroring `circuit_breaker.py`'s
  established `_save_state()` shape exactly -- read, decide, and write all
  happen under one lock acquisition (`_NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_FILE_LOCK`), not two
  separate ones, to avoid a TOCTOU race between concurrent callers. Fails
  OPEN (fires the alert) on a missing or corrupt cooldown file -- a
  bookkeeping failure must never silently suppress a real system alert,
  matching `paper.is_accuracy_halted()`'s precedent for this failure class.
  `send_system_alert()` now calls this instead of reading/writing the
  shared `_last_notified` dict; `alert_strong_signal()`'s own use of
  `_last_notified` is completely untouched. Also fixed the stale "Windows
  Task Scheduler" framing this entry's own Problem section had (see the
  CORRECTED note above) everywhere else it appeared: `send_system_alert()`'s
  docstring and the emergency-copy-monitor comment block in cron.py (both
  previously said the gap only mattered "under Task Scheduler" -- corrected
  to invocation-mode-agnostic language matching the real root cause).
  New tests (tests/test_notify.py, no prior test coverage existed for this
  function at all): 8 direct tests of `_system_cooldown_elapsed()` (first-
  call fires+persists, second-call-suppressed, the actual cross-invocation
  regression this entry is about, cooldown-elapses-after-window, distinct
  keys don't interfere, missing-file/corrupt-file both fail open, missing
  parent dir auto-created) plus 2 integration-level tests calling
  `send_system_alert()` itself end to end with external channels
  monkeypatched to a fake recorder. All isolated to a tmp_path file via
  monkeypatch -- never touches the real data/.notify_cooldowns.json.
  Mutation-tested twice: (1) reverted to the old in-process-only behavior
  (state always empty) -- 4 tests correctly failed, including the one named
  for this exact regression; (2) flipped the fail-open exception handler to
  fail-closed -- the corrupt-file test correctly failed. Both reverted and
  re-verified green. ruff/ruff-format/mypy clean on notify.py, paths.py,
  cron.py, tests/test_notify.py.

  Independent Agent(opus, effort=high) review before push, given this
  touches the alerting/operational-safety path: found no vacuous claims on
  first pass, but 2 HIGH and 4 MEDIUM real findings, all addressed --
  (1) HIGH -- `cron.py`'s prod-reminder (`:436`) and dead-man's-switch
  (`:582`) callers both omitted `cooldown_key`, defaulting to the shared
  `"__system__"` key. Harmless before this fix (a fresh in-process dict
  each cron run meant the two alert types could only ever collide within
  the SAME process run), but persistence turned this into a real cross-
  process hazard: cron run N's prod reminder would silently suppress run
  N+1's dead-man's-switch alert for 6h, and vice versa -- exactly the
  scenario `send_system_alert()`'s own docstring already warns callers to
  avoid, just never actually fixed at these two call sites. Fixed: gave
  both their own distinct keys (`"prod_reminder"`, `"cron_gap"`).
  (2) HIGH -- the docstring/comments claimed the single lock acquisition
  avoids "a TOCTOU race between concurrent callers (e.g. two processes)" --
  false. `threading.Lock` is process-local; two separate `py main.py cron`
  processes each hold their own independent lock object, so this provides
  NO cross-process serialization, only thread-level protection within one
  process (matching what `circuit_breaker.py`'s own analogous lock actually
  claims -- re-read its comment directly, it only ever claims in-process
  thread safety + Windows os.replace collision avoidance, never cross-
  process). True cross-process locking (e.g. an O_EXCL lockfile) was
  judged out of scope for this pass -- the actual operating model is
  sequential manual invocation today, not concurrent processes -- so the
  fix was correcting the overclaiming wording, not building new lock
  infrastructure. (3) MEDIUM -- valid JSON that isn't a dict (e.g. a bare
  `null`) parsed without error, then crashed on `state.get(...)` with an
  AttributeError, silently swallowed by every caller's own broad
  try/except but breaking `send_system_alert()`'s documented "Never
  raises" contract. Fixed with an explicit `isinstance(state, dict)`
  check inside the same try block. (4) MEDIUM -- on ANY read failure
  (corrupt file, non-dict JSON, or a transient I/O error --
  `circuit_breaker.py`'s own `_load_state()` comment documents a real
  observed Windows PermissionError mid-os.replace for this exact read
  shape), the code fell back to `state = {}` and then wrote back only the
  current key -- silently erasing every OTHER already-persisted cooldown
  key in the file. Fixed: a read failure now fails open WITHOUT writing
  at all, since a call that can't safely see existing state must not
  blindly overwrite it. (5) MEDIUM -- a sustained write failure (state
  read fine, write keeps failing) silently degrades back to the exact
  pre-fix in-process-only behavior forever, with only a warning log line
  -- judged disproportionate to build dedicated escalation for in this
  pass (would need its own design), but documented explicitly rather than
  left silent: `atomic_write_json`'s own emergency-copy fallback plus the
  existing `.emergency/` monitor (`cooldown_key="emergency_copy"`, a
  distinct key from anything this failure mode would affect) already
  independently surfaces a sustained write failure of this kind via a
  separate, working alert channel -- not a fully silent failure mode in
  practice, a residual risk explicitly accepted rather than silently
  dropped. (6) MEDIUM -- the code comment (and this note, before this
  correction) claimed `alert_strong_signal()`'s real duplicate-alert guard
  `previous_tickers` is "in-process-only" -- false, live-verified against
  `main.py`: `_load_watch_state()`/`_save_watch_state()` persist it to
  `data/.watch_state.json` and the function's own docstring says "survives
  restarts." The scope decision itself (send_system_alert() only, this
  pass) still stands -- it was the primary, explicit AskUserQuestion-
  confirmed reason, not this secondary point -- but the comment's
  reasoning was corrected rather than left factually wrong.
  Also fixed 2 LOW findings: a citation of `paper.is_accuracy_halted()` as
  a "fail-open precedent" was backwards -- that function actually fails
  CLOSED (changed 2026-07-09 specifically because fail-open silently
  disabled the halt); the fail-open choice here is correct on its own
  merits for an alerting path, just not modeled on that function, so the
  citation was removed rather than left misleading. And a redundant
  `NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_STATE_PATH.parent.mkdir(...)` call was removed --
  `atomic_write_json()` already does this as its own first step
  (safe_io.py), so the extra call (and the test that only proved atomic_
  write_json's mkdir works, not notify.py's own) was dead weight.
  New tests added addressing the findings: a non-dict-JSON test (finding
  3), a read-failure-doesn't-clobber-other-keys test (finding 4), and a
  real 20-thread concurrency test proving the lock's actual job (finding
  1's neighbor -- nothing in the original suite would have caught the
  lock being deleted). All 3 mutation-tested the same way: reverted the
  specific fix, confirmed the specific new test failed for the right
  reason (the concurrency mutation manifested as write collisions/
  emergency-copy fallbacks rather than a clean logical race, but still
  reliably failed), restored, re-verified green. 13 tests total in
  tests/test_notify.py. Also updated `safe_io.py`'s basename-collision
  note (2026-07-27) to record re-verification against the new
  `.notify_cooldowns.json` call site (still no real collision). Full
  regression sweep re-run clean; ruff/ruff-format/mypy clean on all 5
  changed files (notify.py, paths.py, cron.py, safe_io.py,
  tests/test_notify.py).

  RAIN MARKETS -- MONTHLY MODEL HAS NO DAY-SPECIFIC FORECAST SIGNAL
Priority: Medium -- shadow-only today (RAIN_TRADING_ENABLED gate +
  TRADING_PAUSED both mean nothing sizes off this yet), but should be
  looked at before the rain model is ever trusted for real sizing.

Problem:
  Cron's `check_market_anomalies()` flagged the same 2-3 rain tickers as
  "price drifted against model" on 3 consecutive runs on 2026-07-27:
  KXRAINSTPM-26JUL-8 (our 39-43% vs market 68-70%), KXRAINNYCM-26JUL-6
  (our 7-10% vs market 30-44%), KXRAINNYCM-26JUL-7 (our 1-7% vs market

  hand against real ACIS data (month-to-date actual + 30yr remaining-days

  matching cron's "our" values almost exactly (NYC >6in: 6.7% vs cron's 7%;

  is not malfunctioning, it's doing exactly what Step 2 (`1839d76`) built
  it to do.
  Root cause: the model's only "what's actually going to happen the rest of
  this month" signal beyond the 30yr climatological bootstrap is Open-Meteo
  Seasonal's ECMWF SEAS5 tilt, and that's a *monthly mean* only (already
  flagged as a limitation in this file's own RAIN/SNOW/HURRICANE MARKETS
  entry, Step 2 handoff item 1: "mean-only, no per-member spread ... can
  adjust central tendency but can't itself supply distribution shape") --
  it has no day-level resolution, so it structurally cannot see "a system
  is forecast to bring heavy rain on day 29" the way a trader checking an
  actual short-range forecast (or the market itself) can.
  Pulled Open-Meteo's real 7-day `precipitation_sum` forecast live for the
  divergent cities to check which side of each divergence looks right:
    - NYC: forecast for the remaining accrual days (Jul 27-31) sums to only
      ~0.87in -- nowhere near the 2.31in/3.31in still needed for rungs 6/7.
      The real short-range forecast supports the model's LOW probability,
      not the market's 30%/14% pricing -- on these two rungs the market
      looks like the mispriced side (or reflects something about these
      illiquid deep-OTM brackets this bot doesn't have visibility into),
      not the model.
    - St. Petersburg: forecast shows a building wet pattern right at
      month's end (0/0/0.9/2.7/6.5mm Jul 27-31, continuing into 13.2mm Aug
      1 -- just past this ticker's settlement), consistent with the
      market's higher 68-70% price. This looks like real information the
      climatology-only model can't see, not market noise.

What the fix looks like (not yet designed in detail):
  Blend a real short-range forecast signal for the remaining days of the
  current accrual month into `_analyze_monthly_rain_trade()`, on top of
  (not replacing) the 30yr empirical bootstrap -- Open-Meteo's regular
  forecast API (already used elsewhere in this bot, ~16-day horizon) covers
  "the rest of the month" for any ticker whose remaining days fit inside
  that window, which is most of a typical month once a chunk of it has
  already accrued. Needs its own design pass, not a mechanical wire-up:
  how to combine a per-day deterministic/ensemble forecast total with the
  bootstrap's right-skewed remaining-days resample (add the forecasted

  `_fetch_ensemble_precip`'s existing single-day ensemble fetch (same

  instead of indexing out one date, summing each ensemble member's values
  across the requested date range. Member-index stability across days was
  confirmed live (2026-07-28, direct Open-Meteo API call) before relying on
  it: `precipitation_sum_memberNN` is one continuous simulated trajectory's
  day-by-day values within a single response, not independently-shuffled

  shipping in size-appropriate steps.
  A plan-review pass (10 rounds, user-requested) before any code was
  written caught 4 real issues: the originally-planned insertion point
  preceded where `threshold` is defined (would have been a `NameError`);
  the planned `count_fn` used a raw lambda instead of this codebase's own
  established closure-factory convention (fixed by adding
  `_count_signal_json_key`, mirroring `_count_signal_column`); the plan
  assumed a `result_dict` variable to mutate that doesn't exist (the
  function returns a dict literal directly, fixed via conditional
  dict-unpacking); and the new fetch call needed an explicit defensive
  try/except (a bug in new code must only ever cost the new signal, never
  the already-working bootstrap-only analysis it sits next to).
  Mutation-testing during first-pass implementation caught a real vacuous
  test (the "remaining window exceeds 16 days" test used a raising mock,
  silently swallowed by the new try/except regardless of whether the real
  scope-boundary check was correct -- fixed by switching to a call-counter)
  and 2 pre-existing test files with a hardcoded registry-size assertion
  needing an update to 10, not just new tests for the new signal
  (`test_forecasting.py`'s `test_registry_has_9_entries...`, renamed not
  just bumped, since its own name encodes the count and this project
  already hit the identical stale-count-name bug once before, SIGNAL
  GRADUATION session 2026-07-25; and
  `test_real_registry_entries_all_resolve_against_a_real_empty_db`).

  Independent `Agent(opus, effort=high)` review of the first-pass
  implementation, before push, found it was NOT safe to ship -- 3 real
  HIGH-severity issues, all fixed:
  (H1) `count_settled_signal_rows(json_key=...)`'s query unconditionally
  required `o.settled_temp_f IS NOT NULL`, but KXRAIN*M rows never populate
  that column (they write `settled_value` instead, confirmed against
  `count_settled_rain_predictions()`'s own join, which has no such filter

  have stayed permanently 0 regardless of how much real settled data
  accumulated, silently defeating the entire point of the shadow rollout.
  Fixed with a new `require_settled_temp: bool = True` parameter on
  `count_settled_signal_rows()` (tracker.py), `False` for this entry only,
  verified live end-to-end (a real settled prediction + signal now counts
  1, not 0, both via the tracker function directly and via the actual
  `SIGNAL_REGISTRY` entry's `count_fn()`).
  (H2) Open-Meteo pads a model's response with a FULL-length `time` array
  past that model's own real forecast horizon, filling the tail with
  nulls rather than truncating the array -- confirmed live (2026-07-28,
  direct API call): for a 16-day Denver request, `icon_seamless`'s real
  horizon was only 7 days and `ecmwf_ifs025`'s only 14. The first-pass
  `is_all_null` guard only caught a fully-null model, not a
  partially-covering one, so short-horizon members' truncated (and
  therefore systematically low) totals were being pooled with full-window
  totals as if equivalent -- for the exact ~2-week windows this feature
  actually runs against, not a rare edge case. Fixed by requiring a member
  to have a non-null value on every single requested day to be counted at
  all; a model whose horizon falls short contributes zero members instead
  of a biased partial one.
  (H3) The flagship end-to-end test's mocked members (1.0-6.0in) never
  exceeded its own 7.0in threshold even before the (also-omitted)
  month-to-date term, so its one probability assertion always landed on
  the 0.01 clamp floor regardless of whether the real formula was even
  used -- mutation-verified vacuous against both a wrong mtd term and the
  entire computation replaced with a hardcoded 0.0. Fixed with members
  straddling the threshold and a real non-zero month-to-date mock, plus an
  explicit self-check that the fixture lands strictly inside the clamp
  range.
  4 more MEDIUM/LOW findings, all addressed: the 16-day boundary itself
  had no dedicated test (mutation-verified 3 different wrong boundary

RESOLVED (partially) 2026-08-17: shipped the >16-day far-tail-blend case --
  when a ticket's remaining accrual window EXCEEDS Open-Meteo's 16-day
  forecast horizon (the gap this entry's own "when to revisit" section
  called out), `_analyze_monthly_rain_trade()` no longer skips the
  forecast-blend signal for the whole cycle. It now fetches the near-
  forecast-covered PREFIX of the remaining window and blends it with a
  resampled far-tail climatology for the days beyond it, instead of falling
  back to pure climatology (blended_prob/rec_side/sizing) for the entire
  remaining window the moment any part of it exceeds the horizon. Still
  deliberately shadow/log-only, matching the 2026-07-28 near-only case and
  every other new signal's `SIGNAL_REGISTRY` rollout convention in this
  codebase -- `forecast_blend_prob` is untouched, only
  `signals.rain_forecast_blend_prob` (plus 2 new metadata keys, see below)
  changes.

  Re-verified this entry's remaining claims live before starting (2026-08-
  17): `RAIN_TRADING_ENABLED` confirmed unset in the real `.env`;
  `count_settled_signal_rows(json_key="rain_forecast_blend_prob",
  require_settled_temp=False)` returned 6, confirming the graduation
  decision stays data-gated (floor is 20) and is genuinely unaffected by
  this update, per this entry's own explicit scope split.

  Design (2 decisions surfaced via AskUserQuestion before writing code,
  both later revised in part by the opus review below):
  - Combine each near-forecast member with far-tail climatology via a
    per-member `random.choice()` resample draw (matching this entry's own
    "resample climatology... combining into one distribution per simulated
    trajectory" language) -- REVISED post-review to a deterministic cross
    product; see H2 below.
  - Scope the existing SEAS5 monthly-mean tilt to the tail-only historical
    sums (a second `acis_precip.apply_seasonal_tilt()` call with a later
    `remaining_start_day`, mechanically reusing the function as-is) rather
    than reusing the full-remaining-window tilt already computed for
    `blended_prob` -- kept as designed; the near days now have a real
    forecast and don't need SEAS5's mean-only nudge on top of it, while the
    tail beyond the forecast horizon still does.

  Independent `Agent(opus, effort=high)` review (this entry's 3rd such
  review, after 2026-07-28's implementation review and its own earlier
  10-round plan review) found 2 HIGH + 3 MEDIUM + 5 LOW, all addressed:
  (H1) Verified LIVE against Open-Meteo (Denver, `forecast_days=16`): a
  16-day-out request falls entirely outside `icon_seamless`'s (~7-day) and
  `ecmwf_ifs025`'s (~14-day) real per-model horizons, so
  `_fetch_ensemble_precip_multiday`'s own full-coverage-only rule (the H2
  fix from 2026-07-28, correctly protecting against biased-low partial
  members) silently dropped BOTH every time -- the far case's "ensemble"
  was actually always exactly 30 `gfs_seamless` members, zero ECMWF weight,
  vs. the near-only case's ~130-member, ~77%-ECMWF-weighted ensemble, with
  no way to tell from the logged value alone. Fixed by capping the far
  case's own near-fetch to a real 14-day window (`today + 13`, recovering
  ECMWF's horizon at the cost of 2 fewer forecast-covered days folded into
  the tail instead) -- the near-only branch is untouched, still spans up to
  a genuine 16 days, matching the shipped 2026-07-28 values byte-for-byte
  (verified directly by reading the partition logic, not just asserted;
  mutating the near-only case's own boundary still fails its existing
  tests).
  (H2) With H1's real near-member count only ~30, the originally-chosen
  per-member `random.choice()` resample draw injected ~+/-8pp of pure
  sampling noise into the logged signal on every scan cycle (opus's
  60-repeat repro on an identical input: stdev 0.084) -- the same ticker
  would log a different value on consecutive cycles, directly inflating the
  Brier score this signal will eventually be judged on for graduation.
  Fixed by switching to a deterministic cross product (every near member
  paired with every tail-year value) -- the exact noise-free expected value
  of the same "pair each member with a tail draw" design intent, ~30
  members x ~15-30 tail years = a few hundred to ~1000 terms, negligible
  cost. This was a live revision of the AskUserQuestion-answered design
  mid-session -- surfaced transparently before applying rather than
  silently overridden, since cross-product had been on the original 3-
  option menu before a deflected first ask got simplified to 2 options.
  (M1) The per-member resample's `random.choice()` call consumed the
  SHARED global RNG stream before `acis_precip.bootstrap_ci_month_total()`
  ran later in the same function (also global-RNG-based), meaning the far
  case's own new code could shift the PRE-EXISTING bootstrap CI's stream
  position -- not wrong today (that CI is already unseeded in production)
  but it falsified this block's own stated "a bug here must only ever cost
  this new signal" contract, and would have silently changed sizing under
  any seeded/reproducible backtest. Resolved as a side effect of H2's
  cross-product fix, which removes the RNG call entirely from this block.
  (M2) The tilt-scoping test only recorded the spy's first call argument
  and never asserted on the resulting probability -- mutation-verified 3
  real bug shapes survived it (full_month_sums swapped for the tail sums
  themselves; the wrong full-window full_month_sums passed to the tail
  call; seasonal_mean_mm silently dropped to None for the tail call only).
  Fixed: the test now asserts all 3 call args on both the full-window and
  tail-only `apply_seasonal_tilt()` calls, a call-counter proving
  `seasonal_mean_mm` is reused not re-fetched, and pins the resulting
  probability via an INDEPENDENT direct call to the real (unmocked)
  `apply_seasonal_tilt()` with the same known inputs -- not by reading back
  whatever the code-under-test itself produced.
  (M3) The <15-usable-tail-years fallback (`combined_totals = None`) had
  zero test coverage -- mutation-verified that changing it to
  `combined_totals = member_totals` (silently treating the near-only
  members as if they already covered the full remaining window, missing
  every tail day's rain) passed the entire suite. Fixed with a dedicated
  test constructing history where every year is missing exactly 4 days,
  all inside the tail range -- pushes the tail range's own 20%-missing
  threshold over the edge while staying under it for the full remaining-
  window range, the only way to reach this branch without the earlier,
  unrelated `len(remaining_sums) < 15` check firing first. Also added a
  `_log.debug` on this branch (previously silent, unlike the analogous
  warning at the `len(remaining_sums) < 15` gate above it).
  (L1) The stored signal carried no marker of which regime produced it
  (near-only real-forecast vs. far-case forecast+climatology-blend, and per
  H1, materially different model composition) -- pooling both into one
  future Brier/calibration comparison without being able to stratify.
  Fixed by adding `rain_forecast_blend_tail_days` and
  `rain_forecast_blend_n_members` to the signal payload (both branches,
  `tail_days=0` for the near-only case) -- log-only, must ship before rows
  accumulate since it can't be retrofitted onto already-logged predictions.
  (L2) Opus review found this diff newly makes the "before month starts"
  branch reachable for the forecast-blend fetch for the first time (the
  shipped 2026-07-28 near-only guard structurally could never trigger
  there, since `remaining_end_date - today_local` was always >= a full
  month's length in that branch) -- and when `remaining_start_date` is more
  than ~7 days out, `icon_seamless`'s real horizon (live-probed above)
  means the ENTIRE requested range returns all-null for that model, which
  `_fetch_ensemble_precip_multiday`'s `is_all_null` check treats as a dead-
  model FAILURE recorded on the circuit breaker SHARED with every other
  market's ensemble fetch, not a benign empty result. Not reachable today
  given `RAIN_MAX_DAYS_OUT`'s own days_out gate on the caller side (a
  3-day margin from a plausible future env bump), but this diff's own
  restructuring is what newly exposes it, so fixed inline rather than
  filed separately (same-payload test: it's the same `rain_forecast_blend`
  fetch path this change already touches) with a conservative, explicitly-
  documented 6-day gap guard plus a dedicated regression test proving the
  exact previously-open gap (7-13 day gap, where the general fetch_end_date
  check alone would still have let it through) is now closed.
  (L3) `apply_seasonal_tilt()`'s additive-shift-then-floor-at-0.0 design
  assumes a multi-week distribution; a 1-3 day tail (common once a ticket
  is checked mid-month) is mostly exact zeros, so a dry SEAS5 tilt gets
  floor-clipped on most samples and is under-applied relative to a wet one.
  Accepted as a documented no-op: fixing it means changing
  `apply_seasonal_tilt()`'s own clamp behavior, which also feeds the
  ALREADY-SHIPPED full-remaining-window tilt `blended_prob`/`rec_side`/
  sizing depend on -- genuinely separate surgery, out of this change's
  scope. Magnitude is tiny (a fraction of an inch on a 1-3 day tail) and
  this signal is shadow-only regardless.
  (L4) Added a far-case analogue of the near-only case's own "existing
  calc is byte-identical with vs. without the blend" test
  (`test_far_case_signal_does_not_change_forecast_prob_or_ci`) --
  particularly relevant now that H2's cross-product fix removed the shared-
  RNG risk (M1) the original design carried.
  (L5) The original resample test's headline probability assertion landed
  on the clamp ceiling (every forced draw picked a deliberate outlier),
  the same clamp-collapse shape as 2026-07-28's own H3 finding. Superseded
  entirely by the new cross-product test
  (`test_far_case_cross_product_not_random_sampled`), which uses two clean
  value groups on each axis so the resulting fraction (375/600 = 0.625) is
  an exact combinatorial value strictly inside the clamp range that only a
  true cross product produces.

  Every fix (H1, H2, L2, L3-as-no-op-decision) mutation-tested via the Edit
  tool against a live-reverted version of the real code, confirmed the
  corresponding test fails, restored. Also mutation-tested the untouched
  <=16-day near-only branch's own boundary and off-by-one guards to confirm
  this restructuring didn't relocate a bug into them (it didn't).

  9 new/rewritten tests in `TestRainForecastBlendSignal`
  (`tests/test_rain_markets.py`; 68 tests collected in that file total, up

  updated for the 14-day cap; the tilt-scoping test strengthened (M2); the
  obsolete per-member-resample test replaced with the cross-product test
  (H2/L5); new tests for the 6-day gap guard (L2), the thin-tail-years
