[RESOLVED 2026-07-26 -- explicit guard shipped. UPDATE 2026-08-03: the
  season-total count/category shape now has a real shadow-only model too
  (season-count model, see the dated resolution block after "When to
  revisit" below) -- per-storm-category (KXHURCAT) and per-city landfall
  markets (still 0 open markets) remain completely unbuilt]
  HURRICANE MARKETS -- EXPLICIT GUARD ADDED AFTER A CONFIRMED LIVE GAP
Priority: was believed Low/inert (see the parent RAIN / SNOW / HURRICANE
  MARKETS entry) -- reclassified High for the guard fix itself once live
  testing found the "safe by coincidence" story was actually wrong.

Problem:
  Split out of the combined RAIN / SNOW / HURRICANE MARKETS entry because
  hurricane isn't the same shape as rain/snow's per-city monthly ladder:
  Kalshi's real hurricane series are season-aggregate count/category
  markets keyed by storm name (`KXHURCAT-26FAUSTO-T5`, "Will Fausto become
  a Category 5 hurricane?") or by season (`KXHURCTOT-26DEC01-T9`, "more
  than 9 Atlantic hurricanes in 2026?"), plus a separate family of per-city
  landfall series (`KXHURMIA`, `KXHURTB`, `KXHURNYC`, ...) that show 0 open
  markets as of 2026-07-26 (confirmed live, pre-season -- hurricane season
  peaks Aug-Oct). Neither shape is city-keyed the way a `_KXHUR_MONTHLY_
  CITY`-style dict would assume, so this was never going to get the same
  Step-1 treatment as snow.
  A first-pass plan assumed hurricane tickers were already safe by
  coincidence -- `_parse_city_from_ticker()` returns `None` for count/
  category tickers and `_parse_market_condition()` returns `None` for
  landfall tickers, so `analyze_trade()`'s existing `no_city`/
  `no_condition` gates would catch both. An adversarial re-check against
  real, currently-open Kalshi tickers found this was WRONG: `KXHURCAT-
  26FAUSTO-T5` defeats BOTH gates simultaneously -- `_parse_city_from_
  ticker()` matches `"Austin"` off a substring inside `"FAUSTO"`, and
  `_parse_market_condition()` parses the `-T5` suffix + `yes_sub_title:
  "Category 5 or above"` into a real `{"type": "above", "threshold": 5.0}`
  condition. It was blocked today only by an unrelated, fragile accident --
  `KXHURCAT-26FAUSTO` has no ticker-embedded date, so `analyze_trade()`'s
  earlier `no_date` gate fires first -- and this exact codebase already has
  precedent (`KXRAIN*M`'s `close_time`-derived dating) for removing that
  kind of date dependency on a future pass, which would have silently
  reactivated the misclassification. Separately, `main.py`'s manual
  `cmd_order` path was confirmed to place a real order against ANY ticker,
  including a hurricane one, without `analyze_trade()`'s gates passing at
  all (`paper.py`'s own `check_position_limits()` docstring already
  documented this as "the one call path that can be reached WITHOUT going
  through analyze_trade() first").

What was fixed:
  An explicit `if ticker_up.startswith("KXHUR"): return None` guard, added
  in the three places that matter rather than relying on incidental gate
  ordering: `analyze_trade()` (first check in the function, before every
  other gate), `main.py cmd_order` (refuses the order outright, not just a
  warning), and `paper.check_position_limits()` (one of several call paths
  reachable without `analyze_trade()` -- see the correction below). 11 new
  regression tests (`tests/test_hurricane_gating.py`) pin the new explicit
  guard directly, including the concrete `KXHURCAT-26FAUSTO-T5` ticker that
  proved the old assumption wrong, plus controls confirming ordinary
  daily/rain tickers are unaffected and that `cmd_order` still refuses
  without even fetching the market. `order_executor.py` was deliberately
  NOT touched -- that loop only ever processes opportunities that already
  survived `analyze_trade()`, whose new guard makes it unreachable for this
  ticker family, same reachability shape as rain's own original Step 1
  found for that file (commit `b2171ba`).

  CORRECTION (same-day second opus review, before this ever got committed):
  the first-pass guard used a bare `ticker.startswith("KXHUR")` check in
  all three places. A live series-list scan (291 real "Climate and
  Weather" series) found this missed a large real, currently-open surface:
  `KXTROPSTORM` (8 open markets), `KXFIRSTHURRICANE` (53 open markets),
  `KXNAMEDSTORM`, `KXNEXTHURDATE`/`KXNEXTCAT5HURDATE`, and an entire
  *unprefixed* legacy `HUR*` namespace (`HURCAT`, `HURMIA`, `HURNYC`, ... --
  23 series, registered separately from their `KXHUR*` counterparts, both
  real) -- confirmed live that `HURCAT-26FAUSTO-T5` (no "KX") reproduces
  the exact same `_parse_city_from_ticker`/`_parse_market_condition`
  double-defeat as the original finding, and that `py main.py buy
  KXTROPSTORM-... yes 5 0.50` would have placed a real order under the
  first-pass guard. Fixed by replacing the prefix check with a single
  shared `weather_markets.is_hurricane_ticker()` (substring match on
  `("HUR", "TROPSTORM", "NAMEDSTORM")`, live-verified zero false positives
  against every tracked/known series -- in particular `KXSNOWSTORM`, a
  real but unrelated national snow-event series, does NOT match, which a
  naive `"STORM"`-only check would have wrongly caught) used by all three
  guard sites instead of three independent hardcoded literals. Also added
  the same explicit guard directly in `cmd_order` for monthly-snow tickers
  (previously relied solely on `check_position_limits`, which fails open
  on an unhandled exception in that call site) and corrected the "the one
  call path reachable without analyze_trade()" comments in `paper.py`/
  `order_executor.py` -- `main.cmd_paper` and `web_app`'s `/api/paper-order`
  are two more such paths (both still funnel through `check_position_limits`,
  so no live hole resulted, but the claim was wrong -- the same untraced-
  call-sites shape flagged before in this project, see
  [[feedback_trace_all_call_sites]]). A separately-flagged vacuous test
  (`KXDENSNOWM`'s city resolution passed even with the new dict deleted,
  since the pre-existing "DEN" substring fallback coincidentally agrees)
  was fixed with a mutation-style test pointing the dict at a fake city.
  8 more regression tests added for the broadened marker set (`KXTROPSTORM`,
  `KXFIRSTHURRICANE`, `KXNAMEDSTORM`, legacy `HURCAT`, `KXSNOWSTORM`-must-
  NOT-match, plus the new `cmd_order` snow guard) -- 19 hurricane +
  20 snow tests total, full scoped sweep (504 tests) passing, ruff/mypy/
  ruff-format clean.

What the fix does NOT do:
  No probability model exists for either hurricane market shape. This is a
  safety tightening only -- discovery, a real count/category model, and
  the per-city landfall series (still 0 open markets) all remain
  completely unbuilt. `KNOWN_WEATHER_SERIES`/`check_series_drift()` still
  don't watch any hurricane series at all (deliberately -- adding one
  there without a matching parser branch would just reproduce this same
  bug class for a series check_series_drift would then be actively
  prompting someone to add).
  UPDATE 2026-08-03: the season-total count-market half of "count/category"
  now has a real model (see the dated resolution block below) --
  `KNOWN_WEATHER_SERIES`/`check_series_drift()` now DO watch those 5 exact
  series (and only those 5, by exact series-ticker membership, not
  substring). KXHURCAT (the per-STORM category shape, e.g. "will Fausto
  become a Category 5 hurricane?") and the per-city landfall series (still
  0 open markets) remain completely unbuilt and still fully blocked by
  is_hurricane_ticker()'s original guard.

Why not now (for the real model):
  - Count/category markets aren't city-keyed at all -- they need their own
    data model (storm-name or season-keyed), not a per-city dict like
    rain/snow. The per-city landfall series ARE city-keyed but have 0 open
    markets today, so there's nothing live to build against yet.
  - Effort scales as its own product line, same reasoning the parent
    RAIN / SNOW / HURRICANE MARKETS entry already gives for snow/hurricane
    generally.
  - UPDATE 2026-08-03: this reasoning held for KXHURCAT (per-storm, needs a
    live per-storm NHC forecast/advisory pipeline -- a genuinely different,
    more novel real-time data problem than the season-total shape) and for
    per-city landfall (still 0 open markets, confirmed live again
    2026-08-03 -- unchanged since 2026-07-26) -- both remain deliberately
    unbuilt. It did NOT hold for the season-total count shape once actually
    scoped: NOAA HURDAT2 (public, historical) plus Kalshi's own settled
    markets (for the live tilt) turned out to be a tractable, non-"own
    product line" lift once broken out from the other two shapes -- see the
    dated resolution block below.

When to revisit:
  - Once real per-city landfall markets actually open (re-check once
    hurricane season is underway, Aug-Oct 2026 -- still 0 open as of
    2026-08-03) AND there's real appetite to design that model separately.
  - KXHURCAT (per-storm category): needs a live per-storm NHC forecast/
    advisory data pipeline and a storm-name registry -- a different, more
    novel problem than the season-total shape below. Not started.
  - Independent of that: if `KXRAIN*M`'s close_time-derived dating pattern
    is ever extended to other market families, re-verify this guard still
    covers `KXHURCAT`-style tickers -- the fragile `no_date` accident this
    entry documents would stop being a backstop at that point, though the
    explicit `KXHUR` guard added here does not depend on it.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-03] HURRICANE MARKETS -- SEASON-TOTAL COUNT MODEL SHIPPED SHADOW-ONLY
Priority: was Low (see the parent RAIN / SNOW / HURRICANE MARKETS entry and
  this entry's own "Why not now" above) -- the season-total count shape is
  now Medium, matching rain/snow's own real-shadow-model priority; KXHURCAT
  and per-city landfall remain Low/unbuilt.

Problem:
  Re-verified live 2026-08-03 (this session's own first step, per the
  standing "re-verify before building" workflow): the per-city landfall
  gate this entry's "When to revisit" named had NOT fired -- all ~54
  per-city/regional landfall series (KXHURMIA, KXHURNYC, KXHURPATH*, etc.)
  still show 0 open markets, unchanged since 2026-07-26. But the OTHER
  count/category shape -- season-total hurricane/tropical-storm counts --
  was very much open and tradeable, independent of that gate: 142 open
  markets across 5 series (`KXHURCTOT`/`KXHURCTOTMAJ`/`KXTROPSTORM` for the
  Atlantic, `KXHURRICANE`/`KXNAMEDSTORM` for Eastern+Central Pacific), e.g.
  "Will there be more than 9 Atlantic hurricanes in 2026?". User confirmed
  via AskUserQuestion this should be built first (recommended: climatology-
  only model, no live per-storm tracking needed, largest open-market
  surface), with NOAA HURDAT2 historical data as the primary source, and
  check_series_drift() extended for just these 5 series once they had a
  real parser.

  HURDAT2 only carries FINALIZED seasons (current year's data isn't added
  until ~April the following year), so it supplies the historical base
  distribution only -- the "current season count-to-date" tilt needed a
  different source. Found one requiring no new external dependency: Kalshi's
  own settled `KXHURRICANENAMES` markets (one per pre-assigned storm name
  per basin per season, "will storm X become a hurricane?") directly encode
  NHC's real season-to-date hurricane classifications. Confirmed live this
  session that 2026's Atlantic count is 0 so far and Eastern Pacific is 2
  (Fausto, Genevieve) via this exact derivation.

What shipped:
  New module `hurricane_climatology.py`: fetches/caches NOAA's Atlantic
  HURDAT2 file and combined Eastern+Central-Pacific HURDAT2 file (storms
  distinguished by their own AL/EP/CP storm-ID prefix -- confirmed live the
  Pacific file already covers both basins), parses each storm's max
  sustained wind and the day-of-year it first crossed each of Kalshi's own
  literal settlement thresholds (34kt tropical-storm / 64kt hurricane /
  96kt major-hurricane -- matches rules_primary text exactly, not NHC's own
  separately-evolving classification-code convention). Builds a 30-most-
  recent-complete-season empirical bootstrap distribution per (basin,
  count_type) -- 30 years chosen deliberately (not just copying this
  codebase's existing "30" convention): avoids diluting a current-era
  estimate with the markedly quieter pre-1995 AMO phase. Parser cross-
  checked live against real published 2023/2024 Atlantic season totals
  (18/11/5 and 20/7/3 named-storm/hurricane/major-hurricane counts) --
  exact match both years.

  The live tilt: for each historical window year, computes that year's OWN
  count-as-of the SAME calendar day-of-year as today, then adds (today's
  real current_count minus that year's historical to-date count) to that
  year's real season-end count -- bootstraps the REMAINING count from
  history and adds it to this season's actual progress, mirroring
  acis_precip.historical_remaining_and_full_month_sums's "month-to-date-
  actual + historical-remaining" shape exactly, just discrete counts
  instead of a continuous inches total. Scoped to count_type="hurricane"
  ONLY -- major_hurricane/tropical_storm ship climatology-only (no tilt) in
  this pass; deriving a clean per-basin current count for those two would
  need a per-year storm-name-to-basin mapping table (KXHURCAT's per-storm
  tickers aren't basin-tagged) that doesn't exist yet, an honest, explicit
  scope decision, not a silent gap.

  `weather_markets.py`: `is_hurricane_count_ticker()` narrowly carves out
  the 5 series (by exact series-ticker, NOT substring/startswith --
  "KXHURCTOT" is a strict prefix of "KXHURCTOTMAJ", so anything else would
  misclassify one as the other) from `is_hurricane_ticker()`'s much broader
  marker set, which still blocks everything else. `_parse_hurricane_count_
  condition()` reads floor_strike/strike_type directly off Kalshi's own
  market fields (same established convention as every other ladder-market
  branch here), deriving basin/count_type/season_year from the ticker
  string itself (`_hurricane_count_key_from_ticker`, shared with tracker.py's
  counter below). `_analyze_hurricane_count_trade()` computes the real
  probability/edge/Kelly size via `_price_and_size()` (same shared tail
  every other market type uses) and is dispatched from `analyze_trade()`
  exactly like rain/snow's monthly-ladder fast-paths -- required threading
  a `_is_hurricane_count` bypass through the no_forecast/no_city/no_coords
  gates (this market family has no city at all, unlike rain/snow) and a new
  `HURRICANE_MAX_DAYS_OUT` (260 days -- these markets open ~7-8 months
  before close, confirmed live) replacing `MAX_DAYS_OUT` for this ticker
  family in the days-out gate.

  Shadow-only rollout, same shape as rain/snow: `_hurricane_count_gates_
  active()` (HURRICANE_TRADING_ENABLED env var + >=20 settled distinct
  (basin, count_type, season_year) events, mirroring `_rain_gates_active()`/
  `_snow_gates_active()` exactly) gates real order placement in
  `order_executor._auto_place_trades()`'s per-ticker shadow-routing branch,
  `paper.check_position_limits()`, and all 3 of main.py's manual order paths
  (cmd_order, _quick_paper_buy, cmd_paper buy) -- `analyze_trade()` itself is
  NOT gated (it always computes the real analysis, same as rain/snow, so
  calibration data accumulates regardless of the gate). Explicitly documented
  as a MUCH slower-clearing floor than rain/snow's ~2-month estimate: a
  season-count market settles AT MOST once per year per (basin, count_type)
  -- 9 combinations total across 3 basins -- so this floor could take
  several YEARS to clear, not weeks or months; a real, structural cadence
  difference, not an oversight.

  Current-count-to-date cache: `analyze_trade()`'s call chain has no live
  Kalshi client of its own (unlike every other market type, which only need
  forecast data already attached to `enriched`) -- mirrors
  `refresh_hourly_target_hours()`'s exact division of labor: a new
  `refresh_hurricane_count_to_date()`, called from `cmd_cron` right beside
  `refresh_hourly_target_hours`, fetches settled `KXHURRICANENAMES` markets
  once/basin/day and caches the count to `HURRICANE_COUNT_TO_DATE_PATH`
  (added to `paths.py`, not module-local -- matches `HOURLY_TARGET_HOURS_
  PATH`'s own shared-state precedent); `_analyze_hurricane_count_trade()`
  reads it client-free via `_get_cached_hurricane_count_to_date()`, which
  refuses a cache entry from the wrong season_year (never lets a stale
  prior-season count silently tilt the current season).

  `tracker.count_settled_hurricane_predictions()`: counts DISTINCT (basin,
  count_type, season_year) events, NOT raw prediction rows -- the same
  raw-row-vs-distinct-event inflation risk `count_settled_snow_predictions()`
  was already fixed for (a single season/count-type settles up to ~9 sibling
  strikes from the SAME real outcome).

  `check_series_drift()`/`KNOWN_WEATHER_SERIES` now watch exactly these 5
  series (exact-match, not substring -- deliberately narrower than
  `is_hurricane_ticker()`'s marker set, so this can never start watching a
  hurricane series with no matching parser branch, the exact bug class the
  parent entry above warns about).

  87 new tests: `tests/test_hurricane_climatology.py` (26 -- HURDAT2 parsing
  against a hand-verifiable synthetic fixture, season counting, the tilt
  bootstrap, exceedance probability, bootstrap CI), `tests/test_hurricane_
  markets.py` (60 -- ticker/condition parsing incl. the KXHURCTOT/
  KXHURCTOTMAJ prefix-collision guard, the shadow gate, the count-to-date
  cache, the full `_analyze_hurricane_count_trade` dispatch with mocked
  climatology data, and the `check_position_limits`/`cmd_order` conditional-
  guard tests mirroring snow's own), plus 3 new shadow-routing tests in
  `tests/test_shadow_predictions.py`, 5 new distinct-event-counting tests in
  `tests/test_tracker.py`, and 1 new exclusion test in `tests/test_
  consistency.py`. 3 pre-existing `tests/test_hurricane_gating.py` tests
  updated (KXHURCTOT/KXTROPSTORM/KXNAMEDSTORM no longer hit
  `hurricane_not_supported` -- they now reach `condition_parse`/`no_date`
  instead, a real, correct behavior change, not a broken test); every other
  test in that file (KXHURCAT, per-city landfall, legacy unprefixed HUR*,
  the broadened-marker-set regression controls) unchanged and still passing.
  8 real mutations run against the highest-risk logic (basin/count_type
  classification, exceedance-probability direction, the blanket-guard
  carve-out condition, the distinct-event dedup, the tilt arithmetic,
  paper.py's conditional gate, the fail-closed dispatcher fix, and the
  consistency.py exclusion) -- all caught by the new tests, all reverted
  cleanly. Full scoped regression (test_hurricane_climatology.py +
  test_hurricane_markets.py + test_hurricane_gating.py +
  test_shadow_predictions.py + test_tracker.py + test_series_drift.py +
  test_consistency.py, 482 tests) plus a broader sweep (test_rain_
  markets.py, test_snow_markets.py, test_forecasting.py,
  test_infrastructure.py, test_weather_markets.py, test_price_and_size.py,
  test_city_registry_manifest.py, test_dead_code_scan.py) all pass -- one
  pre-existing, unrelated failure (`test_forecasting.py::TestLearnedWeights::
  test_load_learned_weights_handles_non_numeric_value`) confirmed present
  identically before this session's changes (via git stash), not caused by
  this work. ruff + ruff format + mypy clean on every touched file.

  Independent opus review (3 parallel agents, scoped by subsystem --
  climatology/math, ticker-parsing/dispatch, safety-guard wiring -- effort=
  high): 15 findings total, every one fixed before commit (none skipped as
  out-of-scope, except one explicitly pre-existing gap noted below). Most
  consequential:
  - HIGH (math): `season_end_total_distribution` derived its year window
    from `{s["year"] for s in storms}` rather than an explicit calendar
    range -- silently DROPPING any season with zero storms of the
    requested basin's prefix instead of counting it as a real 0. Invisible
    for Atlantic/Eastern-Pacific (every year has >=1 storm) but measured
    live to overstate Central Pacific's `P(>0 hurricanes)` by 23 points
    (0.600 vs the correct 0.367 over the same 30-year span) -- CPAC has 35
    real gap years out of 77 (1949-2025). Fixed by iterating an explicit
    calendar range and calling `season_end_counts()` for every year in it
    (which already correctly returns 0 for an absent year).
  - HIGH (dispatch): a hurricane-count-series ticker whose OWN fields
    failed to parse (missing `floor_strike`, unexpected `strike_type`) fell
    through `_parse_market_condition()` into the generic temperature-
    threshold parser below -- which matches this family's real "-T9"/
    "-T30" ticker suffix as a °F threshold, reproducing the exact KXHURCAT
    bug class the whole `is_hurricane_ticker()` guard exists to prevent
    (terminates in an `AssertionError` today via this file's own
    `assert city is not None` narrowing, or silently mis-scores under
    `python -O`, where asserts are stripped). Fixed: any ticker whose
    series is one of the 5 hurricane-count series now fails closed
    (returns `None` outright) at that dispatcher, regardless of why its
    own parse failed, rather than falling through.
  - HIGH (safety): adding the 5 series to `KNOWN_WEATHER_SERIES` (so
    `get_weather_markets()` now returns them) exposed them to
    `consistency.find_violations()`, whose output feeds `main.py`'s arb
    auto-placer (`paper.place_paper_order`) DIRECTLY -- with no shadow-gate
    check of its own, and (unlike rain/snow) not merely "safe by
    coincidence": KXHURCTOT-style tickers' real day-level date and "-T9"
    threshold suffix both match `consistency.py`'s grouping regexes; only
    today's real title text (lacking the literal "above"/">" the
    threshold-direction fallback requires) kept it inert -- the exact
    "safe by coincidence" shape this project already burned itself on once
    for this same ticker family. Fixed by adding the same exclusion
    rain/snow/hourly already have in `consistency._group_markets()`.
  - MEDIUM-HIGH (math): an empty (non-exception) `KXHURRICANENAMES` fetch
    response -- series renamed, event-ticker format changed, transient
    API-side filter change -- previously wrote `count=0` for every basin,
    indistinguishable from a real "zero hurricanes so far" season. Fixed:
    only write a basin whose event_ticker matched at least one settled
    market at all; otherwise leave it unwritten so the existing missing-
    entry fallback (climatology-only) applies.
  - HIGH (math): the count-to-date cache's `date` field was written but
    never checked for staleness on read -- a stalled refresh job (repeated
    fetch failures, or cron simply not running) would silently serve an
    arbitrarily-old count-to-date forever, desynced from `as_of_month_day`
    (always derived from TODAY). Verified this can flip a real probability
    from 0.99 to 0.01 with no warning. Fixed: reject any cache entry older
    than 2 days, falling back to climatology-only.
  - LOW-MEDIUM (dispatch): `KXHURRICANE`'s major-vs-total count-type
    derivation (`endswith("MAJ")` else "hurricane") failed OPEN -- any
    other suffix would silently price a major-hurricane market against
    total-hurricane climatology, a materially fatter distribution, with no
    warning. Fixed with an explicit `"MAJ"`/`"TOT"` allow-list, fail closed
    otherwise (also tightened for `KXNAMEDSTORM`, previously unconditional).
  - Also fixed: `season_year` cross-checked against the market's own
    close_time (>1yr mismatch now fails closed -- protects
    `tracker.count_settled_hurricane_predictions()`'s dedup key from a
    malformed ticker); leap-year misalignment in day-of-year threshold-
    crossing comparisons (switched `threshold_day`/`as_of_*` from ordinal
    day-of-year ints to `(month, day)` tuples, which compare correctly
    regardless of either year's leap status); an absurd wind reading
    (e.g. 9999, not the `-999` missing sentinel) no longer fabricates a
    storm; a truncated/stale HURDAT2 download now logs a loud warning if
    its newest storm year falls more than 2 years behind today;
    `_get_cached_hurricane_count_to_date` no longer raises on a corrupt
    non-dict cache entry or a non-int `count`; `count_settled_hurricane_
    predictions()`'s parse-failure warning no longer fires for the
    unrelated `KXHURRICANENAMES` series (a `LIKE 'KXHURRICANE%'` prefix
    collision that would have desensitized the real "gate frozen at 0"
    alarm had that series ever been logged as a prediction).
  - NOT fixed (explicitly out of scope, flagged as a separate follow-up
    task): `cmd_today()`'s "[P] Place" interactive path bypasses
    `TRADING_PAUSED` and every shadow-only gate entirely (rain/snow/
    hurricane-count alike) -- confirmed PRE-EXISTING (rain and snow already
    had this exact gap before this session), not introduced or worsened by
    this work. Fixing it means touching the shared placement path for all
    three market families at once, out of scope for a hurricane-specific
    session.

What this does NOT do:
  Real sizing -- shadow/log-only until HURRICANE_TRADING_ENABLED=1 AND the
  20-distinct-event floor clears (expected to take years, not months, see
  above). major_hurricane/tropical_storm count types have no live tilt yet
  (climatology-only) -- only "hurricane" (category 1+) has a clean, exact,
  basin-tagged Kalshi-settled-market source today. KXHURCAT (per-storm
  category) and per-city landfall markets remain completely untouched --
  still gated by is_hurricane_ticker()'s original blanket guard, still 0
  open markets for landfall as of this session's live re-check.

When to revisit:
  - Once HURRICANE_TRADING_ENABLED is set and real settled data accumulates
    (expect a multi-year timescale, not the ~2-month rain/snow estimate) --
    check get_signal_graduation_report()-style correlation before ever
    relying on real sizing.
  - major_hurricane/tropical_storm live tilt: needs a per-year storm-name-
    to-basin mapping (WMO's pre-assigned name lists are public and fixed
    years in advance) to derive a current-count-to-date from KXHURCAT's
    per-storm settled results the same way KXHURRICANENAMES already does
    for "hurricane". Not started.
  - KXHURCAT/per-city landfall: see the updated "When to revisit" in the
    entry above -- unchanged by this session's work.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-07] HURRICANE MARKETS -- TIME-TO-NEXT-EVENT MODEL SHIPPED SHADOW-ONLY (KXNEXTHURDATE/KXNEXTCAT5HURDATE)
Priority: was Low (see the parent RAIN / SNOW / HURRICANE MARKETS entry) --
  now Medium, matching the season-count model's own priority above.

Problem:
  Re-verified live 2026-08-07 (this session's own first step, per the
  standing "re-verify before building" workflow): the parent entry's own
  summary bracket claimed "hurricane's own probability model remains fully
  open," which was stale -- it predated the season-count model above
  (shipped 2026-08-03) and was never updated afterward. Live re-check found
  three genuinely still-open hurricane shapes: per-storm category
  (KXHURCAT, 3 open markets on the live storm Fausto, needs a live NHC
  advisory/forecast-cone pipeline), first-hurricane-by-name
  (KXFIRSTHURRICANE, 21 open markets, needs an order-of-formation model
  against the season's pre-assigned name list), and time-to-next-event
  (KXNEXTHURDATE/KXNEXTCAT5HURDATE, 8+4=12 open markets, opened 2026-08-06 --
  brand new, pure climatology). Chose time-to-next-event: it reuses
  hurricane_climatology.py's existing HURDAT2 machinery from the count model
  above with no new live-data pipeline, unlike the other two. KXHURCAT and
  KXFIRSTHURRICANE remain fully open, their own future entries, not touched
  this session.

  Market shape (confirmed live against every open market in both series):
  "Will [an Atlantic hurricane / an Atlantic Category-5 hurricane] form
  before <date>?" -- floor_strike/strike_type are null; the entire condition
  is the market's own close_time (e.g. close_time "2026-09-15T03:59Z" <->
  yes_sub_title "Before Sep 15, 2026"). Both series are Atlantic-only in
  every real market (rules_primary says "in the Atlantic"; no EPAC/CPAC
  sibling series exist).

What shipped:
  hurricane_climatology.py: NEXT_EVENT_THRESHOLDS_KT = {"hurricane": 64,
  "cat5_hurricane": 137} (137kt matches KXHURCAT's own live-confirmed
  Category-5 threshold); parse_hurdat2's threshold_day now built from the
  union of COUNT_THRESHOLDS_KT.values() | NEXT_EVENT_THRESHOLDS_KT.values()
  -- one parse serves both models, no new fetch. New first_occurrence_day()
  (earliest day a season's storms first reached a given kt), and
  next_event_outcomes()/next_event_probability()/bootstrap_ci_next_event()
  (day-of-first-occurrence analog of season_end_total_distribution()/
  exceedance_probability()/bootstrap_ci()).

  A real design correction caught during implementation (self-review before
  this ever reached the user, then re-verified against live behavior): the
  first draft always conditioned the historical distribution on "today's
  date," regardless of whether the model actually KNEW the event hadn't
  happened yet this season. For cat5_hurricane (no live signal at all) and
  for hurricane type when the count-to-date cache is stale/missing, that
  would have silently ASSUMED "hasn't happened yet" -- reproducing the exact
  stale-cache "flips a probability with no warning" failure mode
  _get_cached_hurricane_count_to_date's own staleness guard already exists
  to prevent for the count model above. Fixed: next_event_outcomes() only
  conditions on as_of_month_day when the caller passes it explicitly (only
  when live data CONFIRMS "not yet happened"); otherwise it runs fully
  unconditional (every window year contributes, no eligibility filtering) --
  mirrors season_end_total_distribution's own
  "as_of_month_day is None or current_count is None -> unconditional"
  fallback exactly.

  Also caught live during implementation: parse_city_date()'s generic
  ticker-date regex, run against "KXNEXTHURDATE-26DEC01-26SEP15", matches
  the FIRST date-like segment ("26DEC01" -- a season-reference suffix shared
  identically by every "before <date>" sibling) rather than the real
  threshold date in the second segment, producing a non-None but WRONG
  target_date (Dec 1, not the market's real Sep 15 close). Confirmed live
  before writing any gate logic. analyze_trade()'s no_date/no_city/
  no_coords/no_forecast gates are all bypassed for this ticker family (same
  as monthly rain/snow, NOT the same as hurricane-count -- hurricane-count's
  own ticker date suffix IS its real close date, so it safely reuses the
  generic target_date-based past-date check; this family cannot), and it
  gets its own close_time-derived past-close check
  (_hur_next_event_close_dt) instead, exactly like rain/snow's own
  _rain_close_dt/_snow_close_dt.

  weather_markets.py: is_hurricane_next_event_ticker()/
  _parse_hurricane_next_event_condition() (condition carries only
  event_type, never a duplicated kt -- _analyze_hurricane_next_event_trade
  derives kt from hurricane_climatology.NEXT_EVENT_THRESHOLDS_KT, matching
  the count model's own single-source-of-truth discipline for count_type/kt);
  _hurricane_next_event_gates_active() (own env var
  HURRICANE_NEXT_EVENT_TRADING_ENABLED, own 20-sample floor via
  tracker.count_settled_hurricane_next_event_predictions() -- kept fully
  separate from the count model's gate, matching this codebase's
  established one-flag-per-shape precedent: sharing would either block this
  faster-clearing shape on the count model's years-to-clear floor, or

  path -> _analyze_hurricane_next_event_trade(), which reuses the count
  model's EXISTING _get_cached_hurricane_count_to_date("ATL",
  season_year=today's year) cache for event_type="hurricane"'s live tilt
  (zero new cache/cron plumbing) -- cat5_hurricane ships climatology-only
  (unconditional mode always, no live "already occurred" signal in this
  pass, same explicit scope cut the count model already made for
  major_hurricane/tropical_storm); both count as the same "HUR_<basin>"
  exposure-cap key as the count model (correlated Atlantic activity caps
  together, not a second silent key); KNOWN_WEATHER_SERIES/
  check_series_drift() extended with the same exact-series-membership
  (not substring) matching the count model's own 5 series already use.

  tracker.py: count_settled_hurricane_next_event_predictions() -- unlike
  the count model, this market family has no sibling-ladder-brackets-per-
  event risk (each ticker is its own atomic question, not one of several

  sites.

What this does NOT do:
  No live "already occurred" tilt for cat5_hurricane (climatology-only,

Independent opus review: given the size, scoped to 3 parallel Agent(opus,
  effort=high) passes by subsystem (climatology math; ticker-parsing/

  2 HIGH findings, independently surfaced by two different reviewers:
  (1) bootstrap_ci_next_event didn't clamp its output to [0.01, 0.99] the
  way next_event_probability already does -- a unanimous outcome set (the
  common case for kt=64; every recent Atlantic season has a hurricane by
  mid-September) produced an exact (1.0, 1.0)/(0.0, 0.0) CI, which
  _price_and_size's ci_high<=ci_low fallback turns into kelly_fraction(1.0,
  price)==0.0 -- silently zeroing size for the model's own highest-
  confidence signals AND (since shadow logging shares the same size-then-
  log validator) permanently freezing count_settled_hurricane_next_event_
  predictions() at 0, so the 20-sample graduation gate could never open.
  Fixed by clamping. (2) No minimum-sample floor on conditional mode --
  measured against real Atlantic data, the eligible-year subset already
  drops below 15 by ~Aug 1 and hits 0 by mid-September, so the model could
  compute (and shadow-log, poisoning Brier scoring) a full-strength signal
  off 2-3 data points, or fabricate a bare 0.5 from zero. Fixed:
  _analyze_hurricane_next_event_trade now falls back to the unconditional
  baseline (same one used when occurred_this_season is unknown) whenever
  the eligible set is below 15, the same threshold bootstrap_ci_next_event's
  own floor already uses.
  3 more MEDIUM findings fixed: _CONDITION_CONFIDENCE was missing a
  "hurricane_next_event" entry entirely, so the `.get(condition_type, 1.0)`
  fallback silently gave the least-validated model in the codebase the
  MAXIMUM confidence multiplier -- added an explicit 0.50 (below
  hurricane_count's own 0.55, same "a season IS the sample unit" reasoning
  plus this model's extra within-season granularity). target_month_day used
  close_dt's raw UTC date, but Kalshi's "Before <date>" wording is an ET
  calendar date (close_time "...T03:59Z" is 23:59 ET the PRIOR day) --
  measured as a systematic ~1/window_years bias per boundary year, material
  for the smaller cat5 sample; fixed via ZoneInfo("America/New_York")
  conversion before reading .month/.day, mirroring _metar_lock_in's own
  city-local-date pattern. The condition_type exclusion lists gating live-
  trading maturity signals (tracker.count_settled_predictions/_rolling,
  get_rolling_win_rate) and ML training pools (calibration.py, ml_bias.py)
  were never extended for EITHER hurricane sub-model -- closed for both
  hurricane_count (pre-existing gap, closed while touching the same lists)
  and hurricane_next_event across all 9 sites, with regression tests
  (confirmed load-bearing for ml_bias.py's train_all_temperature_scaling in
  particular -- hurricane rows always carry days_out>=1 and a real
  city="HUR_<basin>", so neither of that function's existing NULL-checks
  would have caught them).
  Also fixed: parse_city_date() returned a non-None but WRONG target_date
  (the ticker's shared season-reference suffix, not the real close date) for
  this ticker family -- several downstream consumers (tracker.log_prediction's
  market_date/days_out, order_executor.py, main.py, trade_cycle.py,
  web_app.py) use a "prefer _date, fall back to analysis['target_date'] only
  if _date is None" pattern that only rain/snow's (always-None) and
  hurricane-count's (always-correct) _date values were safe against --
  fixed by making parse_city_date() return None for this series explicitly,
  same as rain/snow. consistency.py's own exclusion test wasn't actually
  mutation-proof (real next-event tickers can't be parsed by _parse_
  threshold's -T/-B suffix regex regardless of the guard, so disabling the
  guard didn't change the test's outcome) -- added a second test using an
  adversarial -T5/-T6-suffixed ticker shape, confirmed via manual mutation
  to actually fail when the guard is removed. The tracker.py counter's SQL
  LIKE prefix (a coarse pre-filter) was broader than is_hurricane_next_
  event_ticker()'s series-exact match -- currently unreachable (a lookalike
  series would contain "HUR" and never pass analyze_trade()'s blanket guard
  to get logged at all) but tightened to exact-match in Python anyway,
  mirroring the sibling counter's own ticker-derived-key validation for the
  identical risk shape. first_occurrence_day() now raises on an unrecognized
  kt instead of silently returning a confidently-wrong all-False result
  (also currently unreachable by construction, same defense-in-depth
  reasoning). Added test coverage for 2 of the 4 main.py sites that lacked
  it (_quick_paper_buy, cmd_paper) -- cmd_today's own "[P] Place" path has
  an identical guard but no existing test anywhere in this codebase reaches
  that function for ANY market family (rain/snow/hurricane-count included);
  building a novel harness for it was judged out of scope for this pass.
  Also strengthened 3 weak tests in test_hurricane_climatology.py (one
  didn't actually test the CI clamp boundary that finding (1) needed, one
  only asserted a list length instead of the specific value, one couldn't
  distinguish "takes the season minimum" from "takes whichever storm is
  parsed first") and fixed a fixture storm-ID typo.
  NOT fixed, documented as explicit known limitations rather than silently
  dropped: (a) a genuine design gap, CONFIRMED (not speculative) via the
  official Kalshi contract terms PDF (assets.kalshi.com/contract_terms/
  STORMDATE.pdf, fetched and read live this session): the real Payout
  Criterion is "any Atlantic tropical storm... reaching <storm category>
  intensity... at any point after Issuance and before <date>" -- anchored to
  this specific CONTRACT'S Issuance (its own open_time), not season start --
  and "After the initial Contract, Contract iterations will be listed on an
  as-needed basis," confirming Kalshi DOES roll this ticker over to a fresh
  "next hurricane" question (a new Issuance point) after each qualifying
  storm. This model's occurred_this_season boolean is keyed off season-wide
  count-to-date, not "since this specific event's Issuance" -- so once a
  rollover happens, the occurred_this_season=True -> 0.99 shortcut would
  misprice a genuinely-still-open post-rollover question as already
  resolved. The two readings coincide TODAY only because the Atlantic count
  is genuinely 0 so far AND this event's own open_time (2026-08-06,
  confirmed live) predates any hurricane this season -- confirmed live via
  client.get_events(series_ticker="KXNEXTHURDATE") that only ONE event
  currently exists (a "KXNEXTHURDATE-0"/"In 2025" event also exists but has
  zero markets ever created under it -- this product never actually
  launched before 2026, so no historical rollover behavior was observable
  to verify against). User's explicit decision after reviewing this
  research: defer as its own follow-up backlog entry rather than fix now
  (see the new entry filed alongside this one) or partially fix -- not
  fixed to any degree in this pass.
  (b) `order_executor._ticker_edge_share`'s event-key (`(city, date, var)`)
  conflates hurricane-count and hurricane-next-event opportunities sharing a
  close date under the same "HUR_ATL"/"max" key, so a shadow-gated opp from
  one sub-model can dilute a live-gated opp's Kelly sizing from the other --
  zero impact today (both sub-models are shadow-gated), only matters once
  one of the two graduates first; redesigning the shared edge-share
  mechanism used by every market type in this bot is out of scope for a
  hurricane-specific change. (c) bootstrap_ci_next_event(outcomes, n=0)
  raises IndexError -- identical latent issue already exists unfixed in the
  sibling bootstrap_ci this codebase has run in production; not exercised at
  the real default n=500 either way, left matching the existing pattern
  rather than hardening only the new sibling function.

When to revisit:
  - Once HURRICANE_NEXT_EVENT_TRADING_ENABLED is set and >=20 distinct
    settled predictions accumulate -- check get_signal_graduation_report()-
    style correlation before ever relying on real sizing. This shape
    settles far more often than the count model's own (multiple "before

    much faster than the count model's multi-year estimate.
  - cat5_hurricane live tilt: needs a Cat5-occurred-to-date signal derived

[RESOLVED (partial) 2026-08-25 -- batch-59 item 3; originally OPEN 2026-08-07 -- new, split out of "HURRICANE MARKETS -- TIME-TO-NEXT-EVENT MODEL SHIPPED SHADOW-ONLY" above per its own "user's explicit decision: defer as its own follow-up entry" note] HURRICANE NEXT-EVENT MODEL'S OCCURRED_THIS_SEASON SIGNAL IS SEASON-SCOPED, NOT ISSUANCE-SCOPED (KALSHI CONFIRMS ROLLOVER)
Priority: Low -- shadow-only, zero live-money risk regardless (see below);
  only affects the accuracy of a shadow-logged signal, not any real order.

Problem:
  Confirmed via the official Kalshi contract terms PDF (assets.kalshi.com/
  contract_terms/STORMDATE.pdf, fetched and read live this session -- not
  speculation): KXNEXTHURDATE/KXNEXTCAT5HURDATE's real Payout Criterion is
  "any Atlantic tropical storm has been classified... reaching <storm
  category> intensity... at any point after Issuance and before <date>" --
  anchored to THIS SPECIFIC CONTRACT's Issuance (its own open_time), not
  season start. And: "After the initial Contract, Contract iterations will
  be listed on an as-needed basis at the discretion of the Exchange" --
  Kalshi confirms it rolls this ticker over to a fresh "next hurricane"
  question (a new Issuance point) after each qualifying storm settles the
  current one early (the PDF's own Expiration Date rule: "If an event
  described in the Payout Criterion occurs, expiration will be moved to an
  earlier date").

  The shipped model (weather_markets._analyze_hurricane_next_event_trade)
  has no concept of "since this event's Issuance" -- occurred_this_season
  (event_type="hurricane") is keyed off `_get_cached_hurricane_count_to_date`,
  a SEASON-WIDE cumulative count, and the unconditional-mode fallback's
  first_occurrence_day() climatology measures "day of the season's FIRST
  qualifying storm" from historical Januarys/Mays, not "days elapsed since
  a specific mid-season Issuance date." Both are season-start-anchored
  proxies for what should be an Issuance-anchored question.

  Confirmed live this session: the currently open event's own open_time is
  2026-08-06 (mid-season, not season start -- itself circumstantial
  evidence this event may already be layered on prior seasons' pattern of
  waiting until real hurricane-season activity picks up before listing, not
  necessarily evidence of a rollover). client.get_events(series_ticker=
  "KXNEXTHURDATE") shows exactly ONE real event today ("KXNEXTHURDATE-
  26DEC01"); a second event ("KXNEXTHURDATE-0", sub_title "In 2025") exists
  but has ZERO markets ever created under it in any status (open/settled/
  closed) -- this product never actually launched with real markets before
  2026, so there is no historical rollover instance to directly observe and
  verify the exact mechanics against (e.g. whether ALL 8 "before <date>"
  siblings in an event settle simultaneously on rollover, or something more
  granular).

  Practical impact today: "since season start" and "since this event's
  Issuance" currently coincide -- the Atlantic hurricane count-to-date is
  genuinely 0 so far this season (confirmed live via the existing
  hurricane_count_to_date.json cache), and this event's own open_time
  predates that. The gap is real but latent -- it activates the first time
  a hurricane forms this season AND Kalshi lists a rollover event, at which
  point occurred_this_season=True would misprice a genuinely-still-open
  post-rollover question as already resolved (prob=0.99), and the
  unconditional-mode fallback's season-wide climatology would still be
  answering "day of season's first hurricane" instead of "days since this
  new Issuance."

Why not now:
  - Correctly fixing occurred_this_season requires a genuinely new live
    signal: WHEN each settled KXHURRICANENAMES storm actually crossed
    hurricane strength (a date), not just a cumulative season count, so it
    can be compared against a specific event's open_time. Real new data/
    cache design work, closer in size to the original count-to-date cache
    itself than to a quick fix.
  - User's explicit decision (asked via AskUserQuestion after this research
    was presented): defer as its own follow-up entry rather than build the
    full signal now or ship a partial mechanical fix (e.g. swapping the
    conditional-mode "as_of" reference from today's date to the market's
    own open_time -- a cheaper, strictly-more-correct change that was also
    on the table and also NOT taken this pass).
  - Entirely shadow-only in the meantime (HURRICANE_NEXT_EVENT_TRADING_
    ENABLED defaults off) -- the mispricing this entry describes can only
    ever affect a logged shadow prediction's accuracy, never a real order.

When to revisit:
  - The moment either (a) hurricane_count_to_date.json's ATL count first
    goes from 0 to 1 this season, or (b) client.get_events(series_ticker=
    "KXNEXTHURDATE") first returns more than the one current event --
    whichever comes first. At that point, check live whether the existing
    open "before <date>" markets settled/closed (confirming the rollover
    actually happened) before assuming the gap has activated.
  - If ever prioritized: build the per-storm-became-hurricane-date signal
    (mirrors refresh_hurricane_count_to_date's shape, sourced from settled
    KXHURRICANENAMES markets' own settlement timestamps rather than just
    their yes/no result), then key occurred_this_season off "any qualifying
    storm since this event's own open_time" instead of season-wide count.

Resolution (2026-08-25 -- batch-59 item 3):
  PARTIALLY SHIPPED -- the mispricing is removed, but the positive signal this
  entry asked for still does not exist, and deliberately was not faked.

  What shipped:
  1. refresh_hurricane_count_to_date now also writes `last_yes_close_time`
     per basin (the latest close_time among "yes"-settled KXHURRICANENAMES
     markets, parsed to a real datetime and normalized to UTC before max()).
     Backward compatible: a cache without the key reads as None = unknown.
  2. New reader _get_cached_last_hurricane_event_time, delegating the
     staleness / season_year / corruption guards to the shared
     _get_cached_hurricane_names_entry like the count and storms-named
     readers do.
  3. _analyze_hurricane_next_event_trade no longer treats a season-wide
     count >= 1 as "already happened". count == 0 still means False ->
     conditional mode, unchanged. ANY count >= 1 now returns None -- no
     signal, no shadow row -- the same path already taken when HURDAT2 is
     unavailable.

  Why no-signal rather than the issuance comparison this entry proposed.
  This entry's own "if ever prioritized" note called for "WHEN each settled
  storm actually crossed hurricane strength (a date)". The available
  timestamp is a SETTLEMENT time, not a formation time, and an opus review
  proved the substitution does not hold. Both halves independently
  re-verified against live data before acting on the review:
    * Direction: settlement lags formation by days-to-weeks and runs in
      batches. Live-verified 2026-08-24/25 -- the three settled ATL name
      markets share close_time 2026-08-21T15:40:37Z (one batch run) while the
      whole open KXNEXTHURDATE ladder shares open_time 2026-08-06T14:00:00Z.
      Settlement landed FIFTEEN DAYS AFTER issuance. So
      `last_yes_close_time >= open_time` does NOT establish "formed after
      issuance" -- and that is the aggressive direction (0.99). The reverse
      inference IS sound: close_time < open_time proves the storm predates
      issuance. A sound negative, an unsound positive.
    * The climatology fallback was not a fail-safe. Measured directly against
      the repo's real HURDAT2 data: unconditional next_event_outcomes answers
      "did the season's FIRST hurricane occur on or before target", which for
      any late-season strike is ~always true -- 30/30 for targets Sep 15,
      Oct 1 and Dec 1, giving probability 0.99 with a ZERO-width bootstrap
      CI. That is the same 0.99 the confirmed branch emits, with a TIGHTER
      CI, so it produced a ~3% LARGER Kelly stake than the bug it replaced.
      Six of the seven open KXNEXTHURDATE markets are Sep 15 or later, so
      this was the live case, not an edge case. Pinned by a regression test
      against real HURDAT2 so nobody reinstates it believing it conservative.

  Consequence, stated plainly: the `occurred_this_season is True` branch
  (method "hurricane_next_event_confirmed", prob 0.99) is now UNREACHABLE.
  It is kept, with a comment saying so, as the landing spot for the day a
  real formation-date signal exists -- not left as silent dead code.

  Still open, and why this is PARTIALLY rather than fully resolved: building
  the per-storm formation-date signal. `last_yes_close_time` is groundwork
  toward it (it already supports the sound negative). That remaining work is
  filed as its own OPEN entry -- "BUILD A PER-STORM HURRICANE FORMATION-DATE
  SIGNAL SO THE NEXT-EVENT MODEL CAN CONFIRM A STORM FELL INSIDE A MARKET'S
  OWN WINDOW" -- specifically so it stays visible in BACKLOG_OPEN.md instead
  of disappearing behind this entry's RESOLVED bracket (backlog_index.py
  excludes on the bracket's literal first word, and "RESOLVED (partial)"
  matches). Live impact of the change today is ~zero: the traded next-event
  basin is ATL and its count is 0, so it takes the count == 0 -> conditional
  path either way; EPAC (2) and CPAC (1) are not traded by this family.

  Mutation-tested: revert to season-scoped True -> 5 tests fail; fall through
  to climatology instead of returning None -> 5 fail; `< 1` -> `< 2` on the
  count boundary -> 1 fails (count == 1 is a live CPAC value and was
  previously untested); market-side tzinfo normalization removed -> raises
  the exact TypeError predicted; writer-side normalization removed -> the
  cache file is not written AT ALL (the function-level except swallows the
  mixed-tz max() TypeError and skips atomic_write_json, losing the count
  refresh for every basin with only a DEBUG trace).

  Opus review findings addressed: HIGH 1 (the fix did not change the outcome
  -- redesigned, above), MEDIUM-HIGH 2 (residual inherited-storm window --
  removed by not taking the positive at all), M5 (count == 1 untested), LM7
  (market-side tz normalization untested), LM8 (writer lacked the reader's
  naive/aware guard). Informational 11: on first deploy, basins with count >=
  1 read as unanchorable until cron's next refresh writes the new field --
  now moot, since count >= 1 yields no signal regardless.

  Tests: 625 passed across the scoped suite; ruff + ruff-format + mypy clean
  via the real pre-commit hook.


[RESOLVED 2026-08-08] hurricane_climatology.fetch_hurdat2_raw's CACHE WRITE ISN'T ATOMIC -- THE ONLY RAW-TEXT CACHE IN THIS CODEBASE THAT SKIPS safe_io
Priority: Low -- currently low-probability (needs two processes racing to
  refresh the SAME stale HURDAT2 cache file within the same narrow window),
  but a real corruption path this project has already been burned by once
  for the identical bug CLASS on JSON caches (see "SAFE_IO -- EMERGENCY-COPY
  FALLBACK SILENTLY CLOBBERED THE ORIGINAL FILE" elsewhere in this file,
  RESOLVED 2026-07-27), and today's routine
  multi-parallel-worktree-session pattern (all worktrees share ONE physical
  data/ directory via paths.py -- see [[feedback_worktree_data_dir_gotcha]])
  makes concurrent collisions on this exact file meaningfully more likely
  than when it shipped as a single-session feature.

Problem:
  hurricane_climatology.py:144 (fetch_hurdat2_raw, shipped 2026-08-03 as
  part of the season-count hurricane model -- not introduced by the
  2026-08-07 time-to-next-event session, just never caught before) writes
  its disk cache with a plain `cache.write_text(text)`. Every OTHER
  cache-shaped write in this same area of the codebase goes through
  safe_io.atomic_write_json() instead -- confirmed live via
  `grep -n "cache.write_text\|atomic_write" hurricane_climatology.py
  acis_precip.py climatology.py`: acis_precip.py and climatology.py both
  consistently use safe_io.atomic_write_json for their own caches (climate
  archive data, forecast_sigma.json); hurricane_climatology.py's HURDAT2
  cache is the lone plain-write holdout. A concurrent write from a second
  process refreshing the same stale cache (two parallel worktree sessions
  both triggering hc.load_basin_storms() around the same time, or a live
  cron cycle overlapping with a manual research script) risks a reader
  seeing a partially-written file mid-write, or one write's content
  silently interleaving with another's -- the same corruption shape
  atomic_write_json's own emergency-copy-fallback bug (fixed 2026-07-27,
  see that entry) existed specifically to prevent for JSON caches.

  Not a drop-in fix: safe_io.atomic_write_json() is JSON-shaped (its own
  name says so); hurricane_climatology.py's cache is raw HURDAT2 text, not
  JSON. There is currently no safe_io helper for atomic raw-text writes --
  confirmed via `grep -n "^def " safe_io.py`: only atomic_write_json and
  atomic_write_json_with_history exist.

What it would look like:
  Add a generic safe_io.atomic_write_text() (or atomic_write_bytes(),
  whichever safe_io's existing tempfile+rename internals generalize to more
  cleanly) mirroring atomic_write_json's own write-to-tempfile-then-
  os.replace() shape, then swap hurricane_climatology.py's
  `cache.write_text(text)` for it. Small, mechanical once the helper exists
  -- the real work is designing the helper to share safe_io's existing
  emergency-copy-fallback/PID-keyed-tempfile conventions rather than being a
  parallel, independently-maintained implementation.

Why not now:
  User explicitly asked for this to be filed rather than fixed immediately
  (2026-08-07) -- currently low-probability (narrow race window: only
  matters when the 30-day cache is actually stale AND two processes refresh
  it in the same window) and shadow-only downstream (a corrupted HURDAT2
  cache would degrade a probability model's accuracy, not place a bad
  order), so not urgent enough to interrupt other in-flight work for.

When to revisit:
  - Before HURRICANE_TRADING_ENABLED or HURRICANE_NEXT_EVENT_TRADING_ENABLED
    is ever flipped on for real (a corrupted cache feeding a real-money
    Kelly size is a materially different risk than feeding a shadow log).
  - If parse_hurdat2 ever starts raising on malformed input (it currently
    doesn't -- see parse_hurdat2's own "stopping parse" comments) a
    corrupted mid-write cache read could produce a hard crash rather than a
    silently-degraded probability; worth re-checking this entry's own risk
    assessment if that changes.

RESOLVED 2026-08-08: Re-verified every claim in this entry live before
  touching code -- all held (hurricane_climatology.py:144's plain
  `cache.write_text(text)`; acis_precip.py/climatology.py both exclusively
  use safe_io.atomic_write_json; safe_io.py had exactly 2 WRITE-shaped
  public functions, atomic_write_json and atomic_write_json_with_history --
  both JSON-only, no raw-text/bytes variant existed). Correction (opus-
  review-caught 2026-08-08): the "2 public functions" phrasing above
  originally undercounted -- safe_io.py actually had 4 public functions
  total (project_root and check_emergency_copies are real, unrelated to
  writing); the substantive claim (no non-JSON atomic-write helper existed)
  was and is correct, the count of ALL public functions was not. Also
  confirmed atomic_write_json_with_history is itself already a thin wrapper
  around atomic_write_json (history-backup, then delegates) rather than a
  duplicate implementation -- the existing precedent for exactly the
  composition this entry's own "What it would look like" asked for.

  Shipped safe_io.atomic_write_text(text, path, retries=3,
  fallback_dir=None, emergency_copy=True) by extracting atomic_write_json's
  write-temp/fsync/rename/retry/emergency-copy core (previously all inline
  in atomic_write_json's own body) into a
  new private _atomic_write_payload(payload: str, ...) helper, then having
  BOTH atomic_write_json (serializes to JSON first) and the new
  atomic_write_text (uses the raw text as-is) call it -- not a parallel,
  independently-maintained implementation. atomic_write_json's external
  behavior is unchanged (all 31 pre-existing safe_io tests pass unmodified).
  Two of the shared helper's own log messages were still hardcoded to say
  "atomic_write_json" even though atomic_write_text now goes through the
  same path -- caught and fixed before it became a real caller-misleading-log
  issue in production, not just a review finding.

  Swapped hurricane_climatology.py's `cache.write_text(text)` for
  `safe_io.atomic_write_text(text, cache)`, matching the exact bare-call
  (no local try/except around just that line, an outer function-level
  try/except already provides the same fail-open safety net) convention
  already used by every safe_io.atomic_write_json call site in
  acis_precip.py/climatology.py.

  fetch_hurdat2_raw had ZERO existing test coverage of any kind before this
  session (confirmed via repo-wide grep). Added a new TestFetchHurdat2Raw
  CacheWrite class (2 tests: successful-fetch-writes-via-atomic_write_text,
  cache-write-failure-still-returns-fetched-text) plus new tests in
  test_safe_io.py: round-trip correctness, parent-dir auto-creation, shared
  retry/raise behavior with atomic_write_json (same total-failure scenario,
  same AtomicWriteError), and emergency-copy-on-failure. A 3rd
  hurricane_climatology test (racing writers never produce a torn cache
  file) was written but moved to test_safe_io.py during opus review round
  1 -- it never actually exercised hurricane_climatology.py's own code, see
  below.

  Mutation-tested the wiring specifically (not just the underlying
  primitive): temporarily reverted hurricane_climatology.py's call back to
  the original bare `cache.write_text(text)`, confirmed 2 of the 3 new
  hurricane_climatology tests correctly failed (the spy-based "atomic_write_
  text was actually called" assertion, and the write-failure-must-not-write-
  a-file assertion, which failed because the mocked failure path no longer
  applied to the reverted code), then restored the fix.

  Independent opus review (effort: high) of that state found the fix was
  sound but incomplete, 6 findings:

  - MEDIUM: the emergency-copy machinery is unconditional, and cron.py's
    check_emergency_copies() monitor pages an operator (notify.
    send_system_alert()) every cycle for ANY file in data/.emergency/,
    described as needing manual attention -- a disposable, trivially
    re-fetchable 4-7MB HURDAT2 cache tripping all 3 retries would falsely
    trigger that alert for data that isn't actually at risk. Fixed by
    adding an `emergency_copy: bool = True` opt-out to atomic_write_text
    (and the shared _atomic_write_payload core), with hurricane_climatology.
    py passing emergency_copy=False. AtomicWriteError still raises on
    total failure either way -- only the recovery-copy attempt is skipped.
  - MEDIUM: the "two racing writers never produce a torn file" test was
    structurally unable to fail. Its 5000-char payloads fit inside a
    single buffered write() syscall regardless of atomicity, and it only
    checked file content AFTER both writers had already joined, never
    sampling DURING the race window. Rewritten with multi-megabyte payloads
    (matching real HURDAT2 cache sizes) and a reader thread polling
    continuously while writers race -- moved to test_safe_io.py since the
    original never actually exercised hurricane_climatology.py's own code
    (it built its own cache_path and called safe_io.atomic_write_text
    directly, making its DATA_DIR monkeypatch dead code).
  - LOW: read/write encoding asymmetry -- atomic_write_text hard-codes
    utf-8, but hurricane_climatology.py's 2 cache.read_text() call sites
    were still locale-default (cp1252 on this box). Fixed both to pass
    encoding="utf-8" explicitly.
  - LOW: the renamed shared-helper log messages lost the calling public
    function's name AND broke a documented operator grep pattern
    (backlog.txt's own FORECAST_SIGMA.JSON ATOMIC WRITE CONTENTION entry
    documents `atomic_write_json attempt.*failed` as the exact recurrence-
    check grep). Fixed by threading a `caller_name` parameter through
    _atomic_write_payload so JSON callers keep the byte-identical original
    message and text callers get an accurate "atomic_write_text attempt..."
    instead.
  - LOW: _atomic_write_payload's own docstring wrongly said `path` was
    "assumed to already exist" and "resolved" -- neither true (it's the
    write target, not resolved until the emergency-candidate comparison
    later). Reworded.
  - LOW (2 narrative-accuracy issues): this note's own "safe_io.py had
    exactly 2 public functions" undercounted (4 exist total; only 2 are
    WRITE-shaped, which was the actual claim) -- corrected above. The new
    test class's docstring claimed hurricane_climatology was "the only
    raw-text cache in this codebase" skipping safe_io -- false:
    climate_indices.py's PDO/PNA cache (feeds apply_pdo_pna_correction(),
    called live from weather_markets.py's analyze_trade) and backtest.py's
    own cache both also write via plain write_text(). Re-scoped the
    docstring's wording; filed as a separate follow-up entry rather than
    fixed here (different module, genuinely out of this entry's own
    scope) -- see "climate_indices.py's PDO/PNA CACHE AND backtest.py's
    OWN CACHE ALSO SKIP safe_io" below.

  While re-verifying the rewritten concurrent-writers test's own
  discriminating power (per this project's mutation-testing discipline --
  temporarily swap in a deliberately non-atomic write, confirm the test
  actually catches it), self-caught TWO further issues before they ever
  reached review:

  - A first version of the harness (tight-loop reader, no sleep, isolating
    nothing) only caught a deliberately non-atomic write 1 of 3 local runs
    -- too unreliable to ship. A stronger version (multi-MB payloads, 8
    reader threads, no sleep) caught it reliably (10/10) -- but a bare run
    of this harness as a standalone script (not yet wired through pytest's
    tmp_path/monkeypatch) left a real 5MB test-payload file in THIS
    repo's actual data/.emergency/ directory (project_root() wasn't
    mocked). Found and deleted immediately; the shipped test always
    monkeypatches safe_io.project_root to tmp_path.
  - The same 8-reader-thread harness, run against the REAL (correct)
    atomic_write_text, surfaced a genuine, 100%-reproducible NEW bug, not
    an artifact of the test: on Windows, os.replace() can fail with
    PermissionError (WinError 5 "Access is denied") whenever another
    thread has the target file open for reading, even briefly -- a
    transient-contention failure unrelated to a real disk-full/permissions
    problem (POSIX rename() has no such restriction). Zero torn reads were
    ever observed (the atomicity guarantee itself held), but the WRITE
    could fail outright under concurrent-read pressure -- exhausting all 3
    retries and firing the emergency-copy path for no real reason. Given
    this project's own routine multi-parallel-worktree-session pattern on
    Windows sharing one physical data/ directory, this is a live risk, not
    a theoretical one. Raised via AskUserQuestion rather than silently
    filing it as yet another follow-up or silently fixing a shared
    primitive with 14 other callers -- user chose fix now. Added
    safe_io._replace_with_retry() (a short, bounded 0.5s retry loop on
    PermissionError specifically, same "retry briefly, don't treat
    transient contention as a hard failure" approach paper.py's own
    msvcrt.locking retry loop already uses for the identical Windows
    file-sharing-contention class), wired into both os.replace() call
    sites (primary write, emergency copy). Re-verified: 5/5 runs, 0 write
    errors, 0 torn reads against the fixed implementation; mutation-tested
    by reverting to bare os.replace(), confirmed the shipped concurrent-
    writers test correctly fails 3/3 runs, then restored.

  Independent opus review round 2 (effort: high) of that state found 9
  more findings (1 MEDIUM-HIGH, 2 MEDIUM, 6 LOW). Most significant:
  _replace_with_retry had ZERO platform-independent test coverage -- every
  mocked os.replace elsewhere in the file raised plain OSError, never
  PermissionError, and this repo's CI runs on ubuntu-latest where POSIX
  rename() never raises PermissionError for an open destination regardless
  of whether the retry logic exists at all. Reviewer proved the gap by
  mutation (swallowing a permanent PermissionError and returning silent
  "success" left 97/97 tests passing on Windows). Fixed with 3 new
  platform-independent unit tests exercising _replace_with_retry directly
  via a mocked os.replace: succeeds after N transient PermissionErrors,
  re-raises after exhausting deadline_secs (destination never created),
  and does NOT retry a non-PermissionError OSError (propagates
  immediately, unretried). Also fixed: worst-case latency compounding
  (documented in _replace_with_retry's own docstring; the emergency-copy
  call site now passes a shorter deadline_secs=0.1, since read contention
  on a data/.emergency/ or system-temp destination isn't the expected
  failure mode there -- caps total worst-case latency at ~3.7s instead of
  ~4.5s); a docstring that misattributed the WinError-5 discovery to the
  review process when it was actually self-caught during mutation-testing;
  4 more unprotected bare os.replace() sites elsewhere in the codebase
  (tracker.py x2, weather_markets.py, alerts.py) -- filed as a separate
  follow-up entry rather than fixed here, out of this entry's own scope
  (see "OTHER bare os.replace() CALL SITES OUTSIDE safe_io.py ALSO
  EXPOSED TO THE SAME WINDOWS SHARING-VIOLATION FAILURE MODE" below); the
  concurrent-writers test's own writer thread only caught
  AtomicWriteError, not any exception, which could have silently let one
  writer do nothing and the test still pass -- broadened to catch
  Exception generally; the new emergency-copy test (and, for consistency,
  its pre-existing JSON sibling) didn't isolate project_root() even though
  an explicit fallback_dir should make that path unreachable in practice --
  added the same belt-and-suspenders monkeypatch this session's own
  data/.emergency/ pollution incident argues for; several new/rewritten
  tests read without explicit encoding="utf-8", the exact asymmetry LOW #3
  above fixed in production code -- fixed in the tests too; and this
  note's own test counts were wrong (measured directly via `pytest
  --collect-only`: 61 hurricane_climatology tests, not 62; 39 safe_io
  tests, not 36).

  Final (re-measured, not estimated): 61 hurricane_climatology.py tests +
  39 safe_io.py tests pass (was 59/31 -- +2/+8 new). Broader sweep
  (test_acis_precip.py, test_climatology.py, test_alerts.py, the other
  real safe_io.atomic_write_json consumers) 106 passed, no regressions.
  ruff + ruff format + mypy clean on all 4 changed files.

[RESOLVED 2026-07-25] NEAR-SETTLEMENT LOG (near_settlement_log) SILENTLY BROKEN SINCE IT SHIPPED -- WRONG FIELD NAMES ON THE TRADE-RECORD DICT
Priority: was Medium -- a shipped calibration-data feature had been a
  complete no-op since it shipped (2026-06-14), with a "success" log line
  every time it ran and zero rows to show for it.

Problem:
  Found via the same "what's next" live-data check that surfaced this
  session's other candlestick-capture bug: `near_settlement_log` had exactly
  0 rows in the live DB. Checked every daily predictions.db backup from
  2026-06-29 through 2026-07-25 (11 backups) -- all 0. bot.log showed 3
  "near_settlement_log: logged 1 trade(s)" INFO lines (all from the very
  start of the retained log, ~2026-06-30), so the code path WAS running and
  believed it succeeded; the DB simply never got the rows.
  Root cause: cron.py's near-settlement block read
  `_tr.get("forecast_prob")` / `_tr.get("recommended_side")` on `_tr`, which
  is a stored paper-trade record (paper.place_paper_order/get_open_trades)
  -- but those two field names belong to the ANALYSIS dict shape
  (order_executor.py's `analysis.get("forecast_prob")` /
  `analysis.get("recommended_side")`), not the trade-record shape, which
  uses "entry_prob"/"side" instead (confirmed against all 198 real trades in
  paper_trades.json: 198/198 have "side" and "entry_prob", 0 have
  "recommended_side" or "forecast_prob" anywhere in the codebase on a trade
  record). This is the same "confused the analysis-dict boundary with the
  trade-record boundary" bug class backtest.py already hit and fixed on
  2026-07-05 (that fix's own comment documents the exact same field-name
  confusion) -- this cron.py call site was a second, still-broken instance
  nobody had re-checked.
  The `trade_side` column is `TEXT NOT NULL`; `_tr.get("recommended_side")`
  always returned None, so every INSERT violated that constraint --
  reproduced live in a standalone SQLite check. The statement was
  `INSERT OR IGNORE`, and SQLite's IGNORE conflict resolution silently drops
  NOT NULL violations (not just UNIQUE/PK ones) without raising -- so the
  code's own success log fired every cycle while writing nothing, for over a
  month, with zero test coverage on this feature to catch it.

What shipped:
  Fixed the two field names (`entry_prob`/`side`). Extracted the insert loop
  into a new `_log_near_settlement_trades(near, db_path) -> (attempted,
  written)` helper (matching the extraction precedent from this session's
  other fix) so it's directly unit-testable and so the caller can tell a
  real write apart from a silently-dropped one: `cmd_cron` now logs a
  WARNING (not the old blanket INFO) whenever written < attempted, closing
  the exact visibility gap that let this run silently for a month.
  Data is not backfillable -- this is a point-in-time snapshot (the
  migration's own comment already said so) -- so the ~40 days of missing
  snapshots are gone; this only fixes collection going forward.
  6 new tests: 5 unit tests on the extracted helper (correct write with real
  field names; a mutation-style regression reproducing the exact original
  silent-failure shape -- a trade dict using "recommended_side"/
  "forecast_prob" instead of "side"/"entry_prob" -- asserting written=0,
  attempted=1, not an exception; dedup via the existing unique index;
  multiple trades all written; days_out defaulting to 0 for pre-days_out
  trade records); 1 new end-to-end test through the real cmd_cron path
  (places a real open paper trade via paper.place_paper_order closing
  within the 0-2h window, runs cmd_cron, asserts the real row lands with
  correct ticker/our_model_prob/trade_side values). Full scoped regression
  (test_near_settlement_log.py + test_cron_integration.py) -- 26 passed.
  ruff + mypy clean. No opus review for this one -- small, single-cause,
  two-field-name fix plus a rowcount hardening, not a multi-subsystem change.
