[RESOLVED 2026-07-17] REAL NBM VIA IEM NBS STATION BULLETINS -- REPLACE THE SILENT best_match SUBSTITUTE
Priority: was Medium-High -- the bot believed it had an "nbm" ensemble
  member; it actually had an arbitrary auto-selected model.

Problem (as originally scoped):
  fetch_temperature_nbm() no longer fetched NBM at all -- Open-Meteo removed
  the model -- and requested models: "best_match" instead, an uncalibrated
  auto-selection, yet still fed model_temps["nbm"] in analyze_trade's
  Phase-C extended ensemble and _compute_ensemble_spread. mos.py already
  integrated IEM's MOS API but only ever requested GFS/NAM.

CORRECTION during implementation -- the original entry's field-name claim
  was wrong:
  This entry's own "Live-verified 2026-07-16" note claimed NBS rows carry
  "n_x (the NBM day-max/night-min field)". Re-verified live 2026-07-17
  against 7 stations across all 4 CONUS timezones: n_x is None on every
  single NBS row, for every station. The actual field carrying the daily
  extreme is "txn" (confirmed against IEM's raw CSV export, where it's an
  unlabeled trailing column matching the classic NWS raw-MOS-bulletin "X/N"
  convention), and it is populated only on rows whose forecast-valid time
  lands exactly on a 00Z or 12Z boundary -- not a dedicated always-present
  field the way n_x was assumed to be. This also meant the "Why not now"
  risk below (per-station 12-hourly semantics, same timezone care as CLI
  settlement) was real and had to be solved, not just verified-and-shipped:
  which of the 00Z/12Z rows is the local daytime max vs. nighttime min
  depends on each station's UTC offset in general, but empirically (checked
  KNYC/Eastern, KMDW/Central, KDEN/Mountain, KLAX/Pacific) the 00Z-ending
  12h period is ALWAYS the higher (max) value and 12Z-ending ALWAYS the
  lower (min), station-timezone-independent -- because CONUS UTC offsets
  are always whole hours, so each station's ~12h local daytime window
  always falls entirely inside one UTC-anchored period or the other, never
  split. This is a genuine, verified, general rule for all 20 traded
  cities, not a KNYC-specific coincidence.

What shipped:
  mos.py: new _fetch_nbs_daily_extremes(station, city_tz) parses every
  available txn row into {(local_date, "max"|"min"): temp_f} using the
  00Z=max/12Z=min rule above (local_date computed by converting ftime to
  the station's timezone and taking .date(), which safely lands inside the
  12h period without crossing local midnight for any CONUS zone). Cached
  per (station, city_tz), 1h TTL, matching _MOS_CACHE_TTL. New public
  fetch_nbm_iem(station, target_date, city_tz, var) wraps it. Also removed
  two now-redundant local `from datetime import UTC, datetime` imports
  mos.py had (dead weight once UTC/datetime moved to the top-level import
  this entry's datetime.strptime parsing needed anyway).

  weather_markets.fetch_temperature_nbm() now tries fetch_nbm_iem() first
  (via _metar_station_for_city(city), which covers all 20 traded cities --
  NOT mos.py's 6-city _MOS_CITIES subset used by GFS/NAM MOS, per this
  entry's original "extend beyond" note), and only falls back to the old
  Open-Meteo best_match substitute when NBS has no coverage for that
  station/date (expected for same-day markets -- NBS's own forecast
  horizon is short and same-day rows are frequently absent in the current
  cycle; the METAR pipeline already covers same-day elsewhere in this
  codebase). No changes needed to analyze_trade's Phase-C ensemble or
  _compute_ensemble_spread -- both already consume fetch_temperature_nbm()'s
  return value, so the real-vs-substitute swap is fully transparent to them
  ("wire it in now" was the explicit choice made here, not log-only-first,
  since this replaces an already-live-blended signal's data source rather
  than introducing a brand-new one).

  Tests: tests/test_mos_nbs.py -- the 00Z=max/12Z=min rule verified against
  both an Eastern and a Pacific station (proving it's genuinely
  timezone-derived, not hardcoded), a mutation-proof swapped-assignment
  check, off-cycle/missing-txn row handling, cache-hit/network-failure
  behavior. tests/test_nbm.py updated (the IEM path is tried first, so its
  two pre-existing Open-Meteo-mock tests needed mos.fetch_nbm_iem patched
  to return None to keep exercising the fallback path they were written
  for) plus two new tests for the IEM-first preference and the
  no-station-mapped skip path. Mutation-tested the max/min assignment by
  hand-flipping it and confirming 6 of the new tests fail with the exact
  expected wrong values, then reverting.

  Drive-by fix: tests/test_forecasting.py's
  test_log_prediction_called_with_forecast_cycle (an AST-based check that
  main.py's log_prediction call passes forecast_cycle=) was stale --
  broken by the 2026-07-17 LOG_PREDICTION KWARGS ASSEMBLY TRIPLICATED
  consolidation (main.py now passes it via
  **_prediction_kwargs_from_analysis(...), not a literal keyword) but not
  caught at the time because that session's test run didn't include this
  file. Updated the AST check to accept either form; mutation-tested by
  stripping the unpack from main.py and confirming the test fails, then
  reverting via git checkout.

  Independently reviewed (Agent, opus) before commit, matching this
  project's standard for anything touching a live probability-blend input.
  Confirmed the core claims sound (00Z=max/12Z=min holds for every CONUS
  offset including Phoenix's no-DST America/Phoenix, no off-by-one-day in
  the local-date attribution, tests genuinely correct not just plausible)
  and caught one real bug fixed before commit: fetch_temperature_nbm's
  Open-Meteo fallback opportunistically dual-writes both max and min
  _NBM_CACHE entries from one HTTP response (an existing optimization,
  pre-dating this entry) -- but NBS has per-var coverage gaps at its ~3-day
  horizon edge (a date can have a real IEM max with no IEM min yet, or vice
  versa), so the unconditional dual-write could silently clobber a real,
  already-cached IEM value with the Open-Meteo best_match placeholder,
  order-dependently, with no error raised -- reintroducing the exact bug
  this entry exists to fix. Fixed: the fallback now only opportunistically
  writes the OTHER var's cache slot when it isn't already fresh. Added
  tests/test_nbm.py::test_openmeteo_fallback_does_not_clobber_iem_value_for_other_var,
  mutation-tested by restoring the old unconditional-dual-write and
  confirming it fails (60.0 instead of the real 81.0), then reverting.
  Also hardened mos.py's ftime parsing per the review's second finding: if
  IEM ever changes the timestamp format, every txn row would silently fail
  to parse and the feature would permanently no-op to the Open-Meteo
  fallback with no signal -- now logs a warning when every txn-bearing row
  fails to parse, rather than looking identical to genuine no-coverage.

Known residual (not fixed here, correctly out of scope):
  - Pairs naturally with the NBM PROBABILISTIC QUANTILES entry below (same
    IEM/NBM surface, still open) -- scope together if picked up next.
  - fetch_mos()'s existing GFS/NAM path filters rows by

  - A pre-existing, unrelated flaky test was discovered and fixed in a
    separate commit: tests/test_data_freshness.py::
    test_enrich_with_forecast_stamps_data_fetched_at was failing when run
    in the same session after tests/test_forecasting.py (two tests in

    _forecast_cache/_ensemble_cache singletons without cleanup, leaking a

[RESOLVED 2026-07-17] DISCRETIZATION-CONSISTENT T-BUCKET THRESHOLDS -- HALF-DEGREE CONTINUITY
Priority: was Medium-High -- systematic, direction-consistent probability
  skew on every tail-bucket trade; bordered a correctness issue, not just a
  feature idea.

Problem (as originally scoped):
  _parse_market_condition already reasons explicitly about integer
  settlement for between-buckets -- B87.5 -> [86.5, 88.5], with a comment
  that brackets "must tile without gaps" (weather_markets.py:3719-3723).
  But T-buckets kept raw integer thresholds: T92 -> {"above", 92.0}, and
  every prob path taking condition raw (_forecast_probability,
  ensemble_cdf_prob, EMOS, nws_prob, ...) used that raw value directly,
  so the ladder didn't tile under the code's own between-bucket
  convention -- dropping probability mass near every tail-bucket boundary.

CORRECTION during implementation -- the original "What it would look
  like" below had the sign backwards:
  This entry's own original proposal ("above: val-0.5; below: val+0.5")
  was never live-verified and turned out to be wrong. Before writing any
  code, fetched real rules_primary text from 8 live Kalshi T-bucket
  markets across 4 cities (KXHIGHNY/CHI/DEN/MIA) via the API. Every
  sample showed the same pattern: a "T{val} above" ticker's actual rule
  is "greater than {val}" -- e.g. T86 "above" has subtitle "87° or above"
  and rules_primary "is greater than 86" -- meaning integer settlement
  must be val+1 or higher, not val or higher as this entry originally
  assumed. Matching the between-bucket code's own already-committed
  tiling convention (a "85-86" between-bucket is B85.5 -> [84.5, 86.5]),
  the correct continuous boundary is val+0.5 for above and val-0.5 for
  below -- the OPPOSITE sign from the original proposal. Shipping the
  original proposal as written would have shifted every T-bucket
  threshold a full 1.0°F in the wrong direction (turning a 0.5°F bug into
  a 1.0°F bug on the other side), not fixed it. Full ladder check around
  a boundary: T67-below (wins <=66) -> 66.5; B67.5 -> {67,68}; T68-above
  (wins >=69) -> 68.5. Integer 68 lands in exactly B67.5 and not in
  T68-above (68 > 68.5 is false) -- tiles with no gap or overlap.

What shipped:
  _parse_market_condition (weather_markets.py) now returns a second,
  sibling key on above/below condition dicts: "prob_threshold" (val+0.5 /
  val-0.5), alongside the existing "threshold" (raw ticker/rule value,
  UNCHANGED). Deliberately did not mutate "threshold" in place -- several
  consumers must keep comparing against the literal raw rule value
  (tracker.audit_settlement's archive cross-check against Kalshi's actual
  rule text, weather_markets._metar_lock_in's same-day METAR lockout
  check, and condition_threshold= DB/logging bookkeeping in
  main.py/order_executor.py) and mutating threshold would have silently
  corrupted all three. A single shared helper, utils.prob_threshold(condition)
  (falls back to raw "threshold" for between/precip conditions, which
  don't have "prob_threshold"), is now the one place every genuine
  continuous-probability consumer reads from, instead of each site
  reimplementing its own shift/fallback -- avoiding the
  triplicated-logic-one-drifts pattern already hit elsewhere in this file
  (LOG_PREDICTION KWARGS, KALSHI CENTS/DOLLARS NORMALIZATION). Updated
  every genuine probability-math call site: ensemble_cdf_prob,
  _forecast_probability, _bootstrap_ci, _get_consensus_probs (model-
  consensus safety gate), analyze_trade's EMOS exceedance/interval calls,
  raw ensemble-fraction fallback, gaussian_probability call, extended-
  ensemble (NBM/ECMWF) raw fraction, near-threshold detection, the
  climate-index adj_condition shift (now shifts both threshold and
  prob_threshold by index_adj so they stay consistent), and the
  persistence-baseline _tlo lookup -- plus nws.py's nws_prob and
  obs_prob, climatology.py's _climatological_prob_inner, and backtest.py
  (so backtest results keep matching live behavior). Confirmed
  audit_settlement, _metar_lock_in, settlement_monitor.py, and the DB/
  logging call sites were left untouched and still read raw "threshold".
  Tests (tests/test_weather.py): parse-time above/below prob_threshold
  values, a tiling-identity test (between-bucket upper == adjacent
  T-bucket's prob_threshold, live-ticker-verified), utils.prob_threshold's
  fallback behavior, and mutation-proof tests for _forecast_probability
  and ensemble_cdf_prob (forecast/members placed exactly in the old
  gap -- verified these fail if the fix is reverted, by actually
  reverting one line, running the suite, confirming the expected failure,
  then restoring it).

  Independently reviewed (Agent, opus) before commit: re-derived the
  sign/magnitude from the tiling argument independently (confirmed
  correct), audited every touched call site (confirmed each is a genuine
  probability computation, not a should-stay-raw site), searched for
  missed consumers, and checked the None-handling `or 0` idiom used at
  two sites for a silent-remap-of-a-real-0.0-threshold bug (confirmed
  safe -- T-ticker thresholds are always half-integers, never exactly
  0.0, and both sites are already type-guarded so the fallback can't
  fire on a real market anyway). No bugs found.

Known residual (not fixed here, correctly out of scope):
  - sigma_audit.py's _forecast_prob() replicates the Gaussian CDF from DB
    columns threshold_lo/threshold_hi, which tracker.py populates from
    the raw (unshifted) threshold by design -- so this diagnostic-only
    script still carries the same tail skew. Revisit if/when sigma_audit
    output is used for more than diagnostics.
  - nws.py's nws_prob_from_quantiles() is dead code (only referenced by
    tests/docs/backlog, not wired into analyze_trade or any live path,
    confirmed via the existing NBM PROBABILISTIC QUANTILES entry above).
    If it's ever wired in, its caller must pass prob_threshold, not raw
    threshold.
  - Calibration-reset interplay (per-city Platt/temperature scaling may
    have been partially absorbing the average skew this fixes) not
    separately audited post-ship -- watch get_calibration_by_city /
    condition-type Brier over the next batch of settled trades per this
    entry's original note.

[RESOLVED 2026-07-19] AMEND ORDER (V2) -- REPLACE CANCEL-VERIFY-REPLACE IN THE REPRICE LOOP
Priority: was Medium -- removes the exact client-side race window the
  reprice feature needed hardened plumbing to work around, and halves
  write-call count per reprice.

RESOLVED 2026-07-19:
  Re-verified the endpoint shape against Kalshi's live docs before coding
  (https://docs.kalshi.com/api-reference/orders/amend-order-v2) rather than
  trusting this entry's 2026-07-16 summary alone -- confirmed POST
  /portfolio/events/orders/{order_id}/amend, request {ticker, side, price,
  count, client_order_id?, updated_client_order_id?, exchange_index?},
  response {order_id, client_order_id, remaining_count?, fill_count?,
  average_fill_price?, average_fee_paid?, ts_ms}. One clarification the
  original entry didn't capture: count is NOT "how many more to add" --
  it's the order's TOTAL desired fillable count (already-filled +
  desired-remaining-resting), the same semantics as create-order's count.
  For this bot's only use (reprice at an unchanged quantity), that means
  passing the same count used at original placement, unchanged -- Kalshi
  computes the filled/still-resting split internally.
  Shipped kalshi_client.amend_order() (V2 fixed-point body via the existing
  _to_v2_side_price mapping, deterministic updated_client_order_id via the
  same hash-based idempotency pattern as place_order, client_order_id
  included only when the caller has it) and order_executor._amend_live_order
  (mirrors _replace_live_order's gate-recheck + execution_log bookkeeping
  shape). Wired into _reprice_or_cancel_pending_orders's reprice-improve
  branch only (same order, new price) -- the taker-cross branch stays on
  cancel+replace exactly as before, since it changes time_in_force to
  immediate_or_cancel, a different order type amend cannot express, matching
  this entry's own original scoping.
  Execution_log design decision (surfaced via AskUserQuestion -- amend keeps
  the SAME exchange order_id, unlike cancel+replace's genuinely-new one, so
  this needed a real call): user chose the "new row, chained via
  replaces_order_id" option over "update the row in place", matching this
  entry's own "Log replaces_order_id chains the same way" plan. The old
  row gets a new status="amended" (deliberately distinct from "canceled" --
  the original order was never actually canceled, just repriced).
  Found and fixed a real live-money correctness gap this design choice
  would otherwise have introduced, caught by tracing every consumer of
  orders.status before finalizing the new status string (per
  [[feedback_trace_all_call_sites]]): execution_log.get_today_live_spend()
  (the MAX_DAILY_SPEND gate's data source) sums quantity*price across every
  row NOT IN ('failed','canceled','cancelled') -- 'amended' wasn't in that
  exclusion list, so an amended order's old row AND its new row would both
  count, double-counting the same resting position's capital on every
  reprice and inflating the live spend cap toward premature (fail-safe-
  direction, not fail-unsafe, but still a real bug) halts. Fixed by adding
  'amended' to that query's exclusion list. Checked every other
  orders.status consumer in execution_log.py (was_recently_ordered,
  was_traded_today, was_ordered_this_cycle: harmless either way, since the
  new row already signals "traded" regardless of the old row's status;
  get_open_live_positions's exact status='pending' match and
  order_executor._count_open_live_orders's exact status='pending' match:
  both naturally exclude 'amended' already, no change needed) -- only
  get_today_live_spend needed the fix.
  Adjacency note, NOT fixed (flagging per this project's convention rather
  than silently folding it in): execution_log.log_order_result() always
  overwrites response/error/error_code/error_type (not COALESCEd) even when
  the caller only means to update status -- _amend_live_order's mark-old-
  row-as-"amended" call inherits this same pre-existing behavior already
  present in _finalize_cancel's cancel-marking call (nulls out the old
  row's response JSON on every cancel too, not something this change
  introduced). Worth a real fix if execution_log.py is next open for
  other reasons.
  Not verified against DEMO_BASE (no live/demo order was actually placed) --
  ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE=False and TRADING_PAUSED throughout this session, same
  as every other live-order-path change to date; implemented and tested
  against the documented shape (live docs fetch above), matching how the
  original V2 create/cancel migration was done. Worth a real demo-order
  smoke test whenever live trading is actually being prepared to resume.
  20 new tests: kalshi_client.amend_order() body construction (V2 side/price
  mapping reused correctly, client_order_id included/omitted correctly,
  updated_client_order_id deterministic+idempotent, raw response passthrough
  -- tests/test_kalshi_client.py::TestAmendOrder, 7 tests);
  order_executor._resolve_amend_status's fill/no-fill/partial-fill/
  unparseable boundary cases (4 tests, mutation-tested by flipping the
  remaining_count<=0 comparison and confirming the boundary test fails for
  the right reason, then restoring); get_today_live_spend's 'amended'
  exclusion (2 tests, one directly proving the double-count bug by running
  the pre-fix query alongside the real one and asserting they diverge);
  updated 2 existing reprice-branch tests
  (test_rested_past_blanket_gate_but_not_taker_gate_reprices_not_crosses,
  test_price_moved_reprices_as_new_maker_order) from asserting cancel_order/
  place_order calls to asserting amend_order calls, since those tests were
  exercising an implementation detail (the mechanism) that genuinely
  changed by design, not just an outcome; replaced
  test_fill_race_during_cancel_skips_replacement (which tested the
  cancel+verify fill-race protection this change makes moot for the
  reprice-improve branch -- amend's atomicity closes that race window by
  construction) with test_amend_that_crosses_the_book_is_logged_as_filled,
  proving the analogous scenario (amend's own price change immediately

  of a separate verification call; added 2 new execution_log bookkeeping
  tests for the amend success/failure paths (old row -> "amended" only on

  602 tests pass across the full scoped regression sweep (every test file
  touching order_executor.py/kalshi_client.py/execution_log.py); ruff +
  ruff format + mypy clean.
  Independent second-opinion review (Agent, opus) caught one real issue
  before push: _amend_live_order's try/except wrapped BOTH the exchange
  amend_order() call AND the two subsequent execution_log bookkeeping
  writes in one block -- if the exchange call succeeded but a bookkeeping
  write then raised (e.g. a genuine SQLite "database is locked", plausible
  given web_app.py's dashboard and the WS thread can touch the same DB
  concurrently), the new row got marked "failed" even though the order had
  genuinely repriced live on the exchange, orphaning it (never picked up
  again by _poll_pending_orders' status='pending' filter). Fixed by
  splitting into two try/except blocks: only the amend_order() call itself
  can produce a "failed" classification and a False return; once a
  response is in hand, a bookkeeping failure is logged loudly (error, not
  warning) but the function still returns True, since the exchange-side
  reality is what matters for whether a future cycle should retry.
  New regression test (test_amend_exchange_success_survives_bookkeeping_
  failure) mocks execution_log.log_order_result to raise after a
  successful amend_order() call and asserts True is still returned --
  mutation-tested by reverting to the single-try-block shape and
  confirming the test fails with the exact predicted symptom (an
  unhandled RuntimeError instead of a clean True), then restoring. 126
  tests pass in the two most directly affected files after the fix; ruff/
  ruff format/mypy clean.

POST-RESOLUTION REGRESSION, FIXED 2026-07-19 (see the "is_liquid() (AND 4
  MORE SITES)..." entry for the full narrative): fit_market_implied_
  distribution()'s weighting line read plain market.get("volume") only,
  never the current API's volume_fp -- so on real live data every sibling
  bracket's weight computed as 0, and the fit almost certainly returned
  None on every real scan since it shipped below. The "verified...
  essentially exact" claim in the original resolution was true of the fit
  math (checked against synthetic fixtures using plain "volume"), but
  those fixtures never matched real API field-name shape, so the bug was
  invisible to the test suite that shipped with this feature. Fixed with
  the same `volume_fp or volume or 0` coalescing used everywhere else in
  this codebase, plus a new regression test built from live-API-shaped
  fixtures (volume_fp only, no "volume" key) confirming a real fit comes
  back. Lesson for future signals in this codebase: a synthetic-fixture
  test proving the MATH is correct is not the same as proving the
  function works against real API data shape -- verify field names
  against a real live payload (or at least against analyze_trade()'s own
  known-correct coalescing pattern) before calling a new market-data
  consumer "verified."

RESOLVED 2026-07-18: shipped as scoped in "What it would look like" below,
  with two design decisions surfaced to and confirmed by the user via
  AskUserQuestion first (call-site scope; liquidity-weight field), plus one
  reversal caught by re-deriving rather than restating a first-pass
  recommendation (the delta column -- see below).
  weather_markets.fit_market_implied_distribution(siblings) fits a Normal
  (mean, sigma) by weighted least squares: each liquid bracket's mid-price
  is the implied probability mass over its threshold (above/below/between),
  weighted by volume (chosen over open_interest because is_liquid() -- the
  same function gating the thin-book floor -- only ever checks volume,
  keeping one definition of liquidity instead of introducing a second).
  Reuses _forecast_probability's exact above/below/between mass formula
  conceptually, but reimplements it as a vectorized numpy expression rather
  than calling it per-point per-optimizer-iteration: profiling showed scipy.
  stats.norm.cdf's per-call overhead dominates (~200ms/fit via the
  non-vectorized version vs ~29ms vectorized, for a 6-bracket event) --
  documented inline so a future reader doesn't "simplify" it back to the
  slow, more-obviously-DRY version. weather_markets.
  compute_market_implied_distributions(markets) groups a scan's full market
  list by (city, date) via parse_city_date and fits each event once.
  Verified against a synthetic ladder built from a known Normal(70,5) (and
  separately an all-"between" ladder, since real weather markets are
  commonly all-between with no above/below siblings at all): fit recovered
  (70.0009, 5.0013) -- essentially exact.
  Wired into predictions via 3 new columns (implied_mean, implied_sigma,
  fit_residual -- migration v43/v44/v45, tracker.log_prediction()) and
  order_executor._prediction_kwargs_from_analysis (reads a.get(

CORRELATION CHECK RUN 2026-07-30 (per this entry's own ENABLEMENT TRIGGER --
  a one-off analysis against live data, not a wiring decision; picked up as
  the higher-value of the 2 signals a same-day backlog audit found had just
  cleared their 20-sample floor, over LIQUIDITY-AWARE SIZING's gated_edge
  check, because this one's needed columns -- implied_mean, forecast_temp_f,
  settled_temp_f -- are all logged directly, while gated_edge's check needs
  an unlogged `adjusted_edge` re-derived from other fields):
  n=22 settled predictions with non-NULL implied_mean/forecast_temp_f.
  Tested market_delta = implied_mean - forecast_temp_f against forecast_error
  = settled_temp_f - forecast_temp_f (does the market's tilt away from our
  forecast predict which direction the actual outcome misses our forecast
  by, the same directional-persistence hypothesis this entry's own text and
  run_trend's ENABLEMENT TRIGGER use). Result: Pearson r=0.405, sign
  agreement 14/22 (64%, vs 50% chance), two-sided p=0.061 (90% CI for r:
  [0.05, 0.67]) -- borderline, not conventionally significant at n=22, but
  directionally consistent with the market carrying real information rather
  than pure noise.
  One real wrinkle surfaced and checked before trusting the headline number:
  implied_sigma ranges from 1.06 to 47.30 across these 22 rows -- some fits
  are tight (a plausible real forecast sigma), others are numerically
  degenerate (a 47°F sigma is meaningless for a daily temp forecast, almost
  certainly an under-constrained thin-ladder fit). Re-ran the correlation
  filtered to sigma<=5 and sigma<=10 to confirm the degenerate-sigma rows
  weren't driving the result -- r stayed 0.37-0.41 across all three cuts, so
  the finding isn't an artifact of the noisiest fits.
  Real caveat for any FUTURE wiring decision (not relevant to whether the
  signal is real, only to how it could ever be used): market_delta's
  magnitude is ~3x forecast_error's (mean |market_delta|~=7.7°F vs mean
  |forecast_error|~=2.7-3.4°F depending on the sigma cut) -- even rows where
  the market points the right direction overshoot badly, so this could never
  be wired in as a raw additive correction; it would need heavy shrinkage.
  Conclusion: NOT wired into the blend (correctly stays log-only) --
  directionally promising but n=22/p=0.061 isn't conclusive. Re-run this
  same check once more settled rows accumulate; unlike run_trend/richer-ML
  (which are still far from their own floors), this signal is right at the
  edge of a real answer, so it's worth checking again soon rather than
  waiting for another full backlog audit to resurface it.

RESOLVED 2026-08-03 (one of the two deferred analysis passes -- "did
  informed flow precede settlement-direction moves"; the other, adverse
  selection around our own fill times, is still open, see below): picked
  up as part of the same session that redirected PUBLIC TRADE-FLOW SIGNAL
  here (see that entry's 2026-08-03 note above) -- both its own
  WS-continuity trigger and SIGNAL GRADUATION's registry-building scope had
  already been overtaken by events, so the user chose this fully-unblocked
  analysis pass instead, via explicit AskUserQuestion rather than either
  path being assumed.
  Checked live before designing anything: execution_log.orders (198 rows)
  has ZERO rows with filled_at or market_mid_at_fill populated -- no live
  order has ever actually filled (matches ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE being off) --
  so the "adverse selection around our own fills" half is structurally
  unanswerable right now, not just thin. Dropped from this pass per
  explicit AskUserQuestion confirmation rather than built against a 0-row
  table.
  Confirmed trade_history and price_history now have real accumulated data
  (70,362 trade rows / 43 tickers; 13,820 candle rows / 274 tickers; full
  43/43 ticker overlap between the two tables) -- comfortably past a cold
  start.
  Shipped tracker.get_trade_flow_settlement_correlation(
  min_trades_per_market=10, min_candles_per_market=4, min_markets=15,
  min_early_trades=3) -- for each ticker with both trade_history and
  price_history rows, splits the trade series at its own time midpoint
  (half the trades before, half after, using each trade's parsed
  created_time epoch) and computes early signed flow ((yes-taker volume -
  no-taker volume) / total volume in the early half, in [-1, 1], requiring
  at least min_early_trades contributing trades so a single trade at a
  timestamp tie can't swing it to +-1.0) against late price drift (the last
  candle with a real, non-NULL price_close minus the earliest candle at/
  after that same midpoint that also has a real close -- both walks skip
  past NULL closes rather than trusting the first/last candle blindly, and
  candles are filtered to the earliest candle's own period_interval first
  so two OHLC resolutions can never silently interleave), then
  Pearson-correlates across markets using the same manual formula as
  get_recent_city_correlations (matching that function's convention, not
  because scipy is otherwise unavailable in this project -- it is, see
  weather_markets.py's scipy.stats/scipy.optimize imports). Markets below
  the trade/candle/early-trade floors are counted under
  markets_skipped_thin; markets that clear those floors but have no usable
  price at either end of the drift window are counted separately under
  markets_skipped_no_price, so a "thin" report never conflates two
  unrelated failure reasons.
  Real finding, run live against the actual DB: n=42 markets cleared the
  floor (43 considered, 1 skipped thin, 0 skipped for missing price),
  r=-0.035 -- indistinguishable from zero at this sample size. Early signed
  taker flow does NOT show a detectable relationship with each market's
  subsequent price drift in the current dataset. This is informational, not
  dispositive (n=42, single fixed early/late split point per market, no
  significance test attached) -- but it does NOT support building the live
  WS mechanism PUBLIC TRADE-FLOW SIGNAL describes on urgency grounds.
  get_trade_flow_settlement_correlation is a real, callable, tested query,
  not a one-off script -- re-run it as trade_history keeps accumulating
  rather than re-deriving the analysis from scratch next time.
  14 new tests (tests/test_tracker.py TestTradeFlowSettlementCorrelation):
  no-data, perfect 3-market correlation (3 collinear points -> r==1.0
  exactly, verifying the Pearson formula), a zero-variance guardrail
  (identical flows across markets -> r stays None, not a divide-by-zero),
  below-min-markets (n reported, r=None), thin-market skips (too few
  trades / too few candles / zero early volume / below the early-trade-
  count floor), the trade_history-without-price_history join-exclusion
  case, a mixed-period_interval-candles filter case, and 3 tests directly
  targeting the NULL-price-handling fix below.
  Independent Agent(opus, effort=high) review (before push, per standing
  workflow) reproduced the live result independently (byte-identical
  reimplementation) and found 1 HIGH, 4 MEDIUM, and several LOW/informational
  issues in the first draft -- all fixed, not just the HIGH one:
  (1) HIGH -- the new function had no dead-code-scanner allowlist entry
  (tests/test_dead_code_scan.py), which would have failed CI on push exactly
  like the count_fn miss noted in an earlier session's `9eec753` fix --
  added, matching get_price_history/get_trade_history's existing entries.
  (2) HIGH-severity-in-practice correctness bug -- the first draft used
  candles[-1]["price_close"] directly for the "last" price. 24% of all
  price_history rows have a NULL price_close (a period with no trades), and
  13 of the 43 real join tickers -- among the highest-volume markets in the
  set -- had a NULL close on their literal final candle, so they were
  silently mis-counted as "thin" and dropped (n was 29, not 42, before this
  fix; r was -0.042, not -0.035). Fixed by walking backward from the end
  until a real close is found, recovering all 13 markets.
  (3) MEDIUM -- the matching fix on the other end: the first draft took the
  first candle at/after the trade-series midpoint regardless of whether
  that specific candle had a real price, silently substituting an unrelated
  index-based fallback price when it didn't. Fixed to walk forward past any
  NULL-close candles at that boundary too.
  (4) MEDIUM -- the first draft's fallback (when no candle at/after the
  midpoint existed at all) computed drift entirely from candles before the
  midpoint, which could invert the lead-lag relationship the function
  exists to test (measuring a window that precedes the "early flow" window
  rather than following it). Removed the fallback entirely -- such a market
  is now skipped and counted under the new markets_skipped_no_price
  counter instead of silently contributing a wrong-direction data point.
  (5) MEDIUM -- docstring and a single skip counter undercounted/mislabeled
  the actual skip reasons once (2)-(4) existed -- split into
  markets_skipped_thin and markets_skipped_no_price and rewrote the
  docstring to describe all three real skip paths.
  (6) LOW -- the created_time parse only caught ValueError; broadened to
  also catch AttributeError/TypeError so a future non-string created_time
  (e.g. if Kalshi ever changed format) fails soft instead of crashing the
  whole report.
  (7) LOW -- added an explicit min_early_trades=3 floor (a market could
  previously reach the volume-only floor via a single early trade at a
  timestamp tie); LOW -- added a period_interval filter so two OHLC
  resolutions for one ticker could never silently interleave (not observed
  live as of this writing, but not structurally prevented either); LOW --
  gave the function an explicit `-> dict[str, int | float | None]` return
  type instead of a bare `dict`; LOW -- reworded a docstring line that
  implied scipy was unavailable in this project (it isn't -- the manual
  Pearson formula matches get_recent_city_correlations' own convention,
  nothing else) and another that overstated "settlement" when the measured
  endpoint is the last logged candle, not necessarily literal settlement.
  Two of the new tests initially had real gaps caught only by re-verifying
  the review's own mutation-testing claims by hand, not just trusting the
  review's summary: the first version of a NULL-close-boundary mutation
  test silently passed because its candle timestamps were small toy
  integers nowhere near the trade series' real 2026 epoch values, so the
  time-aligned code path never actually executed; and the first version of
  the period_interval-filter test used only 2 markets, which is
  mathematically always exactly r=+-1 regardless of the underlying values
  (any 2 distinct points are collinear), so it could not have caught the
  filter being removed entirely -- both rebuilt (real epoch-aligned
  timestamps; a 3-market design where a wrong value measurably moves r off
  1.0) and re-confirmed against the actual mutation.
  350 tests pass across tests/test_tracker.py (was 344); ruff + ruff format
  + mypy clean on tracker.py, tests/test_tracker.py, and
  tests/test_dead_code_scan.py (one pre-existing, unrelated ruff-format nit
  elsewhere in test_tracker.py left untouched -- confirmed via diff scope,
  not introduced by this change).
  Zero live-trading-behavior change: read-only query function, no existing
  code calls it (by design -- see the dead-code-scanner allowlist entry),

  Still open: the "adverse selection around our own fills" half (execution_

  CROSS-CITY RECENT-ERROR POOLING -- SYNOPTIC-REGIME BIAS SHARE
Priority: Low-Medium -- the spatial correlation structure is already
  learned and stored; it's only ever used to *penalize risk*, never to
  *improve the forecast*.

Problem (as originally scoped):
  Bias correction is strictly per-city and slow: _get_combined_station_bias
  (weather_markets.py:303-337) blends a static table with
  tracker.get_dynamic_station_bias (min 10 samples, weeks of
  accumulation, 4h cache). Nothing used the last 24-48h of realized
  errors in *other* cities to nudge today's forecast -- even though
  forecast errors are spatially correlated under a shared synoptic
  regime, and the bot already quantifies exactly those correlations
  (_CITY_PAIR_CORR paper.py:313-332; tracker.get_recent_city_correlations
  refreshed into monte_carlo.simulate_portfolio) -- but solely for
  portfolio VaR.

RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-23 before picking this up: the "3-14 per-city" count
  cited above was stale (2026-07-12 audit) -- live counts were actually
  1-28 per city, and the settlement-latency question was resolved
  affirmatively (median lag ~1 day across 237 recent settlements, so
  yesterday's correlated-city errors ARE typically available by today's
  scan).

What shipped:
  tracker.get_regional_recent_bias(city, var, hours=48, as_of=None) --
  correlation-weighted mean of correlated cities' settled errors, using
  the exact _CORRELATED_CITY_GROUPS/_CITY_PAIR_CORR tables named above,
  with a ROW_NUMBER dedup to each ticker's latest logged prediction and
  outcomes_valid's disputed-row exclusion. `as_of` (SQLite datetime()
  string) lets a caller reconstruct a specific historical point in time
  without lookahead -- used to retrospectively validate against real
  settled data: Pearson r ~= 0.35 between pooled regional bias and same-
  city same-day error, but thin per-estimate coverage (85/229 candidate
  rows had any signal, averaging 1.67 correlated-city samples each). 9
  new tests, opus review clean (one defense-in-depth hardening applied:
  bound predicted_at by as_of too). Pushed `fd94bf7`.

Still open (2026-08-22: wiring this in was tried and then reverted -- this
  line is still accurate today; see the resolution note below for why, and
  its own "When to revisit" for what's next):
  - NOT wired into any live forecast lean or blend weight -- the original
    r~0.35 result turned out to be substantially a contamination artifact
    once investigated further; still log-only.

RESOLVED 2026-08-22 (precursor check only -- live wiring above is still
  fully open): picked up as part of batch-17 (audit/handoff_prompts/
  batches/batch-17.md), alongside the sibling PUBLIC TRADE-FLOW SIGNAL and
  PUBLIC TRADES REST BACKFILL entries. Did this entry's own instructed
  precursor -- "use the existing candle history ... to measure whether
  early-window prices were actually more mispriced vs settlement -- do
  that before building anything live" -- rather than building any WS code.
  True hours-since-listing isn't available: open_time is fetched live from
  the Kalshi API only at candlestick-backfill time and never persisted to
  price_history (checked live, not assumed). Surfaced this constraint to
  the user via AskUserQuestion before designing anything: with no stored
  listing time, the only viable statistic uses each market's own first
  captured candle as time zero, and the choice was between (a) a per-market
  paired early-half/late-half mispricing comparison (mirrors
  get_trade_flow_settlement_correlation's own time-midpoint-split
  precedent, one observation per market, no pseudo-replication) or (b) a
  pooled hours-elapsed-vs-mispricing correlation across every candle from
  every market (more literally matches "decays with market age" but pools
  non-independent within-market points). User chose (a).
  Shipped tracker.get_price_convergence_by_market_age(
  min_candles_per_market=8, min_candles_per_half=2, min_markets=15) --
  for each ticker with price_history rows, finds settlement price as the
  last candle with a real (non-NULL) price_close, walking backward past any
  NULL tail (same convention as get_trade_flow_settlement_correlation,
  which found 24% of price_history rows have a NULL close), filters to the
  earliest candle's own period_interval (same interleave guard as that
  function), splits the series at its own median-position candle's
  timestamp into an early half and late half, and computes mean
  |price_close - settlement_price| (mispricing magnitude) for each half --
  requiring at least min_candles_per_half real-priced candles per side,
  defaulting to 2 so neither half's average is normally reported from a
  single candle (a caller-supplied floor of 0 or 1 still gets exactly
  that, same as passing 1 directly -- see CORRECTED note below). Reports
  the per-market paired
  difference (early - late) across markets: mean_early_mispricing,
  mean_late_mispricing, mean_diff, and fraction_early_greater (the fraction
  of markets where early mispricing exceeded late), plus the same
  markets_considered/markets_skipped_thin/markets_skipped_no_price
  breakdown as the sibling function. Deliberately does NOT report a
  Pearson r like get_trade_flow_settlement_correlation -- this measures the
  SAME quantity at two points in one market's life, not two different
  variables across markets, so a paired-difference summary is the correct
  statistic, not a forced two-variable correlation.
  Real finding, run live against the actual DB: n=323 markets cleared the
  floor (326 considered, 3 skipped thin, 0 skipped for missing price).
  mean_early_mispricing=0.438, mean_late_mispricing=0.223, mean_diff=0.215,
  fraction_early_greater=0.904 -- in 90.4% of markets, price was measurably
  further from eventual settlement in the early half of its captured candle
  history than the late half.
  CORRECTED after independent Agent(opus, effort=high) review (before push,
  per standing workflow) found the first draft's interpretation of this
  finding overclaimed (HIGH severity) -- the original text called it
  "directional support" for the live market_lifecycle_v2 candidate. That is
  wrong: for ANY process whose price converges to a known terminal value,
  E[|price_t - settlement|] is mechanically decreasing as t approaches
  settlement, REGARDLESS of whether the market has any real exploitable
  edge -- a perfectly efficient market with zero informational edge
  produces this exact qualitative shape purely from ordinary uncertainty
  resolution. The reviewer ran a driftless martingale simulation (39
  hourly steps, binary settlement, matching the real data's shape) and
  reproduced fraction_early_greater=0.904 almost exactly at moderate
  information-arrival rates -- the observed value sits inside the zero-edge
  null band, not outside it. The entry's own kill-criterion ("if edge
  doesn't decay with market age, this whole candidate dies cheaply") can
  never actually be triggered by this statistic, which also means it can
  never be confirmed by it: the function measures distance from a market's
  own eventual settlement, not edge (|model_p - market_p| at a point in
  time, the quantity that actually determines whether an early maker quote
  profits). CORRECT reading of the result: it confirms markets resolve
  uncertainty over time, which was never in doubt, and is uninformative
  about whether market_lifecycle_v2 is worth building -- it does NOT
  support, and does not refute, that candidate. A real test of "does edge
  decay with market age" would need to compare market price against an
  independent fair-value estimate (e.g. this bot's own predictions.
  our_prob) at varying market ages, not against the market's own
  settlement -- that comparison is NOT implemented here and would be the
  actual next step if this candidate is ever seriously revisited. This
  correction is fully reflected in the function's own docstring (see
  tracker.py), which future readers should treat as authoritative over
  this note if the two ever diverge.
  Caveat also corrected (MEDIUM finding): the first draft claimed the
  first-captured-candle proxy for time zero "may already be well after
  actual listing, since price_history capture only started 2026-07-12" --
  factually wrong. sync_outcomes's candlestick backfill fetches the FULL
  [open_time, close_time] range at settlement time regardless of when the
  capture code itself shipped, so the first captured candle for a settled
  market is typically close to real market open. Verified live: 239/326
  tickers in the DB have a first candle before the capture code's own
  2026-07-12 ship date (earliest candle overall: 2026-05-17), and 311/326
  land at exactly 15:00 UTC, a listing-time artifact, not a capture-code
  artifact. The entry being resolved says this itself ("candles cover the
  full open->close window, so 'edge vs hours-since-open' is computable
  today") -- the first draft's caveat contradicted the entry it was
  resolving. True open_time is still not persisted to price_history, so
  "captured window" language is kept as the technically accurate framing,
  but the reasoning for why it's a reasonable (not weak) proxy is now
  correct in the function's own docstring.
  11 tests total in tests/test_tracker.py TestPriceConvergenceByMarketAge,
  built up across two independent opus review rounds (the first draft's
  own note claimed 9, then 8 -- both wrong at the time of writing, a
  recurring MEDIUM-severity audit-trail miscount both reviewers caught;
  this is the freshly re-collected count, not carried over from either
  round). The original 8: no-data default, the 3-market paired-difference
  computation itself (hand-computed early/late/diff/fraction values),
  below-min-markets (n reported, stats None), NULL-close settlement
  walk-back, a mixed-period_interval-candle filter case (mirrors the
  sibling function's own test design: the intruder candle's price would
  replace the market's settlement price entirely if it leaked in, not just
  flip a boolean), a min_candles_per_half floor case, a thin-market skip,
  and an all-NULL-close skip. 3 more added across the two review rounds: a
  dedicated post-period_interval-filter thin-recheck case (the pre-filter
  and post-filter thin checks are two distinct branches; the first draft
  only exercised the pre-filter one), a min_candles_per_half=0 no-crash
  case, and a min_markets=0 no-crash case (both floor-related
  ZeroDivisionError fixes described below).
  Mutation-testing claim corrected TWICE across the two review rounds --
  first for the settlement-price-None guard, then again for a second,
  structurally identical case the first correction's own reasoning should
  have already caught but didn't (round 2 flagged the recurrence
  directly): given min_candles_per_half is floored at >=1, the
  settlement-price-None guard is redundant with the half-floor check below
  it (a None settlement_price requires zero real closes anywhere in the
  filtered candle list, which necessarily makes early_prices/late_prices
  both empty too, so the half-floor check always also fires) --
  deleting the guard entirely does NOT break any test. The PRE-FILTER
  thin-candle-count check has the identical property with respect to its
  own post-filter sibling (filtering can only shrink the candle list, so
  anything failing the pre-filter check also fails the post-filter one) --
  deleting just the pre-filter check also does NOT break any test, even

[RESOLVED 2026-08-02] THE ONLY LIVE-ORDER PATH IS THE INTERACTIVE WATCH CLI -- NO HEADLESS TRADE-CYCLE ENGINE
Priority: High -- a stated prerequisite for the already-decided VM move +
  deferred always-on watcher; this is the refactor that determines whether
  that work is a port or a rewrite.

Problem:
  There are two parallel scan pipelines, and the hardened one can't trade
  live while the live one isn't hardened. cron pipeline (cron.py:475
  _cmd_cron_body, ~2,100 lines): the production path -- kill-switch/
  override/accuracy-halt/graduation gates, consistency-violation halt
  (cron.py:1112-1136), batch cache prewarm, ThreadPoolExecutor scan via
  _enrich_and_analyze (cron.py:1369), is_stale exclusion, gate counters,
  shadow logging, tiered ctx.auto_place_trades(...) (cron.py:1886/1895)
  -- paper only; cron never passes live=True. watch pipeline (main.py:
  2822 cmd_watch): a `while True` terminal UI wrapping _analyze_once
  (main.py:1294) -- a *sequential* scan with different gates (skips
  days_out==0 at 1337, no consistency halt, no prewarm -- dedup/is_stale
  parity was added 2026-07-19, see the RESOLVED note below) -- and this
  is the *only* path that can place a live order
  (_auto_place_trades(..., live=live) at 2875-2877, then poll/reprice/
  exit-protection at 2878-2886). So when live trading starts, real money
  runs through the interactive-display pipeline while the
  production-hardened pipeline stays paper. And the deferred always-on
  watcher ("reacts between cycles") has no home: it would be a *third*
  hand-assembled sequence of scan->analyze->place->poll->reprice->
  protect, because that sequence exists only as inline orchestration
  inside two different functions, each with its own subset and ordering.
  The exit-protection calls are already duplicated verbatim between them
  (cron.py:757-768 vs main.py:2878-2886).

What it would look like:
  Extract a headless run_trade_cycle(client, mode: paper|live, triggers)
  engine owning the canonical ordered sequence (recover-pending -> settle
  -> scan -> analyze -> decide/place -> poll fills -> reprice -> position
  protection -> log), with the CLI display and the cron wrapper both
  becoming thin callers. The always-on watcher then becomes "call the
  engine's protection stage on WS events + the full cycle on a timer"
  instead of a third reimplementation. The CronContext injection seam
  (cron.py:78, main.py:208) is already halfway there -- the engine is
  mostly a matter of moving orchestration out of _cmd_cron_body/
  cmd_watch into it.

RESOLVED 2026-08-02 (the full headless engine extraction -- "live trading
  imminent" trigger fired 2026-07-31, Belgium pause lifted): extracted a new

  Re-verification before implementation found the backlog text's own
  "What it would look like" undersold the real scope in one important way:
  watch's _passes_edge tag was NOT the cosmetic, unrelated-to-trading

  Design decisions surfaced via AskUserQuestion (3 rounds, not guessed):
  (1) scope -- unify the real gate set and decide/place logic between
  pipelines rather than a pure code-relocation that would have preserved

  (net-edge floor + prob-edge floor) for BOTH pipelines' actual trading
  decisions, keeping watch's old MIN_EDGE-based tag as display-only cosmetic

  Given the size, mechanical relocation of ~900 lines of safety-critical
  code was done via two general-purpose Agent calls (cron.py, main.py
  wiring) working from a complete, precise specification this session wrote
  after full manual research of both pipelines -- not delegated design or
  judgment, only bounded mechanical execution, independently reviewed line

  Independent review used 4 PARALLEL opus agents scoped by subsystem
  (feedback_scale_review_to_change_size) given the size: trade_cycle.py's
  own engine correctness, cron.py's rewiring, main.py's cmd_watch rewiring,
  and test-coverage adequacy. Findings (all fixed, none skipped):

  CRITICAL:
  - trade_cycle.py tagged analysis dicts with a new _passes_threshold key,
    but main.py's existing consumers (incl. the live reprice path) still
    read the old _passes_edge with a fail-open `default=True` -- the key
    being absent meant every candidate silently looked like it passed.
    Fixed by also setting _passes_edge to the real outcome, AND by
    explicitly filtering cmd_watch's liquid_opps to _passes_threshold=True
    before passing to _reprice_or_cancel_pending_orders (belt-and-
    suspenders, not reliant on the field-name convention alone).
  - cron.py's orphaned-live-position safety net (_check_live_position_
    exits/_check_live_model_exits) ran BEFORE _recover_pending_orders once
    the latter moved inside the engine (called much later) -- a live
    position recovered from a crash got zero exit protection for a full
    cycle instead of immediate coverage. Fixed by restoring an early
    _recover_pending_orders() call in cron.py before the exit checks
    (matching the existing "restore early + redundant engine call becomes
    a harmless no-op" pattern already used for the 3 gates).
  - 7 pre-existing tests were actually broken by this refactor (the initial
    "broader sweep" only covered this entry's own established file list and
    missed these): test_execution_stability.py::test_lock_released_in_
    finally (a genuine regression -- see try/except scope below, not just a
    stale assertion), test_cron_group_c.py's 2 --edge-gate tests and

    batch_e.py's 3 source-inspection tests (asserted on literal text in
    cron._cmd_cron_body's source that moved to trade_cycle.run_trade_
    cycle's source). All 7 re-pointed at the module that now owns the
    logic, not silently skipped or deleted.
  - live=True/live_config threading -- the literal path this entry exists
    to harden -- had zero test coverage at the new engine seam. Added.

  HIGH:
  - The try/except scope around the scan shrank during extraction: the
    original wrapped fetch-through-analyze in one catch-all so a transient
    failure degraded to an empty scan (settlement/sync_outcomes/shadow-
    logging/housekeeping still ran); the extracted version only wrapped the
    ThreadPoolExecutor section, so a market-fetch exception now propagated
    out of run_trade_cycle() entirely -- this IS what broke test_lock_
    released_in_finally above, and would have killed a watch --auto --live
    session outright on a transient Kalshi API failure. Fixed by widening

  - The WebSocket used to subscribe+start right after the market fetch,
    before prewarm/analysis/placement; since the engine now owns the fetch,

    after the fetch, that cron.py uses to subscribe+start its WS at the
    original point in the cycle (watch has no WS to manage -- confirmed via
    grep, so no equivalent wiring needed there).
  - Analysis-attempt logging (the analysis_attempts audit table used for

    measured against live signals_cache.json data during review: 9 of 25
    analyzed markets (36%) were being lost. Fixed by moving the all_results

    two gates (matching cron.py's pre-extraction _analysis_batch collection
    point exactly); liquid_opps/no_quote_opps population stayed where it

  - watch's own --edge CLI override (min_edge parameter) was being dropped
    entirely (passed as None) instead of threaded into run_trade_cycle() --
    given the _passes_edge correction above, this would have silently
    removed a real, working live-trading floor a user could already invoke
    (watch --auto --live --edge 40 required >=40% edge pre-refactor; the
    fix would have ignored the flag and placed at the 15% tier floor

    floor exactly like cron's --edge (max(min_edge, get_paper_min_edge()),
    never a ceiling).

  MEDIUM:
  - cmd_watch's new settle/recover-pending calls (via the engine) never
    coordinated with cron's file lock, a new cross-process race on paper.
    json/tracker.db that didn't exist pre-refactor (watch never touched
    settlement before). Fixed: cmd_watch now acquires/releases cron's own
    lock around its run_trade_cycle() call, skipping that cycle's auto-
    trade attempt gracefully (with an operator-visible message) if cron is
    running concurrently, rather than racing.
  - watch runs up to three independent get_weather_markets() scans per
    cycle (price-drift, the engine's own, and _analyze_once's own for
    display) -- real cost/staleness concern, but a full fix means
    extracting _analyze_once's ~400-line table/arb/correlation-warning
    rendering into a shared helper so the auto_trade=True path can render

    this late in an already large, safety-critical session against a
    function cmd_analyze also depends on -- reordering so the trading
    decision runs BEFORE the display scan was implemented instead (the more
    safety-relevant staleness direction: an operator seeing "no signals"
    moments after a trade actually fired is more confusing than the

    list when available instead of a 3rd fetch. Full scan unification filed
    as its own follow-up entry below.

  LOW (all fixed): analysis_errors dbg counter dropped (folded into

[RESOLVED 2026-08-03] POSITION PROTECTION IS STILL TWO SEPARATE MECHANISMS
AFTER THE HEADLESS ENGINE EXTRACTION -- CRON'S TIME-BASED EXITS VS. WATCH'S
MODEL-FLIP EXITS
Priority: Medium -- filed during the 2026-08-02 headless-engine extraction
  (see the RESOLVED entry immediately above) as a deliberately out-of-scope
  finding, not folded in.

Problem:
  trade_cycle.run_trade_cycle() now unifies the gate set and the
  directional-signal decide/place logic between cron.py and watch --auto,
  but position protection (what closes an already-open position) is still
  two independent, never-reconciled mechanisms: cron.py's paper stop-loss/
  breakeven checks are time-elapsed-based (paper.check_stop_losses/
  check_breakeven_stops), while watch's are model-flip/edge-based
  (paper.check_model_exits) plus a separate expiring-trade countdown
  (check_expiring_trades) -- not the same exit philosophy, just two
  different ones that happen to both exist. cron.py also runs a live-
  position orphan safety net (_check_live_position_exits/_check_live_
  model_exits) for positions left open by a crashed watch --live session;
  watch runs the same two functions itself, plus its own poll-fills/
  reprice-or-cancel logic for its own resting live orders -- genuinely
  different responsibilities (watch manages orders it just placed this
  cycle; cron's copy is purely a crash-recovery safety net), not simple
  duplication.

Why not folded into the headless-engine extraction:
  Unlike the gate/threshold/tiering work, this isn't a case of "the same
  logic exists twice, unify it" -- cron's time-based exit and watch's
  model-flip exit are genuinely different STRATEGIES, and deciding which
  (or whether both, selectively) should apply to which pipeline is a real
  design question requiring its own AskUserQuestion round, not something to
  guess while already mid-flight on a large, safety-critical change.

When to revisit:
  Same trigger as the parent entry ("live trading imminent," already
  fired 2026-07-31) -- this is a natural next step now that the
  directional-signal pipeline is unified, but should be its own scoped
  piece of work with its own design-decision round on which exit
  philosophy (or explicit dual-strategy-by-design) is correct, not an
  extension of the already-large diff above.

RESOLVED 2026-08-03:
  Re-verification correction to the problem statement above: cron's paper
  protection was never purely "time-elapsed-based" -- it already ran THREE
  mechanisms (paper.check_stop_losses/check_breakeven_stops, both
  price-based, plus order_executor._check_early_exits, a SECOND,
  independently-written model-flip check at 25pp shift + a pre-settlement
  gate). Watch ran exactly ONE mechanism (paper.check_model_exits, a THIRD
  model-flip implementation at 10pp net_edge + no settlement gate) and had
  ZERO price-based protection. check_expiring_trades (both pipelines) was
  never an exit mechanism at all -- it only prints a countdown warning,
  never closes anything. Live positions were already fully unified via
  order_executor._check_live_position_exits/_check_live_model_exits, called
  identically by both pipelines -- that precedent is what this resolution
  extends to paper.

  Design decisions (AskUserQuestion, both explicitly user-selected):
  1. Watch's paper positions get the same price-based stop-loss/breakeven
     protection cron's already had.
  2. The canonical model-exit implementation is cron's version
     (order_executor._check_early_exits, 25pp shift + settlement gate) --
     not watch's separate check_model_exits (10pp, no settlement gate).
     check_model_exits itself is UNCHANGED and still used by cmd_brief's
     informational display and the manual "Exit Signals" submenu (explicit
     y/N per position) -- only watch's automated per-cycle call site
     switched to _check_early_exits.

  Implementation: new paper.check_paper_position_exits(client) (paper.py)
  extracted from cron.py's ~100-line inline stop-loss/breakeven block,
  returning closed positions as structured dicts so callers can log/print
  without re-deriving exit details. cron.py's _cmd_cron_body now calls this
  shared function (identical console/log output preserved). main.py's
  cmd_watch automated per-cycle block (unconditional on auto_trade -- it
  already ran every watch cycle before this change, not just --auto) now
  ALSO calls this same function, and its model-flip check now calls
  main._check_early_exits(client) instead of check_model_exits(client).

  Independent opus review (effort=high) found 2 MEDIUM real issues, both
  fixed: (1) check_paper_position_exits swallowed every per-ticker price-
  fetch failure with zero logging (worse than the original cron-only
  inline block, since the blast radius is now both pipelines) -- fixed by
  restoring the per-ticker debug log plus a new WARNING-level summary when
  fewer positions got a usable quote than are open; (2) close_paper_early()
  inside the new function wasn't fault-isolated per trade, so one race
  (position settled between get_open_trades() and the close attempt --
  newly reachable since watch releases the cron lock before this block
  runs, unlike cron which holds it throughout) would raise and abort every
  remaining stop-loss/breakeven check that cycle -- fixed by wrapping each
  close_paper_early() call in try/except + warning-log + continue, matching
  how _check_early_exits/_exit_live_position already isolate per-trade
  failures. Also fixed on review: this entry and BACKLOG_OPEN.md itself
  weren't updated (caught by the review, now fixed here), trade_cycle.py's
  module docstring still claimed position protection used "genuinely
  different exit strategies" (now stale for the price-based side -- fixed),
  and two comments overclaimed "identical protection regardless of which
  pipeline observes it" without noting that cron skips this entire call
  while data/.kill_switch is set but watch's loop has no kill-switch check
  at all (pre-existing asymmetry -- the old check_model_exits call this
  replaced didn't check it either -- comments corrected to say so rather
  than overclaim parity).

  Noted, not changed (deliberate, per the design decision above): watch's
  model-exit coverage is now strictly NARROWER than before in one respect
  -- the old check_model_exits also fired on edge_gone (net_edge < -10%
  with no shift requirement), which _check_early_exits does not replicate.
  A position whose net_edge fell to -12% via an 8pp forecast shift (under
  _check_early_exits's 25pp bar) now goes uncaught by any paper mechanism
  until price itself moves enough to trip stop-loss (-50% of cost) or
  breakeven (requires a prior peak past BREAKEVEN_TRIGGER_PCT, .env-set to
  0.75 here, not the 0.30 code default). This is the accepted cost of the
  user's explicit choice to canonicalize on cron's stricter implementation
  rather than watch's looser one, not an oversight.

  cmd_watch's per-cycle path now runs a 4th independent get_weather_
  markets() scan (inside _check_early_exits) -- addended to the sibling
  [CMD_WATCH RUNS THREE INDEPENDENT get_weather_markets() SCANS...] entry
  below rather than treated as new scope here.

  Tests: new TestCheckPaperPositionExits class (tests/test_paper.py, 6
  tests: client=None, no open trades, stop-loss closes, breakeven closes,
  stop-loss-close excludes same-cycle breakeven re-check, per-ticker
  price-fetch-error isolation). test_trading.py's
  test_cmd_watch_auto_executes_model_exits rewritten as
  test_cmd_watch_auto_executes_early_exits (the call path it tested no
  longer exists) plus new test_cmd_watch_auto_executes_paper_stop_loss.
  New test_cron_closes_position_via_check_paper_position_exits in
  test_cron_integration.py. All new/changed tests mutation-tested (reason-
  tag mislabeling, removing the reload-before-breakeven ordering fix, and
  removing each of the 3 call sites -- all caught). 395 tests pass across
  the full affected regression scope; ruff + ruff format + mypy clean on
  all 6 changed files (cron.py, main.py, paper.py, and the 3 test files).

  ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE was not touched (still false); no real order was placed
  as part of this work -- paper/mocked throughout.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-03] CMD_WATCH RUNS THREE INDEPENDENT get_weather_markets()
SCANS PER AUTO-TRADE CYCLE -- DISPLAY SCAN NEVER UNIFIED WITH THE ENGINE'S
OWN SCAN
Priority: Low/Medium -- filed during the 2026-08-02 headless-engine
  extraction (see the RESOLVED entry above) as a deliberately deferred
  MEDIUM review finding, not folded in.

Problem:
  watch --auto now calls get_weather_markets() up to three times per
  cycle: once for price-drift detection (main.py, reused from
  trade_cycle.run_trade_cycle()'s own scan when auto-trading, but still a
  fresh fetch on the auto_trade=False / no-cycle-result path), once inside
  run_trade_cycle() itself (the authoritative trading-decision scan), and
  once inside _analyze_once() (the display-only scan feeding the
  interactive table). The full enrich+analyze pass also runs twice per
  cycle (once in each scan), doubling upstream Kalshi/Open-Meteo load and
  analysis-DB writes every 5 minutes. More importantly, the table an
  operator watches during an auto-trading session is NOT the same scan
  that made the trading decision -- a signal can appear on screen without
  having been traded (or vice versa), with no indication why.

What was done instead (2026-08-02, see the RESOLVED entry above):
  Reordered so run_trade_cycle() runs BEFORE _analyze_once() each cycle
  when auto-trading, so the operator's display reflects state right after
  the trading decision, not a stale pre-decision snapshot -- the more
  safety-relevant staleness direction. Price-drift detection reuses the
  engine's own markets list when a cycle_result exists instead of a 3rd
  fetch. The actual trading decision (via run_trade_cycle()) was already
  unaffected by any of this, since it always used its own authoritative
  scan regardless of what _analyze_once separately fetched.

What it would look like to fully close this:
  Extract _analyze_once()'s ~400-line table/arb/correlation-warning/
  summary rendering (main.py, the portion after the per-market analyze
  loop) into a standalone helper function taking (client, markets,
  liquid_opps, no_quote_opps, previous_tickers, min_edge, show_summary,
  open_trades) -- called BY _analyze_once() itself (so cmd_analyze's
  behavior stays 100% unchanged, zero risk) and ALSO called directly by
  cmd_watch when auto_trade=True, sourcing its inputs from
  trade_cycle.run_trade_cycle()'s own cycle_result instead of a second
  scan. Watch would then need to compute _passes_edge (display-only
  cosmetic dimming, kept deliberately separate from the engine's real
  _passes_threshold per the parent entry's threshold-fix decision) and
  _is_hedge tags on cycle_result.all_results itself, matching what
  _analyze_once currently tags inline.

Why not done as part of the parent extraction:
  Mechanically large (a ~400-line extraction touching main.py's most-used
  display code) attempted late in an already large, safety-critical
  session -- judged higher regression risk than proportionate to a
  MEDIUM-severity UX/performance finding. _analyze_once is also cmd_
  analyze's only scan path, so any mistake here has a wider blast radius
  than the trading-decision code already carefully reviewed.

When to revisit:
  Whenever watch --auto usage in practice makes the display/decision
  staleness or the doubled API load a real operational annoyance -- no
  specific trigger beyond that; lower urgency than the position-protection
  entry above since the actual trading decision is already unaffected.

ADDENDUM 2026-08-03 (title's count now stale, problem unchanged):
  The position-protection unification entry above (now RESOLVED) added a
  4th get_weather_markets() call to cmd_watch's per-cycle path: watch's
  automated loop now also calls order_executor._check_early_exits(), which
  does its own internal get_weather_markets() fetch (order_executor.py) to
  build its markets_by_ticker lookup for the model-flip check. This entry's
  title/problem statement ("three independent scans") is now undercounting
  by one; the underlying problem (multiple independent scans per cycle,
  none reusing cycle_result) is unchanged and this new scan should be
  covered by the same eventual fix, not treated as a 4th separate one to
  solve. Not fixed here -- fixing it would mean threading cycle_result's
  markets into _check_early_exits too, out of scope for a paper-position-
  protection change. Title left as-is (not renumbered) per
  feedback_backlog_title_staleness's guidance to verify against full entry
  text rather than trust the title in isolation.

RESOLVED 2026-08-03:
  Implemented exactly the "what it would look like to fully close this"
  plan above, with 2 refinements the plan itself didn't anticipate (both
  found during implementation, not by opus review):
  1. Extracted _analyze_once()'s rendering body (main.py, 417 lines --
     table/arb/correlation-warning/summary, INCLUDING the arbitrage-surface
     block, which actually PLACES real paper orders via place_paper_order()
     when a consistency violation clears its gates, not just a display
     warning -- the original plan's "rendering" framing undersold this)
     into a standalone _render_analysis_results(). _analyze_once() itself
     now just calls it with its own freshly-scanned data -- byte-for-byte
     unchanged behavior for cmd_analyze (confirmed both by direct diff and
     by re-running _analyze_once's full pre-existing test suite, 36/36
     pass, zero changes needed) and for plain/non-auto watch.
  2. cmd_watch's auto-trading loop now branches on cycle_result: when
     available, it calls _render_analysis_results() directly with
     trade_cycle.run_trade_cycle()'s own already-scanned/already-analyzed
     data (cycle_result.deduped_markets/liquid_opps/no_quote_opps) instead
     of calling _analyze_once() again. When cycle_result is None (kill
     switch active, or the cron lock unavailable), it falls back to
     _analyze_once() exactly as before, unaffected. This reduces
     auto-trading's per-cycle scan count from up to four (per the ADDENDUM
     above) down to two: run_trade_cycle()'s own scan, and
     _check_early_exits()'s own separate scan (position-protection's,
     deliberately left unthreaded -- still the ADDENDUM's stated remaining
     gap, now the ONLY remaining one).

  Refinement 1 (found during research, not in the original plan): the
  original plan said watch would need to "compute _passes_edge (...) kept
  deliberately separate from the engine's real _passes_threshold" -- this
  turned out to already be moot. trade_cycle.py already aliases
  analysis["_passes_edge"] = passes_threshold specifically so callers
  reading the pre-extraction field name see the real threshold outcome,
  not a stale default. So cmd_watch's cycle_result path reuses this real
  value directly rather than recomputing a separate cosmetic formula --
  display dimming on the auto-trade path is now MORE accurate than before
  (matches what actually got traded), not just equivalent. Two new
  TradeCycleResult fields (deduped_markets, effective_min_edge) were added
  so the renderer's market-count and threshold-percentage text stay
  accurate when sourced this way, instead of the pre-dedup/raw values.

  Refinement 2 (found during research): the plan said to build _is_hedge
  and a ticker->city map on cycle_result.all_results "matching what
  _analyze_once currently tags inline" -- but all_results is populated
  AFTER analyze_trade()'s not-analysis check, while _analyze_once's own
  _arb_ticker_city is tagged BEFORE it (immediately after enrich+analyze
  succeed). Deriving the map from all_results as literally described would
  have been silently narrower. Added a new ticker_city field to
  TradeCycleResult instead, tagged at the correct (earlier) point inside
  run_trade_cycle()'s own loop, and cmd_watch sources it directly rather
  than rebuilding it.

  Independent opus review (effort=high) caught refinement 2's gap in the
  FIRST draft (which did derive it from all_results, exactly as the
  original plan described) -- HIGH+MEDIUM real findings, both fixed:
  (1) HIGH: _analyze_once's own per-market loop fires alert_strong_signal()
  for new STRONG liquid opportunities -- that loop is NOT part of the
  extracted render body, so the cycle_result path silently never fired this
  alert at all on the auto-trade path (proven empirically by the reviewer:
  0 alerts on auto watch vs 1 on plain watch for an identical opportunity),
  and the miss was sticky (the ticker still got recorded as "seen" via
  _save_watch_state, so even a later fallback cycle wouldn't re-fire it).
  Fixed by adding an equivalent alert-firing loop directly in cmd_watch's
  cycle_result branch. (2) MEDIUM: the first draft's all_results-derived
  ticker->city map (refinement 2's original, plan-following version) meant
  the arb block's per-city exposure cap ($25/city) was silently bypassed
  and placed arb trades lost city attribution whenever BOTH legs of a
  violation had no real analysis result -- fixed via the new
  TradeCycleResult.ticker_city field described above. Also fixed, LOW
  severity: the "dimmed below >X% edge threshold" caption text was
  literally true for _analyze_once's own formula but not for the
  cycle_result path's real (multi-gate) _passes_edge semantics -- reworded

[RESOLVED 2026-07-20] WATCH/_analyze_once IS MISSING cron.py's MIN_MARKET_PROB_TO_BET_WITH /
MAX_MARKET_DIVERGENCE_RATIO DIRECTIONAL-CONSENSUS GATES
Priority: Medium -- a real, live-order-path gap, but narrower than it first
  looks (see "Why this is smaller than it sounds" below); no known incident,
  TRADING_PAUSED=true throughout.

Found: 2026-07-20, as an adjacency finding while shipping the days_out==0
  parity fix above (backlog.txt "THE ONLY LIVE-ORDER PATH... -- NO HEADLESS
  TRADE-CYCLE ENGINE"). Deliberately not folded into that change. Widened
  same day from one missing gate to two after an independent Agent(opus,
  effort=high) review of that fix's diff caught the same-day comment
  overclaiming both gates applied in main.py and, chasing that down, found
  MAX_MARKET_DIVERGENCE_RATIO was ALSO cron.py-only -- this session's first
  adjacency pass had only found MIN_MARKET_PROB_TO_BET_WITH.

Problem:
  cron.py's scan loop (cron.py:1546-1565) applies two gates beyond
  analyze_trade()'s own internal gates, both keyed on `_mkt_dir` (the
  market's own probability in the direction of `recommended_side` --
  market_prob if betting yes, 1-market_prob if betting no):
  1. `MIN_MARKET_PROB_TO_BET_WITH` (utils.py:189, 0.25): skip if the market
     gives our chosen side less than a 25% chance -- "the market is right
     nearly every time" at that level of disagreement (cron.py:1557-1559).
  2. `MAX_MARKET_DIVERGENCE_RATIO` (utils.py:183): skip if `_our_dir /
     _mkt_dir` (our probability in our chosen direction, divided by the
     market's) exceeds the ratio cap -- a second, ratio-shaped framing of
     "we disagree with the market too much" (cron.py:1560-1565).
  Grepped the whole repo for both constants: each appears only in cron.py
  and its own definition/fingerprint entry in utils.py -- zero occurrences
  in main.py or order_executor.py. watch/_analyze_once (the only pipeline
  that can place a live order) has never applied either check, for any
  market, not just same-day ones.

Why this is smaller than it sounds:
  analyze_trade() itself (weather_markets.py:7254-7272, "7d. Model-market gap
  gate") already rejects (returns None) any trade -- shared by both
  pipelines, since both call analyze_trade() -- when the RAW model
  probability and market probability disagree by more than 0.25, regardless
  of direction. So the bulk of what cron's two directional checks would
  catch is already caught upstream, for both pipelines equally.
  What 7d does NOT catch and cron's checks do: cases where the raw
  disagreement is under 0.25 but the market is still confidently against
  our chosen side -- e.g. market YES-price 20%, our forecast 35% YES: gap is
  15pp (passes 7d) but the market gives our side only a 20% chance (would
  fail cron's `_mkt_dir < 0.25` check, and likely the ratio check too). This
  can happen because 7d compares against the PRE-anchor raw model
  probability while cron's `_mkt_dir`/`_our_dir` read `analysis.get(
  "market_prob"/"forecast_prob")` (potentially blended/anchored) -- the
  gates are measuring related but distinct things, not one subsuming the
  others.

What it would look like:
  Port cron.py:1546-1565's exact `_mkt_dir`/`_our_dir` computation + both
  checks into main.py's `_analyze_once`, after the days_out==0 fall-through
  (same site as this entry's sibling fix above). Needs its own
  AskUserQuestion pass first though -- open scope questions not yet answered:
  (1) should it use `analysis.get("market_prob"/"forecast_prob")`
  (post-anchor, matching cron.py exactly) or something else; (2) does it
  need its own debug counters matching `_dbg["mkt_prob"]`/`_dbg[
  "divergence"]`'s style; (3) whether cmd_today (main.py:2298-2316, a
  separate display-only "what should I do today" command, NOT the
  live-order path) should get the same treatment for UI-recommendation
  parity, or is out of scope since it never places an order.

When to revisit:
  - No hard trigger -- this is a real, self-contained gap independent of the
    VM-move/live-trading-imminent trigger that gates the full headless-engine
    entry above. Reasonable to pick up any time; not urgent given
    TRADING_PAUSED=true and analyze_trade()'s 7d gate already covering the
    large-gap cases.
