  ForecastCache class directly; or a third option found only by digging
  further -- a new subclass that adds dump/load without touching the base
  class at all). User picked the subclass option after asking for the
  analysis to be double-checked first.
  Also found while re-verifying: _station_cache was a bare, unlocked plain
  dict -- _save_station_cache()'s dict comprehension over .items() racing
  a concurrent _station_cache[key]=... write from a different city's
  lookup was a latent (confirmed currently unreachable -- cron.py's scan
  loop is single-threaded, no ThreadPoolExecutor/threading.Thread touches
  this path anywhere in the repo) RuntimeError risk. The subclass approach
  closes this for free as a side effect, which the plain "extend the
  shared class" option would not have made any cleaner.
  Shipped: `PersistentForecastCache` (forecast_cache.py), a subclass adding
  `dump_to_disk()`/`load_from_disk()` on top of ForecastCache without
  modifying any of its existing methods -- confirmed zero blast radius to
  the other ~14 consumers (AST-hashed all 12 base-class methods pre/post
  diff via an opus review: byte-identical). _station_cache migrated onto
  it (ttl_secs=inf, max_size=100_000 -- "effectively unbounded", matching
  the old never-evicting dict); `_load_station_cache`/`_save_station_cache`
  now thin wrappers calling the new methods, preserving the exact "lat,lon"
  string key format of the existing on-disk file.
  Two rounds of independent Agent(opus) review, all findings fixed (not
  just the obvious one):
  round 1 -- (1) HIGH: the thread-safety regression test didn't actually
  detect a missing lock (default max_size=500 meant the writer thread
  evicted-then-inserted, keeping dict *size* stable, and CPython's
  iteration guard fires on a size change, not a content change -- passed
  identically with or without the lock). Fixed by tuning to a store large
  enough (30,000 pre-seeded + 30,000 written during the race, max_size
  raised so it never evicts) that the race is reliably reproducible --
  mutation-tested 30/30 detection on an unlocked scratch subclass, 0/30
  false positives on the real locked version, both directions fast
  (<1s). (2) MEDIUM: load_from_disk silently truncated a restore to
  max_size (routed through set(), which evicts) -- fixed by writing
  directly into _store under the lock, bypassing eviction on load only.
  (3) MEDIUM: dump_to_disk's file write was non-atomic (plain
  path.write_text, same as the pre-migration code) -- switched to the
  existing safe_io.atomic_write_json (temp file + fsync + rename), which
  cron.py's own comments already cite as the correct pattern for exactly
  this failure mode. (4) MEDIUM: dump/load's docstring pointed at the
  wrong remedy (set_at()) for round-tripping a per-entry-TTL (3-tuple)
  entry, which set_at() can't actually do (needs a wall-clock timestamp
  and recomputed remaining-TTL, not a monotonic one) -- fixed by having
  dump_to_disk raise ValueError on a 3-tuple entry instead of silently
  dropping the TTL, since nothing today needs both per-entry TTL and disk
  persistence. (5) LOW: .get() can't distinguish "no entry" from "cached
  None", so a falsy stationIdentifier would refetch every call instead of
  respecting a cached negative result (a real, if extremely rare, behavior
  difference from the old plain dict, which cached it) -- fixed by simply
  never caching a falsy station_id (worse to permanently cache a bad
  result forever under ttl_secs=inf than to occasionally re-fetch).
  (6)-(9): tests corrected to use production's real ttl_secs=inf config
  instead of the class default, an overclaiming test docstring fixed, a
  legacy on-disk-format compatibility test added using the REAL nws.py
  helpers (not a test-local copy), type annotations added.
  round 2 (verifying round 1's fixes, not re-reviewing from scratch) --
  found 2 more: (a) the new deadlock-risk docstring misattributed which
  code ran under the lock (said "the file write", but the write was
  actually outside it) -- fixed by moving the file write inside the lock
  for real (see next point) rather than just correcting the sentence;
  (b) concurrent dump_to_disk calls for the same path could collide on
  safe_io.atomic_write_json's shared temp filename, since the lock was
  only held for the in-memory snapshot, not the write itself -- reachable
  in principle since _get_obs_station's per-city lock only serializes
  same-city calls, not cross-city ones. Fixed by holding the lock for
  dump_to_disk's entire duration including the write, which closes both
  (a) and (b) at once (blocks set()/get() during the write too -- accepted,
  this cache is written a handful of times per scan cycle, not a hot
  path). Also fixed 2 minor test nits from the same pass (an unused
  fixture arg, a docstring overclaiming which of 2 helper functions a test
  actually exercises).

  migration a guaranteed permanent no-op masking whether the cursor
  advances correctly); every column any function in the file reads/writes
  resolves to either the base table or a migration; the pre-existing-DB
  self-heal scenario by hand; thread-safety of _run_migrations running
  inside the existing double-checked _init_lock (no new issue -- only one
  thread ever runs migrations, flag flips true only after they complete);
  and that the new tests genuinely exercise real code paths rather than
  passing vacuously. One LOW note, not a bug: execution_log's
  _run_migrations catches `sqlite3.OperationalError` specifically where
  tracker.py's catches bare `Exception` -- correct and actually tighter for
  a list that's 100% ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN today; worth revisiting only if
  a future migration here is a CREATE UNIQUE INDEX over dirty data (would
  raise IntegrityError, which should propagate anyway, so still desired
  behavior).

Problem (original framing, resolved above):
  tracker.py migrations are versioned (_MIGRATIONS list + PRAGMA
  user_version cursor, tracker.py:30-255) with guard tests asserting
  _SCHEMA_VERSION == len(_MIGRATIONS) -- and this exact machinery just
  caught and self-healed a real drift on 2026-07-16 (see the FORECAST
  RUN-TO-RUN TREND SIGNAL entry above). execution_log.py instead
  re-attempts a flat list of 16 ALTER statements on every process init
  inside `except sqlite3.OperationalError: pass` (execution_log.py:
  106-129). Structural problems: (a) a genuine OperationalError (locked
  DB, disk error) on a *needed* ALTER is indistinguishable from
  "duplicate column" and is silently swallowed -- the column just doesn't
  exist and the first INSERT referencing it fails later, far from the
  cause; (b) no version cursor means no way to write a data-backfill
  migration (only additive ALTERs are expressible); (c) every new
  live-execution feature grows the list, so the two files' migration
  styles diverge further with each shipped entry.

What it would look like: [DONE, see resolution notes above]

Why not now (resolved):
  - Was gated on doing it while live=1 rows were still empty (the easiest
    this migration would ever be) -- done while that was still true;
    ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE remained False throughout, untouched by this change.

  - N/A, closed.

FOLLOW-UP, same day, pushed separately: the independent Agent(opus) review
  of the deletion above surfaced one adjacency note -- paper.export_
  trades_csv() (paper.py:2120) derives its csv.DictWriter fieldnames from
  trades[0].keys() alone (trades are append-ordered, so trades[0] is the
  OLDEST record) with DictWriter's default extrasaction="raise" -- any
  later trade with a key the oldest one lacks crashes the export. This is
  pre-existing (not introduced by the exit_target deletion, and already
  catalogued as a LOW finding in docs/audit_findings.md) -- caused by
  schema GROWTH (a field added to place_paper_order after the oldest
  on-disk trade was placed), not shrinkage: the review's own follow-up
  check confirmed exit_target's removal is actually the safe direction
  (old trades keep the key, new ones lack it, which trades[0]-keyed code
  handles fine either way) -- corrected a first-draft code comment that
  had this backwards. User asked to fix it regardless, since the growth
  direction is a real, live, already-reachable crash. Checked the other 2
  csv.DictWriter sites in
  the repo (tracker.py:2294, web_app.py:1347) first -- both derive
  fieldnames from tracker.get_history()'s SQL rows, which are uniform per
  query regardless of age (unlike paper.py's independently-evolved JSON
  records), so neither is actually vulnerable to this bug class; scope
  confirmed narrow to paper.py alone. Fixed by unioning every trade's keys
  (first-seen order) into fieldnames instead of reading only trades[0],
  with restval="" so any trade missing a given key renders an empty cell
  instead of raising -- handles both schema growth (a newer trade has a
  field older ones lack) and schema shrinkage (an older trade has a field,
  like exit_target, that newer ones no longer do) correctly. New
  regression test (test_export_trades_csv_handles_heterogeneous_schema)
  builds two trades then directly mutates the on-disk JSON to strip a
  field from the oldest and add a field only the newest has, asserting the
  export doesn't raise and both fields get their own column; mutation-
  tested via git stash (confirmed it fails with the exact predicted
  `ValueError: dict contains fields not in fieldnames` against the
  reverted code, then restored). 152 tests pass in tests/test_paper.py
  (172 including test_debug_fixes.py); ruff + ruff format + mypy clean.

[RESOLVED 2026-07-18] TEST-ORDER-DEPENDENT importlib.reload(order_executor) BROKE main.py's FROZEN-IMPORT IDENTITY CHECK
Priority: was Medium (CI-breaking, safety-adjacent test coverage) -- now Low
  (fixed; only a cousin risk remains, see below)

RESOLVED 2026-07-18: found via real GitHub Actions CI failure output (not a
  local repro -- this repo's local .env masked half of it, see below) after
  pushing the execution_log migration and _current_forecast_cycle cleanup
  commits. Two independent pre-existing bugs, neither caused by those two
  commits, both exposed by the same CI run:
    1. tests/test_execution_stability.py::test_gfs_window_disabled_with_
       zero_lockout did `importlib.reload(order_executor)` to pick up a
       monkeypatched GFS_LOCKOUT_MINS env var. Reloading a module rebinds
       EVERY function in it to a new object -- including
       _prediction_kwargs_from_analysis, which main.py had already imported
       once at process-import time and never re-imports. Since
       test_execution_stability.py sorts alphabetically before
       test_prediction_kwargs.py, this reload made main.py's frozen
       reference permanently diverge from order_executor's live one for the
       rest of the session, breaking test_prediction_kwargs.py's
       `main._prediction_kwargs_from_analysis is
       order_executor._prediction_kwargs_from_analysis` identity check (the
       actual regression guard the LOG_PREDICTION KWARGS ASSEMBLY entry
       shipped). Confirmed by hand via git stash/pop: reverting the fix and
       running both files together reproduces the exact CI failure;
       restoring it removes it. Fixed by replacing the reload with
       `monkeypatch.setattr(order_executor, "_GFS_UPDATE_LOCKOUT_MINS", 0)`
       -- the function only reads that one env-derived constant (its
       sibling _GFS_UPDATE_HOURS_UTC is a hardcoded literal, not
       env-derived, so no coverage was lost), matching this suite's own
       dominant convention elsewhere (test_live_execution.py's
       `monkeypatch.setattr(order_executor, "MIN_EDGE", ...)`).
    2. tests/test_trading_gates.py's test_blocks_when_live_trading_not_
       enabled and test_blocks_when_live_trading_env_absent both called
       gate.check() with no client and patched `main.KALSHI_ENV` -- but
       LiveTradingGate.check()'s no-client fallback reads
       os.getenv("KALSHI_ENV") directly (a 2026-07-09 fix, documented in
       the method's own docstring), never touching main.KALSHI_ENV. The
       patch was a pure no-op in this code path. It passed locally only
       because this dev machine's real, gitignored .env sets
       KALSHI_ENV=prod, loaded into the real os.environ via load_dotenv()
       at import time -- GitHub Actions has no .env, so
       os.getenv("KALSHI_ENV", "demo") returned "demo" there, blocking on
       "not prod" before ever reaching the LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED check these
       two tests actually exist to verify. Read all 16 uses of
       patch("main.KALSHI_ENV", ...) in the file before scoping the fix --
       the other 14 either also set the real env var via
       patch.dict(os.environ, _PROD_ENV) (redundant but harmless), pass an
       explicit client (bypassing the os.getenv fallback entirely), or
       deliberately prove a client's base_url overrides a stale env value
       (test_client_base_url_wins_over_stale_kalshi_env_*). Two more
       (test_check_or_raise_raises_when_blocked,
       test_micro_live_blocked_by_gate) are the same no-op pattern but
       happen to still pass on CI because os.getenv's "demo" default
       coincides with the blocked outcome they assert -- fragile but not
       currently broken, left alone. Fixed the two genuinely broken tests
       by moving KALSHI_ENV into their existing patch.dict(os.environ, ...)
       calls, matching the sibling test_blocks_when_not_prod (already
       fixed for this exact reason in an earlier session).
  Independently reviewed (Agent, opus) -- clean. Verified the setattr fix
  loses no coverage (only env-derived constant the function reads), the
  patch.dict `clear=True` site restores every real env var except the one
  intentionally-removed flag (no PATH-clearing risk, and the gate returns
  before ever importing paper.py in that branch), and no pytest-xdist
  parallelism concern (not installed; os.environ mutation wouldn't cross
  worker processes even if it were). Checked every OTHER cross-module
  identity assertion in the suite for the same reload-vs-frozen-import
  vector -- only one structural cousin exists
  (test_backtest.py's backtest._WEATHER_SERIES is wm.KNOWN_WEATHER_SERIES),
  and it self-heals since weather_markets is never reloaded anywhere.

Problem (original framing): N/A -- found and fixed in the same investigation,
  not a pre-logged backlog item.

Why not now: N/A -- fully resolved.

[RESOLVED 2026-07-19] AUTO UN-RETIREMENT -- RETIRED FORECASTING METHODS COULD NEVER GENERATE FRESH RECOVERY EVIDENCE
Priority: Medium -- surfaced by manually un-retiring 'ensemble' on
  2026-07-19 (justified by the letter of the existing rolling-Brier-
  recovery rule) and then investigating, unprompted, why the "recovery"
  looked thin: a direct DB query showed only 1 ensemble prediction logged
  since its 2026-07-10 retirement (an unsettled shadow row from 07-11) --
  the manual un-retirement was real by the rule as written, but the rule
  itself was measuring stale evidence, not genuine recovery.
======================================================

Problem:
  analyze_trade()'s retired-method gate (weather_markets.py, "Retired
  strategy gate" comment) returns None immediately once `method` resolves
  to a currently-retired value -- before log_prediction() or shadow-
  logging (order_executor._log_shadow_predictions, which only ever
  operates on markets that already produced a real analysis dict) can run.
  So a retired method can structurally never generate a new prediction,
  ever, while retired. auto_retire_strategies()'s rolling-Brier "recovery"
  guard (rolling_brier <= threshold skips re-retirement) was built to stop
  a stale lifetime average from masking real improvement, but with zero
  fresh rows possible, "rolling last-20" for a retired method is just
  whatever pre-retirement predictions haven't yet rolled off -- it
  necessarily converges toward "looks recovered" over time regardless of
  whether the method's forecasts have actually gotten any better, purely
  because old bad predictions age out of the window with nothing behind
  them. There was no automatic path back to trading at all -- only the
  manual `python main.py retire-strategies` / unretire_strategy() CLI path
  existed, and even that had no fresh-evidence signal to act on.

What it would look like (built and shipped 2026-07-19):
  An isolated "probation" checker, structurally unable to affect the live
  scan/trading path, that gives a retired method a controlled way to prove
  itself:
  - analyze_trade(enriched, *, bypass_retirement_check=False) --
    weather_markets.py:5546. New keyword-only param (all ~19 real call
    sites are positional, so this is a zero-behavior-change default for
    every one of them); when True, the retired-method gate no longer
    short-circuits, so the full analysis (including Kelly) runs and
    returns a complete dict even for a retired method.
  - is_probation column (tracker.py predictions table, migration v50,
    _SCHEMA_VERSION 49->50) + is_probation param on log_prediction(),
    mirroring is_shadow's exact shape (including the MIN()-based UPSERT
    merge semantics: a later real write always clears it, a probation
    write can never re-flag an already-real row). Kept as its own column
    rather than folded into is_shadow so the probation query stays a
    clean is_probation=1 filter without needing to also exclude ordinary
    shadow rows for other (non-retired) methods.
  - tracker.brier_score_probation_rolling(method, window=20,
    min_samples=15) -- deliberately separate from
    brier_score_by_method_rolling() (which intentionally does NOT filter
    is_probation, since a probation row is a real forecast and should
    feed the live retirement-decision Brier too). The auto-unretirement
    decision specifically needs a signal that's *exclusively* fresh,
    deliberately-generated post-retirement evidence -- otherwise a rolling
    window still mostly full of old pre-retirement rows would look
    "recovered" long before any genuine new evidence exists, which is the
    exact gap this entry is about. Same days_out=0 exclusion via
    multiday_predictions as every other method-level Brier query.
  - weather_markets.check_retirement_probation(client) -- once per day
    (RETIREMENT_PROBATION_PATH state file, same gate shape as
    check_series_drift()/log_city_registry_report()), own try/except,
    never raises, no-ops immediately if nothing is currently retired.
    Samples up to 25 markets (random.sample) via get_weather_markets(client)
    -- 60s-cached, so calling it again right after cron's main scan is
    normally a cache hit -- runs analyze_trade(bypass_retirement_check=True)
    on each, and logs a probation prediction (is_shadow=True,
    is_probation=True) only for markets whose *resolved* method (dynamic
    per-market, not knowable in advance) is currently retired. Then checks
    brier_score_probation_rolling() for every retired method and calls the
    existing tracker.unretire_strategy() the moment it clears
    _PROBATION_UNRETIRE_THRESHOLD=0.25 -- the same bar
    auto_retire_strategies() uses to retire in the first place, not a
    stricter one, because unretire_strategy() already writes a 72h
    re-retirement-immunity pin, which is what actually protects against
    flapping (no separate hysteresis buffer needed).
  - Wired into cron.py right after log_city_registry_report()'s call site,
    same isolation contract (own try/except at the call site too).

  Design decision surfaced to the user rather than guessed: presented 3
  initial auto-unretirement approaches (all rejected -- "rethink these
  options"), then a 4th ("isolated probation checker, completely outside
  the live scan/trading path") was proposed and explicitly approved
  ("yes, that sounds right -- build it") before any code was written.

  Verified end-to-end with real (non-mock-everything) tests: hand-computed
  Brier arithmetic against a seeded temp DB (15 correct probation
  predictions -> Brier exactly 0.01), mutation-tested to confirm the
  is_probation=1 filter and the days_out=0 / non-probation-row exclusions
  are load-bearing (removing the filter measurably polluted the score:
  0.01 -> 0.0706), and 9 new behavioral tests for
  check_retirement_probation() itself (no-op when nothing retired, once-
  per-day gate, never-raises, logs only for markets whose bypass-resolved
  method is retired, auto-unretires only when probation Brier clears
  threshold and not when it's still bad or still None/insufficient-
  samples) -- each mutation-tested by temporarily breaking the guard being
  tested and confirming the corresponding test fails with the predicted
  symptom, then restoring. Also found and fixed a real pre-existing gap in
  tests/test_p0_11_retired_strategy.py's own fixture while writing the new
  bypass tests: _make_enriched() had no title (direction-keyword parsing
  requires one) and an all-identical 12-member ensemble (trips the
  degenerate-ensemble gate) -- both invisible before because none of that
  file's 4 original tests ever needed a non-None result, only new bypass
  tests that actually need Kelly to run exposed them. Full scoped
  regression (test_retirement_probation.py, test_p0_11_retired_strategy.py,
  test_p9_p10.py, test_shadow_predictions.py, test_series_drift.py,
  test_city_registry_report_logging.py, test_tracker.py, plus all 5 cron
  test files) -- 391 passed. ruff + mypy clean on every changed file.

  Independent opus second-opinion review (before push, per standing
  workflow) found no real bugs -- independently re-derived the migration's
  column/placeholder/param counts, independently re-ran
  brier_score_probation_rolling against its own real temp DB, traced all
  ~19 analyze_trade call sites to confirm bypass_retirement_check is inert
  everywhere except check_retirement_probation's own call, and confirmed
  the 72h re-retirement-immunity pin (is_strategy_pinned gate inside
  auto_retire_strategies) is actually wired up to protect against
  flapping. Two low-severity notes, both addressed: (1) is_stale(m) moved
  inside the per-market try/except (weather_markets.py) so a crash there
  (is_stale has a documented history of TypeError on malformed
  volume_fp/open_interest_fp) skips just that one market instead of
  aborting the whole day's probation run; (2) added 5 committed,
  non-mocked integration tests (tests/test_tracker.py
  TestIsProbationColumn) covering the is_probation column round-trip,
  probation-vs-real-row isolation, the min_samples gate, and both
  directions of the MIN() upsert merge -- previously only manually
  mutation-tested during development, not committed as regression
  coverage.

  trading graduation gate itself, not the monthly-rain/snow probability
  models that session was actually shipping). Touching a gate that decides
  whether ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE is allowed to flip on is not something to

[RESOLVED 2026-08-05] STRONG/MED SIGNAL BANNER OVERCLAIMS "PLACING PAPER TRADES" WHEN 0 ACTUALLY GET PLACED

  Observed 2026-08-05 during a `cron` output-analysis session (two live runs
  from worktree trade-flow-graduation-registry-5e826d). Second run
  (20:16:39-20:19:20 UTC) auto-retired the `ensemble` forecasting method
  mid-cycle (Brier 0.2659 > 0.25 threshold, pin expired and NOT
  auto-renewed since directional_accuracy=0.55 < 0.70 renewal bar --
  tracker's strategy_retirement + main.py's pin-renewal check, both working
  as designed, not a bug). trade_cycle.py's "[cron] Scanned 639 market(s)
  -- 11 with edge (strong=2, med=9)" count fed cron.py's console banners
  "!! 2 STRONG SIGNAL(S) -- placing paper trades (cap=$200) !!" and
  "!! 9 MED SIGNAL(S) -- placing paper trades (cap=$20) !!" (cron.py
  ~1458-1475), but paper balance ($1001.44) and open-trade count (7, via
  `paper results`) were IDENTICAL before and after the cycle -- zero trades
  were actually placed. The two candidates visibly caught right after the
  banners (KXLOWTCHI-26AUG06-T69, KXLOWTDC-26AUG06-T76 -- both already-open
  positions from the prior cycle, being re-scored for early-exit) were
  skipped with "method 'ensemble' is retired (Brier 0.2659)"; presumably
  the same fate hit the other 9 candidates silently, with no equivalent
  "[Auto] Skipped N signal(s): <ticker>: <reason>" listing the way the
  earlier hurricane/rain shadow-only batch gets in the same cron output.

  Root cause: cron.py gates the banners on `_placement_was_attempted and
  result.strong_opps` (non-halted/paused/consistency-skipped AND candidate
  list non-empty) -- it does not check `result.placed_strong` /
  `result.placed_med`, the actual counts trade_cycle.run_trade_cycle()
  already returns (cron.py:1447 assigns `placed_count = result.placed_
  strong + result.placed_med` but only uses it later in the Windows toast
  notification, cron.py:1814-1821, which correctly prints "{signals}
  signal(s), {placed_count} placed" when they diverge). The console banner
  has no equivalent fallback and always describes the pre-placement
  candidate count as if it were the outcome.

  Likely trigger: ctx.auto_place_trades() (order_executor._auto_place_
  trades) re-validates each opportunity via analyze_trade() immediately
  before placing (a deliberate stale-price/stale-state guard per existing
  project pattern) -- any candidate whose method got retired between
  analysis and placement (or that fails any other last-moment check)
  silently contributes 0 to placed_strong/placed_med with no per-candidate
  skip reason surfaced at the "[cron]" banner's verbosity level.

  What it would look like: gate the STRONG/MED banners (and/or add a
  follow-up line) on result.placed_strong/placed_med rather than only
  candidate-list emptiness, so operators reading cron output can tell
  "announced N, placed M" the same way the toast notification already can
  -- and ideally surface the per-candidate skip reason (mirroring the
  "[Auto] Skipped" format) when M < N so it's clear WHY, not just that
  fewer were placed than announced.

  Separately worth noting, not filed as its own entry (same root symptom):
  ensemble's retirement means check_early_exits() (cron.py ~1665-1668)
  silently can no longer re-score any open position that was opened under
  the ensemble method for early-exit-on-model-flip -- price-based
  stop-loss/breakeven protection (paper.check_paper_position_exits,
  cron.py ~1579-1609) is unaffected since it doesn't call analyze_trade, so
  this is a monitoring gap on those positions, not an unprotected-position
  gap. (Separately, ensemble was manually un-retired and pinned for 168h
  the same session via `py main.py unretire ensemble --pin 168`, so this
  particular monitoring gap is not currently live.)

  RESOLVED same session: added cron._placement_outcome_phrase(placed,
  found), a pure module-level helper, and wired both banners to it instead
  of a hardcoded "placing paper trades". Deliberately does NOT name a
  specific cause the way this entry's own "What it would look like"
  originally sketched ("pre-placement re-check failed") -- an opus review
  caught that framing as wrong for most real shortfall causes (whole-batch
  skips like a position cap or drawdown pause never even reach a
  per-candidate re-check), so the wording instead points at the existing
  "[Auto] Skipped N signal(s): <ticker>: <reason>" / "[Auto] Position cap
  reached" lines already printed nearby, which already satisfy this
  entry's "ideally surface the per-candidate skip reason" ask -- no new
  plumbing needed there, they already exist for the hurricane/rain
  shadow-only batch and just weren't being pointed to. Also fixed: the
  cap=$ suffix now only prints when something was actually placed against
  it (previously read as a second, contradictory parenthetical when 0 got
  placed); the all-placed case dropped its redundant restated count
  ("placing paper trades", not "placing N paper trade(s)" next to a banner
  that already says N). 4 new tests: a direct unit-test class for
  _placement_outcome_phrase (all-placed/none-found/partial/zero, pure
  function, no cmd_cron cycle needed) plus 2 full-cycle banner tests, one
  of which an opus review caught making an unbound assertion (a swapped

  suite pass; ruff + ruff format + mypy clean on cron.py and the test file.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-07] SIGNAL LABEL DIRECTION IGNORES RECOMMENDED_SIDE

  Found 2026-08-07 while auditing a live cron run's 25 flagged market
  anomalies. weather_markets._edge_label(edge) inferred its "YES"/"NO "
  direction word from the SIGN of whichever edge value it was passed. For
  the "signal" field that's the raw, side-agnostic (blended_prob -
  market_prob) value, whose sign matches recommended_side by construction
  -- fine. But every "net_signal" field (the text trade_cycle.py builds
  into each signal's cache entry, which cron.py then writes to
  data/cron.log and prints in the [cron]/[Auto] console banners)
  is _edge_label(adjusted_edge), where adjusted_edge is a time-decayed
  net_edge -- an EV-per-dollar-of-the-recommended-side figure computed off
  the entry ASK price. net_edge is virtually always POSITIVE for any
  genuinely good trade regardless of which side got recommended (a good NO
  bet has positive expected value exactly like a good YES bet does), so
  _edge_label's sign-as-direction convention systematically mislabeled
  good NO recommendations as "YES". Confirmed live: KXHIGHTSEA-26AUG07-T85
  logged "STRONG BUY YES" (net_edge +0.335) in the same cron cycle that
  order_executor's own validate() correctly computed recommended_side="no"
  and rejected it for raw_edge=-0.1456 < MIN_EDGE=0.15. A full data/
  cron.log audit (excluding the fake-ticker lines from the entry below)
  found an 11,142:833 YES:NO label ratio across 4 months and hundreds of
  cities/dates -- an impossible skew for real weather markets, confirming
  this wasn't a rare corner case but the normal outcome for most real NO
  signals.

  Actual trade placement is unaffected -- _auto_place_trades/
  _validate_trade_opportunity always gates on recommended_side and raw
  edge, never on the text label -- so this was a display/logging-only bug,
  not a live-money or paper-money sizing bug. But it directly misleads any
  operator reading cron console output, data/cron.log, or the web
  dashboard's /api/signals feed about which side the bot actually
  evaluated.

  Fix: _edge_label(edge, side) now takes the caller's already-decided
  recommended_side explicitly and uses IT for the direction word; `edge`'s
  own magnitude (abs()) still drives the STRONG/BUY/WEAK/NEUTRAL tier word,
  unchanged. All 14 call sites across the 7 duplicated analyze-trade paths
  (temperature/precip/snow/hurricane-count/hourly) updated to pass
  rec_side. No test previously asserted on real _edge_label output or a
  real analyze_trade() call's signal/net_signal text (existing tests all
  construct mock analysis dicts with hardcoded net_signal strings), so
  this required new coverage, not just fixing existing assertions: see
  tests/test_weather_markets.py for hand-computed direction-vs-magnitude
  cases including the exact edge>0-but-side=="no" scenario that reproduces
  the original bug.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-07] TEST FIXTURE TICKER LEAKED 467 FAKE SIGNALS INTO PRODUCTION data/cron.log

  Found 2026-08-07 in the same cron-output-analysis session as the entry
  above, while trying to explain a net_edge/recommended_side discrepancy
  that turned out to be unrelated (see above) -- two lines above a real
  cron entry in data/cron.log sat an entry for ticker
  "KXHIGH-NYC-26APR17-B70" (and 4 sibling tickers: -26APR25-B70,
  -26APR26-B70, -26APR17-LIVE, -26APR17-MED), a naming convention that
  never appears anywhere else in this bot's real ticker vocabulary
  ("KXHIGH-NYC-" with an inner hyphen and 3-letter city code, vs every real
  ticker's "KXHIGHNY-"/"KXHIGHTSEA-" style with no inner hyphen), with a
  hardcoded, never-varying net_edge=0.35.

  Root cause: tests/conftest.py has an established pattern (see
  isolate_forecast_ensemble_disk_cache, isolate_crash_log) of redirecting
  every production data-file path a test might write through to tmp_path
  -- except CRON_LOG_PATH was never among them. cron.py's
  _cmd_cron_body() appends one JSONL line straight to the real
  data/cron.log (paths.CRON_LOG_PATH) for every passes_threshold signal;
  7+ test files (test_cron_integration.py, test_cron_group_c.py,
  test_main_cron_smoke.py, etc.) drive cmd_cron()/_cmd_cron_body() through
  a hardcoded "KXHIGH-NYC-26APR17-B70"-ticketed fake market to exercise a
  STRONG-signal scenario -- with no CRON_LOG_PATH isolation, every such
  test run appended straight into the real production file. Same bug
  class as the L4 paths.py migration's forecast_cache.json/crash.log
  incident (both fixed the same way, both discovered live), just a file
  that fix didn't cover. 467 fabricated lines had accumulated from
  2026-04-19 through 2026-08-07 (including entries written minutes before
  this was caught, from a pytest run mid-session) out of ~12,442 total --
  and this is the exact file web_app.py's /api/signals endpoint reads
  for the live dashboard, so the dashboard's signal history has been
  showing fake data mixed with real for 4 months.

  Fix: new tests/conftest.py autouse fixture isolate_cron_log redirects
  both cron.CRON_LOG_PATH and web_app.CRON_LOG_PATH (two separate
  module-level bindings of the same paths.py constant) to a per-test
  tmp_path file -- a synchronous open()/write() inside _cmd_cron_body(),
  not an atexit-deferred buffer, so no pytest_sessionfinish companion is
  needed the way isolate_forecast_ensemble_disk_cache required one. The
  467 already-contaminated lines were removed from the real data/cron.log
  (backup kept at data/cron.log.pre-cleanup-backup-2026-08-07) after
  confirming every removed line matched the fake ticker pattern exactly
  and zero were JSON-parse failures needing manual review.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-07] STRONG/MED TIER CLASSIFICATION AND FINAL PLACEMENT VALIDATION USE DIFFERENT, DISAGREEING EDGE MEASURES
Priority: Medium -- no live-money impact and not a correctness bug in
  isolation (both thresholds are individually defensible), but distorts
  every cycle's announced STRONG/MED signal counts against what can
  actually place, and reconciling it is a real trading-behavior decision
  that needs before/after count data, not a quick fix.

  Surfaced 2026-08-07 while fixing the signal-label bug above (same root
  data, different problem -- the label fix does NOT address this).
  trade_cycle.py classifies a candidate into TIER_STRONG/TIER_MED using
  abs(adjusted_edge) against eff_strong_edge/MED_EDGE, where adjusted_edge
  is net_edge (EV-per-dollar-of-the-recommended-side, priced off the entry
  ASK, fee-adjusted) times a time-decay factor. order_executor.py's
  _validate_trade_opportunity, the gate every candidate must clear
  immediately before placement, instead checks raw `edge`
  (blended_prob - market_prob, priced off the market MID, no fee/ask
  adjustment) against a completely different threshold (MIN_EDGE) and a
  sign-consistency check against recommended_side. These are legitimately
  different quantities -- net_edge answers "is this bet worth taking at
  the price I'd actually pay," raw edge answers "how much does my
  probability estimate disagree with the market's" -- and nothing here
  says one of the two thresholds is simply wrong. But because a candidate
  only needs to clear the net_edge-based bar to be announced as a STRONG
  or MED signal, and a different, unrelated raw-edge bar to actually get
  placed, some fraction of every cycle's announced STRONG/MED count is
  structurally unable to place regardless of price/timing luck -- not a
  marginal, "edge decayed between scan and placement" miss, the same
  category of miscount cron.py's own "[cron] filter breakdown" line
  already reports for other gates. Live example from the same cron cycle
  that surfaced the label bug: 3 STRONG signals announced, 1 placed;
  KXHIGHTSEA-26AUG07-T85 was one of the 2 that couldn't have placed at any
  price because its raw edge (-0.1456) never cleared MIN_EDGE (0.15),
  independent of its net_edge (+0.335) qualifying it for STRONG in the
  first place.

  Not fixed this session -- deliberately deferred per explicit user
  decision (2026-08-07): reconciling which quantity governs tier
  classification (or requiring both to agree) is a real trading-behavior
  change on a live paper account, not a display fix, and needs its own
  dedicated review rather than being bundled into the label-bug fix above.

  What it would look like: decide whether STRONG/MED classification
  should require the SAME edge quantity validate() checks (raw edge vs
  MIN_EDGE) -- which would shrink announced STRONG/MED counts to only
  what can actually place -- or keep two independent bars but make that
  explicit in the console banners (e.g. distinguish "N found, M
  clear-to-place" the way the [Auto] skip lines already do per-candidate,
  just aggregated). Whichever direction, needs before/after STRONG/MED
  count data across a representative window to judge the real-world size
  of the effect before changing live gating thresholds.

  Resolved 2026-08-07: re-read the entry's own ambiguous "before/after"
  phrasing first -- could have meant before/after this fix or before/after
  the label-bug fix above. Confirmed it can only mean the former: the
  label fix was display-only (net_signal text) and never touched tier
  classification or net_edge/edge, so any before/after comparison
  straddling it would be identical on both sides -- not the meaningful
  size-of-effect data the entry was actually asking for. Checked whether
  that data was even retroactively obtainable from data/cron.log: it
  isn't -- cron.py's JSONL write only ever persisted {ts, ticker, signal,
  net_edge, city} per line, never market_prob/forecast_prob/side/raw
  edge, so no historical reconstruction of "how many STRONG/MED signals
  would have failed the raw-edge gate" is possible from existing logs.

  Chose option (a) (require the same edge quantity validate() checks) over
  option (b) (dual-bar transparency only) after determining option (a) is
  NOT actually the trading-behavior risk the entry assumed it was: every
  candidate this gate removes from STRONG/MED was ALREADY unconditionally
  rejected by validate() before this fix -- the gate change only stops
  mislabeling dead-on-arrival candidates as actionable, it never changes
  which trades place. That makes the "gather before/after data first"
  caution inapplicable here (there's no risk/reward tradeoff to size),
  though the caution remains sound in general for genuine threshold
  changes -- see the follow-up entry below for one that still needs it.

  Fix: trade_cycle.py's per-candidate tier-assignment block (search
  "_clears_placement_gate") now requires TWO of order_executor.py's
  _validate_trade_opportunity gates to also pass before a candidate earns
  TIER_STRONG/TIER_MED: (1) net_edge must be positive, (2) raw `edge`
  (blended_prob - market_prob, side-agnostic, priced off the market MID)
  must agree in sign with recommended_side and clear MIN_EDGE in
  magnitude. Both are skipped/defaulted-to-passing under the same guards
  validate() itself uses (missing "edge" key = passes). New
  dbg["placement_gate"] counter and matching cron.py "[cron] filter
  breakdown" field report how many otherwise-qualifying candidates this
  gate now excludes, going forward (the exact "N found, M clear-to-place"
  visibility option (b) would have added, now folded into option (a)'s
  own diagnostics instead of a separate dual-bar banner).

  Deliberately NOT mirrored despite being equally real and opus-review-
  caught -- see the new follow-up entry below for both:
  (1) validate()'s ci_adjusted_kelly/fee_adjusted_kelly >= 0.002 floor --
      omitted because every existing STRONG/MED-tier test fixture across
      this suite hand-builds its analysis dict without ever setting
      kelly (defaults to 0.0, which would fail the floor), a materially
      larger and harder-to-fully-audit blast radius than this fix's own
      scope given this suite's separate pre-existing test-hang issues.
  (2) validate()'s confidence-tiered/A-B-test min_edge check -- omitted
      because it's provably subsumed today (edge_confidence() always
      discounts, never amplifies, so a tiered candidate's net_edge is
      always >= its adjusted_edge >= MED_EDGE, which is >= every
      confidence-tier/AB-test threshold that exists at current env
      values) but that subsumption is a real dependency on MED_EDGE
      staying >= those thresholds, not a general guarantee.

  Also still real after this fix, not addressed: trade_cycle.py's
  dashboard "stars" rating and main.py's watch-mode alert_strong_signal
  both key off `"STRONG" in signal` text (from _edge_label, driven by
  adjusted_edge magnitude alone), never off the `tier` field this fix
  gates -- so a candidate this fix untiers can still show 2-3 stars on
  the dashboard or fire watch's desktop STRONG alert. Pre-existing
  decoupling, not introduced by this fix, but means this fix only
  partially closes the "announced as actionable but can't place" gap;
  the stars/alert paths would need their own pass to read `tier` instead
  of re-deriving from signal text.

  4 new tests reproducing the exact live shape (net_edge<=0 while
  adjusted_edge still qualifies; the actual KXHIGHTSEA incident's
  side="no" magnitude failure; the sign-mismatch and boundary cases) plus
  a 5th cross-check test class (TestPlacementGateMirrorsValidateOpportunity)
  that feeds the same analysis dict through both run_trade_cycle() and the
  real _validate_trade_opportunity() and asserts a tiered candidate always
  clears validate()'s own edge gates -- added specifically because 4
  one-directional assertions on trade_cycle's own gate can't catch future
  drift between it and the function it mirrors, a gap opus review flagged
  directly. Each new deterministic check individually mutation-tested
  (temporarily disabled, confirmed the corresponding test fails with the
  exact live-incident console output reproduced, restored).

  Independent opus review (effort=high), all findings fixed or explicitly
  deferred with reasoning recorded above:
  - HIGH: first draft mirrored only the raw-edge block and missed
    validate()'s net_edge<=0 check immediately above it -- a real,
    reproducible gap (a wide bid/ask spread can produce negative net_edge
    while adjusted_edge, which preserves sign but is compared via abs(),
    still qualifies for a tier). Fixed.
  - MEDIUM (x3): Kelly floor unmirrored (deferred, see above); MIN_EDGE
    imported at module level instead of function-local like
    order_executor's own pattern, going stale after a live Settings-
    screen edit (fixed -- moved to local import); the original comment's
    reasoning for skipping the confidence-tier/AB-test gate incorrectly
    called pick_variant() "stateful" (it isn't -- ab_test.py only mutates
    state in record_outcome(), called on settlement) -- corrected to the
    real, numeric domination argument instead.
  - LOW (x4, all addressed): missing side="no" test coverage reproducing
    the actual incident shape (added); no cross-check test binding the
    mirror to its source (added, see above); stale require_liquid_for_
    placement docstring still describing pre-fix tier semantics (fixed);
    no dbg counter for the new gate the way every other gate in that loop
    has one (added, plus cron.py banner). A 6th finding
    (order_executor._validate_trade_opportunity crashes with TypeError if
    opp["edge"] is present but explicitly None, rather than absent) is a
    separate, pre-existing, currently-unreachable bug in a different
    function -- filed as its own standalone follow-up rather than fixed
    here.
  - Also reviewer-caught in passing (not a defect, a process note): while
    investigating why the full test file wouldn't run to completion for
    its own verification, the review agent found and fixed 2 pre-existing
    test hangs (unmocked trade_cycle._run_batch_prewarm making real
    network calls from engine_env/cron_env fixtures) -- see commits
    0c31fdd and 4fbcdfd, same session.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-07] PRELOAD_ALL CAN PERMANENTLY TRUNCATE forecast_sigma.json TO ONE CITY ON A PARTIAL CALL
Priority: Medium -- not a live-money bug (this only affects the sigma-based
  dynamic forecast adjustment, which degrades to the static _HISTORICAL_SIGMA
  table on failure, not a crash or a wrong trade) but a real, currently-
  reachable correctness gap that silently degrades exactly the cities this
  feature was built to help (LasVegas/NewOrleans/StPetersburg, absent from
  the static table).

  Found 2026-08-07 (opus-review-caught) while migrating climatology.py's
  _sigma_mem_cache onto ForecastCache with a constant cache key -- the
  migration itself doesn't cause this, an identical exposure existed with
  the old plain dict, since the bug lives at the disk-file layer, not the
  in-memory caching layer.

  climatology.load_all_sigmas(city_coords, force=...) computes and
  unconditionally overwrites data/forecast_sigma.json with a table built
  from EXACTLY the city_coords dict it's given -- there is no merge with
  whatever the file already contained. preload_all(city_coords) (also
  climatology.py) calls load_all_sigmas(city_coords, force=True) with
  whatever subset it itself received, gated only on "does forecast_sigma.json
  exist yet / is it stale" -- NOT on whether city_coords is the complete
  registry. main.py's first-run setup wizard (~line 4603) calls
  preload_all({city: CITY_COORDS[city]}) in a per-city loop (so progress can
  be reported one city at a time). On a fresh install: iteration 1 (say NYC)
  finds no forecast_sigma.json, computes+writes a table containing ONLY NYC,
  and memoizes it. Iterations 2..21 now see a file that exists and is fresh
  (_SIGMA_CACHE_AGE = 30 days), so the guard is false and load_all_sigmas is
  never called again for the wizard's remaining 20 cities. The real,
  multi-city table is never built until something else forces a recompute
  (force=True, or the file going stale a month later) -- for that whole
  window, weather_markets.get_historical_sigma() silently falls through to
  the static table for every city but NYC, and LasVegas/NewOrleans/
  StPetersburg (absent from the static table entirely) fall through further
  to _DEFAULT_SIGMA.

  Not fixed this session -- deliberately out of scope for the cache migration
  that surfaced it (a different subsystem: main.py's setup wizard's call
  pattern, not climatology.py's caching internals) and needs a real design
  decision, not a mechanical fix.

  What it would look like: pick one of -- (a) change the wizard to call
  preload_all() once with the FULL city registry at the end instead of
  per-city (loses the existing per-city progress messages unless those move
  elsewhere); (b) make load_all_sigmas() merge into the existing file's
  per-city entries instead of unconditionally overwriting the whole table;
  (c) gate preload_all()'s sigma-refresh block on city_coords actually being
  the complete registry (e.g. compare len() against the real city count)
  rather than just file-existence/staleness. Needs a decision on which
  tradeoff is acceptable before implementing.

  RESOLVED 2026-08-07. Re-verified against live code first (confirmed 21
  cities via CITY_COORDS, confirmed the exact mechanism, confirmed the
  wizard call site at main.py:4652). User chose (b) via AskUserQuestion,
  explicitly ruling out (c) because weather_markets.py already imports
  climatology.py at module level, so climatology importing CITY_COORDS back
  would be a real circular import (the only alternatives -- a lazy import or
  a hardcoded city-count constant -- were rejected as fragile/stale-prone).

  (b) alone turned out to be INSUFFICIENT: live-simulating the wizard's
  per-city loop with only the merge fix applied showed forecast_sigma.json
  still stuck at NYC-only, because preload_all()'s own gate
  (file-exists-and-fresh) blocks the call to load_all_sigmas() entirely
  after city 1 writes the file -- the merge logic never even runs for
  cities 2..21. Caught this via a live probe script before proposing a
  fix, corrected the design with the user (still self-contained in
  climatology.py, no main.py changes): added
  _sigma_cache_missing_cities() and gated preload_all()'s sigma-refresh
  block on it too, so a per-city call keeps triggering load_all_sigmas()
  until every requested city is actually present. Re-verified live with
  the same probe -- file now accumulates NYC -> NYC+LasVegas ->
  NYC+LasVegas+NewOrleans across sequential per-city calls.

  Independent opus review (effort=high) of that combined fix then found 4
  more real gaps, all fixed: (1) load_all_sigmas()'s own force=False fast
  path -- the ACTUAL live cron/trading path via
  weather_markets._load_dynamic_sigma(), which never goes through
  preload_all() at all -- had the identical missing-city blind spot, so
  the original bug class still reached production; (2) non-dict JSON
  content (null, [], ...) in forecast_sigma.json crashed instead of
  degrading gracefully; (3) a transient compute failure (empty result)
  could silently overwrite a city's real existing entry with an empty one,
  and an empty entry was never retried since key-presence alone counted as
  "satisfied"; (4) a pre-existing module comment flatly contradicted the
  new merge behavior. 2 LOW findings (per-city staleness not tracked --
  whole-file mtime granularity means a partial write for city X makes city
  Y's actually-stale entry look fresh; orphan entries for cities removed
  from the registry are never pruned) were deliberately left as documented
  residuals rather than fixed -- both need a cache-schema change
  (per-city timestamps) for marginal benefit given today's only partial
  caller (the wizard) runs once per install.

  tests/test_climatology.py: 3 new test classes (TestLoadAllSigmasMerge,
  TestPreloadAllSigmaGate, TestSigmaCacheRobustness), 19 new tests total
  covering the merge, the gate, the live-path fast-path fix, non-dict-JSON
  handling, and the empty-entry-doesn't-clobber/doesn't-stick-forever
  behavior. Every fix individually mutation-tested (reverted, confirmed the
  corresponding test fails, restored) before committing. 40/40 tests pass,
  92 tests in 3 dependent files (test_city_registry_manifest.py,
  test_gaussian_prob.py, test_p1_remaining.py) still pass, lint/mypy clean.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-07] 12 test_weather_markets.py TESTS FAILED INTERMITTENTLY DEPENDING ON LOCAL TIME-OF-DAY

  "analyze_trade returned None"). Re-verified against live state rather
  than trusting the failure alone: ran the 12 tests once while local
  system time was Aug 6 evening (US Eastern) and UTC was already Aug 7 --
  all 12 failed. The system clock then rolled past local midnight; re-ran
  the identical 12 tests immediately after with zero code changes -- all
  12 passed. This proved the tests were never actually broken by any of
  this session's earlier edits (climatology.py, conftest.py); they're
  flaky against real-world local time-of-day, and were failing at the
  exact moment the user happened to ask about them.

  Root cause: these 12 tests build their enriched-market fixture's
  "_date" field via `tomorrow = date.today() + timedelta(days=1)` --
  LOCAL timezone. weather_markets.py's analyze_trade() computes
  `days_out = max(0, (target_date - datetime.now(UTC).date()).days)` --
  UTC. Whenever the local wall-clock date lags UTC's (true for any
  US timezone from roughly 8pm-midnight local, when UTC has already
  rolled to the next calendar day), local "tomorrow" collides with UTC
  "today", so days_out evaluates to 0 instead of the intended 1 --
  silently routing into analyze_trade's same-day-only branch (`if
  days_out == 0 and condition.get("type") != "between": live_obs =
  get_live_observation(...)`), which none of the 12 tests mocked. That
  branch's obs_override then takes 55-95% of the blend weight (scaled by
  local hour), so it dominates blended_prob with today's REAL live NYC
  temperature reading -- in August, a near-certainty that high > 72°F
  (observed: model=0.96), which diverges from the tests' fixed
  market-price assumption (0.67) by more than analyze_trade's own
  model_mkt_gap rejection threshold (0.25), returning None. Not a novel
  bug class: two existing tests in this same file
  (test_metar_locked_trade_has_ecmwf_forecast_mean_keys,
  test_metar_locked_trade_has_nbm_quantile_prob_key) already carry
  comments describing this exact "system-local-behind-UTC" failure mode
  and already use datetime.now(UTC).date() as their fix; a third
  (test_model_consensus_false_when_models_disagree) independently
  discovered the same bug and fixed it a different way (mocking
  get_live_observation directly) -- this anti-pattern has now recurred
  and been independently rediscovered 3 times in one file.

  Fixed at all 9 code sites containing the exact `tomorrow = date.today()
  + timedelta(days=1)` snippet (matches the file's own established fix:
  use datetime.now(UTC).date(), not the alternate mock-get_live_
  observation pattern) -- both sides of the days_out comparison now read
  the same UTC clock, so the skew is impossible by construction rather
  than merely narrowed. One further occurrence
  (TestMosBlendNoCrossVariableFallback._enriched_low_market) was
  deliberately left unfixed after verifying its own tests already mock
  get_live_observation directly, so it isn't exposed regardless.

  Independent opus review (effort=high), findings addressed:
  - MEDIUM: analyze_trade's same-day branch isn't the only unmocked live-
    observation path -- weather_markets._compute_persistence_prob does
    its own function-local `from nws import get_live_observation as
    _get_live_obs`, called whenever days_out <= 1 (so a CORRECTLY-computed
    days_out=1, after this fix, still reaches it). This bypasses
    `monkeypatch.setattr(wm, "get_live_observation", ...)` entirely, since
    the function-local import re-resolves nws.get_live_observation at
    call time, independent of whatever name weather_markets.py's own
    module-level import was bound to. Confirmed live via a real spy: 13
    tests were making real network calls to mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/
    api.weather.gov through this exact path, one of which returned live
    NYC weather (84°F, light rain) feeding a real 15% blend weight into
    persistence_p. Not currently causing failures (stress-tested with
    40°F and 110°F forced values, 231/231 still passed either way) but a
    real hermeticity gap. Fixed by adding
    monkeypatch.setattr("nws.get_live_observation", lambda *a, **kw:
    None) alongside the existing wm.get_live_observation mock at all 9
    sites, matching the pattern TestMosBlendNoCrossVariableFallback
    already used for both.
  - LOW: one of the 9 copy-pasted explanatory comments (on
    test_model_consensus_false_when_models_disagree) falsely claimed
    "this test doesn't mock [get_live_observation]" and "failed exactly
    this way" -- that test already mocked it and was never one of the 12
    failures. Rewritten to state the true (defense-in-depth, not a live
    exposure) reasoning for that specific site.
  - LOW: 2 of the 9 sites are shared DATA-only helper functions
    (_analyze_trade_enriched_fixture, _ecmwf_gap_test_enriched) used by 3
    tests each, not tests themselves -- "this test failed" had no
    referent there. Reworded to name the actual failing callers and the
    shared setup helper (_analyze_trade_base_mocks/_stub_ecmwf_gap_common)
    where the corresponding get_live_observation mocks now live.
  - LOW: redundant `from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta` at all
    9 sites -- UTC is already imported at module level (line 11).
    Simplified to `from datetime import datetime, timedelta`.
  - LOW (verified, not changed): confirmed the other ~19 date.today()
    occurrences elsewhere in this file use timedelta(days=3)/days=5, not
    days=1 -- real UTC-offset skew is always under 24h, so those can
    shift days_out by at most 1 in either direction and can never
    collapse to exactly 0 the way a days=1 "tomorrow" can. Spot-checked:
    of the 14 remaining date.today() sites, only 2 (this entry's fixed
    ones aside) even reach analyze_trade at all; the rest build cache
    keys or call already-mocked functions directly. Also verified
    test_analyze_trade_accepts_today_and_future (uses date.today() +
    timedelta(days=0 or 1) but only asserts analyze_trade doesn't raise,
    explicitly tolerating a None result either way) is genuinely
    unaffected regardless of the same local/UTC skew.
  - LOW, not fixed (informational): reviewer noted the comment block is
    duplicated verbatim across 8 of the 9 sites (~90 lines for what could
    be one canonical explanation + short pointers) -- left as-is, purely
    stylistic, not a correctness issue.
  - LOW, not fixed (informational, deliberately deferred): no test in
    this file guards against date.today() + timedelta(days=1) reappearing
    in test_weather_markets.py itself (weather_markets.py's own
    TestUtcTodayDate::test_no_date_today_calls_remain only source-scans
    production code, not test code) -- this exact anti-pattern was
    independently rediscovered 3 times in this one file before this
    session. A narrowly-scoped guard flagging that specific literal
    string in test_weather_markets.py (allowlisting the one confirmed-
    safe TestMosBlendNoCrossVariableFallback occurrence) would stop a
    4th recurrence, but isn't added now -- designing it correctly without
    false-flagging the confirmed-safe days=3/days=5 sites is a real,
    separate task, not a one-line fix.

  Full regression: test_weather_markets.py 231 passed / 4 skipped / 0
  failed (was 219/4/12 before); broader sweep (test_infrastructure.py,
  test_phase2_batch_m.py, test_hurricane_climatology.py,
  test_p1_remaining.py, test_climatology.py) 389 passed / 4 skipped / 0

  Independent opus review: given the size (17 files, ~2000 lines), scoped to
  3 parallel Agent(opus, effort=high) passes by subsystem (climatology math;
  ticker-parsing/dispatch; safety-guard wiring across main.py/paper.py/
  order_executor.py/consistency.py/tracker.py/ml_bias.py/calibration.py),
  mirroring both sibling models' own precedent -- then a 2nd round on the
  climatology-math file alone once the 1st round's CRITICAL finding forced a
  real redesign, since the other 2 reviewers were reading the file mid-fix.

  1 CRITICAL finding, round 1: first_hurricane_position()'s original
  implementation used HURDAT2's raw storm-ID embedded sequence number (e.g.
  "AL062026" -> 6) as the position, on the false premise that it equals a
  storm's rank among that season's real NAMED storms. Verified against the
  real cached Atlantic file: 27 of 30 window years contain at least one
  UNNAMED system (unnamed tropical depressions/subtropical storms, spelled-
  out-number placeholder names like "ELEVEN"/"TWENTY-ONE") consuming a
  sequence number with no name of its own, and 3 years have literal ID gaps
  -- both of which shift every later name's raw ID away from its real name-
  index. Measured to mis-rank 11 of 30 window years and shift ~10 percentage
  points of probability mass between positions -- a 2x mispricing on a
  market whose fair values live in the 3-33% band, larger than any edge
  threshold this bot trades on. Fixed round 1: filter out UNNAMED/placeholder
  systems, then sort the remainder by ID sequence number.

  That round-1 fix was itself caught incomplete by the SAME reviewer's 2nd
  pass (requested once the other 2 reviewers' own findings implied the fix
  needed re-checking): named storms are not always even in real ID order --
  HURDAT2 IDs are assigned by post-season REANALYZED genesis order, NHC
  names are assigned in REAL TIME, and the two genuinely diverge in at least
  6 of the last 30 years (2007, 2012, 2019, 2021 KATE/JULIAN, 2022
  IAN/HERMINE, 2023 GERT/EMILY/FRANKLIN). Independently re-verified live
  against the cached file. Fixed round 2: sort named storms ALPHABETICALLY
  by name instead of by ID sequence number -- not a proxy or heuristic,
  alphabetical assignment IS what "NHC naming order" definitionally means,
  and it reproduces the real list exactly in every one of the 6 divergent
  years (re-verified live). Known, accepted limitation: does not handle the
  rare Greek-letter/WMO-supplementary-name overflow for a >21-storm season
  (2020 only, in the 30-year window) -- immaterial for this model's real use
  (KXFIRSTHURRICANE only ever asks about the 21 regular names; a season's
  first hurricane landing on an overflow name at all is a vanishingly rare
  edge case, and _parse_storm_order_condition already fails closed for any
  name outside the known 21 either way).

  1 HIGH finding: the sample-floor fallback (< 15 eligible years -> revert
  to unconditional, same shape the next-event model's own review already
  established) had no matching short-circuit for a position that is
  DEFINITIVELY eliminated (its own name's KXHURRICANENAMES market has
  already settled "no", meaning NHC has fully stopped reporting on that
  storm -- confirmed via the real HURCAT contract-terms PDF's own expiration
  clause that a "no" settlement requires the storm to be completely
  resolved, never merely "currently active"). Measured against real
  Atlantic data: the eligible-year count after conditioning drops below the
  15-sample floor for essentially every M>=2 (a typical season reaches 2
  named storms by ~late June), so without a short-circuit the fallback would
  silently reset an already-eliminated position back to its FULL
  unconditional climatological probability -- e.g. position 2 getting 33%
  instead of ~0% against a market correctly pricing it near-zero, a
  confident wrong answer, not just a less-sharp one. Fixed: added an
  explicit `position <= storms_named_so_far` short-circuit to 0.01/degenerate
  CI, checked BEFORE the sample-floor fallback, mirroring
  _analyze_hurricane_next_event_trade's own occurred_this_season=True
  shortcut.

  2 MEDIUM findings fixed: (1) the season_year/close_time cross-check used
  the sibling count-model parser's +-1 tolerance, copied without noticing
  that here season_year DETERMINES `position` (indexes
  _ATLANTIC_STORM_NAMES_BY_SEASON) rather than merely keying a cache lookup
  the way it does for the count model -- tightened to an exact match, since
  this function's own docstring already asserts these markets never span a
  year boundary. (2) the new storms_named cache field's writer (extending
  refresh_hurricane_count_to_date) and reader (_get_cached_storms_named_
  to_date) had zero real round-trip test coverage -- every _analyze_storm_
  order_trade test monkeypatched the reader directly, so a field-name typo
  or a dropped write would have degraded silently to storms_named_so_far=0
  forever with only a debug-level log line. Added real (non-monkeypatched)
  writer->JSON-file->reader tests.

  Several LOW findings also fixed: _CONDITION_CONFIDENCE, is_storm_order_
  ticker exact-membership, and the storms_named_so_far diagnostic being
  silently overwritten by the sample-floor fallback (split into a separate
  storms_named_so_far_raw field so shadow logs can tell "no live signal
  existed" apart from "a live signal existed and was discarded") -- plus
  test-quality fixes: a vacuous CI-reuse test that never actually exercised
  bootstrap_ci_next_event's resampling path (the 5-outcome fixture always
  hit its <15-sample degenerate-CI early return), an untested placeholder-
  name-filtering branch (fixture only covered the literal "UNNAMED" spelling,
  not spelled-out-number placeholders like "FOUR" -- genuinely load-bearing
  on real data, e.g. 2017), and a fixture-construction bug self-caught before
  even reaching review: the first fixture draft reused the sibling models'
  "UNNAMED" placeholder-name convention for every storm, which -- once the
  CRITICAL fix started filtering UNNAMED systems -- silently emptied every
  single fixture season.

Independent opus review also confirmed CLEAN (no gaps found) across: every
  one of the 4 main.py call sites got both required changes (own refuse
  block + blanket-exclusion extension) with the correct variable name in
  each; order_executor's shadow-routing branch (mutation-tested: disabling
  the guard produces a real placed order in the test); consistency.py's
  exclusion (also mutation-tested, including a 2nd test using an adversarial
  ticker shape since the real KXFIRSTHURRICANE ticker shape can't reach
  _parse_threshold's regex regardless of the guard -- same "not actually
  mutation-proof" gap the next-event entry's own review already fixed once,
  closed here from the start); all 5 tracker.py raw-SQL exclusion tuples;
  all 3 ml_bias.py and 1 calibration.py tuples; the season-count/next-event/
  storm-order gates' mutual independence.

What this does NOT do:
  KXHURCAT (per-storm category) remains completely untouched -- still
  blocked by is_hurricane_ticker()'s blanket guard, no model; needs a new
  live per-storm NHC forecast/advisory pipeline, a genuinely bigger and more
  novel build than this session's, per the user's own AskUserQuestion
  decision. Per-city landfall markets remain 0 open (unchanged). Real sizing
  stays shadow/log-only until STORM_ORDER_TRADING_ENABLED=1 AND >=20 distinct
  settled predictions exist for this shape specifically. Does not handle the
  Greek-letter/WMO-supplementary-name overflow case for a >21-storm season
  (see the CRITICAL finding's own "known, accepted limitation" note above).

When to revisit:
  - Once STORM_ORDER_TRADING_ENABLED is set and >=20 distinct settled
    predictions accumulate -- check get_signal_graduation_report()-style
    correlation before ever relying on real sizing. This shape settles once
    per name per season (up to 21 opportunities/season across 21 names,

  - KXHURCAT: see the parent entries' own "When to revisit" -- unchanged by

  1. Kelly floor (ci_adjusted_kelly, falling back to fee_adjusted_kelly,

     STRONG/MED-tier-qualifying test fixture across the whole suite that
     currently hand-builds its analysis dict without setting kelly (which
     defaults to 0.0 and would fail the floor) -- confirmed present in at
     least tests/test_trade_cycle_engine.py's _strong_market_analysis/
     _med_market_analysis and tests/test_cron_integration.py's
     fake_analysis, likely more not yet found. This suite also has (had,
     as of this session -- see the 2 hang-fix commits above) pre-existing

     run_trade_cycle()/cmd_cron()/cmd_watch() with a mocked analyze_trade
     result for STRONG/MED-tier-qualifying analysis dicts, add a realistic
     ci_adjusted_kelly to each that's missing one, THEN add the mirror
     check to trade_cycle.py, confirming nothing regresses.

  2. Confidence-tiered/A-B-test min_edge (utils.get_min_edge_for_confidence
     + order_executor._MIN_EDGE_AB_TEST.pick_variant()). Provably subsumed
     at CURRENT env values: edge_confidence() in weather_markets.py always
     returns a factor in (0, 1] (horizon discount x per-condition
     discount, both <= 1.0), so adjusted_edge = net_edge * edge_confidence
     never exceeds net_edge in magnitude -- a candidate tiered via
     abs(adjusted_edge) >= MED_EDGE therefore always has abs(net_edge) >=
     MED_EDGE too. MED_EDGE defaults to 0.15, which is >= every
     confidence-tier threshold in utils._EDGE_TIERS (max 0.15, the LOW-
     confidence live tier) and every _MIN_EDGE_AB_TEST variant (max 0.09).
     This is a real numeric dependency, not a structural guarantee -- if
     MED_EDGE is ever lowered via env override below the highest
     confidence-tier/AB-test threshold, this gap reopens silently with no
     test currently guarding it. What it would look like: either (a) add
     a regression test asserting MED_EDGE >= max(_EDGE_TIERS values,
     _MIN_EDGE_AB_TEST variant values) so a future env/constant change
     that breaks the domination fails loudly instead of silently, which
     is cheap and doesn't require touching trade_cycle.py's runtime logic
     at all, or (b) actually thread `live` through run_trade_cycle's
     candidate loop and call get_min_edge_for_confidence for real (leaving
     the AB-test variant unmirrored regardless, since pick_variant()'s
     random tie-breaking makes a second call at classification time
     genuinely nondeterministic relative to the real call at placement
     time -- not stateful/consuming as an earlier draft of the resolved
     entry above incorrectly reasoned, but still not safely reproducible
     twice for the same candidate).

[RESOLVED 2026-08-08] DASHBOARD STARS + WATCH-MODE STRONG ALERT KEY OFF SIGNAL TEXT, NOT THE tier FIELD
Priority: Low -- cosmetic/notification-only, not a placement-path bug. A
  candidate untiered by validate()'s gates still can't actually get placed
  (strong_opps/med_opps membership is gated on `tier`, not on this text) --
  the only consequence is a misleading star rating or an unwarranted desktop
  alert.

Problem:
  Filed 2026-08-08 as an explicit follow-up, surfaced by the same opus
  review that produced both the "[RESOLVED 2026-08-08] STRONG/MED TIER:
  REMAINING VALIDATE() GATES NOT MIRRORED..." and "[RESOLVED 2026-08-08]
  _validate_trade_opportunity() HAS 2 MORE LATENT None-VALUE CRASH SITES..."
  entries above, deliberately kept out of scope for both (genuinely separate
  concern: display/notification, not the placement gate itself).

  Two sites key off `"STRONG" in signal`-style text instead of the `tier`
  field trade_cycle.py's classification loop actually assigns:
  - trade_cycle.py's dashboard "stars" rating (~line 696-703 as of
    2026-08-08): `stars = "★★★" if passes_threshold and "STRONG" in
    signal and time_risk == "LOW" else "★★" if passes_threshold and
    "STRONG" in signal else "★" if passes_threshold else ""` -- `signal` is
    `analysis.get("net_signal", analysis.get("signal", ""))`, driven by
    adjusted_edge magnitude alone (weather_markets.py's _edge_label), with
    no awareness of whether the candidate actually cleared any of
    validate()'s placement gates (raw-edge sign/magnitude, net_edge sign,
    Kelly floor, confidence-tiered min_edge -- all now mirrored into `tier`
    as of the two entries above).
  - main.py's watch-mode auto-trade STRONG desktop alert (~line 3548 as of
    2026-08-08): `if "STRONG" in _cw_alert_analysis.get("net_signal", "")
    and _cw_alert_ticker not in previous: alert_strong_signal(...)` -- same
    text-based check, independent of `tier`.

  Net effect: a candidate that trade_cycle.py's classification loop now
  correctly leaves `tier=None` (because it fails the raw-edge, net_edge,
  Kelly-floor, or confidence-tier placement gate) can still show 2-3 stars
  on the dashboard and still fire watch's desktop "STRONG signal" alert --
  both read as "this is a real, placeable STRONG/MED opportunity" to an
  operator, when validate() would actually reject it. Not a live-money risk
  (placement itself is correctly gated on `tier`), but misleading UX/
  notification surface that could waste an operator's attention or erode
  trust in the STRONG alert.

  What it would look like: change both sites to read
  `analysis.get("tier") == trade_cycle.TIER_STRONG` /
  `analysis.get("tier") == trade_cycle.TIER_MED` instead of re-deriving from
  `signal`/`net_signal` text. For the dashboard stars, this changes the
  3-tier "★★★/★★/★" ladder to key off (tier==STRONG and
  time_risk==LOW) / (tier==STRONG or tier==MED) / passes_threshold instead
  of the current (STRONG-text and LOW risk) / STRONG-text / passes_threshold

  ```
  def _rating(net_edge: float, risk: str) -> str:
      ae = abs(net_edge)
      if ae >= STRONG_EDGE and risk != "HIGH":  return green("★★★")
      elif ae >= 0.12:                          return yellow("★★ ")
      else:                                     return dim("★  ")
  ```
  renders the Rating column in `_render_analysis_results`'s console table

[RESOLVED 2026-08-14 -- see resolution below. Originally found via opus

  REACT DASHBOARD'S CLOSE BUTTON IS A FOURTH PAPER-CLOSE SITE, WITH A
  PRICING CONVENTION WORSE THAN EITHER BUG THE SIBLING ENTRY FIXED
Priority: Medium -- same live/paper-P&L-overstatement class as the sibling
  entry (booking a more optimistic exit than the position could actually
  realize), but with a larger per-trade error and, for NO positions, a
  wrong-side price rather than just a wrong-convention one. Currently
  gated behind a manual operator click in the web dashboard, not an
  automated path, which is the only reason this isn't higher.

Problem:
  frontend/src/useData.js:172's mapTrades() computes `mark:
  t.current_yes_ask ?? t.actual_fill_price ?? t.entry_price ?? 0` for every
  open position with NO side-branching (`side` is carried on the object
  separately but never read when computing `mark`). frontend/src/App.jsx's
  handleClose() (~line 638-641) posts that value straight through:
  `body: JSON.stringify({ trade_id: pos.id, exit_price: pos.mark || 0 })`
  to POST /api/close-position (web_app.py:2886-2919), which accepts any
  client-supplied exit_price in the (0, 1] range (enforced server-side,
  see web_app.py:2905-2912's existing WA-security comment/check -- so this
  is not a wide-open injection, just a wrong-but-in-range price) with no
  side- or market-cross-check against what the position could actually
  realize. `current_yes_ask` itself is populated at web_app.py:1393 from
  the SSE live-market snapshot's raw `yes_ask` field, unadjusted for side.

  Concrete failure modes, both verified against the current code (not
  assumed):
    1. A YES holder's Close button books the *ask* (what a buyer pays to
       open more), not the *bid* (what a holder can realize by closing) --
       overvalued by the FULL bid-ask spread, twice as wrong as the
       midpoint bug the sibling entry just fixed (which averaged bid and
       ask, an overstatement of half the spread).
    2. A NO holder's Close button books the raw YES ask directly -- not
       even the right SIDE's price (should be `1 - yes_ask`, the NO bid).
       A NO position in a 60/62-cent (yes_bid/yes_ask) market books 0.62
       instead of the realizable 0.38: a ~$0.24/share fabricated gain,
       independent of and much larger than the midpoint-vs-liquidation gap
       the sibling entry addressed.
    3. When the SSE snapshot has no quote for a ticker,
       `current_yes_ask` is null/undefined and `mark` falls through to
       `t.actual_fill_price ?? t.entry_price ?? 0` -- entry_price is
       exactly the fallback this project's sibling entry deliberately
       REJECTED for the model-exit family (see that entry's Resolution,
       decision 2), reintroduced here via the frontend instead.

What it would look like:
  Compute `mark` the same way the now-fixed Python paths do: for a YES
  position, the realizable bid; for a NO position, `1 - yes_ask` (the NO
  bid) -- i.e. mirror positions.liquidation_price()'s logic in useData.js,
  which needs `current_yes_bid` (not just `current_yes_ask`) threaded
  through from web_app.py:1393's SSE-snapshot enrichment alongside the
  existing `current_yes_ask` field, plus `side` read at the mark
  computation (currently ignored). On the no-quote fallback, either match
  the sibling entry's skip-this-cycle convention (disable/hide the Close
  button rather than falling back to entry_price) or, since this is a
  human-in-the-loop UI unlike the automated Python paths, surface a
  manual-price-entry field instead -- genuinely a UX design decision, not
  a mechanical port, surface via AskUserQuestion per this project's
  standing workflow rather than assuming. Needs its own before/after test
  (or manual verification plus a written note, given this is a React/Flask
  boundary without this repo's Python test harness) proving the posted
  exit_price changes for a representative YES and NO fixture.

Why not now:
  Genuinely a separate change from the sibling entry that found this:
  different language/file pair (JSX + Flask route, not the sibling's
  pure-Python order_executor.py/main.py sites), different UI/UX surface
  (a manual dashboard click, not a cron-driven or CLI-menu close), and
  would need its own review of whatever frontend test coverage (if any)
  exists for useData.js/App.jsx before shipping -- bundling it into the
  sibling entry's already-large diff would have blurred two independently
  reviewable changes together for no benefit.

When to revisit:
  Soon -- per-trade dollar impact here is structurally larger than the
  sibling entry's (full spread for YES, a wrong-side price entirely for
  NO, vs. half-spread for both sides in the sibling), and it silently
  fabricates a price via the entry_price fallback exactly when the
  operator most needs an accurate one (a stale/missing quote). No blocking
  dependency on the sibling entry -- that one is already resolved.

Resolution (2026-08-14):
  web_app.py:689-694 (the SSE snapshot cache `_get_live_market_snapshot.
  _cache`, previously "yes_ask" only) now also stores "yes_bid" from the
  raw market dict, mirroring the existing yes_ask line exactly. web_app.py

  Two scope/design decisions surfaced via AskUserQuestion before
  implementing, per this project's standing workflow:
    1. No-quote fallback UX -- manual price-entry field (chosen) vs.
       disabling the Close button entirely. Investigated first: the SSE
       snapshot cache is populated ONLY by the Jinja /analyze route
       visiting, and only holds the top-10 markets by currently-positive
       net edge -- nothing in cron.py/main.py auto-refreshes it, and an
       already-held position's edge routinely decays below that bar. So a
       missing quote is plausibly the COMMON case for held positions on
       this dashboard, not a rare edge case -- disabling Close whenever
       that's true would make the button frequently unusable, which is
       almost certainly why the entry_price fallback existed in the first
       place. Chose manual entry instead: App.jsx's Close panel now shows
       a small number input (prefilled with the same fallback value used

       validated client-side to (0, 1] before the request fires; the

       API-cost/latency design question of its own (per-ticker
       client.get_market() calls vs. an unverified batch-by-tickers REST
       param), not something this entry's own scope asked for.
