  Independent opus review (effort=high), per this project's standing
  workflow: found 1 HIGH, 3 MEDIUM, 8 LOW findings. All addressed --
  none dropped regardless of severity:
    HIGH -- web_app.py's snapshot-cache population (`_get_live_market_
      snapshot._cache`) read raw `m.get("yes_bid"/"yes_ask", 0)` directly,
      bypassing coalesce_market_price() (this codebase's established
      cents-vs-dollars normalizer, used everywhere else a Kalshi price
      field is read). Under a legacy-cents API response this produced
      garbage marks and a `markIsLive: true` state that was actually
      unsubmittable (server rejects out-of-range prices), silently
      defeating the manual-entry fallback this fix exists to provide; pre-
      existing on yes_ask, but the fix made it load-bearing by adding
      yes_bid on the same unguarded path. Fixed: both fields now go
      through coalesce_market_price(*YES_BID_KEYS/YES_ASK_KEYS), wrapped
      in a per-item try/except (a malformed price on one market must
      degrade only that market to "no quote", not crash the whole
      /analyze route -- this comprehension sits outside the per-market
      try/except above it in the same route).
    MEDIUM 1 -- a NO position with yes_ask exactly 1.0 (a normal quote on
      an illiquid/extreme-strike market, not an error -- order_executor.py
      synthesizes this exact value when no real ask exists) computed
      liveSidePrice=0, which passed the `!= null` liveness check but the
      server's `exit_price > 0` gate then rejected it, hard-blocking Close
      with the manual-entry fallback suppressed (since markIsLive read
      true). Fixed: markIsLive now additionally requires
      `liveSidePrice > 0`. Mutation-tested (reverted to the `!= null`-only
      check via Edit, confirmed the new test for this exact case fails,
      restored).
    MEDIUM 2 -- `selectedPos` was a detached object reference to whatever
      position array existed at click time; M.positions is a brand-new
      array of brand-new objects every 60s poll (mapTrades rebuilds it),
      so the selected position's mark/markIsLive were frozen the instant
      it was clicked and never picked up a fresher (or staler) quote --
      Close could submit an arbitrarily stale price, and the UI never
      switched between live/manual-entry mode as quotes came and went.
      Fixed: selection is now keyed by id (`selectedId`), with
      `selectedPos` derived fresh from `M.positions` every render via
      useMemo. The prefill-on-select effect is deliberately keyed on
      `selectedId` alone (not the derived object), so it fires only on a
      genuine reselection, not every poll -- otherwise it would wipe an
      operator's in-progress manual-entry edit every 60 seconds.
    MEDIUM 3 -- manual entry widens the pre-existing WA-security gap
      (client-supplied exit_price, range-checked but not market-cross-
      checked) with no audit trail distinguishing a manually-typed price
      from a market-derived one. Fixed: the frontend now sends a `manual`
      boolean (never a free-form reason string, to prevent a buggy/
      malicious client stuffing arbitrary text into the ledger);
      web_app.py translates `manual: true` into
      `close_paper_early(..., reason="manual_close")`, matching this
      codebase's existing reason-tagging convention (paper.py:1501's
      `reason="stop_loss"`).
    LOW 1-8 -- side default now matches liquidation_price()'s if-yes/else-
      NO convention (was defaulting unrecognized/missing side to YES,
      backwards from Python -- unreachable with real data today, fixed
      for correctness anyway); client validation tightened to `>= 0.01`
      matching the input's declared min and its own error message text;
      current_yes_bid/current_yes_ask now coerced via Number() so a
      string-shaped quote can't crash `.toFixed()` downstream; added 5
      more vitest cases closing the gaps a reviewer found in the original
      7 (the ask=1.0 zero-price case, a live-mark-is-never-0 companion
      assertion, the side-default case, and 2 string-coercion cases -- 12
      total, all passing, the zero-price one mutation-tested per above);
      the vacuous `selectedPos.mark != null` null-check was dropped (mark
      is never null by construction) as part of the MEDIUM 2 rewrite;
      closeMsg now clears on genuine reselection (row click, Dismiss,
      Escape) but deliberately NOT inside the selectedId effect itself,
      since handleClose's own success path also drives selectedId to null
      and clearing there would blank the just-set success message before
      the operator sees it; `trades.open?.length`/`trades.closed?.length`
      changed to `!= null` checks so closing the last open position (or
      genuinely zero closed trades) actually clears the UI instead of
      leaving stale data displayed; fallback price order swapped to
      entry_price-first (was actual_fill_price-first) since entry_price is
      what the displayed cost-basis (cost/qty) is derived from, so the
      no-quote fallback shows exactly $0 phantom P&L instead of a few
      cents of drift from actual_fill_price's extra fill precision.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-14 -- fixed, see Resolution below. Originally filed by
  adjacency while resolving the REACT DASHBOARD'S CLOSE BUTTON entry above:
  investigating that entry's no-quote fallback UX decision surfaced this as
  the actual root cause, not just a rare edge case.] `/API/TRADES`'S LIVE
  QUOTE ENRICHMENT (current_yes_bid/
  current_yes_ask) ONLY EVER COVERS THE TOP-10 CURRENTLY-POSITIVE-EDGE
  MARKETS, NOT ARBITRARY HELD POSITIONS
Priority: Low-Medium -- not a live-money correctness bug (the entry above's
  fix makes whatever quote IS present correct; this is about how often a
  quote is present at all), but it means the Close-button's manual-entry
  fallback path -- meant for the rare stale-quote case -- is plausibly the
  COMMON path for any position whose edge has decayed since entry, which
  was never the intent.

Problem:
  web_app.py's `_get_live_market_snapshot._cache` (the sole source of
  current_yes_bid/current_yes_ask on /api/trades' open positions, per the
  entry above) is written ONLY by the Jinja /analyze route's handler
  (web_app.py ~line 689), and only ever holds the top-10 markets with
  currently-positive net_edge (`if a.get("net_edge", ...) > 0`). Nothing in
  cron.py or main.py auto-visits /analyze -- the cache is populated purely
  as a side effect of a human loading that page, and even then only covers
  markets that still look like fresh entry opportunities right now. An
  already-held position's edge routinely decays or goes negative after
  entry (that's normal, expected behavior, not a bug) -- once it does, its
  ticker silently drops out of this cache and /api/trades stops reporting
  a live quote for it at all, even though the position is still open and
  the underlying market still has a real, fetchable price.

What it would look like:
  Fetch each open position's own ticker directly rather than depending on
  the opportunistic top-10 cache -- kalshi_client.py already has a
  single-ticker `get_market(ticker)` method (line 339) that would work,
  though calling it once per open position on every /api/trades poll (60s
  interval per useData.js) adds N live API calls per poll, an API-
  cost/latency tradeoff worth deciding deliberately rather than
  defaulting into. A batched alternative (Kalshi's GET /markets accepting
  a `tickers=` query param) was NOT found in use anywhere in this codebase
  during a grep sweep -- don't assume that shape works without verifying
  against Kalshi's actual API docs or a live test call first.

Why not now:
  Genuinely a different-sized problem than the mark-computation fix that
  found it -- that fix corrects the math for whatever quote is present;
  this is about redesigning WHICH positions get a live quote at all, which
  touches API call volume/rate-limit exposure on every dashboard poll.
  Surfaced via AskUserQuestion during the sibling entry's own design
  discussion and explicitly deferred rather than silently expanding that
  entry's scope.

When to revisit:
  Soon-ish -- not urgent (no bug ships worse numbers, positions just show
  the honest "no live quote" state more often than intended), but worth
  fixing before the manual-price-entry UX becomes the dashboard's default
  experience rather than its intended rare-case fallback.

Resolution (2026-08-14, chosen off a "what's next in the backlog" menu
  after the PositionsTab.jsx fix shipped): the "What it would look like"
  section above explicitly warned not to assume a batched Kalshi endpoint
  exists "without verifying against Kalshi's actual API docs or a live test
  call first" -- verified directly against https://docs.kalshi.com/
  api-reference/market/get-markets rather than trusting a web-search
  summary alone: `GET /markets` genuinely accepts a `tickers` parameter
  ("Comma-separated list of market tickers to retrieve"), and
  kalshi_client.py's existing `get_markets(self, **params)` already passes
  arbitrary params straight through to that endpoint, so
  `client.get_markets(tickers="A,B,C")` needed zero client-side changes.
  This eliminated the entry's original N-calls-per-poll cost concern
  entirely -- one batched call now covers every open position, not one per
  position -- so the AskUserQuestion this session asked was narrower than
  the entry anticipated: not "how do we afford per-position live fetching"
  but "given batching is free, opt into one new live call every 60s?" User
  chose yes.

  Shipped in web_app.py's `/api/trades`: batch-fetch every open position's
  ticker in one `client.get_markets(tickers=",".join(tickers),
  limit=min(len(tickers), 1000))` call, falling back per-ticker to the
  existing SSE opportunistic-cache enrichment if the live call raises
  entirely or a specific ticker isn't in the batch response. No open
  positions -> no tickers -> get_markets is never even called. Also
  extracted the price-coercion helper (`_safe_snapshot_price`, previously a
  function nested inside the /analyze route, unusable elsewhere) to a
  module-level `_safe_market_price()` and reused it for the new batch path
  too, rather than writing a second, potentially-diverging copy of the same
  coalesce_market_price()-wrapping logic -- this codebase has a documented
  HIGH-severity history (the REACT DASHBOARD'S CLOSE BUTTON entry above) of
  bugs from bypassing that exact coalescer.

  First-draft design mistake, caught by opus review and redesigned before
  shipping (recorded here since the mistake itself is the useful lesson,
  not just its fix): the first version constructed a FRESH `KalshiClient`
  locally inside `/api/trades` on every call (matching `/api/paper-order`'s
  existing pattern of doing this for a one-shot, user-initiated action).
  For a route polled every 60s by every open dashboard tab, that meant
  re-validating the private key file's Windows ACL (`icacls`) and
  re-parsing the PEM on every single poll indefinitely -- a real, repeated
  filesystem-ACL mutation on the live trading private key, not just wasted
  CPU. It also meant an unmocked construction in
  `test_api_trades_returns_correct_shape` would build a REAL client with
  REAL credentials: main.py's `load_dotenv()` (triggered at conftest.py
  collection time) searches upward from cwd for a `.env` file and finds the
  MAIN CLONE's real one when pytest runs from a nested worktree (this
  worktree has no `.env` of its own) -- so that test was on track to hit
  Kalshi's actual demo API for a fake ticker on every run, a regression
  introduced by this session's own first draft, not a pre-existing
  condition (an earlier version of this note wrongly called it
  "pre-existing" -- corrected here). The actual fix for all of this:
  `_build_app(client)`'s own `client` parameter is already a live
  `KalshiClient` captured in every route's closure (three OTHER routes --
  `get_weather_markets(client)` -- already reuse it this exact way); the
  module-level `_client` global is genuinely unused elsewhere in the file,
  but that's a red herring, not evidence there was no client to reuse.
  Switching `/api/trades` to `client.get_markets(...)` instead of
  constructing its own removes the repeated-icacls cost entirely AND makes
  the test-isolation problem structurally impossible rather than
  patched-over: the test fixtures pass either a plain `object()` (fails
  closed via AttributeError, caught by the route's own broad except -- no
  mock needed, no real client ever exists) or a `MagicMock` (for tests that
  need to control what the live path returns), and no code path in
  `/api/trades` imports or constructs `kalshi_client.KalshiClient` at all
  anymore.

  Also added, from the same review: a warning log when the batch returns
  fewer tickers than requested (previously silent -- a wrong `KALSHI_ENV`
  or similar misconfiguration would make this whole fix a silent no-op with
  zero diagnostic signal, since Kalshi returning `[]` for unrecognized
  tickers isn't an exception, just an empty result); `limit=min(len(tickers),
  1000)` on the batch call so an unrecognized/ignored `tickers` filter can't
  degenerate into `get_markets`'s cursor-pagination loop enumerating Kalshi's
  entire market list every 60s.

  Reviewed and deliberately left as-is (reasoning stated, not silently
  dropped): a live network call inside a 60s-polled route has no per-call
  timeout override of its own (inherits kalshi_client.py's existing 15s
  timeout + 3-retry backoff, worst case longer than one poll interval under
  a real Kalshi outage) -- fixing this needs a client-level API change
  (an optional timeout override threaded through `get_markets`) that's a
  bigger, separate piece of work than this entry's own scope, and the
  existing read-path circuit breaker eventually short-circuits it anyway.
  Also: the live-vs-SSE fallback is per-ticker, not per-field, so a market
  that returns a genuine `{yes_bid: 0, yes_ask: 0}` (no resting quote on
  either side) is treated as "live and $0" rather than falling through to a
  possibly-better SSE value for that one field -- but this fails safe
  either way (computeMark's own `> 0` gate already routes a $0/no-quote
  price through manual entry, never a silent submit), and per-field
  fallback would add real complexity for a case this safe.

  7 new tests in tests/test_web_app.py's `TestApiTradesLiveQuoteEnrichment`
  (live-batch-used-when-it-succeeds, live-quote-wins-over-a-DIFFERENT-
  SSE-value-for-the-same-ticker -- the opus review's own coverage-gap
  finding, the original draft only tested disjoint-ticker cases --
  falls-back-on-exception, ticker-missing-from-batch-falls-back-per-ticker,
  no-positions-skips-the-call-entirely, N-positions-batch-into-ONE-call,
  malformed-price-degrades-not-crashes), using a new `client_and_kalshi_mock`
  fixture (a MagicMock client) alongside the existing `client` fixture
  (plain `object()`, still sufficient for tests that don't care about live
  quotes). 42 tests pass in tests/test_web_app.py. Two claims
  mutation-tested via Edit (not string-replace): (1) "live quote is
  actually used, not just present, even against a differing SSE value" --
  reverting to always-use-the-SSE-snapshot broke 4 tests including the new
  precedence one; (2) "a live-fetch failure falls back instead of 500ing"
  -- removing the except-fallback (re-raising instead) broke the fallback
  test with an unhandled RuntimeError instead of a clean 200.
  ruff/ruff-format/mypy clean on both changed files.

Resolution (2026-08-14):
  Two real, independent bugs, both found by reading frontend/src/useData.js
  and its sibling "weather app site V_3 (3)/src/useData.js" (the tree
  confirmed by an earlier session to be the one actually built and served
  to the browser) rather than by guessing at browser Basic-Auth quirks --
  the earlier "browser-native caching" and "hmac.compare_digest encoding"
  theories were both ruled out; server-side _check_auth was never touched.

  Bug 1 (both trees) -- 401-storm on batch fetch: useData.js's fetchAll()
  fires 17 (frontend/) or 22 (V_3(3)/src) concurrent endpoint fetches via
  Promise.allSettled. The old apiFetch() called window.prompt() itself on
  every individual 401, so any batch where the stored password was
  missing/stale produced up to N blocking password dialogs in a row --
  entering the correct password on an early one couldn't retroactively fix
  the later ones, since their requests had already been sent (and 401'd)
  before that password existed. This alone explains "keeps spamming."

  Bug 2 (V_3(3)/src) -- missing CSRF header, corrected mid-session: commit
  54b0c576 (verified via `git show --stat`) added a server-side requirement
  that every state-changing request (POST/PUT/DELETE) carry an
  `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest` header (web_app.py's _check_auth, CSRF
  mitigation) and updated the TRACKED frontend/src/useData.js's authHeader()
  to send it -- but never touched "weather app site V_3 (3)/src/useData.js"
  in git history (confirmed: not a `git log -S`-followed copy). HOWEVER: an
  independent opus review (effort:high) of this session's own diff found
  that the MAIN CLONE (C:\Users\thesa\claude kalshi, not this worktree) had
  ~130 lines of UNCOMMITTED changes sitting in exactly these two files
  (useData.js, tabs/PositionsTab.jsx) -- already including this same CSRF
  header, the ee22c44c computeMark/mapTrades fix, AND a full manual
  close-price-entry UI in PositionsTab.jsx that goes beyond what the
  sibling entry below described as "deferred." Confirmed live in the
  actually-served bundle (static/dist/assets/index-B0PKsZq3.js). So Bug 2
  had ALREADY been hand-patched out-of-band, uncommitted, sometime after
  the ee22c44c session -- it was NOT actively live at the moment this
  session started, but was never captured in git anywhere, and this
  session's branch (built from the stale committed version) would have
  either conflicted with or risked silently discarding that work on the
  next pull/merge. Per explicit AskUserQuestion, that uncommitted work was
  read from the main clone (read-only -- nothing in the main clone was
  modified or discarded) and ported into this branch as the new baseline,
  with this session's fetchAllSafe fix layered on top, so the committed
  result is now a strict superset of both. Bug 1 (the prompt storm) WAS
  still genuinely live in the served bundle at session start (confirmed:
  the bundle contained the old per-request window.prompt() and an
  unauthenticated scan-version poll) and remains the primary explanation
  for the reported symptom.

  Shipped, both files: extracted apiFetch's per-request window.prompt() out
  into a new exported `fetchAllSafe(endpoints, promptFn)` that runs the
  whole batch via Promise.allSettled first, then prompts exactly ONCE for
  any 401s across the batch and retries only the endpoints that actually
  failed auth -- a correct password now completes that same fetch cycle
  instead of leaving other endpoints null until the next 60s poll. Also
  hardened against two overlapping fetchAllSafe() calls (60s poll vs. the
  5s "cron just finished" fast-refresh) each independently prompting for
  the same real auth event: snapshot the stored password before the batch,
  skip the prompt if it already changed underneath this call, retry
  directly instead (opus review LOW 1). Fixed the same missing-
  Authorization-header gap in both trees' 5s scan-version poll, plus (V_3
  (3)/src only, opus review MEDIUM 3) three more unauthenticated fetch()
  calls found by the same grep: AnalyticsTab.jsx's /api/edge-realization
  and /api/reliability/<city>, and OverviewTab.jsx's /health -- all behind
  the same unconditional @app.before_request gate, all silently 401ing
  forever once a password is set. V_3(3)/src additionally got authHeader()
  's X-Requested-With addition (Bug 2, now redundant with the ported
  main-clone version but kept as the single source of truth going forward).

  Tests: frontend/src/useData.test.js gained 6 new fetchAllSafe cases
  (all-succeed/never-prompts, all-401/prompts-exactly-once, correct-
  password-retries-with-the-fresh-credential, selective-retry-doesn't-
  refetch-successful-siblings, concurrent-batch-skips-its-own-prompt,
  cancel-leaves-endpoints-rejected). 18/18 pass (12 pre-existing computeMark
  + 6 new), re-counted via `npm test` immediately before writing this
  sentence. Mutation-tested three separate claims by temporarily reverting
  each fix (Edit tool, not a string-replace script) and confirming the
  relevant test(s) failed before reverting: (1) "prompts exactly once" --
  reverting to per-endpoint prompting broke 2 tests (6 and 3 prompt calls
  instead of 1); (2) "retry uses the FRESH password" -- moving
  sessionStorage.setItem() to after the retry (so the retry would go out
  with stale/no credentials) broke the retry test, which an opus review
  found the ORIGINAL call-count-only mock could NOT have caught (a real
  gap in the first version of this test, now fixed by having the mock
  check the actual Authorization header sent); (3) "concurrent batch skips
  its own prompt" -- hardcoding havePwd=false broke the new concurrent-
  batch test. V_3(3)/src/useData.js and the 3 .jsx files have no
  package.json/vite.config/index.html in this worktree (confirmed absent
  -- they exist only in the main clone, untracked) so none of them run
  through vitest here; syntax-verified instead via esbuild's own JSX
  transform (`esbuild.transformSync`, the same transformer Vite uses
  internally) since plain `node --check` can't parse JSX. Per the same

[RESOLVED 2026-08-14 -- fixed, see the Resolution below (after the Update
  note). Originally
  deliberately deferred (not silently skipped) while resolving the REACT
  DASHBOARD'S CLOSE BUTTON entry above: an opus review finding (MEDIUM 2 in
  that entry's Resolution) was fixed in both the tracked frontend/src/

  loads.] "weather app site V_3 (3)/src/tabs/PositionsTab.jsx"'S
  selectedPos/confirmClose ARE THE SAME DETACHED-OBJECT-REFERENCE BUG THE
  SIBLING ENTRY JUST FIXED ELSEWHERE, STILL UNFIXED HERE
Priority: Medium -- same staleness class as the sibling entry's MEDIUM 2
  (a submitted Close price can go stale indefinitely, and the UI won't
  switch between live/manual-entry mode as quotes come and go), on the
  file that's actually live rather than a reference copy.

Problem:
  M.positions is a brand-new array of brand-new objects every 60s poll
  (mapTrades rebuilds it from scratch). This file's `selectedPos` (set via
  row click) and `confirmClose` (set via handleClose, which is what the
  Close-position confirm modal actually reads) both hold direct object
  references captured at click time, not ids re-resolved against the live
  array -- identical to the bug the sibling entry's MEDIUM 2 finding
  described and fixed in App.jsx. Whatever mark/markIsLive the position
  had at the moment it was clicked is what stays displayed and what gets
  submitted to /api/close-position, no matter how long the confirm modal
  sits open or how much the underlying quote has moved (or disappeared)
  since.

What it would look like:
  Same shape as the fix already shipped in App.jsx: key selection by
  `p.id` instead of the object itself, derive `selectedPos`/`confirmClose`
  fresh from `M.positions` every render (e.g. via useMemo keyed on
  [M.positions, selectedId]), and re-derive the close-price prefill only
  on a genuine reselection (keyed on the id, not the derived object) so
  polling refreshes don't wipe an in-progress manual-entry edit. This file
  additionally has a Set-based bulk-selection (`selectedIds`) and a
  keydown handler with `confirmClose` in its own dependency array
  (Enter-to-confirm) that the sibling fix's App.jsx didn't have to
  contend with -- both need to keep working correctly through the same
  refactor, which is exactly why this wasn't attempted inline (see "Why
  not now").

Why not now:
  This file has no test harness at all (same zero-frontend-test-coverage
  gap noted throughout the sibling entry) and a genuinely more complex
  selection-state shape (bulk Set + single selection + a keyboard handler
  with its own dependency array) than the file the fix was already proven
  against. Attempting an unverified structural refactor of unfamiliar code
  on the one file the user's actual browser loads was judged a worse risk
  in the moment than shipping the smaller, already-tested price-
  correctness fix and leaving this specific staleness gap for a session
  that can build proper coverage around it first.

When to revisit:
  Soon-ish -- not as urgent as the price-correctness bugs already fixed
  (a stale price is wrong but bounded by how long the modal stays open,
  not systematically wrong on every close the way the pre-fix mark
  computation was), but it's the same bug class already fixed elsewhere
  in this exact feature, just not here yet.

Resolution (2026-08-14, same session as the Update note above, chosen off a
  "what's next in the backlog" menu after the auth-loop fix shipped):
  Applied the exact shape prescribed in "What it would look like" above.
  `selectedId`/`confirmCloseId` (primitive ids) replace `selectedPos`/
  `confirmClose` as the actual useState values; `selectedPos`/`confirmClose`
  are now derived via `useMemo(() => M.positions.find(p => p.id === id) ??
  null, [M.positions, id])`, re-resolving to the CURRENT object (or null, if
  the position closed/disappeared elsewhere) on every M.positions poll
  instead of staying frozen on whatever was captured at click time.
  `closePriceInput` is set only inside `handleClose(pos)`, itself only
  called from a genuine row-click -- never touched by the id->object
  derivation -- so a poll landing mid-edit can't wipe an in-progress manual
  price entry, exactly the constraint the original entry called out.

  `selectedIds` (the Set-based bulk-selection) needed no change -- it was
  already storing ids, not objects; `handleBulkClose` already resolves
  `filtered.filter(p => selectedIds.has(p.id))` fresh from the live array at
  click time, never a captured reference. Confirmed this by reading it
  again rather than assuming "same file, must have the same bug."

  Found and fixed a second, independent bug in the SAME keydown `useEffect`
  this refactor already had to touch (adjacency, not part of the original
  report): the effect depended on `[confirmClose]` alone, an object that
  (pre-refactor) only changed once per modal-open -- so typing into the
  manual-entry input after opening the modal updated `closePriceInput` state
  without re-subscribing the listener, meaning Enter-to-confirm could submit
  the closure's STALE pre-typing price instead of what the operator actually
  typed. Fixed by widening the effect's dependency array to
  `[confirmCloseId, confirmClose, closePriceInput]`, so the closure Enter
  calls into is always current.

  Verification: no test/build infrastructure exists for this tree in this
  worktree (same gap the original entry cited, confirmed still true; per an
  explicit AskUserQuestion this session, decided against standing up test
  infra here to match the smaller-scope precedent already set twice today
  for this same tree). Syntax-verified via `esbuild.transformSync` (JSX-
  aware). Correctness manually traced across the well-formed-id paths --
  row-click select/deselect, poll refresh while the detail panel is open,
  poll refresh while the confirm modal is open (does not touch
  closePriceInput), typing then Enter (fresh closure, no longer stale),
  Escape, Cancel, backdrop click -- but this trace initially missed a real
  gap the opus review below caught, so it should NOT be read as exhaustive.

  Independent opus review (effort=high) found 1 MEDIUM + 2 LOW, both
  addressed:

  MEDIUM -- a position with no `id` became permanently unclickable, not just
  "same as before": `setSelectedId(p.id)`/`setSelectedId(confirmCloseId)`
  stored `undefined` for such a position, and the `!= null` derivation guard
  treats `undefined` the same as "nothing selected," so the row silently
  stopped opening at all. This wasn't hypothetical -- mockData.js's 8 MOCK
  positions (the initial render state before the first successful
  /api/trades response) have no `id` field, and useData.js's fetchAll()
  keeps MOCK positions indefinitely on a failed fetch rather than clearing
  them, so a real dead-click window exists on load and stays open under
  sustained auth/network failure; paper.py's own defensive id-filtering
  comment (H-8) also implies a real trade with a null id has existed before.
  Fixed with a `rowKey = (p) => p.id ?? p.ticker` UI-selection key, used for
  `selectedId`/`confirmCloseId`/`selectedIds` everywhere a row needs to be
  identified for selection -- but never for the actual `/api/close-position`
  request body, which still sends the real `p.id`/`pos.id` and still hits
  the existing "No trade ID" guard if it's missing. Extending the fallback
  to bulk-selection (`selectedIds`) surfaced the same gap one level deeper --
  `handleBulkClose` would have POSTed `trade_id: undefined` for a
  ticker-keyed position now that it's selectable -- fixed by adding
  `p.id != null` to `handleBulkClose`'s live-quote filter, mirroring
  `handleCloseConfirm`'s existing guard.

  LOW (accepted as-is, not fixed, reasoning stated per finding rather than
  silently dropped): (1) if a position leaves M.positions entirely while the
  confirm modal is open (bot settles it elsewhere), confirmClose resolves to
  null and the modal just disappears with no message -- confirmed
  unreachable in the current codebase (ids aren't reused, a failed fetch
  keeps prior state rather than emptying it) and net still better than the
  pre-fix behavior (a dead, no-longer-real position staying submittable
  indefinitely); a considered fix (auto-clear + toast on id-set-but-
  unresolved) was rejected because it would also fire during the
  MOCK-to-real-data transition for a mock position's ticker-based rowKey,
  producing a misleading "no longer open" message for something that was
  never a real trade. (2) A poll landing while the confirm modal is open can
  flip markIsLive underneath the operator (manual input appears/disappears
  mid-decision) -- both directions fail safe money-wise (never silently
  submits a fabricated price; an empty-then-typed input fails the existing
  0.01-1.00 validation) and is arguably the correct, intended consequence of
  making the modal live rather than frozen; not fixed, no visual "quote
  updated" cue added.

  NOT built, run, or browser-tested, per the same scope decision noted in
  the sibling entry's Resolution (a past session's build attempt from this
  exact worktree overwrote the main clone's live static/dist). Whoever next
  builds/deploys this tree should manually exercise the confirm-modal flow
  (open, wait for a poll tick, confirm) and the bulk-select-with-mock-data
  edge case before trusting it end-to-end.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-18 -- found by max-depth forensic audit (AUD-0004), fixed
  same session] TRACKER.BRIER_SCORE() HAS NO CONDITION_TYPE FILTER --
  CONTAMINATES THE MASTER LIVE-TRADING GRADUATION GATE
Priority: Critical -- brier_score() is the value paper.graduation_check()
  gates ALL live trading on (LiveTradingGate.check() -> graduation_check()
  -> brier <= 0.23). Reproduced against real production data: this bug
  flips that gate's outcome on today's live data.

Problem:
  brier_score() (tracker.py, primary-source query) had zero condition_type
  filtering, unlike its sibling count_settled_predictions() (fixed
  2026-07-30, see that RESOLVED entry above) which already excludes
  condition_type='between'/'precip_month_total'/'snow_month_total'/
  'hurricane_count'/'hurricane_next_event'/'storm_order'. Shadow-only
  non-temperature predictions (routed in since 6845b62c/9a7583aa,
  2026-08-06/07) silently contaminated the calibration score used to
  authorize real-money trading. graduation_check() already gated its
  SAMPLE COUNT via the correctly-filtered count_settled_predictions(), but
  computed the actual Brier VALUE via the unfiltered brier_score() -- two
  different populations feeding one gate.

Resolution: added the identical exclusion list (byte-for-byte mirror of
  count_settled_predictions()'s WHERE clause, verified) to brier_score()'s
  primary-source query only -- NOT the paper_trades.db fallback path (see
  follow-up entry below; different, larger-scoped fix). Re-verified against
  real production predictions.db this session (independently, not just
  trusting the audit's numbers): unfiltered last-50-of-any-type Brier =
  0.2169 (<=0.23, PASSES graduation_check()'s criterion); true
  last-50-temperature-only Brier (this fix) = 0.2397 (>0.23, FAILS it).
  Sample guard independently satisfied (count_settled_predictions()=83 >=
  MIN_BRIER_SAMPLES=30), so this is a genuine, decisive flip on today's real
  data, not a hypothetical one -- confirmed by re-deriving both numbers a
  third time (once by the audit, once by me, once by the independent opus
  reviewer below) via direct read-only SQL against the live DB.

  6 new tests (tests/test_tracker.py::TestBrierScoreConditionTypeFilter):
  excludes each of the 6 types individually and all-at-once; does NOT
  exclude 'below' or NULL condition_type (a specific list, not an
  accidental allowlist); last_n reaches further back in time to find a
  full N temperature-only rows rather than diluting on a naive
  filter-after-limit; the min_days_out=0 (same-day, `predictions` table)
  branch is filtered too, not just the default multiday branch; and a test
  pinning that when every settled row is an excluded type, the function
  correctly falls through to the paper_trades fallback -- and that
  fallback is genuinely unfiltered (contamination-and-all), documenting a
  real exposure rather than asserting safety that doesn't exist yet (see
  follow-up entry below). Mutation-tested via Edit (not a string-replace
  script): 3 of these 6 tests fail when the WHERE-clause addition is
  reverted; the other 3 are deliberate positive controls / different-branch
  coverage not meant to be sensitive to this specific mutation.

  Scoped regression: full tests/test_tracker.py (405 tests) +
  tests/test_graduation_gate.py + tests/test_alerts_side.py all pass.
  ruff/mypy/pre-commit (ruff, ruff-format, mypy) all clean.

  Independent opus review (effort=high) found 1 HIGH + 3 MEDIUM + 4 LOW +
  5 INFO, all addressed:

[RESOLVED 2026-08-20 -- fixed as batch-06 item 1 (audit/handoff_prompts/
  batches/batch-06.md); see Resolution below] BRIER_SCORE()'S
  PAPER_TRADES.DB FALLBACK HAS NO
  CONDITION_TYPE FILTER, AND IS NOW MORE REACHABLE THAN BEFORE
Priority: Medium -- not exercised today (83 filtered tracker-DB rows
  exist, so the primary query never returns zero rows for
  graduation_check()'s actual call pattern), but no longer purely
  hypothetical: the sibling fix above means any future DB state where
  every settled multi-day prediction is an excluded condition_type now
  falls through to this completely unfiltered path instead of erroring or
  returning a filtered-but-smaller result.

Problem:
  tracker.brier_score()'s fallback path (paper.get_all_trades(), used when
  the primary tracker-DB query returns 0 rows) has no condition_type
  filter of any kind. Paper trade records carry no condition_type field at
  all -- only ticker and var -- unlike tracker-DB prediction rows, which
  store condition_type explicitly via log_prediction's analysis dict.
  Filtering this fallback correctly would require deriving condition type
  from the ticker string prefix (e.g. distinguishing KXRAIN*/KXBETWEEN*/
  KXDENSNOWM*-style tickers), a parsing mechanism that doesn't exist
  anywhere else for paper trades today. tests/test_tracker.py::
  TestBrierScoreConditionTypeFilter::
  test_when_every_settled_row_is_excluded_falls_through_to_unfiltered_paper_fallback
  pins the current (unfiltered) behavior with a real reproduction: an
  all-excluded tracker DB + one contaminated paper trade (entry_prob=0.9,
  outcome='no', error=0.81) produces brier_score()==0.81 with no filtering
  applied at all.

Why not now: needs its own scoped design decision (which ticker-prefix
  parsing scheme to use, whether to add it as a shared helper other paper-
  trade consumers could also use, whether var-based classification -- see
  paper.py's own KXHIGH*/KXLOW* ticker-prefix disambiguation logic used
  elsewhere -- is the right model to follow) rather than a same-shape
  mirror of the tracker-DB fix.

  via Edit mutation (removing either one alone still passes; removing both
  reproduces the original crash).

[RESOLVED 2026-08-20 -- fixed as batch-06 item 2 (audit/handoff_prompts/
  batches/batch-06.md); see Resolution below] BRIER-FAMILY CONDITION_TYPE
  EXCLUSION LIST HAS NO COUPLING TO RAIN/SNOW/HURRICANE GRADUATION GATES
Priority: Medium -- latent today (RAIN_TRADING_ENABLED unset per this
  worktree's env), but production is at 17 settled precip_month_total rows
  against weather_markets._rain_gates_active()'s 20-row graduation

  flips, not discovered after.

Problem:
  count_settled_predictions()'s and (as of the entry above)
  brier_score()'s condition_type exclusion list
  ('between'/'precip_month_total'/'snow_month_total'/'hurricane_count'/
  'hurricane_next_event'/'storm_order') is a hardcoded tuple with no
  coupling to whether those market families are actually shadow-only or
  live. The moment RAIN_TRADING_ENABLED (or the equivalent snow/hurricane
  flag) flips, these functions will permanently exclude the calibration of
  a market family receiving real capital, with nothing to notice the
  mismatch or prompt a review. This is a pre-existing gap inherited from
  count_settled_predictions() (2026-07-30), but the entry above propagates
  it into the Brier VALUE that gates ALL live trading, not just a sample
  count -- a strictly larger blast radius once triggered.

Why not now: needs a real design decision (should the exclusion list read
  from the same flags that gate each market family's live-trading
  activation? should there be a startup/cron-time consistency check that
  alerts if an excluded condition_type's live-trading flag is enabled?) --
  a genuine judgment call for AskUserQuestion when picked up, not
  something to decide silently while fixing an unrelated Brier-score bug.

Resolution 2026-08-20 (batch-06 item 2): re-verified live -- rain count is
  17 settled precip_month_total rows against the 20-row floor today,
  confirming the "close to flipping" priority note still holds.
  AskUserQuestion picked "dynamic per-family coupling": exclusion is now
  computed by tracker._excluded_brier_condition_types(), which excludes a
  condition_type only while its own market family's gate
  (weather_markets._rain_gates_active()/_snow_gates_active()/
  _hurricane_count_gates_active()/_hurricane_next_event_gates_active()/
  _storm_order_gates_active()) is inactive; the moment a family's env flag
  is set AND its sample floor clears, its settled rows start counting
  toward every Brier/calibration value this feeds. Fails closed if a
  gate's own state can't be determined (exception -> stays excluded).

  Correction to this entry's own framing during implementation: 'between'
  is NOT one of the 5 gate-backed types and is NOT coupled to anything --
  unlike the other 5, it isn't shadow-only (KXHIGH*/KXLOW* between-brackets
  are fully live today); it's excluded because it has a structurally larger
  calibration gap than above/below (T~=6.8 temperature-scaling factor, see
  backlog.txt's EMOS confirm-gate opus-review finding #4), a permanent
  calibration-quality exclusion, not a graduation-pending one. There is no
  "_between_gates_active()" and none should be added.

  Applied to BOTH functions this entry named: brier_score() and
  count_settled_predictions(). Also applied, via adjacency (workflow step
  27 -- same literal exclusion tuple, same file, same live-trading-
  readiness data-flow), to 5 more tracker.py sites that had the identical

  warns about, inside the same file. All 5 gate-check functions currently
  return False (no *_TRADING_ENABLED flag set), so the exclusion set is
  IDENTICAL to the old static tuple today -- this change moves zero live

  NOTE for whoever next touches calibration.py/ml_bias.py/main.py: those 3

[RESOLVED 2026-08-18 -- fixed as part of batch-01 (AUD-0001/AUD-0002/AUD-0005/AUD-0009/AUD-0012, same root cause); see Resolution below] check_position_limits() exposure caps are structurally blind to live positions opened via cmd_order (regression introduced by the e5331a8d live-fill-routing fix)
Priority: HIGH (audit id AUD-0001, status CONFIRMED, confidence VERY HIGH, evidence E2)
Files: paper.py, main.py

Problem:
  check_position_limits()'s exposure accounting was designed around a single ledger (paper_trades.json) that, prior to e5331a8d, happened to also receive live fills. e5331a8d correctly stopped writing live fills into that ledger but did not add execution_log-sourced live exposure into check_position_limits' accounting.
  Evidence: Independently read paper.py:3447-3686 (check_position_limits full body), paper.py:1299-1301 (get_open_trades reads only paper_trades.json), paper.py:1598-1673 (all four exposure getters call get_open_trades exclusively), main.py:4528 (_is_live derivation) and main.py:4546-4569 (cmd_order buy path calling check_position_limits). Grepped paper.py for 'execution_log' -- zero functional references,...
  Financial risk: Real live money: once LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true, repeated manual cmd_order live buys on the same city/date (or correlated group) can silently exceed all configured exposure caps, with the CLI...
  Security risk: None -- internal risk-control gap, not attacker-facing.
  Recommendation: Have check_position_limits() also incorporate open live positions from execution_log (via order_executor._get_live_open_positions()) into its exposure accounting before comparing against caps. Already tracked in backlog.txt.
  Full record: audit/AUDIT_REPORT.json (id AUD-0001), audit/AUDIT_REPORT.md.

Resolution 2026-08-18 (batch-01: AUD-0001+AUD-0002+AUD-0005+AUD-0009+AUD-0012
  fixed together as one coordinated change, all sharing the same root cause
  -- risk gates reading only paper_trades.json, blind to execution_log's
  real live positions/losses. Full narrative here since this is the anchor
  entry; AUD-0002/0005/0009/0012 below point back to this one rather than
  repeating it):

  Design decisions (both surfaced via AskUserQuestion before implementing):
  1. Exposure caps enforce ONE combined paper+live total, not two
     separately-tracked totals -- matches this project's existing
     single-shared-enforcement-point convention (check_position_limits'
     own docstring) and the F6 same-cycle-append precedent in
     _auto_place_trades, which already merges live trades into the same
     list structurally.
  2. Live drawdown has no persisted peak/starting balance to compute a true
     high-water-mark drawdown from (unlike paper's), and this project
     deliberately chose NOT to add one (a new SQLite table + a balance-
     snapshot writer that would need to run on some cadence) for a
     currently-dormant feature. Used a trailing 14-day realized-loss window
     against the live client's CURRENT balance instead --
     LIVE_DRAWDOWN_WINDOW_DAYS env var, mirrors get_today_live_loss()'s own
     shape per this entry's own Recommendation text.

  paper.py:
  - New get_all_open_positions() = get_open_trades() +
    order_executor._get_live_open_positions(). get_open_trades() itself
    left unchanged -- it has 14 other callers (P&L reporting, paper-only
    position management, dashboard stats) requiring paper-only semantics.
  - get_total_exposure/get_ticker_exposure/get_city_date_exposure/
    get_directional_exposure/get_correlated_exposure, PLUS
    check_position_limits' own separate inline per-market existing_cost sum
    (a second blind spot this entry's Problem text didn't name, caught by
    this session's own test suite after the first pass missed it) all now
    read get_all_open_positions().
  - check_aged_positions/get_expiry_date_clustering/
    check_correlated_event_exposure (paper.py) and web_app.py's /api/risk
    endpoint's own inline get_open_trades() call also switched to
    get_all_open_positions() -- all four feed the SAME dashboard JSON
    response as get_total_exposure(), so leaving them on paper-only would
    have made that one response self-contradictory (total_exposure
    including a live position the breakdown fields couldn't see).
  - is_paused_drawdown()/is_streak_paused() gained an optional client=None
    param; when passed, OR in a live-side check (execution_log-sourced)
    alongside the existing paper-only check. Degrades to "no live signal"
    (not a halt) if the live balance can't be fetched, matching
    _resolve_live_balance's own established convention; fails closed on an
    unexpected error.

  order_executor.py:
  - _get_live_open_positions() now backfills city/target_date onto each
    live position dict (parsed from the ticker alone via
    weather_markets.parse_city_date -- the raw execution_log rows have
    neither field, so the city/date-keyed caps couldn't see a live
    position without this).
  - _auto_place_trades' _open_trades_list now seeds with
    get_open_trades() + _get_live_open_positions() (prior-cycle live
    positions), unconditionally -- not gated on live=True/False, per this
    finding's own explicit scope ("regardless of live=True/False"): a
    PAPER cycle placing trades must still see real live exposure.
  - _count_open_live_orders() (AUD-0009/0012, detailed in that entry below)
    and is_paused_drawdown/is_streak_paused's 3 direct call sites now pass
    client through, matching is_daily_loss_halted's existing pattern.

  execution_log.py: 3 new functions -- get_pending_live_orders()
  (unbounded, AUD-0012), get_live_realized_loss_since(days) and
  get_live_settlement_streak() (both AUD-0005, detailed in that entry).

  trading_gates.py: LiveTradingGate.check() now passes client through to
  is_paused_drawdown/is_streak_paused (previously called with zero args).

  A real backward-compat break was caught and fixed along the way: ~30
  existing tests across 13 files monkeypatched is_paused_drawdown/
  is_streak_paused with strict zero-arg lambdas; widened them to accept
  (and ignore) an optional client arg rather than retreating from making
  _auto_place_trades' direct calls live-aware (which the AUD-0005 finding
  explicitly requires, not just the trading_gates.py gate).

  Separately discovered and NOT part of this fix (flagged, not fixed here):
  the tests/conftest.py mock_balance_1000 fixture patches paper.DATA_PATH
  and then calls importlib.reload(paper), which re-executes paper.py's
  module-level `DATA_PATH = _project_root() / "data" / "paper_trades.json"`
  and silently undoes the patch -- confirmed empirically this session that
  paper.DATA_PATH under that fixture resolves to the REAL production data
  file (200+ real trades). Any test using that fixture and calling
  place_paper_order or reading open-trade state risks reading/writing real
  production data. This session's own new tests avoid the fixture entirely
  (direct paper.DATA_PATH patch, no reload). Worth its own follow-up --
  out of scope for this batch (affects the whole test suite's isolation
  infrastructure, not this fix's 5 findings).

  Independent opus review (effort:high, isolated worktree) before push found
  25 findings (2 HIGH, 10 MEDIUM, 13 LOW). ALL addressed:
  - HIGH: is_streak_paused(client)'s live signal never reached the actual
    Kelly-halving code (kelly_bet_dollars still called is_streak_paused()
    zero-arg) -- threaded client through kelly_bet_dollars/kelly_quantity
    and all their call sites in order_executor.py/main.py.
  - HIGH: live position dicts had no days_out, so the same-day cap couldn't
    see same-day live positions AND wrongly double-counted them against the
    multi-day cap -- _get_live_open_positions() now reconstructs days_out
    from target_date vs. entered_at, mirroring the exact snapshot semantic
    order_executor.py's own same-day-cap comment describes.
  - MEDIUM (10): exposure-cap denominator combined live dollars with a
    paper-only balance (fixed via a new _exposure_denom(client) combining
    paper balance + live effective balance -- see this entry's own new
    Design decision 3 below); position_age_kelly_scale/covariance_
    kelly_scale/get_factor_exposure still paper-only (position_age and
    get_factor_exposure fixed directly -- no denominator involved in
    either; covariance fixed alongside the denominator work); rain/snow
    tickers got
    target_date=None forever (added a close_time fallback); the drawdown
    window function skipped the degraded-data check its sibling has
    (added); the live balance denominator excluded deployed capital
    (added _live_effective_balance = cash + open live position cost,
    mirroring get_effective_balance()'s same-day-cost add-back); an
    uncached live API call fired per-candidate even on pure-paper cycles
    (scoped to live=True only); 3 test-quality gaps (a "partial exit" test
    that didn't actually exercise a partial exit, a cap test with an opp
    dict no gate would ever pass, missing coverage of the fail-closed/
    degrade branches) all rewritten with genuine positive controls;
    /api/risk's try/except covered only the import, not the new
    DB-touching calls (widened to the whole route body).
  - LOW (13): 2 more production call sites (main.py's cmd_paper/cmd_order
    display warnings) not passing client; same-day live settlements
    weren't excluded from the streak (paper's own convention); no SQL
    tiebreaker on settled_at ties; a days<=0 window silently returning 0.0
    loss (clamped, plus an upper bound against future-dated rows); merged
    paper+live ids collide visually in CLI displays (live entries now
    prefixed); a shadow-logging dedup check stayed paper-only; 3 comments
    citing a nonexistent /api/exposure endpoint (real name is /api/risk);
    one comment's misleading analogy corrected; two "mutation tests" that
    swapped in a hand-written reimplementation rather than mutating the
    real function were replaced by directly Edit-reverting the actual
    production code (order_executor.py/paper.py) via this session's own
    Edit-run-revert-back cycle, confirming the DIRECT tests already catch
    the regression, then removing the redundant reimplementation tests.
    One finding (L6, partial-exit quantity overstatement) was independently
    re-verified and found FALSE -- record_live_partial_exit already
    correctly reduces the tracked fill_quantity on a genuine partial exit;
    no code change. One (L10, lambda arity precision) and one (L12,
    get_all_open_positions() called 5x per check_position_limits
    invocation -- a real perf note, not correctness) accepted as-is:
    low-value relative to a broader signature refactor this late in an
    already-large session.

  Design decision 3 (surfaced via AskUserQuestion after the opus review,
  same pattern as decisions 1-2 above): exposure-cap denominator now
  combines paper's balance with the live client's effective balance
  (_exposure_denom(client) = max(STARTING_BALANCE, paper_balance) +
  live_cash + live_open_position_cost) when a client is passed --
  threaded through all 5 exposure getters, check_position_limits,
  portfolio_kelly_fraction, and covariance_kelly_scale, plus every call
  site in main.py/order_executor.py/web_app.py that has a client in scope.
  Degrades to paper-only (unchanged behavior) when no client is available.

  A SECOND independent opus review (effort:high, isolated worktree) then
  reviewed the fixes above for new bugs the fixes themselves might have
  introduced -- exactly the pattern that has burned this project before
  (a round-1 fix's own round-2 review once found 2 new severe bugs a
  round-1 finding-checklist review would never have caught). Found 22 more

[RESOLVED 2026-08-20 -- batch-04] cron._acquire_cron_lock() has a TOCTOU race with no OS-level exclusive-create primitive — reproduced
Priority: HIGH (audit id AUD-0006, status CONFIRMED, confidence VERY HIGH, evidence E2)
Files: cron.py

Problem:
  _acquire_cron_lock() checks `if lp.exists(): ...` and, several lines later, calls `lp.write_text(json.dumps(lock_data))` with no intervening OS-level exclusive-create (no O_EXCL open, no msvcrt.locking, no atomic rename-based claim). Two processes racing to acquire the lock when it does not yet exist (or has just gone stale) can both observe exists()==False and both proceed to write, each believing it holds exclusive ownership. This is the ONLY mechanism serializing cmd_cron (cron.py:2409) against cmd_watch --auto's own trade cycle (main.py:3622), web_app.py's /api/run_cron spawn path, and...
  Root cause: Check-then-act file existence test followed by a plain (non-exclusive) write, instead of an atomic O_EXCL create or a real OS file lock (contrast with paper.py's _CrossProcessDataLock, which does use msvcrt.locking for its own file).
  Evidence: Self-reproduced this session by running audit/reproductions/cron_lock_race_repro.py (redirects cron.LOCK_PATH to a tempdir, monkeypatches pathlib.Path.exists to rendezvous two threads at a threading.Barrier the instant both have evaluated `if lp.exists():`, then releases both into the write path). Output: `results: [True, True]` — both callers of _acquire_cron_lock() returned True, i.e. both...
  Financial risk: If two lock holders both run a trade cycle concurrently, each can independently detect the same open live position needing a protective exit (verified cron.py:912-919 calls...
  Security risk: None (not attacker-reachable — requires two legitimate local invocations racing).
  Recommendation: Replace the exists()-then-write_text() pattern with an atomic exclusive-create, e.g. `open(lp, 'x')` (raises FileExistsError if the file already exists) wrapped in the same fail-closed exception handling already present, or reuse paper.py's msvcrt-based _CrossProcessDataLock primitive for this file...
  Full record: audit/AUDIT_REPORT.json (id AUD-0006), audit/AUDIT_REPORT.md.

Resolution 2026-08-20: Rejected the audit's own first-listed fix (O_EXCL
  exclusive-create) after re-deriving it via AskUserQuestion: it would break
  the legitimate stale/dead-PID lock override path, which must overwrite an
  EXISTING file -- O_EXCL raises on that, silently removing automatic
  recovery from a crashed process's stale lock. Instead wrapped the whole
  check-then-decide-then-write critical section in a real OS mutex: added
  safe_io.CrossProcessLock (msvcrt-based on Windows, no-op elsewhere,
  non-reentrant) as a shared primitive, per user's AskUserQuestion choice to
  reuse it for both this fix and AUD-0051's below rather than writing two
  bespoke locks. cron._acquire_cron_lock() now acquires a mutex keyed off
  LOCK_PATH + ".mutex" (kept separate from the lock file itself so its
  on-disk format and every existing test are untouched) before the
  exists()-check, and releases it in a finally covering every return path;
  failure to acquire the mutex itself fails closed (returns False), matching
  the function's existing contract. Zero changes needed to any of the ~15
  pre-existing tests in tests/test_cron_lock.py / tests/
  test_execution_stability.py -- the mutex path is derived from LOCK_PATH at
  call time, so tests that only monkeypatch LOCK_PATH keep working unchanged.
  New tests (tests/test_cron_lock.py::TestAcquireCronLockClosesRace):
  reproduces the audit's own repro technique (a Barrier inside a patched
  Path.exists forcing two threads to the exact check-then-act instant the
  bug needed) and asserts exactly one winner; a second test confirms
  mutex-acquisition failure fails closed. safe_io.py also got a direct
  CrossProcessLock unit-test class (tests/test_safe_io.py::
  TestCrossProcessLock: acquire/release round-trip, second-holder-blocked,
  two-threads-exactly-one-winner-eventually). Mutation-tested: reverting the
  mutex wrap makes the race test fail with results.count(True) == 2 (both
  callers win) instead of 1 -- confirmed live by temporarily reverting and
  re-running.

  Independent opus review (effort:high, single agent covering all 4 items in
  this batch given the shared subsystem) found 9 issues, all fixed (see
  batch-04's combined note on AUD-0051 below for the shared review process
  across all 4 items). Of the 9, one belongs to this entry specifically:
  _release_cron_lock() unlinked the lock file WITHOUT taking the same
  mutex the acquire-side fix above added -- a concurrent _acquire_cron_lock()
  could see lp.exists()==True (under its own mutex hold) and then have
  release's unlink() race its own lp.read_text() a moment later, turning a
  perfectly free lock into a spurious "unreadable lock file" fail-closed
  skip (an entire cron cycle silently dropped). Fixed by wrapping
  _release_cron_lock() in the same CrossProcessLock too (best-effort: still
  unlinks even if the mutex itself can't be acquired, since leaving the
  lock file behind is worse than the narrow race). New regression test
  (tests/test_cron_lock.py::TestAcquireCronLockClosesRace::
  test_release_serialized_against_concurrent_acquire_no_spurious_skip) uses
  a two-event handshake (not incidental thread scheduling, which proved
  non-deterministic on the first attempt at this test) to force the exact
  interleaving; mutation-tested by reverting the release-side mutex --
  confirmed the test then fails with the exact spurious "unreadable lock
  file" log line and a False return where True was expected.

  Full scoped suite (531 tests across cron/settlement/paper/safe_io + every
  file monkeypatching LOCK_PATH, re-counted fresh via --collect-only at
  writing time) passes; ruff+ruff-format+mypy clean via the actual
  pre-commit hooks. Commit: (added post-push).

[RESOLVED 2026-08-19 -- batch-02] Ambiguous place_order() failure can leave a real live position permanently untracked, unprotected, and re-orderable
Priority: HIGH (audit id AUD-0007, status CONFIRMED, confidence HIGH, evidence E1)
Files: kalshi_client.py, execution_log.py, order_executor.py, main.py

Problem:
  place_order() catches any exception from the create-order POST and tries to determine whether the order landed anyway via _find_order_by_client_id (3 sequential GET-based lookups: resting, executed, canceled). If all 3 lookups also fail, place_order re-raises the original exception even though the order may have genuinely landed on Kalshi. The caller then logs the row status='failed'. Every dedup/anti-thrash guard in execution_log.py deliberately excludes status='failed' rows, and...
  Root cause: The 'failed' status is overloaded to mean both 'genuinely never sent' (correctly excluded from dedup) and 'sent, but outcome unknown due to a correlated failure in both the placement call and its own reconciliation check' (a rarer but real case). No distinct status/recovery path exists for the...
  Evidence: Independently re-read the full chain: kalshi_client.py 517-534 (place_order except block re-raises only when _find_order_by_client_id returns None), 551-608 (all 3 lookup passes independently swallow exceptions), execution_log.py's 4 dedup functions (278-380, all exclude status='failed'), order_executor.py 269-355 (_recover_pending_orders filters strictly on status=='pending'), and...
  Financial risk: A real live position could sit completely unmanaged indefinitely, and a subsequent retry could double real capital exposure on the same signal with neither copy protected.
  Recommendation: Distinguish 'confirmed never sent' from 'ambiguous outcome, reconciliation itself failed' with a separate status (e.g. 'unknown'), and have a recovery routine periodically re-check 'unknown'/'failed' live-order rows against the Kalshi API until confirmed.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-21 -- batch-08] Between-bucket settlement lock-in can lock YES off the instantaneous METAR reading despite a lower authoritative daily-high, contradicting its own documented invariant
Priority: MEDIUM (audit id AUD-0016, status CONFIRMED, confidence VERY HIGH, evidence E2)
Files: settlement_monitor.py, metar.py, cron.py, tests/test_settlement_monitor.py

Problem:
  settlement_monitor._check_between_settlement()'s YES branch computes `comp_temp = max(current_temp_f, max_temp_f)` and locks YES when `max_temp_f is not None and lower_f <= comp_temp <= upper_f`. When the freshest instantaneous reading (current_temp_f) exceeds the independently-cached authoritative running daily high (max_temp_f), comp_temp reduces to current_temp_f and the lock is decided purely by the instantaneous reading -- contradicting the function's own docstring ('YES only from a REAL max_temp_f; never locks YES from the current_temp_fallback alone') and the test named for that exact...
  Root cause: The `max(current_temp_f, max_temp_f)` combination silently substitutes the instantaneous reading for the authoritative running extreme whenever the instantaneous reading is larger, defeating the 'requires a REAL max_temp_f' guard exactly in the still-rising-temperature case the guard exists to...
  Evidence: Reproduced this session: `_check_between_settlement(current_temp_f=67.0, lower_f=66.5, upper_f=68.5, max_temp_f=65.0)` returns `{'locked': True, 'outcome': 'yes', 'confidence': 0.7749999999999999, 'comp_temp_f': 67.0}` — comp_temp_f == current_temp_f, confirming the lock is decided by the instantaneous reading while max_temp_f (65.0) is still below the band. Verified...
  Financial risk: Feeds paper.close_paper_early() with no human review; a forced YES close on a temperature that has only just entered the band and may still climb books an incorrect settlement outcome, corrupting...
  Recommendation: Gate the in-band/YES check on max_temp_f itself, not max(current_temp_f, max_temp_f); use current_temp_f only for the already-correctly-reasoned NO branch. Add a regression test with max_temp_f present-but-lower-than-current_temp_f.
  Full record: audit/AUDIT_REPORT.json (id AUD-0016), audit/AUDIT_REPORT.md.

Resolution 2026-08-21: Three-pass fix, each pass caught by an independent
  opus review (effort:high) finding a real regression in the previous
  pass -- self-review alone would have shipped either of the first two.
  PASS 1 implemented the recommendation literally: gate strictly on
  max_temp_f, drop comp_temp/max(current_temp_f, max_temp_f) entirely for
  the YES branch. Review 1 found this let a merely-stale max_temp_f
  override a FRESHER current_temp_f that had already cleared the band
  (current=70.0 above a [66.5,68.5] band, stale max_temp_f=66.5 still
  in-band -> locked YES) -- reopening the exact "two independently-cached
  METAR fetches momentarily disagreeing" hazard this module's NO branch is
  documented to guard against, just in the YES direction (confirmed via
  fetch_metar_daily_extreme's own docstring: current_temp_f and max_temp_f
  are genuinely separate cached fetches that CAN disagree). Surfaced the
  resulting design choice via AskUserQuestion given the financial stakes
  (paper P&L feeds is_accuracy_halted -> LiveTradingGate) rather than
  guessing.
  PASS 2 (user-selected fix): keep gating membership on max_temp_f (still
  addresses the original audit's concern) but ADD a fresher-reading veto
  -- refuse YES if current_temp_f itself has cleared upper_f. Review 2
  found this veto only covers the extreme sub-case: it kept using
  max_temp_f (not comp_temp) for the CLEARANCE calculation, which is
  STRICTLY MORE PERMISSIVE than pre-batch HEAD for the whole disagreement
  window between max_temp_f and upper_f (e.g. current=68.0, stale
  max_temp_f=66.5, band=[66.5,68.5]: HEAD correctly refused; pass 2 locked
  YES at confidence 0.800 -- exactly cron.py's force-close threshold). The
  batch's own "positive control" test encoded this regression as intended
  behavior.
  PASS 3 (FINAL, review-2-recommended minimal fix): keep membership gated
  on max_temp_f (unchanged, addresses the original audit's concern), but
  measure CLEARANCE against comp_temp instead of max_temp_f, and remove
  the pass-2 veto entirely (redundant once clearance uses comp_temp: since
  comp_temp >= max_temp_f always, using comp_temp can only SHRINK the
  measured clearance relative to max_temp_f, never grow it -- so this
  can't resurrect the original AUD-0016 bug, which required max_temp_f
  itself to be in-band independent of comp_temp -- while it correctly
  refuses the lock the instant a fresher current_temp_f eats into the
  margin, all the way to current_temp_f clearing upper_f outright, which
  drives clearance negative and fails the margin check with no separate
  veto needed). Returned "comp_temp_f" on a YES lock now reports comp_temp
  (the value clearance/confidence were actually computed from), not
  max_temp_f -- safe because locked=True guarantees comp_temp <= upper_f -
  margin, so it's never outside the band that justified the lock.
  Also fixed, same review passes, same file/function area (adjacency, step
  18): (1) check_city_settlement's between-bucket signal log line
  unconditionally said "daily-high" even when the logged comp_temp_f value
  was really just current_temp_f (whenever current > max_temp_f, which
  comp_temp_f can still equal even with max_temp_f present) -- exactly the
  mislabeling class the AC3 bug's own postmortem says let it go unnoticed.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-19 -- fixed as part of batch-03] cmd_order's unmatched-sell settlement fallback can leave the exact phantom-position shape its own fix was designed to prevent
Priority: MEDIUM (audit id AUD-0026, status CONFIRMED, confidence HIGH, evidence E1)
Files: main.py, execution_log.py

Problem:
  When a manual live sell via cmd_order has no matching tracked position, the code immediately calls record_live_early_exit(row_id, price, 'unmatched_sell', 0.0) specifically so the just-logged row isn't later misread as a new open position by the automated exit scanner. That call is wrapped only in a broad except Exception with a warning log and no retry or alternate fail-closed handling.
  Root cause: If the record_live_early_exit DB write itself fails, the row is left exactly in the dangerous shape (live=True, status='filled', settled_at=NULL, closes_position_id=None) the surrounding comment says must never happen -- there is no retry and no compensating mechanism.
  Evidence: Independently re-read main.py's unmatched-sell branch (4806-4829): the try/except around record_live_early_exit only logs a warning, no retry. Confirmed execution_log.get_filled_unsettled_live_orders() (535-556) WHERE clause matches exactly `live = 1 AND status = 'filled' AND settled_at IS NULL AND closes_position_id IS NULL` -- exactly the row shape this failure leaves.
  Financial risk: Low direct financial risk (spurious exit orders should be rejected by Kalshi as there's no real position to sell), but produces a recurring, silent operational anomaly and log/alert noise, and...
  Recommendation: Add a bounded retry to this specific settle call, or fail closed by writing a distinct marker/flag file the operator is alerted to.
  Full record: audit/AUDIT_REPORT.json (id AUD-0026), audit/AUDIT_REPORT.md.

Resolution 2026-08-19: per explicit design decision (AskUserQuestion), took
  the combined "bounded retry + marker file" option over retry-only or
  flag-only. New execution_log.record_live_early_exit_with_retry() wraps
  record_live_early_exit with up to 3 attempts (short backoff between
  retries -- ordinary lock contention is already absorbed by sqlite3.connect's
  own 30s busy-timeout before an exception ever reaches this function, so a
  retry here only helps the rarer non-lock transient failure); if every
  attempt still fails, appends {order_id, exit_reason, error, flagged_at} to
  a new persistent sentinel file (execution_log_unsettled_exit_rows.json,
  mirroring the existing _degraded_flag_path pattern) instead of only a
  warning log line, and logs at ERROR level. cmd_order's unmatched-sell
  branch now calls this wrapper instead of a single bare attempt. New tests
  (tests/test_execution_log.py, TestRecordLiveEarlyExitWithRetry, 4 tests):
  first-attempt success writes no flag; recovers within the retry budget
  after 2 simulated transient failures; exhausted retries writes the
  sentinel flag and returns False (row genuinely stays unsettled -- the
  wrapper cannot conjure a write the DB refuses); flag file accumulates
  across multiple failed rows rather than overwriting. Full scoped suite +
  broader regression sweep (see AUD-0003's resolution note for the exact
  file list/counts) pass. ruff + ruff-format + mypy clean via the actual
  pre-commit hook.

Every mutation-testing claim independently verified via Edit-revert-restore, including on both review rounds' own fixes.
  Two full independent opus reviews (effort=high), each targeted specifically at this live-order path: round 1 found the HIGH-severity exit-price flaw above plus the DEBUG-logging and _settlement_sigs-clobber MEDIUMs and 2 LOWs (missing non-fill test, missing ticker-mismatch/client=None tests) -- all fixed. [RESOLVED 2026-08-25 (batch-60 item 4) -- originally found by max-depth forensic audit and filed for tracking. Priority: LOW (audit id AUD-0036, status CONFIRMED, confidence HIGH, evidence E1)

Problem:
  Multiple live positions can legally share a ticker+side because nothing prevents duplicate live entries (same root cause as the check_position_limits() blindness finding). closes_position_id supports referencing only one prior row per exit.
  Evidence: Read main.py:4577-4666 directly, confirming the code, the 'Opus review (2026-08-17), NEW-M1' comment, and the yellow warning print exactly as described. Additionally verified the 'oldest' claim at the SQL level (beyond the original finding's evidence): order_executor._get_live_open_positions() (order_executor.py:1077-1115) calls execution_log.get_filled_unsettled_live_orders()...

  Recommendation: Already correctly deferred by its own authors pending the exposure-cap fix (Finding 1), which is the real root cause preventing duplicate live entries from accumulating. No independent action recommended.
  Full record: audit/AUDIT_REPORT.json (id AUD-0036), audit/AUDIT_REPORT.md.

Resolution (2026-08-25, batch-60 item 4):
  Re-decided via AskUserQuestion rather than inheriting "no independent
  action recommended" -- that recommendation was explicitly conditional on
  the exposure-cap root cause being open, and it closed 2026-08-18. Options
  put to the user: (a) operator selects which position, (b) FIFO cascade,
  (c) keep oldest-only and downgrade to a documented accepted risk. Chose
  (b).

  Re-deriving the entry from source first turned up a sharper defect than
  it describes. The entry frames this as "closes the oldest and warns" --
  an incompleteness. But record_live_exit_fill CLAMPS its fill_count to the
  named position's own quantity, so a sell spanning two positions (10 sold,
  oldest holds 4) fully closed the 4 and left the other 6 marked OPEN in
  execution_log with no contracts behind them on the exchange. That
  overstates open exposure and invites the protective-exit scanner to try
  selling them again. It is a corruption, not just a gap.

  Shipped: the filled count is consumed oldest-first across every match,
  each settled against its own entry price. closes_position_id still names
  only the first match (the schema supports one referenced row per exit),
  so the operator warning stays -- reworded, since "only closes the oldest
  one" is no longer true; it now says the sell is applied oldest-first and
  that only the oldest is recorded as the linkage. An over-sell beyond
  every tracked position is now reported rather than silently clamped away.

  Two defects the cascade itself introduced, both caught by opus review and
  fixed here:
  - F2: with a trailing PARTIAL leg, the sell row's closes_position_id
    still named the OLDEST match (it is resolved before placement, as it
    must be -- log_order writes the row up front so a crash mid-flight
    leaves a reconcilable record), but the leg whose P&L lands on that row
    is the LAST one touched. export_live_tax_csv self-joins on that column
    for the entry price and reads COALESCE(fill_quantity, quantity) for the
    amount, so a 4+6 cascade exported 4 contracts at 0.40 and 10 contracts
    at 0.40 -- 14 disposed for a 10-contract sale, the second leg against
    the wrong cost basis. Rolled-up P&L (get_live_pnl_summary) was correct
    throughout; this was a quantity-and-basis defect, which on a tax export
    is its own kind of wrong. Fixed by a new
    execution_log.set_exit_row_attribution(order_id, position_id,
    fill_quantity), called immediately before record_live_early_exit in the
    partial branch. A no-op in the single-match case both the pre-cascade
    code and order_executor._exit_live_position produce, so it is called
    unconditionally rather than only when the cascade spanned. The first
    version of the test for this branch had PINNED the bug
    (asserting closes_position_id == older_id); corrected, and the export
    is now asserted at the CSV level.
  - F11: record_live_exit_fill raises RuntimeError for exactly one cause --
    a concurrent writer (cron / `watch --auto --live`) settled the position
    between the pre-placement snapshot and now. Lumping that in with the
    generic handler meant a benign race on the FIRST match aborted the
    whole cascade, leaving 100% of a real sale unattributed and a later
    position marked open with contracts that no longer exist: exactly the
    state this item exists to prevent, in the one scenario the guard was
    written for. RuntimeError now skips to the next match WITHOUT
    decrementing the remaining fill (those contracts were never ours to
    attribute); every other exception still stops the cascade, since an
    unknown-cause failure must not silently re-attribute one position's
    contracts to another.

  Tests (tests/test_batch60_trade_entry_guards.py has its own; these are in
  tests/test_trading_gates.py::TestCmdOrderLiveRecording): a fill that fits
  inside the oldest match still behaves exactly as before (regression lock,
  newer position still open via a _get_live_open_positions positive
  control); a fill spanning two positions settles both against their own
  distinct entry prices (0.40/0.45, chosen so crediting the wrong one shows
  up as wrong P&L rather than a coincidental match) and leaves nothing
  claiming phantom contracts; a fill landing partway into the second leaves
  it open at the reduced size with the partial P&L on the sell row,
  attributed to the position it actually came from; the tax export reports
  each leg exactly once totalling the real 10; an over-sell warns with a
  positive control that both positions genuinely settled; an unknown-cause
  failure (sqlite3.OperationalError, deliberately not a RuntimeError) stops
  the cascade and reports the unattributed remainder; and a mid-flight
  concurrent settle is skipped with the full fill moving to the surviving
  match. The pre-existing
  test_live_sell_with_multiple_tracked_positions_closes_only_oldest was
  renamed and rewritten -- its name and its "only closes the oldest"
  assertion both described the old behaviour.

  Not fixed here, filed as its own entry at the top of this file:
  order_executor._settle_recovered_exit_order still does the old
  oldest-only thing on the ASYNC route (cmd_order re-raises on
  OrderStatusUnknownError before the cascade block is ever reached, and
  _recover_pending_orders settles that row later from the single stored
  pointer). Different function, different trigger, and it needs a
  retry-semantics decision the synchronous path does not have -- step 27's
  same-payload test puts it in a separate entry rather than stretching this
  change to cover it.

  instead of an uncaught crash. (2) The stale-.tmp-restore guard
  restructured from a single `if exists and not kill_switch_exists` into an
  if/else: the new else branch discards an orphaned .kill_switch.tmp when
  .kill_switch is ALSO present (the exact black-swan-recreated-it-mid-hard-
  kill scenario this finding describes) instead of leaving it on disk
  forever. New tests (tests/test_cron_integration.py::
  TestKillSwitchOverrideRenameRace, 3 cases): the exact audit scenario
  (orphaned .tmp + re-created .kill_switch, answer 'y' to override) no
  longer crashes and the orphan is discarded; the original restore-from-
  orphan path (no .kill_switch present) still works unchanged; a normal
  override with no orphan involved still completes. Mutation-tested by
  reverting BOTH changes together (reverting only the guard, with the
  replace fix still in place, did NOT reproduce the crash -- overwrite-safe
  replace semantics alone already prevented it, so isolating the guard's
  own necessity required reverting both): the first test then fails with
  the exact real-world `FileExistsError: [WinError 183] Cannot create a
  file when that file already exists` the audit's own evidence section
  reproduced standalone.

  Opus review (see AUD-0006's note above) found 3 issues in this fix,
  all fixed: (a) HIGH -- the initial implementation used bare os.replace()
  at all 3 sites, which this repo's own tests/test_bare_os_replace_guard.py
  bans outside safe_io.py precisely because bare os.replace() on Windows
  can raise a transient PermissionError/WinError 5 whenever another
  thread/process has the destination open even just for reading (self-
  caught 2026-08-08, see that guard's own docstring) -- the guard test
  itself was failing and "full scoped suite passes" as first written above
  was false, since that guard wasn't in the scoped run. Fixed by routing
  all 3 sites through safe_io._replace_with_retry() instead (the same
  retry-wrapped helper every other Windows file-replace in this codebase
  already uses), and adding a `tests/test_cron_integration.py` allowlist
  entry for 2 docstring mentions of the old rename()/os.replace() semantics
  gap this fix closed. (b) MEDIUM -- the restore-back step in the finally
  block (former L384-388) was left completely unguarded despite (a)'s fix
  guarding the move-aside step -- an OSError there would replace any
  in-flight exception from the cron cycle and escape as an uncaught
  traceback, skipping the "restored" confirmation. Wrapped in try/except
  OSError with an ERROR log, matching the move-aside step's own guard
  shape. (c) LOW/MEDIUM -- in the narrow TOCTOU window between checking
  .kill_switch.exists() and acting on it in that same finally block, a
  black-swan check on a genuinely separate process could re-create
  .kill_switch with a fresh reason between the check and the act; the
  fix's own re-check-then-branch structure (unlink the stale .tmp if
  .kill_switch reappeared, else restore from it) already handles this
  correctly by construction -- documented explicitly in a comment rather
  than changed further, since eliminating the TOCTOU window entirely would
  need locking .kill_switch itself, out of scope given the audit's own
  "financial risk: low/none, diagnostics loss only" framing) held even
  with this narrower race included. Full scoped suite (531 tests,
  re-counted fresh via --collect-only at writing time) passes;
  ruff+ruff-format+mypy clean via the actual pre-commit hooks (including
  the bare-os.replace guard, now passing).
