UPDATE 2026-08-20 (2nd independent opus review, effort=high, reviewing the
  redesigned code fresh rather than just re-checking review 1's checklist):
  found 0 HIGH, confirming the redesign's core statistic and every review-1
  fix (cache keys, fetch/blend split, floor logic, all 8 rewritten test
  arithmetic, EMOS boundaries) as actually correct this time. Found MEDIUM-
  1/2/3 + LOW-1..4 + INFO-1/2/3/5 (INFO-4 noted, no action needed -- stale
  4-element disk-cache keys from before this change are simply unreachable
  and expire via TTL, not a live problem). All addressed:
  MEDIUM-1 (the one real remaining statistical gap): z's denominator used
  only own's standard error, treating peer_mean as a known constant --
  but peer_mean is itself estimated from 1-2 peers with their own sampling
  uncertainty. Re-querying live prod data with the correct two-sample
  pooled SE showed this mattered concretely: gfs_seamless (still the live
  motivating case) sat right at the trip boundary, with ~16% of z's value
  coming purely from the omitted peer-uncertainty term (worse, ~41% at
  k=1 peer, the case once one member is already quarantined). Fixed:
  se = sqrt(own.std^2/own.n + sum(peer.std^2/peer.n for peer in peers) /
  len(peers)^2) -- the standard pooled two-sample formula.
  MEDIUM-2: neither threshold had a practical-significance floor -- since
  se shrinks as ~1/sqrt(n) and get_member_accuracy's window can grow to
  ~420 observations as trading coverage improves, the z-test alone would
  eventually treat an arbitrarily small, real-world-meaningless MAE gap as
  "significant." Added _QUARANTINE_MIN_EFFECT_F=0.5 (°F) as an ADDITIONAL
  requirement alongside (not instead of) the z-threshold for TRIP
  specifically -- release stays purely ewma_z-gated, since an already-
  quarantined member's recovery is about its z normalizing, not a fresh
  minimum-effect test. New regression test constructs n=10,000 to make the
  z-only threshold trip on a sub-0.5°F gap, confirms the effect floor
  blocks it.
  MEDIUM-3 (the other one the reviewer flagged as must-fix): load_member_
  quarantine_state() returns the SAME cached dict object on a cache hit,
  and scan_member_quarantine() was mutating it in place -- so a failed
  _save_member_quarantine_state() call (write error, disk full) still left
  this process's in-memory cache holding the never-persisted mutation for
  the rest of the process's life, meaning it kept "trading" against a
  decision disk never actually recorded, while every other process
  (reading disk directly) silently disagreed. This is the exact hazard
  save_learned_weights() already documents and guards against for the
  identical reason. Fixed: scan_member_quarantine() now works on
  `copy.deepcopy(load_member_quarantine_state())`, never the cached object
  itself; _save_member_quarantine_state() now returns a bool so a failed
  persist gets its own ERROR log line (computed-but-unsaved) instead of
  silently reporting success. New regression test forces the write to
  raise, confirms a fresh read after the "failure" still returns the
  pre-scan (unmutated) state.
  LOW-1: pre_scan_quarantined's set comprehension lacked the isinstance
  guard the rest of the module already has -- a corrupted per-model state
  value would AttributeError, silently caught at _log.debug by cron.py's
  broad except and permanently disabling quarantine. Added.
  LOW-2: get_quarantined_members()'s defensive read-time floor clamp
  (added in review 1's own MEDIUM-10 fix) sorted by -ewma_z with NO
  secondary key -- an exact tie fell through to set-iteration order,
  which isn't guaranteed stable across processes, so two processes reading
  an identical corrupted state file could each keep a DIFFERENT model
  quarantined, splitting the ensemble cache's quarantine-tag namespace
  between them. Added the same (-ewma_z, model_name) tiebreak pass 2
  already used. New test constructs an exact tie inside an over-floor
  state file, confirms both processes would agree.
  LOW-3: the "3 real blend models" tuple was independently reconstructed
  in 3 places (_QUARANTINE_CANDIDATE_MODELS, batch_prewarm_ensemble's
  _real_blend_models, get_ensemble_temps' inline list) -- a future edit to
  one without the others would blend DIFFERENT model sets under an
  IDENTICAL _quarantine_cache_tag()-keyed cache entry, corrupting whichever
  path filled it last, silently. Consolidated to one source of truth
  (_QUARANTINE_CANDIDATE_MODELS); _model_weights()'s own "graduating a
  model needs BOTH steps" docstring checklist updated to name it as the
  now-single required 3rd edit site (previously said "the live-blend fetch
  lists," plural, which no longer describes the code).
  LOW-4: scan_member_quarantine()'s candidate_models= parameter had no
  caller and no test, and using it with a subset would have silently
  diverged from get_quarantined_members()'s own floor (which always
  clamps against the FULL candidate set regardless of what a caller passed
  the scan) -- two floors that could disagree. Removed the parameter
  entirely rather than leave untested, unused optionality with a latent
  correctness trap.
  INFO-1: a test docstring said "raw z >= 1/lambda = 10"; 1/lambda is 5,
  2/lambda is 10 (the actual value that reaches the 2.0 trip line from a
  cold seed in one scan). Fixed; the module docstring already had this
  right.
  INFO-2: get_member_accuracy() used population stdev (pstdev, ddof=0); a
  standard-error calculation conventionally uses sample stdev (ddof=1).
  At n>=20 the difference is under 2.6% and both push z the same
  direction as the more consequential MEDIUM-1, but switched for
  correctness. Updated the one dependent test.
  INFO-3: the mtime memoization cache was keyed on mtime alone, not
  (path, mtime) -- two different files sharing a coarse-resolution
  filesystem's mtime tick (plausible across different tests each
  redirecting MEMBER_QUARANTINE_PATH to their own tmp_path) could serve
  one's cached contents for the other. Re-keyed by (str(path), mtime).
  INFO-5: the docstring called the window "recent (14-day) MAE" without
  clarifying it's actually "scored (logged_at) within the last 14 days,"
  not "for a target_date within the last 14 days" -- a backfill re-scoring
  old target dates would land in the window under the real semantics.
  Clarified in the docstring.
  Full re-run after this round of fixes: 20/20 in the quarantine test
  classes (up from 14 -- 2 new tests for MEDIUM-2/MEDIUM-3, 1 for the
  read-time tiebreak, plus the existing set re-derived against the new
  pooled-SE formula via a shared _se() test helper that mirrors production
  exactly, rather than hand-recomputed literals that could silently drift
  out of sync with a future formula change again); full
  test_weather_markets.py (286 passed/4 skipped) and test_tracker.py (408
  passed/1 pre-existing unrelated failure, same UTC-vs-local-today flake

  first run this time.
  A 3rd opus review round was NOT run for this batch -- judgment call,
  not a process skip: these fixes were surgical corrections to specific,
  already-enumerated findings (a formula substitution, a copy-before-

[RESOLVED 2026-08-25 -- batch-59 item 4; originally OPEN 2026-08-20 -- filed as a review-caught follow-up (MEDIUM-9) rather
  than expanded into the quarantine change above; genuinely separate
  consumer/file, not this change's own file-line citations.]
  ANALYZE_TRADE'S model_consensus CHECK (AND ORDER_EXECUTOR'S KELLY-HALVING)
  DOESN'T EXCLUDE A QUARANTINED ENSEMBLE MEMBER
Priority: Low-Medium -- not a correctness bug (halving position size when a
  known-biased model disagrees is a conservative, not dangerous, side
  effect), but it means weather_markets.py's own quarantine module
  docstring's original "the only way to actually stop trading on it" claim
  was an overclaim until corrected -- quarantine only excludes a member
  from the ENSEMBLE BLEND, not from this independent consensus/sizing
  signal.

Problem:
  weather_markets.py's analyze_trade() computes `model_consensus` by
  directly comparing icon_seamless's and gfs_seamless's own probabilities
  (via _get_consensus_probs, which is deliberately quarantine-unaware so
  accuracy tracking/recovery continues) -- `if abs(icon_p - gfs_p) > 0.12:
  model_consensus = False`. order_executor.py then applies `consensus_mult
  = 0.5 if not model_consensus else 1.0` to position sizing. If
  gfs_seamless is quarantined for a confirmed bias, it still fully
  participates in this check -- and since it's biased, it will disagree
  with icon more often, which means positions get MORE conservatively
  sized (not more aggressively) exactly when the quarantine fired. Low risk
  today, but the behavior doesn't match what an operator would reasonably
  expect from "this model is quarantined."
Recommendation: decide explicitly (AskUserQuestion -- this is a judgment
  call, not obviously correct either way) whether model_consensus should
  (a) skip the comparison entirely when either compared model is
  quarantined (falls back to model_consensus=True, i.e. no penalty), or
  (b) keep comparing but substitute a non-quarantined peer's probability
  for the quarantined model's own, or (c) leave as-is and just keep the
  corrected docstring. Needs its own scoped change to order_executor.py/
  weather_markets.py's analyze_trade, not a stretch of the quarantine
  module itself.

Resolution (2026-08-25 -- batch-59 item 4):
  SHIPPED, option (a) from this entry's own Recommendation, chosen by the
  user via AskUserQuestion exactly as the entry asked for.

  analyze_trade's model_consensus check now skips the icon-vs-gfs divergence
  comparison entirely when either member of that pair is quarantined, leaving
  model_consensus at its True default -- identical to what the branch already
  does when either probability comes back None. Membership is
  `get_quarantined_members() & set(ENSEMBLE_MODELS)`, reusing the same
  quarantine source of truth blend_models uses rather than a third hand-copied
  pair of model-name literals; ENSEMBLE_MODELS is exactly the pair
  _get_consensus_probs fetches, pinned by its own test.

  Option (b) (substitute a non-quarantined peer) was rejected for the reason
  the code already documents: _get_consensus_probs deliberately does not
  return ecmwf_aifs025_ensemble's probability, its Gaussian/vote-fraction
  methodology differs, and picking a 3-way divergence threshold is its own
  unscoped backlog item. There is no second surviving comparator, so
  excluding one member leaves nothing to compare -- the check cannot be
  "kept," only skipped.

  Exposure trade-off, recorded explicitly because this is the one item in
  batch-59 that INCREASES position size: during a quarantine window
  consensus_mult goes 0.5 -> 1.0, doubling the stake relative to prior
  behaviour, in the regime where the blend is thinnest. An opus reviewer
  argued for the opposite (leave model_consensus=False, the conservative
  direction this repo picks elsewhere) on the grounds that a wide icon-gfs
  spread is a forecast-uncertainty proxy independent of which model is more
  accurate. That counter-argument was put to the user as a third option and
  fail-open was reaffirmed: a quarantined model is one the blend has already
  stopped trusting, so shrinking positions on its disagreement is penalising
  noise -- which is precisely what this entry was filed to stop. Currently
  inert: all three candidates are quarantined=false in
  data/member_quarantine.json.

  Interaction with the adjacent open entry (EMOS/anomaly/bimodal guards fit
  on the unfiltered 3-model blend) checked as the batch required: this change
  does not make it worse -- it touches neither the blend nor its spread -- but
  it does make the pipeline asymmetric during a quarantine window, removing
  the bad model where it made the system more cautious while leaving it where
  it contaminates calibration. Noted on that entry too so the two get
  sequenced together.

  Also flagged by review, filed rather than fixed: model_consensus now
  conflates "the models agreed" with "we did not check", and that value is
  persisted to predictions.model_consensus and fed to main.py's
  model_agreement feature, so quarantine-window rows are unmarked. A third
  state cannot simply be written -- order_executor.py's
  `0.5 if not a.get("model_consensus", True) else 1.0` treats None as falsy
  and would apply the halving it was just decided not to apply -- so it needs
  its own consumer change. See the new entry "MODEL_CONSENSUS CONFLATES
  'AGREED' WITH 'NOT CHECKED'".

  Mutation-tested: quarantine exclusion disabled -> 2 tests fail; the
  `& set(ENSEMBLE_MODELS)` pair filter removed (so quarantining the non-pair
  ecmwf member also suppresses the check) -> 1 fails.

  Tests: 625 passed across the scoped suite; ruff + ruff-format + mypy clean
  via the real pre-commit hook.


[OPEN 2026-08-20 -- filed as a review-caught follow-up (2nd review's

  QUARANTINE CHANGES THE LIVE ENSEMBLE BLEND'S SPREAD, BUT SPREAD-BASED
  CALIBRATIONS (EMOS, ANOMALY/BIMODAL GUARDS) ARE FIT ON THE UNFILTERED
  3-MODEL BLEND
Priority: Low today (EMOS is not active -- no data/emos_params.json exists,
  and the ~80-row go-live bar this same change corrected the cron banner
  to reflect is not yet cleared), but worth tracking explicitly since this
  same change is what steers the operator toward EMOS activation crossing
  that bar on roughly the same timescale a real quarantine event might
  first fire on.

Problem:
  _compute_ensemble_prob feeds the blend's ens_stats["std"]**2 into
  emos_exceedance_prob's variance term, and EMOS's own c/d variance-
  calibration coefficients (when eventually fit via `py main.py emos-train`)
  will be fit from historical ens_var rows produced by the CURRENT 3-model
  blend's spread. The same spread also feeds is_forecast_anomalous's
  threshold and the bimodal-ensemble Kelly-reduction guard. Excluding a
  quarantined member systematically narrows (or otherwise shifts) that
  spread relative to what any of these were calibrated against -- so the
  first time a real quarantine event coincides with EMOS being live, EMOS's
  variance calibration would be evaluating a distribution shape it was
  never actually fit on.
Recommendation: before (or as part of) ever activating EMOS, check whether
  its training data should be filtered to only ens_var rows logged while
  the same set of members was active (or whether refitting after any
  quarantine state change is needed), and whether is_forecast_anomalous's/
  the bimodal guard's fixed thresholds implicitly assume a fixed 3-model
  spread. Not urgent while EMOS stays inactive; revisit at the EMOS
  activation decision itself, not before.

  MATERIAL FINDING -- the number moved a lot, but the verdict did not
  flip. Measured on the live corpus 2026-08-24:
      before (unfiltered):  BSS = -0.147866   n=152
      after  (filtered):    BSS = -0.272531   n=94
  The model already showed NO skill against the market before this fix,
  and shows roughly twice as large a shortfall after it. Mechanism: the
  41 'between' rows the filter removes were dragging the MARKET's baseline
  Brier UP (0.2186 -> 0.2008 once gone) while barely moving the model's

  the bracket markets specifically, and pooling them in was flattering our
  relative standing. Same direction as AUD-0004's graduation_check()
  finding (contamination made the model look better than it is), just on a
  display statistic rather than a gate.

  All 5 sites now derive from tracker's registry; none carries a literal.

  ml_bias/main.py take the PERMANENT constant, per the M5 test this entry
  itself demanded be applied per-site: all four fit temperature-shaped

  separately above as item 1). Consumers re-grepped first, as the entry
  asked -- all four are display/reporting, none gates live trading:
    get_brier_by_days_out    -> web_app.py:516 (dashboard)
    get_brier_by_tier        -> web_app.py:526 (dashboard)
    get_brier_by_version     -> main.py:6519 cmd_version_compare (CLI)
    get_pnl_by_signal_source -> output_formatters.py:523 (CLI)
  All four take the DYNAMIC gate-coupled set (M5 test: each is a
  model-quality signal, not a scale-specific curve fit).

  Measured before/after on the live corpus 2026-08-24:
    get_brier_by_days_out  same_day 0.2665 (n=190) -> 0.2628 (n=120)
                           1-2d     0.2588 (n=137) -> 0.2555 (n=94)
                           (3-5d and 6-10d fall below the existing
                            5-per-bucket floor and stop being reported)
    get_brier_by_tier      med      0.2500 (n=135) -> 0.2543 (n=89)
    get_brier_by_version   v1.0     0.2451 (n=145) -> 0.2583 (n=90)
  get_brier_by_version is the clearest pooled-aggregate case: a version
  spans every condition_type at once, and the contamination was making
  the only shipped version look better than it is -- same direction as
  AUD-0004.

  get_pnl_by_signal_source: EXCLUSION APPLIED, BUT AS A SPLIT, NOT A DROP.
  The entry was right to flag it, and the data confirmed the concern is
  real rather than hypothetical. Checked first, and the name is
  misleading in BOTH directions:
   (a) it is not P&L -- its own docstring says so ("this is a calibration
       hit-rate, not real trade P&L -- it has never joined against
       placed-trade data"); it computes a Brier and a win rate. So the
       "a shadow signal's P&L may be genuinely interesting" concern does
       not apply on those grounds: it is a Brier function like its
       siblings.
   (b) BUT it is the only one of the five already segmented by a
       dimension that is ~1:1 with condition_type, so a plain filter
       would not have CLEANED any group -- it would have DELETED whole
       groups. Live cross-tab 2026-08-24: 'ensemble' is 100%
       above/below/between; 'monthly_rain_bootstrap_tilted' is 100%
       precip_month_total (n=16, brier 0.1713). A plain filter erases the
       rain row outright -- the one place a shadow signal's own
       calibration currently surfaces, and the entire reason it is being
       run in shadow.
  Resolution: excluded rows are scored the same way and returned under a
  reserved sub-dict key (tracker._PNL_EXCLUDED_SHADOW_KEY,
  "_excluded_shadow") instead of entering the top-level per-source
  entries. This mirrors the label-don't-drop convention the function
  ALREADY established for the orthogonal is_shadow flag (n_shadow is
  reported separately rather than the rows being dropped). The exclusion
  still earns its keep on the mixed group: 'ensemble' sheds its 'between'
  rows, 0.2641 (n=130) -> 0.2623 (n=90), with the shed rows visible as
  their own 0.2682 (n=40) entry in the excluded section. The split
  happens per-ROW before grouping, not per-source, so a source spanning
  both populations contributes to each section separately rather than
  being assigned wholesale by its first row. output_formatters.py's
  cmd_pnl_attribution renders the excluded set as a labelled second
  section. The reserved key cannot collide with a real source: every
  signal_source written is a code-controlled method identifier
  (order_executor.py passes analysis["method"], web_app.py passes
  "dashboard") and none begins with an underscore.
  Decision confirmed with the user before implementing.

  ADJACENCY FIX, same change (workflow step 18/27 -- same payload):
  get_brier_by_tier had NO min-sample floor, so it would render a Brier
  computed over any n >= 1. The tier split is by abs(edge), which is not
  independent of condition_type, so the new filter guts the sparse tiers
  specifically: 'strong' n=10 -> 2, 'weak' n=7 -> 3, and the dashboard
  would have shown a two-sample 0.5658 as a real "strong-signal Brier".
  Added min_samples (default 5, matching get_brier_by_days_out's existing
  per-bucket floor); under-populated tiers now report brier=None with
  their real n, and all three keys stay present so web_app.py cannot
  KeyError on a thin corpus. Pre-existing defect, but this change makes
  it materially more likely to fire, so it was fixed here rather than
  deferred. Confirmed with the user before implementing.

  NOT changed, as the entry itself already established:
  get_sameday_calibration() stays unfiltered -- it is the dashboard-facing
  sibling that deliberately differs from get_sameday_calibration_cli() by
  design (see that function's own docstring). The entry classed it as
  "NOT itself a bug, just an existing asymmetry this note is tracking";
  re-read and still true, so it was left alone rather than swept in.
  Also verified NOT a contradiction: docs/grade_audit/preamble.md lists
  get_brier_by_days_out under "SQL -- intentionally unfiltered". That
  note is about days_out only (the function segments by horizon in
  Python and needs the raw `predictions` table for its own same_day
  bucket); it never covered condition_type. The function still reads raw
  `predictions`, and a test pins that the same_day bucket keeps working.

  Tests: 12 new across tests/test_tracker.py (days-out exclusion +
  same_day-still-populated), tests/test_signal_quality.py (tier
  exclusion, floor suppresses-but-keeps-n with a positive control, all
  three keys survive, default floor is 5), tests/test_p9_p10.py (version
  exclusion), tests/test_pnl_attribution.py (excluded family moves to the
  reserved key, a mixed source splits across both sections, reserved key
  absent on a clean corpus, min_samples enforced per-section) and
  tests/test_output_formatters.py (two-section render, shadow-only corpus
  is not reported as "no data", truly-empty still prints the hint).
  Every exclusion assertion is value-first and mutation-tested to a
  numerically distinct number, not just a different row count:
    days_out bucket  0.04     -> 0.34     unfiltered
    tier brier       0.025    -> 0.286667 unfiltered
    version brier    0.09     -> 0.29     unfiltered
    pnl ensemble     0.09     -> 0.365    unsplit
  The min_samples floor was mutation-tested separately (reverting to the
  old `if errs` makes the two floor tests fail with 0.025 and 0.04
  instead of None).

[RESOLVED 2026-08-21 -- see resolution below.] MEMBER QUARANTINE DETECTION
STATISTIC SWAPPED FROM MAE TO PER-MODEL BRIER SCORE
Priority: High -- gates the live ensemble blend; this is the same
  mechanism as the ENSEMBLE MODEL QUALITY entry above (backlog.txt:22540),
  which shipped MAE-based.

Problem:
  Monitoring the MAE-based quarantine mechanism (shipped 2026-08-19/20,
  commits 2315636d/ae4a823b/b018aa24) against real production cron runs
  found it would not trip in time: the "ensemble" method's trade-level
  directional accuracy sat at 35% (7/20, paper.get_all_trades()) while
  gfs_seamless's peer-relative MAE z-score sat only barely over the 2.0
  trip threshold -- EWMA's asymptotic-approach property meant another
  ~18+ days of scans before it would actually trip, despite the underlying
  problem being severe and unchanged. Digging further: a cruder per-model
  directional check (does each model's raw forecast cross the market
  threshold on the correct side) showed gfs_seamless was actually the BEST
  of the three models (57.9% win rate) -- not the worst -- because its
  known warm bias happened to align with "above-threshold" outcomes during
  a hot stretch, by luck, not skill. Neither MAE (magnitude-only, blind to
  threshold proximity) nor raw threshold-crossing win/loss (rewards a
  biased-but-lucky call) is a trustworthy signal for this failure mode.

Resolution (2026-08-21):
  Swapped the detection statistic to per-model BRIER SCORE: each model's
  raw forecast temp is converted to a calibrated implied probability (the
  existing weather_markets.gaussian_probability() + get_historical_sigma())
  and scored against the real trade outcome, matching how the rest of this
  codebase already treats Brier score as the authoritative accuracy metric
  (tracker.brier_score_by_method, strategy retirement/graduation gates).
  The EWMA/pooled-SE/asymmetric-hysteresis/floor machinery in
  scan_member_quarantine() needed zero structural changes -- it only ever
  consumes own[stat]/peer[stat]/.std/.n, agnostic to which stat that is.
    - Schema: ensemble_member_scores gained implied_prob/brier columns
      (_SCHEMA_VERSION 59->61).
    - tracker.log_member_score() gained optional implied_prob/brier params.
    - paper._score_ensemble_members() (the live settlement-time hook) now
      also resolves condition_type from the raw predictions table (NOT the
      multiday_predictions view, which excludes days_out=0 and would
      silently blank same-day trades) and computes implied_prob/brier per
      model when condition_type is above/below and a threshold exists;
      soft-degrades to brier=None (MAE logging still fires) for quick-buy
      trades with no predictions row, or non-directional conditions.
    - New tracker.get_member_brier(days_back=14) mirrors get_member_accuracy()'s
      shape exactly ({model: {brier, n, std, city_breakdown, city_n_breakdown}}).
    - New tracker.backfill_member_brier(trades) -- ensemble_member_scores has
      no ticker column (can't iterate it directly), so this takes paper trade
      records as a param and joins ticker->condition_type/settled_temp_f the
      same way the live path does. Safe to re-run (UPDATE ... WHERE brier IS
      NULL); per-trade try/except so one malformed record doesn't abort the
      batch. Wired as `backfill-member-brier` CLI command (main.py, mirroring
      the existing backfill-ensemble-var precedent).
    - scan_member_quarantine(): renamed _QUARANTINE_MIN_EFFECT_F ->
      _QUARANTINE_MIN_EFFECT (dropped the °F-specific naming/units -- the
      WARNING log line's "%.2f°F" format was also fixed to a unitless
      "%.4f", since Brier scores need more precision than a 2-decimal °F
      value). Added a one-time state-reset: a model whose stored state
      predates this swap (has last_own_mae but no last_own_brier) has its
      ewma_z reset to 0.0 rather than carrying an MAE-scale EWMA value
      forward into the Brier-scale one -- the two statistics are on
      incompatible units and silently blending them would corrupt the
      running average. Legacy MAE-era keys are stripped once an entry is
      rewritten.
  Independent opus review (effort=high) before push found 2 HIGH and 7
  MEDIUM real issues in the first implementation, all fixed here (not
  deferred):
    HIGH-1: implied_prob/brier used the RAW ticker threshold
      (trade["condition_threshold"], e.g. 85.0 for a T85 "above" ticker)
      instead of the continuous decision boundary the rest of this codebase
      uses for probability math (utils.prob_threshold()/weather_markets.
      _prob_threshold(): threshold+0.5 for above, threshold-0.5 for below --
      Kalshi's real rule is "greater than N", so integer settlement must be
      N+1 or higher; the live engine's own Gaussian call already does this,
      weather_markets.py's analyze_trade path). Every stored implied_prob
      was systematically biased toward YES. Fixed in both
      paper._score_ensemble_members() and tracker.backfill_member_brier().
    HIGH-2: sigma used the raw, undiscounted get_historical_sigma() output
      instead of sigma * sigma_mult, where sigma_mult is the time-of-day/
      horizon uncertainty discount from _time_risk() that the live engine
      always applies (up to 2x tighter near close). Fixed by giving
      _time_risk() an optional now= override (existing 2 live call sites
      unaffected, default unchanged) so both scoring paths can reconstruct
      what sigma_mult WOULD HAVE BEEN as of trade["entered_at"], not "now"
      (which is long after close_time by the time a trade settles).
    Both together moved the real 14-day-window numbers only modestly (gfs
    z: 0.459->0.454; see corrected real-data verification below) -- the
    review's own re-derivation found this was "luck of this sample, not a
    bound," i.e. NOT guaranteed to stay small in general.
    MEDIUM-1/MEDIUM-2: the original calibration (25% of the real observed
    worst-vs-peer-mean gap, n=32) was unstable -- a single new settlement
    moved the observed gap ~39%, and at the real observed dispersion the
    resulting floor (0.008) was ~17x smaller than the effect size the
    z>=2.0 threshold alone already requires, making it a near no-op.
    Re-anchored _QUARANTINE_MIN_EFFECT to 0.02 instead -- this codebase's
    OWN already-load-bearing Brier decision gap (graduation gate 0.23 vs
    retirement threshold 0.25), a fixed constant rather than a small live
    sample.
    MEDIUM-3: the legacy-state ewma_z reset (see below) left the
    `quarantined` flag untouched, so a model quarantined under MAE would
    silently auto-release on the very first Brier-scale scan (ewma_z =
    0.2*fresh_z sits at/below the 0.5 release line for essentially any real
    z). Fixed: release is explicitly suppressed for exactly one scan when
    a currently-quarantined model hits the legacy-reset path; ewma_z still
    updates normally so the next scan's release check uses real momentum.
    MEDIUM-4: log_member_score()'s INSERT OR IGNORE means a second
    settlement for an already-logged (city,model,target_date,var) key with
    NULL brier can never get a computable Brier retroactively without
    running the (not cron-wired) backfill. Documented as a known,
    accepted gap -- not fixed here, backfill_member_brier() already exists
    as the repair path.
    MEDIUM-5/MEDIUM-6: backfill_member_brier()'s early `continue`s (not
    settled, no model_forecast_means) didn't increment any counter, so
    "238 trades, 198 rows updated, 0 errored" looked like near-total
    success when only 34/238 trades were ever evaluated. Fixed: every
    `continue` now increments `skipped`, and the except block now logs the
    real exception via _log.debug instead of swallowing it silently.
    MEDIUM-7: `condition_type='below'` was completely untested in both
    scoring paths -- a hardcoded 'above' at either call site would have
    passed every other test. Added a below-direction test (with an exact
    expected-probability assertion) to both test_paper_metrics.py and
    test_tracker.py.
    Also added a regression guard (opus-review finding, no severity tier
    assigned) pinning _QUARANTINE_MIN_EFFECT to a sane fraction of the
    Brier scale (0, 0.1) -- previously nothing in the suite would have
    caught the floor being raised past 1.0 (a permanent quarantine
    disable), since the largest effect any existing test constructs is 4.5.
  Calibrated _QUARANTINE_MIN_EFFECT against real data (after the HIGH-1/
  HIGH-2 fixes): re-ran the corrected backfill against live production data
  (238 trades, 198 ensemble_member_scores rows updated, 204 now correctly
  counted as skipped, 0 errored), then measured the real worst-vs-peer-mean
  Brier gap on the current 14-day window (tracker.get_member_brier, n=32/
  model): gfs_seamless (own=0.3549) vs peer mean of icon_seamless/
  ecmwf_aifs025_ensemble (0.3202) = 0.0347 gap -- close to but not identical
  to the pre-fix 0.0321, confirming the bugs' net effect on THIS sample was
  modest. Floor set to 0.02 per the re-anchored methodology above (not a
  fraction of this sample); 0.0347 > 0.02, so the floor stays genuinely
  binding without accidentally gating the real motivating case.
  Real-data verification (important, non-obvious result, unaffected by the
  HIGH-1/HIGH-2 corrections): computing the actual peer-relative z-scores on
  the real 14-day window gives gfs_seamless z=0.454, ecmwf_aifs025_ensemble
  z=0.274, icon_seamless z=-0.892 (best). gfs_seamless is still the worst by
  Brier, consistent with the original MAE-era finding -- but the z is
  nowhere near the 2.0 trip threshold. This is NOT a bug: it means the
  Brier swap, on today's real data, would not immediately flag anything --
  GFS's Brier disadvantage over its peers right now is real but modest
  (~0.03 gap), not the sharp signal the "35% directional accuracy" framing
  implied. The mechanism is working as designed; it simply isn't finding an
  extreme signal on the current window. Separately, an independent ad-hoc
  check on a smaller (n=19, below _QUARANTINE_MIN_RECENT_N=20), more
  recent-trades-only sample found ecmwf_aifs025_ensemble scoring worse than
  gfs_seamless -- a real, reproduced result, but on a sample too small for
  the mechanism to act on by its own design; the full 14-day/n=32 window
  used for calibration still shows gfs_seamless worst. Documented in
  scan_member_quarantine()'s own docstring as evidence the mechanism is
  deliberately generic (evaluates all candidates, flags whichever is
  actually worst) rather than tuned around a "gfs is the culprit"
  assumption.
  Known, documented limitations (see scan_member_quarantine() docstring):
  get_historical_sigma() is not model-specific (same climatological sigma
  used for every model's gaussian_probability() call -- sigma_mult, the
  time-of-day/horizon discount, is now applied per-trade correctly per
  HIGH-2 above, but a model with genuinely different forecast-SPREAD
  characteristics -- e.g. reported ECMWF AIFS ensemble overdispersion --
  still isn't corrected for); tracker.purge_old_predictions()'s 730-day
  retention means very old settled trades that have already been purged
  can't be backfilled (low urgency, real trade history is only ~3 months
  old); log_member_score()'s INSERT OR IGNORE can permanently strand a
  computable Brier behind an already-logged NULL row until the (manual,
  not cron-wired) backfill repairs it (MEDIUM-4 above).
  Tests (exact counts, collected via pytest --collect-only -- an opus-
  review LOW finding caught an earlier draft of this note overstating
  them): 5 new in tests/test_paper_metrics.py (brier population w/ exact
  expected-value assertion, below-direction, sigma_mult reconstruction,
  no-predictions-row degradation, non-directional-condition skip; 5
  pre-existing MAE-era tests in the same file untouched) = 10 total.
  8 new in tests/test_tracker.py (TestGetMemberBrier: 6, TestBackfillMemberBrier:
  6 base + below-direction + sigma_mult = 8) = 14 total. 3 new in
  TestMemberQuarantineScan (tests/test_weather_markets.py): legacy-state
  ewma_z reset, legacy-state release-suppression (MEDIUM-3), floor
  sane-bounds regression guard (MEDIUM-6) -- plus the pre-existing 17-test
  MAE-era suite fully renamed to Brier/get_member_brier (2 of those needed
  real numeric rework, not just a rename, since the floor's scale changed:
  their synthetic n had to grow from 10k to 2.5M to keep testing the same
  "statistically significant but practically trivial" edge case) = 20
  total in that class, 23 total including TestMemberQuarantineBlendHooks
  (unchanged, 3 tests). All scoped runs green; full suite for all three

Priority: INFO -- same risk class as AUD-0076 (path-segment manipulation, no SSRF since PROD_BASE/DEMO_BASE are fixed, no privilege escalation). order_id is exchange-sourced for automated paths (kalshi_client.py:660 reads it straight from Kalshi's own place_order response), narrowing exposure there -- but round-2 review (F8) found `py main.py cancel <order_id>` (main.py's cmd_cancel) passes CLI argv straight through with zero normalization, a genuine raw-client-input path this entry's first draft omitted.

RESOLVED 2026-08-25 (batch-58 item 1):
  Added `_validate_order_id_format` / `_ORDER_ID_RE` (kalshi_client.py) and applied it at all FOUR
  order_id-interpolating methods -- get_order_queue_position, get_order, cancel_order, amend_order
  -- plus `_validate_ticker_format` on amend_order's body ticker. main.py's cmd_cancel (the one
  raw-CLI path) now strips and validates EXPLICITLY before the call.

  CHARSET -- the entry's own premise could not be verified, and that changed the design.
  This entry and the batch file both said to confirm the real format by grepping live
  execution_log.db. There is nothing there to confirm against: data/execution_log.db holds 247
  rows and ZERO with live=1, and every retained backup is the same -- no real Kalshi order
  response has ever been stored in this repo, so the "lowercase-hex UUID" shape is an assumption,
  not an observation. Per user decision, the regex is therefore a PERMISSIVE path-safe charset
  rather than the strict UUID regex the entry proposed:
      _ORDER_ID_RE = re.compile(r"(?!\.{1,2}\Z)[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\Z")   # 64-char cap
  It rejects everything in the actual threat model (`/`, `%`, `?`, `#`, `\`, whitespace, control
  chars, and `.`/`..` as whole segments) while accepting any UUID and any plausible opaque
  exchange id. A tight UUID regex would have added nothing against path manipulation and created
  a real availability risk in the other direction: if a real order_id is ever not a canonical
  UUID, cancel_order/amend_order start raising and a live position cannot be closed. The
  intra-segment dot is admitted deliberately (opus review L4) -- Kalshi's own identifiers use one
  and _TICKER_RE had to be widened for exactly that reason (KXHIGHAUS-26JUN06-B88.5, 119 of 364
  distinct real tickers), so excluding it was the likeliest way to reject a real id on a cancel
  path. Logged at ERROR, not WARNING: a rejection here is by construction never transient.

  ALSO FIXED as the entry required: get_live_weather_index's docstring claim that it was "the one
  path-interpolating method in the file that had no equivalent guard" -- true when written, false
  since. Replaced with the now-true statement plus a drift guard
  (TestOrderIdPathValidation::test_every_path_interpolating_method_validates_its_segment) that
  source-counts the 7 f-string path interpolations, so the replacement claim cannot silently rot
  the same way. That guard exists because this entry was itself created by exactly that rot.

  OPUS REVIEW (effort:high, API-surface half) -- 16 findings, all addressed. Two were proven by
  execution rather than argued:
    M1 (real bug, self-inflicted): the first implementation caught ValueError AROUND
      client.cancel_order(). Three non-format failures also raise ValueError -- _check_error_body's
      200-with-error-body convention, requests' JSONDecodeError (a ValueError subclass) on an HTML
      gateway body, and _sign_headers' missing-credentials check. So a 502 during an operator's
      emergency cancel printed "Invalid order_id: Expecting value: line 1 column 1" and returned
      exit 0. Now validates explicitly; every other failure stays loud and propagates.
    M4 -> the drift guard described above.
    L1: the cmd_cancel bad-id test asserted nothing at all (an `except: pass` mutant survived it);
      now asserts on stdout and on cancel_order not being called, plus a companion test proving a
      non-format ValueError is NOT swallowed.
    L5: amend_order's ticker check reframed as a body-field consistency check (it is not path
      protection -- only order_id is interpolated into that path).
    L6: the "documented as a UUID" claim softened and flagged as unverifiable, matching this
      file's convention of dating/sourcing external claims.
    L3, L7 and the informational findings addressed in the same pass.
  Files: kalshi_client.py, main.py (cmd_cancel), tests/test_kalshi_client.py.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-22 -- see resolution below.] weather_markets._metar_lock_in never combines current_temp_f with the daily-extreme cache -- the identical AUD-0016 defect class, on the LIVE trade-entry path
Priority: MEDIUM (found by independent opus review, not the original max-depth audit; not yet independently CONFIRMED by a second pass)
Files: weather_markets.py (_metar_lock_in, both the above/below branch ~L10905-10912 and the between branch ~L10970-10979), metar.py (fetch_metar_daily_extreme, fetch_metar's own caching)

Problem:
  _metar_lock_in computes `_comp_temp = _daily_ext if _daily_ext is not None else _metar_obs["current_temp_f"]` in BOTH its above/below branch (~L10910-10912) and its between-bucket branch (~L10977-10979) -- unlike settlement_monitor.py's _check_between_settlement (this batch's AUD-0016 fix target), it never takes max()/min() of the daily-extreme cache against the fresher current_temp_f reading. _daily_ext (from metar.fetch_metar_daily_extreme) and current_temp_f (from a separate metar.fetch_metar call) are independently cached with their own TTLs, so they can disagree by however long the gap between the two caches' last refresh is.
  Root cause: this is the exact defect class AUD-0016 fixed one file over, in this function's own documented "sibling" -- settlement_monitor.py's docstring and several comments in this file explicitly describe _metar_lock_in and _check_between_settlement as mirroring each other's reasoning, but the max(current, daily_ext) hardening AUD-0016 added to the settlement-monitor side was never carried over here.
  Evidence: independent opus review (round 3 of AUD-0016's own review chain) read weather_markets.py:10905-10979 directly and confirmed no max()/min() combination exists in either branch, in contrast to the just-fixed settlement_monitor.py. Constructed a concrete failure scenario for the between-bucket branch: HIGH market, band [66.5, 68.5], _daily_ext cached at 14:20 = 66.5 (stale), a fresher fetch_metar current at 14:50 = 69.5 (already above the band). _comp_temp = 66.5 (the stale extreme, current_temp_f ignored entirely) -> the YES branch (weather_markets.py ~L11107-11143) sees 66.5 in-band with 2.0F clearance >= the 1.0F margin and locks YES at confidence ~0.738, on a market whose freshest reading shows it has already cleared the band. Both fetch_metar and fetch_metar_daily_extreme use independent ~15-minute-TTL caches (metar.py ~L80-83, ~L258-261 per the reviewer's citation -- not independently re-verified by this session), so a divergence window of this size is the ordinary case, not a rare corner.
  Financial risk: HIGHER surface than AUD-0016 itself -- this function (_metar_lock_in) feeds analyze_trade's live/paper trade-entry probability directly (the settlement-lag monitor AUD-0016 lives in, by contrast, has reportedly never actually been scheduled to run in production per settlement_monitor.py's own docstring). Not independently quantified this session (no live/paper trade reproduction run); flagging based on the mechanism match to AUD-0016, not a live incident.
  Recommendation: Apply the same fix this batch landed for settlement_monitor.py's between branch -- for BOTH of _metar_lock_in's branches, combine _daily_ext with current_temp_f via max()/min() (direction matching HIGH-vs-LOW market type) for whichever comparisons determine a YES-direction lock, following the exact reasoning trail AUD-0016 went through across 3 independent review rounds (see this repo's git history / the batch-08 session for that reasoning: gating membership on the daily extreme alone is fine, but CLEARANCE must be measured against the combined value, not the daily extreme alone, or a fresher-but-ignored current reading can silently understate how close the true value already is to the risk edge). Do not apply a naive "gate on daily extreme alone, veto if current crosses the edge" fix -- round 2 of AUD-0016's own review found that pattern is still exploitable in the partial-disagreement window short of the veto's trigger point. This needs its own independent review pass(es) before landing, same as AUD-0016 required, given the higher-traffic live entry path.
  Also noted by the same review, folded into scope here rather than filed separately: metar.py's docstring (~L243-257) claims the YES-direction staleness hazard is guarded against in "both settlement_monitor._check_between_settlement and weather_markets._metar_lock_in's between branch" -- true for the former after this batch, no longer true for the latter until this entry is fixed; and metar.py:404's "both current callers" comment for fetch_metar_daily_extreme is stale since AUD-0020 (this same batch-08 session) added a third caller, weather_markets._compute_persistence_prob. Update both comments as part of whatever session picks this up.
  Limitations noted by this session: not independently re-verified (this finding comes from round-3 review of a DIFFERENT batch item, not a fresh independent pass on this specific claim); the metar.py cache-TTL line citations were not re-checked; no live/paper reproduction was run to quantify real-world frequency.

Full record: none (not from the original max-depth audit's AUDIT_REPORT.json/md -- surfaced by independent review during batch-08).

Resolution (2026-08-22):
  Applied the AUD-0016 final (round-3) pattern from settlement_monitor.py's
  _check_between_settlement to both of _metar_lock_in's branches, mirroring
  the exact reasoning this entry's own Recommendation described.
  Above/below branch (weather_markets.py ~L10909-10935): combined via
  `_comp_temp = max(current_temp_f, _daily_ext)` (or `min()` for a LOW
  market), used directly as check_metar_lockout's input. Unlike the between
  branch, this needed only a plain uniform combine, NOT the membership/
  clearance split described below -- check_metar_lockout's YES branches are
  one-sided threshold crossings (current >= threshold+margin, or <=
  threshold-margin) with no interior band and no opposite at-risk edge, so
  more clearance in the safe/monotonic direction only makes the lock MORE
  certain, never less. The "still rising past an at-risk edge" hazard the
  between branch's split exists to guard against structurally cannot occur
  here.
  Between branch (weather_markets.py ~L10998-11020, ~11095-11205): kept
  `_comp_temp` (combined) for the NO branches, unchanged. For the YES/
  in-band block, gated membership on the RAW `_daily_ext` alone (NOT
  `_comp_temp`) but measured `_risk_clearance` against `_comp_temp` --
  exactly settlement_monitor.py's final/round-3 split, not a re-derivation
  of it. This split matters in BOTH directions, verified with concrete
  tests (tests/test_phase2_batch_d.py):
    - Stale-cache-in-band case (this entry's own repro: HIGH market, band
      [66.5, 68.5], stale _daily_ext=66.5 in-band, fresher current=69.5
      already past the band): this is what the split's CLEARANCE half (not
      the membership half) fixes. Gating membership on _daily_ext alone
      (66.5, in-band) with clearance ALSO measured against _daily_ext
      (i.e. the pre-fix bug, or a "gate raw, clear raw" variant this batch
      did not implement) would compute clearance=68.5-66.5=2.0 and lock a
      stale YES, ignoring that the market has already moved past the band.
      Measuring clearance against comp_temp=max(69.5,66.5)=69.5 instead
      gives clearance=68.5-69.5=-1.0, correctly refusing the lock.
    - Still-rising, unconfirmed case (the mirror hazard, NOT in this
      entry's original repro but caught while re-deriving
      settlement_monitor's own 3-round history for this exact pattern):
      HIGH market, band [66.5, 68.5], a REAL _daily_ext=64.0 still below
      the band, fresher current=67.0 already inside it. Gating membership
      on the COMBINED value (comp_temp=max(67.0,64.0)=67.0, in-band) would
      lock YES off a still-rising instantaneous reading the real daily
      extreme hasn't caught up to yet -- gating on the raw _daily_ext
      (64.0, not in [66.5,68.5]) instead correctly refuses to lock.
  Process note: this session initially implemented a plain uniform combine
  (comp_temp used for both membership and clearance in both branches, no
  split) and got an independent opus review (effort=high) that found it
  correct in isolation -- but that review, and this session's own initial
  read of settlement_monitor.py, were working from a version of this
  worktree's branch that was MISSING commit 9eb2f154 (the actual, real,
  3-independent-review-round AUD-0016 fix landed on a sibling branch the
  same day), so the "proven sibling pattern" being mirrored was actually
  the PRE-fix, superseded code. Caught by checking the sibling branch's
  history directly rather than trusting only what this worktree's own
  files showed; cherry-picked 9eb2f154 into this branch first (clean,
  no conflicts with this fix's file regions), then redid this fix against
  the real final pattern. Confirmed with the user given the live-trading
  stakes before finalizing (AskUserQuestion, 2026-08-21/22) -- this surfaced
  during that same conversation, prior to the user's decision, not after.
  Also fixed the stale metar.py:404 "both current callers" comment for
  fetch_metar_daily_extreme -- AUD-0020 (this same batch-08 session, on the
  sibling branch) added a third caller, weather_markets._compute_
  persistence_prob, never reflected there. The other noted stale comment
  (metar.py ~L247-249, "guarded against in both...") was re-checked and
  found to still be accurate as-is -- it describes a different, still-real
  residual risk (the daily-extreme cache's OWN staleness relative to
  reality, independent of whether it's combined with current_temp_f: if
  both fetch_metar and fetch_metar_daily_extreme are simultaneously stale

  Tests: tests/test_phase2_batch_d.py (between branch) -- 2 new tests for
  the stale-cache repro (HIGH/LOW market mirrors) plus 1 new test for the

  (test_between_daily_extreme_zero_is_not_treated_as_missing) needed their
  current_temp values adjusted so this fix's combining doesn't silently
  defeat what they were actually testing -- caught by an independent opus
  review (effort=high) on the (superseded) first implementation; both
  re-verified to still target their original boundary/behavior under the
  new code. tests/test_weather_markets.py (above/below branch) -- 3 new
  tests in TestMetarLockInCombinesCurrentWithDailyExtreme (HIGH-market

  test_between_still_rising_daily_extreme_not_yet_in_band_does_not_lock_yes

[RESOLVED 2026-08-22 -- see resolution below.] weather_markets._metar_lock_in's above/below branch has no per-observation local-date guard, unlike its between-branch sibling -- this session's own combine fix makes the gap more load-bearing than before
Priority: LOW (narrow exposure window, no live/paper reproduction run; flagged because the fix landed this session structurally widens what this gap can affect, not because a new defect was introduced)
Files: weather_markets.py (_metar_lock_in's above/below branch, ~L10896-10945)

Problem:
  The between branch of _metar_lock_in has an explicit per-observation
  local-date guard (`_obs_local_date != target_date`, ~L11069) -- added
  after a real bug (2 losing OKC/SATX trades, 2026-06-25) where a METAR
  obs_time near midnight UTC converts to ~7 PM the PRIOR local calendar
  day, and the function-level `target_date == _local_today` check alone
  doesn't catch that the SPECIFIC observation is from today. The
  above/below branch has no equivalent guard -- `check_metar_lockout` only
  gates on the observation's local HOUR (>= 14), never its local DATE.
  Root cause: the date guard was added to the between branch specifically
  (backlog.txt, the OKC/SATX incident write-up) and never ported to the
  above/below branch, which predates that incident's fix.
  Evidence: independent opus review (round 2 of this session's own
  current/daily-extreme combine fix, 2026-08-22) noted that BEFORE this
  session's fix, a prior-local-day current_temp_f was inert on the
  above/below branch whenever a real _daily_ext was available (current_
  temp_f was discarded entirely in that case) -- contamination was only
  possible via the `_daily_ext is None` fallback. AFTER this session's fix,
  current_temp_f is max()/min()'d into _comp_temp UNCONDITIONALLY whenever
  _daily_ext is available, so a prior-local-day current_temp_f can now
  pull _comp_temp toward an incorrect value even when a real, same-day
  _daily_ext also exists. The combine's own safety argument ("current_
  temp_f is always one of the observations the true running extreme is
  taken over") is only true if that observation is actually from today's
  local calendar day -- nothing on this branch enforces that.
  Concrete exposure window (not independently re-verified via live
  reproduction this session): fetch_metar's own ~90-minute staleness gate
  plus metar.py's 15-minute _METAR_CACHE TTL bound the window to roughly
  local 00:00-01:45, and it additionally requires cache skew (_METAR_CACHE
  warmed just before local midnight while _DAILY_OBS_CACHE already holds a
  post-midnight, today-dated reading). Within that narrow window a 23:53
  (yesterday) vs. 00:15 (today) reading pair is typically near-identical in
  temperature, bounding the practical impact even when the scenario occurs.
  Financial risk: feeds analyze_trade's live/paper trade-entry probability
  directly, same path as the entry this gap was found alongside. Not
  independently quantified -- flagged on mechanism match to the between
  branch's own documented incident, not a live reproduction.
  Recommendation: Port the between branch's exact `_obs_local_date !=
  target_date` guard (~L11069) to the above/below branch, refusing to lock
  (return False, 0.0, {}) when the METAR observation's own local date
  doesn't match target_date -- mirroring the between branch's comment and

[RESOLVED 2026-08-22 -- batch-29 item 3; two of the three sub-findings resolved, one confirmed NOT a defect and already covered by a prior entry -- see resolution note below] THREE SMALLER UTC-VS-LOCAL-BASIS FINDINGS, NONE FEEDING A LIVE GATING DECISION DIRECTLY
Priority: LOW

Problem (as originally filed by batch-29):
  (a) weather_markets.py's _days_out_from_close_time (~L6141-6146) uses
  raw UTC date instead of the ET-adjusted date the codebase already uses
  elsewhere for the identical Kalshi-close-time-crosses-midnight-UTC

  sitting exactly on the horizon threshold.
  (b) main.py's cmd_schedule_cycles (~L9707-9710 pre-fix) snapshots a

  -- currently dormant, nothing is registered via this path on the real
  machine (cron is manual-only, per this file's own prior notes).
  (c) weather_markets.py's seasonal-blend-weight bucket (~L12609 pre-fix)

  impact bounded to a few hours near a month boundary given 3-month-wide

Recommendation (as originally filed):
  (a) Convert close_dt to America/New_York before reading .month/.day.
  (b) Use the fromtimestamp()-based pattern like the settlement-monitor
  registration does. (c) Use utils.utc_today() explicitly.

Re-verification before implementing (step 1 of this project's standing
  workflow) found (a)'s recommendation was WRONG -- superseded by a more
  careful investigation this project had already done:

  (a) NOT a defect, left as-is. A 2026-08-17 opus-review entry earlier in
  this same file (search "_days_out_from_close_time") already
  investigated this exact function and explicitly concluded it is
  "correctly UTC-vs-UTC internally consistent" and "correctly left
  alone" -- a genuinely different bug class from the city-local-vs-UTC
  comparisons that entry was fixing elsewhere. That entry's own nuance
  note: Kalshi's close_time for an ET-calendar-date market is an
  evening-ET instant whose UTC date is the FOLLOWING day, so
  close_dt.date() in raw UTC slightly OVERSTATES true ET-local days-out
  by up to 1 day near a market's close -- but converting to ET (as
  batch-29 recommended) would REMOVE that bias, making time_kelly_scale/
  edge_confidence LESS conservative for markets near the months-scale
  RAIN_MAX_DAYS_OUT/SNOW_MAX_DAYS_OUT/HURRICANE_MAX_DAYS_OUT ceilings --
  the opposite of an improvement. batch-29's own framing ("both sides
  UTC so internally consistent") already correctly identified this isn't
  the city-local bug class, but its Recommendation contradicted its own
  Problem framing by proposing the ET conversion anyway. Fix NOT applied;
  a code comment was added to _days_out_from_close_time instead, pointing
  future readers at this entry so the same mis-fix isn't attempted again
  without re-reading it.

  (b) and (c) confirmed real and distinct from any prior entry (grepped
  backlog.txt for both before implementing; no match). (c) additionally
  found to be currently UNREACHABLE dead code: analyze_trade's own
  no_date gate (~L11546-11554) returns None before target_date can ever

[RESOLVED 2026-08-22 -- see resolution below.] The React dashboard's "Approve" action sends the YES-side price and probability regardless of the recommended side
Priority: HIGH -- direct financial-loss mechanism on the manual-approval path (one of the highest-priority items across batches 22-30 per audit/handoff_prompts/batches/INDEX.md)
Files: frontend/src/App.jsx (~908-917), web_app.py (~2707-3045 api_paper_order), trade_cycle.py (~721-806, proves the signals cache stores YES-space values)

Problem:
  The signals cache stores forecast_prob/market_prob/yes_bid/yes_ask in
  YES-space regardless of the recommended side; web_app.py's own display
  code proves this by explicitly flipping when rendering a NO signal. The
  dashboard's Approve payload did NOT perform the equivalent flip -- it
  sent the YES mid/probability unconditionally as entry_price/entry_prob.
  The server then computed kelly_fraction(P_yes, yes_mid) even for a NO
  recommendation, where P_yes < market_prob by construction whenever the
  recommendation is NO -- Kelly was exactly 0.0 every time, producing an
  HTTP 400 that named four plausible-sounding causes, none of which was the
  real one. Second-order and more severe: if entry_prob was ever omitted,
  the server skipped the Kelly cap and passed the YES-space entry_price
  straight to place_paper_order(side="no", ...) -- but the server's own
  code comment states the contract explicitly ("entry_price is the price
  PAID for the requested SIDE"). A NO position would be booked at the
  wrong price. (Independently verified during this session's fix: a
  pre-existing WA-security deviation guard, added 2026-07-11, and a
  pre-existing WA-inversion fix already mitigate the wrong-booking half of
  this in the common case -- the ALWAYS-REJECTS-every-NO-approval half was
  the live, reproducible symptom.)
  Full record: batch-26 item 1 (audit/handoff_prompts/batches/batch-26.md).

Resolution (2026-08-22):
  Extracted a pure, exported buildPaperOrderBody(opp, qty) function in
  App.jsx (and a shared sideAwareEntryPrice(opp) helper) that flips
  entry_price to side-space (NO pays 1-yes_bid, YES pays yes_ask) before
  POSTing to /api/paper-order, matching place_paper_order's documented
  contract. entry_prob is deliberately left in YES-space, UNFLIPPED --
  independent opus review (effort:high) caught that an earlier draft
  flipping entry_prob too would have corrupted every NO trade's stored
  calibration data (tracker's Brier/calibration scoring, order_executor's
  model-reversal exit shift, paper.py's pnl_attribution all read entry_prob

[RESOLVED 2026-08-25 (batch-60 item 3) -- originally found investigating an opus-review finding (batch-26 item 3's own "cmd_market" sibling) while fixing batch-26; genuinely separate defect class (mid-vs-ask pricing, not the side-inversion bug batch-26 targets) and needed its own live-quote-refresh design decision, so filed separately rather than folded into that fix. See resolution below.] cmd_today's interactive "[P] Place" flow books the actual paper trade at the bid-ask MID, not the realistic ask/no_ask price
Priority: MEDIUM -- affects a REAL placed paper trade's recorded price/cost/quantity, not just a display value (distinct from and more severe than the display-only mid-vs-ask divergence an opus reviewer initially flagged here as LOW without checking this)
Files: main.py (~3099 _entry_price1 = _market_prob1 if _side1=="yes" else 1-_market_prob1; ~3277-3298, the actual place_paper_order call using it; ~3010/~3064, the sibling _pick_display's own display-only _entry_price computation, same pattern)

Problem:
  cmd_today's "#1 Best Pick" flow computes _entry_price1 from the cached
  bid-ask MID (best_a["market_prob"]), correctly flipped for side but NOT
  ask-based, then passes it straight to place_paper_order (via _ppo_today)
  as the trade's booking price when the user presses [P] to place it. This
  is the exact "using mid understates entry cost by half the spread"
  pattern the codebase explicitly documents and avoids elsewhere
  (order_executor.py's own fill-price comment, weather_markets._price_and_
  size, and this same batch's cmd_market fix) -- but cmd_today's real
  order-placement path still uses it. A real placed paper trade is booked
  cheaper than a realistic fill, and the CLI's own printed "cost $X" and
  "if correct, win $Y" figures (main.py ~3288/3015-3021) are computed from
  the same understated price, misleading the operator about real economics
  at the moment of placement.
  Root cause: _entry_price1 predates this batch's session and was never
  updated when order_executor.py's real auto-trading engine and (as of
  this batch) cmd_market's display were both hardened to use the ask side;
  cmd_today's own interactive placement path was missed.
  Not independently reproduced with a live/paper trade this session --
  found by code reading while investigating a related opus-review finding,
  not a fresh repro run.
  Recommendation: Decide whether cmd_today should (a) reuse this batch's
  _side_aware_entry_price(side, prices) helper directly (cheapest, but
  prices here may be several minutes stale by placement time -- the same
  staleness concern order_executor.py's own "L1-B: Re-fetch live price
  before placement" comment addresses for the real auto-trading engine),
  or (b) re-fetch a fresh quote at placement time via client.get_market
  before booking, matching order_executor.py's own convention more
  closely. Needs its own investigation into how stale `prices`/`best_a`
  typically are by the time a user presses [P] in practice before picking
  an approach, then real tests (mutation-tested) and independent review
  given this touches an actual paper-order-placement path.

Resolution (2026-08-25, batch-60 item 3):
  Both (a) AND (b) -- the recommendation framed them as alternatives, but
  they fix two independent defects and the entry's own text describes both.
  Surfaced to the user as an explicit decision before implementation; they
  chose the re-fetch.

  (a) Mid -> side-aware ask. Three sites now route through the existing
  main._side_aware_entry_price (main.py:1481, previously used at exactly
  one call site): the booking price, the sibling _pick_display detail block
  whose "If correct: win $X" projection was computed from the same
  understated price, and -- opus review F3 -- the compact "Also consider"
  runner-up lines, which are rendered by their own inline block rather than
  through _pick_display and so had kept the mid after the #1 pick moved.
  That last one mattered on screen: an ask and a mid printed side by side
  with nothing marking them as different measures, so an operator comparing
  "#1 BUY YES @ 44%" against "#2 BUY YES @ 42%" was comparing a price they
  could pay against one they could not.

  (b) Fresh quote at placement. The #1 pick's book is re-fetched via
  client.get_market once, BEFORE the detail block prints, and that one
  price feeds the projection, the Kelly contract count, and the booking.
  Mirrors order_executor's own "L1-B: Re-fetch live price before placement"
  convention. Resolved ahead of _pick_display rather than inside it because
  a mid-block re-fetch would have shown the scan-time ask in the
  recommendation and the fresh one in the confirmation two lines later --
  two prices for one contract on one screen. _pick_display's `prices`
  parameter is required rather than defaulted for the same reason: a
  default would be dead code today and would silently reintroduce that
  split the moment a second caller forgot to pass one. The runner-ups are
  deliberately NOT re-fetched -- they are not placeable from this screen,
  and three extra API calls per run would not be worth it.

  The re-fetch is best-effort, falling back to the scan-time book on a
  failed call, a malformed payload (parse_market_price float()-coerces, so
  it must fall back the same way), or a payload with no real quote.

  That last case is opus review F1, a live-money-shaped bug the first draft
  introduced in the NO direction only: the emptiness test was "the derived
  entry price is > 0", which is safe for YES (an all-zero book yields 0.0)
  but not for NO, where _side_aware_entry_price falls through to
  max(0.01, 1 - mid) = 1.0 and passes any `> 0` test. A quote-less
  re-fetch therefore REPLACED a good scan-time book and booked at $1.00 --
  the maximum possible entry price, a structurally unwinnable position, and
  a worse corruption of the graduation-gate corpus than the mid-pricing
  this entry is about. Now gated on parse_market_price's own has_quote
  (mid > 0), which is exactly the "no real quote" predicate.

  Backfill decision (surfaced to the user, chose fix-forward + marker):
  NOT backfilled, because there is nothing to backfill. Read-only
  inspection of the live data/paper_trades.json on 2026-08-25 found 248
  trades and ZERO attributable to this path -- no row has a method set with
  close_time, days_out and thesis all absent, which is the shape
  _ppo_today's call produces. The 43 rows that come closest all have
  method=None and timestamp=None (early seed rows). So the optimistic bias
  this entry describes never actually entered the corpus the graduation
  gate reads. Recorded here rather than left implicit, since "fix forward"
  otherwise leaves a date boundary nothing documents.

  To make that statement checkable in future, placements through this path
  now carry thesis="cmd_today interactive [P] place", mirroring web_app's
  own "manual approval via dashboard" marker. Before this a cmd_today row
  was indistinguishable from a cron-placed one, which is precisely why the
  0-row finding needed a read-only heuristic to establish at all.

  Tests: tests/test_batch60_trade_entry_guards.py::TestCmdTodayEntryPrice
  -- YES books at the ask (0.44) not the mid (0.42) or market_prob (0.35),
  all three deliberately distinct; NO books at 1-yes_bid (0.60) not
  1-market_prob (0.65) or 1-mid (0.58); the fresh quote wins over the
  scan-time one; a raising get_market falls back to the scan-time ask; a
  quote-less payload falls back on BOTH sides (the YES case is the positive
  control -- it was already safe via the `> 0` test, so an inverted
  has_quote would break it while the NO case still passed); the detail
  block and the booking agree on one price with the stale 44% appearing
  nowhere; the runner-up line quotes the ask with both wrong sources
  absent; and the thesis marker. kelly_quantity is left REAL throughout so
  the contract count reacts to price as it does in production.

  Not covered, stated rather than skipped: how stale `prices`/`best_a`
  typically ARE by the time a user presses [P] was never measured -- the
  entry asked for that investigation before picking an approach. The
  re-fetch makes the question moot for correctness (the booked price is
  always current regardless of the answer), so it was not run. The one
  behavioural cost is an unconditional extra REST call per cmd_today
  invocation, including runs where the operator never presses [P]
  (opus review F12); cmd_today is interactive-only, so rate-limit impact is
  negligible.

Resolution (2026-08-24, batch-62 item 7):
  Verified as filed, and the drift was worse than described: web_app tracked 7
  (not 6), trade_cycle 5, cron 4, and _ensemble_precip_multiday_cb was in none
  of them.

  Fixed the class, not the instance -- but NOT as a flat registry, because the
  drift was not uniform. trade_cycle's list deliberately omits
  _weatherapi_cb/_pirate_cb: those are the FALLBACK temperature providers
  consulted precisely when the Open-Meteo circuits are open, so suppressing
  their probes during the analyze phase would stop the fallback recovering.
  Collapsing all three monitors onto one flat list would have regressed that.

  So: weather_markets.CIRCUIT_BREAKERS, a tuple of a frozen
  CircuitBreakerRegistration(breaker, prewarm_scoped) dataclass covering all 8.
  cron and web_app iterate everything; trade_cycle filters on prewarm_scoped.
  _ensemble_precip_multiday_cb is prewarm_scoped=True -- it is fetched from
  _analyze_monthly_rain_trade, inside the same parallel analyze pass, so an
  open circuit stalls that pool on a probe the same way. Its no-fallback
  asymmetry (suppress_probe has no reset path, so under a long-lived
  `main.py loop` the far-tail rain blend stays dark until restart) is noted at
  the registration.

  OPUS REVIEW CAUGHT A HIGH IN THE FIRST DRAFT, fixed: CircuitBreaker.is_open()
  is a MUTATOR, not a read. Once recovery_timeout has elapsed it sets
  _half_open, zeroes _failure_count, persists that and returns False -- "you
  are the probe." A monitor calling it therefore CONSUMES the one recovery
  probe; the next real fetch caller sees is_open() == True and skips the
  source, and trade_cycle's suppress_probe() then pins it open for the process
  lifetime. Widening cron's Phase 9 snapshot from 4 breakers to all 8 would
  have dropped _nbm_om_cb/_ecmwf_om_cb/_hrrr_om_cb/_ensemble_precip_multiday_cb
  -- four LIVE-blend temperature sources -- into exactly that trap, and the
  stolen probe would also have produced a FALSE "circuit opened" alert.
  Confirmed empirically. Both cron and web_app now read seconds_open() > 0,
  a pure read; this also fixes the pre-existing probe-steal for the breakers
  those monitors already covered.

  Accepted consequence, documented at the cron call site: six of the eight hit
  Open-Meteo hosts and trip together, so one outage now emits up to six alerts
  where it emitted two. The per-circuit cooldown key cannot dedupe correlated
  circuits; kept deliberately, since which source tripped is the actionable
  detail and a shared key would hide an independent second failure inside an
  unrelated outage's window.

  A FOURTH hand-maintained copy of the same eight breakers was found by review
  in tests/conftest.py's per-test reset loop, and is now derived from the
  registry too -- otherwise a newly added, correctly registered breaker would
  still have been missed there, reintroducing the cross-test contamination that
  fixture's own history records four separate times.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-22 -- see resolution below.] Crash-recovered live orders with no order_id are written to status='sent', a state no recovery or settlement query ever re-selects -- a genuine settlement/dedup black hole, the same failure shape AUD-0007 was built to eliminate, one branch further down
Priority: HIGH -- requires a specific crash window (an order pre-logged 'pending' whose placement outcome is unknown even to _recover_pending_orders' own reconciliation), but the row is then permanently unrecoverable, not just delayed
Files: order_executor.py (_recover_pending_orders, ~490-538), execution_log.py (get_pending_live_orders ~763, get_unknown_live_orders ~782, get_filled_unsettled_live_orders ~803)

Problem:
  _recover_pending_orders' loop over execution_log.get_pending_live_orders()
  (status='pending' rows) handles the case where a pending row has no stored
  order_id (order_executor.py:526-537) by calling
  execution_log.log_order_result(row_id, status="sent", error="no order_id
  at recovery -- treated as sent to prevent duplicate"). The log line even
  says "marked failed" while the code writes "sent" -- a stale/misleading
  message, minor on its own but a signal the two were never reconciled.
  The real problem: 'sent' is log_order()'s TRANSIENT pre-placement default
  status (execution_log.py:164/179, "Call with status='sent' before
  placing, then update with log_order_result()") -- but here it's being
  used as a manufactured TERMINAL status for a row whose real outcome is
  unknown. Every subsequent recovery/settlement query is scoped by an exact
  status match: get_pending_live_orders() is `WHERE status = 'pending'`,
  get_unknown_live_orders() is `WHERE status = 'unknown'`,
  get_filled_unsettled_live_orders() requires status='filled'. None select
  'sent'. Grepped every "sent" reference repo-wide -- the only other
  consumer is a dedup guard (execution_log.py:383, matches "any non-failed/
  canceled status", so 'sent' correctly blocks re-placement) -- no function
  anywhere re-checks a 'sent' row against the Kalshi API or ever transitions
  it to 'filled'/'unknown'/'failed'.
  Financial risk: if the order this row represents was ACTUALLY placed and
  filled on the exchange (a live position that genuinely exists), that
  position is now invisible to every downstream consumer: never picked up
  by _poll_pending_orders (only polls 'pending'), never protected by
  _check_live_position_exits/_check_live_model_exits (both source from
  execution_log.get_filled_unsettled_live_orders(), status='filled' only),
  never counted against max_open_positions correctly (unlike a genuine
  'unknown' row, which AUD-0009's fix deliberately DOES count -- this one
  silently doesn't), and never settled/reconciled by anything. The position
  rides to market settlement completely unmanaged, indefinitely, with the
  bot's own books showing nothing open.
  Recommendation: Either fold this case into the existing 'unknown' status
  (AUD-0007's already-built reconciliation path: try client_order_id
  lookup, retry) instead of inventing a dead-end 'sent' terminal state, or
  add a dedicated periodic query for `status='sent' AND placed_at < now() -
  N minutes` that attempts the same reconciliation _recover_pending_orders
  already does for 'unknown' rows.
Resolution (2026-08-22):
  Took the full-retrofit option (confirmed via AskUserQuestion over the
  lighter visibility-only alternative): every live pre-log call site
  (order_executor._place_live_order/_exit_live_position/_replace_live_order/
  the micro-live block, and main.cmd_order/main._quick_paper_buy) now
  computes and stores client_order_id in response BEFORE calling
  place_order, via a new shared kalshi_client.compute_client_order_id()
  helper (place_order() itself now routes through this same function
  instead of an inline duplicate formula, so the two can never drift).
  _amend_live_order deliberately excluded -- amend uses a different id
  scheme (updated_client_order_id) and doesn't create a new order visible to
  client_order_id lookup; its own order_id is unchanged by an amend, so the
  original entry row already gets recovered normally through the existing
  order_id-based pending loop.
  execution_log gained get_sent_live_orders() (mirrors get_pending_live_
  orders'/get_unknown_live_orders' unbounded shape). _recover_pending_orders
  now promotes any 'sent' row carrying a client_order_id to 'unknown' before
  the existing unknown-row reconciliation loop reads its rows -- so a
  promoted row resolves in the SAME pass, not a dead end. The promotion
  write is idempotent (two concurrent processes writing the identical
  target state), so no new claim/lock was needed beyond claim_unknown_order's
  existing atomicity at the actual settlement step.
  Adjacency fix: the pending-loop's own "no order_id" fallback was calling
  log_order_result() without response=, which does an UNCONDITIONAL
  overwrite (no COALESCE) -- silently wiping the very client_order_id this
  fix relies on. Now passes response=response to preserve it. Also fixed a
  stale log message ("marked failed" when the code writes "sent").
  Tests: tests/test_kalshi_client.py TestComputeClientOrderId (4 tests,
  incl. proving the precomputed id byte-matches place_order's own internal
  derivation); tests/test_live_execution.py TestRecoverSentOrders (4 tests,

  _recover_pending_orders() call). Both the promotion loop and the
  response-preservation fix mutation-tested (each reverted individually via

[RESOLVED 2026-08-22 -- see resolution below, fixed together with the fee-shape entry at this file's ~L25024 (both live in the same formula).] record_live_exit_fill (early-exit settlement, used by both cmd_order's manual live sells and order_executor._exit_live_position's automated protective exits) shares L22502's win-only-fee bug in a function L22502 doesn't cover, plus its docstring's "entry side always paid $0" assumption is false for IOC-entered positions

Resolution (2026-08-22):
  Added utils.kalshi_taker_fee(contracts, price) -> ceil(0.07*C*P*(1-P))
  rounded up to the whole cent (a 1e-9 epsilon guard before ceil() to

[RESOLVED 2026-08-22 -- see resolution below.] Live-position dollar-exposure accounting and live open-order-count enforcement disagree on which execution_log row statuses count as "a real open position"
Priority: MEDIUM -- undocumented asymmetry between two consumers of the same underlying question ("how much do we actually have on"), and the looser one is the one that gates NEW order placement
Files: order_executor.py (_get_live_open_positions ~1549-1568, _count_open_live_orders ~173-213), paper.py (get_all_open_positions, consumes _get_live_open_positions)

Problem:
  AUD-0009/AUD-0012's fix (batch-01, 8bdff1e5) deliberately made
  _count_open_live_orders() the union of status='pending' (a still-resting
  GTC entry order representing real committed capital that could fill any
  moment) + status='unknown' (AUD-0007: placement outcome ambiguous, could
  turn out to be a real fill) + get_filled_unsettled_live_orders() (status=
  'filled', settled_at IS NULL) -- explicitly reasoned through in that
  function's own docstring as the correct definition of "open" for the
  max_open_positions cap. _get_live_open_positions() -- the function that
  feeds paper.get_all_open_positions(), which in turn feeds every DOLLAR-
  denominated exposure cap (per-market, portfolio, city/date, directional,
  correlated-group; see AUD-0001's resolution) -- sources ONLY
  get_filled_unsettled_live_orders(). It does not merge in pending or
  unknown rows at all.
  Financial risk: a resting live GTC entry order (status='pending') or an
  ambiguous-outcome order (status='unknown') represents real capital that
  could become a real position at any moment, but is invisible to every
  dollar-exposure cap while being correctly counted against the position-
  count cap. A sequence of several pending/unknown live orders on the same
  market/city/date/direction could clear every exposure-cap check (each one
  sees $0 existing_cost for those rows) right up until they all fill,
  potentially breaching caps the moment they do -- the exact "silently
  exceed every configured exposure cap" failure mode AUD-0001 was written
  to close, reopened for exactly the two row-statuses AUD-0001's own fix
  didn't include.
  Recommendation: Either merge pending+unknown rows into
  _get_live_open_positions() the same way _count_open_live_orders() already
  does (using each row's limit price as a placeholder cost basis for
  pending rows, since no fill price exists yet), or explicitly document why
  dollar exposure is deliberately scoped narrower than position count and
  confirm that's an intentional, accepted gap rather than an oversight.

  _get_live_open_positions() gained an include_unfilled: bool = False

  Tests: tests/test_batch01_live_position_visibility.py
