[RESOLVED 2026-08-24 -- batch-34 item 2 (M-7)] api_resume's and api_override_clear's unlink() lack missing_ok, re-opening batch-25's own M5 race
Priority: MEDIUM -- kill-switch/override safety-adjacent (dashboard can toggle the kill switch)
Files: web_app.py (api_resume, api_override_clear), tests/test_web_app.py

Problem:
  Both routes read `existed = _path.exists()` then, if True, called a bare `_path.unlink()` -- a
  TOCTOU race against a concurrent writer removing the file between the two calls. The api_resume case
  is the dangerous one: main.py's cmd_cron manual-override flow parks (renames away) the live kill
  switch at `.kill_switch.tmp` for the duration of a one-shot override. If that rename lands between
  api_resume's exists() check and its unlink() call, unlink() raises FileNotFoundError -> unhandled
  500 -> the parked-copy cleanup 15 lines below (which already had missing_ok=True, from batch-25's own
  M5 fix) never runs -> the kill switch silently re-arms itself once the override window ends, even
  though the operator explicitly resumed. api_override_clear has the identical pattern racing cron's
  own expiry auto-clear of the same manual-override file.
Resolution (2026-08-24):
  Both unlink() calls now pass missing_ok=True. api_override_clear's unlink is additionally wrapped in
  try/except OSError, returning this route's own JSON error shape (matching every other route in this
  file) instead of Flask's raw HTML 500 for any OTHER OSError (e.g. a permission failure) -- api_resume
  was left unwrapped, matching the batch item's literal scope (only api_override_clear's wrap was
  called for).
  Tests: TestKillSwitchAPI.test_resume_survives_kill_switch_removed_between_exists_and_unlink and
  TestOverrideClearRaceAndErrorHandling (two tests: the race-survival case and a genuinely different
  OSError getting the JSON 500 shape) added to tests/test_web_app.py. Each race test uses a small fake
  Path stand-in whose exists() always reports True while unlink() raises FileNotFoundError unless
  missing_ok=True -- deterministic, not dependent on real filesystem TOCTOU timing. Mutation-tested:
  reverted each fix via Edit (dropped missing_ok=True, and separately removed api_override_clear's
  try/except entirely), confirmed each corresponding test fails (FileNotFoundError propagates
  unhandled for api_resume's test; 500 instead of 200, or an unhandled PermissionError, for
  api_override_clear's two tests), restored.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-24 -- batch-34 item 7 (L-17, web_app.py-only parts a-f)] same-file low-severity sweep of web_app.py
Priority: LOW
Files: web_app.py (api_paper_order, /api/stream, /api/stream/markets, /api/trades), tests/test_web_app.py

Problem / Resolution per sub-item:
  (a) `quantity = int(body.get("quantity", 1)) or 1` sat outside any try -- a non-numeric quantity
  raised an unhandled ValueError (Flask HTML 500) instead of this route's usual JSON error shape.
  Wrapped in try/except (TypeError, ValueError), falling back to the documented default of 1, matching
  the file's own WA-input-validation pattern (e.g. /history's ?n=abc coercion).
  (b) api_paper_order read the kill switch via `from cron import KILL_SWITCH_PATH` while every sibling
  route in this file reads the module-level `_KS_PATH` -- a monkeypatch blind spot (a test or tool
  patching one binding doesn't affect the other, even though both start out as the same underlying
  paths.KILL_SWITCH_PATH object). Unified on `_KS_PATH`. Five existing tests that patched
  `cron.KILL_SWITCH_PATH` (always to `.exists.return_value = False`, i.e. they never actually exercised
  the engaged-switch path through this binding) were updated to `monkeypatch.setattr(web_app, "_KS_PATH",
  ...)` instead, matching the rest of the file's convention -- otherwise they'd have silently stopped
  patching anything meaningful post-fix, passing only because a real kill-switch file happens not to
  exist in the test environment.
  (c) The deviation-check guard `_expected_side_price > 0 and abs(entry_price - _expected_side_price) >
  0.15` skipped the check entirely when the expected side price is exactly 0 -- a legitimate boundary
  (a NO order on a yes_bid==1.0 market has expected NO price = 1-1.0 = 0), not the "degraded/missing
  quote" case the guard seems to have been meant for (already excluded by the outer `has_quote` gate).
  Removed the `> 0` guard; the check now runs unconditionally within the has_quote branch.
  (d) `_days_out = max(0, (_tdate_dash - _today_dash).days)` clamped a negative raw value (server-derived
  target_date already in the past -- a stale/expired market or ticker-parse mismatch) to 0, mislabeling
  a stale multi-day market as same-day and dodging the MAX_POSITIONS_PER_DATE multi-day slot cap this
  derivation feeds. Now rejects with 400 instead of clamping.
  (e) Both /api/stream and /api/stream/markets SSE generators added an explicit `except GeneratorExit:
  break`. Verified on inspection this is a no-op relative to prior behavior -- GeneratorExit isn't an
  Exception subclass, so it was never caught by the existing `except Exception` clause and already
  propagated correctly on client disconnect, cleanly terminating the generator via normal Python
  semantics. Kept as explicit documentation/defense-in-depth per the batch item's literal request (no
  live bug found here, so no mutation test was written for it -- there is no code-level difference to
  detect).
  (f) `_get_live_market_snapshot()`-fallback enrichment in /api/trades used `live["yes_bid"]`/
  `live["yes_ask"]` verbatim even when `_safe_market_price` had degraded a malformed field to 0 (its
  documented "=no quote" sentinel) -- a degraded field never fell back to the snapshot cache, contrary
  to the surrounding comment's documented intent ("falling back ... if the live call failed entirely or
  a specific ticker wasn't returned"). Now treats a degraded-to-0 field the same as "ticker missing from
  the batch" (falsy check -> fall back to snapshot).
Resolution notes:
  Tests: TestPaperOrderWebSweepL17 (four new tests covering a/b/c/d) and
  TestApiTradesLiveQuoteEnrichment.test_degraded_live_price_falls_back_to_snapshot_cache (f) added to
  tests/test_web_app.py; the pre-existing test_malformed_live_price_degrades_to_no_quote_not_a_crash
  was updated in place (its old assertion of a literal 0 enshrined the pre-fix bug -- now asserts None,
  since the snapshot cache is empty in that scenario too). All mutation-tested individually via Edit
  revert-confirm-restore except (e), for the reason given above. Four pre-existing tests
  (TestPaperOrderCityDateServerDerived x2, TestPaperOrderNoSideEndToEnd x2) used hardcoded
  server-derived dates that had drifted into the past relative to the real system clock by the time
  this batch ran -- harmless before item (d)'s fix, but item (d) would now reject them with 400. Bumped
  to year-2099 sentinel dates (matching the file's own "2099-01-01" far-future convention elsewhere),
  since none of those four tests exercise days_out and the exact date value wasn't otherwise asserted on.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-24 -- go/no-go FAILED, google_weathernext2_ensemble NOT onboarded, zero code changed] GOOGLE WEATHERNEXT 2 TRACK-ONLY ONBOARDING -- GATE FAILED
Priority: Low -- batch-50 Item 1 (dossier B5, score 7.5 rank 4). Not the same
  thread as the older "WeatherNext (GraphCast/GenCast)" note above (~L11054-
  11058) -- that one is the gatekept GCP/zarr product; WeatherNext 2 is a
  free, no-auth Open-Meteo ensemble endpoint
  (ensemble-api.open-meteo.com/...&models=google_weathernext2_ensemble, 64
  members) that sidesteps that barrier entirely. This entry is about the
  Open-Meteo one.
  Per the batch's own "go/no-go validation experiments FIRST ... a failed
  gate = file numbers to backlog and stop that item" instruction: ran the
  gate before touching any code, it failed, so KNOWN_FORECAST_MODEL_NAMES/
  TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES/analyze_trade were never touched for WN2.
  Methodology: fetched google_weathernext2_ensemble and icon_seamless hourly
  member series (ENSEMBLE_BASE, temperature_2m) for target_date =
  2026-08-25 (tomorrow, well within WN2's 15-day horizon) for all 21 cities
  in CITY_COORDS's hardcoded fallback (the batch spec says "20 cities" --
  the live fallback dict actually has 21; StPetersburg is the extra one
  added post-dossier for KXRAINSTPM). Per city: took the per-member implied
  daily TMAX (max of that member's hourly series) for both models, then the
  MEDIAN TMAX across each model's members; city-level clipping bias =
  icon_median - wn2_median. Gate metric = median of the 21 per-city biases.
  Result: median clipping bias = +1.10F (gate requires <1.0F) -- FAILED,
  narrowly, on a single-day/single-run sample. Individual city biases ranged
  from -11.3F (LA, WN2 running HOTTER than ICON -- raw model disagreement,
  not clipping) to +4.2F (Miami); most cities clustered +0.1 to +3.5F. Fetch
  latency: mean 0.55s, max 0.65s per city -- comfortably under the <10s/city
  gate (that half of the gate passed easily). Failure rate: 0/21 (0%).
  Caveat on methodology: a single day's cross-model comparison conflates
  WN2's genuine 6-hourly-native interpolation-clipping effect (the thing the
  gate is meant to measure) with ordinary day-to-day model disagreement
  (LA's -11.3F outlier is almost certainly the latter, not the former) --
  the gate as specified in the batch spec ("fetch WN2 for all 20 cities
  once") is explicitly a single-run check, not a multi-day study, so this
  result is taken as authoritative per the spec's own letter rather than
  re-run or averaged across days. The literal number (1.10F) is very close
  to the 1.0F threshold; if this is revisited, re-run across several days
  and/or exclude outlier cities where model disagreement (not clipping)
  plainly dominates before concluding the source is unusable outright --
  the current failure could plausibly flip on a less noisy sample.
  Known caveats the batch spec asked to be encoded if onboarded (recorded
  here since onboarding didn't happen, for whoever revisits this): 12-hourly
  update cadence (stale vs hourly HRRR at short leads); 6-hourly native
  resolution (interpolation cannot recover a mid-afternoon spike -- this IS
  the clipping effect the gate measures); free tier is non-commercial-use
  only, same flag as the bot's other Open-Meteo usage.
  Raw per-city results (wn2_tmax_median, icon_tmax_median, bias) saved to
  the implementing session's scratchpad as wn2_gate_results.json (not
  committed -- ephemeral validation artifact, numbers summarized above are
  the durable record).
  Re-check trigger: none scheduled -- optional future work, not a deadline.
  If revisited, re-run the same script with >=3-5 days sampled and consider
  a trimmed/city-filtered median before deciding again.
  Source: audit/handoff_prompts/batches/batch-50.md (Item 1).

  For this batch the REASONING is the deliverable; the diff is small.

  "there is currently NO operator-facing way to close an open position at
  all" was wrong when written and is wrong now. main.py's interactive paper
  menu (P -> 4, "Exit signals") has always ended in a per-position
  "Close this position now? (y/N)" prompt that calls close_paper_early
  directly, inside cmd_menu, with NO kill-switch and NO TRADING_PAUSED
  check. batch-63's own handoff file repeats the error, listing that call
  site as one of the "automated paths". It is not automated; it is the
  operator. (_cmd_settle_open, P -> 3 -> 2, is likewise ungated, though it
  settles at an outcome rather than closing at market.)

  So the real starting position was worse than "no path": an UNDESIGNED,
  SILENT, partial bypass. Partial because that prompt only ever offers the
  positions check_model_exits flags (model reversed >=10pp, or edge gone,
  and past EXIT_MIN_HOLD_HOURS) and refuses outright without a live
  realizable quote -- so an arbitrary position, or any position during a
  quote outage, still had no path. Silent because nothing told the operator
  a halt was engaged and nothing recorded that one had been bypassed.

  WHY (a) AND NOT (c), GIVEN BATCH-58. 58 (320740aa) built
  trading_gates.pre_live_exit_check, a reduced gate for risk-REDUCING live
  orders, and deliberately KEPT the kill switch and TRADING_PAUSED in it
  while dropping every risk-limit halt. Read shallowly that says "the kill
  switch is absolute, even for exits", which would argue for (c). It does
  not, for two reasons, and 58's own docstring says so:
    1. 58 gates the BOT. Its one caller is
       order_executor._exit_live_position -- automated exit logic deciding
       on its own to sell. The kill switch is precisely the instruction
       "stop deciding things on your own", so keeping it there is right.
       An operator typing a trade id at a shell prompt is not the bot
       deciding anything. pre_live_exit_check's docstring hands this
       question here by name ("backlog L30045 (batch 63) owns the separate
       question of giving the operator a deliberate way to close a position
       while they are engaged, and the answer to that must be an explicit
       operator action, not this gate quietly deciding on their behalf").
       A CLI command IS that explicit operator action. (a) completes 58's
       reasoning rather than contradicting it.
    2. Two of the four checks 58 kept -- prod-ness and
       LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED -- are real-money interlocks with no meaning
       on a paper close. close_paper_early writes paper_trades.json and
       nothing else. Only TRADING_PAUSED and the kill switch were ever in
       question here.
  (b) was rejected: putting the bypass on /api/close-position would make it
  reachable by a misclick on a dashboard button, which is exactly the
  failure mode the kill switch protects against. The gate's deliberateness
  has to come from the interface, and typing a trade id supplies it in a
  way a red button cannot.

What shipped:
  - main.cmd_close(client, args), reachable as `py main.py paper close
    <trade_id> [exit_price]` and the top-level alias `py main.py close
    <trade_id> [exit_price]`. Works on ANY open paper position, not just a
    model-flagged one. exit_price is optional: omitted, it derives the
    EXIT-side realizable price (yes_bid for a YES holder, 1 - yes_ask for
    a NO holder) via positions.liquidation_price, the same convention the
    menu path and /api/close-position already use. With no realizable
    quote it REFUSES and tells the operator to state a price, rather than
    fabricating one from entry_price -- a one-sided overnight book
    (yes_bid = 0) would otherwise book a phantom total loss into balance
    -> drawdown tier -> peak_balance -> graduation P&L. Validates
    exit_price in (0, 1], the contract /api/close-position enforces and
    close_paper_early itself does not. Shows ticker/side/qty/price/est.
    P&L and requires a y/N confirm.
  - main._engaged_halt_gates() / _warn_halt_bypass(), one shared REPORTING
    helper (not a gate) used by cmd_close AND the menu's exit-signals
    close, so the two operator paths cannot drift into disagreeing about
    which gates a close is bypassing -- this repo's recurring
    one-caller-forgot-its-copy bug class.
  - The menu's exit-signals close now ANNOUNCES an engaged halt and logs
    the bypass at WARNING with the gates named. Its behavior is unchanged
    (it still closes); what changed is that the bypass is deliberate,
    visible and reconstructible from the log instead of silent.
  - cmd_close logs every close at WARNING, naming any bypassed gates.
  - /api/close-position is UNCHANGED and still returns 503 under either
    gate. Do not mirror the bypass there; cmd_close's docstring says why.
  - COMMANDS.md documents `paper close`, including that the bypass is
    intentional.

Opus review (effort:high) then a second opus review of the fixes. Round 1
  raised no HIGH on this half; every MEDIUM/LOW/INFO was addressed:
  - MEDIUM: LIVE_TRADING_RUNBOOK.md still asserted, in bold, that no
    operator path existed -- in the emergency doc, under "Immediate halt",
    i.e. exactly where an operator would look during the halt this feature
    was built for. Rewritten: the batch-41 note is marked superseded and a
    batch-63 note documents the command, its paper-only scope, the
    deliberate bypass, the WARNING record, and that /api/close-position
    still 503s on purpose. The "Live exit blocked" alert row was qualified
    to say it concerns LIVE positions.
  - MEDIUM: a TYPED exit_price had no live-quote cross-check, while
    /api/close-position has had a +/-0.15 one since audit-M-9. `close 42
    0.95` against a 5c book would book a fat-fingered WIN into balance ->
    peak_balance -> graduation P&L, and the confirmation preview renders
    it as +P&L rather than as an error. Added, mirroring the route --
    including its stance of SKIPPING the check when no quote is reachable,
    since that is the case a typed price exists for.
  - MEDIUM (test quality): the alias test's docstring claimed it covered
    the top-level `close` branch while only exercising cmd_paper, so that
    branch had ZERO coverage. A real dispatcher test was added; mutating
    `args[1:]` to `args` now fails it.
  - LOW: the DERIVED price was bounded below but not above. kalshi_client.
    get_market is deliberately warn-only on an out-of-range field, so a
    malformed yes_bid of 105 coalesces to 1.05 and would book proceeds
    above the $1.00/contract maximum payout. The (0, 1] bound now applies
    to the final price whatever its origin.
  - LOW: _liquidation_price sat inside the broad `except`, so a future
    signature change would have been misreported to the operator as "no
    quote available". Extracted `_exit_side_quote`, whose try covers only
    the lookup/parse -- the boundary web_app's own close route documents.
  - LOW: reason= collapsed typed and derived closes into one tag.
    Now "operator_close_manual" vs "operator_close", so a later P&L
    anomaly can be traced to the closes whose price skipped the
    cross-check. Verified against every exit_reason consumer first.
  - LOW: the two callers logged differently (CLI unconditionally, menu
    only on a bypass), making bot.log an incomplete history that looked
    complete. Extracted `_log_operator_close`; both now log every close.
  - LOW: the WARNING record -- the entire reason the bypass is acceptable
    -- had no test at all. Two added.
  - LOW: get_balance() ran outside the try AFTER the close had committed,
    so a corrupt-ledger read would show a traceback and no confirmation,
    telling the operator the close FAILED when it had not.
  - INFO: fixed the _compute_live_orders_possible test's argv shape; moved
    a loop's output assertion inside the loop so a silently-rejected value
    cannot hide.
  DELIBERATE NO-OPS, each an explicit decision rather than a drop:
  - `close` was NOT added to main()'s credential-free early-return block
    (alongside kill/resume). That block returns before build_client(), so
    `close` there would ALWAYS have client=None and could never derive a
    price from the live quote -- breaking the normal case to serve the
    broken-key case. Documented in COMMANDS.md and the runbook instead.
  - No interactive-menu entry for closing an ARBITRARY position: the
    design's whole argument is that a typed trade id is deliberate in a
    way a menu selection is not.
  - main.KILL_SWITCH_PATH (not cron's) is the right read here -- it
    matches every other main.py site and what the tests patch.
  - `close 42 --verbose` reports "exit_price must be a number"; confusing
    wording, but it correctly refuses to act.

  A THIRD review round reviewed those fixes, and found two more real bugs
  the round-2 fixes had themselves introduced or left:
  - MEDIUM: the new (0, 1] clamp was applied to the derived price but the
    UNCLAMPED value was still used as the cross-check REFERENCE. A
    malformed yes_bid of 105 -> 1.05 therefore refused an operator's
    correctly-typed 0.60 with "deviates from ... $1.050" -- the command
    that exists to work when things are broken, blocked by the broken
    thing. The clamp moved inside _exit_side_quote, so a nonsense quote now
    reads as "no realizable quote" and the typed price goes through.
  - LOW: when the EXIT side of the book is empty (yes_bid = 0, "common
    overnight" per liquidation_price's docstring) there is no realizable
    price to deviate from, so the whole cross-check silently dropped and
    ANY typed price was accepted -- reopening the exact fat-finger hole it
    was added to close. _exit_side_quote now also returns a ceiling from
    the OPPOSITE side (a holder can never realize more than the other side
    is asking) and a typed price above it is refused.
  - LOW: the menu's new audit-log call sat inside the pre-existing `except`
    that prints "Could not close", AFTER the ledger write commits -- the
    same misreporting the CLI path had just been fixed for. Given its own
    try/except.
  - LOW (tests): the "exactly on the bound" case cannot be tested at all --
    0.15 has no exact binary representation and every realistic pair lands
    a few ULPs to one side, so `>` vs `>=` is unobservable here. The claim
    was dropped from the docstring rather than faked, and the test now pins
    what is observable. Also: no NO-side position was exercised anywhere, so
    a sign inversion in the 1 - yes_ask derivation would have gone unseen;
    and the alias test leaked main()'s process-wide logging.disable and
    depended on the ambient .env. All three fixed.
  - INFO: the close mock returned a bare {"pnl": ...}, a shape the real
    close_paper_early never returns.

Tests: tests/test_menu_ux.py 38 (20 in TestOperatorClose, plus one added
  to TestExitSignals for the menu's bypass notice); tests/

[CLOSED 2026-08-25 -- batch-63 item 2; decision made: option (c), accept and document. No code change, by design. See the Resolution block at the end of this entry] HURRICANE NEXT-EVENT MODEL LOGS ZERO PREDICTIONS -- GENERIC trade_cycle.py GATES FILTER EVERY REAL CANDIDATE, NOT A ROUTING/DB BUG
Priority: Low -- shadow-only, zero live-money risk; only affects whether a
  shadow-logged calibration sample accumulates at all for this one family.

Problem:
  _analyze_hurricane_next_event_trade (shipped 2026-08-07, KXNEXTHURDATE/
  KXNEXTCAT5HURDATE) has logged ZERO condition_type='hurricane_next_event'
  rows in predictions.db as of 2026-08-24, while its two siblings shipped
  the same week (hurricane_count: 116 rows, storm_order: 11 rows) log
  fine -- proving the general shadow-logging pipeline itself isn't broken.

  Traced live (not just read statically) via a diagnosis agent that
  reproduced the full path against real Kalshi markets (7 open
  KXNEXTHURDATE + 4 open KXNEXTCAT5HURDATE, matching a live count taken
  independently this session). analyze_trade() DOES correctly reach
  _analyze_hurricane_next_event_trade() and DOES produce valid, non-None
  results with real (sometimes very large) edges for markets with a usable
  quote -- every dispatch/registration/gate-active check along that path
  (is_hurricane_next_event_ticker, the blanket-guard bypass, _parse_
  market_condition's routing, _hurricane_next_event_gates_active only
  gating REAL order placement not shadow-logging) is confirmed working as
  designed.

  The actual mechanism: order_executor._log_shadow_predictions() (called
  from _auto_place_trades(), called from trade_cycle.run_trade_cycle())
  only shadow-logs opps that already made it into strong_opps/med_opps,
  which requires analysis["tier"] to be non-None -- which requires
  clearing, IN ORDER: (1) two hard `continue` gates in trade_cycle.py
  BEFORE tier logic runs at all -- mkt_dir >= MIN_MARKET_PROB_TO_BET_WITH
  (0.25) and our_dir/mkt_dir <= MAX_MARKET_DIVERGENCE_RATIO (2.0, "don't
  bet more than 2x against what the market believes"); (2) passes_
  threshold's abs(adjusted_edge) >= effective_min_edge (0.15) AND
  prob_edge >= min_prob_edge_gate.

  Live run today against all 11 open markets, both series: 9/11 never
  reach a real probability at all -- gated by extreme_price (6) or spread
  (3) in analyze_trade() itself, because these contracts are ALREADY
  priced near-certain by the market (e.g. KXNEXTHURDATE-26DEC01-26OCT15's
  real yes_ask=0.99, correctly tripping the >1-MIN_MARKET_PRICE gate --
  "before Oct 15" is climatologically near-certain by August, real market
  pricing, not a bug). Of the 2 remaining: KXNEXTHURDATE-26DEC01-26SEP01
  (8 days out) computed forecast_prob=0.90 vs market_prob=0.255 --
  our_dir/mkt_dir = 3.53 > 2.0, killed by the divergence-ratio gate BEFORE
  tier is ever computed. KXNEXTHURDATE-26DEC01-26SEP15 (22 days out)
  computed forecast_prob=0.99 vs market_prob=0.81 (ratio 1.22, clears that
  gate fine), but net_edge=0.207 gets crushed by edge_confidence(days_
  out=22, "hurricane_next_event") = 0.60 (horizon floor, days_out>14) x
  0.50 (_CONDITION_CONFIDENCE["hurricane_next_event"], deliberately
  conservative per its own comment) = 0.30, producing adjusted_edge=0.062
  < the 0.15 threshold -- killed by the edge gate.

  Both real candidates today died for the SAME underlying structural
  reason: this model's climatology-only probability estimates run far more
  extreme (0.80-0.99, "a hurricane will form by climatologically-typical
  date X" is true almost every season) than Kalshi's live market pricing
  for the same "before <date>" contracts (0.25-0.81) -- exactly what trips
  a ratio-based divergence gate, and the rare case that stays in range
  gets discounted below the edge floor by the days-out horizon curve
  stacked with the family's own conservative confidence multiplier.
  hurricane_count/storm_order share similar _CONDITION_CONFIDENCE values
  (0.55/0.50) and the SAME generic gates, so the difference isn't the
  gates themselves -- it's that THIS model's specific probability shape
  diverges more sharply from market pricing than the sibling models' do.
  Combined with most of this family's markets sitting in extreme-price
  territory most of the time, it's entirely plausible this family has
  never produced a candidate clearing every generic gate since shipping,
  with zero involvement of any dispatch/logging/DB defect.

  Secondary finding from the same diagnosis (real bug, NOT the cause of
  the zero rows, already fixed in the main batch-51 entry above):
  enrich_with_forecast()'s own separate date-parsing regex never got the
  same _HURRICANE_NEXT_EVENT_SERIES guard parse_city_date() already has.

Why not fixed now:
  Not a code defect to fix -- a genuine design/modeling question. Three
  options surfaced, deliberately NOT decided unilaterally: (a) bypass the
  generic MAX_MARKET_DIVERGENCE_RATIO/edge-threshold gates for this one
  family so shadow-logging can accumulate faster -- risky, those gates
  exist specifically to protect against betting against a well-informed
  market, and shadow-only logging exists to score "would-have-traded"
  candidates, so bypassing them would score candidates the real placement
  path would never have taken anyway (contaminating the very calibration
  sample the 20-settled floor is supposed to validate against); (b)
  recalibrate/temper this model's raw climatology probability toward
  market consensus before pricing it -- a real modeling change needing its
  own validation pass, not a mechanical fix; (c) accept the low logging
  rate as an inherent property of this market shape and just wait for more
  data across a wider range of live market states before concluding
  anything is actually broken. The diagnosis's own recommendation: do NOT
  change the generic gates to accommodate one model family; lean toward
  (c) unless/until a dedicated calibration-improvement pass is prioritized
  for (b).

When to revisit:
  - If HURRICANE_NEXT_EVENT_TRADING_ENABLED is ever considered, first
    check whether ANY shadow rows have accumulated in the meantime --
    zero rows after N more weeks across a genuinely wider range of market
    states (not just today's snapshot) would be much stronger evidence
    this needs (b) before it can ever graduate, vs. today's single-day
    read which only proves it's rare, not impossible.
  - If a future session wants to build (b) (probability recalibration
    toward market consensus), treat it as its own scoped design task with
    its own go/no-go-style validation, not a quick tweak to the existing
    climatology formula.

Resolution 2026-08-25 (batch-63 item 2) -- DECISION: (c), accept and
  document. This is an explicit, reasoned close, not an inconclusive drop:
  the question was put to the user with all three options and (c) was
  chosen. NO CODE CHANGED -- config.py, trade_cycle.py's gates and
  weather_markets._CONDITION_CONFIDENCE are all untouched.

  Re-verified against live data 2026-08-25 before deciding, since six
  sibling batches landed after this entry was written:
    predictions.db  hurricane_next_event = 0 rows (the family is absent
    from the table entirely), hurricane_count = 120, storm_order = 11.
    trade_cycle.py's two hard gates are unchanged and still fire before
    tier logic; utils.MIN_MARKET_PROB_TO_BET_WITH = 0.25 and
    MAX_MARKET_DIVERGENCE_RATIO = 2.0; _CONDITION_CONFIDENCE
    ["hurricane_next_event"] = 0.50.

  Why (c) over (a) -- and note this contradicts batch-63.md's own
  Recommendation, which said (a). The handoff file's recommendation was
  written without weighing the live-traced diagnosis already recorded in
  this entry, which recommends (c) and says outright "do NOT change the
  generic gates to accommodate one model family". That diagnosis is the
  more careful document and it wins. Concretely: shadow logging exists to
  score would-have-traded candidates, so loosening the gates for one
  family would log candidates the real placement path would never have
  taken -- contaminating the very calibration sample the 20-settled
  graduation floor exists to validate against. Buying rows at the cost of
  the rows meaning something is a bad trade.

  Why not (b): raising _CONDITION_CONFIDENCE cannot fix this even
  mechanically. Of the two real candidates traced live, only ONE died at
  the edge floor (where confidence applies); the other
  (KXNEXTHURDATE-26DEC01-26SEP01, forecast_prob 0.90 vs market_prob 0.255,
  ratio 3.53) died at the divergence-ratio gate, which runs BEFORE tier
  logic and never consults confidence at all. (b) also conflates "how much
  do we trust this model" with "we would like more samples", which is
  exactly what that constant must not become.

  Why not retiring the family: 9 of the 11 markets traced were gated on
  extreme price (e.g. yes_ask 0.99 for "a hurricane before Oct 15", correct
  market pricing in August), which is a SEASONAL condition, not a permanent
  property. Retiring now would discard a model on evidence from one point
  in the season.

  The zero-row state is therefore the correct output of gates working as
  designed, on a model whose climatology-only probabilities (0.80-0.99)
  structurally diverge from Kalshi's pricing of the same contracts
  (0.25-0.81). The entry's existing "When to revisit" triggers stand
  unchanged and are the follow-up path: re-check the row count after more
  weeks across a genuinely wider range of market states before concluding
  anything, and treat (b) as its own scoped design task with its own
  go/no-go validation if it is ever prioritized.


[RESOLVED 2026-08-24 -- batch-61 item 3; fetchedAt freshness primitive added
  and the card now has a distinct STATUS UNAVAILABLE state] RISKTAB
  ANOMALY-DETECTION CARD CANNOT
  DISTINGUISH "HEALTHY AND QUIET" FROM "/api/anomaly-status IS DOWN"
Priority: Low -- not a crash, not a data-integrity issue; a monitoring
  blind spot on a safety-relevant card.
Files: frontend/src/tabs/RiskTab.jsx (anomaly detection window section,
  ~line 289-365), frontend/src/useData.js (mapAnomalyStatus, fetchAll)

Problem:
  RiskTab's "Anomaly detection window" card renders a grey INACTIVE badge
  whenever `M.anomalyStatus.active` is falsy. Two very different real
  situations produce that exact same falsy value and therefore the exact
  same badge: (a) the anomaly monitor is genuinely healthy and hasn't
  accumulated enough settled multi-day trades yet to activate (the normal,
  intended INACTIVE state), and (b) the /api/anomaly-status endpoint itself
  is down/erroring, in which case useData.js's fetchAll() simply preserves
  whatever `M.anomalyStatus` already held (MOCK's seed data on first load,
  which also has `active: false`) -- see the `if (anomalyStatus) next.
  anomalyStatus = anomalyStatus` line, a deliberate "keep last known good
  state on fetch failure" pattern used consistently across this file's
  mappers. An operator watching the dashboard cannot tell these apart from
  the UI alone; the card would need its own staleness/fetchedAt marker
  (e.g. compare the endpoint's last-successful-fetch timestamp against now,
  or surface a distinct "data unavailable" visual state) to close the gap.

  Found during batch-44's independent opus review while auditing the same
  anomaly-status normalization the batch was already touching (mapAnomalyStatus
  M-3 fix) -- explicitly NOT caused or worsened by that fix (the ambiguity
  predates it), and explicitly scoped OUT of that batch since closing it
  needs a genuinely separate mechanism (a staleness/fetchedAt concept,
  likely wanted on other cards too) rather than a per-field normalization
  tweak.

When to revisit:
  - If a general per-endpoint staleness/fetchedAt indicator is ever added
    to useData.js (worth considering for ALL cards reading endpoint state,
    not just this one), wire this card to it as part of that same change
    rather than building a one-off marker just for anomaly-status.
  - Lower priority than most open entries: this is a monitoring
    nice-to-have, not a correctness or safety-gate defect -- the underlying
    kill-switch/halt logic itself is unaffected either way.

Resolution (2026-08-24, batch-61 item 3):
  Built the general per-endpoint staleness mechanism this entry's own "When
  to revisit" asked for, rather than a one-off marker for this card.

  THE PRIMITIVE (batch-63 is designed to reuse this -- names are stable):
    - `M.fetchedAt` -- a plain object on the useData state, keyed by feed
      name, holding the epoch-ms of that endpoint's last SUCCESSFUL fetch.
      Seeded as `{}` in mockData.js (never with a timestamp: before the
      first real poll everything on screen is mock data, so every feed is
      legitimately untrusted). fetchAll copies it per merge
      (`next.fetchedAt = { ...prev.fetchedAt }`) and writes a key ONLY
      inside the same `if (mapped)` guard that assigns the value, so a
      timestamp can never certify data the merge did not take. This batch
      populates exactly one key, `fetchedAt.anomalyStatus`; other feeds add
      their own keys the same way.
    - `feedFreshness(fetchedAt, { now, maxAgeMs, since })` in
      frontend/src/shared.jsx
      -> `{ state: 'fresh'|'stale'|'pending', stale: boolean, ageMs }`.
      Three states on purpose: 'pending' (never fetched successfully this
      session) is worded differently from 'stale' (was live, has gone quiet)
      because the operator's next action differs, but BOTH carry
      `stale: true` so a consumer that only asks "may I trust this?" reads
      `.stale` and cannot accidentally trust either.
    - `FEED_STALE_MS = 180_000` -- 3x the 60s main poll, so two consecutive
      missed polls are tolerated and the third trips it. Overridable per
      caller via maxAgeMs for a different cadence.
    - `formatFeedAge(ageMs)` -- coarse "4 min ago" / "2 hrs ago" label,
      returns null for the null ageMs 'pending' reports (so a safety banner
      can never render "NaN min ago").
    - `useFeedClock(tickMs)` -- supplies `{ now, visibleSince }`. See the
      F1/F3 findings below for why both halves are load-bearing. Backed by a
      MODULE-LEVEL singleton (one interval and one visibilitychange listener
      for the whole app, surviving component unmounts) -- see round-2 F1.
    - `FEED_HARD_STALE_MS` (4x FEED_STALE_MS = 12 min) -- a ceiling the
      visibility credit can never exceed.
    - `alarmSafeFlag(value, stale)` -- how a boolean safety reading degrades
      when its feed dies: a reassuring `false` collapses to `undefined`, an
      alarming `true` survives. See F2 below.
    A backwards client clock reads FRESH, not stale: a clock step must not
    fabricate an endpoint outage. A forward step can briefly fabricate one,
    self-correcting within a poll; both are accepted rather than switching to
    performance.now(), because fetchedAt is deliberately a wall-clock epoch so
    the banner can say WHEN the last good reading was.

  THE CARD: RiskTab's anomaly card now renders an amber STATUS UNAVAILABLE
  badge plus an explicit banner naming the endpoint and the age of the last
  good reading. Badge precedence is HALT TRIGGERED > ANOMALY > STATUS
  UNAVAILABLE > NORMAL > INACTIVE -- unavailable outranks the two "all is
  well" states (neither can be honestly asserted from a feed that stopped
  answering) but NOT a last-known alarm, because demoting a real HALT to a
  neutral "unavailable" would suppress it. Last-known values stay on screen
  under the banner rather than being blanked; losing a HALT reading because
  the feed died would be worse than showing it labelled stale. The
  "Needs N settled multi-day trades to activate" sentence -- the exact
  reassurance this entry is about -- is now suppressed while stale, since it
  is a positive claim about a live state we no longer know.

  ADJACENCY FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE: RiskTab's KillSwitchCriteriaCard (the
  checklist that tells the operator whether it is safe to turn the kill
  switch OFF) derived a green "Anomaly clear -- Pass" row straight from
  `anomaly_detected === false`, the same keep-last-known-good field. A dead
  endpoint would have kept asserting Pass from an arbitrarily old reading --
  the same blind spot on a strictly more dangerous surface. A stale feed now
  collapses that value to `undefined`, which routes through the row's
  already-existing third state ('?' / grey / "Unknown") and drops it out of
  `allPass`, rather than inventing a fourth state.

REVIEW FINDINGS ADDRESSED (independent opus review of this diff):
  - F1 (severe): feedFreshness() is pure and evaluated during render, and
    EVERY re-render source dies in exactly the failure mode this feature
    exists to surface. Renders come only from fetchAll's setData,
    handleSSEEvent and fetchWeatherAlerts; apiFetch has no timeout, so a
    backend that HANGS rather than dies never settles Promise.allSettled and
    never re-renders, while /api/stream's generator blocks inside
    _build_stream_data() so neither an SSE message nor an SSE error fires.
    The card would have sat on a green NORMAL badge indefinitely. Fixed with
    useFeedClock, an independent interval that makes staleness observable
    without any request completing. The underlying apiFetch timeout gap is
    real but is a change to all 23 endpoints' fetch path with its own
    decisions, so it was filed as its own OPEN entry at the end of this file
    rather than stretched into a display fix.
  - F2: KillSwitchCriteriaCard's first version downgraded a last-known
    `anomaly_detected: true` to grey "Unknown" when the feed died -- the row
    got LESS alarming as a direct result of losing visibility, and in the
    opposite direction to the badge precedence three cards below. Now routed
    through alarmSafeFlag(): only the reassuring `false` is withheld.
  - F3: the main poll is visibility-gated, but SSE is not and keeps
    re-rendering a hidden tab, so returning from any alt-tab longer than 3
    minutes painted a full-width "the safety monitor is not responding"
    banner that vanished ~300ms later -- alarm fatigue on the one banner
    this entry exists to make credible. feedFreshness now takes `since`
    (useFeedClock's visibleSince, reset on becoming visible), so only time we
    could actually poll counts against a feed. Wall-clock elapsed still trips
    the threshold, which is what keeps F1's hung-backend case alarming.
  - F4: 'pending' was a trap state -- an endpoint that NEVER answers (route
    404s on an older backend, a proxy blocking the path) showed "hasn't
    loaded yet, wait a moment" forever over mock numbers. It now ages from
    `since` and escalates to 'stale' with ageMs null, which the card words as
    "has not responded since this page loaded".
  - F5: 'pending' fires on every reload that lands on the Risk tab (the tab
    is restored from the URL hash), so it now renders a neutral grey
    LOADING... badge rather than the amber safety banner. Still visually
    distinct from INACTIVE, which is the entry's actual requirement.
  - F7: the two useData.test.js tests added in the first draft were
    near-duplicates of existing mapAnomalyStatus tests and asserted nothing
    about the fetchedAt merge they claimed to cover. Replaced by extracting
    mergeFetchedAt() and testing it directly (7 tests: stamps on success,
    does not stamp OR erase on failure, carries unrelated feeds forward,
    never mutates prev -- fetchAll passes MOCK itself on the first merge --
    handles a missing prev, a clock-advance positive control, and the
    mapAnomalyStatus-null-return gate end to end).
  - F8/F9/F10: removed a dead unreachable branch in formatFeedAge, added
    Number.isFinite guards on the `now`/`maxAgeMs` options (an unguarded
    NaN made every comparison false, i.e. a caller bug silently reporting a
    HEALTHY feed), added whiteSpace/flexShrink to the badge so the new longer
    label cannot wrap inside its pill, and gave the previously-unreachable
    "unknown time" fallback real wording now that F4 makes it reachable.
  - F12 is documented rather than changed: fetchedAt means "the endpoint
    answered", not "the reading is current". That is the right guarantee for
    reachability and matches the banner's wording, but batch-63 should not
    read more into it.

ROUND-2 REVIEW (the fixes above reviewed independently, since a fix can
introduce new bugs at the same or higher severity than what it fixed):
  - R2-F1 (MEDIUM/HIGH, a bug the round-1 fix INTRODUCED): `useFeedClock`
    seeded `visibleSince` from component state, and App renders tabs as
    `<ErrorBoundary key={activeTab}>`, so RiskTab and KillSwitchCriteriaCard
    fully unmount and remount on EVERY tab switch. Each visit therefore reset
    the tolerance window -- while the polling that produces `fetchedAt` lives
    in App/useData and keeps running, so the reset discarded evidence that had
    actually been collected. Measured: a dead feed still read `fresh` at a
    real age of 751s and climbing when revisiting Risk every 150s, i.e. green
    NORMAL on the card AND a green "Anomaly clear -- Pass" on the kill-switch
    checklist for the first 3 minutes of every visit. That reinstates the
    exact L30717 blind spot on the more dangerous surface, precisely while the
    operator is reading the checklist to decide whether to lift the kill
    switch. Before the round-1 `since` change, landing on the tab with a dead
    feed alarmed immediately.
    Fixed two ways: (a) the clock is now a module-level singleton, so a
    remount cannot reset it (page load is genuinely when we started watching)
    -- this also collapses the two consumers onto one interval and one
    listener; (b) FEED_HARD_STALE_MS caps the credit at 12 minutes of TRUE
    feed age, so repeated hidden->visible transitions (an operator alt-tabbing
    every couple of minutes) can no longer defer the alarm indefinitely.
    Regression test reproduces the measured revisit-every-150s sequence and
    asserts it now trips.
  - R2-F2: three PRE-EXISTING tests still patched paper.get_balance/
    get_open_trades around /api/status and _build_stream_data, which this
    change made silent no-ops -- they were passing only because they assert on
    unrelated fields, and were really running against conftest's tmp ledger.
    Repointed at paper.load_ledger_snapshot.
  - R2-F3: the two new write-route tests asserted only `spy.called`, so moving
    _invalidate_req_ledger() to the FIRST statement of the route would have
    kept them green while destroying the guarantee (it must run AFTER a
    partial write). Both now record call ORDER via a shared Mock parent and
    assert [write, invalidate]. Mutation-tested: moving the call before the
    write fails the test.
  - R2-F4: feedFreshness could return state:'fresh' alongside an arbitrarily
    large ageMs when `since` suppressed the alarm -- harmless today (no
    consumer renders both) but self-contradictory for batch-63. Now exposed
    explicitly as `suppressedBySince`.
  - R2-F5: alarmSafeFlag preserved only strict `true`, so a truthy
    non-boolean alarm was WITHHELD on staleness -- the opposite of the
    intended asymmetry. Unreachable via anomaly_detected (bool()-coerced
    server-side) but the sibling should_halt is NOT coerced and
    mapAnomalyStatus passes both through raw, so nothing enforced the
    invariant. Now any truthy reading normalizes to `true`, and the return is
    genuinely three-valued (a fresh `null` used to leak through as a fourth
    value the test's own claim excluded).
  - R2-F6: useFeedClock's tickMs is now validated like feedFreshness's
    options bag -- an unguarded 0/NaN became setInterval(fn, 0), re-rendering
    the whole Risk tab every tick.
  - R2-F7: KillSwitchCriteriaCard took the clock as a prop instead of its own
    subscription; it renders null whenever the kill switch is off and had no
    reason to hold a subscription and re-render every minute, and this makes
    it structurally impossible for the two cards to read different clocks.
  - R2-F8 (informational, accepted as no-ops with reasons): (a) if
    _invalidate_req_ledger() itself raised inside a `finally` it could mask
    the original exception -- it is has_request_context() + g.pop(), neither
    of which realistically raises, and wrapping it would add a bare except on
    a path that should fail loudly if it ever did; (b) /api/status's
    `balance` now comes from the snapshot taken at the Monte-Carlo block, so
    it is marginally more skewed against the live-read peak_balance/
    drawdown_tier/today_pnl row than before while being newly CONSISTENT with
    open_count. That is the intended trade of this change, and the reviewer
    confirmed nothing between the snapshot and the response build writes the
    ledger.
  - Round 2 found NO production defect in the Python half (items 1 and 2),
    and re-confirmed the auth removal independently a second time.

  Tests: frontend/ has no jsdom/RTL, so every decision was extracted into
  pure functions in shared.jsx/useData.js and unit-tested there (the
  established pattern -- see gradGateStatus, heatStatus, resolveByKey).
  34 new tests. `npm test`: 220 passed (was 186). Mutation-tested
  individually via Edit, each restored after: `>` -> `>=` broke the boundary
  test; `Math.abs(ageMs)` broke the clock-skew test; `pending` returning
  `stale: false` broke the never-fetched test; dropping the `Math.max` on
  `since` broke both visibility-grace tests; an unguarded `now` broke the
  options-validation test; dropping alarmSafeFlag's `value === true` branch
  broke two alarm-preservation tests; and stamping mergeFetchedAt
  unconditionally broke two success-gate tests.

  Also verified in a real browser (vite dev server, Risk tab) that all three
  states render distinctly and that the fix is not sticky: pending -> STATUS
  UNAVAILABLE + "has not loaded yet, placeholders"; a successful fetch ->
  INACTIVE + "Needs 5 settled multi-day trades..."; then a 500 plus 5
  simulated minutes -> STATUS UNAVAILABLE + "/api/anomaly-status is not
  responding -- last successful update 5 min ago."

  static/dist rebuilt in the same commit (Flask serves the built bundle, so
  a frontend source change without a rebuild ships nothing).
  Lint: no eslint/lint tooling exists in this repo for frontend/ (verified:
  no config, no lint script), so that step is a genuine no-op here.

  Same-timestamp comparison (index value at each real METAR ob's exact minute, n=33): mean|diff|

  (index at HH:00 vs nearest METAR ob, n=24): mean|diff| 1.28F, max 4.32F, 12/24 points >=1.0F.

Verdict:
  Divergence clears the spec's >=1F-at-any-settle-hour bar decisively and repeatedly, not a
  single-point outlier -- consistent with 9-16 of 16-33 sampled points across the day, not a
  borderline call needing the user's input per the spec's own protocol. Per batch-52 item 1:
  MANDATORY to build the full index-aware path -- items 2 (registration), 3 (kalshi_weather_index.py
  module + per-city observation-source seam), and 4 (settlement monitor) all shipped in full, not
  the lighter registration+cross-check-only alternative.

Batch-56 gate verdict:
  Divergence >=1F confirmed -- batch-56 (Synoptic nearby-station observations) is GO per
  INDEX-ROADMAP.md's trigger condition ("ONLY if batch-52's index-vs-METAR divergence test shows
  >=1F divergence"). Next session picking up batch-56 can proceed without re-running this
  experiment, though re-verifying against a fresh sample before that batch starts is still
  reasonable given config_version's observed churn rate.

Caveat:
  Single trailing-day sample (both endpoints' own history retention), not a live multi-day poll --
  the spec's "poll... for one afternoon" was satisfied by both endpoints already carrying ~24-34h
  of retained history rather than a dedicated real-time poll loop. Given the divergence margin is
  4-9x the 1F bar across most sampled points, a larger sample seems unlikely to overturn the
  verdict, but this hasn't been re-confirmed on a second day.

[OPEN -- filed 2026-08-24 by batch-52's opus review, item M-1] Miami hourly pools into the shared T_hourly calibration + hourly gate sample count despite a mis-referenced model
Priority: Medium
Files: ml_bias.py (train_all_temperature_scaling, _hourly_prefixes), tracker.py
  (count_settled_hourly_predictions) -- no code changed by this entry, design/data question only

Problem:
  ml_bias.py fits ONE single T_hourly temperature-scaling coefficient across all 6 hourly cities
  (_hourly_prefixes built from _KXTEMP_HOURLY_CITY, no per-city split), and
  tracker.count_settled_hourly_predictions() likewise pools all 6 for the
  HOURLY_TRADING_ENABLED settled-sample gate. KXTEMPMIAH is already ~2230 settled markets at
  ~6-7K contracts/day -- high enough volume to dominate that pool by count once it starts
  settling in bulk. Miami's own _analyze_hourly_trade probability is systematically mis-
  referenced relative to its real settlement source (batch-52's decision experiment: mean
  1.6-2.0F, max 4.68F divergence between the Kalshi Weather Index and the KMIA METAR/CLI-report
  bias correction _get_combined_station_bias actually uses) -- large enough that a city whose
  model is mis-referenced by this much could drive the calibration temperature applied to the
  5 correctly-referenced cities too, not just distort its own.
  NOT a live-trading risk today (see the paired H-2 fix below, already shipped this batch) --
  this is specifically about calibration QUALITY contamination, a separate axis from live-order
  eligibility.

Note: outcomes.settled_temp_f-based dynamic station bias (get_dynamic_station_bias) is NOT
  affected by this -- hourly writes settled_value, not settled_temp_f, so that specific pathway
  stays clean. Only the shared T_hourly fit and the pooled gate COUNT are affected.

Why not fixed now:
  A real per-city T-scaling split (or excluding Miami from the pooled fit until it has its own
  validated calibration) is genuine modeling work needing its own validation pass -- batch-52's
  explicit constraint was "no new model design in this batch." A mechanical fix attempted without
  that validation risks introducing a NEW, unreviewed modeling bug in the exact same breath as
  fixing this one.

What it would look like:
  Either (a) split ml_bias.train_all_temperature_scaling's hourly pool into a Miami-specific T
  and an others-pooled T (mirrors the existing sameday/above/below/global split shape already in
  that function), or (b) exclude Miami from BOTH the T_hourly fit's training data AND
  count_settled_hourly_predictions()'s gate count until Miami has enough of its OWN settled
  samples post-index-cross-check to validate a Miami-specific T independently. Either needs a
  real go/no-go-style validation once enough Miami-specific settled data exists, same discipline
  as batch-52 item 1's own decision experiment.

[OPEN -- filed 2026-08-24 by batch-52's opus review, item M-4] Miami hourly settlement-instant/aggregation methodology unconfirmed
Priority: Medium
Files: tracker.py (audit_settlement's Miami index cross-check), kalshi_weather_index.py
  (get_miami_index_reading_near's tolerance_min=5.0 default) -- documentation/investigation only

Problem:
  Neither batch-52 nor Kalshi's public docs establish the EXACT instant/aggregation KXTEMPMIAH
  settles on -- the index value at the literal top of the hour? A windowed aggregate over some
  interval? tracker.audit_settlement's Miami cross-check assumes "nearest index point within 5
  minutes of HH:00 local" as a reasonable approximation, not a confirmed match. If Kalshi's real
  methodology differs (e.g. an average over the preceding N minutes, or a different anchor
  instant), the cross-check's MISMATCH alert path could fire on a systematic basis unrelated to
  any real bug -- alert fatigue that would erode trust in the one mechanism this batch built
  specifically to catch a genuine settlement-source problem. (The alert text itself was already
  softened this session to note this uncertainty explicitly, so a false-positive mismatch doesn't
  read as a confirmed bug report to whoever sees it.)
  Related, smaller note: _fetch_asos_hour_temp (the METAR half of the comparison) picks the
  observation nearest HH:00, but routine METAR reports land at :51-:56 past the hour -- so the
  "metar=..." and "index=..." values logged side-by-side in the same audit_settlement log line
  can be sampled ~7 minutes apart while being presented as directly comparable.

Why not fixed now:
  There's no way to determine Kalshi's real methodology without either (a) Kalshi documenting it
  explicitly, or (b) enough real KXTEMPMIAH settlements accumulating to empirically correlate the
  index's own minute-resolution history against Kalshi's actual declared outcomes and back out
  the aggregation window statistically -- neither is available yet this session.

What it would look like:
  Once enough real Miami hourly settlements exist (the same 20-settled-sample scale this
  project's other gates already use as a floor), run a correlation pass: for each settled
  KXTEMPMIAH ticker, pull the index's full minute-resolution history around the target hour and
  test which candidate aggregation (instant-at-HH:00, N-minute trailing average, etc.) best
  predicts Kalshi's actual declared result. Revisit tolerance_min and the cross-check's framing
  based on the result.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-25 -- batch-63 item 3; soft warn naming the age, on all four order actions, at ORDER_STALE_MS = FEED_STALE_MS / 2] No data-freshness gate on order actions (Approve/Close) -- batch-47's visibility-gated polling made a pre-existing gap materially wider
Priority: Medium
Files: frontend/src/App.jsx (Nav's Override button aside, no relevant order actions there),
  frontend/src/tabs/SignalsTab.jsx (Approve button, buildPaperOrderBody), frontend/src/tabs/
  PositionsTab.jsx (Close Position button), frontend/src/useData.js (stats.timestamp, the only
  freshness marker that exists today) -- no code changed by this entry, design/scope question only

Problem:
  Order flows price entirely off frontend-cached data: SignalsTab's Approve button sends
  buildPaperOrderBody's entry_price derived from the cached opportunity's yes_bid/yes_ask;
  PositionsTab's Close Position button sends a price derived from the cached position's mark.
  Nothing in the frontend currently gates either action on how stale that cached data actually
  is -- stats.timestamp (set once per successful fetchAll(), read only by App.jsx's
  RefreshCountdown label) is the only freshness signal that exists, and it isn't checked anywhere
  before submitting an order.
  This gap existed before batch-47 too, but batch-47's visibility-gated polling (item 1: pause
  every poll loop while document.hidden, one catch-up fetch + resume on return) makes the
  possible staleness window materially larger. Before batch-47, a backgrounded tab's setInterval
  polls kept ticking (Chrome throttles a hidden tab's timers to roughly once/minute after ~5
  minutes hidden, but never fully stops them), so cached quotes were stale by at most roughly a
  minute or two even after hours backgrounded. After batch-47, the poll loops are explicitly
  stopped while hidden -- data can now be genuinely hours-stale (however long the tab sat
  backgrounded) the moment the operator returns and clicks Approve/Close before the catch-up
  fetch (itself a batch of ~22 concurrent requests, not instant) has resolved.

Why not fixed now:
  Confirmed with the user (2026-08-24, opus review of batch-47): a real staleness gate is a new
  safety feature for order-placement flows, not one of batch-47's four scoped items (polling
  visibility-gating, NaN/Infinity KPI guards, tab-registry consolidation, lazy tab loading).
  Bolting a gate onto SignalsTab/PositionsTab in the same change as an unrelated polling
  refactor risks under-designing it (wrong threshold, wrong set of gated actions, block-vs-warn
  UX not actually decided) under the same review pass meant to catch bugs in the polling change
  itself.

What it would look like:
  Add a threshold check (e.g. ~90s, informed by the 60s main-poll interval) against
  Date.now() - stats.timestamp before allowing Approve/Close to submit -- either disable the
  button outright with a "data is stale, refreshing…" state, or allow submission with an
  explicit confirm-dialog warning naming how stale the quote is. Needs its own design decision on
  which actions to cover (Approve in SignalsTab, Close in PositionsTab -- check RiskTab and any
  other order-adjacent controls too) and whether hard-block or soft-warn is the right UX for a
  paper-trading dashboard versus what it should be if/when live trading is enabled.

Resolution 2026-08-25 (batch-63 item 3) -- three decisions, taken together.

  THRESHOLD: ORDER_STALE_MS = FEED_STALE_MS / 2 (= 90s today).
  A DELIBERATE divergence from batch-61's 180s display banner, not a second
  accidental constant. The cost profile inverts between the two surfaces:
  for a banner a false alarm is expensive (an operator learns to ignore a
  badge that cries wolf) and being 30s late to say "feed down" costs
  nothing, while for an order confirm an unnecessary "95s old" line costs
  one extra glance and a MISSED stale quote books a real mispriced trade
  into the ledger, balance, drawdown tier and graduation P&L. It is
  written as `FEED_STALE_MS / 2` rather than `90_000` precisely so the two
  numbers stay structurally linked -- retune the banner and this follows,
  instead of the dashboard ending up with two unrelated magic numbers that
  quietly disagree about what "stale" means.

  BLOCK vs WARN: soft warn, naming the age.
  A hard disable would trap an operator who needs to act on a stale quote
  -- the same trap batch-63 item 1 exists to undo on the close path -- and
  a tab returning from a long background stretch is mid-catch-up (~22
  concurrent requests, not instant) exactly when they may most need to
  act. Naming the age informs the decision instead of removing it. This is
  a paper dashboard; the note in shared.jsx says to revisit toward a hard
  block if live trading is ever enabled from this surface.

  SCOPE: all four order actions -- Approve, bulk Approve (SignalsTab),
  Close, bulk Close (PositionsTab). Verified this is the COMPLETE set, not
  a partial sweep: RiskTab has no POST at all, and SettingsTab's only POST
  is configuration, not an order.

What shipped (frontend only; no Python touched):
  - shared.jsx: ORDER_STALE_MS, orderQuoteStaleness(fetchedAt, {now,
    maxAgeMs, since}) and staleQuoteWarning(staleness, noun) as pure,
    unit-tested functions, plus a presentational StaleQuoteNotice so all
    four surfaces render identical copy.
  - This REUSES batch-61's staleness layer rather than building a second
    one. orderQuoteStaleness is a thin specialization of feedFreshness,
    and the ticking clock is 61's useFeedClock singleton -- which matters
    here for 61's own reason: every other re-render source (fetchAll's
    setData, SSE, the alerts poll) dies in exactly the failure mode this
    warning exists to surface, so without the independent heartbeat the
    age would freeze at whatever it was when something last re-rendered.
  - ONE deliberate behavioral difference from the banner: a reading that
    is only "fresh" because the `since` visibility credit restarted the
    tolerance window counts as STALE for an order. That credit is the
    right rule for "is the backend alive" and the wrong rule for "is this
    price current" -- the price is that old either way. batch-61 exposed
    exactly this distinction as feedFreshness's `suppressedBySince`,
    naming batch-63's order gate as the intended consumer; this is that
    consumer.
  - useData.js: `positions` and `opportunities` added to the SAME
    mergeFetchedAt map 61 built (not a parallel one), each keyed off its
    own merge's resolved value, so a timestamp can never claim freshness
    for data the merge did not take. mapTrades exported so that predicate
    is mutation-testable, matching resolveOpportunities/mapAlerts.
    Verified fetchAll is the only writer of both: the SSE stream patches
    stats (balance/open_count/brier) and nothing else.
  - PositionsTab's bulk Close is the one order action with NO confirm
    modal (it submits every selected position's p.mark immediately), so
    its notice lives in the selection bar beside the button. The wording
    is number-agnostic for that reason. The single-close modal shows the
    notice only on the live-mark branch -- the other branch is the
    operator typing the price themselves, which no feed staleness can
    make out of date.
  - static/dist rebuilt in the same commit.

  NOT double-counted: batch-48 already closed the stale-MODAL half on the
  Signals side (resolveByKey re-derives the opportunity from live data
  every render). This closes the different half -- M.opportunities and
  M.positions being minutes old underneath.

Opus review (effort:high) then a second opus review of the fixes. Round 1
  found one HIGH and four MEDIUMs on this half; all addressed:
  - HIGH: useFeedClock's mount path ADOPTED the singleton's `now` without
    refreshing it. App renders tabs as <ErrorBoundary key={activeTab}>, so
    when the last consumer unmounts, _stopFeedClock clears both the
    interval and the visibilitychange listener -- from then on nothing
    writes `now` and it freezes, while useData keeps polling and keeps
    advancing fetchedAt. Returning to the tab adopted the frozen value, so
    a 20-minute-old mark read FRESH and NO warning rendered for up to a
    full tick -- the exact window in which the operator selects rows and
    clicks Close. This was batch-61's bug, not this batch's, and it also
    silently reinstated the blind spot on RiskTab's kill-switch checklist.
    Fixed at the source: mount now refreshes before adopting.
  - MEDIUM: the effective threshold was 90-150s, not 90s, because the gate
    read the 60s-lagging clock. Both tabs now use useFeedClock purely as a
    re-render heartbeat and measure with Date.now() at render. (Passing a
    smaller tickMs would NOT have worked: _startFeedClock returns early if
    a timer exists, so the first subscriber's tick wins -- documented in
    place as a trap.)
  - MEDIUM: the gate measured POLL age, not QUOTE age -- feedFreshness's
    own docstring warns fetchedAt means only "this endpoint answered".
    Two real holes, both closed: (a) /api/live_signals serves
    signals_cache.json for up to FOUR HOURS with a 200, so Approve could
    submit an hours-old scan price under a seconds-fresh timestamp -- the
    gate now also reads signalsMeta.generatedAt/.stale, combined via the
    new worstStaleness; (b) /api/trades falls back to the SSE snapshot
    cache ("stale/partial", per its own comment) whenever the live Kalshi
    batch-fetch fails, still answering 200 with a live-LOOKING mark -- so
    the Kalshi-unreachable/dashboard-healthy outage gave Close a cached
    price with nothing to warn about. Added `quote_is_live` to /api/trades
    (both sides must be live) and carried it through mapTrades as
    `quoteIsLive`; undefined from an older backend makes no claim.
  - MEDIUM: a fetchedAt in the FUTURE (backward NTP/DST/manual clock step)
    reported fresh, which would silence all four gates at once until every
    stamp caught up. A negative age is now stale, with the "no trustworthy
    age" wording.
  - MEDIUM: the stamping predicates were unreachable from any test --
    mutating `positions: trades.open != null` to a bare `true` left all
    235 tests green. Extracted as the pure `orderFeedSuccess`; that
    mutation now kills four tests.
  - LOW: `.not.toBeNull()` passes for undefined, so the "an empty list
    stamps" test could not catch the bug its own comment described; LOW:
    mapTrades treated a 200-with-error body as success, which would clear
    positions AND stamp fresh (not reachable through today's backend, now
    closed by construction); LOW: orderQuoteStaleness threw on an explicit
    null options bag, during render, at the top of both tabs; LOW: the
    notice was unlikely to reach screen readers -- both approve dialogs now
    point aria-describedby at it; LOW: the bulk bar's restructured flex
    container left the buttons off-centre when the notice showed.
  DELIBERATE NO-OPS: the hard 720s ceiling inside feedFreshness is inert
  for this gate (the suppressedBySince OR subsumes it) -- documented in
  place, with a note to change the two together; the palette literal
  matches existing amber usage; and one extra re-render per minute on two
  tabs is accepted. WHICH fetchedAt key each tab reads remains untestable
  (no jsdom/RTL) and is an accepted, stated risk.

  A THIRD review round reviewed those fixes and found a HIGH that round 2
  had INTRODUCED, plus three more:
  - HIGH: the new scan-age source was gated at ORDER_STALE_MS (90 SECONDS)
    -- but the scan is produced by a cron that runs every THREE HOURS, and
    /api/live_signals serves its cache for four. So the Approve and bulk
    Approve modals would have shown the amber warning on EVERY click
    forever, while the header chip ten lines above said "Last scan: 45m
    ago" in neutral grey. A permanent warning is one nobody reads -- and
    because it is the same component, wording and colour as the Close-path
    notice, which does fire meaningfully, it would have corroded that one
    too. Exactly the alarm-fatigue cost ORDER_STALE_MS's own comment says
    the design is optimising against, introduced by the fix for it. Added
    SCAN_STALE_MS = 90 min: not a new number, but the threshold the header
    chip has always used, which the chip now reads from the same constant
    so the two cannot disagree on screen.
  - MEDIUM: the cached-quote path forced `stale` but carried the FETCH age
    through, so the notice read "Last refreshed less than a minute ago"
    in precisely the scenario it exists for (dashboard polling happily,
    Kalshi unreachable) -- reassurance that invites the click. It now says
    the live quote was unavailable and the mark came from a cached
    snapshot.
  - LOW: refreshing `_feedClock.now` on mount without `visibleSince` left
    the pair inconsistent, so feedFreshness's `since` credit was
    unavailable right after a background stretch and RiskTab could flash a
    false "monitor not responding" amber. Now refreshed together, but ONLY
    across a genuinely stopped clock, so batch-61's own fix stays intact.
  - LOW: a clock-stepped reading passed its NEGATIVE age through, which is
    finite and therefore ranked BELOW every real age in worstStaleness --
    so an unknowable age lost to a merely old one, contradicting that
    function's own documented rule. Now reports a null age.
  - LOW: quote_is_live was a PAIR-level flag, so an ordinary overnight
    one-sided book marked a live exit-side quote as cached. Now answered
    for the side the position would actually realize on.
  - LOW: the bulk notice ranged over selected rows that handleBulkClose
    then silently skips (no id, or no live mark), tainting the batch for a
    row not in it. Now uses the exact submit set.
  - LOW/INFO: useFeedClock had no coverage at all and its
    __resetFeedClockForTests seam was dead, so reverting the round-1 HIGH
    fix broke nothing; parseFeedTimestamp's `includes('+')` heuristic
    (inherited verbatim from the inline version it replaced) mangled
    NEGATIVE UTC offsets. Both addressed.
  REMAINING ACCEPTED RISK, stated rather than dropped: with no jsdom/RTL,
  WHICH fetchedAt key each tab reads, and whether the notice is rendered at
  all, cannot be tested -- those four insertion points are guarded by
  review only. PositionsTab's close modal has no role="dialog" to hang
  aria-describedby on (pre-existing), so its notice keeps the same
  screen-reader limitation the Signals modals just had fixed; giving that
  modal real dialog semantics is its own accessibility task.

Tests: frontend/src/shared.test.js 156 (+29) and useData.test.js 103
  (+10); tests/test_web_app.py 99, with four quote_is_live cases.
  Mutation-tested individually: ORDER_STALE_MS = FEED_STALE_MS fails 5;
  SCAN_STALE_MS = ORDER_STALE_MS fails 2; dropping
  `|| f.suppressedBySince` fails the since-credit test; passing the
  negative age through fails the clock-step ranking test; dropping the
  cached-reason wording fails 1; mapTrades returning [] instead of null on

  an empty open list returning undefined fails 4; inverting

  cached-wording tests each carry a positive control, so none can pass
