[RESOLVED 2026-08-24 -- built as A14 from the "Weather V3 additions" design
  handoff; the finding arrived before the panel did] MODEL-VS-MARKET BRIER
  SHOWS NO MEASURABLE FORECAST SKILL
Priority: High -- the scanner's claimed edge is unsupported by forecast
  accuracy on every slice with usable sample size.
Files: tracker.py (_paired_advantage, _brier_series_stats,
  get_model_vs_market_brier, brier_skill_score), web_app.py (/api/analytics),
  tests/test_model_vs_market_brier.py

Problem:
  Nothing scored the market's own mid-price with the same yardstick we score
  ourselves with, so "our probability disagrees with the price" was never
  separated into "we have edge" versus "we are wrong". brier_skill_score()
  came closest but reads the multiday_predictions view, which filters
  days_out >= 1 OR NULL and therefore discards D+0 -- 56% of settled rows --
  and pooled every remaining horizon into one number with no climatology
  reference.

  Measured on 214 settled, non-disputed, condition-filtered rows:
    model Brier 0.2596  vs  market 0.2201  vs  climatology 0.2482
    skill -0.179
  Unfiltered (n=342): skill -0.142, paired t=2.59 on per-row Brier
  differences, 95% CI [+0.008, +0.057], bootstrap P(model worse) = 0.9965.
  Against a flat 0.50 forecast: t=0.69 -- statistically indistinguishable
  from a coin flip. Every slice agrees in sign and rough magnitude
  (D+0 real -0.144, D+1 real -0.173, shadow -0.057, real -0.178).

  Verified apples-to-apples before trusting it: market_prob is the YES mid
  (yes_bid+yes_ask)/2 from weather_markets.parse_market_price's
  "implied_prob", our_prob is the blended YES probability, and
  outcomes.settled_yes is 1 when YES won -- all three in YES-space.

What shipped:
  get_model_vs_market_brier() scores both against the same outcome, split by
  lead (D+0 / D+1 / D+2+) and by is_shadow, with in-sample climatology
  reported and leave-one-out climatology used for gating. Joins
  outcomes_valid and applies _excluded_brier_condition_types() like every
  other Brier-quality query. Served via /api/analytics as
  `model_vs_market_brier`, replacing brier_skill_score in that payload so
  the dashboard cannot show two disagreeing "skill vs market" figures.

  The `policy` label is display-only -- nothing in the sizing, gating or
  order path reads it, same convention as log_prediction()'s gated_edge. It
  is gated on a paired significance test (beat both the market and
  leave-one-out climatology by more than 1.645 SE) rather than a fixed
  sample floor. A first attempt used n >= 100; an opus review measured that
  emitting "trade" on ~22% of pure-noise samples at this bot's own
  disagreement level (sd(our_prob - market_prob) = 0.22), because a fixed
  relative threshold cannot track a noise floor that shrinks as 1/sqrt(n).

  brier_skill_score() now delegates its arithmetic to _brier_series_stats
  (verified bit-identical over 200k randomised row-sets) so the two can never
  drift. Its ROW SELECTION is deliberately unchanged, so it remains listed on
  the open "MORE BRIER-FAMILY FUNCTIONS WITH NO CONDITION_TYPE FILTER" entry.

  Tests: 46 in tests/test_model_vs_market_brier.py. Regression sweep 651
  passed across test_tracker, test_calibration, test_disputed_row_guard,
  test_web_app. Two opus review rounds (16 + 11 findings, all addressed) and
  9 mutation checks. Round 2 caught a sign inversion in _paired_advantage
  that made "significantly better" test the opposite of its name, and a
  surviving mutant proving the significance margin itself was untested; both
  are now pinned by dedicated tests.

  Caveats are in the docstring and must not be dropped: Brier measures
  calibration, not P&L; the statistic is unconditional on the SIZE of the
  disagreement with the price; the population is self-selected. See the
  follow-up entry below before concluding anything about profitability.


[RESOLVED 2026-08-25 -- batch-66 item 1; filed 2026-08-24 as a follow-up to the A14 no-skill finding above] MEASURE
  BRIER SKILL CONDITIONED ON THE SIZE OF OUR DISAGREEMENT WITH THE PRICE
Priority: High -- decides whether the A14 finding means "no edge anywhere"
  or "no edge on average, with edge in the tail we actually trade".
Files: tracker.py (get_model_vs_market_brier)

Problem:
  A14's pooled Brier skill is unconditional: it scores every market the
  scanner analyzed, including the many where our probability broadly agreed
  with the mid. Those rows contribute almost nothing to the model-minus-
  market difference and pull the statistic toward zero. Trading edge, if it
  exists, lives specifically in the subset where the disagreement was large
  enough to act on -- which is exactly the subset the pooled number cannot
  see.

  So a pooled skill of -0.179 is consistent with real edge on the traded
  tail, and a positive pooled skill would have been consistent with no edge
  there. The measurement as it stands cannot distinguish these.

  Two further confounders, both already noted in the A14 docstring:
  - Population is self-selected. `predictions` holds only markets the
    scanner chose to analyze; is_shadow=0 holds only those it chose to
    trade. There is no record of markets it never looked at.
  - Brier measures probability calibration, not P&L. A model can be badly
    calibrated and still profitable if it is directionally right at the
    moments it trades, and well calibrated yet unprofitable after fees and
    spread.

Recommendation:
  Add an optional `min_edge` parameter to get_model_vs_market_brier() and
  report a second series conditioned on
  abs(our_prob - market_prob) >= min_edge, at the edge floor the scanner
  actually uses. Report n alongside it -- the tail will be small, and the
  same paired significance test the policy gate already uses should decide
  whether anything can be concluded from it rather than a raw threshold.

  Pair it with a P&L-side read before drawing any conclusion about the
  strategy: realized return on settled trades bucketed by claimed edge is
  the A1 "edge attribution" panel from the same design handoff, and answers
  the profitability half that Brier structurally cannot.

  Until this lands, treat the A14 headline as "the forecast is not better
  calibrated than the price on average", NOT as "the strategy has no edge".
  Live trading is dormant; this is a reason to keep it dormant pending the
  conditional read, not evidence to rebuild the model.

Resolution (2026-08-25, batch-66 item 1) -- ANSWERED, and the answer is NO edge
in the tail. This is the go/no-go for panel-backend track D (batches 72-74).
  Shipped: get_model_vs_market_brier() gained an optional `min_edge` parameter
  and a `conditioned` ladder -- the same statistic restricted to rows where
  abs(our_prob - market_prob) >= each rung of BRIER_CONDITIONAL_LADDER
  (0.10/0.15/0.20/0.25/0.30), with n, n_markets and a per-rung n_by_lead
  disclosing the horizon mix. `pooled` and `buckets` stay unconditional so the
  rungs have an honest baseline to be read against. The verb on each rung comes
  from _paired_advantage, NOT from a raw skill threshold -- explicitly, because
  a fixed threshold on a small tail is the defect an opus review already caught
  once in this function.

  Measured on the live DB, 2026-08-25 (n=214 filtered settled rows; the pooled
  figures reproduce A14's published numbers exactly, so this is the same
  population, not a re-scoped one):
      rung    n    model   market    skill    z     policy
      pooled 214  0.2596   0.2201  -0.1793  -2.64  (stand down)
      0.10   211  0.2590   0.2203  -0.1760  -2.56  stand down
      0.15   206  0.2573   0.2198  -0.1705  -2.43  stand down
      0.20    97  0.2864   0.2322  -0.2333  -1.94  stand down
      0.25    46  0.3105   0.2301  -0.3491  -1.63  inconclusive
      0.30    27  0.2967   0.2073  -0.4315  -1.27  inconclusive

  The hypothesis is not merely unsupported, it is inverted. The model's Brier
  gets monotonically WORSE as the disagreement grows (0.2596 pooled -> 0.2864
  at 0.20 -> 0.3105 at 0.25) while the market's stays flat near 0.22. Probed
  past the last shipped rung during the investigation, the trend continues:
  0.3483 at >=0.35 (n=18) and 0.3639 at >=0.40 (n=10) -- both below the
  reporting floor, which is why the ladder stops at 0.30 rather than rendering
  them.
  We are most wrong exactly where we disagree most with the price. The paired
  advantage never turns positive at any rung; it goes from -0.0395 to -0.1281
  and only loses statistical significance as n shrinks -- "inconclusive" at the
  top rungs is loss of power, not a hint of edge.

  A second finding makes the whole conditioning exercise nearly moot on this
  data: THE POPULATION IS ALREADY THE TAIL. 100% of the 214 settled rows have
  abs(our_prob - market_prob) >= 0.07 (the live MIN_EDGE default) and 96.3%
  clear 0.15; the 10th percentile of disagreement is 0.1556 and the median is
  0.1943. The scanner only logs candidates that already cleared its own edge
  bar, so the low-disagreement rows the entry hypothesised were diluting the
  statistic largely DO NOT EXIST in the table. There was never a pooled-vs-tail
  distinction to recover below ~0.20; only the 0.20+ rungs partition anything,
  and those are where the model looks worst.

  Both stated confounders remain, unfixed and deliberately so (they are now
  written into the function's own docstring rather than only here):
  - Self-selection still applies, and bites HARDER on the conditioned rungs
    than on the pooled figure for the reason just given. Conditioning narrows
    an already-narrow observational sample; it does not randomise it.
  - Brier measures calibration, not P&L. That half is item 3
    (tracker.get_edge_capture / paper.get_edge_capture): capture ratio 0.378,
    intercept -0.197, over 243 settled trades, with a MEAN REALIZED RETURN of
    -0.040 per dollar of cost and three of four claimed-edge buckets negative.
    The waterfall (202 held-to-settlement rows) attributes what positive return
    exists overwhelmingly to post-entry market drift (+0.0668 per dollar of
    cost) rather than to settlement surprise (+0.0162) -- i.e. the P&L is not
    obviously coming from forecast skill either. Neither read supports "edge in
    the tail"; the P&L read is actively against it.
    NOTE, because the first pass got this wrong: an initial version reported
    0.519 / 203 trades. That filtered settled rows on outcome in ("yes","no"),
    which silently dropped all 40 outcome == "early_exit" rows -- the stop-loss
    and model-flip exits, i.e. the positions closed BECAUSE the edge evaporated,
    mean realized -0.625. Excluding them turned a losing population into a
    winning one. Caught by opus review; the shipped predicate is the
    `settled and pnl is not None` one get_parameter_sweep/get_attribution
    already use.

  Consequence for track D: batches 72-74 (A4 order-book depth, A8, A17
  execution plumbing, A9 intraday METAR) are machinery for COLLECTING edge more
  efficiently. On this evidence there is no measured edge for them to collect,
  and INDEX-PANEL-BACKENDS.md's own sequencing rule makes 66 the gate on them.
  Recommend NO-GO on 72-74 pending a model change that actually moves the
  conditional Brier, not more collection machinery. Live trading stays dormant.

Go/no-go experiment (run FIRST, before any code was written):
  The batch spec's own bar: "blend beats single-station by >=0.3F RMSE" against the Kalshi
  Weather Index. Blocker found immediately -- Synoptic Data's free open-access tier requires a
  registered API token (confirmed live: unauthenticated -> HTTP 401 "Missing token"; a bogus
  token -> HTTP 403), and registering an account is not something this session could do.

  Ran the experiment on free ASOS instead: aviationweather.gov multi-station METAR for the 8
  nearest South Florida stations, scored against the Kalshi index at every KMIA observation
  time over the endpoint's full retained ~24h window (2026-08-24 01:53 -- 2026-08-25 02:53 UTC,
  n=33 paired points). Split into two temporal halves to rule out config-selection overfit,
  evaluating ONLY the design the batch file pre-registered ("5-10 nearest stations,
  distance-weighted") rather than an argmax over the whole config sweep:

    kernel 1/(d+10km), k=5   1st half +0.369F   2nd half +0.793F   full +0.682F
    kernel 1/(d+10km), k=8   1st half +0.589F   2nd half +1.195F   full +1.033F

  (RMSE improvement of the blend over KMIA-alone. Baseline KMIA-alone RMSE over the full
  window: 2.055F, bias -0.436F -- consistent with batch-52's independently-measured 1.6-2.0F.)
  Every pre-registered slice clears +0.300F; k=8 dominates k=5 on every slice. PASS.

  Diagnostic worth recording: an unsmoothed inverse-distance kernel does NOT pass. With the
  anchor station at d=0 clamped to 0.5km it takes ~96% of the total weight and the blend
  collapses back onto KMIA (+0.005F improvement, a null result). The smoothing term is what
  makes the blend a blend -- hence SMOOTHING_KM, and a dedicated mutation-tested regression
  guarding it.

What shipped:
  nearby_station_obs.py -- SHADOW/DATA-COLLECTION ONLY. Deliberately NOT named synoptic_obs.py
  (the batch file's suggestion): the gate passed without Synoptic, so the implemented backend is
  NWS /points/{lat,lon}/stations for discovery (returns ~20 nearby stations with coordinates;
  nws._get_obs_station already calls this exact endpoint and discards everything but
  features[0]) plus aviationweather.gov batched multi-station METAR for observations (one HTTP
  request for the whole set, the endpoint metar.py already wraps). A StationSource Protocol is
  the seam a Synoptic backend plugs into later without touching blend/QC/recorder logic.

  A Synoptic backend was deliberately NOT written blind. The only Synoptic responses this
  session ever observed were its 401/403 error bodies, and mocking a success shape never seen
  live is precisely the failure mode this project has already been burned by (batch-52's
  predecessor mocked a Kalshi order status the real exchange never returns). Synoptic's real
  added value is CWOP + state-mesonet density, which neither free source provides -- that
  remains the reason to add the backend if a key is ever registered.

  QC replaces what Synoptic's own quality flags would have supplied (the batch's explicit
  "a bad station must not degrade a calibrated pipeline" constraint). Four fail-closed gates:
  plausibility (-60/130F), staleness (>90 min, AND a >5-min future-skew lower bound), median
  outlier rejection (>8F from the surviving set's median -- loose on purpose, real South Florida
  sea-breeze gradients reach 4-6F and this must catch a broken sensor, not a real gradient), and
  a 3-station quorum. Gate ordering matters and is regression-tested: the outlier median is
  computed over plausibility survivors, never over raw readings.

  cron._cmd_cron_body calls record_shadow_sample(client) once per cycle, next to batch-52's
  config_version drift watch. It never raises, and is idempotent within a METAR hour (samples
  are keyed by the anchor station's observation time) so the accumulating RMSE is weighted by
  distinct observations rather than by how often cron happens to run. Unlike
  consistency.record_shadow_observations it is deliberately NOT skipped on --sameday-only: its
  population is weather stations and the index feed, neither derived from the cycle's market
  list, so every cycle genuinely could produce a sample and cycles_observed stays honest.
  Index points with status != "normal" are counted as an observed cycle but never scored --
  batch-52's module passes status through unfiltered and puts the obligation on the caller;
  this is that caller honoring it.

Explicitly NOT done (shadow-only, per INDEX-ROADMAP.md's standing rule):
  Nothing wires the blend into any probability, lock-in, or order path. weather_markets.py's
  obs-weight integration (analyze_trade's _obs_w blend at ~:13933 and obs_weight_used at
  ~:14899) is UNTOUCHED -- get_live_observation remains the sole observation source for
  probability. A regression test asserts that structurally: weather_markets.py, trade_cycle.py,
  order_executor.py, metar.py and nws.py must not reference nearby_station_obs at all, paired
  with a positive control that cron.py does. The graduation decision -- whether this blend
  should ever feed KXTEMPMIAH's probability -- is a human call made later against
  get_shadow_report()'s accumulated multi-day history. A 24h go/no-go justifies COLLECTING,
  not TRADING; get_shadow_report's meets_gonogo_bar field is a reporting value nothing reads
  as a switch.

Scope decision (user, this session):
  Miami only. It is the one tracked family whose settlement variable IS a multi-station index,
  so the blend approximates the real settlement target AND the Kalshi live_data feed supplies
  independent ground truth to score against. For the other 20 cities in MARKET_STATION_MAP the
  settlement variable is a single station the bot already reads directly, so a blend would
  diverge from settlement by construction -- it would measure regional smoothing, not
  settlement tracking. The batch file makes the same point ("for 39 of 40 tracked series the
  settlement variable is a single station the bot already reads directly").

Independent opus review (effort=high) -- 3 HIGH, 6 MEDIUM, 10 LOW, 7 INFO, ALL addressed:

  H-1 TEST ISOLATION LEAK, already realised in production data. tests/conftest.py's
    isolate_cron_generated_files fixture exists precisely to redirect "every production path
    _cmd_cron_body() (or something it calls) can write to" -- and its own body already
    redirects consistency.RAIN_ARB_SHADOW_PATH for this exact leak class. The new recorder's
    _SHADOW_PATH was not added, so this batch's OWN test runs wrote 110 phantom cycles into
    the main clone's real data/nearby_station_shadow.json (paths.py resolves data/ to the main
    clone regardless of worktree -- [[feedback_worktree_data_dir_gotcha]] again). cycles_observed
    is the denominator get_shadow_report() divides by, so the module's entire deliverable was
    corrupted before production cron ever ran it. Fixed (fixture + the two module-level cache
    resets and the _obs_cb breaker reset, added to the same proactive lists batch-52's
    _index_cb went into), polluted file deleted, and verified BOTH directions: 112 cron tests
    now leave no production file, and disabling the fixture again immediately recreated it with
    18 cycles.

  H-2 A single transient OSError on read destroyed the whole accumulated history. _load_state()
    caught OSError in the same branch as malformed JSON and returned an empty state, which
    record_shadow_sample then wrote straight back over the real file. Self-healing is correct
    for corrupt CONTENT and wrong for a transient I/O fault. Not hypothetical on Windows:
    circuit_breaker.py documents this precise race for its own state file (an unlocked read
    landing mid-os.replace of a concurrent locked write raises PermissionError), and two cron
    processes can both write this file every cycle. Now raises a distinct _StateReadError and
    the recorder writes NOTHING that cycle.

  H-3 The HALF-OPEN circuit-breaker probe was consumed and then blocked, wedging the breaker
    permanently. CircuitBreaker.is_open() is STATEFUL: the first call after recovery_timeout
    sets _half_open and returns False ("this caller is the probe"). blend_nearby_observation()
    and get_nearby_stations() each called it, so the outer call took the probe and the inner
    one returned True -- discover() never ran, neither record_success() nor record_failure()
    fired, and _half_open stayed latched forever. In a long-lived loop/watch --auto process the
    collector went silent after 3 consecutive upstream failures and never recovered. Every
    sibling module calls is_open() exactly once per fetch. Fixed: exactly one check per real
    fetch, and the discovery cache is now consulted BEFORE the check (static geometry is still
    good while open). The original circuit test could not catch this because it reset _opened_at
    by hand; the new one drives the real recovery path via a monkeypatched clock.

  M-4 Dedup keyed on a single "last seen" scalar, defeated by the settlement station dropping
      out and returning -- the same observation scored twice. Now checks membership across the
      whole retained sample tail.
  M-5 The blend could mix readings up to 95 minutes apart and score them against a single-minute
      index value; MAX_OBS_AGE_MIN gates each station individually, which is all metar.py ever
      needed. Added QC gate 2b (MAX_OBS_SPREAD_MIN = 30), which drops the laggard rather than
      the whole sample.
  M-6 rmse_single_f silently meant "whatever the nearest working station was", not KMIA-alone,
      because the anchor falls back when the settlement station fails QC -- and meets_gonogo_bar
      had no sample floor, reporting True off n=1 in a module whose stated convention is the
      20-sample gate. Fixed: blend now reports primary_* (the metar.MARKET_STATION_MAP
      settlement station) separately from anchor_*, the recorder scores ONLY primary_*, and the
      verdict stays None below MIN_SAMPLES_FOR_VERDICT = 20.
  M-7 get_shadow_report's docstring promised None on an unreadable file but returned a zeroed
      report, making corruption indistinguishable from a fresh install. Now returns None.
  M-8 The shadow-only structural test hand-listed 5 modules, so wiring the blend into
      trading_gates.py or ml_bias.py would have kept it green. Now sweeps every root module with
      a glob, plus a positive control on the sweep itself and on cron.py's CALL (not just its
      import -- I-21).
  M-9 StationSource.discover()/observe() were called outside any try, so the documented
      fail-closed contract of both public functions was actually provided by their caller. A
      future Synoptic backend that raised would have propagated. Both now wrapped.

  LOW/INFO, all fixed: breaker+cache reset fixtures (L-10); nearby_station_shadow.json added to
    test_cleanup_data_dir's required set (L-11); a boundary test whose docstring claimed both
    plausibility bounds were KEPT when the fixture actually had both rejected as outliers
    (L-12); a normalization test passing by ~8e-17 of margin and asserting rounded rather than
    real weights (L-13); no _OBS_CACHE coverage at all -- the cache could have been deleted
    outright with the suite green (L-14); no test exercising the real blend->recorder path or
    the rejected-row JSON serialization (L-15); a cron comment claiming "at most one cached
    round-trip" that is wrong for one-shot cron, where both in-memory caches are cold every
    invocation -- comment corrected and timeouts tightened to (3, 8) so the worst case stays
    well inside the watchdog window (L-16); an empty observe() result recording breaker SUCCESS
    and positively caching {} for 15 min, blinding the breaker to a total outage (L-17);
    _parse_obs_time not falling through to reportTime on a bad epoch, unlike the metar.py
    handling it claims to reuse (L-18); the cached station list handed out by reference and a
    cache key omitting coordinates (L-19); observe() mocks using `tmpf`, a Fahrenheit field
    metar.py's own live audit concluded the real API never returns -- switched to Celsius
    `temp` (I-20); the observationStations URL followed from a remote response without a host
    check (I-23); two docstring slips (I-24); no coverage of quorum failing AFTER the outlier
    gate (I-25); the state file rewritten every cycle purely to increment cycles_observed
    (I-26, accepted as-is and documented -- the write is what makes cycles_observed an honest
    denominator, and at the retained-sample cap it is far smaller than the review estimated).

Open follow-up (not blocking) -- Synoptic access, CORRECTED 2026-08-25 against live pages:
  The batch-56 spec's premise that a usable free Synoptic tier exists is WRONG, and this entry
  originally repeated it ("if a Synoptic free-tier key is ever registered"). Re-verified directly:

    - Open Access (the no-cost tier) is academic-only. Verbatim from synopticdata.com/
      open-access-program: "The Open Access Program is available to members of accredited U.S.
      educational institutions who register with a valid .edu email address", eligible uses are
      "Student research projects", "Faculty-led or on-campus research", and "Non-commercial
      educational coursework". A trading bot qualifies as none of those. It also states
      "1 simultaneous API response", a CONCURRENCY limit, not a monthly quota.
    - The spec's "free open-access tier = 5,000 API requests + 5M service units/month
      (verified 2026-08)" numbers do not appear on the open-access page, the pricing page, or
      the commercial-pricing page. Treat that line in batch-56.md as unsupported.
    - Commercial pricing is quote-only ("three standard tiers or ... a custom commercial
      pricing plan"), no figures published, no free commercial tier.
    - A 14-day free trial exists with no stated academic requirement, but the Weather API trial
      is "US Networks Only" and carries only 7 days of history.

  This trips batch-56's own written constraint ("Free tier only; flag immediately if any needed
  capability turns out paid"), so it is flagged here rather than left implied.

WHY A SYNOPTIC KEY WOULD STILL BE WORTH BUYING (re-derived, and stronger than the spec's own
argument, which was only about CWOP/mesonet station density):

  1. It is the literal settlement source, not a proxy. Re-confirmed 2026-08-25 from the live
     market rules of KXTEMPMIAH-26AUG2501-T85.99: "determined strictly by the temperature
     reported by Synoptic Data, calculated in accordance with the Kalshi Weather Index
     Methodology."
  2. TEMPORAL RESOLUTION is very likely the dominant error term today, ahead of station
     density. Measured on the live feed 2026-08-25: over 1434 status=normal points the index
     value changes on a MEDIAN of every 4 minutes (mean 4.78, max run 34). The contributors are
     therefore genuinely sub-hourly (~5 min). This module feeds it HOURLY METAR -- 33 KMIA
     observations across the same 24h window. That mismatch is structural and no amount of
     re-weighting free ASOS stations can close it.
  3. Index reconstruction becomes possible. contributors is a constant 5 across every point
     sampled. With access to the same network at the same cadence, the contributor set and
     weights are a solvable fit against the index's own retained history -- turning this
     module from an APPROXIMATION of the settlement variable into a RECONSTRUCTION of it. The
     trial's 7-day history is more than enough to attempt that, since the Kalshi feed itself
     only retains ~24h.

  Suggested sequencing: do NOT burn the 14-day trial immediately. The shadow collector shipped
  with zero samples, so let it accumulate a real multi-week baseline first, then spend the
  one-shot trial on a head-to-head against that baseline rather than against the single-day
  go/no-go. Decision rule: if reconstruction drives RMSE materially below the accumulated
  free-ASOS number, a paid plan is justified; if it plateaus near it, it is not.

  Baseline to beat, stated precisely so the comparison is honest: the SHIPPED config
  (1/(d+10km), k=8) measured blend RMSE 1.022F against the index over the go/no-go window.
  Note the best-measured config in that sweep was actually EQUAL-weight k=8 at 0.759F, which
  also cleared every pre-registered slice (+0.405/+1.609/+1.296); 1/(d+10km) was shipped because
  it is the form the batch spec pre-registered ("distance-weighted"), not because it scored
  best. Worth revisiting on the accumulated multi-week data before treating 1.022F as the
  number Synoptic has to beat.

  Also still open: KTMB is discovered by NWS but never appears in the aviationweather payload
  (confirmed live twice); it is silently skipped, which is correct, but a station that
  permanently never reports effectively reduces k from 8 to 7 for Miami.

[OPEN -- filed 2026-08-25 by batch-56's follow-up verification] The other 5 hourly cities settle on THE WEATHER COMPANY, not METAR -- same mis-reference class batch-52 found for Miami, never measured
Priority: Medium -- not a live-trading risk today (hourly live orders are gated), but it is the
  same defect batch-52 spent a whole batch fixing for ONE city, now suspected for five.
Files: kalshi_weather_index.py (docstring corrected by batch-56, no logic change),
  weather_markets.py (_analyze_hourly_trade / _get_combined_station_bias), metar.py
  (MARKET_STATION_MAP) -- no code changed by this entry, measurement/design question only.

Problem:
  batch-52 established that KXTEMPMIAH settles on the Synoptic-sourced Kalshi Weather Index
  rather than KMIA METAR, and measured 1.6-2.0F mean divergence to prove the model was
  referencing the wrong variable. Its module docstring then asserted, as the contrast case,
  that "the other 5 hourly cities (KXTEMPNYCH/AUSH/CHIH/LAXH/DCH)" settle on METAR.

  Re-read live from the Kalshi markets API on 2026-08-25, that contrast is false. All five
  settle on **The Weather Company**:

    KXTEMPNYCH-26AUG2501-T71.99 rules_primary: "If the temperature recorded at Central Park,
    New York City for Aug 25, 2026 1 AM EDT as reported by The Weather Company (for coordinates
    KNYC), is above 71.99, then the market resolves to Yes."

    rules_secondary: "the official and final value used to determine this market is the
    maximum/minimum temperature as reported by the Weather Company. ... Preliminary Weather
    Company data may be subject to rounding and conversion differences from the final reported
    value."

  Checked across all six hourly series (3 open markets each): Miami -> Synoptic, the other five
  -> The Weather Company. No production module in this repo mentions The Weather Company at all
  -- the only occurrences are in tests/test_batch51_holiday_rain.py, i.e. batch-51's
  settlement-source watcher fixtures, which is the watcher built to catch exactly this and
  which may well already be flagging it.

  So the bot models all 6 hourly cities off METAR/CLI-derived station bias while ZERO of them
  actually settle on METAR. TWC ingests ASOS as an input so the divergence is plausibly much
  smaller than Miami's multi-station-index case -- the rules text explicitly warns about
  "rounding and conversion differences", which is a small-magnitude hint, not a large one. But
  it has never been measured, and "plausibly small" is precisely the assumption batch-52
  disproved for Miami.

Why not fixed now:
  Out of batch-56's scope by the same-payload test -- batch-56 owns a Miami-only shadow
  observation collector, while this is the hourly probability path for five different cities,
  needing its own measurement pass and possibly its own data source. Fixing it blind (e.g.
  swapping in a TWC feed) without first measuring the divergence would repeat the mistake this
  project keeps re-learning.

Next step (cheap, and it is a measurement not a change):
  Run batch-52's own experiment shape against one non-Miami hourly city -- poll TWC's published
  value for the market's coordinates (weather.com/kalshi is named in Kalshi's own help centre as

  Note the asymmetry that makes this worth doing even though hourly live trading is gated:
  KXTEMPMIAH already pools into the SHARED T_hourly calibration fit and the pooled hourly
  settled-sample gate (see the batch-52 opus-review M-1 entry above). If five more cities are
  also mis-referenced, that pooled fit is not "one bad city among five good ones" -- it is six
  for six, which changes the reading of M-1 entirely.

[OPEN 2026-08-25 -- opus-review finding M4 during batch-57's own review;
  filed rather than fixed inline because the fix moves live trade
  probabilities, which is out of a condition_type-filtering batch's scope]
  TRAIN_ALL_TEMPERATURE_SCALING NEVER FITS THE 'BETWEEN' T ITS OWN DOCSTRING
  PROMISES
Priority: Medium -- affects the probability every 'between' bracket market
  is priced with, and 'between' trades with real capital today (it is NOT
  a shadow-only family). Not High only because the fallback is a real
  fitted value (the global T), not a no-op, so the effect is
  under-compression rather than an unbounded error.

Problem:
  ml_bias.train_all_temperature_scaling()'s docstring says, verbatim,
  "Condition-specific T values capture the fact that 'between' markets
  have a much larger calibration gap than 'above'/'below' markets and need
  a different compression factor," and gives the example
  {"global": {...}, "between": {"T": 6.8, ...}}.

  But its row query excludes tracker._ALWAYS_EXCLUDED_CONDITION_TYPES,
  whose 6th member IS 'between'. So the per-condition loop never sees a
  'between' bucket, existing["between"] is never written, and
  data/temperature_scale.json currently holds only above/global/sameday --
  confirmed live 2026-08-25:
      {'above': 1.2739, 'global': 4.6013, 'sameday': 3.8294}
  apply_temperature_scaling() therefore falls through
  table.get("between") -> None to table.get("global") = 4.60, versus the
  ~6.8 the design calls for. There is no _T_BETWEEN_PRIOR either (only
  _T_BELOW_PRIOR/_T_ABOVE_PRIOR), so nothing else supplies it.

  PRE-EXISTING, not a batch-57 regression: the hardcoded literal batch-57
  replaced already contained 'between', so the consolidation is
  behaviour-identical. Raised because batch-57's new comment initially
  asserted the permanent constant was the right choice here, which would
  have converted an unnoticed defect into a documented decision. That
  comment now records the defect instead of blessing it.

  The reasoning that makes 'between' permanently excluded elsewhere does
  NOT transfer to this one site: everywhere else the reason is "don't let
  a structurally different calibration gap distort a SHARED AGGREGATE."
  This loop is not a shared aggregate -- it is precisely the per-condition
  split that exists to give 'between' its own T.

Why not now: changing it re-fits a value consumed by
  weather_markets.apply_temperature_scaling() on the live pricing path, so
  it needs its own before/after measurement and its own review, not a
  drive-by edit inside a filtering batch. Suggested shape when picked up:
  pass frozenset(_ALWAYS_EXCLUDED_CONDITION_TYPES - {"between"}) for the
  multi-day `rows` query ONLY, leaving sameday_rows and hourly_rows alone,
  then verify a "between" key actually appears in temperature_scale.json
  and compare the fitted T against the ~6.8 the docstring predicts.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-26 (batch-79 item 3) -- opus-review finding M5 during
  batch-57's own review, filed 2026-08-25]
  CMD_WALKFORWARD'S PER-CONDITION BRIER SILENTLY DROPS 'BETWEEN'
Priority: Low -- display-only (`py main.py walkforward`), no gate or
  pricing consumer.

Problem:
  main.py's cmd_walkforward builds a "Per-condition Brier" breakdown from
  a query carrying its own hand-written one-element exclusion:
      AND (p.condition_type IS NULL OR p.condition_type != 'between')
  It is billed as a per-condition comparison yet unconditionally omits one
  of the three temperature conditions, so 'between' never appears in a
  breakdown whose entire purpose is comparing conditions.

  Found while consolidating batch-57 item 2's five exclusion sites: this
  is a sixth site, missed by that item's enumeration because its literal
  has a different shape (a single != rather than a NOT IN list). Batch-57
  deliberately did NOT wire it to tracker's shared registry, and that part
  is correct: the query GROUPS BY condition_type downstream, so each
  family lands in its own bucket and nothing is pooled -- the shadow-family
  exclusion the registry provides would remove rows without fixing any
  contamination. An in-code comment at that site now records both halves.

Why not now: it changes `py main.py walkforward` output, which is a
  behaviour change rather than the consolidation batch-57 was scoped to.
  Whoever picks it up should decide whether 'between' belongs in a
  per-condition breakdown (probably yes, clearly labelled) rather than
  simply deleting the predicate.

Resolution (2026-08-26, batch-79 item 3): 'between' is INCLUDED. The
  predicate is deleted and the in-code comment now records the reasoning
  rather than the doubt.

  The decision was made from the exclusion's own stated reason, not by
  default. tracker._ALWAYS_EXCLUDED_CONDITION_TYPES excludes 'between'
  because between-brackets carry a structurally larger calibration gap
  (T~=6.8 vs global/above/below's much smaller correction) that would
  distort a SHARED AGGREGATE Brier meant to stand for overall model quality.
  That reason cannot apply to this query, which GROUPs BY condition_type:
  every family lands in its own bucket and no number is shared, so there is
  nothing for between's gap to distort.

  What the drop was actually doing, measured 2026-08-26 against the live DB
  over this exact query's rows:
    above    n=131  Brier=0.2498  pred=52.4%  actual=54.2%
    between  n=114  Brier=0.2794  pred=20.4%  actual=40.4%
    below    n= 78  Brier=0.2657  pred=53.5%  actual=52.6%
  'between' is the second-largest bucket (33% of all settled rows) and the
  WORST-calibrated of the three temperature conditions. A panel named
  "Per-condition Brier" was hiding it.

  TWO CORRECTIONS from this batch's own review, both now carried in the code
  comment as well:

  (i) That 0.2794 must NOT be quoted as evidence about the CURRENT between
      implementation. 69 of the 114 rows are metar_lockout rows predicted
      before the 2026-08-09 re-enable (tracker._BETWEEN_METAR_REENABLED_AT)
      -- exactly the population batch-40's handoff said not to cite because
      it measures deleted code. The finding survives the split, which is why
      the predicate is deleted rather than merely re-scoped. Re-measured on
      the correct axis (metar_lockout AND predicted_at < 2026-08-09 is the
      dead population; the 40 ensemble/days_out=1 rows are a different code
      path, not dead code):
        dead-code rows      n=69  Brier=0.2758  pred=15.2%  actual=39.1%
        ALL OTHER between   n=45  Brier=0.2848  pred=28.4%  actual=42.2%
      So on clean rows between is still the worst of the three (0.2848 vs
      below 0.2657 vs above 0.2498) and still under-predicts, by ~14 points
      rather than 20. The panel shows the unsplit number by design -- it is
      a whole-history comparison -- and the comment now says to read it as
      "between is the weak one", never as a measurement of today's formula.

 (ii) "the only CLI display that would have surfaced that gap" was FALSE.
      tracker.check_sameday_condition_type_weakness() emits a

      duplicative: that one is the clean-rows alert, this one is the

  This is the opposite call from tracker.get_station_bias_by_lead's, which

  batch-57's other conclusion stands unchanged and is still in the comment:

[RESOLVED 2026-08-26 by batch-76 item 1 -- resolution at the end of this
  entry. Originally filed 2026-08-25 as adjacency found while tracing
  batch-59 item 1's HIGH-market
  veto; filed as its own entry per workflow step 27 rather than stretched into
  that change, because it affects the monotone-SAFE locks item 1 does not touch
  and needs its own design decision] METAR-LOCKED PATH'S RECOMMENDED SIDE CAN
  CONTRADICT THE LOCK'S OWN OUTCOME -- AND THE DIVERGENCE GATE IS SKIPPED THERE
Priority: HIGH -- live trade-entry path, unblocked by any existing gate, and
  the arithmetic below was verified rather than reasoned about. Not
  hypothetical: an opus reviewer independently reproduced the same inversion
  end-to-end through analyze_trade on the OKC/SATX incident shape.
Files: weather_markets.py (analyze_trade's `rec_side = "yes" if blended_prob >
  market_prob else "no"`, and the `if not metar_locked:` guard that skips the
  market-divergence gate a few lines above it), weather_markets.py
  (_price_and_size's entry_side_edge), metar.py (_dynamic_lock_in_confidence,
  the 0.72 floor)

Problem:
  A METAR lock produces BOTH a categorical verdict (outcome "yes"/"no") and a
  probability, and nothing enforces agreement between them. The probability is
  _dynamic_lock_in_confidence's output, floored at 0.72 and capped at 0.97,
  which for a monotone-safe lock badly understates the truth (~99.9%). Because
  side selection is a bare `blended_prob > market_prob`, that understatement
  does not merely under-bet -- it flips the side.

  Worked example, monotone-SAFE YES lock (running max already past
  threshold+margin, so the outcome is structurally settled): blended_prob =
  0.72 against a market at 0.90 -> rec_side = "no". _price_and_size then
  computes entry_side_edge = (1 - 0.72) - (1 - 0.90) = +0.18. A positive 18%
  edge, so nothing downstream blocks it: the bot buys NO at 10c on a market
  that is essentially certain YES.

  Mirror case, NO lock: blended_prob = 1 - confidence = 0.28 against a market
  at 0.10 -> rec_side = "yes", entry_side_edge = 0.28 - 0.10 = +0.18 -> buys
  YES on the outcome the lock just ruled out. batch-59 item 1's veto removes
  the specific unsafe-direction locks that produced this shape, but the safe
  direction still produces it.

  Two aggravating factors, both verified:
  - The market-divergence gate ("if the market is >70% confident and we are
    <25%, skip rather than bet against a well-informed crowd") is explicitly
    disabled on this path by `if not metar_locked:` -- so the one guard that
    would have caught a confident-market disagreement does not run precisely
    where the disagreement is manufactured.
  - apply_metar_calibration makes it worse, not better: an opus reviewer
    measured a NO-lock's raw P(yes)=0.221 being calibrated UP to ~0.536,
    which sits above a 0.275 market price and inverts the side on its own.

Recommendation: a design decision, not a mechanical fix -- take it to
  AskUserQuestion. Options: (a) refuse any recommended side that contradicts
  metar_lockout["outcome"] (cheap, direct, but silently drops trades where the
  market is genuinely mispriced against a correct lock); (b) recalibrate the
  confidence floor so a monotone-safe lock reports something near its true
  ~99% -- batch 37 owns that calibration loop, and note the existing fit was
  measured on a lock population batch-59's veto partly eliminates, so it needs
  a refit either way; (c) re-enable the divergence gate on the metar_locked
  path. (a) and (b) are not mutually exclusive. Whichever is chosen, pair it
  with a test asserting recommended_side agrees with the lock outcome.
  Full record: none -- surfaced by batch-59, not by the original audit.

Resolution 2026-08-26 (batch-76 item 1, verified against master 6b116698):
  analyze_trade now has a "10b. METAR lock side-agreement override" section,
  placed immediately after `rec_side` is chosen and -- deliberately -- AFTER
  the METAR beta-calibration block, so it sees the probability the side was
  actually chosen from. When the lock is monotone-safe and its categorical
  outcome disagrees with `rec_side`, `rec_side` is set to the lock's outcome
  and the new write-only field `metar_side_override` records which side was
  enforced. Chosen over the three alternatives via AskUserQuestion; see below
  for why each was rejected, since two of them were this entry's own
  recommendation.

  THE ENTRY UNDERSTATED THE PROBLEM AND MISATTRIBUTED ITS CAUSE.
  - The 0.72 floor alone CANNOT reach a live order, contrary to "unblocked by
    any existing gate". trade_cycle requires mkt_dir >= MIN_MARKET_PROB_TO_BET
    _WITH (0.25) and prob_edge >= max(CITY_MIN_PROB_EDGE[city],
    min_prob_edge_for_days_out(0) = 0.12). An inverted YES lock needs market
    <= 0.75 to clear the first and blended <= 0.63 to clear the second, while
    the raw lock probability is >= 0.72 by construction; the NO mirror needs
    blended >= 0.37 against a raw <= 0.28. Both jointly unsatisfiable. What
    the floor mechanism did reach is the analysis DICT, rendered verbatim as
    "BUY NO" by cmd_market and the market table an operator reads before
    typing a manual cmd_order.
  - What IS unblocked is the beta-calibration path, which this entry credited
    to apply_metar_calibration in settlement_monitor. It is in analyze_trade
    too, via a local import, and it rewrites blended_prob in place by up to
    _METAR_CORRECTION_LIMIT (0.60) BEFORE the side is chosen. Under the fit
    live at the time of writing (data/metar_lockout_calibration.json,
    a=b=0.2262 c=0.4001 n=33, fitted 2026-08-24, no env gate) every YES lock
    arrives at rec_side at 0.649-0.766 and every NO lock at 0.405-0.547. The
    entry's own cited example -- raw P(yes) 0.221 calibrated to ~0.536
    against a 0.275 market -- clears mkt_dir 0.275, prob_edge 0.261 and
    divergence ratio 1.949, i.e. every downstream gate, and WOULD place a
    real order on the ruled-out side. So the entry's HIGH rating is right,
    for a reason it attributed elsewhere.
  - And it is not a corner case, which a parallel session's independent
    re-derivation sharpened. The calibration floors every NO lock near 0.40
    however certain the lock was, and the most marginal one (conf 0.72)
    lands at 0.5465 -- above even money -- so a NO lock recommends YES
    against any market priced below it. Solving all three downstream gates
    (mkt_dir >= 0.25, prob_edge >= 0.12, divergence ratio <= 2.0) for the
    market range that would actually trade the wrong side:
        lock conf 0.72  blended 0.5465  ->  market [0.273, 0.427]
        lock conf 0.90  blended 0.4758  ->  market [0.250, 0.356]
        lock conf 0.97  blended 0.4046  ->  market [0.250, 0.285]
    Open at every confidence level, widening as the lock gets LESS certain.
    The ~0.40 floor under those blended values is NOT a property of the
    calibration -- unclamped the beta map runs to 0.062 -- it is
    _dynamic_lock_in_confidence's 0.97 cap seen through a strictly
    increasing map (a = b > 0). The two live in different files with
    nothing connecting them, so raising the cap silently drops the floor
    (0.99 -> 0.345, 0.999 -> 0.238) and widens every range above. Named in
    BOTH places this session: metar.py's docstring now carries the table
    and points at analyze_trade's section 10b, and 10b points back.
    The raw floor's window is empty at every level by contrast: prob_edge
    >= 0.12 forces market >= raw + 0.12 >= 0.84, so mkt_dir = 1 - market
    <= 0.16 < 0.25, and it only gets more impossible as raw rises.
  - Note the floor half's impossibility survives by only ~1.9pp under that
    same fit (calibrated YES minimum 0.6488 vs the 0.63 bar), and the fit is
    a JSON file a weekly cron retrains. It is not a permanent protection.
  - The entry's `entry_side_edge = (1-0.72)-(1-0.90) = +0.18` is really
    `edge`; `_esmp` on the NO side is `1 - yes_bid` and only falls back to
    `1 - market_prob` on an empty bid book, and the whole thing is scaled by
    time_decay. At the regression test's own prices (bid 0.88 / ask 0.92) the
    real figures are entry_side_edge +0.16 and net_edge +1.33 -- net_edge
    being the number that drives tier classification and
    paper.check_model_exits, and the more alarming of the two. batch-76.md
    was corrected in place.

  SCOPE: monotone-safe locks ONLY, which is narrower than this entry asked
  for. _metar_lock_in now tags each locked dict with `monotone_safe`. Every
  lock surviving the above/below branch is safe by construction of batch-59's
  two vetoes (all four market-side x direction combinations checked), as are
  both between-NO branches. The between-YES branch is tagged False: its
  extreme is INSIDE the band and can still drift to the edge the monotonic
  direction has not foreclosed -- its own comment and analyze_trade's
  between_edge gate both say so. There the probability, not the verdict, is
  the honest signal, and overriding would permanently forfeit the contrarian
  side of a genuinely mispriced in-band lock (opus review, MEDIUM). Note
  "monotone-safe" means only that further intraday drift AT OUR STATION
  cannot reverse the verdict; it is not a confidence claim, and this module's
  own measured lock accuracy (70.4% actual vs 89.6% predicted for YES locks,
  n=27) is why the beta-calibration exists at all.

  WHY OVERRIDE RATHER THAN SKIP. Returning None was implemented first and
  rejected on review. It takes forecast_prob with it, and cmd_order records
  `entry_prob=_analysis.get("forecast_prob") if _analysis else None` --
  so a manual order on a dropped market logs entry_prob=None, which
  order_executor._check_live_model_exits skips on, leaving that live position
  invisible to the model-exit checker. cmd_market would also have printed
  "no forecast or unrecognised ticker format", false on both counts, on
  exactly the markets whose display this change exists to fix. Overriding
  keeps the market visible and honest; placement is still refused, by two
  independent pre-existing checks in _validate_trade_opportunity (net_edge
  <= 0, and raw edge's sign must agree with the recommended side), both of
  which a forced side fails by construction -- asserted directly in the
  tests. Because nothing is rejected, this is NOT a scan-funnel gate and has
  no ScanGate entry; an interim implementation that added one was removed.

  WHY NOT (c), THIS ENTRY'S THIRD OPTION. Re-enabling the skipped
  model-vs-market gates fixes nothing. The divergence gate fires only on
  market>0.70 & ours<0.25 or market<0.30 & ours>0.75; on the raw lock
  probability an inverted YES lock has ours >= 0.72 and an inverted NO lock
  has ours <= 0.28, so no inversion satisfies either clause, and both gates
  would instead suppress locked trades that AGREE with the lock. (A parallel
  session correctly pointed out that model_mkt_gap is a SECOND gate skipped
  the same way, in a different `if not metar_locked:` block -- so (c) was
  really two changes. Same conclusion applies to both.) Left untouched.

  WHY NOT (a)/(b), RAISING THE FLOOR. It fixes the magnitude but leaves side
  selection a bare magnitude comparison, so any future under-confident lock
  re-opens the identical inversion; and it would raise Kelly sizing and newly
  qualify trades that today fail the 12pp same-day prob-edge gate, on a
  calibration nobody has refit. batch-37 still owns that refit.

  OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, stated deliberately rather than discovered later:
  under the current calibration this override fires on essentially every
  above/below NO lock (calibrated 0.405-0.547 against a market of 0.05-0.20)
  and on every YES lock the market has repriced past ~0.77. Those were all
  inverted recommendations, so correcting them is right -- but the practical
  effect is that the METAR-locked book goes largely quiet until the
  calibration is refit. Logged at INFO, not WARNING, for that reason.

  Tests: 10 new in tests/test_weather_markets.py covering both inversion
  polarities, both agreeing controls, the between-YES exemption, the
  between-NO inclusion, the non-"yes"/"no" outcome guard, the unlocked path,
  and the calibration-driven case; 3 more pinning the monotone_safe tags at
  their source in _metar_lock_in. Every causal claim mutation-tested
  individually via Edit-revert: disabling the override reproduces
  recommended_side="no" at adjusted_edge +0.33 on a YES lock; removing the
  `metar_locked` guard, the `monotone_safe` scope, or the `in ("yes","no")`
  membership test each fails exactly one dedicated test (the last also fails
  8 pre-existing ones). Full record: none -- surfaced by batch-59.

UPDATE 2026-08-25 -- batch-68 found a THIRD downstream consumer, and closed the
  one path that would have made it destructive:
  The mislabel does not stop at analysis. condition["var"] is threaded onto the
  paper trade and paper._score_ensemble_members() logs an
  ensemble_member_scores row under var="max" whose actual_temp is the day's

  cell, so once this family trades, a ~20-30F sign-flipped sample lands in the

  batch-68's new backfill_member_actual_temp() would have amplified it: its

  so ONE mislabelled trade would have rewritten every daily-max row for that
  city/date, including rows a normal KXHIGH* ladder created. That specific
  amplification is closed -- the backfill now derives var from the ticker alone
  via _var_from_ticker_prefix and SKIPS a ticker whose prefix cannot resolve
  one, rather than defaulting to "max" (opus review, HIGH). The upstream

  Worth noting for whoever fixes it: batch-68's fail-closed treatment is the
  shape to copy. Widening the HIGH/LOW substring test alone is not obviously
  right -- TMAX/TMIN is a different naming convention, and widening it risks

  Verified via an exhaustive sweep of the 120 registered series that
  KXHOLIDAYTMAX/TMIN are the only two None-yielding families that reach the
  above/below branch at all; every other None family (rain, snow, hourly,

  Note batch-59 item 1's HIGH veto now also applies to these tickers (None ->
  not "min" -> treated as HIGH). That is strictly MORE conservative than

  (e.g. check for "TMIN"/"TMAX" alongside "LOW"/"HIGH" in

  Full record: none -- surfaced by batch-59.

Resolution 2026-08-26 (batch-76 item 2, verified against master 6b116698):
  _var_from_ticker_prefix now resolves the family from a new
  _KXHOLIDAY_TEMP_SERIES_VAR map ({"KXHOLIDAYTMAX": "max", "KXHOLIDAYTMIN":
  "min"}), keyed on the ticker's first hyphen-delimited segment -- the same
  shape is_holiday_temp_ticker() uses, whose membership frozenset is now
  DERIVED from that map so the two cannot disagree at import about which
  series belong to the family. Every other neither-match family (hourly,
  monthly rain/snow, hurricane, tornado) still returns None, so each caller's
  own distinct fallback tail is unchanged for them.

  NOT the substring test this entry recommended. KXHIGHTMIN and KXLOWTMIN --
  the two Minneapolis daily ladders, both live and traded -- each CONTAIN the
  substring "TMIN". A `if "TMIN" in ticker` rule is correct for them only
  because "HIGH"/"LOW" happen to be checked first, so it is one reordering

[RESOLVED 2026-08-25 -- batch-80 item 1. Originally filed 2026-08-24 by
  batch-61's opus review (F1), out of scope for that batch's display fix]
  useData.js's apiFetch has no request timeout, so
  a HUNG backend freezes the whole dashboard silently instead of degrading
Priority: Medium -- not a crash and not a data-integrity issue, but it
  defeats every "is this data still live?" signal the UI has, including the
  anomaly-monitor staleness banner batch-61 item 3 just added.
Files: frontend/src/useData.js (apiFetch, safe, fetchAllSafe, fetchAll),
  frontend/src/tabs/OverviewTab.jsx and RiskTab.jsx (consumers of the
  resulting frozen state)

Problem:
  `apiFetch` does a bare `await fetch(path, ...)` with no AbortController
  and no timeout. A backend that ACCEPTS the connection but never answers
  -- Flask handler threads blocked on a tracker.db sqlite lock, a wedged
  gunicorn worker, a proxy holding the socket open -- produces a promise
  that never settles. Consequences, all silent:
    - fetchAllSafe's Promise.allSettled never resolves, so fetchAll's
      setData is never called and NOTHING in the app re-renders from a poll.
    - /api/stream's generator blocks inside _build_stream_data() the same
      way, so the SSE connection emits neither a `message` nor an `error`
      event -- the socket just stays open. `connected` therefore stays
      green.
    - App's RefreshCountdown keeps cycling 60 -> 1 -> 60 because it runs on
      its own local interval, not on data arrival, so the UI actively looks
      alive.
  Every fail-FAST variant (connection refused, 4xx/5xx, JSON parse error,
  auth cancel) is handled correctly today -- those all reach setData. It is
  specifically the hang that is invisible.

  Batch-61 item 3's staleness banner is partially protected from this
  already: shared.jsx's useFeedClock ticks on its own interval, so RiskTab's
  anomaly card DOES go STATUS UNAVAILABLE after FEED_STALE_MS even when no
  fetch ever resolves. That was a deliberate design response to this
  finding. But every OTHER consumer of poll-derived state (balance,
  positions, open count, the cron-staleness banner, `connected`) still
  freezes at its last value with no indication.

Why it was scoped out of batch-61:
  Adding a timeout changes the fetch path for all 23 endpoints plus the
  weather-alerts poll, and needs its own decisions -- what timeout value
  (the NWS alerts endpoint is documented as slow, and /api/opportunities
  does live Kalshi calls, so one global number may not fit), whether a
  timeout should count as a failure for keep-last-known-good purposes, and
  whether an aborted request should be retried. That is a fetch-layer
  change with its own failure modes, not the display fix batch-61 item 3
  was scoped to.

Recommendation:
  Give apiFetch an AbortController with a per-endpoint-overridable timeout
  (a global default in the 15-30s range, longer for /api/weather-alerts and
  /api/opportunities), so a hung request rejects, `safe()` maps it to null,
  and the existing keep-last-known-good + fetchedAt machinery reports it as
  a failed feed exactly like a 500 already does. Pair it with a test that a
  never-resolving fetch mock still lets fetchAllSafe settle. Consider also
  surfacing "no successful poll in N minutes" globally (the `connected`
  indicator is SSE-only today and cannot see this).

Resolution (batch-80 item 1):
  Two halves: make a hang degrade like an error, and make the degraded state
  visible.

  TIMEOUT. apiFetch takes a timeoutMs and passes AbortSignal.timeout(). Two
  budgets rather than the entry's per-endpoint-overridable scheme:
  API_TIMEOUT_MS = 30s for the 23 polled endpoints, SCAN_VERSION_TIMEOUT_MS
  = 4s for the raw /api/scan-version fetch. The scan-version poll had the
  same missing-timeout defect and needs it MORE, not less: it runs every 5s,
  the tightest loop in the file, so a hung backend accumulates a pending
  request twelve times faster there than on the main poll.

  The entry worried one global number might not fit because "/api/weather-
  alerts is documented as slow". Checked rather than assumed: that handler
  fans out to NWS through a ThreadPoolExecutor with a per-city timeout=5
  (web_app.py:2987), so its realistic worst case is ~5-6s and 15s covers it
  with ~2.5x headroom. The binding constraint is the other end anyway -- a
  timeout at or above its own poll interval lets requests stack, which is
  the unbounded accumulation the item is about. Both constants are asserted
  against their intervals in useData.test.js so a later edit past them fails
  a test rather than reaching production.

  "Whether a timeout should count as a failure for keep-last-known-good
  purposes" -- yes, and it already does, by construction. A TimeoutError
  carries no `isAuth`, so safe() maps it to null exactly like a 500, and
  every branch of fetchAll's merge is already null-tolerant. That is what
  stops a timeout putting `undefined` where OverviewTab/RiskTab expect data,
  i.e. trading a frozen dashboard for a crashing one. No retry was added:
  the next scheduled poll is the retry.

  VISIBILITY, which is the larger half. With keep-last-known-good, a dead
  backend renders identically to a healthy one whose numbers have not moved
  -- confirmed by running the dev server with no Flask behind it, where the
  dashboard cheerfully displayed "$1247.83 / +24.8% / graduation gate
  cleared" from MOCK with nothing to say none of it was real.
    - orderFeedSuccess gained a `stats` key, in the SAME map batch-63 built
      rather than a second freshness path. Its predicate is
      `status && !status.error`, byte-for-byte mapStats' own gate, so the
      timestamp cannot vouch for a merge that did not happen.
    - shared.jsx gained staleFeedState() (pure, tested) + StaleFeedBanner,
      rendered by OverviewTab and RiskTab from OVERVIEW_FEED_KEYS /
      RISK_FEED_KEYS in useData.js. STALE-WITH-A-MARKER, not an error state
      that blanks values -- following batch-61 F2's precedent that a safety
      surface must not get LESS informative because its feed died.
      anomalyStatus is deliberately excluded from RISK_FEED_KEYS: its own
      card already reports it.
    - stats.timestamp (which resets App's refresh countdown) now stamps only
      via nextStatsTimestamp(), i.e. only when at least one endpoint
      actually returned. It used to stamp unconditionally, so a poll in
      which all 23 endpoints timed out reset the header to "60s" as if data
      had just landed. Decided with the user rather than assumed.

  A per-tab banner is a POOLED gate, so a key that is misspelled, renamed or
  newly added and never listed goes unwatched with no visible symptom.
  useData.test.js asserts the key lists mechanically against the names
  orderFeedSuccess actually emits.

  KNOWN GAP, stated rather than implied: the one line assigning
  nextStatsTimestamp's result inside fetchAll's setData updater is not test-
  covered, and mutating it back to a bare Date.now() leaves the suite green.
  frontend/ has no jsdom or RTL, so the updater body cannot be exercised at
  all; the decision was extracted into nextStatsTimestamp precisely to
  shrink the untested surface to that single assignment. Same shape of gap
  batch-63's opus review (F5) found here before. Adding RTL was out of scope.
  Likewise the banner's amber branch was verified by unit tests but not
  visually -- staging a real stamp and then stopping it needs a live
  backend; the pending branch was confirmed in a browser on both tabs.

  Mutation-verified: removing the AbortSignal fails 2 tests; `stats:
  Boolean(status)` (dropping the error-body check) fails 2; staleFeedState
  reporting only the first key instead of the worst fails 4;
  nextStatsTimestamp returning `now` unconditionally fails 2. The first
  round of the timeout test passed under the signal-removal mutation for the
  wrong reason and was strengthened with an explicit `aborted` assertion
  until it failed.

  frontend: 303 passed (was 259). static/dist rebuilt, per this repo's
  convention that every frontend/src commit ships its build artifacts.

REVIEW FINDINGS ADDRESSED (independent opus review of this diff, effort:high).
All 15 were fixed; none was dismissed.
  - H1 (the real one): StaleFeedBanner used `formatFeedAge(feed.ageMs) == null`
    as its test for "pending", and feedFreshness returns a null ageMs for TWO
    states -- 'pending' AND an escalated 'stale' (never answered, now past
    maxAgeMs from `since`). Since worstStaleness ranks a null age as Infinity,
    a never-answered feed also always WINS the pool. So a backend that hung at
    page load sat on a calm grey "waiting…" forever over MOCK's fabricated
    balance, and two feeds two hours dead were masked behind the same wording.
    That is verbatim the trap batch-61's F4 closed one layer down,
    re-introduced one layer up by the banner meant to surface it. Now keyed on
    `feed.state === 'pending'`.
    The fix needed a second step: reintroducing the bug left all 293 tests
    green, because the decision lived in a component and frontend/ has no
    jsdom/RTL. So the decision was extracted to a pure `staleBannerCopy(feed)`
    in shared.jsx, with the component keeping only style application. The same
    mutation now fails 2 tests. A wrong decision no test can reach is the same
    failure mode this whole item exists to remove.
  - M1/M6: the 15s budget was sized against server time alone. Corrected to
    30s. AbortSignal.timeout starts at signal CREATION and fetchAllSafe creates
    all 23 at once, while the backend is plain HTTP/1.1 (~6 connections/origin,
    one held by the EventSource) -- so requests 6-23 burn budget queued in the
    browser, and a server-time-sized budget truncates the TAIL of the array
    deterministically, the same endpoints every poll. M6 separately: the
    /api/weather-alerts worst case is ceil(N/8) x 5s, not 5s -- ThreadPoolExecutor
    (max_workers=8) over every open-position city, up to ~15s at CITY_COORDS'
    21-city fallback. The old comment's "~2.5x headroom" was wrong.
  - M2: SCAN_VERSION_TIMEOUT_MS stays 4s, now documented honestly -- bounded
    above by its own 5s interval, so it will abort roughly once a minute when
    it lands inside the main poll's burst. Accepted: the cost is one missed
    cron-completion detection, retried 5s later.
  - M3: the scan-version `signal:` had ZERO coverage -- deleting it left the
    suite green, so half the TIMEOUT deliverable was unproven. pollScanVersion
    was lifted out of the mount useEffect to an exported
    makeScanVersionPoller(onNewVersion, fetchImpl), same injection pattern as
    fetchAllSafe's promptFn. 4 new tests.
  - M4: the pooled-key test only asserted `listed subset of produced`, which is
    satisfied by an EMPTY list -- deleting 'positions' from OVERVIEW_FEED_KEYS
    passed, as did adding a key to orderFeedSuccess and never listing it, the
    exact case the comment claimed to cover. Now asserts exact contents AND the
    reverse direction against an explicit exclusion list.
  - M5: the "never settles" test really waited 15 real seconds while its own
    comment claimed a "tiny budget", and apiFetch's timeoutMs parameter had no
    caller at all. timeoutMs is now threaded through safe/fetchAllSafe and the
    test passes 50ms. Suite went from 15.4s to 0.4s.
  - L1: nextStatsTimestamp coerced a missing prior stamp with `?? null`.
    MOCK.stats deliberately carries no timestamp and App.jsx keys
    RefreshCountdown's effect on [M.stats?.timestamp], so undefined -> null IS
    a dependency change -- one spurious "60s" reset on a cold load against a
    hung backend, i.e. the exact false reassurance this function removes. Now
    returns the previous value untouched.
  - L2: AbortSignal.timeout is Chrome 103+, Vite 5 targets ~Chrome 87 and
    polyfills no runtime APIs. In makeScanVersionPoller the bare call would
    throw during ARGUMENT evaluation, before fetch() returns a promise, so the
    trailing .catch() could not attach -- uncaught, every 5s. Added
    timeoutSignal() with an AbortController fallback.
  - L3: an abort now pre-empts a 401 that would have arrived later, so no
    password prompt. Documented as an accepted cost at the call site.
  - L4/I9: "no response from the backend" was the wrong diagnosis -- one
    endpoint at 500 stops only its own feed stamping. Reworded to "Some data
    has stopped updating", and "since 5 min ago" de-duplicated.
  - L5: RiskTab duplicated the `feedState.stale` predicate around a banner that
    already returns null when fresh. Dropped; the margin rides on the banner.
  - I1: "22 endpoints" was wrong in three comments -- ENDPOINTS has 23.
  - I2: stray double blank line. I4: the constants had only range assertions,
    now pinned to their exact values as well.
  - I3: every staleFeedState test passed `visibleSince: null`, the one value
    for which the escalated branch is unreachable -- so the exact input that
    broke H1 was structurally excluded from the suite that covered it. Added.
  - I5/I7/I8 acknowledged as benign: OverviewTab now re-renders once per 60s
    via useFeedClock (required -- staleness must become visible with no fetch
    completing), RiskTab shows two amber messages on a total outage, and the
    pooled banner reports "since this page loaded" rather than the age it does
    know for a sibling feed.
  - I6 partially actioned -- see round 2 below, which found the same gap was
    larger than I6 described and fixed the two worst members inline.

ROUND-2 REVIEW (independent opus review OF THE ROUND-1 FIXES, effort:high).
The workflow requires this because a fix can introduce new bugs distinct from
what it fixed. It did, and the round-1 H1 fix turned out to be incomplete:

  - H1 (round 2): THE ROUND-1 FIX WAS HALF A FIX. Keying tone on
    `feed.state === 'pending'` removed the ageMs confusion but not the
    underlying problem, because the tone was still read off the POOL WINNER
    and worstStaleness ranks an unknown age as Infinity -- so a member that
    has never answered always wins. Measured: two feeds 13 minutes dead
    alongside one that never answered still reported {state:'pending'}, i.e.
    a calm grey "waiting" over two dead safety feeds.
    Second, independent half: with no stamp, feedFreshness measures from
    `since`, and FEED_HARD_STALE_MS is gated behind `hasStamp` -- so nothing
    caps that credit. _onFeedClockVisible resets visibleSince on EVERY
    hidden->visible transition, so a total hang from page load showed amber
    at 180s and then reverted to grey on every alt-tab, forever. An operator
    switching away more often than every three minutes would never have seen
    it. That is precisely the "repeated alt-tabbing must not defer an alarm

[OPEN -- filed 2026-08-25 during batch-61] the `graphify update` CLI path still
  rebuilds the WHOLE repo even though manifest.json is now portable, because
  the AST cache is keyed by content hash rather than by path -- so a scoped
  step-29 refresh is only reachable via the manual extract workaround, never
  the documented command
Priority: Low -- zero runtime or trading impact (graphify-out/ is a developer
  knowledge-graph artifact the bot never reads). It costs every session that
  reaches workflow step 29 a decision, and makes that step dead weight.
Files: graphify-out/cache/ast/v0.9.48-s2/**, graphify-out/manifest.json,
  graphify-out/graph.json

Context -- what is ALREADY fixed, do not redo:
  The absolute-path manifest keying is RESOLVED by commit 599a0225
  ("chore(graphify): un-key manifest.json so the cache is portable across
  worktrees"). Verified on origin/master 2026-08-25: manifest.json holds 544
  keys, zero absolute. Before that migration it held 1,697 keys for 544 real
  files -- four generations layered together, three of them absolutely
  anchored to worktrees that no longer exist. A worktree branched from before
  599a0225 still carries the old 1,697-key copy, which is what prompted this
  entry; that is a stale checkout, not a live bug.

Problem (the part that is NOT fixed):
  There are TWO caches and the migration only fixed one.
    - manifest.json is keyed by file PATH -- now relative and portable.
    - graphify-out/cache/ast/<version>/ is keyed by CONTENT HASH, and its
      entries correspond to older file content.
  So `graphify update` re-extracts every file regardless of how the manifest
  is keyed. Measured immediately after the manifest migration, same session:
  227/227 files reported uncached (100%), producing a 1,007,745-line graph.json
  diff (+548,673 / -468,496), 526 communities renamed by hub, 183 paths
  touched, and 64 extraction warnings (32x nodes missing `label`, 32x missing
  `source_file`). The 415/544 "cache hit" figure measurable from the
  manifest's own ast_hash is NOT what `graphify update` consults.

  Net effect: a change touching 3 files still produces a near-whole-file diff
  across a 13,671-file tracked directory, so the honest move is to skip the
  refresh -- which is what recent batches have done, batch-61 included.

Update 2026-08-25 (commit 14162c46, batch-59's refresh): a scoped refresh IS
  achievable and was done -- five changed files re-extracted, 883 nodes
  substituted positionally, clustering metadata preserved per node id so no
  repo-wide re-cluster fired, 245k-line diff instead of 475k. That was the
  MANUAL workaround, not `graphify update`. So the accurate statement is that
  the CLI path is unusable, not that scoped refreshes are impossible; the same
  commit also repaired 12,994 backwards edges the corruption had left behind.

Recommendation:
  Until the CLI path is fixed, either use the manual extract workaround (as
  14162c46 did) or state plainly that step 29 is being skipped -- do not run
  `graphify update` expecting it to be scoped. If it is picked up:
  work out whether the AST cache can be re-anchored or rebuilt once so that
  subsequent runs hit (a one-time full rebuild is acceptable; a full rebuild
  EVERY run is not), and confirm the property that is broken today -- two
  consecutive `graphify update` runs from different worktrees should produce
  no diff on the second. Note the separate, still-live failure modes before
  touching this: graph.json edge-direction corruption on reload+resave, and
  the Obsidian regen pruning unrelated notes. The manual scoped-extract
  workaround (call graphify.extract.extract() on an explicit file list, merge
  into graph.json by hand, skip Obsidian/HTML regen) is the only path that has
  actually worked here.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-25 -- batch-80 item 3. Originally found by opus review during batch-62 item 1, while tightening an assertion that had been hiding it] tests/test_trade_improvements.py::test_trades_placed_below_cap has never exercised the 20-position cap it is named for
Priority: LOW -- a permanently-vacuous test, not a production bug. No live path is affected.
Files: tests/test_trade_improvements.py (TestMaxConcurrentPositions), order_executor.py (_auto_place_trades sizing gates)

  The bound was therefore left at `<= 2`, with a KNOWN-VACUOUS comment in the
  test naming this entry, rather than left as a silent green tick.
Recommendation:

  sizing gate -- realistic tickers that parse to a city/date, plus whatever

Resolution (batch-80 item 3):
  Both tests in TestMaxConcurrentPositions are now non-vacuous. The sibling
  warning in the paragraph above was right: test_no_trades_placed_when_at_cap
  was equally vacuous, and is fixed in the same pass.

  ROOT CAUSE, which is NOT the one recorded above. This entry and the
  in-test comment both blamed the synthetic ticker "KXHIGH-CHI-0" not
  parsing to a real city/target-date, so that one of
  portfolio_kelly_fraction / corr_kelly_scale / liquidity_kelly_scale
  zeroed adj_kelly. Traced against the live code, that is not what happens:
  with city and target_date both absent, portfolio_kelly_fraction takes its
  `if not city or not target_date_str` branch and PASSES the value through
  as min(base_fraction, remaining), and liquidity_kelly_scale returns 1.00
  for the fixture's volume 500 + open_interest 1000. The real cause was a
  missing dict key: _auto_place_trades sizes from `ci_adjusted_kelly` or
  `fee_adjusted_kelly` (order_executor.py:4761-4765) and never reads
  `kelly_fraction`, which is the only Kelly field the fixture set. ci_kelly
  therefore fell back to 0.0 and every opportunity died at
  kelly_too_small(0.0000) before reaching any cap.

  A SECOND fixture defect surfaced once sizing worked: the open positions
  were {"cost": 10.0, "qty": 1}, which is not a position that can exist (a
  Kalshi contract settles at $0 or $1, so one contract cannot cost $10), and
  it spelled the size `qty` while monte_carlo.simulate_portfolio reads
  `quantity` (defaulting to 1) and `entry_price` (defaulting to 0.50).
  Measured via portfolio_var(): 18 rows in that shape project $174 of VaR
  against the $200 MAX_VAR_DOLLARS limit, and the candidate pushes it to
  $217, so every opportunity was skipped as var_limit($217>$200). The 18-open
  case is the operative one -- at 20 open the concurrent-position gate
  returns before VaR is reached. (An earlier draft paired the 20-row figure,
  $194, with the 18-row $217; both are real but belong to different
  portfolios -- opus review M-5.) The same 18 positions in a consistent
  shape (0.40 x 25 == $10.00) project $30, and $24 with the candidate.
  The fixture was manufacturing a near-limit portfolio out of an impossible
  position rather than exercising a real risk gate.

  THE CAP IS AN ENTRY GATE, NOT A PER-PLACEMENT COUNTER. This entry's
  "restore the `== 2` assertion" is based on a misreading that the fix had
  to correct. MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS is checked exactly once, before the
  opportunity loop (order_executor.py:4368): at or above the cap it returns
  0 for the whole cycle, and below it imposes no limit at all. Nothing
  decrements toward it inside the loop. So with 18 open and 5 placeable
  opportunities the correct expectation is 5, not 2, and the assertion is
  now `== 5`. Equality, not a bound -- `<= 5` would pass at 0 all over
  again, which is exactly how this test spent months green.

  The two tests now share a _run_with_open(monkeypatch, repatch, n_open)
  helper so the open-position count is the ONLY difference between them,
  which is what makes them a matched pair rather than two assertions that
  happen to sit together. They had already drifted as separate setup blocks:
  the at-cap one stubbed place_paper_order with a bare MagicMock() and
  omitted the execution_log stub, invisible while it returned at the gate,
  but capping the observable count at 1 instead of 5 the moment the gate was
  mutated away -- i.e. exactly when the test had to do its job.

  MUTATION EVIDENCE (order_executor.py:4367's `int(os.getenv(
  "MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS", "20"))` default, edited and reverted; the file
  is otherwise unchanged by this batch and was restored byte-identical):
    "99" -> test_no_trades_placed_when_at_cap fails, "got 5"
    "21" -> test_no_trades_placed_when_at_cap fails, "got 5"  (one above 20,
            so the gate stops firing at exactly one past the real value)
    "18" -> test_trades_placed_below_cap fails, "got 0"  (18 >= 18 fires the
            gate a rung early), while the at-cap test still passes
  21 breaks one half and 18 breaks the other, so the pair brackets the cap
  at 20 from both sides rather than merely proving "a cap exists".

  And the vacuity was MEASURED rather than asserted: the ORIGINAL tests were
  run against all three of those mutations in a throwaway worktree at
  6b116698, and passed under every one -- including "99", which removes the
  cap's effect entirely.

  - H-1: THE EXPECTED COUNT WAS A PROPERTY OF ONE MACHINE'S .env, NOT OF THE
    CODE. `import main` inside the helper runs main.py's load_dotenv(), and
    find_dotenv() walks UP OUT OF THE WORKTREE to the main clone's .env,

  - M-4: "the pair brackets the cap at 20 from both sides" WAS NOT TRUE. The
