[RESOLVED 2026-08-25 -- DESIGN BATCH, user go/no-go answered NO. KXAVGT NOT
  onboarded, zero production code changed.] BATCH-55: KXAVGT WEEKLY
  AVERAGE-TEMPERATURE CONSECUTIVE-DAY STREAK MARKETS -- DECLINED
Priority: Closed -- batch-55 (Expansion Dossier B8, score 6.1, rank 10 of 11,
  the worst effort-to-capacity ratio on the roadmap). Shaped like batch 40:
  an AskUserQuestion go/no-go before any code, not a build order. The user
  was given four options (document the no / no + drift watcher / run the
  <1-day validation first / build it) and chose to document the no. The
  reasoning below IS the deliverable.

What the family is:
  11 weekly per-city series (KXAVGTK{AUS,IAH,SAT,LAS,SAN,MSY,DEN,DFW,PHX,OKC}
  plus KXAVGTATL), each event a 5-rung ladder of "N+ consecutive days within
  the week whose daily AVERAGE temperature is strictly greater than 90F",
  N = 2..6 (the batch file said 3..6+; live it is 2..6+). Settlement is the
  arithmetic mean of The Weather Company's hourly values for the station,
  00:00-23:59 local, rounded to the nearest whole degree, published at
  weather.com/kalshi; exactly 90 does not satisfy; a day with fewer than 18
  reported hourly values does not satisfy AND breaks the streak.

What re-verification confirmed (live Kalshi API, 2026-08-25):
  All 11 series exist with the tickers the batch file listed. Prior-week
  contract volume matches its figures closely: AUS 131,820 (it said 124K),
  IAH 56,233 (50K), SAT 40,850 (38K), LAS 15,661 (16K), SAN 16,486 (17K),
  MSY 16,266 (16K), ATL 21,552 (13K); it did not quote OKC 148,671, DFW
  53,587, PHX 19,438, DEN 11,293. The settlement rule text is verbatim,
  18-hourly-value streak-breaker included. Prerequisites hold: batches 51
  and 52 are merged, and batch 56 never touched weather_markets.py (it
  shipped as a standalone nearby_station_obs.py), so the "collides with
  56's registry region" note in INDEX.md was wrong and is corrected there.

Why the answer is no -- six findings, all from live data:
  1. The family is eight days old. Every one of the 11 series was created
     2026-08-17. Exactly ONE completed week of history exists. The batch
     file's "live-verified" volume IS that single week.
  2. Atlanta is already gone -- one event ever (KXAVGTATL-26AUG23), closed,
     no open event this week. Family stability is unproven in both
     directions.
  3. The brackets are overwhelmingly near-degenerate. In the one completed
     week, 53 of 55 brackets settled at ~1c or ~99c; only OKC's 3+ rung
     (0.62) was genuinely uncertain. The reason is structural, not a fluke:
     a daily MEAN above 90F needs roughly a 103F+ high with a 78F+ low, so
     it is a standing NO in AUS/IAH/SAT/SAN/MSY/ATL/DEN and a standing YES
     in LAS/DFW/PHX. This is decisive against the batch's own premise: the
     joint day-dependence problem it identifies as the crux matters most at
     middling probabilities, and this family has almost none.
  4. Contract count badly overstates the opportunity. ~532K contracts in the
     completed week, but the bulk trades at 1c. Valued at terminal price the
     entire 11-city family is ~$127K/week, and ~$88K of that is
     Vegas/Dallas/Phoenix paying 99c for a near-certainty -- not a
     forecastable edge. The batch's "$100-300K/week family volume" is right
     in dollars and misleading as a measure of addressable opportunity.
  5. The book is one-sided and unexitable. Mid-week snapshot (week of
     Aug 24, ~1.3 days in): bid sizes 0-10 contracts against ask sizes
     350-970; Austin 2+ quoted 3c/44c, Houston 2+ 2c/67c, and
     Vegas/Dallas/Phoenix 2c/98c. liquidity_dollars was 0.0000 on every
     market checked. A taker can buy at a punitive ask and cannot sell.
     Caveat, stated honestly: this is one snapshot early in the week, and
     the book may tighten late-week when brackets become arithmetically
     decidable -- but late-week is exactly when a forecast adds least.
  6. The 20-settled-sample gate is statistically hollow for this family. The
     5 rungs of a city-week are NESTED monotone events (2+ contains 3+
     contains ... contains 6+) resolved by one week of weather, so 20
     "settled samples" is about 4 independent city-weeks. The batch's "gate
     fills in ~2-3 weeks" is true in count and false as evidence -- it would
     graduate a signal on ~4 effective observations.

Two cost items the batch file understated:
  a. No Weather Company access exists anywhere in the repo.
     kalshi_weather_index.py is Synoptic-backed -- a DIFFERENT source, which
     batch-52's own experiment measured at mean |diff| 1.6-2.0F (max 4.68F)
     against METAR. AVGT rounds the daily mean to a whole degree against a
     strict >90 threshold, so a ~2F source divergence flips individual days,
     and one flipped day breaks a streak and flips up to 5 nested rungs at
     once. Any reconstruction we could build is not the settlement source.
  b. Neither the forecast target nor the joint model is reusable. The bot
     forecasts daily max/min; mean_temp at weather_markets.py:9459 is the
     ensemble mean of the max/min distribution, NOT a daily mean
     temperature, so the 24-hour arithmetic-mean target is new. And
     monte_carlo.py's correlation machinery is cross-CITY (portfolio risk),
     not cross-DAY -- the AR(1) day-to-day model the batch recommends as
     "reuses existing machinery" is new work; only the Cholesky/PSD-repair
     scaffolding carries over.

Context that framed the decision:
  A14 (7f0acc7a) measured the existing forecast as having no skill against
  the market -- model Brier 0.2596 vs market 0.2201 on 214 settled rows --
  and batch-57's condition filtering widened that to BSS -0.2725 (n=94). The
  open follow-up entry "MEASURE BRIER SKILL CONDITIONED ON THE SIZE OF OUR
  DISAGREEMENT WITH THE PRICE" (batch 66) is what decides whether that means
  "no edge anywhere" or "no edge on average, edge in the traded tail", and
  it has NOT been run. Committing the roadmap's largest new surface -- a new
  condition type, a new settlement variable, a new forecast target and a new
  joint model -- while that is unresolved was the trade-off put to the user,
  and the answer was no.

Re-check trigger: none scheduled. If revisited, the questions that would
  have to flip first are, in order: (1) does the family still exist and has
  Atlanta returned; (2) after several more weeks, does any city produce
  brackets that settle away from 1c/99c with real frequency -- OKC is the
  only current candidate; (3) is there two-sided depth we could actually
  exit into; (4) can the settlement source itself be read, rather than
  approximated by a source with ~2F divergence against a whole-degree
  rounding boundary. Nothing below (1)-(3) makes the modelling work worth
  doing, and (4) gates correctness regardless. The two monthly US-average
  series (AVGTEMP, KXAVGTEMP) also exist and were not evaluated -- they are
  a different product (single national average, not a per-city streak) and
  out of this batch's scope.

Declined deliberately, not deferred for capacity: the option to extend
  check_series_drift() to KXAVGT* and add the 11 tickers to a
  KNOWN_UNTRACKED_AVGT_SERIES set (the convention at
  weather_markets.py:5183, which already has a precedent for recording a
  failed go/no-go in the comment) was offered and not taken. If the family
  is revisited, that is the cheapest first step and costs one small change
  plus scoped tests.
  Source: audit/handoff_prompts/batches/batch-55.md.

The previous status line here said "isolate_tracker_db remains", which its own addendum below had already superseded the same day.] Autouse fixture setup is 85% of test wall time; two fixtures account for 99.6% of it
Priority: MEDIUM -- pure test-suite latency, no production behaviour involved. Affects every local run and every developer iteration.
Files: tests/conftest.py (reset_open_meteo_circuit_breaker, isolate_tracker_db), circuit_breaker.py (_save_state, record_success)

Problem:
  Measured on Windows, main clone, idle machine, `pytest tests/test_safe_io.py
  tests/test_forecast_cache.py` (98 tests), summing pytest's own --durations=0
  output by phase:

    wall            35.82s
    setup           30.52s   (85.2% of wall)   98 uses, mean 311.4 ms/test
    call             5.00s   (14.0% of wall)   55 uses, mean  90.9 ms
    teardown         0.00s

  The test bodies are not the cost. Per-fixture attribution (pytest_fixture_setup
  hook wrapper, same run):

    reset_open_meteo_circuit_breaker   18.24s   186.1 ms/test   (74% of setup)
    isolate_tracker_db                  6.18s    63.1 ms/test   (25% of setup)
    all 25+ other autouse fixtures      ~0.17s    negligible

  Those two are 99.6% of all fixture setup.

  Root cause (reset_open_meteo_circuit_breaker): the fixture resets 20 breaker
  singletons per test by calling `cb.record_success()`. record_success()
  (circuit_breaker.py:240-251) ends with `self._save_state()`, and _save_state
  (circuit_breaker.py:122+) is a full read-modify-write of the SHARED
  .cb_state.json: read the file, json.loads it, merge one key, mkdir the parent,
  then safe_io.atomic_write_json -- temp file + fsync + os.replace. So resetting
  in-memory counters costs 20 fsync'd read-modify-write cycles per test: 1,960
  of them for these 98 tests alone. Windows makes this worse (Defender scanning
  data/, and _replace_with_retry's sharing-violation retries), which is why
  186 ms/test.

  Root cause (isolate_tracker_db): calls tracker.init_db() per test, rebuilding
  the entire schema in a fresh temp sqlite DB every time.

  Scale: 5,399 tests are collected suite-wide. If the 311 ms/test setup holds
  (it is a conftest-global autouse stack, so it plausibly does), that is roughly
  28 minutes of pure fixture setup on this machine.
  NOT VERIFIED for CI: CI runs ubuntu-latest, where fsync and AV scanning are far
  cheaper, so the Linux figure is likely much smaller. Do not quote the 28 min
  against CI's ~23 min total without measuring there first.

Recommendation:
  1. reset_open_meteo_circuit_breaker should reset the in-memory fields WITHOUT
     triggering persistence -- e.g. set `cb._persist = False` for the duration,
     or assign _failure_count/_opened_at/_wall_opened_at/_half_open/
     _last_failure_at directly instead of going through record_success(). The
     fixture only wants in-memory state clean; it never needs the write. Check
     first whether any test asserts on .cb_state.json contents after a reset.
  2. isolate_tracker_db could build the schema ONCE per session into a template
     file and copy it per test, rather than running init_db() 5,399 times.
     Verify tests that mutate schema-adjacent state still get a clean DB.
  3. Re-measure with the same method (--durations=0 summed by phase, plus the
     per-fixture hook) to confirm, and measure on Linux before claiming any CI
     benefit.

Resolution (2026-08-25) -- recommendation 1 implemented; 2 and 3 still open:
  tests/conftest.py's reset_open_meteo_circuit_breaker now sets cb._persist =
  False around the record_success() call and restores it in a finally, so the
  reset clears the in-memory counters without triggering _save_state()'s
  fsync'd read-modify-write of .cb_state.json.

  Chose the _persist toggle over assigning the cleared fields directly, so
  record_success() stays the SINGLE definition of "what a reset clears" -- a
  hand-copied field list would silently stop covering any field added there
  later, which is exactly the drift this repo keeps getting bitten by.

  Verified safe first: the only tests that exercise breaker persistence
  (test_p1_remaining.py, TestCircuitBreakerPersistence and neighbours) build
  their OWN CircuitBreaker instances and redirect _CB_STATE_PATH themselves --
  they never touch the module-level singletons this fixture resets, so the
  temporary flag cannot reach them. Nothing else in tests/ reads the state
  file's contents after a reset.

  Measured, same machine, same session, 98 tests (test_safe_io +
  test_forecast_cache):
    reset_open_meteo_circuit_breaker   186.1 ms/test  ->  0.0 ms/test
    wall (two runs each)               85.40s/84.80s  ->  28.58s/29.06s
  The ms/use figure is the reliable one; the wall figures were taken on a
  contended machine, but both before and after within the same window, so the
  ~2.9x ratio holds for that slice.

  Guarded by two new tests in tests/test_circuit_breaker_registry.py:
  test_reset_fixture_leaves_breakers_clean_and_restores_persist (behavioural --
  every registered breaker enters each test clean AND with _persist back True,
  so dropping the finally fails loudly) and
  test_reset_fixture_does_not_persist_during_reset (source-level guard on the
  optimisation itself, which would otherwise be silently revertible without
  failing anything). The second was mutation-tested: restoring the bare
  cb.record_success() fails it.

  Regression: 667 passed / 4 skipped across every breaker-touching file
  (test_circuit_breaker, test_circuit_breaker_registry, test_flash_crash_cb,
  test_p1_remaining, test_infrastructure, test_nws, test_rain_markets,

Resolution addendum (2026-08-25) -- recommendation 2 implemented:
  isolate_tracker_db no longer calls tracker.init_db() per test. A new
  session-scoped _tracker_db_template fixture builds the schema ONCE into a
  template file; the per-test fixture copies it. Safe because init_db() is
  pure schema -- one executescript of CREATE TABLE/INDEX plus a loop of
  idempotent ALTERs, no inserts, no environment dependency -- so a byte copy
  of an initialised file is semantically identical to re-running it.
  _db_initialized is now set True rather than False, matching the end state
  the old init_db() call left behind.

  Measured (Windows, same 98-test slice, test_safe_io + test_forecast_cache):
    isolate_tracker_db        63-207 ms/test  ->  0.5 ms/test
    _tracker_db_template      n/a             ->  139.3 ms ONCE per session

  Combined with the circuit-breaker fix above, that slice's wall time went
  35.82s -> 28.58s (CB) -> 6.18s (tracker), i.e. ~5.8x on this machine. The
  ms/use figures are the reliable ones; wall times move with machine load.

  Guarded by tests/test_conftest_tracker_db_isolation.py: the template arrives
  schema-complete and empty, a row written by one test is NOT visible to the
  next (deliberately ordered, with the write acting as the positive control),
  and DB_PATH never points at the real data/predictions.db. Mutation-tested:
  handing out the template itself instead of a copy fails the freshness test.

  Regression: 1,601 passed / 4 skipped across tracker, weather_markets, paper,
  trading, web_app, safe_io, forecast_cache, ml_bias, execution_log,
  infrastructure, p1_remaining and both conftest-isolation files; plus 633

[OPEN 2026-08-25 -- found while benchmarking pytest-xdist; xdist was NOT adopted and is not installed, but the flake it exposed is real and probably predates it] Intermittent single-test failure (~1 in 11) when the paper/lock/isolation test files run in parallel processes
Priority: MEDIUM -- a latent order/timing dependency between test files. Harmless today because the suite runs serially, but it is the kind of hidden coupling that makes any future parallelisation unsafe.
Files: unknown -- somewhere in the 11-file slice below

Problem:
  Benchmarking pytest-xdist, this slice was run repeatedly with
  `-n auto --dist loadfile` (one file's tests stay on one worker, but different
  files run concurrently in separate processes):

    tests/test_paper.py, tests/test_starting_balance.py,
    tests/test_state_consistency.py, tests/test_drawdown_tiers.py,
    tests/test_p1_remaining.py, tests/test_trade_improvements.py,
    tests/test_cron_lock.py, tests/test_paper_cross_process_lock.py,
    tests/test_safe_io.py, tests/test_circuit_breaker_registry.py,
    tests/test_conftest_paper_isolation.py

  Result: 359 passed on 10 of 11 runs; ONE run reported "1 failed, 358 passed".
  The failing test's identity was not captured (the run was grepped for its
  summary line only -- a mistake), and 12 subsequent runs did not reproduce it.

  What was ruled out:
  - NOT the timing-sensitive lock files in isolation: test_safe_io.py,
    test_paper_cross_process_lock.py and test_cron_lock.py were run 12 times at
    `-n 16` together with zero failures. Both lock test files isolate their lock
    paths to tmp_path.
  - NOT production-state corruption: across every parallel run,
    data/paper_trades.json, data/.cb_state.json and data/seasonal_weights.json
    were byte-identical before and after (md5), and predictions.db / tracker.db /
    execution_log.db kept mtimes predating the runs. No worker wrote to real
    state -- which is a positive result for batch-62's isolation sweep.
  - It requires the full 11-file slice to appear, so it is an interaction
    between files running on different workers, not one intrinsically bad test.

  Serial runs of the same slice have not been observed to fail, but the serial
  case was not run enough times to rule out a pre-existing flake that
  parallelism merely makes more likely.

Recommendation:
  Reproduce with full output captured (`--tb=long -rf`, tee each run to its own
  file) rather than grepping summary lines, looping until it recurs -- budget
  ~20 runs at ~80s each. Once the test is named, the likely suspects are shared
  OS-level resources that tmp_path does not cover: the .cb_state.json file lock
  (_CB_STATE_FILE_LOCK is in-process only, so separate worker processes do not
  serialise against each other), system-temp files keyed by PID, and any
  subprocess spawned by test_paper_cross_process_lock.
  Worth fixing on its own merits even though xdist was declined: a hidden
  cross-file coupling is a latent flake in serial runs too.
[CLOSED 2026-08-25 -- batch-53's go/no-go replay ran; the gate failed. The

  to backlog.txt, close the idea, done -- that is a successful batch outcome

  -- GATE FAILED, IDEA CLOSED
Priority: n/a -- closed. Recorded for the numbers, so the idea is not
  re-proposed from the dossier without them.
Files: none changed. The replay ran entirely as scratchpad scripts;
  ml_bias.py and calibration.py were not touched, per batch-53's own
  "productionizing waits for the cluster's slot" carve-out.

Problem:
  Expansion Dossier B3 proposed Isotonic Distributional Regression
  (nonparametric, hyperparameter-free, CRPS-optimal within monotone models)
  as a challenger to the current EMOS/temperature-scaling calibration, to be
  gated on: IDR mean CRPS >= 5% better than the incumbent on held-out data.

What the replay found:
  Population: predictions JOIN outcomes_valid where forecast_temp_f and
  settled_temp_f are both present -- 313 market rows, 2026-05-18..2026-08-23,
  20 cities, D+0 and D+1 only. 103 of those rows were then EXCLUDED as
  contaminated (see the separate metar_lockout entry filed alongside this
  one), leaving 210 deduped clean pairs / 208 events.

  Expanding walk-forward (train strictly on earlier market_dates, >= 60
  training events), 148 held-out rows, reference = the deployed above/below/
  between sigma-Gaussian including _BETWEEN_SIGMA_*_CAP and the below-market
  x1.5. _time_risk's sigma_mult is not reconstructable per row, so it is
  swept rather than pinned:

    sigma_mult   reference    EMOS     IDR    EMOS gain   IDR gain
      1.00        1.6200     1.5597  1.7814     +3.72%     -9.96%   FAIL
      0.85        1.6299     1.5597  1.7814     +4.30%     -9.30%   FAIL
      0.70        1.6599     1.5597  1.7814     +6.04%     -7.32%   FAIL
      0.50        1.7381     1.5597  1.7814    +10.26%     -2.49%   FAIL

  IDR vs EMOS: -14.21% (95% CI ~ -22%..-7%, paired t = -3.55). IDR loses to
  the fit_emos() estimator this repo already has, at every sigma_mult.

  NOTE that EMOS also fails the same 5% bar on clean data (+3.72% / +4.30%
  at the plausible multipliers). Neither calibrator earns activation here.

  Learning curve (fixed most-recent-60-event held-out block, growing training
  window): IDR minus EMOS = -32.0%, -21.6%, -14.3%, -3.9%, -3.7%, -0.1%,
  -4.7% at 40/60/90/120/160/200/246 training events. IDR converges toward
  EMOS but never overtakes it -- more settled data will not rescue it. That
  is the reason this is CLOSED rather than deferred-pending-more-data.

  Monotonicity (batch-53 asked explicitly for this): on CLEAN rows the
  pooled Spearman rho(forecast, error) is -0.012 with no sign flip across
  the forecast range -- decile bias +0.33 +2.76 +0.92 +1.09 +1.04 +0.92
  +1.80 +2.27 -0.26 +0.95. The forecast carries a single near-constant
  ~+1.2F cold bias. That is exactly what EMOS's `a` absorbs in one
  parameter and what a pooled isotonic map on 60-200 points can only
  reproduce with far more variance. IDR's failure is a sample-size/variance
  story, not a monotonicity-violation story.

  (An earlier draft of this analysis reported a sign-flipping bias and a
  monotonicity problem. That was the metar_lockout contamination, not real.)

Does better calibration close the model-vs-market Brier gap? No -- it widens
  it. Same walk-forward clock, each predictive CDF converted to P(market
  condition) and scored against settled_yes on the same population
  get_model_vs_market_brier uses (above/below only), clean rows, n=144:

    our_prob (recorded)  0.2480     market_prob  0.2113
    EMOS                 0.2775  (+0.0295 vs our_prob, t=+1.38)
    IDR                  0.2972  (+0.0492 vs our_prob, t=+1.81)
    reference Gaussian   0.3049  (+0.0569 vs our_prob, t=+2.23)

  Every recalibrated challenger is WORSE than the probability the bot already
  emits, and none approaches the market. A "fraction of the gap closed"
  statistic is not quotable here -- bootstrapped it is -80.5% with a 95% CI
  of -534%..+30%. The durable statement is the table.

  Cross-check that this is not a lockout artifact: our_prob vs market on
  above/below rows -- all 202 rows gap +0.0397 +/- 0.0149 (t=+2.68);
  non-lockout 169 rows gap +0.0378 +/- 0.0140 (t=+2.69). A14 / batch-57's
  "no skill vs the market" verdict survives the contamination correction
  intact, and it is NOT explained by temperature miscalibration.

Method / reproducibility:
  Scratchpad scripts, read-only against a COPY of data/predictions.db behind
  a safe_io.project_root() redirect with sockets blocked. IDR built as
  per-threshold sklearn IsotonicRegression on exceedance indicators (the
  PyPI `isodistrreg` package requires Python >= 3.13; this repo is on 3.12),
  CRPS via properscoring.crps_ensemble with the per-threshold masses as
  weights -- validated against a 1.2M-point numerical integration of
  INT (F(x) - 1{x>=obs})^2 dx to 2.5e-05. Shuffling the forecast collapses
  IDR from 3.98 to 6.44 against a climatology 7.13, confirming the harness
  is not manufacturing skill.

  Caveats carried, none of which change the verdict: walk-forward trains on
  market_date < cutoff, which is not identical to "settled before the test
  row's decision time" (286 of 44,704 training rows, 0.64%, are not yet
  settled); sklearn's isotonic interpolates linearly off-grid where
  reference IDR steps (mild smoothing, if anything favours IDR); EMOS here
  is fit_emos(forecast_temp_f, ens_var:=1) rather than production's
  fit_emos(ens_mean, real ens_var), so its c/d are not separately
  identifiable and nothing here transfers to production EMOS's variance
  structure.

Why this is closed rather than deferred:
  The calibration/ML cluster's standing deferral is about SEQUENCING, not
  about whether the idea works. This measured it: it does not work here, it
  loses to an estimator already in the repo, and the learning curve says
  more data will not change that. Re-opening should require a NEW argument
  (e.g. a covariate-conditioned IDR, which is a different proposal), not
  simply a larger settled sample.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-25 (batch-75) -- found by batch-53's replay experiment, then

  is the RUNNING DAILY EXTREME at lock time, not an instantaneous reading --

  METAR TEMPERATURE ON method='metar_lockout' ROWS, NOT A DAILY-EXTREME
  FORECAST -- SILENTLY CORRUPTS ANY ANALYSIS KEYED ON THAT COLUMN
Priority: HIGH -- RAISED 2026-08-25, see the CORRECTION under "Live impact"
  below. The first version of this entry said "NOT a live-money bug today (no
  production path consumes the corrupted values)". That is WRONG. A live path
  does consume them: paper._score_ensemble_members writes
  trade["forecast_temp"] into ensemble_member_scores as model='blended', and
  get_dynamic_station_bias() PREFERS exactly those rows, feeding
  weather_markets._DYNAMIC_BIAS_CACHE and therefore live forecasts. It has
  also already produced one wrong retrospective validation number and it
  silently destroyed the first pass of batch-53's replay. It is invisible
  unless you split by `method`, which no existing consumer does.
Files: trade_cycle.py (~920, "forecast_temp_f": analysis.get("forecast_temp")
  -- the writer), weather_markets.py (analyze_trade's `if not metar_locked:`
  block, ~13870), tracker.py (get_regional_recent_bias ~8797, the one query

UPDATE 2026-08-25 -- batch-68 (A13 settlement-source audit) independently hit this while tracing
  what get_dynamic_station_bias trains on, and filed a duplicate entry that has since been deleted
  in favour of this one. Three things it adds:

  1. SHARE OF THE CORRUPTED POPULATION, measured: 69 of the 151 model='blended' rows in
     ensemble_member_scores (46%) trace back to a metar_lockout trade. That is the fraction of
     get_dynamic_station_bias's PREFERRED row set that is not a forecast at all.
  2. THE Files LIST ABOVE IS NOW ONE SHORT. It says get_regional_recent_bias is "the one query that
     joins forecast_temp_f to settled_temp_f with no method filter". batch-68 added a second such
     join, tracker.get_station_bias_by_lead() (the A15a panel) -- but WITH the filter: it excludes
     method='metar_lockout' explicitly, and its docstring records why. So the panel is unaffected
     by this bug, and is the natural place to validate a fix from.
  3. A CLEAN COMPARISON EXISTS NOW. Because that panel measures the same quantity
     (forecast_temp_f - settled_temp_f, per city/var/lead) over the UNCONTAMINATED subset, whoever
     fixes this can diff the corrected get_dynamic_station_bias against it rather than having to
     trust the corrected number on its own. batch-68 measured the panel's uncontaminated D+0/D+1
     residuals at mostly within +-1F, against the +8.63/-10.42F this entry reports for lockout rows.

  Note also that batch-68's separate ensemble_member_scores.actual_temp repair
  (backfill_member_actual_temp, see "A13 SETTLEMENT-SOURCE AUDIT") fixes the OTHER half of the same
  table's corruption -- the `actual` column, frozen from a pre-2026-08-10 METAR proxy. The two are
  independent: that one is the label, this one is the prediction. Both were present at audit time,
  and fixing either alone still leaves get_dynamic_station_bias training on bad pairs.

Problem:
  On rows where analyze_trade took the METAR lock-in path
  (predictions.method = 'metar_lockout'), the stored forecast_temp_f is the
  instantaneous METAR ambient temperature at decision time, not a forecast
  of the day's high or low. analyze_trade puts the entire ensemble/Gaussian
  block behind `if not metar_locked:` -- when METAR locks, blended_prob comes
  from _metar_blended_prob and no temperature distribution is produced at
  all -- but a temperature is still persisted into the same column that
  ensemble rows use for a genuine daily-extreme forecast.

  Measured on the settled join (313 rows: ensemble 208, metar_lockout 103,
  normal_dist 2), D+0:

    method          var   n   mean forecast_temp_f   mean settled    bias
    metar_lockout   max   65        78.40               87.03       + 8.632
    metar_lockout   min   38        82.21               71.79       -10.421
    ensemble        max   47        85.49               85.68       + 0.193
    ensemble        min   28        70.15               71.71       + 1.567

  The tell is unambiguous: on lockout rows the HIGH-market forecast (78.40)
  is COLDER than the LOW-market forecast (82.21). That is impossible for
  daily extremes and is exactly what you get from a single mid-day ambient
  reading standing in for both. Lockout RMSE is 10.9-11.7F against 2.5-3.4F
  for ensemble rows on the same days.

  It is NOT fixed and NOT self-correcting. The lockout bias by half-month
  (max markets) is +8.60, +7.65, +14.52, +15.55 -- flat to growing. What
  changed is the MIX: lockout share of settled D+0 rows ran 95%, 69%, 46%,
  8%, 6%, 0% from 2026-06a to 2026-08b. The artifact simply stopped
  appearing in the settled sample; the writer is unchanged.

Live impact (traced, not assumed):
  - CORRECTION 2026-08-25: get_dynamic_station_bias() IS reachable, and the
    original entry got this wrong. It does read a different table
    (ensemble_member_scores.predicted_temp/actual_temp), but the contaminated
    value flows INTO that table: paper.py:1464 calls _score_ensemble_members
    on every settled paper trade, and paper.py:1569 sets
    model_means["blended"] = trade.get("forecast_temp") -- which on a
    metar_lockout trade is the METAR lock value, not a daily-extreme
    forecast. paper.py's own comment at that line says "blended" is
    "preferred by get_dynamic_station_bias() over the per-model means", and
    tracker.py:7377-7382 confirms it (WHERE model = 'blended'). From there
    weather_markets.py:401 loads it into _DYNAMIC_BIAS_CACHE and applies it
    to live forecasts. So the chain is complete: lock value -> blended score
    -> per-city station bias -> live forecast adjustment.
  - NOW QUANTIFIED -- REPLACES the "NOT QUANTIFIED" note filed here on
    2026-08-25 (which said the join was unreliable and the magnitude
    unmeasurable). Both statements were true when written and are now
    obsolete. The join was never the problem: ensemble_member_scores.
    actual_temp held an IEM ASOS proxy reading rather than Kalshi's settled
    value, which is why it matched outcomes.settled_temp_f on only 41 of 151
    blended rows. Batch-68's in-place repair (2026-08-25 ~04:34; 228
    actual_temp values rewritten, predicted_temp untouched, zero row-count
    change) fixed that -- the same join now matches 151/151 exactly, mean
    |difference| 0.000.
    Re-derived on the repaired data, bias = predicted_temp - actual_temp:
      metar_lockout only    n= 69   -2.759F   rmse 10.620
      no lockout            n= 81   -1.370F   rmse  3.008
      ALL                   n=151   -1.969F   rmse  7.517
    and per var, which is how get_dynamic_station_bias actually queries it:
      metar_lockout / max   n= 48   -8.213F
      metar_lockout / min   n= 21   +9.706F
      no lockout    / max   n= 48   -1.194F
      no lockout    / min   n= 33   -1.626F
    So 69 of 151 blended rows (46%) are contaminated at +/-8-10F with
    OPPOSITE SIGNS BY VAR -- the running-extreme signature. The pooled
    -2.759F understates it badly because max and min cancel; the per-var
    query never sees that cancellation. The superseded "~40% at +3.4F"
    figure was computed on the broken join: right on share, wrong on
    magnitude and sign. Do not quote it.
    Consequence: adding a ticker column to ensemble_member_scores is NO
    LONGER needed to measure this and must not gate the fix. It remains a
    defensible robustness improvement (a (city, target_date, var) key cannot
    separate two markets on the same city/date/var, and silently excludes
    the 49 rows where var IS NULL), but it is optional.
  - WHAT BATCH-68 DID NOT FIX: predicted_temp was untouched (0 of 176 rows
    changed). On lockout rows it is still the running extreme, so
    get_dynamic_station_bias now computes a clean-actual-minus-dirty-
    predicted error -- the repair fixed the observed half and left the
    predicted half contaminated. Live effect measured across the repair:
    OklahomaCity/max is the only city currently over the 10-sample floor,
    and its bias moved from +7.27F to -7.06F, a 14.33F swing in a value the
    caller SUBTRACTS from the raw forecast. Sub-floor cities are larger
    still (Phoenix/max -17.1F, Seattle/max -12.7F, Denver/max -12.7F) and
    will land as they accumulate samples.
  - get_regional_recent_bias() IS affected: it selects
    predictions.forecast_temp_f joined to outcomes_valid.settled_temp_f with
    no method filter. It has NO production call site (tests only; see
    tests/test_dead_code_scan.py's own allowlist entry for it) -- it is the
    unwired "cross-city recent-error pooling" candidate signal.
  - CONSEQUENCE worth noting: that signal's recorded validation --
    weather_markets._SignalRegistryEntry(key="cross_city_pooling"),
    "Last check (2026-07-23): Pearson r~=0.35" -- was computed over a window
    where most settled D+0 rows were lockout rows. That r is not
    trustworthy and must be recomputed on method-filtered data before it is
    ever used to justify wiring the signal live. Same pattern as the
    contamination lesson in feedback_reverify_correlation_after_contamination_fix.
  - sigma_audit.py reads the column but is diagnostic-only by its own
    docstring.

What the fix looks like:
  Decide what the column means and make it mean that consistently. Two
  defensible options, and this is a genuine design call rather than an
  obvious bug-swat:
  (a) Stop writing forecast_temp_f on lockout rows (write NULL), so every
      non-NULL value is a daily-extreme forecast and every existing consumer
      becomes correct without changing its query. Loses the ability to
      reconstruct what the lock-in saw.
  (b) Keep writing it but add a sibling column (e.g. observed_temp_f) and
      move the METAR value there, leaving forecast_temp_f NULL on those
      rows. Preserves the audit trail; needs a migration.
  Either way, add the method filter to get_regional_recent_bias and
  recompute the cross_city_pooling correlation note.

Why not now:
  Needs the (a)-vs-(b) call from the user, plus a migration decision for the
  103 existing contaminated rows (leave them, NULL them, or move them). No
  live path is currently reading the bad values, so there is no urgency
  forcing a rushed choice.

When to revisit:
  Before ANY of these: wiring cross-city pooling live; building the
  data-driven sigma in [DATA-DRIVEN SIGMA FROM SETTLED HISTORY]; or any
  future analysis that joins forecast_temp_f to settled_temp_f. All three
  would silently inherit the corruption.

RESOLVED 2026-08-25 (batch-75). Note the "Why not now" paragraph above was
  itself stale when this was picked up -- it still read "No live path is
  currently reading the bad values, so there is no urgency", contradicting
  the CORRECTION under "Live impact" directly above it. The live path was
  real; that sentence is superseded.

  User decisions (AskUserQuestion, both halves asked before any code):
  (1) new column + distinct model key + a shadow sample; (2) repair BOTH
  tables rather than forward-only.

  What shipped:
  - weather_markets.analyze_trade's METAR-locked branch no longer assigns
    the running extreme to forecast_temp. It now sets forecast_temp=None,
    observed_extreme=<running extreme> and model_forecast_temp=<the RAW,
    uncorrected deterministic 3-model daily-extreme forecast>. Both new
    fields are initialised beside disagree_f OUTSIDE the locked branch --
    the result dict reads them unconditionally, so scoping them inside it
    would UnboundLocalError on every non-locked scan (the same bug an opus
    review caught for blend_exclusions in batch-64).
  - Schema v76 adds a SECOND column, predictions.model_forecast_temp_f, for
    a reason that is about DATA ACCRUAL RATE rather than correctness, and is
    recorded here because it is not derivable from the diff. Every
    live-trading gate in this repo is a sample-count floor, and at the rate
    samples were accruing several are not reachable on any realistic
    timeline -- that pressure is why the METAR value was being written into
    forecast_temp_f in the first place. On a lockout row the model's own
    daily-extreme forecast is already computed (analyze_trade uses it as the
    fallback when the METAR value is missing) and was then discarded.
    Persisting it costs one nullable column and multiplies the usable sample:
    the metar_lock_model_fc member-score row only lands when a lockout trade
    is PLACED and later SETTLES, whereas a predictions row is written for
    every market SCANNED -- historically 106 vs 70, and far wider going
    forward since most scanned markets are never traded. RAW, uncorrected,
    and read by NOTHING; it is a measurement substrate, not a signal. Do not
    promote it into a live path before its own bias is measured, or the fix
    trades a known contamination for an unmeasured one.
  - Schema v75: predictions.observed_extreme_f. Plain overwrite in the
    UPSERT, deliberately NOT the COALESCE its forecast_run_inits/
    blend_exclusions neighbours use -- it is one of a mutually-exclusive
    TRIPLE with method and forecast_temp_f, and COALESCE would let an
    observation survive onto a row a later ensemble scan has relabelled
    method='ensemble'.
  - paper.place_paper_order now STORES `method` on the trade record (it was
    already a parameter, used only for Kelly scaling, and never persisted --
    which is precisely why _score_ensemble_members could not tell a lockout
    trade from an ensemble one), plus observed_extreme/model_forecast_temp.
    _score_ensemble_members resolves method from the trade first and falls
    back to the predictions row for trades placed before the field existed.
  - On a lockout trade it logs metar_lock_extreme + metar_lock_model_fc
    instead of 'blended'. The observation is preserved and RELABELLED rather
    than dropped -- a silent skip is how this class of bug hides.
  - tracker.repair_metar_lockout_rows() + `py main.py repair-metar-lockout-rows
    [--dry-run]`. One transaction; re-runnable by construction (selects on
    current state, never on a date, so rows written between this landing and
    the next run are picked up later). Ambiguous rows -- an ems row matching
    BOTH a lockout and a non-lockout prediction for one (city,target_date,var)
    -- are counted and LEFT ALONE, matching backfill_ensemble_member_scores_var's
    leave-NULL-where-ambiguous discipline. Measured on the live DB before
    landing: 106 predictions rows to move, 70 blended rows tracing to a
    lockout of which 1 is ambiguous, i.e. 69 re-keyable -- which reconciles
    exactly with the 69/151 and the separate "mixed n=1" this entry reported.

  THE FINDING THAT WAS NOT IN THE BATCH FILE, and the reason this took a
  constant rather than a third literal: ensemble_member_scores has SIX
  per-model queries that each hardcoded `model != 'blended'` --
  get_member_accuracy, get_member_brier, get_member_bias,
  get_model_brier_scores, get_ensemble_member_accuracy and get_model_weights.
  get_model_weights reads its model names FROM THE TABLE, not from a declared
  list, so BOTH new keys would have silently joined the live blend-weight
  softmax the moment they cleared its 10-observation floor, perturbing every
  real model's normalised weight through the shared denominator -- the exact
  leak TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES's own docstring describes. Replaced all six
  with tracker.NON_MODEL_SCORE_KEYS / _non_model_keys_sql().
  NOT added to weather_markets.TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES despite the apparent
  fit: that set means "a real model we DO fetch but do not weight", and
  batch_prewarm_ensemble iterates it to issue actual Open-Meteo requests
  (`TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES - {"ncep_hrrr_conus"}`) while _model_weights()
  treats its members as ensemble candidates. Putting a non-model key there
  would have sent the bot fetching a dataset named "metar_lock_extreme".

  Item 4 (registry note): weather_markets' _SignalRegistryEntry(
  key="cross_city_pooling") advertised "Last check (2026-07-23): Pearson
  r~=0.35". Replaced with the post-contamination-fix 2026-08-22 result
  (r=0.08, n=35, sign agreement 51% -- no signal), which was buried in
  tests/test_dead_code_scan.py's allowlist string while the registry -- the
  surface a future session actually consults -- kept the optimistic number.
  get_regional_recent_bias also gained the method filter, using
  get_station_bias_by_lead's COALESCE idiom (a bare `!=` drops rows whose
  method is NULL, since SQLite's NULL != 'x' is NULL).

  Item 3 (ticker column on ensemble_member_scores): DELIBERATELY SKIPPED.
  The batch re-scoped it to optional after batch-68's repair made the
  (city,target_date,var) join exact, and it is not needed to verify this fix.

  ADJACENT, fixed here because it is the same contamination in a LIVE GATE:

  with "forecast_temp_f runs ~4.6F cold (6/7 samples)". 2 of Miami's 7 settled
  rows are metar_lockout and average -10.98F; on the 5 clean rows the bias is
  -3.25F. Direction holds, magnitude overstated ~40%. Comment corrected; the

  Tests: tests/test_batch75_metar_lock_contamination.py, 19 tests, all

  the regional-bias test's control initially FAILED, exposing that its absence
  assertion was passing vacuously because the source city's own bias had not
  cleared the maturity floor, so no candidate ever reached the method filter.
  Mutation testing also DELETED code: a guard against writing a NULL 'blended'
  row survived its own mutation, proving the real protection is

  the redundant guard was removed rather than left as reassuring dead weight.
  Because every other test feeds forecast_temp in explicitly, none of them
  would catch someone restoring `forecast_temp = _metar_ct` at the writer

  TWO INDEPENDENT OPUS REVIEWS (effort=high), scoped by subsystem. Neither
  found a HIGH. Every finding was addressed; the ones that changed behaviour:
  - M1 (data): the repair's UPDATEs keyed on id alone while its SELECTs ran
    in autocommit (sqlite3 issues BEGIN at the first DML, not the first
    SELECT), so a concurrent scan between read and write could NULL a fresh
    ensemble forecast and stamp a stale observation on a row now labelled
    'ensemble'. Both UPDATEs now repeat the SELECT's predicates and count
    skipped rows as *_raced.
  - M1 (writer): _score_ensemble_members classified LEGACY trades (no
    `method` on the record) entirely from the predictions lookup, and the
    except reset only condition_type -- so a transient sqlite lock at
    settlement fell through to the else branch and re-wrote the running
    extreme as a 'blended' sample, re-injecting the contamination AFTER the
    one-off repair had run. Now fails CLOSED: unresolvable provenance logs a
    warning and writes nothing.
  - M2 (data): the ems join was INNER, so a blended row with no predictions
    row behind it (paper.py's own comment records that quick-buy paths never
    call log_prediction) was indistinguishable from "not a lockout" and could
    be re-keyed -- permanently deleting a legitimate sample, since
    idx_ems_dedup is UNIQUE per city/date/var. Now LEFT JOIN with an explicit
    ems_unmatched bucket.
  - M3 (data): a minimal log_prediction write NULLs `method` via the plain
    overwrite, and the repair keys its decision off it. Such rows are now
    counted as ems_unknown_method rather than silently classified clean.
  - L4 (writer): metar_lock_model_fc had no fallback to the predictions row,
    so a call site not threading it dropped the shadow sample v76 exists for.
  - L5 (writer): cmd_today's place path threaded neither new field.
  - A legacy-shape fallback was added while fixing M1: on a pre-batch-75
    lockout trade the running extreme lives ONLY in trade["forecast_temp"],
    so without a third fallback every such trade still settling would lose
    its observation entirely.
  The ems_* buckets are now DISJOINT and sum to the table's own blended row
  count (69 + 1 + 25 + 81 = 176 on the live DB), so the operator output is
  self-reconciling -- the "counted nowhere" gap the review found is closed by
  construction rather than by adding one more counter.

  Mutation testing during the review fixes was worth more than the fixes:
  THREE tests passed with their target deleted and had to be rewritten. The
  fail-closed test needed two mock revisions (an always-raise mock broke the
  earlier settled_temp_f lookup, so the function returned before reaching the
  guard; a raise-after-first mock broke the WRITE instead -- only failing
  exactly the second _conn() call tests the guard). The migration test needed
  rebuilding entirely: rewinding schema_version on a migrated DB proves
  nothing because the columns already exist, so it now builds a genuine v74
  DB from a truncated _MIGRATIONS list. Verified by moving the v76 entry to
  the FRONT of the list -- the append-only violation -- which the rewritten
  test correctly fails and the original passed.

[OPEN 2026-08-25 -- found by batch-53's replay while trying to test whether
  the market prices temperature uncertainty wider than realized; the test
  could not be run because this signal is unusable.]
  fit_market_implied_distribution() RETURNS A DEGENERATE FIT ON ~19% OF
  ROWS AND ITS SANITY BOUNDS ARE TOO LOOSE TO CATCH IT
Priority: Medium -- log-only signal, no live consumer today, so nothing is
  mispriced by it. But it is recorded as if it were usable, and the one
  analysis that tried to use it got nonsense. Any future "market-implied
  volatility" work inherits this.
Files: weather_markets.py (fit_market_implied_distribution ~7950, its
  sigma_bounds default at :7952, the bounds check at :8095), tracker.py
  (predictions.implied_sigma / implied_mean / fit_residual columns),
  sigma_audit.py (diagnostic reader)

Problem:
  fit_market_implied_distribution() fits a Normal to an event's sibling
  bracket ladder by weighted least squares and stores implied_mean /
  implied_sigma / fit_residual. Its guard is
  `sigma_bounds: tuple[float, float] = (0.1, 50.0)` (:7952), enforced at
  :8095. For a daily temperature market a 50F upper bound is not a sanity
  check -- it accepts essentially any degenerate solution.

  Measured over all 160 rows carrying implied_sigma (live DB, 2026-08-25):

    p5   0.702    p25  1.286    p50  1.820    p75  2.211
    p90 13.052    p95 20.819    p99 41.630    max 47.298

    implied_sigma >  5F:  30 rows (18.8%)
    implied_sigma > 20F:   9 rows ( 5.6%)

  The median (1.82F) is entirely sensible. The distribution is bimodal:
  roughly 81% good fits and 19% garbage. fit_residual does NOT flag them --
  its median is 0.0035 and p90 0.0794, so the optimizer is "succeeding"
  numerically; it is finding a genuinely flat/thin ladder and fitting a
  huge sigma to it.

  implied_mean goes with it: |implied_mean - forecast_temp_f| > 20F on 10
  of 82 comparable rows (12.2%).

  Direct test of usability, on the 69 settled non-metar_lockout rows that
  have implied_sigma: z = (settled_temp_f - implied_mean) / implied_sigma
  has mean -3.288 and sd 6.563. A usable fit would give mean ~0, sd ~1.
  For comparison the bot's own sigma on the same rows gives mean z +0.228,
  sd 1.194 -- imperfect (about 19% too narrow) but usable.

  Consequence for the analysis that surfaced this: the question "does the
  market price temperature uncertainty wider than we do" could not be
  answered on the mean (market/our = 3.41x, driven entirely by the garbage
  tail). On medians it is 1.41x, with the market wider on 55.1% of rows --
  suggestive, not conclusive, and not worth acting on until the fit is
  trustworthy.

Prior art in this same function, worth reading before choosing a fix:
  A tighter bound was ALREADY added for the rain ladders (see the
  "Sanity bounds for fit_market_implied_distribution()'s fitted sigma when
  fitting KXRAIN*M monthly-rain siblings" comment, weather_markets.py
  ~5823). Its own text says the function's "default bounds of (0.1, 50.0)
  were tuned for temperature and never validated at rain's much smaller
  scale" -- so the rain caller got a real bound and the temperature caller
  was left on the untightened default. This entry is the temperature half
  of that same observation.

What the fix looks like:
  - Tighten the temperature sigma bound to something defensible. Realized
    forecast-error RMSE on clean rows is ~3F and the bot's own capped sigma
    tops out at _SIGMA_2DAY_CAP = 4.0F, so a bound in the 8-12F range would
    reject every observed degenerate fit while leaving enormous headroom
    over any plausible real ladder. Derive it, don't guess it.
  - Decide what a rejected fit should do: return None (the function already
    has that path) vs. store the fit with a quality flag. Returning None
    loses the ability to count how often it fails, which is how this stayed
    invisible.
  - Consider WHY the flat fits happen -- likely thin ladders with few finite
    boundaries. If so, a minimum-bracket-count precondition is a better
    guard than a post-hoc sigma bound, and would fail loudly instead of
    silently.
  - Backfill decision for the ~30 existing bad rows: leave, NULL, or
    recompute.

Why not now:
  No live consumer, so no urgency. Wants the bound derived from real ladder
  geometry rather than picked, and that is a small analysis in its own
  right.

When to revisit:
  Before ANY use of implied_sigma/implied_mean in a live path, and before
  any market-implied-volatility analysis -- the "is the market wider than
  us" question is genuinely interesting (see the measured 1.41x median) and
  is blocked on this.

  from this entry's own Hanley-McNeil table), 20 kept as a silent tripwire,
  and signal values now logged onto the unbiased analysis_attempts
  population so the new floor is reachable in days rather than months. Full
  narrative at the end of this entry.]
  THE SIGNAL REGISTRY'S sample_floor=20 CLEARS AT ~27% STATISTICAL POWER --
  IT CANNOT DISTINGUISH A REAL SIGNAL FROM NOISE
Priority: Medium-High -- no signal has been wired live on the strength of a
  cleared floor yet, so nothing is broken today. But the floor is the
  headline number on the graduation surface (`main.py`'s report prints
  "20/20 -- floor cleared" in GREEN and _notify_feature_activation fires an
  alert saying "ready for the correlation check"), and it is the thing a
  future session will most plausibly act on. This is a bad-decision trap,
  filed before it springs rather than after.
Files: weather_markets.py (_SignalRegistryEntry ~8623, the nine
  sample_floor=20 entries between ~8721 and ~8850,
  get_signal_graduation_report's floor_cleared / _notify_feature_activation
  block ~8918-8945), main.py (the report printer ~7418-7440)

Problem:
  [CORRECTED 2026-08-26 by batch-81, which enumerated the _SignalRegistryEntry
  blocks rather than trusting this paragraph. The original text read "Nine of
  the eleven registry entries use sample_floor=20" and listed
  richer_ml_features among them and rain_forecast_blend among the Nones. All
  three claims were wrong; the corrected text follows.]

  TEN of the TWELVE registry entries use sample_floor=20: run_trend,
  market_implied, market_implied_rain, gated_edge, nbm_quantile_prob,
  ecmwf_consensus_gap, gem_graduation, ukmo_graduation, hrrr_graduation,
  rain_forecast_blend. (richer_ml_features and cross_city_pooling use None.)

  At n=20-26, a binary-outcome signal cannot be distinguished from noise.
  Worked through on nbm_quantile_prob, which cleared the floor with 26
  settled rows on 2026-08-25 and has the best-looking point estimate of any
  component measured (AUC 0.657, Brier 0.2162 against the market's 0.2102
  on the same rows). Hanley-McNeil SE at that AUC and base rate:

     n     SE(AUC)    95% CI at the observed AUC    power vs 0.5
     26     0.1176         [0.426, 0.887]                27%
     50     0.0845         [0.491, 0.822]                46%
    100     0.0589         [0.541, 0.772]                76%
    200     0.0418         [0.575, 0.739]                96%

  So at the floor, a signal with a genuinely good AUC of 0.657 has a 27%
  chance of being called better than a coin flip -- and, symmetrically, a
  worthless signal has ample room to look good. The floor is cleared before
  the evidence exists either way.

  The registry's own design already hedges this: correlation_note is a
  free-text "still a human call", and main.py's header prints
  "Sample-floor status only -- the correlation check for each signal is
  still a manual judgment call". So the intent was never "20 = graduate".
  The problem is the affordance: a GREEN "floor cleared" plus a proactive
  notification reads as an invitation, and nothing anywhere states what
  sample size would actually settle the question.

What the fix looks like:
  - Raise sample_floor to a power-derived number rather than a round one.
    ~150-200 gives 76-96% power at a plausible effect size; pick per signal
    if their effect sizes differ meaningfully.
  - Or keep 20 as a "start looking" tripwire and add a SECOND, higher
    "enough to decide" threshold, with the report distinguishing them. This
    is probably better -- 20 is genuinely useful as "the pipeline works and
    rows are arriving", which is a real thing to be notified about.
  - Either way, soften the notification text and the green: "floor cleared"
    should not be the loudest thing on the screen when it means "you may now
    begin collecting evidence".
  - Record the power basis next to the number so the next person does not
    have to re-derive it.

Cross-reference:
  The nbm_quantile_prob signal is the concrete case and is worth its own
  look regardless -- it is the only component measured that has resolution
  comparable to the market's (see the batch-53 replay findings recorded in
  the "IDR/EasyUQ AS A CALIBRATION CHALLENGER" entry). It should NOT be
  wired live on 26 rows; it should keep accumulating. Its data only starts
  2026-07-25 and it is skipped entirely on the METAR-locked path
  (weather_markets.py:14752).

  See also the cross_city_pooling precedent, which is exactly this failure
  mode having already happened once: an r=0.38 signal was wired live on
  2026-08-22, an opus review found a contamination path, and re-validating
  against the fix gave r=0.08 (n=35), sign agreement 51%. It was reverted.
  That signal used sample_floor=None, so the floor is not what let it
  through -- but the "looked good on a thin sample" shape is identical.

Why not now:
  Wants the replacement number derived rather than picked, and a decision on
  one-threshold-vs-two, which is a judgment call for the user.

When to revisit:
  Before any signal is wired live on the strength of a cleared floor. If
  that is about to happen, this entry is the blocker.

RESOLUTION 2026-08-26 (batch-81, both items):

  ITEM 1 -- the floor. sample_floor is now 112 on all ten entries that had
  20, via a named constant weather_markets.SIGNAL_GRADUATION_FLOOR whose
  derivation is recorded beside it (this entry's own closing ask). 20
  survives as weather_markets.SIGNAL_TRIPWIRE_FLOOR: reported, dimmed,
  labelled "above the 20 tripwire, not yet decisive", and firing no alert.
  That is this entry's own preferred option, chosen by the user over a
  single floor.

  Deriving 112. Re-solving the Hanley-McNeil table above (AUC 0.657, 9
  positives / 17 negatives, two-sided alpha=0.05) for 80% power: 112 is the
  smallest INTEGER n reaching it (power 80.4% at n=112, 79.7% at n=111).
  The continuous crossing is n=111.2; a sqrt(n)-scaling approximation of the
  same curve gives 112.45, which is the figure an earlier draft of this
  block quoted and then rounded DOWN -- the exact error the next paragraph
  criticises in the handoff. The integer solve is the one that matters and
  is what the test pins. The re-derivation reproduces this entry's own published
  SE/CI/power at n=26, 50, 100 and 200 to rounding, so the basis is the one
  this entry already established, not a new one. tests/
  test_batch81_signal_floors.py recomputes it from Hanley-McNeil rather
  than restating the number, and pins both bounds (n=112 reaches 80%,
  n=111 does not).

  Two numbers in the batch-81 handoff did NOT survive that re-derivation
  and are recorded here so they are not reintroduced. It proposed 86, back-
  solved from "n=20 -> 27% power" -- but this entry's 27% is at n=26 (the
  row count nbm_quantile_prob actually cleared on), not 20. And even on its
  own effect size the formula gives 86.52 taking its stated delta=0.3012
  at face value (86.50 from the unrounded back-solve) -- either way above
  86, so it was rounded the wrong way and buys 79.8% power, not the 80%
  claimed. On the corrected basis 86 is
  ~69% power. The floor of 20 this replaces bought 21.4%, not 27%.

  Caveat worth carrying: 0.657 is an observed point estimate on 26 rows, so
  it is optimistic. If a signal's true AUC is 0.62, 80% power needs n=198.
  112 makes the question answerable for a good signal; it does not promise
  a marginal one will resolve.

  Measured effect, 2026-08-26. Seven signals reported "floor cleared" in
  green under 20 -- run_trend (28), market_implied (78), gated_edge (89),
  nbm_quantile_prob (27), ecmwf_consensus_gap (77), gem_graduation (42),
  ukmo_graduation (42). Under 112, none do. Note the ordering flip that
  motivated the entry: nbm_quantile_prob, the signal that cleared the floor
  and fired the activation alert, was the second-furthest of all of them
  from being measurable. It looked ready because the bar was wrong.

  (The batch-81 handoff's own cost table was also wrong, in a way worth
  recording: its counts came from a query WITHOUT the settled_temp_f filter
  the registry actually applies -- it read gated_edge as 110 against a real
  89, and run_trend as 40 against a real 28. Re-derive registry counts by
  running count_settled_signal_rows, not by hand-writing a similar query.)

  ITEM 2 -- the population, which is the larger half. Every floor counted
  settled `predictions` rows: a population log_prediction only writes past
  the placement gate, so it structurally holds nothing below
  |forecast_prob - market_prob| = 0.0984. `analysis_attempts` holds every
  analysed market (measured minimum 0.0011) and accrues ~6-7x faster, but
  carried no signal values, so none of it reached a floor. (19.3 scored
  analysis_attempts rows/day against 2.93 settled predictions rows/day,
  each over a fully-settled 14-day window. Quote this as ~6-7x rather than
  the 6.59x the division gives: the two are measured on different date
  columns -- analyzed_at against the market date -- and across the
  fully-settled windows checked the ratio ran 6.2-7.3.)

  It does now: migration v79 adds analysis_attempts.signal_values, a JSON
  dict mirroring predictions.signal_values -- one column, no per-signal
  migration ever, and the generic a["signals"] path flows through it so a
  future log-only signal needs no wiring at all. Built by
  weather_markets.signal_values_from_analysis from values analyze_trade and
  the scan loop already computed, so no network call is added to a scan.
  run_trend is the one exclusion, and the painful one -- it is the slowest-
  accruing signal in the registry, and it is also the only one not on the
  analysis dict, fetched instead with up to 3 sequential HTTP calls per row.

  Projected accrual from zero at each signal's measured coverage:
  gated_edge 6 days to 112, ecmwf_consensus_gap 7, implied_mean 8,
  nbm_quantile_prob 17. On the biased population, the same from-zero
  measure over the same fully-settled window is 42 / 44 / 52 / 112 days
  (run_trend, which has no unbiased counterpart, is 121). So roughly a 6x
  compression -- graduation becomes a weekly question instead of a
  quarterly one.

  The two populations are reported side by side and NEVER summed --
  different settlement definitions (a settled temperature vs a resolved
  binary outcome), and analysis_attempts is a SUPERSET of the traded
  markets rather than their complement, so a pooled count would double-
  count every trade. `py main.py signals` prints them as separate
  "modelled:" and "unbiased:" lines and each fires its own alert naming its
  own population. A test mutation that pools them fails.

  Two implementation details that are load-bearing and easy to undo by
  accident. (a) The upsert merges the blob PER KEY via json_patch rather
  than replacing it: a market is re-analysed every scan and this table
  upserts on (ticker, target_date), and 366 of the 584 scored rows are
  days_out=0 -- where nbm_quantile_prob is skipped entirely on the METAR-
  locked path -- so wholesale overwrite would have erased most of exactly
  the signal that motivated this batch. (b) Because of (a) a row's values
  can come from different scans, so each value's lead time is stamped
  beside it under a reserved "_days_out" key. That cannot be retrofitted
  onto rows already written, which is why it ships with the column.

  Also: the activation-alert dedup key now embeds the floor value and the
  population (signal_<key>_floor112_predictions). It used to be
  signal_<key>_floor, which -- since _notify_feature_activation writes once
  per key and never overwrites -- would have let an alert fired at 20
  permanently suppress the alert at 112. The signal would have crossed the
  real floor in silence.

  Tests: 78 in tests/test_batch81_signal_floors.py, plus 4 new and 4
  rewritten in tests/test_p1_remaining.py's TestCmdSignals (4 -> 8), 1
  updated in tests/test_forecasting.py, and a _RAW_OUTCOMES_ALLOWLIST entry
  in tests/test_disputed_row_guard.py. The
  report-row fixture in tests/test_p1_remaining.py's TestCmdSignals was
  hand-listed and broke as a shape drift; it now derives the row from
  get_signal_graduation_report itself.

  Mutation testing: every production guard this batch adds was mutated
  individually and confirmed to break a named test. Three reviewers ran
  their own batteries on top of that (44 mutations in one case) and found
  two SURVIVORS, both since closed: the merge's NULL-stored-side guard --
  whose only real exercise is "first scan computed nothing, a later one
  did", an ordering no original test used -- and a registry entry
  hardcoding `sample_floor=112` instead of naming the constant, which a
  count-by-value assertion cannot see. Both now have tests. Recorded
  because an earlier draft of this block claimed "every causal claim
  mutation-tested", which was not true at the time it was written.

  WHAT THE REVIEWS CAUGHT. Three independent opus reviews (effort=high,
  scoped to item 1 / item 2 / the tests+records) returned 33 findings, no
  HIGH. All three independently re-derived the power table and the
  population measurements and reproduced them. The findings worth carrying
  forward, because each is a trap the next signal-logging change can fall
  into the same way:

  * The temperature and monthly-rain market-implied fits share ONE slot on
    the analysis dict -- implied_mean is degrees F for KXHIGH*/KXLOW* and
    INCHES for KXRAIN*M. `predictions` avoids pooling them only by
    accident: count_settled_signal_rows' require_settled_temp=True default
    excludes rain rows. This population has no settled_temp_f to filter on,
    so the first draft would have pooled 27 of 584 scored rows of inches
    into the temperature signal's graduation count -- reintroducing, one
    layer down, exactly the conflation this batch exists to remove. The fit
    is now written under implied_mean_rain, and `ticker` is a REQUIRED
    argument of signal_values_from_analysis so no future call site can
    silently pool them again.
  * ensemble_spread_f is 0.0, not None, on the METAR-locked same-day path,
    where there is no ensemble at all. Dropping only None let that sentinel
    overwrite a real longer-lead reading through the per-key merge AND
    stamp itself as a genuine same-day capture -- on the 63% of rows that
    are days_out=0. Now skipped when n_ensemble_members == 0.
  * NaN reaches the same "delete this key" outcome as an explicit null:
    json.dumps emits bare NaN by default and SQLite's JSON5 parser maps it
    to null. Fixed with allow_nan=False. The None-strip and the non-dict
    rejection also moved into tracker's _signal_values_json, so the module
    that owns the RFC 7396 merge owns its invariants rather than trusting
    callers.
  * json_patch raises on an unparseable STORED blob, and the batch writer
    is one executemany in one transaction -- so a single corrupt row would
    have rolled back a whole scan's attempt batch, losing analyzed_at /
    forecast_prob / market_prob / days_out / was_traded for 100+ markets.
    A json_valid() guard now costs that one row its blob instead.
  * The attempts count inherits no disputed-row filter (outcomes_valid is a
    join this query does not make), and tests/test_disputed_row_guard.py
    scans for `JOIN outcomes` so is structurally blind to it. Zero disputed
    rows exist today, so this was latent; the exclusion is now explicit,
    written as NOT EXISTS rather than a join so orphaned attempts -- the
    whole point of this population -- are not dropped.
  * A typo'd attempt_json_key would have failed silently forever, the exact
    hazard _count_model_obs' build-time validation already exists for.
    _validate_attempt_json_keys() now runs at module import.

  WHAT THE SECOND REVIEW ROUND CAUGHT, i.e. bugs the FIXES introduced.
  Worth recording separately, because this repo's workflow requires a fix
  round to get its own independent review for exactly this reason, and it
  paid for itself again:

  * The ensemble-sentinel guard was written as `n_ensemble_members == 0`,
    but _compute_ensemble_spread returns its 0.0 placeholder at
    `len(values) < 2`, and model_temps only ever holds "nbm" and "ecmwf" --
    so the domain is {0,1,2} and n=1 (one provider fetched, the other
    raised: a routine upstream hiccup) produced the identical placeholder
    and was NOT skipped. The first fix missed a third of its own domain.
    Now `>= 2`, failing closed on missing/None/bool, via a named constant
    tied to the producer's own threshold.
  * The activation alert had "selection-biased predictions" hard-coded per
    population slot, which is false for the four entries whose count_fn
    reads ensemble_member_scores or distinct city-months. The alert is
    write-once and persisted, and is read days later without the report's
    surrounding context -- so it is now a per-entry
    count_population_label. This was a REGRESSION the first fix round
    introduced: the pre-batch text was population-neutral.
  * The generic-path collision guard compared against `values` (what was
    actually collected) rather than the named-key namespace, so a named
    field that had legitimately been dropped -- including by the sentinel
    guard above -- left its slot open for a generic key to occupy, with no
    unit routing.
  * `test_cron_files_the_blob_under_the_key_the_writer_reads` was VACUOUS:
    it scanned every dict literal in cron.py for a "signals" key, and
    cron.py has a second, unrelated one for the web dashboard. Renaming the
    real key survived it. It now binds to the dict that lexically contains
    the builder call.
  * The _RAW_OUTCOMES_ALLOWLIST entry written for the dispute fix asserted
    that an inner join "would silently drop the majority of the sample".
    Measured: 0 of 584 scored attempt rows lack an outcomes row. The 494
    figure is rows with no PREDICTIONS row, which is a different
    orphanhood. It also claimed anti-joining outcomes_valid would read
    absence as "not disputed" when it in fact returns disputed-OR-absent,
    the inverse. Both rewritten -- an allowlist entry carrying a false
    measurement is worse than the failing test it silences.
  * `test_every_producible_key_is_countable` hand-recomputed the producible
    set instead of reading _ATTEMPT_PRODUCIBLE_KEYS, omitting the three
    "_rain" keys -- the ones carrying the entire unit-separation half of
    item 2 -- so dropping implied_mean_rain from the allowlist survived the
    whole suite.

  A pleasing consequence of that last dispute fix: adding the exclusion made
  tests/test_disputed_row_guard.py START failing, because its regex looks
  for `JOIN outcomes` / `FROM outcomes` and the query previously referenced
  no outcomes table at all. The guard was blind to this divergence for
  exactly as long as the divergence existed, and became able to see it only
  once it was fixed. It now carries a _RAW_OUTCOMES_ALLOWLIST entry that is
  the inverse of every other entry there: this query touches raw `outcomes`
  precisely IN ORDER TO exclude disputed rows, and cannot use
  outcomes_valid, because an attempt row need not have an outcomes row at
  all (an orphaned attempt is the unbiased population) and because a
  disputed ticker's absence from that view would read as "not disputed".

  Not in scope, deliberately: weather_markets._RAIN_GATE_MIN_SAMPLES is
  also 20 and rain_forecast_blend's floor used to be annotated as matching
  it. That constant gates whether rain markets may be TRADED at all, which
  is a different question from whether a log-only signal has enough
  evidence to graduate, and only the second is this entry's subject. The
  annotation is corrected in place rather than left asserting a match that
  no longer holds. Whether a live trading gate should also sit at n=20 is
  its own question and is NOT answered here.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-26 -- found while answering "how long until this could
  graduate to live trading?". The answer is dominated by one number, and
  this entry is that number. DRAINED 2026-08-26; see the RESOLUTION block at
  the end of this entry. The title's "NEVER SCORED" was true when filed and
  is now false -- 584 of 709 are scored. Kept verbatim for history.]
  SETTLE analysis_attempts.outcome -- THE
  UNBIASED EVALUATION POPULATION IS ALREADY BEING LOGGED AND NEVER SCORED,
  WHICH IS THE ONLY REAL LEVER ON THE GRADUATION TIMELINE
Priority: HIGH -- not a correctness bug; nothing is wrong in production.
  It is the binding constraint on ever being able to answer "does this
  model have an edge", and everything else on the roadmap is downstream of
  it. Cheap: one settlement sweep, no new data source, no trading change.
Files: tracker.py (settle_analysis_attempt ~8590-8615, get_unselected_bias's
  KNOWN LIMITATION docstring ~8621-8634, batch_log_analysis_attempts),
  cron.py (where the sweep would run), order_executor.py
  (_log_shadow_predictions ~3931, for why `predictions` is selection-biased)

Problem -- two facts that only matter together:

  (1) `predictions` is a selection-biased population. It is written by
      tracker.log_prediction(), and order_executor._log_shadow_predictions'
      own docstring states the rule: "_auto_place_trades normally calls
      tracker.log_prediction() only after a trade is actually placed", and
      the shadow mirror covers only opps that "would have been traded",
      applying "the same quality/dedup gates the real placement loop
      applies". So a row exists only if it cleared the full placement gate
      chain, including the edge floor.

      Measured consequence: across ALL 563 prediction rows, the minimum
      |our_prob - market_prob| is 0.0984. There is not one row below ~10pp.
      Every model-vs-market statistic this repo computes -- including
      get_model_vs_market_brier's headline -- is therefore computed on the
      high-conviction tail only, never on the full distribution.

      Note this makes get_model_vs_market_brier's own docstring caveat
      backwards. It warns the statistic "is unconditional on the SIZE of our
      disagreement with the price, so every market where we broadly agreed
      with the mid dilutes the statistic toward zero". There is no such
      dilution -- there are no low-disagreement rows at all. Worth fixing
      that comment when this lands.

  (2) The unbiased population IS already being captured, in
      `analysis_attempts` (ticker, city, condition, target_date,
      analyzed_at, forecast_prob, market_prob, days_out, was_traded,
      outcome). Live DB 2026-08-25: 695 rows, all 695 carrying both probs,
      minimum |forecast_prob - market_prob| = 0.0011, median 0.1507, with
      25.2% of rows below the 0.08 edge floor that `predictions` never sees.

      But only 84 of 695 have `outcome` populated -- and those 84 are
      exactly the rows that also have a predictions row. So the one table
      holding the unbiased sample is scored only on the biased subset.

  tracker.get_unselected_bias's docstring already documents this precisely
  ("this function currently reflects a selection-biased subset, not the full
  'markets we rejected' population its docstring implies") and names the
  fix: "a separate settlement sweep over analysis_attempts tickers lacking a
  predictions row". It was declined at the time on cost -- "~2,000 tickers
  on the live DB, i.e. ~2,000 extra Kalshi API calls per cron cycle" -- and
  because "this function has zero production callers today".

Both of those reasons no longer hold:

  - The cost figure is the wrong SHAPE. Settlement is once per ticker, not
    once per cron cycle: a settled market never needs re-fetching. Measured
    2026-08-25: 569 distinct tickers have no predictions row, of which 494
    are already past their target_date. So the real cost is a ONE-TIME
    ~494-call backfill plus roughly 22 calls/day steady state (measured:
    22.4 distinct tickers analysed per day over the last 30 days). That is
    a rounding error against the existing per-cycle API budget.
    (The "~2,000" figure was recorded 2026-07-10; the table's data now only
    starts 2026-07-25, so it appears to have been cleared or rebuilt since
    -- either way, re-measure before quoting either number.)

  - The reason to do it is no longer get_unselected_bias. It is that this
    is the ONLY lever on how long evaluation takes. Per-contract PnL has an
    irreducible sd of 0.4698 (binary outcomes near 47c), so at n=214 the
    minimum detectable edge is 9.0 cents/contract -- larger than any
    plausible real edge. Sample size needed, and calendar time at each rate:

        edge     n needed   at 3.5/day   at 22/day
        +5c          693        0.5 yr      0.09 yr
        +3c        1,923        1.5 yr      0.24 yr
        +2c        4,327        3.4 yr      0.54 yr
        +1c       17,306       13.5 yr      2.2 yr

    Current settled-scoring rate is 3.53 rows/day (342 settled rows over 97
    days). Settling analysis_attempts moves it to ~22/day -- a 6x
    improvement, turning a multi-year evaluation into a several-month one.

What the fix looks like:
  - A settlement sweep over analysis_attempts tickers with target_date in
    the past and outcome IS NULL, reusing the existing settlement machinery
    (audit_settlement / sync_outcomes' settlement block). One-time backfill
    command plus an incremental pass on the existing cron cadence.
  - Rate-limit/batch it like the other backfills; it is not latency-
    sensitive and can trickle.
  - Then re-run the model-vs-market comparison on the FULL population and
    compare against the tail-only number. They will differ, and the
    difference is itself the answer to "is our edge concentrated where we
    trade, or absent everywhere".
  - Fix get_model_vs_market_brier's dilution caveat while there.

Why not now / open questions:
  - Does audit_settlement work for a ticker with no predictions row? Check
    before assuming; it may key off predictions somewhere.
  - Some analysis_attempts rows have target_date NULL (see
    settle_analysis_attempt's two UPDATE branches) -- decide whether those
    are settleable at all.
  - Kalshi may not serve settlement for very old/delisted tickers; measure
    the hit rate on the 494 before assuming full recovery.

When to revisit:
  Before any further work aimed at proving or improving edge. Every such
  measurement is currently running on the biased tail at 3.5 rows/day, and
  this is the single change that fixes both properties at once.

RESOLUTION 2026-08-26 -- and the finding is that NO CODE WAS EVER NEEDED:
  The sweep was ALREADY BUILT and ALREADY RUNNING.
  tracker.settle_pending_attempt_tickers() is called from sync_outcomes()
  every cron cycle under ATTEMPT_SETTLE_CAP_PER_SYNC, with a one-time drain
  at `py main.py backfill-attempt-outcomes` (which defaults to a DRY RUN and
  needs --run). This entry, and the audit/DATA_ACCRUAL_PLAN.md written from
  it, both described it as work to be done. It was work being BLOCKED.

  What blocked it: a 41.4s clock skew (W32Time Stopped and Manual-start, RTC
  free-running ~0.35s/day over the 117.7 days since the last good sync, ~4ppm
  -- a healthy crystal, simply never corrected). Kalshi rejected the signed
  requests with header_timestamp_expired; five 401s tripped the SHARED

    01:07 UTC cron cycle   -> settled=25 skipped=0 failed=0

  THE POINT OF THE ENTRY IS NOW DELIVERED, and it is the unbiased half that
