[RESOLVED 2026-08-26 (batch-79 item 1) -- filed 2026-08-25 by batch-66 item 2 (surfaced by a round-2 opus review of that batch's own fix)] A standalone `py web.py` server never calls load_dotenv, so every env-derived constant in the dashboard process silently shows the CODE DEFAULT rather than the operator's configured value
Priority: Medium -- display-only today (the dashboard process places no
  autonomous trades), but it makes the console disagree with the bot about
  its own configuration, which is exactly the kind of thing an operator
  reads the console to check.
Files: web_app.py (no load_dotenv call; see the existing comment at the
  manual-order guard noting "standalone `py web.py` runs, which never call
  load_dotenv"), main.py (calls load_dotenv() at import, line 41), utils.py
  (every module-level `float(os.getenv(...))` constant), config.py.

Problem:
  main.py calls load_dotenv() before importing anything else, so any process
  launched through it sees .env. A standalone `py web.py` does not, and the
  constants are evaluated at IMPORT time, so the difference is frozen for the
  life of the process rather than being recoverable later.
  Concretely measured 2026-08-25: .env sets MIN_EDGE=0.15; in a standalone
  web_app process utils.MIN_EDGE is the 0.07 code default. Batch-66's new
  /api/analytics `required_gross_edge_curve` therefore renders a required
  gross edge about 2x too low in that process. That panel is only the symptom
  the review happened to catch -- the same skew applies to every
  os.getenv-derived constant the dashboard displays (STRONG_EDGE, MED_EDGE,
  KELLY_CAP, MAX_DAILY_SPEND, the KALSHI_* fee rates, and so on).
  Note this is NOT fixable by making individual readers late-binding: the
  constants are already frozen at import, so re-reading them per call reads
  the same frozen global. os.getenv() per call does not help either, because
  without load_dotenv the variable was never placed in os.environ at all.

What it would look like:
  Call load_dotenv() at the top of web_app.py (or in web.py before importing
  web_app), matching main.py. Cheap, but it changes the effective config of a
  running dashboard, so it wants a deliberate check of which constants would
  move and whether any of them feed a write path (the dashboard DOES have
  manual-order endpoints -- confirm those are unaffected or intentionally
  affected before flipping it).

Why not now:
  Batch-66 owns analytics query functions and one taker-fee gate, not the web
  server's process bootstrap. Changing which config a live dashboard process
  loads is a behaviour change across every env-derived constant at once, and
  deserves its own scoped verification rather than riding along with an
  analytics batch. Batch-66 corrected the false docstring that claimed late
  binding solved this, and left the underlying gap documented here.

Resolution (2026-08-26, batch-79 item 1):
  web_app.py now calls load_dotenv() immediately after its third-party
  imports and BEFORE its first local import (`from paths import ...`, which
  carries a `# noqa: E402` naming the reason), matching main.py:41's
  convention. utils.py's stale cross-reference in
  effective_min_edge_threshold's docstring was rewritten to point at the fix
  instead of at this entry.

  Two corrections to this entry's own premises, both verified against live
  code before designing anything:

  (a) THERE IS NO web.py, and there never has been -- `git log --all --
      web.py` is empty and the name appears nowhere outside backlog/audit
      prose. The standalone entry point is web_app.py's own `__main__` block
      at the bottom of the file. (An earlier draft of this note cited
      "web_app.py:4713"; that was wrong -- the block was at :4710 in the
      pre-change file and moves with every edit above it, so no line number
      is cited here.) That block used to build a bare KalshiClient() -- no
      key_id, no private_key_path, env defaulting to "demo" -- described in
      its own comment as "read-only paper mode". Review of this change found
      that description had stopped being true; see the MEDIUM-2 entry in the
      review section below for what it now does instead.

  (b) config.py does NOT bind credentials as module constants at import.
      Its fields are `field(default_factory=lambda: os.getenv(...))`,
      evaluated when a BotConfig is CONSTRUCTED. The real freeze is
      get_config()'s `_CONFIG` singleton, which caches the first
      construction for the process lifetime. Measured in an isolated child
      (project_root() redirected): after get_config() then load_dotenv(),
      cfg.kalshi_env is still 'demo' while .env sets prod. The practical
      consequence is identical -- ordering, not the presence of the call,
      decides -- but the mechanism matters for where the call has to go.

  What actually happened on a standalone run, which is worse than this entry
  describes and is why "display-only" understated it: _build_app()'s auth
  gate reads DASHBOARD_PASSWORD, which is itself env-derived, and raises
  RuntimeError("DASHBOARD_PASSWORD must be set") when it is unset. So
  `python web_app.py` did not render stale numbers -- it never started at
  all, unless DASHBOARD_UNPROTECTED=true was set in the real OS environment.
  Confirmed both ways in an isolated child: _build_app(None) raises without
  .env and returns a Flask app with it.

  The measured delta, produced by diffing every uppercase utils constant and
  every BotConfig field across two child processes (one with load_dotenv,
  one without) rather than by reading .env: EXACTLY 15 constants move, 9
  distinct settings --
    utils.MIN_EDGE / config.min_edge                 0.07  -> 0.15
    utils.MAX_DAYS_OUT / config.max_days_out         5     -> 3
    utils.MAX_DAILY_SPEND / config.max_daily_spend   500.0 -> 200.0
    utils.MAX_SAME_DAY_SPEND / .max_same_day_spend   500.0 -> 400.0
    utils.BREAKEVEN_TRIGGER_PCT / config.*           0.30  -> 0.75
    utils.DASHBOARD_PASSWORD / config.*              ''    -> (set)
    config.kalshi_env                                demo  -> prod
    config.kalshi_key_id                             ''    -> (set)
    config.kalshi_private_key_path                   ''    -> (set)
  This entry's guess at the affected set (STRONG_EDGE, MED_EDGE, KELLY_CAP,
  the KALSHI_* fee rates) was wrong in both directions. Those four are not
  set in .env, so they were already reading their code defaults in BOTH

  config are not the whole process. Counting the modules the dashboard
  imports lazily, the review measured at least 24 module-level constants
  across 5 modules and 13 distinct settings: the 15 above plus alerts'

  Write paths, per this entry's own request to confirm them: the manual
  paper-order endpoint builds its market-lookup client from
  os.getenv("KALSHI_ENV", "demo"), so it now points at prod rather than
  demo. That is intentionally affected -- it is what `py main.py web` (the
  supported launch path, which has always had .env loaded) already did, and
  the fail-closed guard below it is unchanged. The stale comment at that
  guard, which cited `py web.py` as a cause of empty env keys, was rewritten.

  Why the call sits where it does, and how that is protected. `import
  web_app` pulls in exactly paths + safe_io at module scope; utils and config
  are imported lazily inside functions, i.e. strictly after load_dotenv().
  tests/test_web_app.py::TestStandaloneDotenvBootstrap (6 tests) pins the
  whole chain in CHILD processes, because the pytest process has already
  frozen every constant via conftest importing main:
    - a value set in the child's .env reaches utils.MIN_EDGE, parametrized
      over two different configured values (0.42, 0.31), neither of them the
      code default, so a pass cannot come from a constant or a leaked .env;
    - importing utils BEFORE web_app leaves MIN_EDGE at 0.07 while
      os.environ carries 0.42 -- the positive control proving the .env WAS
      read and that ordering alone is what does the work;
    - _build_app returns a Flask app with a configured DASHBOARD_PASSWORD,
      and still refuses when one is genuinely unset (paired control, so a
      future "fix" that weakens the auth gate instead of loading .env fails);
    - `import web_app` adds exactly {paths, safe_io, web_app} to sys.modules
      and no other local module (completeness: this is what makes the fix
      cover EVERY moved constant, not just the asserted ones), with an
      `after` assertion proving the probe can see local modules when they
      are imported. Asserted as the whole set difference rather than an
      allowlist of names -- an earlier version checked only utils and
      config, and would have stayed green if someone added a module-scope
      `import weather_markets` above load_dotenv();
    - the startup gate fails CLOSED in the utils-first ordering (MEDIUM-1);
    - the __main__ block's client matches the configured environment
      (MEDIUM-2).
  Env keys under test are scrubbed from the child's inherited environment --
  load_dotenv() does not override an already-set variable, so an inherited
  value would silently make an assertion measure the operator's real config.
  That is not theoretical: the MEDIUM-2 test initially passed while reading
  the operator's REAL KALSHI_KEY_ID, and only failed once the assertion got
  specific enough to notice. KALSHI_ENV / KALSHI_KEY_ID /
  KALSHI_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH joined the scrub set as a result.
  Mutation-tested via Edit revert, four separately: removing load_dotenv()
  fails 5 of the value-carrying tests; reverting the gate to os.getenv fails
  the fail-closed test; reverting the client to a bare KalshiClient() fails
  the parity test. The module-scope probe stays green under the load_dotenv
  mutation by design and its docstring says so -- it is a sufficiency
  tripwire, not a guard on the call.

  THREE INDEPENDENT OPUS REVIEWS (effort:high, one per subsystem) ran against
  the finished diff. Every finding was addressed; the two that changed
  behaviour:

  MEDIUM-1, a fail-OPEN auth path this change would have created. _build_app's
  startup gate read os.getenv("DASHBOARD_PASSWORD") while _check_auth enforces
  utils.DASHBOARD_PASSWORD, which utils freezes at import. Those are the same
  value only if utils is imported after web_app. In the other ordering,
  load_dotenv() fills os.environ so the gate PASSES -- silently, since the
  DASHBOARD_UNPROTECTED branch is not taken either, so nothing is logged --
  while the auth hook sees "" and its `if not pwd: return None` opens every
  route. The reviewer reproduced an unauthenticated POST /api/halt returning
  200, i.e. the kill switch. No in-repo caller has that ordering today, which
  is precisely why it needed a test. The gate now reads the same constant the
  hook enforces, so the two cannot disagree at all; DASHBOARD_UNPROTECTED
  stays an os.getenv read (deliberate operator escape hatch, no frozen
  counterpart, consulted only after the password is already empty).

  MEDIUM-2, the standalone process was left half-configured. The __main__
  block built a bare KalshiClient() -- demo, no credentials -- while the two
  manual-order endpoints build their own from os.getenv("KALSHI_ENV"), which
  after this change resolves to prod, and /api/status's is_live (same env var)
  painted a red "LIVE" badge over demo market data. The panels and the order
  path disagreed about which exchange they were looking at. Confirmed with
  the user, then fixed by building the client exactly as main.build_client()
  does, so `python web_app.py` and `py main.py web` are one process. This is
  not new live-order exposure: web_app.py places no orders at all (both
  inline clients only call get_market), the server binds 127.0.0.1, and every
  route sits behind the password plus the X-Requested-With CSRF check.

  Also from the reviews, non-behavioural: the "15 constants" figure scoped to
  utils+config with the wider 24-across-5-modules set recorded (MEDIUM-3);
  the completeness tripwire rewritten as a sys.modules set-difference so it
  cannot stay green when a future module-scope import of weather_markets /
  alerts / order_executor / ml_bias lands above load_dotenv() (MEDIUM-4);

[RESOLVED 2026-08-26 (batch-79 item 2) -- found 2026-08-25 during a new-PC
  migration audit, while working out which files a fresh clone would and
  would not carry.] `git restore .` OR
  `git checkout -- data/` SILENTLY RESETS FIVE LEARNED-CALIBRATION FILES TO
  THEIR UNCALIBRATED SEED VALUES, WITH NO WARNING AND NO ERROR
Priority: Medium -- destroys learned model state, but only when someone runs
  a broad git-restore command in the main clone. No automated path does it.
  Filed because the hazard is completely invisible: the command succeeds,
  exits 0, prints nothing, and the bot keeps running on defaults.
Files: .gitignore (`data/` at :9), calibration.py (writes city_weights,
  condition_weights, seasonal_weights), ml_bias.py + web_app.py (write
  temperature_scale), ml_bias.py + main.py (~:8590, write
  metar_lockout_calibration), paths.py (the five *_PATH constants)

Problem:
  `data/` is gitignored (.gitignore:9), but five files inside it were
  force-added and are TRACKED:

    data/city_weights.json
    data/condition_weights.json
    data/metar_lockout_calibration.json
    data/seasonal_weights.json
    data/temperature_scale.json

  All five are also WRITTEN BY THE BOT AT RUNTIME -- calibration.py writes
  three, ml_bias.py/web_app.py write temperature_scale, ml_bias.py/main.py
  write metar_lockout_calibration. So they are simultaneously version-
  controlled source AND live mutable state.

  Three consequences, in increasing order of severity:

  1. Every calibration run dirties the working tree. `git status` in the main
     clone shows a modified data/*.json more or less permanently, which
     trains everyone to ignore it -- including in the moment when it matters.

  2. A fresh clone starts UNCALIBRATED. The committed copies are neutral
     seeds. Measured 2026-08-25, data/seasonal_weights.json summer weights:

       committed : ensemble 0.3333  climatology 0.3333  nws 0.3333
       live      : ensemble 0.8793  climatology 0.0016  nws 0.1191

     The seed pattern itself looks deliberate and is defensible --
     calibration.py sets "_uncalibrated": true and _blend_weights checks that
     flag, so the code can tell a seed from a learned file. That is not the
     bug.

  3. THE BUG: `git restore .`, `git checkout -- .`, `git checkout -- data/`
     or `git reset --hard` in the main clone rewrites all five back to seeds.
     Git reports success. Nothing logs it. The bot's next run silently blends
     with uniform 1/3 weights instead of the learned ones, and the only
     evidence is a "_uncalibrated": true flag nobody is looking at.

     This is a realistic command to run: the working tree is chronically
     dirty (see 1), so "clean up the repo before pulling" is exactly the
     reflex that triggers it. It nearly happened during this session's own
     fast-forward of the main clone -- three files needed restoring and
     `git restore .` would have been the natural command; the files were
     named individually only because seasonal_weights.json was known to be
     dirty at that moment.

  Note the asymmetry that makes it worse: only seasonal_weights.json is
  currently diverged from HEAD. The other four match, so a restore looks and
  feels harmless right up until the run that has just recalibrated them.

What the fix looks like (pick one; this is a judgment call, not an obvious
  bug-swat):
  (a) Untrack all five (`git rm --cached`), and ship the seeds under
      different names (e.g. `defaults/seasonal_weights.seed.json`) that the
      loader copies in on first run when the live file is absent. Removes the
      hazard entirely and stops the working tree being permanently dirty.
      Costs a loader change and a first-run path per file.
  (b) Keep them tracked but add a pre-restore guard -- e.g. a git hook, or a
      `make safe-restore` that stashes data/ first. Cheap, but a hook cannot
      catch `git checkout -- data/` reliably and does nothing for a fresh
      clone's uncalibrated start.
  (c) Document only: a comment at each writer and a line in the README's
      graduation section. Zero risk, does not remove the hazard.

  (a) is the real fix. It also removes consequence 1 and 2, which (b) and (c)
  leave in place.

Also fix regardless of which option is taken:
  The migration procedure now depends on restore ORDER -- clone first (brings
  seeds), THEN copy the bundle's data/ over it (brings learned values). Doing
  it the other way silently discards the learned state. That ordering is
  currently only implicit in migrate_backup.py's closing instructions and
  should be stated explicitly, since getting it backwards produces no error.

Why not now:
  (a) needs a first-run-seed path designed per file and a decision about
  where the seeds live. Not hard, but it touches five loaders and wants doing
  once, properly.

When to revisit:
  Before the machine move if convenient -- the restore-order trap is live
  during exactly that operation. Otherwise, next time anyone touches
  calibration.py's write path.

Resolution (2026-08-26, batch-79 item 2): option (a), as this entry
  recommends. Confirmed with the user before implementing, since the entry
  correctly framed "where do the seeds live" as the open question.

  All five files are untracked (`git rm --cached`; `git ls-files data/` is
  now empty). Their fresh-clone copies live in a new tracked seeds/ directory
  with a README documenting each file's writer and reader.
  paths.materialize_missing_seeds() copies a seed into data/ only when data/
  does not already have that file, and is called once at import.

  Why paths.py rather than a per-loader first-run path, which is what this
  entry assumed the cost would be ("touches five loaders"): it does not have
  to touch any of them. Every module that READS one of the five reaches
  paths.py at module scope (calibration.py, ml_bias.py, weather_markets.py
  and web_app.py all do `from paths import ...`), so one call there covers
  every reader, including the two furthest away --
  weather_markets._load_metar_calibration and ml_bias's temperature-scale
  reader. (An earlier draft claimed "every entry point in the project"
  reaches paths.py. That is false and the review caught it: backlog_index.py
  and migrate_backup.py import paths not at all. Neither reads calibration,
  so the coverage that matters is over READERS, not entry points -- but the
  claim as written was wrong, and it was the sole stated justification for
  the placement.) All five loaders ALREADY return {} or
  None for a missing file, so nothing needed a new absent-file branch; the
  degraded outcome of this function doing nothing is an already-supported
  state, which is why every failure in it is per-file and swallowed.

  Creation is ATOMIC: a temp file in data/, fsync'd, then os.link() onto the
  target. The first implementation used open(dst, "xb") + write, which is
  exclusive but NOT atomic, and the review showed the gap is not academic --
  the file exists from the moment of open(), so a crash between open() and
  close() leaves a zero-length or partial data/*.json that is NEVER repaired,
  because materialization does not overwrite. Reproduced: an empty
  city_weights.json stays empty forever and load_city_weights() returns {}
  behind a log warning, i.e. permanent silent uncalibrated operation -- the
  same failure class this entry exists to remove, reintroduced by its own
  fix. A concurrent reader could also observe the half-written file in that
  window. os.link raises FileExistsError when the target already exists, so
  it supplies the exclusivity AND the atomicity in one step and the target
  only ever appears fully-formed. Verified on NTFS and on both CI runners
  (ubuntu-latest, windows-latest).

  The catch is `Exception`, not `OSError`. tests/prod_data_guard.py raises
  ProdDataWriteError, which derives from RuntimeError: if the guard were ever
  armed before `import paths` (a `-p` plugin's module scope does run that
  early, and this repo already uses that pattern), an OSError-only catch
  would fail the entire suite at COLLECTION rather than reporting one
  violation. Not reachable today -- verified that conftest imports main, and
  therefore paths, before pytest_configure() installs the guard -- and
  conftest's pytest_configure docstring now records that the ordering is
  load-bearing for five file creations, not just one idempotent mkdir.

  The one-time landing step, verified in a throwaway repo rather than assumed.
  git removes a previously-tracked path from the working tree on checkout, so
  the merge that lands this commit does touch data/. Two cases, both safe:
    - file identical to HEAD (4 of the 5 today): removed, then recreated
      byte-identically from seeds/ by the next process that imports paths.py;
    - file diverged (seasonal_weights.json today, whose summer weights are
      really learned): git REFUSES the merge -- "error: Your local changes to
      the following files would be overwritten by merge". It fails loudly
      rather than deleting anything.
  LIVE_TRADING_RUNBOOK.md gained a "Rolling back code without rolling back
  calibration" section carrying that procedure.

  "Also fix regardless of which option is taken" (the migrate_backup.py
  restore-ORDER trap): option (a) removes the trap rather than needing it
  documented. The clone now brings no data/ files at all, and seeds only ever
  fill in an ABSENT file, so a seed can never overwrite a value from the
  backup bundle whichever is put down first. migrate_backup.py's step 2 now
  says exactly that, including what the old behaviour was.

  ONE CONTENT REPAIR, not a byte-for-byte copy, and not a new judgment call.
  seeds/seasonal_weights.json's "summer" entry gained the
  "_uncalibrated": true flag its three siblings already carried. This is
  batch-37 item 5(a)'s own fix applied to the copy that predates it:
  _best_weights' brier-improvement-gate rejection path used to return uniform
  1/3 weights WITHOUT the flag, commit fa183f65 committed exactly that output
  for summer, and batch-37 fixed the code path on 2026-08-24 after confirming
  the LIVE file had self-healed -- so no data repair looked needed. The git
  blob still held the pre-fix output, and that blob is what would have become
  this seed. Left as found, it tells weather_markets._blend_weights that
  summer IS calibrated at uniform weights, suppressing the hardcoded days-out
  schedule for every summer trade on a fresh clone. (Generalizes the
  "a source fix leaves frozen copies stale" pattern.) The other four seeds
  are byte-identical to their committed blobs, verified by git hash-object.

  Tests: tests/test_paths.py, new, 13 tests. Copy-when-absent; NEVER
  overwrite an existing file (with a positive control in the same test
  proving the call is not simply inert); all five copied; absent seeds/ and
  unwritable data/ are silent no-ops; seeds/ holds exactly the declared
  filenames and each is valid JSON; the declared names match the five path
  constants the loaders actually open; every uniform weight entry carries
  _uncalibrated (with a positive control that the flag and the uniform shape
  travel together, so the scan is not skipping every entry vacuously);
  import-time materialization seeds a fresh clone, with a seedless-clone
  control proving the files come from seeds/ and not from anywhere else; and
  `git ls-files data/` is empty, with a `git ls-files seeds/` positive
  control so an empty result cannot mean "git returned nothing". The
  import-time tests use a child process rather than importlib.reload(paths),
  which would rebind DATA_DIR for the rest of the pytest session and re-run
  materialization against the REAL data/ on the way back out.

  Mutation-tested via Edit revert, three separately: "xb" -> "wb" fails the
  never-overwrite test; removing the import-time call fails the fresh-clone
  test; `git add -f data/city_weights.json` fails the tracking test.

  Consequences 1 and 2 from the problem statement are gone with it: the
  working tree is no longer permanently dirty from calibration runs, and a
  fresh clone still starts from the same seeds it always did.

  Docstring corrections made necessary by the untracking:
  tests/prod_data_guard.py, tests/test_prod_data_guard.py (including a test
  method still NAMED ...tracked_production_file...) and
  tests/test_schema_validator.py (two places) all described these as "tracked"
  or "currently-tracked" data/*.json files. All now say the files are seeded
  from seeds/ instead. README.md's project-layout block gained seeds/ and a
  note that nothing under data/ is tracked. (tests/conftest.py:635's claim
  that temperature_scale.json "is not git-tracked" was FALSE when written and
  is now true -- fixed for free, left alone.)

  REVIEW FINDINGS (independent opus review, effort:high). Beyond the atomicity
  and exception-breadth fixes recorded above:

  The runbook procedure as first written was itself dangerous, which is a poor
  look for a durability fix. It copied ONE file to %TEMP%, then ran
  `git checkout --` on it with no check that the copy had succeeded -- and the
  block is fenced ```cmd while this repo's sessions run PowerShell, where
  %TEMP% does not expand, so step 1 could fail silently while step 2 destroyed
  the only copy. It also hardcoded seasonal_weights.json although git's abort
  message lists EVERY diverged file. Worst, its stated verification ("git
  ls-files data/ prints nothing, and all five files are present") PASSES in
  the exact failure case: skip the copy-back and the seed re-materializes, so
  both checks succeed while the learned values are gone -- the very silent
  reversion this entry is about. Rewritten to back up the whole directory
  first, require the operator to confirm the listing before deleting
  anything, and verify by CONTENT (fc against the backup; a seeded
  seasonal_weights.json has every season at 0.3333 with "_uncalibrated").

  migrate_backup.py's new note claimed "order no longer matters" because
  materialize_missing_seeds() never overwrites. That reasoning is wrong --
  step 2 is a manual file copy by the operator, which the never-overwrite
  property does not touch at all. What actually makes it safe is only that
  the clone brings no data/ files; run ANY entry point between clone and copy
  and the seeds materialize, turning the copy into an overwrite prompt whose
  decline silently keeps the seed. The note now states that precondition
  instead of the false mechanism.

  Test additions/corrections: a test pinning
  _SEEDED_FILENAMES is a subset of main._PERMANENT_DATA_FILES. That invariant
  already held, but it CHANGED MEANING with this commit -- before, cleanup_
  data_dir() deleting a calibration file meant "uncalibrated until the next
  fit"; now it means "silently restored to the frozen seed on the next
  import", and metar_lockout_calibration.json's seed is real fitted
  coefficients that pass _load_metar_calibration's validity gates and would
  reach live pricing. The uniform-weights test was rewritten to derive its
  file list from _SEEDED_FILENAMES rather than hardcoding a pair: one of the
  two named files is literally {} so that arm was entirely vacuous, and the
  list omitted condition_weights.json even though _blend_weights' tier 2
  applies the same _uncalibrated semantics. It now also asserts how many
  weight vectors it actually scanned, so it cannot pass by skipping
  everything. Deriving the list also means the files batch-82 plans to add
  are covered without anyone extending it; seeds/README.md documents the
  two-step process for adding one.

  Documented, not changed: from a worktree, SEEDS_DIR resolves through
  safe_io.project_root() to the MAIN CLONE, so materialization is a silent
  no-op in a worktree until this lands on master. That is consistent with how
  DATA_DIR already behaves and is deliberate; tests/test_paths.py now says so
  where it uses the worktree's own seeds/ for content assertions and a
  redirected child for the runtime path.

[OPEN 2026-08-25 -- surfaced while answering "how do we get more data faster".
  Full reasoning and the measured tables live in audit/DATA_ACCRUAL_PLAN.md.]
  EVERY SAMPLE-COUNT FLOOR SHOULD BE AUDITED FOR WHICH QUESTION IT GATES --
  CALIBRATION IS ~16x CHEAPER TO ANSWER THAN EDGE AND MAY ALREADY BE ANSWERED
Priority: Medium -- nothing is broken; this is unspent time. Cheapest item on
  the whole accrual list, and it needs measurement rather than new machinery.
Files: the floors themselves -- weather_markets.py (_SignalRegistryEntry
  sample_floor, _hourly_gates_active), tracker.py (get_dynamic_station_bias's
  min_samples=10, STATION_BIAS_MIN_SAMPLES/BRIER_POLICY_MIN_SAMPLES),
  ml_bias.py (EMOS/T-scaling training floors), paper.py (_method_kelly_
  multiplier's min_samples)

Problem:
  The two questions this bot asks have wildly different sample costs, because
  they use estimators with wildly different variance:

    question              estimator            sd       n for effect
    is it calibrated?     forecast error, F    2.889    262  (0.5F)
    does it beat market?  realized PnL, $/ct   0.4698   4,331 (2c)

  (Two-sided 95% + 80% power. The PnL column reproduces the existing
  "SETTLE analysis_attempts.outcome" entry's 693/1,925/4,331/17,323 table
  exactly, which is how the convention was confirmed.)

  Measured on the live DB 2026-08-25: on 208 clean ensemble rows a 0.56F bias
  is already detectable, and 1.0F needs only n=66. On 321 settled rows the
  smallest detectable edge is 7.3c/contract -- larger than any plausible real
  edge, and batch-66 measured skill NEGATIVE anyway.

  So any floor that gates a CALIBRATION decision (station bias, sigma, EMOS,
  per-city offsets) behind a PnL-sized n is costing calendar time for no
  statistical reason. Nobody has checked which floors are in that category.

Plan:
  1. Enumerate every sample-count floor and classify what each one gates:
     a calibration statistic (F, continuous, cheap) or a P&L/skill statistic
     (binary, expensive).
  2. For the calibration ones, re-derive the floor from the actual variance of
     the quantity being estimated and the effect size worth acting on, instead
     of a round number.
  3. Do NOT touch floors gating live-money skill claims -- those are correctly
     expensive, and are the only thing between a negative-skill model and real
     orders.
  4. Anything re-floored needs its own before/after note; a floor that drops
     is a claim that the old one was measuring the wrong thing, and should
     read that way in the diff.

Why not now:
  Wants doing deliberately with the user, one floor at a time -- several of
  these are live gates, and "lower the floor" is exactly the move that looks
  like progress while removing a safety property.


[OPEN 2026-08-25 -- same origin; see audit/DATA_ACCRUAL_PLAN.md.]
  A ONE-OFF previous-runs-api BACKFILL WOULD ~4x CALIBRATION RESOLUTION
  IMMEDIATELY, AND THE ARCHIVE WINDOW CANNOT BE BOUGHT RETROACTIVELY
Priority: Medium -- the one-off half is a large, immediate gain with no
  waiting; the daily-harvest half is low-urgency but its cost compounds the
  longer it is deferred.
Files: backtest.py (_PREV_RUN_MODELS and the previous-runs-api call site,
  grep `previous-runs-api`), tracker.py (wherever the pairs would land),
  acis_temps.py / metar.py (ground truth)

Problem / opportunity:
  backtest.py already reads archived forecasts from
  previous-runs-api.open-meteo.com. Over 21 cities x 2 vars, a single backfill
  across the available window yields roughly:

    window        pairs    smallest detectable bias
    today (live)    208    0.561F
    past_days=41  ~1,722   0.195F
    past_days=92   ~3,864  0.130F

  i.e. a ~4x improvement in calibration resolution available with NO waiting.
  Ground truth is already reachable via ACIS/METAR, both already used here.

  Three constraints, all real and all already documented in this repo:
  - temperature_2m_previous_day0 is NOT a real field (silently ignored), so
    the minimum reconstructable lead is previous_day1 (~24h). This cannot
    reconstruct a same-day 15Z decision.
  - The API exposes whole-day run offsets only, not intraday run selection.
  - It measures the DETERMINISTIC 3-model blend, a different estimator from
    the live ensemble mean. Usable for station bias (largely estimator-
    independent) and sigma; NOT a substitute for measuring the live blend.
    Same caveat as batch-75's model_forecast_temp_f column.

  The second half: the window is bounded, so history beyond it cannot be
  bought retroactively at any price. Storing previous_day1 daily costs almost
  nothing and in a year yields an archive nothing can reconstruct later.

Plan:
  1. VERIFY the real past_days ceiling first. The existing call site passes
     max(41, days_out + 2), which is evidence of that caller's needs, not of
     the API's limit. Every number above scales off this.
  2. One-off backfill into a table that records the ESTIMATOR alongside the
     value, so these pairs can never be silently pooled with live-blend rows
     (the exact confusion batch-75 existed to remove).
  3. Re-derive station bias and sigma on the enlarged sample; compare against
     the live-blend figures rather than replacing them.
  4. Separately decide whether to harvest daily going forward.

Why not now:
  Step 1 is a live API probe and step 2 is a schema decision; both want doing
  deliberately. Also genuinely lower priority than settling analysis_attempts,
  which fixes the SELECTION BIAS this does not touch -- a bigger sample of the
  same biased population answers a different question than an unbiased one.

RESOLVED 2026-08-25:
  1. block_outbound_network, a new autouse conftest fixture, default-denies
     every outbound call for every test at two chokepoints:
       - requests.adapters.HTTPAdapter.send -- one patch covering every
         module-level requests.get and all ~13 requests.Session() singletons,
         and the only layer that still knows the URL. Patching the adapter
         class rather than each session means a new module is covered the day
         it is written.
       - socket.socket.connect/connect_ex -- for callers that never touch
         requests (notify.py's urllib.request posts, kalshi_ws.py's
         websocket). Loopback stays open so a test with its own local server
         still works.
     The error names the URL, the leaking test's nodeid, the both-bindings
     rule and the opt-out. BlockedNetworkCall derives from BaseException, not
     Exception, deliberately: nearly every fetch here sits inside
     "try/except Exception: log-and-continue", and this entry's own 2026-08-07
     predecessor already recorded that a raise-on-call stub "falsely passes
     even with a mock removed" for exactly that reason.
     Opt in with @pytest.mark.allow_network (registered in pyproject); the
     pre-existing "integration" marker is honoured too.

  2. weather_markets.py no longer imports get_live_observation into its own
     namespace -- "import nws" plus nws.get_live_observation(...) at both call
     sites (section 5 and _compute_persistence_prob), so there is exactly one
     patchable target. 34 test sites retargeted from
     "weather_markets.get_live_observation" to "nws.get_live_observation";
     5 of them were patching both and became duplicates, removed.
     No production behaviour change.

  3. Two more suite-wide conftest defaults, both for unconditional cron-cycle
     side effects that no cmd_cron test mocked and that only leak on a cold
     cache -- i.e. always, on CI:

Independent review: two opus effort=high agents, scoped by subsystem (core
  mechanism / the test-file fixes), 25 findings between them, all addressed.
  The four that changed the design:
    - The guard was a function-scoped autouse fixture on the shared
      `monkeypatch`. Autouse fixtures order ALPHABETICALLY, not by definition
      order, so anything sorting ahead of it would have set up unguarded; and
      three tests call monkeypatch.undo() mid-body (test_backtest.py:393,
      test_batch64_forward_writers.py:1426, test_settlement_monitor.py:68),
      which reverts every setattr recorded so far and stripped the guard for
      the rest of those tests -- reproduced. Now installed once on a
      SESSION-scoped pytest.MonkeyPatch, with a function-scoped fixture that
      lifts it for @pytest.mark.allow_network / integration. Both are pinned
      by tests.
    - A BaseException still cannot fail a test if it is raised inside a plain
      threading.Thread target: pytest turns that into
      PytestUnhandledThreadExceptionWarning and the test PASSES. main.py's
      auto_settle/auto_backtest threads and kalshi_ws.py's reader all qualify,
      as does the one deliberate `except BaseException` in test code. Added a
      pytest_runtest_makereport hook that fails any passing test which
      recorded a block, plus expect_blocked_network() for the guard's own
      tests to acknowledge a block they provoked on purpose. Deliberately NOT
      done by promoting that warning to an error suite-wide:
      test_live_execution.py already emits one from plyer's Windows
      balloon-tip backend, which is a separately filed bug in another file.
      Also narrowed test_state_consistency.py:132's `except BaseException` to
      `except SystemExit`, which is all it ever needed.
    - The HURDAT2 test (test_hurricane_markets.py) was left blocked with a
      cache-only stub. data/ is gitignored, so on CI that turned a real

      repo that genuinely needs the network (its docstring explains why a

      pytest.skip(...)` escape. With every input pinned, the only remaining

      temperature_adjustment patches were also aimed only at the source

  Smaller ones, all fixed: a false historical claim in the ExitStack docstring

[RESOLVED 2026-08-26 -- filed as adjacency from the default-deny network
  guard above (that entry's scope was one name, get_live_observation), and
  done as its own change immediately after.]
  weather_markets.py RE-EXPORTED SIX NAMES FROM OTHER MODULES, SO EACH ONE HAD
  TWO PATCHABLE BINDINGS THAT COULD DISAGREE
Priority: Low -- the default-deny guard now catches the consequence loudly
  (a mis-aimed patch fails the test naming the URL) instead of silently
  serving live data. This is about removing the trap, not about a live bug.
Files: weather_markets.py:26-30 (the import block), plus the test sites listed
  below. No production behaviour would change.

Problem:
  weather_markets.py binds these at import:

    from climate_indices import get_enso_index, temperature_adjustment
    from climatology import climatological_prob
    from nws import fetch_nbm_forecast, nws_prob, obs_prob

  Each creates a second object. monkeypatching the SOURCE module
  ("nws.nws_prob") does not rebind weather_markets' copy, and vice versa, so
  the same name resolves two different ways depending on which call site runs
  -- exactly the trap that made df7cd97f's two HRRR tests fetch NYC's real
  temperature. get_live_observation was removed from this list by the entry
  above; these six were left.

  Two of them are already being patched inconsistently across the suite, which
  is how a future instance would arrive (counts measured 2026-08-25):

    nws_prob               47 sites patch weather_markets.nws_prob,
                            5 patch nws.nws_prob
    temperature_adjustment 45 sites patch weather_markets.…,
                            5 patch climate_indices.…
    climatological_prob    40 sites patch weather_markets.…,
                            5 patch climatology.…
    get_enso_index          8 sites, all weather_markets.…
    fetch_nbm_forecast      5 sites, all weather_markets.…
    obs_prob                2 sites, all weather_markets.…

  Two of the source-module-only sites (in test_gaussian_prob.py) were found by
  the new guard mid-fix: they patched nws.nws_prob and
  climate_indices.temperature_adjustment only, and analyze_trade's own call
  sites went to api.weather.gov and www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov anyway. Fixed there
  by patching both bindings, which is the workaround this entry would delete.

What the fix looks like:
  Same shape as the get_live_observation change: drop each name from its
  "from X import" line, keep/add "import X", call it as X.name(...) at each
  production call site, then retarget the test patches to the source module.
  monkeypatch.setattr and patch.object both raise on a missing attribute, so
  every stale test site fails loudly rather than silently no-opping -- the
  churn is mechanical, just wide (about 150 test sites in total).

Why not now:
  Wide but shallow, and it wants doing per-name with the affected files' tests
  re-run each time, not as one 150-site sweep. Also genuinely optional now
  that the guard makes the failure mode loud.

When to revisit:
  Next time one of these six is at the centre of a flaky-test investigation,
  or if the guard surfaces a third instance of the same trap.

  ONE `if result is None: pytest.skip(...)` TRAPDOOR LEFT IN

Priority: Medium -- these are not flaky-and-occasionally-skipped. All four skip

  4 skipped, always the same four), so the assertions below them have not

Files: tests/test_weather_markets.py:1205, :4467, :4499, :4543.

Problem:
  Each site calls analyze_trade(), and when it returns None -- which a gate
  firing also produces -- calls pytest.skip() instead of failing. So the test
  reports "skipped" in exactly the situation it exists to catch, and CI stays

  body then asserts the P0-14 fix (entry_side_edge > 0 for a valid NO,
  recommended_side == "no"). That body is dead code right now. P0-14 was a

Resolution (2026-08-26, batch-83) -- the fourth site is fixed:
  TestAdjustedEdgeInAnalyzeTrade::test_analyze_trade_returns_adjusted_edge_key.

  The gate was days_out, and this one was worse than its three siblings. They
  targeted today+5, which the operator's own .env (MAX_DAYS_OUT=3) rejected
  locally but CI's default of 5 admitted -- so they at least ran on CI. This
  one targeted today+10, which EXCEEDS EVERY CONFIGURATION THIS REPO HAS: 10 >
  5 (utils.py:460 default, what CI uses) and 10 > 3 (the operator's .env). Its
  assertions had therefore never executed anywhere, on any machine, since the
  test was written.

  Three defects were behind the skip, all invisible while it skipped:
    1. days_out=10, above every MAX_DAYS_OUT. Now parametrised over 2 and 3,
       with wm.MAX_DAYS_OUT pinned to 5 in the test so neither case depends on
       the operator's .env -- reading it live is what made this a permanent
       skip in the first place.
    2. `"temps": [72.0] * 50` -- all members identical, which trips the
       daily_degenerate_ens gate on its own. Same defect the YES sibling had.
       Now 10 members at 72.0 and 10 at 68.0, straddling the T70 threshold, so
       ens_prob lands near the 0.36 market mid and stays inside the 0.25
       model_mkt_gap gate.
    3. The assertion called `wm.edge_confidence(10)` with NO condition_type,
       and the comment above it claimed days_out came from datetime.now(UTC).
       Both wrong: analyze_trade builds _local_today from ZoneInfo(city)
       (weather_markets.py:14863), and edge_confidence takes a condition_type
       whose real value here is "above".

  WHY TWO PARAMETRISED CASES rather than one. edge_confidence's horizon is a
  flat 1.00 for days_out <= 2, and _CONDITION_CONFIDENCE["above"] is also
  1.00, so a single case at days_out=2 asserts `factor == 1.0` -- which a
  hardcoded 1.0, or a factor wired to nothing, satisfies just as well. This
  was caught by mutation-testing rather than by reasoning: the first repair
  used only days_out=2 and a guessed condition_type of "high_temp", and both
  the guess and the value were vacuous because every path returns 1.0.
  days_out=3 is the first value off the plateau (0.96).

  Mutation-tested, via the Edit tool, with weather_markets.py verified
  byte-identical to HEAD (git hash-object) after each revert:
    * horizon flattened (`elif days_out <= 7: horizon = 1.0`): the [3-0.96]
      case fails 1.0 != 0.96; the [2-1.0] case still PASSES, which is the
      direct evidence that one case would not have been enough.
    * factor not applied (`adjusted_edge = net_edge`, all 10 assignment
      sites): the adjusted_edge == net_edge * factor assertion fails on
      [3-0.96]. A first attempt at this mutation matched only 8 of the 10
      sites and SURVIVED -- the Edit tool's "found 8 matches" error is what
      surfaced the discrepancy; a string-replace script would have reported
      success and left the survivor looking like a vacuous test.

  Also added: an `assert result is not None, f"gate counts: {...}"` carrying
  get_gate_counts(), so a future gate regression names the gate instead of
  skipping, and an assertion tying adjusted_edge to net_edge * factor -- #63's
  actual claim, which key-presence alone never tested.

  tests/test_weather_markets.py now has ZERO pytest.skip() CALL sites,
  verified by an AST walk rather than by grep -- `grep -c pytest.skip` on that
  file still returns 1, because the new test's own docstring names the pattern
  it replaced. A grep would have been satisfied by that prose either way,
  which is the same file-wide-scan trap this repo has hit before.
  Scoped regression: see the batch-83 commit message.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-26 (batch-77) -- observed live in the 00:28 UTC cron run, whose log shows
  the whole cascade end to end. Found while analysing that run line by line.]
  ONE SHARED 'kalshi_api_read' CIRCUIT BREAKER LETS AUTH FAILURES ON PRIVATE
  ENDPOINTS DISABLE PUBLIC MARKET-DATA READS -- WHICH SILENTLY LEAVES EVERY
  OPEN POSITION WITHOUT STOP-LOSS PROTECTION
Priority: HIGH -- this is a risk-control path. On the observed run it left
  8 of 8 open positions unprotected for a full cycle, and the trigger was a
  fault that could not have affected the endpoint it disabled.
Files: kalshi_client.py (:93 the single CircuitBreaker(name="kalshi_api_read",
  failure_threshold=5); :588 _get(auth=False|True) -- both routes share it;
  :732 get_market public; :1088 get_balance authenticated),
  paper.py (:1998-2030 the stop-loss quote loop and its M-1 warning)

Problem:
  kalshi_client.py declares ONE circuit breaker for every read, and _get()
  routes both authenticated and unauthenticated calls through it. So a fault
  that only affects PRIVATE endpoints trips the breaker for PUBLIC ones.

  Observed 2026-08-26 00:28 UTC. A 41s clock skew (W32Time was stopped and
  Manual, ~0.35s/day RTC drift over 118 days) made Kalshi reject signed
  requests:
    401 ... /portfolio/positions      <- authenticated
    401 ... /portfolio/balance  x6    <- authenticated
    Circuit 'kalshi_api_read' OPEN after 5 failures
  and then, for the rest of the cycle:
    get_unrealized_pnl_paper: ticker <8 tickers> failed: Circuit open
    [StopLoss] got a usable quote for 0/8 open position(s) this cycle -- the
      rest fall back to entry_price and are effectively unprotected
    sync_outcomes: failed to fetch/record <~48 tickers>: Circuit open
    sync_outcomes: analysis_attempts sweep settled=0 skipped=0 failed=25
    check_fee_change call failed: Circuit open

  The critical part: paper.py's stop-loss loop calls client.get_market(),
  which is PUBLIC (_get with auth=False, no signature). A clock skew CANNOT
  make that endpoint 401. It was disabled purely because it shares a breaker
  with the portfolio endpoints that did fail. With no quote, every position
  falls back to entry_price -- unrealized P&L reads 0.00, so no stop can ever
  trigger.

  The M-1 WARNING at paper.py:2028 is working exactly as designed and is how
  this was caught -- the problem is not visibility, it is that a WARNING is
  the only consequence of losing price-based protection on every open
  position.

  Compounding: the breaker's 60s recovery_timeout never elapses inside one
  cron cycle (this one ran 00:28:28-00:32:49, and the breaker opened at
  00:32:39), so once it opens the entire remainder of the cycle is degraded.

Plan (design decision, wants the user):
  1. SPLIT the breaker at minimum into public-read vs authenticated-read.
     An auth fault must not be able to disable unauthenticated market data.
     Check every _get(auth=...) call site when doing this.
  2. Consider not counting 401 toward the breaker at all: a 401 is a
     credential/clock fault, not the overload condition a breaker exists to
     protect against. Retrying will not fix it and backing off does not help
     -- it needs a different signal entirely.
  3. Decide what SHOULD happen when stop-loss cannot price a position. Silent
     fallback to entry_price is the least safe option available: it reports
     "no loss" precisely when the bot is blind. Candidates: refuse to open new
     positions while blind, escalate past WARNING, or treat an unpriceable
     position as at-risk rather than at-breakeven.
  4. A startup/periodic clock-skew assertion against a server Date header
     would have caught the root cause before any of this. Note the machine is
     used intermittently -- it was powered off May-August -- so the check
     belongs at STARTUP, where a long shutdown shows up as a large offset.

When to revisit:
  Before live trading. In paper mode this costs simulated money; the same
  cascade with LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED leaves real positions unprotected, and
  the same run's banner read "REAL MONEY TRADES ENABLED".

RESOLUTION 2026-08-26 (batch-77) -- all four options shipped, and the entry's
  own stated REASON was wrong while its conclusion was right:

  THE REASON, CORRECTED. This entry (and batch-77.md) said get_market() is
  "PUBLIC (_get with auth=False, no signature)". It is not: kalshi_client.py
  passes auth=True on every market-data read, since 18997527 (2026-04-13,
  "Add auth=True to public market endpoints that now require
  authentication"). The only auth=False call site in the whole file is
  get_live_weather_index. A second session traced the same fact and drew the
  natural inference -- signed, therefore the skew would have 401'd it
  directly, therefore splitting the breaker fixes nothing. That inference is
  ALSO wrong.

  What settled it was data/predictions.db's api_requests table (method,
  endpoint, status_code, latency_ms, logged_at) -- written by
  _request_with_retry itself. Over the incident window 00:28:00-00:33:00 UTC:
      /markets*     83 requests -> 83x 200
      /portfolio*    8 requests ->  8x 401
  interleaved inside 484ms of one process on one expired timestamp:
      00:32:39.187  401  /portfolio/balance
      00:32:39.236  200  /markets/KXHIGHTHOU-26AUG24-T99
      00:32:39.274  200  /markets/KXLOWTSEA-26AUG24-T56
      00:32:39.315  200  /markets/KXLOWTDAL-26AUG24-T85
      00:32:39.403  200  /markets/KXLOWTPHIL-26AUG25-T64
      00:32:39.486-.671  401 x5  /portfolio/balance   <- breaker opens
      (nothing at all until 01:01:29, the next process)
  Kalshi ignores an expired KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP on market data and
  enforces it only on /portfolio/. Those four 200s ARE the stop-loss quote
  fetches; they were succeeding until the breaker opened 268ms later and
  stopped only because it opened. So the collateral-damage diagnosis holds
  and the breaker split IS the main fix -- the entry was right for a reason
  it did not state.

  GENERAL LESSON, worth more than this entry: api_requests answers "what did
  the exchange actually do" and no amount of source reading can. Two sessions
  independently reasoned from code to a wrong conclusion about a remote
  service's behaviour. Start there for any API incident.

  HOW THE 401s REACHED THE BREAKER. Not the status-code branch --
  `_is_failure = status >= 500` already exempted 4xx (since 39e08a6d,
  refined by 555bf1e0). The bypass was check_error_body, whose guard was
  `if not _is_failure`, i.e. every non-5xx, while its own docstring said "a
  200 response". Confirmed live rather than deduced: GET /portfolio/balance
  with a deliberately stale KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP (no real credentials)
  returns
      401  {"error":{"code":"header_timestamp_expired",
                     "message":"header timestamp expired"}}
  -- a top-level "error" key, so _is_failure flipped to True and the
  documented exemption two lines above was defeated. That literal is now the
  test fixture.

  WHAT SHIPPED
  1. Breaker split by PATH PREFIX (not by the auth kwarg, which would have
     protected only get_live_weather_index): _kalshi_cb_private_read for
     /portfolio/*, _kalshi_cb_read for market data, _kalshi_cb_write for
     writes. _select_breaker(method, url) checks host, then method, then the
     marker. A non-Kalshi host gets NO breaker -- weather_markets' Pirate
     Weather fetch imports this same helper and has its own _pirate_cb, so
     the two were cross-contaminating in both directions (a Pirate 5xx
     counted against Kalshi's read breaker; an open Kalshi breaker raised
     into Pirate's except and became a _pirate_cb failure).
  2. check_error_body gated to 2xx only, matching its own contract. A 4xx now
     records NEITHER failure nor success -- it used to record_success(),
     which zeroed an in-progress 5xx streak, so an outage interleaved with
     auth errors could never reach failure_threshold. EXCEPT 429, which trips
     like a 5xx: that is the exemption's own reasoning applied honestly (a
     401 is exempt because backing off cannot fix a credential fault; 429 is
     exactly where backing off IS the remedy).
     Separately, 401/403 DO count as failures -- but only on
     _kalshi_cb_private_read, never on the public or write breakers. Decided
     explicitly after the reviews: backing off still cannot fix a credential
     fault, but it stops the hammering, and _resolve_live_balance caches only
     successes so without it a skew emits ~60 futile 401s per cycle forever.
     The old shared breaker capped the observed incident at 6 -- at the cost
     of taking market data down too. This keeps the cap and drops the cost,
     which is only safe BECAUSE of the split above. Verified nothing catches
     CircuitOpenError by type, so the changed exception is transparent to
     callers. The signal that actually diagnoses the fault is the clock-skew
     probe, not the breaker.
  3. Stop-loss/daily-loss blindness is no longer indistinguishable from
     breakeven. get_unrealized_pnl_paper returns n_open/n_markable/blind;
     is_daily_loss_halted(client) FAILS CLOSED when open positions exist and
     none can be marked, with its own alert (cooldown_key
     "daily_loss_blind") because every caller otherwise renders a True as
     "Daily loss limit reached ($0.00 incl. MTM)". check_paper_position_exits
     escalates a 0-of-N cycle to ERROR + alert. Exits are NOT gated:
     pre_live_exit_check deliberately excludes is_daily_loss_halted.
  4. Startup clock-skew probe: one unauthenticated GET /exchange/status,
     Date-header comparison over the round-trip INTERVAL (a slow response can
     only shrink reported skew, never manufacture it), once per process, only
     when a private key is loaded. ERROR + alert past 15s; never blocks,
     never raises.

  NOTE ON THE ENTRY'S OWN WORDING: "every position falls back to entry_price"
  was also imprecise. check_stop_losses gets None from liquidation_price and
  `continue`s -- the position is SKIPPED. The entry_price fallback only sets
  the exit price after a stop has already fired. Same net effect (no stop can
  trigger), different fix surface. The $0.00 came from get_unrealized_pnl_paper,
  which likewise `continue`s -- and that value feeds the daily-loss placement
  gate, so the bot kept ENTERING while blind. That second gate was not in the
  entry at all.

  FOUR ROUNDS OF OPUS REVIEW, and rounds 2 caught more than round 1:
  - A 4xx recording nothing STRANDED a HALF-OPEN probe forever (_half_open is
    cleared only inside record_failure/record_success). Fixed with a new
    CircuitBreaker.record_reachable(): closes iff it was the probe, no-op
    otherwise. Both halves mutation-tested separately.
  - The test helper's importlib.reload leaked paper's _LOSS_OVERRIDE_PATH to
    the REAL data/ -- the same leak backlog L24334 and batch-62 each fixed
    once before. is_daily_loss_halted short-circuits on that file, so the
    regression guard for a risk-control path would have inverted for a whole
    UTC day whenever the operator used reset_daily_loss_limit(). The
    prod-data guard cannot catch it (it does not count Path.exists()).
  - `blind` counted positions whose market had already CLOSED, so one stuck
    unsettled position would halt every new entry permanently. Live at the
    time of writing: 3 of 8 open trades (247/248/249, close_time 2026-08-25)
    were already past close. Now only markable positions count; a missing or
    unparseable close_time still counts, so an empty-close_time ledger cannot
    mask a real outage.
  - has_quote (mid > 0) and liquidation_price (rejects a 0 side) disagreed,
    so a one-sided overnight book read as "1/1 priced" while the stop was
    inoperative and nothing above DEBUG said so.
  - _kalshi_cb_private_read was missing from conftest's hand-maintained
    breaker-reset list -- the EIGHTH time that loop's own docstring records
    the missed-until-added pattern. Added, plus an introspective anti-drift
    test so a ninth is caught automatically.
  - 429 both never tripped the breaker and CLOSED an overload-opened one via
    the probe. Reproduced, then fixed (see 2).

  TESTS: +76 (test_kalshi_client 106 -> 150, test_paper 178 -> 208,
  test_circuit_breaker_registry 10 -> 12), counts re-derived at the moment of
  writing. Scoped run across 30 files: 1647 passed, 1 pre-existing error
  (test_live_execution's plyer balloon-tip thread writing data/crash.log --
  reproduced identically on unmodified origin/master, so not from this
  change). Randomized-order run clean. 21 mutations applied via the Edit tool
  and every one caught, including the 8 that a round-2 reviewer demonstrated
  were surviving (the trailing-slash argument, parsed.path vs raw URL, the
  host-check ordering, the skew attempt bound, the retry-on-unmeasurable
  rule, the no-retry skew session, the 5s timeout, and the naive-tz guard).

  STILL OPEN, deliberately, and filed separately rather than stretched into
  this batch:
  - Nothing monitors any Kalshi breaker. /api/circuit-status and cron's
    newly-opened-circuit alerter both derive from
    weather_markets.CIRCUIT_BREAKERS, which holds only weather sources, so an
    open kalshi_api_read/_private_read/_write produces no dashboard row and
    no alert -- a log line is the only signal. Pre-existing, but this batch
    adds a third such breaker and it gates the daily-loss inputs.
  - main.py's unrealized panel reads "total_unrealized_pnl"/"unrealized_pnl";
    the real keys are total_unrealized/mark_pnl, so it has always printed
    $0.00. Pre-existing and in a file this batch does not own.
  - In `main.py loop`/web_app.py the clock-skew probe's retry path is nearly
    dead: one client is built at startup and reused, so a single failed probe
    means no check for that process's life. A periodic re-check would close
    it; the root cause (W32Time stopped) is an OS-level fix.
  - positions.liquidation_price guards ask == 0 but not ask == 1.0, so a NO
    position on a yes_ask=1.0 book returns 0.0 rather than None and would be
    closed at $0.00. Pre-existing; this batch now leans on that function as
    the definition of "protectable", so it inherits the gap.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-26 (batch-83) -- the harness and the script-facing arming
  entry point both shipped; see the resolution at the end of this entry. The
  bulk migration of the 24 older scripts is deliberately NOT included and is
  filed as its own entry below.]
  audit/reproductions/ SCRIPTS RUN OUTSIDE PYTEST AND SO
  BYPASS EVERY TEST GUARD -- THEY NEED AN ISOLATION CONVENTION OF THEIR OWN
Priority: Medium -- no known active damage, and the one incident that
  motivated it has self-healed and been separately fixed at its own site. This
  closes the last structural hole rather than a live bug.
Files: audit/reproductions/*.py (~10+ standalone scripts), tests/conftest.py
  and tests/prod_data_guard.py (the guards that do NOT cover them),
  safe_io.project_root(), paths.py

Why this is the remaining hole:
  Two guards now protect the suite -- 3cca1e8e default-denies outbound network
  for every test, and 27949ffa blocks any test write to the real data/ dir.
  Both hook pytest. A script executed directly (`py audit/reproductions/x.py`)
  loads neither, so it inherits the real project_root(), the real data/ and
  unrestricted network.

  This is not hypothetical. On 2026-08-25/26 a MagicMock repr was persisted
  into data/miami_index_state.json as the stored config_version, and the next
  real cron cycle read it back, diffed it against the live value and fired
  kalshi_weather_index's red "Miami settlement methodology may have changed"
  alert via notify.send_system_alert. Miami is the ONLY settlement source for
  KXTEMPMIAH, so a test artifact burned a real operator alert on a live
  settlement guard -- and, worse than the false positive, it overwrote the
  BASELINE the guard diffs against, so a genuine methodology change in that
  window would have been indistinguishable from the artifact.

  That specific path is now fixed (conftest patches
  kalshi_weather_index._STATE_PATH, commit 2aa04bc3) and the suite is measured
  hermetic (10,324-file snapshot across 205 cmd_cron tests, zero diffs, twice).
  So the pytest side is closed. What is not closed is the out-of-pytest side.

  Attribution, as far as three sessions could take it: NO production module
  imports unittest.mock -- verified repo-wide; the only non-test hits are a
  docstring in order_executor.py and two scripts under audit/reproductions/.
  So main.py's ~70 subcommands are EXONERATED as the source: they cannot
  produce a MagicMock. The vector is code that imports unittest.mock, run
  outside pytest. The two reproductions scripts that do import it
  (repro_target_date_due.py, test_csrf_header_gap_repro.py) were checked and
  touch none of the affected paths, so they are not the source either -- but
  they are the SHAPE of thing that can be.

The distinction that must survive into any fix:
  Writing data/ outside pytest is CORRECT and intended -- it is what ~70
  main.py operator subcommands exist to do (repair-metar-lockout-rows,
  backfill-attempt-outcomes, backfill-ensemble-var all wrote real data this
  session, deliberately). A guard built on "no out-of-pytest write to data/"
  would break the maintenance tooling it is meant to protect. The defect is
  narrower: TEST-OR-MOCK-IMPORTING code executing outside pytest against the
  real data dir.

Plan:
  1. A convention, documented at the top of audit/reproductions/ (a README or
     a shared helper): any script there must redirect safe_io.project_root()
     or the specific paths.py constant it touches BEFORE importing anything
     that binds it. At least one script already does this correctly --
     cron_lock_race_repro.py redirects cron.LOCK_PATH to a tempdir -- so this
     is codifying existing good practice, not inventing it.
  2. Prefer a shared import-first helper over per-script discipline, e.g.
     `from audit.reproductions._isolate import isolate_all` as line 1. Per
     -script discipline is what failed here.
  3. When auditing which constant a script must redirect, the answer is a
     (consumer, binding-site, import-timing) triple, NOT a per-constant
     verdict: `from paths import X` at module scope needs the IMPORTER's
     binding patched, a call-time `from paths import X` inside a function
     needs paths.X, and a module doing both needs both. A name-match of
     paths.py constants against conftest text cannot see the first case --
     that error was made and retracted during this investigation.
  4. Optionally make an out-of-pytest write to data/ VISIBLE (logged) rather
     than blocked, so the legitimate operator commands stay working while an
     unexpected writer is attributable next time. Attribution was the thing
     three sessions could not do.

When to revisit:
  Next time anyone adds a script to audit/reproductions/, or before running
  any existing one against the main clone.

Resolution (2026-08-26, batch-83) -- plan items 1, 2 and 4 implemented:

  1. tests/prod_data_guard.arm_for_script(data_dir=None, *, mode, label) is a
     script-facing entry point. install() was reachable only from conftest, so
     until now the guard protected the test runner -- the LEAST dangerous
     caller -- and nothing else. data_dir defaults to the real data dir and is
     resolved AT ARM TIME, so a caller that subsequently redirects
     project_root() still has the guard aimed at production rather than at its
     own sandbox.

  2. audit/reproductions/_isolate.py + a README. `isolate()` is line 1 of a
     script; it puts the repo root on sys.path, redirects
     safe_io.project_root() to a fresh temp dir, and arms the guard in BLOCK
     mode against the real data/. Run as
     `python -m audit.reproductions.<name>`. audit/__init__.py and
     audit/reproductions/__init__.py make that import work; pyproject pins
     testpaths=["tests"], so pytest still does not collect anything here.

  4. AUDIT mode, which is the half the original plan cared most about and the
     reason this is not simply "block everything". This entry's own
     "distinction that must survive into any fix" is honoured exactly:
     `isolate(allow_real_data=True)` redirects NOTHING and arms the guard in
     AUDIT mode, so the ~70 main.py operator subcommands that legitimately
     write real data/ keep working, while every mutation is printed with the
     script and pid that made it. Attribution was the thing three sessions
     could not do; it is now a two-line change to any script.

  MEASURED, not argued. With the guard armed in BLOCK mode against the real
  data dir, a bare `import main` from a plain script -- no script body at all
  -- attempts:
      open(mode='wb')  <repo>/data/.city_weights.json.seed-<pid>.tmp
      Path.unlink      <repo>/data/.city_weights.json.seed-<pid>.tmp
  That is paths.py resolving DATA_DIR at import time and then calling
  materialize_missing_seeds(). It is the same mechanism by which
  `py main.py validate` applied schema migrations v77 and v78 to the
  production database on 2026-08-26. Under isolate() the same import is clean.

  isolate() REFUSES if paths or safe_io is already imported, rather than
  redirecting after the constants are bound and reporting success -- a silent
  no-op there is precisely the failure this harness exists to prevent.

  Two safety properties, both tested: an already-armed BLOCK guard can never
  be downgraded to AUDIT (otherwise any imported helper could disarm the
  suite's own guard for every test after it), and uninstall() resets the mode.
  install() cannot select AUDIT at all.

  DISCLOSED GAP: isolate() does not block network. The default-deny guard is a
  pytest fixture in tests/conftest.py, not a reusable module, so there is
  nothing to arm without extracting it first. Documented in the README and in
  _isolate.py's docstring rather than left as a silent hole.

  Tests: tests/test_repro_isolate.py (5) and
  tests/test_prod_data_guard.py::TestArmForScript (5). Both behavioural sets
  run a real SUBPROCESS -- install() is idempotent and conftest has already
  armed this process in BLOCK mode, so an in-process test of AUDIT mode would
  be testing the early-return, not the mode. No test points the guard at the
  real data dir in AUDIT mode; they arm it against a tmp_path standing in for
  data/, so the mode that lets writes THROUGH writes only into tmp_path.

  Mutation-tested: removing the arm_for_script() call from isolate() must fail
  test_isolate_blocks_a_write_to_the_real_data_dir. The first version of that
  test read the target directory out of the guard's own _data_prefixes and so
  died with an IndexError when unarmed -- red, but for the wrong reason, and
  without ever attempting the write it claims to test. It now takes the target
  from the parent process instead, and under the same mutation the probe file
  really does land in the real data/ (confirmed, then deleted).

  OPUS REVIEW (effort high) -- 2 HIGH, 5 MEDIUM, 9 LOW, 6 INFO, all addressed:
    * HIGH x2, and the most valuable finding in the batch: .pre-commit-config
      .yaml sets `exclude: ^audit/` on ruff, ruff-format AND mypy, but
      .github/workflows/ci.yml runs bare `ruff check .` and `mypy .` with NO
      exclusion. So the new _isolate.py was unlinted locally and linted on CI.
      Both would have turned CI red before a single test ran: an I001 import
      sort, and "Cannot infer type of lambda" on the project_root override.
      Fixed (a def replaces the lambda); CI's own two commands now verified
      directly rather than via the hook that cannot see the file.
    * MED-1: the allow_real_data branch returned _REPO_ROOT (the worktree)
      rather than project_root() (the main clone). An operator-style script
      would have written a throwaway worktree data/ while the guard, armed on
      the main clone, stayed silent -- and that silence reads as "nothing was
      written". Exactly the stale-worktree-data class paths.py exists to
      prevent, reintroduced inside the harness meant to prevent it.
    * MED-2/MED-3/LOW-1/LOW-2, all in arm_for_script's mode handling, fixed
      together: a second arm can no longer silently discard a different
      data_dir (it raises), AUDIT is refused outright once BLOCK has been
      armed via a latch that deliberately survives uninstall(), and
      set_current_test() is no longer called on an already-armed guard (it
      sweeps pending violations into _orphaned, which conftest only PRINTS --
      so the new API was a way to launder a swallowed write past
      assert_clean()). Four new subprocess tests cover the tighten-allowed,
      loosen-refused, cannot-re-point and no-laundering cases.
    * MED-4: the sandbox had no seeds/, so every calibration loader fell back
      to "uncalibrated" and a repro of any calibration-dependent bug would
      have quietly exercised the wrong path and looked unreproducible.
      seeds/ is now copied in.
    * MED-5, LOW-5/6/9: docstrings that overstated what the code does --
      _repo_root_on_sys_path cannot make the repo root importable from
      nothing, one test's docstring claimed a positive control it did not
      contain, and the too-late rule omitted its allow_real_data exception.
    * LOW-3/LOW-4: AUDIT mode had unbounded memory and stderr for its stated
      use case (an operator backfill rewrites hundreds of files), and

      one phrasing accurate under both modes.
    * LOW-7: fixing this one introduced a bug and the fix had to be redone.
      The obvious cleanup -- unlink the probe after asserting -- is itself
      blocked by the guard, so assert_clean failed the test on the CLEANUP.
      The probe name is now unique per run instead, which neither bypasses the
      guard nor lets one regression poison every later run.
    * INFO-5: conftest.pytest_sessionfinish now asserts the session ended in
      BLOCK mode, so the outcome is checked rather than the mechanisms trusted.
    * INFO-1 was the one finding REJECTED, on evidence. The reviewer said 16
      scripts carry the dead worktree path, "one of the 17 grep hits being

    * INFO-2/3/4 accepted as documented no-ops: nothing in production arms the
      guard yet (main.py is batch-82's file this cycle, and the follow-up

  SECOND OPUS REVIEW, of the round-1 FIXES (the workflow requires this, and it
  earned its keep: 1 HIGH, 4 MEDIUM and 4 LOW were bugs the round-1 fixes
  THEMSELVES introduced, none of which re-checking the round-1 findings would
  have surfaced). All addressed:
    * A1 HIGH -- the AUDIT de-duplication I added keyed on (operation, path)
      alone, so once ANY writer touched a file a later writer of the same file
      was completely silent. That is this module's own motivating incident
      exactly: a legitimate cron write to data/miami_index_state.json followed
      by a MagicMock repr to the same path -- the second being the one worth
      seeing. A cap meant to stop attribution drowning in noise had instead
      destroyed the attribution. The key now includes nodeid and thread, and
      repeats are COUNTED ("x47") rather than discarded.
    * A2/A4 MEDIUM, both fail-OPEN -- install() early-returned BEFORE latching
      BLOCK and never validated its data_dir, so anything arming AUDIT before
      pytest_configure left conftest's install() a no-op and ran the whole
      session permissive AGAINST THE WRONG DIRECTORY with the latch still
      False; and arm_for_script assigned _mode before install() could raise,
      leaving mode=AUDIT with nothing patched for conftest to then inherit.
      install() now forces BLOCK unless called from arm_for_script, validates
      the directory on every call, and arm_for_script commits the mode only
      after install() returns.
    * A3 MEDIUM -- the pytest_sessionfinish assert I added as INFO-5 destroyed
      the entire run report. Raising there propagates out of wrap_session's
      finally, so TerminalReporter's post-yield half never runs: no pass/fail
      line, no short summary, no traceback for whatever actually failed, and
      on CI no coverage report and no --cov-fail-under evaluation -- at exit
      code 1, indistinguishable from an ordinary failure. Now prints and sets
      session.exitstatus = INTERNAL_ERROR, which wrap_session honours. (An
      assert would also have vanished under `python -O`.)
    * A5/A6/A7/A9/A10 -- _audit_seen was the one unbounded structure and was

    * A8 -- the new fixture's NOTE claimed importing main at conftest module
      scope would be harmful. conftest ALREADY does exactly that at line 31,

    * B1 MEDIUM, and a pre-existing suite-wide leak this batch happened to

      That fix then broke tests/test_ml_bias.py's
      test_directional_bias_warning_labels_global_and_condition, which asserts

    * B2/B3/B4/B7 -- the ratio assertion was vacuous at net_edge == 0 (now

    * B5/B6/B8 recorded as scope notes in the test's own comments: the

    * A11/A12/A13/A14/A15/A16 accepted as documented no-ops or corrections:
      the cap counts a list shared with BLOCK entries; the mode/latch globals
      are mutated outside _lock (single-threaded at arm time); the
      "pytest" in basetemp assertion matches existing precedent in
      test_conftest_tracker_db_isolation.py; _block() does NOT in fact run on
      every open() (only on a real-data hit, so AUDIT adds no per-open cost,
      and the BLOCK path was verified byte-for-byte unchanged); the seeds

[RESOLVED 2026-08-26 by batch-84 item 2 -- originally OPEN 2026-08-26,

  Two things the fix hardened beyond the entry's ask:
  - The dotenv import is wrapped in try/except ImportError with a no-op
    fallback (opus L-1). Without it, a broken venv would make cron.py's
    `from watchdog import update_heartbeat` -- which sits inside a bare
    try/except -- silently stop writing the heartbeat, and the watchdog

    "pip install -r requirements.txt" guard for this; watchdog.py had none.
  - Windows stdout is reconfigured to UTF-8 as main.py:16-19 does. The
    no-topic fallback print()s a message containing U+2014, so `py
    watchdog.py > log.txt` would have raised UnicodeEncodeError inside the
    very branch that exists to say the bot is down.

  because conftest imports main (which calls load_dotenv at import), so

  environment (before is None, after is the .env value); an already-set
  variable beats the file; the source position of the call precedes the
  first local import; and the module's import-scope local-module set stays
  within {watchdog, paths, safe_io}.

  now read, `NTFY_TOPIC=` (the shape you get by uncommenting
  .env.example:60 and deleting the placeholder) yields "" rather than None.
  send_alert's `if not topic` already handles it, but mutating that to `if
  topic is None` left all eight tests green, and the resulting behaviour is
  a dead man's switch POSTing to the bare https://ntfy.sh/ root and logging

  an HTTP-error response must not be logged as a delivered alert (deleting
