[RESOLVED 2026-08-26 by batch-84 item 1 -- originally OPEN 2026-08-25,
  filed by batch-80 item 2 while fixing the 256-char truncation in the same
  function]
  NOTIFY.PY RECORDS THE DESKTOP CHANNEL AS DELIVERED WHENEVER PLYER'S
  notify() RETURNS, BUT ON WINDOWS THAT ONLY MEANS "A THREAD WAS STARTED"

Resolution (batch-84 item 1):
  notify._desktop_notify() now runs plyer's balloon_tip on a thread THIS
  module owns, captures whatever it raises (BaseException, so nothing
  escapes uncaught the way it did through plyer's), and joins for
  DESKTOP_CONFIRM_SECS = 0.5. Both call sites append what it observed
  instead of an unconditional True. macOS/Linux are untouched:
  _WIN_BALLOON_TIP is None there and the plyer facade is called exactly as
  before, since all four non-Windows backends are synchronous.

  THE ENTRY'S OWN FIRST SUGGESTION WOULD HAVE BEEN A REGRESSION, and this
  is the measurement that decided it. The entry rated this Low partly on
  NOTIFY_CHANNELS defaulting to all five channels. But this deployment's
  .env has NTFY_TOPIC, PUSHOVER_TOKEN/USER, DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL(S) and
  SMTP_* ALL unset, and each of those senders returns False without
  credentials -- so desktop's phantom True is the ONLY reason
  send_system_alert() ever returns True today. "Stop treating desktop as a
  channel that can report success" would therefore have turned EVERY system
  alert into status="failed", rolling back both the 6h cooldown and
  alerts.check_halt_transition's edge state, and re-firing each halt alert
  every cron cycle for as long as the condition lasted -- including when the
  toast was appearing perfectly well. Confirmed with the user before
  implementing; they chose owning the thread.

  DESKTOP_CONFIRM_SECS is a failure-DETECTION window, not a completion
  deadline. WindowsBalloonTip.__init__ sleeps `timeout` (10s) AFTER its
  Win32 work, so a successful call is still running when the join expires,
  by construction; every failure mode raises before that sleep, in
  ctypes/Win32 calls that take well under a millisecond. A failure pushed
  past the window reports True -- exactly the pre-fix behaviour, never worse
  -- and, since opus review M-1, still logs at the moment of the catch
  rather than into a list nobody re-reads. That mattered: main.py installs a
  threading.excepthook writing THREAD EXCEPTION blocks to data/crash.log, so
  an escaping plyer exception previously had a durable record, and catching
  it without logging would have been a net loss of a safety net.

  What this does NOT promise: if the backend fails PERSISTENTLY, retry-
  forever is the outcome. That is correct rather than a bug -- with desktop
  the only channel, a dead backend means nothing reaches the operator and
  the per-cycle WARNING is the only signal anything is wrong -- but the
  realistic way to enter that state is the planned VM / Scheduled-Task move
  (session 0 has no tray). Filed separately, see "THE ALERT PATH HAS NO
  HEADLESS-CAPABLE CHANNEL, WHICH THE VM MOVE MAKES LOAD-BEARING".

  Latency, corrected after opus review L-4: 0.5s per alert ACTUALLY SENT,
  and the cooldowns bound repeats of one alert rather than the number of
  distinct alerts in a pass -- so it is N x 0.5s in the two loops that fire
  per item (order_executor._park_stale_unknown_order's per-row
  "unresolved_live_order:{row_id}" key, and alert_strong_signal's per-ticker
  key in main.py's two market loops). No call site holds a lock across it
  (AST-checked across ten modules) and none is on the live order-PLACEMENT
  path. Measured: no existing test in the alerting suites reaches the real
  backend at all (0 hits under a probe plugin over test_batch24_alerting,
  test_batch33_reliability, test_batch69_alerting_correlation,
  test_cron_integration).

  batch-80's UTF-16 truncation is intact on BOTH paths -- kwargs is built
  once before the Windows/facade split -- and its comment block, which used
  to conclude "there is no wrapper this module can add that catches it", is
  corrected in place rather than removed: that was true of a wrapper around
  plyer's FACADE, and truncation is still what actually delivers an
  over-long toast rather than merely reporting its loss.

  Tests: tests/test_notify.py 23 -> 41. The doubles are recording doubles,
  not raising mocks of _notif -- a raising _notif is caught by the very
  `except Exception` this defect is about and can only demonstrate the path
  that already worked. Every absence-assertion is paired with a positive
  control. Mutation-tested and killed: reverting either call site to
  `successes.append(True)`; the failure branch returning True; dropping
  truncation; the resolver always returning None; `worker.join(0)`;
  `daemon=True`; `except Exception`; `"timeout": 0`; moving the warning back
  after the join; and routing the Windows path through the facade.
  `worker.join(0)` initially SURVIVED -- the doubles raised fast enough that
  Thread.start()'s own handshake usually recorded the failure first -- which
  is a race, not a proof; a double that raises only after a delay now pins
  the wait.

  CI (opus review M-2): tests/test_notify.py was added to the
  windows-latest job. test_resolve_win_balloon_tip_matches_the_installed_
  plyer is the load-bearing test of this item -- everything else injects a
  double, so a resolver that stopped returning the real balloon_tip would
  silently reinstate the phantom True with the suite green -- and on ubuntu
  it only ever runs its `else: assert resolved is None` branch, which a
  BROKEN resolver satisfies too.
Priority: Low -- affects the accuracy of a delivery tally and of
  send_system_alert's bool contract, not whether other channels deliver.
Files: notify.py (send_system_alert_detailed's desktop branch,
  alert_strong_signal's desktop branch) -- no code changed by this entry.

Problem:
  Both desktop branches do:

      _notif.notify(...)
      successes.append(True)

  On Windows, plyer's WindowsNotification._notify is
  `thread(target=balloon_tip, kwargs=kwargs).start()` -- it spawns a thread
  and returns immediately. The return therefore carries no information about
  whether the toast was actually shown. balloon_tip can still fail on that
  thread (balloontip.py raises Exception('Shell_NotifyIconW failed.') on
  either of two API calls), and every such failure is recorded as a
  SUCCESSFUL desktop delivery.

  Consequences, in increasing order of consequence:
  - send_system_alert_detailed's (status, n_succeeded, n_attempted) tuple
    over-reports n_succeeded to the batch-69 delivery log.
  - `if not any(successes)` cannot fire when desktop is the ONLY configured
    channel and it failed, so the disk-persisted cooldown is NOT rolled back
    and the alert is suppressed for the full 6h window despite never having
    reached anyone. That is the exact failure mode the rollback added by
    batch-24 item 3 exists to prevent -- it just cannot see this case.

  Batch-80 item 2 removed the one failure that was actually being hit (a
  ValueError from an over-long string, now truncated before it can happen),
  so this is currently latent rather than active. It is a distinct defect
  about plyer's fire-and-forget contract, not about field widths, which is
  why it was not folded into that fix.

What it would look like:
  There is no clean fix from inside notify.py -- the thread is plyer's and
  nothing this module does is on its stack. The options are to stop treating
  desktop as a channel that can report success at all (append True only when
  it is the sole channel, or exclude it from the `any(successes)` rollback
  decision so a desktop-only failure still rolls back), or to bypass
  plyer.notification on Windows and call balloon_tip directly on a thread
  this module owns and can wrap. The first is small and honest; the second
  couples notify.py to plyer internals. Worth deciding before any operator
  runs with NOTIFY_CHANNELS=desktop alone.


[RESOLVED 2026-08-26 by batch-84 item 3 -- originally OPEN 2026-08-25,
  filed by batch-80 item 1, which fixed the same defect in useData.js's
  apiFetch but does not own these files]
  EVERY OTHER RAW fetch() IN THE FRONTEND STILL HAS NO REQUEST TIMEOUT

Resolution (batch-84 item 3):
  All raw call sites now go through a new shared.jsx `withTimeout(options,
  ms)` that reuses batch-80's own `timeoutSignal` (AbortSignal.timeout with
  an AbortController fallback below Chrome 103) and its API_TIMEOUT_MS as
  the default, rather than inventing a second mechanism.

  COUNT CORRECTION, since three different numbers were in circulation: there
  are 14 call sites, not 13 (this entry's Problem prose) and not 15 (the
  batch-84 handoff). The 15 comes from `grep -n "fetch(" | grep -v apiFetch`
  returning 15 LINES, one of which is a comment inside shared.jsx's
  haltOrResume block quoting the old code. This entry's own Files list
  already enumerated 14 correctly. Verified independently by the reviewer.

  Only ONE site deviates from the default: App.jsx's 3s cron-status poll
  takes CRON_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS = 2_500, bounded ABOVE by its own interval for
  the same reason batch-80 gave SCAN_VERSION_TIMEOUT_MS that treatment -- a
  budget at or past the interval lets requests stack, which is the
  accumulation being fixed. The mount-time one-shot on the SAME endpoint
  deliberately keeps the 30s default: it fires inside useData's 23-request
  burst, where 2.5s would abort it whenever the dashboard is busiest.

  An earlier draft also gave /api/weekly-report a 120s budget on the grounds
  that it renders a PDF inside the request and "can run to minutes". Opus
  review MEDIUM-2 traced the handler and disproved the premise --
  pdf_report._collect_data does only local JSON/SQLite reads and
  _generate_pdf is fpdf2 text with no matplotlib and no HTTP anywhere in the
  module, so it is sub-second. The constant was deleted rather than
  re-justified: a second budget defended by a claim that is not true is
  worse than no second budget.

  HONEST FAILURE COPY on the mutating POSTs, confirmed with the user before
  implementing. An aborted /api/paper-order may still have placed the order
  (check_position_limits enforces per-market cost and portfolio caps but has
  no already-open-on-this-ticker guard), and /api/close-position writes
  before it responds -- so a flat "Request failed" is what turns a timeout
  into a duplicate position. actionFailureMessage() renders a timeout as
  "Timed out — <what may have happened>. Refresh before retrying." while an
  ordinary network failure keeps the original wording, which is what it has
  always meant. haltOrResume drops "Halt FAILED" (a definite statement we no
  longer have) for wording that still names the manual fallback command.
  App.jsx's run-cron branch stops saying "is the server running?" for an
  abort that may well have spawned a scan.

  For the two bulk paths, summarizeBulkResults folds a timeout into `failed`
  like any other rejection -- "✗ 3 failed" for three orders that may all
  have landed is the one wrong answer -- so countTimeouts() splits them out
  and bulkOutcomeMessage() renders both buckets. That message builder lives
  in shared.jsx rather than inline in the two tabs specifically because this
  repo's frontend has NO component-render tests: the inline version
  mutation-tested as unobserved (reverting the timeout branch to a dead
  condition left all 327 tests green). Extracting it also fixed a
  pre-existing SignalsTab wart where an all-timed-out batch opened with a
  green "✓ 0 placed".

  Two deliberate non-changes, each argued rather than defaulted:
  - The timeout branches say "Refresh before retrying" instead of calling
    M.refresh() themselves. A timeout means the backend is already slow or
    hung, and M.refresh() fires the 23-request burst straight into it.
  - handleRunCron's timeout branch does not arm the cron poll. Because
    /api/cron-status reports exit_code from api_run_cron._proc, which
    persists across runs, a poll started when no new scan actually began
    would read running:false/exit_code:0 from the PREVIOUS scan, resolve to
    'done', and fire both the "scan complete" toast and a desktop
    Notification for a scan that never ran.

  Tests: frontend 303 -> 334 (shared.test.js 177 -> 208). Includes a source
  scan, which is the only mechanism available for the call sites
  themselves: per-file pinned counts for the six files that have fetches,
  plus a tree-wide sweep asserting no OTHER src file has a raw one (the
  hand-written six-file list was only as wide as its author -- opus review
  MEDIUM-4), plus a containment-bound assertion tying CRON_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS
  to the setInterval body rather than to the file (MEDIUM-1: dropping that
  second argument put the 3s poll back on 30s and left everything green).
  The matcher has its own self-test; its earlier `apiFetch` control was
  vacuous (capital F never matched) and was hiding a `window.fetch(` blind
  spot (LOW-1). isTimeoutError is pinned against the reason the REAL
  timeoutSignal aborts with, on both its native and fallback paths, not
  against hand-built DOMExceptions.

  Known and documented: isTimeoutError accepts AbortError as well as
  TimeoutError, which also claims a BROWSER-initiated abort (Firefox rejects
  with AbortError when the user presses Esc; Chrome gives TypeError) as a
  timeout. Left folded in deliberately -- the only wrong word is "Timed
  out", while everything after it stays correct, and narrowing to
  TimeoutError alone would drop a real timeout on any engine below Chrome
  103 back to "Request failed". Making the two genuinely distinguishable
  needs an explicit abort reason in useData.js's timeoutSignal fallback,
  which this change does not own; filed as a follow-up.

  static/dist was rebuilt (`npm run build`), as every prior frontend commit
  in this repo does -- the bundle is tracked.

graphify-out was deliberately NOT refreshed by batch-84, with a measurement:
  The standing process refreshes the knowledge graph's AST layer for changed
  files before committing. Measured instead that a load+save round-trip of
  graphify-out/graph.json through graphify's own load_node_link_graph()
  rewrites 12,276 of 22,371 links with source and target transposed.

  That is NOT corruption: the artifact declares "directed": false, and the
  multiset of undirected {source,target}+type edges is byte-for-byte
  identical before and after (verified with a Counter comparison -- an
  earlier sorted()-based check said otherwise and was wrong). networkx
  simply canonicalises the endpoint order of an undirected edge on
  re-serialisation.

  It is still a reason to skip. A 12,276-line transposition inside a tracked
  18MB artifact is indistinguishable in review from the real thing -- commit
  14162c46 ("repair 12,994 backwards edges") is this repo reacting to almost
  exactly this number once already -- and dragging it into a batch that
  changed two Python files would bury the actual diff. The graph is in any
  case already stale by roughly eight batches (last refreshed at aa7c15ed
  for batch-76), and its own built_at_commit stamp (5f1b4290) is not a valid
  object in this repository at all, so a two-file scoped refresh would not
  meaningfully restore its accuracy either.

  What a future refresh should do first: pass the artifact's own `directed`
  flag through the loader and sort links deterministically before writing,
  so a refresh produces a diff proportional to what actually changed.
Priority: Low -- these are operator-initiated actions and per-tab loads
  rather than the 60s poll that drives the whole dashboard, so a hang
  stalls one button or one card instead of freezing every number on screen.
Files: frontend/src/App.jsx (/api/cron-status x2, /api/run_cron,
  /api/cancel-cron), frontend/src/shared.jsx (haltOrResume's /api/halt |
  /api/resume), frontend/src/tabs/AnalyticsTab.jsx (/api/edge-realization,
  /api/reliability/<city>), frontend/src/tabs/PositionsTab.jsx
  (/api/close-position x2), frontend/src/tabs/SettingsTab.jsx
  (/api/weekly-report, /api/override x2), frontend/src/tabs/SignalsTab.jsx
  (/api/paper-order x2) -- no code changed by this entry.

Problem:
  Batch-80 item 1 gave useData.js's apiFetch an AbortSignal.timeout(), which
  covers the 23 polled endpoints and the scan-version poll. Thirteen other
  call sites across six files still call fetch() bare, so a backend that
  HANGS rather than errors leaves each of them pending forever.

  The consequences differ from the poll's, which is why this is filed rather
  than assumed equivalent:
  - The POST actions (run_cron, cancel-cron, halt/resume, close-position,
    paper-order, override) mostly set a local "in flight" flag and clear it
    in .then()/.finally(). A never-settling fetch leaves the button disabled
    or spinning with no way back except a page reload.
  - PositionsTab's and SignalsTab's order paths are the ones worth looking
    at first: an operator who cannot tell a hung submit from a slow one may
    retry, and these submit a price.
  - AnalyticsTab's two GETs just leave a card in its loading state.

What it would look like:
  Import API_TIMEOUT_MS from useData.js (already exported) and add
  `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(API_TIMEOUT_MS)` at each site, then check
  each one's existing .catch()/.finally() actually restores its UI state on
  an abort rather than only on an HTTP error. The POST sites need more care
  than the GETs: aborting a submit that the server may already have
  processed is not the same as aborting a read, so "timed out" must not be
  rendered as "did not happen".


[OPEN 2026-08-25 -- filed by batch-80 item 3, surfaced by making
  TestMaxConcurrentPositions actually exercise the cap it is named for]
  MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS IS A PER-CYCLE ENTRY GATE, SO ONE CYCLE CAN OPEN
  MORE POSITIONS THAN THE CAP ALLOWS
Priority: Low -- paper trading is dormant and the overshoot is bounded by
  the spend and per-date caps, but it is a real gap between what the cap is
  documented to do and what it does.
Files: order_executor.py (_auto_place_trades, the check at line 4368) -- no
  code changed by this entry.

Problem:
  The cap is evaluated exactly once, before the opportunity loop:

      if len(_open_trades_list) >= MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS:
          ... return 0

  `_open_trades_list` is the snapshot taken at the top of the cycle and
  nothing re-checks it, or increments a counter toward it, as placements
  happen. So the cap is all-or-nothing per cycle: at 20 open it places
  nothing, and at 19 open it may place every qualifying opportunity in the
  batch.

  Measured, not inferred: tests/test_trade_improvements.py::
  test_trades_placed_below_cap now starts from 18 open positions and places
  all 5 of its opportunities, ending at 23 -- three past a cap the class
  docstring describes as "must refuse new trades once 20 open positions
  exist". That test asserts `== 5` because that is what the code does today;
  it is deliberately pinned to the real behaviour so this entry's fix has to
  come back and change it.

  Bounded in practice by MAX_DAILY_SPEND / MAX_SAME_DAY_SPEND, the per-date
  concentration caps, and the VaR gate, all of which ARE evaluated per
  opportunity inside the loop. So the realistic overshoot is a few positions
  on a batch of unusually diverse, cheap signals, not an unbounded one.

What it would look like:
  Count placements inside the loop and re-test
  `len(_open_trades_list) + placed >= MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS` per
  opportunity, the way the same-day and per-date caps already do
  (`_same_day_open >= _eff_sameday_cap` / `_multiday_date_counts[...] >=
  MAX_POSITIONS_PER_DATE`). Small change, but it alters live sizing
  behaviour, so it needs its own decision rather than riding along with a
  test repair -- and test_trades_placed_below_cap's `== 5` becomes `== 2`
  when it lands, which is what the batch-62 entry originally expected the
  code to already do.

    2026-06:  above 17,  below 3,  between 69

Diagnostics -- what is ruled OUT:
  1. NOT a mislabel/rename. batch-75's `observed_extreme_f` is written only
     on the lockout path and was backfilled across history; it is populated
     on exactly 89 / 13 / 4 rows for June / July / August and on no row of
     any other method. If the lock were still firing under a different
     `method` label, those counts would diverge. They do not.
  2. NOT a settlement backlog. Every metar_lockout row is settled:
     89/89, 13/13, 4/4.
  3. NOT reduced scanning. analysis_attempts at days_out=0 is flat:

   - Seasonal. Locks fire on clearance from the strike; June's heat may
     simply have produced more lockable days. This is the benign reading
     and it is plausible. Test it on clearance/margin DISTRIBUTIONS, not
     on prediction counts -- counts are the thing in question.
   - A gate tightened. `git log -L` `_metar_lock_in` and its caller across
     2026-06-01..2026-08-26 and diff the conditions.
   - Strike ladders moved relative to climatology, so the same weather no
     longer clears any strike by the required margin.

What this invalidates right now:

ANSWERED 2026-08-26 -- IT IS A GATE CHANGE, NOT SEASONAL. Two separable
halves, and only one of them was ever a mystery:

  HALF 1 -- 'between' (69 of June's 89 rows). A deliberate, documented
  toggle. between locks ran 69 in June, ZERO for all of July, and 4 in
  August. `bded3d6a` (2026-08-09, "re-enable between-bucket METAR lock-in
  on the daily extreme, not instantaneous temp") is the re-enable. Nothing
  to investigate; this half is fully explained and correct.

  HALF 2 -- above/below. THIS is the real finding. Expressed as a lock RATE
  over same-day above/below predictions rather than as a count:

    month     locked   same-day above/below preds   lock rate
    2026-06     20                39                  51.3%
    2026-07     13                49                  26.5%
    2026-08      0                28                   0.0%

  Market supply went UP, not down: analysis_attempts at days_out=0 for
  above/below went 90 (July) -> 224 (August). There were more chances in
  August than ever, and the lock took none of them.

  This is not consistent with seasonality. If August's true lock rate were
  even July's already-reduced 26.5%, the probability of observing 0 locks
  in 28 opportunities is 0.735^28 ~= 1 in 10,000. A weather-driven decline
  produces a thin tail, not an exact zero.

  Dated cause, with the cliff inside a single month: splitting July in
  half, non-'between' locks ran 11 in 2026-07-01..15 and 2 in
  2026-07-16..31. The commit on the boundary is `3e6af667` (2026-07-10,
  "Fix ~35 bugs in weather_markets.py found by a full-file Fable
  adversarial review"), which added a monotone-safety veto that UNLOCKS an
  already-locked market when the branch check_metar_lockout used is not
  monotone-safe:

    + if _is_low_mkt and _lockout.get("locked"):
    +     # "min already fell below threshold - margin" is monotone-safe
    +     # threshold + margin" is NOT safe -- evening cooling can still...
    +     _margin = 3.0  # matches check_metar_lockout's own default

  That veto is correct on its own terms -- it is the same monotone-safety
  reasoning batch-76 later built section 10b on -- and it is very likely
  what took the rate from 51% to 27%.

  RESOLVED 2026-08-26 (same session, second pass). The paragraph below was
  written before the per-family numbers existed and is WRONG in two ways;
  both corrections are stated here rather than by deleting it.

  CORRECTION 1 -- the max veto is NOT missing. It exists, at
  weather_markets.py ~:15052, `elif not _is_low_mkt and _lockout.get(
  "locked")`, the exact mirror of the LOW block. It was added by batch-59
  item 1 (`d65decff`, 2026-08-25) against a backlog entry titled
  "_metar_lock_in's above/below branch has no monotonic-safety veto for
  HIGH markets". It carries its own measurement: over 22,799 real
  station-days, P(running max still rises >=3F after the stated local hour)
  = 26.9% at 14:00 and never below ~2.8% even at 21:00.

  CORRECTION 2 -- the "1 in 10,000" statistic above is WRONG. It pooled
  above+below into one rate, but the two ticker families are governed by
  DIFFERENT gates (the LOW veto is `_is_low_mkt`-scoped), so pooling them
  mixes populations with different code. Note also that condition_type
  above/below is the strike DIRECTION, not the market's variable: every
  August same-day "above" row is a KXLOWT (daily-minimum) ticker. Split by
  ticker family, non-'between' only:

    family     2026-06        2026-07        2026-08
    KXLOWT     15/25  60.0%    9/22  40.9%    0/11   0.0%
    KXHIGH      5/22  22.7%    4/27  14.8%    0/14   0.0%

  Binomial, against each family's OWN July rate:
    KXLOWT   P(0 of 11 | 0.409) = 0.591^11 = 0.0031   -- significant
    KXHIGH   P(0 of 14 | 0.148) = 0.852^14 = 0.104    -- NOT significant

  So the answer differs by family:

   * KXLOWT (min markets): REAL, and the cause is dated. The LOW
     monotone-safety veto in `3e6af667` (2026-07-10) rejects exactly the
     unsafe-direction min lock. Split July at the 15th: 11 non-'between'
     locks in 07-01..15, 2 in 07-16..31, 0 thereafter. Date, mechanism and
     significance all agree.

   * KXHIGH (max markets): NOT ESTABLISHED, and there is no second gate to
     find. 0 of 14 at July's own 14.8% rate is p=0.10 -- ordinary
     small-sample variation. The KXHIGH rate had already fallen to 22.7% in
     June and 14.8% in July, and August's zero is consistent with it. The
     HIGH veto that WOULD zero this family landed 2026-08-25, after every
     row in this table.

  Two hypotheses tested and eliminated rather than assumed:
   - NOT the `_daily_ext is None` hard gate above both vetoes. Called
     `metar.fetch_metar_daily_extreme(station, city_tz, target_date,
     extreme)` live for KMDW/KDFW/KATL/KSEA/KPHL on 2026-08-26: every
     station returned real max and min values. That gate is not firing.
   - NOT a var-derivation regression from `276af72a` (2026-08-01).
     `_var_from_ticker_prefix` returns 'min' for every KXLOWT ticker and
     None for KXTEMP hourly, which is correct; no max ticker is
     misclassified as a min market.

  WHAT THIS MEANS GOING FORWARD, and it is the part worth acting on. Both
  vetoes are correct -- each rejects a direction that genuinely is not
  monotone-safe, and the HIGH one is backed by a 22,799-station-day
  measurement. But together, and with the HIGH veto live only since
  2026-08-25, the non-'between' METAR lock is now closed by design in the
  unsafe direction for BOTH families. The lock's remaining live surface is
  effectively the 'between' path. That is a deliberate outcome of two
  correctness fixes, not a bug -- but nothing records it, and it means
  batch-75's and batch-76's non-'between' work governs a path current code
  has largely closed. Say so explicitly somewhere the next person will
  look, and re-measure the lock rate after 2026-09-25 to see where it
  settles with both vetoes live for a full month.

  (Superseded text follows, kept for auditability:) that veto is scoped to
  `_is_low_mkt`, so it cannot by itself explain ZERO `above` (max-market)
  locks across 14 August opportunities. Either a second narrowing landed
  after 2026-07-10, or the veto's scope is wider in effect than its
  condition reads. Candidate commits touching this area after the cliff:
  `276af72a` (08-01, var-derivation consolidation across 7 files),
  `0100bffe` (08-11, target_date vs city-local today), `9eb2f154` (08-21,
  batch-08 METAR audit fixes). Start by instrumenting a single live
  above-market same-day scan and logging which branch declines to lock --
  that is one cron cycle's worth of evidence and settles it outright.

Plan:
  1. DONE -- see ANSWERED above. Remaining: find what zeroes the `above`
     half, per the paragraph directly above.
  2. Decide seasonal-vs-regression on clearance/margin distributions across
     the three months, not counts.
  3. Independently of the answer: make the calibration panel state its

  Before citing any same-day calibration number, and before treating

  today neither has enough August traffic to have been exercised.


[OPEN 2026-08-26 -- promoted from a sub-bullet of the entry "THE METAR LOCK
  HAS STOPPED FIRING" above, which found it. Filed as its own entry rather
  than left folded in because it is a different subsystem with a different
  fix, and because three separate wrong numbers were produced from this same
  class of error in one session -- see "The pattern" below.]
  THE CALIBRATION PANEL POOLS POPULATIONS WITH DIFFERENT GOVERNING CODE AND
  THEN PRINTS A REASSURING VERDICT OVER THEM
Priority: Medium -- operator-facing and actively misleading rather than
  merely absent. It renders an authoritative table plus an explicit
  all-clear, and both are wrong in ways an operator cannot see from the
  output. No trading gate reads it, which is the only reason this is not
  higher.
Files: main.py (cmd_walkforward's "Multiday/Sameday Calibration Curve"
  blocks and the "No significant systematic bias detected" line), tracker.py
  (get_sameday_calibration_cli / get_multiday_calibration_cli /
  _calibration_curve). Note web_app.py:3139 has its own _calibration_curve
  for the dashboard -- check whether it shares the defect before fixing only
  one.

Problem -- three distinct faults, all visible in one `py main.py validate`
run on 2026-08-26:

  1. THE VERDICT IS COMPUTED ON A MEAN, SO CANCELLING TAILS READ AS CLEAN.
     Actual output:

       7% bucket:  predicted  7.1%  actual 43.8%  N=16   -36.6%
      34% bucket:  predicted 33.6%  actual 50.0%  N= 6   -16.4%
      53% bucket:  predicted 53.1%  actual 51.9%  N=52    +1.2%  OK
      69% bucket:  predicted 69.4%  actual 62.5%  N=16    +6.9%
      91% bucket:  predicted 90.8%  actual 72.7%  N=33   +18.1%

      "No significant systematic bias detected."
      Mean predicted 58.4% | Mean actual 57.7% | N=123

     A same-day "7%" resolves YES 43.8% of the time and a "91%" resolves
     72.7%. The two errors point opposite ways, so the MEAN is off by
     0.7pp and the check passes. The statistic answers "is the average
     right", which is not the question a calibration curve exists to ask.

  2. THE POPULATION IS STALE AND THE PANEL DOES NOT SAY SO. Of the 49
     same-day tail rows, 48 are June/July 2026 and exactly one is August.
     All 33 same-day metar_lockout rows are June (20) and July (13). The
     code that produced them has since been changed by the METAR beta-
     calibration (first fit ~2026-08-20), the 2026-08-09 'between'
     re-enable, batch-75, batch-76 and batch-59's HIGH monotone veto
     (2026-08-25). The panel presents a seven-week-old population with no
     date range shown.

  3. IT POOLS ACROSS GOVERNING CODE. The same-day population mixes
     method='ensemble' and method='metar_lockout' rows, and those two are
     priced by entirely different machinery gated by different code. The
     91% bucket is 24/33 metar_lockout; the 53% bucket is 52/54 ensemble.
     One curve over both describes no actual system.

The pattern, which is why this is worth fixing rather than caveating:
  In a single session on 2026-08-26, THREE separate wrong numbers were
  produced by pooling populations with different governing code --
  (a) a "1 in 10,000" significance claim on the METAR lock that pooled two
  ticker families governed by different vetoes (corrected in the entry
  above); (b) batch-81's accrual table, which pooled rows the registry's own
  filter excludes (corrected at 0374c3a2); and (c) this panel. The first two
  were caught. This one is still live and is the one an operator actually
  looks at.

Plan:
  1. Make the verdict refuse rather than reassure. "No significant
     systematic bias detected" should require every bucket with N above
     some floor to be within tolerance, not the pooled mean. A per-bucket
     rule would have flagged both tails immediately.
  2. Print the population's date range, and withhold or loudly caveat the
     verdict when the newest row is older than a threshold. This is the
     cheapest of the three and would have prevented the whole
     investigation that found this.
  3. Decide whether to split the same-day curve by `method`, or at minimum
     print the method mix per bucket. Do NOT silently pool -- that is the
     defect batch-75 spent a session removing from forecast_temp_f, in a
     different place.
  4. Check web_app.py:3139's own _calibration_curve for the same three
     faults before considering this closed.

When to revisit:
  Before quoting any calibration-curve number, and before trusting an
  all-clear from this panel. Coordinate with batch-82 if it is still open --
  it owns main.py, tracker.py and the same-day calibration surface.

[OPEN 2026-08-26 -- surfaced by batch-84 item 3's opus review (LOW-2);
  frontend/src/useData.js was outside that batch's file scope]
  timeoutSignal's FALLBACK ABORTS WITHOUT A REASON, SO A USER-CANCELLED
  REQUEST IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM OUR OWN TIMEOUT
Priority: Low -- the resulting copy is mislabelled but its advice stays
  correct, and the ambiguous path only exists on engines below Chrome 103.
Files: frontend/src/useData.js (timeoutSignal, ~:105-113)

Problem:
  batch-84 item 3's shared.jsx isTimeoutError() has to accept BOTH
  'TimeoutError' (what AbortSignal.timeout rejects with) and 'AbortError'
  (what timeoutSignal's AbortController fallback rejects with), because
  narrowing to the first would render every timeout on an older engine as a
  flat "Request failed" -- the same shape as batch-80's freshness-banner
  bug, where one helper returned null for two states the caller then had to
  tell apart.

  The cost is that a BROWSER-initiated abort is also claimed as a timeout.
  Firefox rejects an in-flight fetch with AbortError when the user presses
  Esc or navigates away (Chrome gives TypeError), and Esc is a live key in
  this dashboard, so an operator who cancels a POST on Firefox is told it
  "timed out". Only the label is wrong -- the request WAS dispatched, the
  order may well have landed, and refreshing before retrying is right -- so
  batch-84 folded it in deliberately rather than narrowing.

  Not verified against a real Firefox: there is no browser in the agent
  environment, so this rests on reading isTimeoutError plus known engine
  behaviour, not on an observed repro. Confirm before acting.

What it would look like:
  Give the fallback an explicit reason -- `c.abort(new DOMException('signal
  timed out', 'TimeoutError'))` -- so both paths reject with the same name.
  AbortController.abort(reason) is Chrome 98 / Firefox 97 / Safari 15.4,
  slightly EARLIER than AbortSignal.timeout, and an engine too old for it
  ignores the argument and still aborts, so this degrades to today's
  behaviour rather than breaking. isTimeoutError can then drop 'AbortError'
  and shared.test.js's "recognises BOTH names" test becomes a test that the
  fallback carries the reason. Check useData.js's own apiFetch first: safe()
  treats every non-auth rejection identically, so nothing there depends on
  the current name.

When to revisit: next time anyone touches useData.js's request layer.


[OPEN 2026-08-26 -- surfaced by batch-84 item 2's opus review (L-3);
  main.py belongs to a batch running in parallel]
  cmd_settings SIGNALS "KALSHI_ENV WAS UNSET" BY DELETING IT FROM os.environ,
  WHICH ANY LATER load_dotenv() SILENTLY UNDOES
Priority: Low -- NOT reachable in this deployment today (see below), but the
  guard it weakens is the M-25 prod/demo desync fix, which is a live-money
  concern if it ever does fire.
Files: main.py (cmd_settings, ~:8109-8133; _kalshi_env at ~:708-710)

Problem:
  cmd_settings snapshots KALSHI_ENV, runs load_dotenv(env_path,
  override=True) to pick up an operator's edit, then restores the snapshot
  -- and when the snapshot was None it does os.environ.pop("KALSHI_ENV",
  None). That deliberate ABSENCE is the carrier of intent: _kalshi_env()
  falls back to "demo" when the variable is unset, which is the safe
  direction.

  Absence is a fragile carrier. Any later non-overriding load_dotenv() in
  the same process sets the variable precisely BECAUSE it is absent,
  resurrecting the popped value from .env and undoing the guard. batch-84
  item 2 added one such call to watchdog.py, which cron.py imports lazily at
  runtime -- and cmd_menu offers both "S" Settings and "L" Cron in the same
  process, so the sequence is: Settings edit -> Cron -> first-ever watchdog
  import -> KALSHI_ENV back.

  Reachability, stated honestly: NOT reachable here today. This deployment's
  .env sets KALSHI_ENV=prod, so main.py:41's startup load_dotenv() always
  puts it in os.environ, the snapshot is never None, and the pop branch
  never runs. It needs a .env WITHOUT KALSHI_ENV at process start, then the
  operator hand-adding it mid-session -- which is exactly the external-edit
  scenario main.py's own comment says that block was written to defend
  against.

What it would look like:
  Stop using absence-from-os.environ as the signal. A module-level
  _KALSHI_ENV_PINNED sentinel that _kalshi_env() consults ahead of
  os.getenv, set by cmd_settings when the snapshot was None, is immune to
  any later dotenv load. Nothing in watchdog.py can or should fix this.

When to revisit: next time anyone touches cmd_settings or _kalshi_env, or
  when the batch that currently owns main.py lands.


[OPEN 2026-08-26 -- the first measurement ever taken on the UNBIASED population.
  Possible only because the analysis_attempts settlement sweep drained on
  2026-08-26 (115 -> 584 scored rows), so markets the bot DECLINED to trade now
  carry outcomes. Every model-vs-market number this repo has ever produced was
  computed on the high-conviction tail alone.]
  THE MODEL'S "EDGE" IS ITS OWN MISCALIBRATION: ON MARKETS WHERE IT DISAGREES
  WITH THE CROWD BY >=0.15 THE CROWD IS RIGHT ~90% OF THE TIME, AND MIN_EDGE
  SELECTS FOR EXACTLY THOSE ROWS
Priority: HIGH -- this is the premise the whole strategy rests on, and it is
  the first time it has been testable. Nothing is broken in code; the finding
  is about whether the edge signal carries information at all. Live trading is
  dormant and paper sizing is gated, so there is no active loss -- but no
  further work aimed at "improving edge" should start before this is settled.
Files: measurement only (analysis_attempts). Consumers implicated:
  weather_markets.py (blended_prob, MIN_EDGE / PAPER_MIN_EDGE gating),
  ml_bias.py + data/temperature_scale.json (calibration fitted on the WRONG
  population), calibration.py.

Method:
  analysis_attempts JOIN on outcome IS NOT NULL, forecast_prob and market_prob
  both present. `outcome` is written as int(settled_yes) -- verified at
  tracker.py:13757 and :13802, not assumed. 584 scored rows, of which 535 were
  NEVER TRADED. Restricted to the core temperature families (KXHIGH + KXLOWT)
  for every headline number below: 538 of the 584. Shadow families are a
  rounding error here (KXRAIN 27, KXTEMP 18, KXNEXTHUR 1) and are NOT driving
  any of it -- checked explicitly, because pooling populations with different
  governing code produced three separate wrong numbers earlier the same day.

Finding 1 -- the market beats the model decisively, on the unbiased population:

    family     n     model    market     diff       t
    KXLOWT   297    0.1474    0.1040   +0.0434   +7.16
    KXHIGH   241    0.2025    0.1025   +0.1000   +7.54

  (Brier, lower is better; paired t on the per-row difference.)

Finding 2 -- THE GAP GROWS WITH THE CLAIMED EDGE. All 584 rows, bucketed on
  |forecast_prob - market_prob|:

    edge bucket        n     model    market      diff       t
    [0.00, 0.02)      35    0.0862    0.0875   -0.0014   -1.11
    [0.02, 0.05)      60    0.1815    0.1796   +0.0019   +0.48
    [0.05, 0.08)      43    0.1247    0.1167   +0.0079   +1.14
    [0.08, 0.15)     153    0.1397    0.1164   +0.0234   +3.56
    [0.15, 1.01)     293    0.2048    0.0894   +0.1154   +9.36

  Monotone. Where the model agrees with the market it is fine; the more it
  disagrees, the more wrong it is. MIN_EDGE / PAPER_MIN_EDGE are 0.15, so the
  bot trades from the bottom row.

Finding 3 -- direction, on the rows the gates actually select. Core temperature,
  |f - m| >= 0.15, n = 275:
    model's direction correct   30 / 275  =  10.9%   (z = -12.96 vs a coin flip)

Finding 4 -- THE MECHANISM, and it is NOT inverted information. The correlation
  between the model's deviation (f - m) and the market's residual (y - m) is
  -0.066, t = -1.52 -- NOT significant. There is no anti-signal to harvest by
  flipping the sign. What there is, is compression plus bias. Calibration
  regression y = a + b*p over the 538 core rows:

    MODEL   slope 1.233 (se 0.078)  intercept -0.238   slope-vs-1  t = +2.98
    MARKET  slope 1.107 (se 0.044)  intercept -0.067   slope-vs-1  t = +2.45

  b > 1 means probabilities too COMPRESSED toward 0.5. Seen directly by
  splitting the high-disagreement rows by which way the model leans:

    model leans YES (f>m)  n=212   market 0.129   model 0.427   ACTUAL  9.4%
    model leans NO  (f<m)  n= 63   market 0.820   model 0.633   ACTUAL 84.1%

  In BOTH directions the market is nearly exact and the model is pulled toward
  the middle. Overall mean model 0.468 vs mean market 0.366 vs actual 0.338.

  So `|forecast - market| >= MIN_EDGE` does not select markets where the model
  knows something. It selects markets the CROWD prices near an extreme, because
  those are precisely where a compressed probability is furthest from the price.
  The gate is a filter for the model's own miscalibration.

  This is the failure mode the memory note "under-confident signal flips the
  side" describes, now measured on real settlements at n=275.

Why this was invisible until today:
  `predictions` only ever contains rows that cleared the gates, so its minimum
  |forecast - market| is 0.0984 and it holds ZERO rows below the 0.08 floor.
  Every Brier, skill-score and calibration fit in this repo was computed on the
  top-left cell of finding 2's table. analysis_attempts now supplies the other
  cells -- 138 scored rows below the 0.08 floor, minimum separation 0.0011.

Plan (decision required -- do NOT start "improve the edge" work first):
  1. Refit calibration on analysis_attempts rather than predictions. Every
     existing fit -- temperature_scale.json included -- is trained on the
     selected tail, which is the one population where the model's compression
     is invisible. This is the single highest-value action and it is cheap.
  2. Re-derive whether MIN_EDGE should be a |f - m| threshold at all. On this
     evidence a calibrated model would produce far fewer, different signals;
     a threshold on a miscalibrated probability is selecting the wrong rows by
     construction.
  3. Re-run findings 1-3 AFTER recalibration, on rows logged after the refit.
     Do not re-score the same rows with a fit trained on them.
  4. Treat every historical "edge" measurement as provisional until 1-3 are
     done, including A14's headline.

When to revisit:
  Before any live-trading decision, and before any further work whose
  justification is "improves edge". This entry supersedes the framing of the
  no-Brier-skill note (model 0.2596 vs market 0.2201, n=214) -- that was the
  same phenomenon seen through the selected population, at a quarter of the
  effect size.

  ADDENDUM 2026-08-26 -- DOES RECALIBRATION RECOVER THE EDGE? NO, BUT IT
  HALVES THE GAP. Temporal split, no look-ahead: Platt scaling fitted on the
  earlier 322 core-temperature rows (2026-07-25..08-13), applied to the later
  216 (08-13..08-24). Fitted a=-0.6833, b=1.4168 -- b>1 confirms compression
  independently of the earlier linear fit.

    HELD-OUT Brier (n=216)   raw model 0.1756   CALIBRATED 0.1473   market 0.1106
    calibrated - market      diff +0.0366   t = +3.50

  Calibration is real and worth doing -- it removes ~44% of the excess Brier.
  It does not create edge: the market still wins at t=3.50 on data the fit
  never saw. And of the rows that STILL clear |f-m|>=0.15 after calibration
  (n=86), the model is 0.2088 against the market's 0.1236 -- the surviving
  signals are still the adverse ones.

  NO SUBPOPULATION WINS. Checked exhaustively on the unbiased set:
    by horizon   d=0  n=348  model 0.1964  market 0.1143  t=+8.44
                 d=1  n=190  model 0.1274  market 0.0833  t=+5.60
    by city      0 of 18 cities with n>=15 have the model ahead
    by method    *** SOURCED FROM `predictions`, NOT analysis_attempts ***
                 ensemble n=211 t=+2.88;  metar_lockout n=106 t=+1.90
                 CORRECTION 2026-08-26, caught by the batch-87 session:
                 this one sub-check was run as
                   SELECT p.method ... FROM predictions p JOIN outcomes_valid o
                 i.e. on the SELECTED population, while every other number in
                 this entry is on the unbiased set. It cannot have come from
                 analysis_attempts, which has no `method` column at all
                 (ticker, city, condition, target_date, analyzed_at,
                 forecast_prob, market_prob, days_out, was_traded, outcome,
                 status, not_found_at, last_checked_at). Independently
                 reconciled: the 106 matches predictions.method='metar_lockout'

                 The OBSERVATION still stands on its own population -- the

    by family    KXLOWT t=+7.16;  KXHIGH t=+7.54

  Honest limits: 538 rows over one month (2026-07-25..08-24), summer only, and
  analysis_attempts covers only markets the scanner actually looked at. That is

  SNAPSHOT, and it rots: every count here is as of 2026-08-26 ~03:00 UTC, when

  UNLANDED MEASUREMENT WORTH KEEPING (batch-87 session, 2026-08-26; its session

[OPEN 2026-08-26 -- follow-up to the entry above ("THE MODEL'S 'EDGE' IS ITS OWN
  MISCALIBRATION"). That entry established the model loses to the market. This
  one records the three exits that were then tested, two of which are now dead
  and one of which is the only positive result in the whole analysis. Filed so
  nobody re-runs the negatives.]
  TWO WAYS OUT OF THE NO-EDGE RESULT ARE NOW CLOSED; THE ONE THAT SURVIVES
  NEEDS NO WEATHER MODEL AT ALL (FAVOURITE-LONGSHOT BIAS IN THE LADDER)
Priority: HIGH as a decision input -- it changes what "keep going" would mean.
  No code implied yet; item I below is a hypothesis to validate FORWARD, not a
  strategy to wire in.
Files: measurement only (analysis_attempts). Method as the parent entry: core
  temperature families (KXHIGH/KXLOWT), 538 rows, temporal split 322 train /
  216 test, everything below evaluated ONLY on the held-out later window.

CLOSED -- G. Does the model add information ON TOP OF the price?
  The standard test when a signal loses to a benchmark: fit
  y ~ a + b*logit(market) + c*logit(model) and ask whether c is non-zero.

    market-only    a=-0.123  b=1.487
    market+model   a=-0.120  b=1.507   c = -0.0408
    HELD-OUT Brier  market-only 0.1078   +model 0.1080
    (+model) - (market-only)  diff +0.00014   t = +1.01

  The model's marginal weight is ~zero and slightly negative. It carries NO
  orthogonal information. This is the strongest available form of the no-edge
  test and it comes back clean -- blending the model with the price does not
  help. Do not revisit without new inputs, not just a retuned blend.

CLOSED -- H. Fade the model (use its direction as a contrarian filter).
  Motivated by the parent entry's 10.9% direction rate. Held-out:

    |f-m| >= 0.15  leans YES -> buy NO  n=97  edge +0.012  z=+0.37
                   leans NO  -> buy YES n=25  edge -0.054  z=-0.67
    |f-m| >= 0.08  leans YES -> buy NO  n=123 edge +0.024  z=+0.77
                   leans NO  -> buy YES n=53  edge -0.021  z=-0.39

  Opposite signs, |z| < 1 everywhere. The ~3.5pp that appeared in-sample did
  not survive the split. There is no anti-signal to harvest.

OPEN -- I. The market itself is compressed. Model-free.
  Fell out of G: recalibrating the PRICE ALONE improved held-out Brier with no
  model input whatsoever.

    y ~ a + b*logit(market)     b = 1.4871    z = +3.03 vs 1
    HELD-OUT Brier  raw 0.1106  recalibrated 0.1078  (diff -0.0028, t=-0.94)

  Classic favourite-longshot bias: prices compressed toward 0.5, favourites
  underpriced. Betting the side recalibration favours, held-out, gross and net
  of Kalshi's ~0.07*p*(1-p):

    thr    n    mean price   win rate   gross     z      net
    0.05  135      0.791      0.852    +6.06%  +1.98   +4.98%
    0.08   42      0.739      0.857   +11.77%  +2.18  +10.46%

  WHY THIS IS NOT YET AN EDGE, and these caveats are the entry:
   - z~2 across FOUR thresholds tried, after two failed hypotheses on the same
     data. Corrected for that search it is not significant. Garden of forking
     paths -- I found this by looking for it.
   - The Brier improvement is NOT significant (t=-0.94), which sits badly with
     a real effect of this size.
   - Every pick is a favourite at 0.74-0.86. Risking 0.79 to win 0.21 is severe
     downside skew: small Kelly, and a few losses erase many wins.
   - Liquidity untested. Filling at 0.79 in these books is exactly the "a gap
     against the mid of a thin spread is not edge" trap this repo has hit before.
   - One month, summer, scanner-visible markets only.

  Correct next step: log the rule's picks in SHADOW for ~60 days and judge it
  on data it was not found in. Do not size anything off this table.

OPEN -- J. Ladder-internal coherence arbitrage. Untested, model-free.
  Strikes on one underlying must form a monotone CDF; mutually inconsistent
  rungs are arbitrage requiring no forecast at all. `compute_market_implied_
  distributions()` already exists. Blocked on data: orderbook_depth_snapshots
  holds 0 rows because the WS depth path has never run. Turning that on is the
  prerequisite, and it is cheap.

When to revisit:
  I and J together are the only paths here that do not require beating a price
  that is already better than the model. Any decision to continue the project
  as a TRADING system should be argued from these two, not from the forecast.

  entries above. Kept as one entry so the options and the evidence for each do
  not drift apart. Update this entry rather than re-deriving it.]
  PROJECT DIRECTION AFTER THE NO-EDGE RESULT -- THE REMAINING OPTIONS
Priority: HIGH -- this is the decision every other open item now hangs off.
  Nothing in the backlog aimed at "improving edge" should start before it is
  taken.
Files: none (decision record).

Two eliminated by measurement, one by the user. Recorded so they are not
re-proposed:
  * BLEND MODEL WITH PRICE -- dead. c = -0.0408, held-out t = +1.01. The model
    carries no information orthogonal to the price. See the entry above.
  * FADE THE MODEL -- dead. Opposite signs, |z| < 1 at both thresholds.
  * WIND DOWN -- removed by the user, 2026-08-26. The argument against it: the
    marginal cost of leaving it running is ~zero (cron is unattended, ~23
    analysed markets/day), the apparatus produced its first real answer only
    this week, and winding down forfeits the 60-day forward test that option 5
    needs. Its only real case was the user's own attention cost, and option 1
    covers that at the same price while preserving the option value.

THE OPTIONS THAT REMAIN

 1. STOP DEVELOPMENT, KEEP MEASURING.
    For: zero risk, near-zero cost, data keeps accruing so the seasonal
      question answers itself. The guards/sweep/audit trail are what produced
      the result; they run unattended.
    Against: no revenue path; "measurement platform" can quietly become
      "abandoned".

 2. RECALIBRATE, THEN RE-MEASURE IN ~60 DAYS.
    For: the one unambiguously-correct code change available. Held-out
      0.1756 -> 0.1473 against a market at 0.1106 -- removes ~44% of the excess
      Brier. Every current calibration fit is trained on `predictions`, the one
      population where the compression is invisible. Cheap, well-scoped.
    Against: does NOT create edge (t = +3.50 held-out). Real sunk-cost risk --
      only defensible if named as hygiene, not as an edge play.

 3. STRUCTURAL EDGE -- MARKET-MAKING / SPREAD CAPTURE.
    For: a well-calibrated market is an asset here, not an obstacle; the WS
      feed, execution log and risk gates already exist.
    Against: a different discipline (inventory, adverse selection, latency);
      the forecasting code becomes irrelevant; orderbook_depth_snapshots holds
      0 rows, so there is ZERO measurement on the thing it depends on; needs
      real capital to test.

 [4. THIN / LESS-EFFICIENT MARKETS -- REMOVED by the user 2026-08-26, and the
     data is more damning than the original "against" said. Measured on
     analysis_attempts: ALL non-temperature families together hold 46 settled
     rows, and 18 of those are KXTEMP (hourly temperature, not a different
     family). The genuinely different families have 28 settled observations
     between them -- rain 27, hurricane 1 -- and snow, tornado and storm-order
     have ZERO. Against the 112-row floor batch-81 derived for a single
     signal, this is not a slow path, it is not a path.
     The deeper objection, which applies even if the data existed: the failure
     measured on temperature was in the MODEL, not the market -- probabilities
     compressed toward 0.5 (slope 1.233 vs the market's 1.107). The shadow
     models were built by the same approach on far less data. There is no
     reason to expect them better calibrated, and far less ability to detect
     that they are not. The one family with any settled data points the same
     way: rain model 0.1536 vs market 0.1405.]

 5. MODEL-FREE FAVOURITE-LONGSHOT CAPTURE.   <-- the only positive result
    For: needs no weather model at all. b = 1.4871 (z = +3.03 vs 1); held-out
      thr=0.05 gives n=135, gross +6.06%, net +4.98% after fees. Requires no
      new infrastructure and is measurable with what already exists.
    Against: z~2 across four thresholds tried AFTER two failed hypotheses on
      the same data -- forking paths, not significant once corrected; the Brier
      improvement itself is not significant (t=-0.94); every pick is a
      favourite at 0.74-0.86 with severe downside skew; liquidity untested;
      one month of summer.
    Status: a hypothesis to validate FORWARD. Shadow-log its picks ~60 days and
      judge on data it was not found in. Size nothing off the discovery table.

 6. LADDER-INTERNAL COHERENCE ARBITRAGE.  (untested)
    For: model-free; strikes on one underlying must form a monotone CDF, so
      inconsistent rungs are arbitrage. compute_market_implied_distributions()
      already exists.
    Against: unmeasured, because orderbook_depth_snapshots has never been
      written. Turning the WS depth path on is the cheap prerequisite.

 7. FIX THE BLEND'S DATA SOURCES, MEMBERSHIP AND WEIGHTS.  (added 2026-08-26
    after the user challenged the blanket "do not improve the forecast")
    For: concrete and measured, not speculative. gfs_seamless shows ~2x the
      error of both peers on max (3.963 vs 2.020/2.138 over 21 paired cells)
      while weighted equal to the best member, and the blend is beaten by its
      own best member on both variables. Crucially, published verification
      puts GFS SECOND GLOBALLY after ECMWF -- so this contradiction points at
      the local product/config, i.e. a BUG, not a skill gap. That is a
      different thing from "build a better model", which is the distinction
      the earlier recommendation missed.
    Against: n=21, one month, summer; MAE and Brier disagree (min-Brier has
      gfs BEST); the drop-gfs figures are member-mean arithmetic, not a
      pipeline counterfactual; and closing it is not shown to narrow the
      model-vs-market gap, which lives on a different population.
    Status: diagnose the product/resolution and returned member count FIRST --
      one live call discriminates the two hypotheses. Do not reweight before
      that. See its own entry.

RECOMMENDATION AS OF 2026-08-26 (revised)
  Do 2 and 7, then 1, with 5 running in shadow alongside. The earlier version
  of this line said to avoid "improve the forecast" work wholesale; that was
  too broad and the user was right to push back. The distinction that matters
  is between BUILDING a better model -- which the evidence argues against --
  and FIXING a data source that is measurably misbehaving, which is cheap,
  concrete, and probably a bug. What still should not be started is the
  former:
  0 of 18 cities, both horizons, all three methods and both families lose, and
  recalibration (the single largest available improvement) closes less than
  half the gap.
  If the goal is a trading system rather than a research platform, argue it
  from 5 or 6 -- they are the only paths that do not require beating a price
  that is already better than the model. 3 is viable but is a new project.

When to revisit:
  Immediately on any live-trading proposal, and at the 60-day mark
  (~2026-10-25) when autumn data makes the seasonal caveat testable.

  checking member-level data. Measured after the challenge, then checked
  against published verification, which REVERSED the interpretation.]
  gfs_seamless HAS ~2x THE ERROR OF ITS PEERS ON max IN THIS PIPELINE -- WHICH
  CONTRADICTS ITS PUBLISHED GLOBAL RANKING, SO SUSPECT THE PRODUCT/CONFIG, NOT
  THE MODEL
Priority: MEDIUM -- concrete and cheap, unlike the modelling work the no-edge
  entries argue against. If the leading hypothesis holds this is a data-source
  defect, which is a bug, not a skill gap.
Files: weather_markets.py (_model_weights' `baseline` dict ~:2148 --
  gfs_seamless 1.0, ecmwf_ifs025 ecmwf_w, icon_seamless 1.0; ecmwf_w = 1.5
  summer / 2.5+ winter with an ENSO bump). NOTE: ENSEMBLE_MODELS (~:884) is
  NOT the live membership -- its own comment says "keep for backward compat".
  The live temperature blend is that three-key baseline dict.

Measured on ensemble_member_scores, PAIRED -- only (city, target_date, var)
cells where all three live members are present, so it is like-for-like:

    var=max  n=21 cells            var=min  n=21 cells
      icon_seamless   2.020          ecmwf_ifs025    1.914
      blended         2.052          blended         2.037
      ecmwf_ifs025    2.138          icon_seamless   2.155
      gfs_seamless    3.963  <--     gfs_seamless    2.752  <--

    recomputed from the stored member means:
      equal weight          2.397          2.001
      live weight 1/1.5/1   2.341          1.975
      DROP gfs_seamless     1.914  -18.2%  1.831  -7.3%

  Also: the blend is beaten by its own best member on BOTH variables (2.052 vs
  2.020; 2.037 vs 1.914). Blending is supposed to beat the best member.

THE ONLINE CHECK IS WHY THIS ENTRY EXISTS IN THIS FORM. Published verification
(2026) puts GFS SECOND GLOBALLY after ECMWF, trailing it by roughly one day of
forecast skill -- i.e. ahead of or comparable to ICON, and nowhere near 2x its
error. The measurement above says the opposite. Two numbers that disagree that
badly mean the local pipeline, not NOAA's model.

  Leading hypothesis, and it is checkable: PRODUCT MISMATCH. Open-Meteo's
  `gfs_seamless` ensemble product is a GFS+GEFS blend at ~50 km resolution
  (documented as lower-resolution, extending to 35 days), while `ecmwf_ifs025`
  is 0.25 deg (~25 km). If the repo requests the coarse seamless product for
  GFS and a finer one for ECMWF, the comparison is between grid resolutions,
  not between forecasting centres -- and reweighting would paper over a fixable
  configuration choice.

  Second hypothesis, with direct precedent IN THIS REPO: member-count asymmetry.
  The far-tail rain entry records that a 16-day request silently fell outside
  icon_seamless's ~7-day and ecmwf_ifs025's ~14-day horizons, leaving "the
  ensemble" as EXACTLY 30 gfs_seamless members with ZERO ECMWF weight, versus a
  ~130-member ~77%-ECMWF ensemble in the near case -- undetectable from the
  logged value alone. Whatever fixed that for rain may not cover temperature.

  Both hypotheses predict the same symptom and need different fixes. Do not
  reweight before establishing which.

What this does NOT establish -- the caveats are load-bearing:
  - n=21 paired cells, one month, summer. Far below this repo's own floors
    (batch-81 derived 112 for a single signal).
  - MAE is not probability skill, and the two DISAGREE here: on unpaired
    per-member Brier the ordering partly inverts, with min-Brier putting
    gfs BEST (0.3613) and ecmwf_ifs025 WORST (0.4008). Any decision must be
    made on Brier over paired cells.
  - The "drop gfs" rows are arithmetic on stored member means, NOT a pipeline
    counterfactual -- the real path applies sigma/EMOS/temperature-scaling on
    top. Direction, not magnitude.
  - Fixing this is not shown to narrow the model-vs-market gap, which is
    measured on a different population (analysis_attempts: model 0.1724 vs
    market 0.1076). Do not assume they combine.

Plan:
  1. Compare the actual Open-Meteo product/resolution requested per model, and
     the member COUNT actually returned per model per call. That is one live
     call and it discriminates both hypotheses.
  2. Re-measure paired, on Brier not MAE, once n clears a defensible floor.
  3. Only then revisit weights, held out the same way the calibration work is.

When to revisit:
  Alongside the recalibration option in the direction entry. These are the two
  cheap, concrete, data-grounded improvements available, and neither is the
  speculative "better model" work the no-edge finding argues against.
